sortKey: 0|9999-99-99|00404|1915 dwight d eisenhower - westpoint and beyond
plotSynopsis: A documentary account of Eisenhower’s formative military years, from West Point and early Army assignments through his marriage to Mamie, professional development under senior officers and the experience that prepared him for eventual Allied supreme command.

plotSynopsis: Cavalcade of America follows William F. Cody through the frontier experiences that make him famous as Buffalo Bill. title: 1849 Cavalcade of America - Edwin Booth
plotSynopsis: Cavalcade of America traces Edwin Booth's development from the son of a celebrated actor into a major American stage performer in his own right. title: 1800 Election Song - Jefferson and Liberty
plotSynopsis: The recording is a short musical performance with no reliably intelligible lyrics or spoken narration in the available exact audio.

sortKey: 0|9999-99-99|00421|1948 election song - im just wild about harry truman

sortKey: 0|9999-99-99|00426|1757 last of the mohicans the part 08

plotSynopsis: John Kennedy reviews federal efforts during the Birmingham civil-rights crisis, praises steps toward negotiation and desegregation and urges white and Black leaders to continue peaceful progress toward equal opportunity.

title: President Eisenhower - on Korea
plotSynopsis: Dwight Eisenhower reflects on the Korean War, saying the United States answered aggression by calling on the courage of its youth and praising the valor of Americans fighting on Korean battlefields.

title: 1874 Cavalcade of America - Humanitarian Urge
plotSynopsis: Cavalcade of America traces changing attitudes toward the protection of children. title: 1962 South Vietnam Youth Prop
plotSynopsis: A South Vietnamese youth pledge declares absolute loyalty to the fatherland and president and a willingness to sacrifice in defense of the country and regime.

title: 1866 Adventures in Research - the Cash Register
sortKey: 0|9999-99-99|00431|1866 adventures in research - the cash register

sortKey: 0|9999-99-99|00432|1960 president john f kennedy - ask not

plotSynopsis: A doctor becomes worried about scientist Farlow, whose recurring dream continues night after night as if he is being transported to another time and place. Each new dream brings armed horsemen closer, and Farlow fears the sequence will eventually reach the moment when they kill him.

title: Beyond Midnight xx-xx-xx (xx) Let Me See Your Face
plotSynopsis: Writer Simon Crutchley, staying at a hotel in Rouen, repeatedly sees a sorrowful woman in a walled garden who disappears before he can reach her. Hotel staff warn him that whatever he does, he must not see the woman's face.

title: Beyond Midnight xx-xx-xx (xx) Maderia Wine
plotSynopsis: Down-and-out Robinson takes a job as clerk at the shabby Sailor's Rest, run by the enormous and unsettling Mrs. Ambrose Manifold. Rumors about her earlier success in Singapore and the recurring smell of Madeira wine suggest that her past has followed her home.

title: Beyond Midnight xx-xx-xx (xx) Man Who Sold His Soul
plotSynopsis: Sir Dominick Sarsfield inherits an Irish estate and rapidly squanders his fortune through gambling, drinking, and racing. Near ruin and despair, he encounters a supernatural bargain that offers relief at a price far more serious than money.

title: Beyond Midnight xx-xx-xx (xx) Mrs Smiff
plotSynopsis: A writer stays with his cousin at a rural vicarage while finishing a book and becomes increasingly fascinated by the attractive housekeeper, Mrs. Smiff. His interest turns to fear when he notices an impossible detail: she casts no shadow.

title: Beyond Midnight xx-xx-xx (xx) My Daddy Had No Gun
plotSynopsis: Riley McGraw kills Stoney Likens but the death is ruled self-defense. Likens's son Verge believes his father was murdered and begins pursuing McGraw, turning the disputed killing into a cycle of revenge.

title: Beyond Midnight xx-xx-xx (xx) Party, The
plotSynopsis: Actress Laura Laine has finally become a star and is preparing to face the press at an opening-night party when the husband she believed dead returns. He knows the secrets behind her carefully rebuilt life and immediately threatens everything she has achieved.

title: Beyond Midnight xx-xx-xx (xx) Something on His Mind
plotSynopsis: Borneo planter George Thring discovers that his wife Rona is having an affair with his business partner Peter Macey. Rather than confront them openly, he devises a grotesque revenge involving one of the huge insects of the jungle.

title: Beyond Midnight xx-xx-xx (xx) Tangled Way
plotSynopsis: Young Alexander Tavert visits an uncle in the Shetlands and becomes disturbed by strange symbols and occult signs around the household. His concern deepens when a female visitor arrives and the family's hidden allegiance appears to place them both in danger.

title: Beyond Midnight xx-xx-xx (xx) Terror Killed the Laughter
plotSynopsis: Kyra Vaughan and her husband encounter Lewis Banning in a remote Carpathian village where local men have been disappearing and villagers whisper about a werewolf. Vaughan and Banning take turns acting as bait while trying to hunt whatever is responsible.

title: Beyond Midnight xx-xx-xx (xx) The Death Wish
plotSynopsis: Ambitious food-industry executive Burton Grunzer, a man with plenty of enemies, is approached by a group whose members practice a form of coordinated voodoo. Their first question is simple and dangerous: has he ever wished someone dead?

title: Beyond Midnight xx-xx-xx (xx) The Locked Room
plotSynopsis: Penniless David Snowden marries young heiress Bonnie Daniels despite the hostility of her wealthy mother. While the newlyweds scheme to escape her interference, David becomes increasingly obsessed with a locked fourth-floor room in the decaying mansion and the secret hidden behind its door.

title: Beyond Midnight xx-xx-xx (xx) The Marble Room
plotSynopsis: Sculptor Boris Yvain develops a chemical process capable of turning living things into marble and reveals the discovery to his friend Alec. The experiment becomes entangled with a romantic triangle and the temptation to use the process on more than sculpture.

title: Beyond Midnight xx-xx-xx (xx) The Room
plotSynopsis: Ronald Todd accepts a large wager to spend the night alone in a supposedly haunted yellow room. Locked inside with candles for light, he discovers that the room can extinguish them one by one without any visible hand.

title: Beyond Midnight xx-xx-xx (xx) The Sheriff's Wife
plotSynopsis: A sheriff becomes convinced that an accused artist has been denied a fair trial and secretly helps him attempt an escape. The act of conscience goes wrong, forcing the sheriff and his wife to face the consequences of challenging frontier justice.

title: Beyond Midnight xx-xx-xx (xx) The Signalman
plotSynopsis: A railway signalman stationed on an isolated stretch of track is haunted by a spectral figure whose appearances seem to warn of terrible accidents. A visitor tries to understand the man's story as the warnings become increasingly specific and ominous.

plotSynopsis: A divinity student is drawn to an abandoned house and secretly watches an old man unlock and enter it. The strange visitor returns regularly to collect a rent that is owed not by the living, but by the ghost of a daughter whose death is tied to an old curse.

title: Beyond Midnight xx-xx-xx (xx) Thing in Cabin 105, The

title: Uncle Gideon Aunt Bessie (1939-11-06)
plotSynopsis: Mr. Dithers wants a model honeymoon cottage that will symbolize happy married life, just as an older couple in the family quarrel and separately flee their home. title: Scrooge (1939-12-25)
plotSynopsis: On Christmas Day, Dagwood complains that Mr. Dithers has given the family nothing and compares him to Scrooge. title: April Fools Day (1940-04-01)

title: Jack the Beanstalk (1940-04-15)

title: The Gypsy Queen (1940-04-22)

title: The Entertainment Committee (1940-05-13)

title: Mr.Dithers Gets Out of the Hospital (1944-04-17)

title: Socialite Blondiesocial Aspirations (1945-05-27)

title: Three Weeks Vacation (1947-07-27)

title: Christmas Show (1948-12-15)
plotSynopsis: Dagwood and Blondie try to discover what Alexander and Cookie want for Christmas without asking them directly. title: Alexanders Valentines Day Dilemma (1949-02-09)
plotSynopsis: Alexander becomes nervous because both Sylvia and Ginger expect to be his Valentine and either choice will anger the other girl. title: Arab in Love with Blondie (1950-01-06)
plotSynopsis: Blondie exchanges recipes with Mustafa bin Akbar Pasha, who visits the Bumsteads and becomes romantically infatuated with her. title: Will Blondie Marry a Middle Easterner (1950-01-13)

title: Alexander the Actor (1950-02-16)
plotSynopsis: Alexander decides to become an actor and adopts an affected theatrical manner that bewilders his family. He practices a sinister voice by frightening Blondie and Dagwood in their bedroom, then abruptly abandons acting for a school judo course and demonstrates his new self-defense move on Dagwood.

title: Fly Worth 2000
plotSynopsis: Dagwood reads that rare insects can be valuable and becomes convinced that a brightly colored fly caught at home is worth two thousand dollars. Alexander eventually admits that he painted an ordinary fly, but Dagwood turns the joke on Mr. Dithers by staging a fake expert appraisal, selling him the fly, and then returning the money after enjoying the prank.

title: Driveride in the Country
plotSynopsis: Mr. Dithers complains that he cannot sleep, and Dagwood promotes a supposedly peaceful drive into the country as the cure. Traffic, arguments with other motorists, roadside mishaps and car trouble turn the restful outing into another exhausting ordeal, leaving the travelers more worn out than relaxed before Dithers finally settles down to rest.

title: The Missing Package
plotSynopsis: Mr. Dithers entrusts Dagwood with five thousand dollars, but Dagwood hides it so carefully that he cannot remember where it is. He searches his dreams and subconscious for the answer while Dithers panics, until Blondie reveals that the money was hidden under the mattress and the missing fortune is recovered.

title: Camping in the Back Yard
plotSynopsis: Dagwood worries that Alexander would rather spend time with friends than with his father, so the two plan a camping trip together. Blondie makes them condition themselves by sleeping outdoors in the backyard, and after several miserable nights she quietly returns their sleeping bags and uses the refund to finance a more comfortable weekend away.

title: Contract Problems
plotSynopsis: Mr. Dithers and Dagwood travel to Sheridan City hoping to win an airport construction contract, but a rival hires a man to provoke Dithers into an assault arrest before the meeting. Blondie uncovers the setup, the hired man exposes the rival's scheme, and the client awards the contract to the Dithers company even while the meeting is held at the police station.

title: Dagwood Raises Chickens While Blondies Away
plotSynopsis: With Blondie away, Dagwood struggles to run the house and decides that raising chickens will save money on eggs. The plan becomes a panic when a diamond earring seems to have been swallowed by one of the birds, but the missing jewel is finally discovered in Dagwood's shirt cuff before Blondie phones home.

title: Storm in a Teacup
plotSynopsis: An overzealous new policeman accuses Blondie of littering when a scrap blows from her handbag and later arrests both her and Mr. Dithers. Blondie rallies women who have had similar trouble with the officer, forcing the mayor to reconsider the situation; the officer resigns rather than accept an unwanted reassignment, and the mayor quickly starts thinking about the next election.

title: The Vacant Lot
plotSynopsis: Blondie reveals that she once bought a nearly worthless vacant lot from a relative, only to find a neighboring factory has long used the property for truck access. When the factory owner bullies the Bumsteads, they discover his building encroaches onto their land and use that leverage to secure an apology and lease the lot back to him for a substantial yearly payment.

title: Blondie Promo W Robert Benchley
plotSynopsis: Robert Benchley appears as a radio critic who visits the Bumsteads after hearing Dagwood's famous rushing exit on the program. Benchley decides to improve Dagwood's racing start, gives him a track-style sendoff, and watches Dagwood shoot out the door while he recommends the Blondie program to listeners.

title: Dagwood Loses Dithers 5000
plotSynopsis: Mr. Dithers entrusts Dagwood with five thousand dollars, but Dagwood hides it so carefully that he cannot remember where it is. He searches his dreams and subconscious for the answer while Dithers panics, until Blondie reveals that the money was hidden under the mattress and the missing fortune is recovered.

title: Inc in Paris W Mr.Mrs.Dithers
plotSynopsis: The Bumsteads and the Dithers arrive in France while Dagwood still faces a threatened duel with Pierre Dupré, an influential man needed for the company's business. Blondie and Cora step in to settle the dispute and uncover a jealous romantic quarrel involving Dupré and Juliette, resolving the crisis when the couple finally become engaged.

title: Circus Outing
plotSynopsis: Dagwood forgets his promise to take Alexander and Cookie to the circus, so the family uses the power of suggestion until he believes the outing is his own brilliant idea. At the circus Alexander becomes determined to keep an animal and threatens to run away and join the show, but Dagwood finds him and brings him home.

title: A Half Million Reasons to Find Gary

plotSynopsis: A company hires Slate to locate a missing pilot who was carrying a half-million-dollar payroll. The first wrecked plane they find is not his, and the search moves to an island where the missing man, the money and rival searchers all become part of the same dangerous chase.

plotSynopsis: Sailor faces the threat of being forced out of Havana while Slate is drawn into a scheme involving an attractive woman, planted documents and accusations of espionage. plotSynopsis: During a violent Havana storm, a frightened young woman arrives at Shannon's Place and Slate and Sailor try to keep her away from people who are after her. title: The Mystery of the Mary K
plotSynopsis: Slate and Sailor find a drifting lifeboat containing four dead men from the Mary K, a ship believed lost long before. Their investigation leads to a clandestine operation transporting refugees toward the United States and disposing of passengers who become a liability.

title: Death At The Wedding
plotSynopsis: A newlywed couple checks into Shannon's Place just as a man is found poisoned, and a private investigator connected to the case is later killed on the beach. plotSynopsis: Slateâ€™s old oil-field partner Matt Wallace returns after twelve years with news that he has finally struck oil and intends to honor their old promise to share the find. title: Voodoo Vendetta
plotSynopsis: A charter to a remote plantation turns deadly after Mrs. Ramsey admits killing her husband and prevents Slate and Sailor from leaving. Surrounded by armed danger and local voodoo beliefs, Slate must act quickly when Sailor is struck by a poisoned dart and begins to weaken.

title: The Search for Tommy Reed
plotSynopsis: Mrs. Reed asks Slate to find her missing husband, whose letters have kept arriving even though he vanished into the Caribbean. Slate discovers that the real Tommy Reed is already dead and that forged letters and an impostor are keeping the deception alive, then the case turns murderous before he can bring the truth home.

plotSynopsis: A diver recruits Slate and the Bold Venture to search a Caribbean wreck for a cargo of gold, but the expedition attracts rivals willing to kill for the location. After ambushes, a missing diver and a dangerous descent, Slate and Sailor recover gold from the wreck and turn the find over to the authorities, apart from one ingot Sailor briefly claims for her hope chest.

plotSynopsis: Slate is reunited with Jenny Ward, an old flame from his wandering days, but the reunion quickly turns into a trap. title: Terminal Key
plotSynopsis: After Mickey is killed, Slate follows a terminal locker key that points to locker 68 and a hidden $100,000. The money draws in the men who murdered Mickey, and Slate uses the locker as bait until the killer comes for the cash and exposes himself.

plotSynopsis: Sailor talks Slate into a formal party aboard the S.S. Huron and rents him a tuxedo for the occasion. title: Murder in the Yucatan Peninsula
plotSynopsis: A former guest, Mr. Raimi, calls Slate to YucatÃ¡n after his wife Martha disappears. title: Slate Shannon Sucker
plotSynopsis: Sailor distrusts a young man named Frank Jordan even as Slate gives him the benefit of the doubt. title: Slate Shannon Held for Ransom
plotSynopsis: A search connected to a missing man and the people around Shannon's Place ends with Slate captured by armed criminals. plotSynopsis: During carnival festivities, an artificial camellia passes through Slate's hands and suddenly attracts armed men who are far more interested in the flower than in him. title: Passage for Mario Carada
plotSynopsis: Slate is paid to bring Mario Carada to Havana, only to find the young man bloodied, hunted and determined to avenge his father. title: Darby and Joan Incorporated
plotSynopsis: An elderly widow who has seen Slate's photograph through the Darby and Joan lonely-hearts organization arrives at Shannon's Place determined to marry him. plotSynopsis: Slate and Sailor rescue two men from a small boat, only to be taken hostage when the supposed fishermen reveal themselves as mutineers from the S.S. Marino Victory. title: Slates Stolen Da Vinci
plotSynopsis: A modest painting by a struggling artist suddenly attracts an art dealer willing to pay far more than it appears to be worth. title: Paolo Framed for Jewel Robbery
plotSynopsis: Paolo, a young man Slate knows from an earlier brush with crime, is accused of a jewel robbery and then found shot. title: Cruise To Batabano
plotSynopsis: Slate agrees to deliver a boat to Batabano, but the errand turns deadly when the man waiting for it is killed by a booby-trapped door. title: Escape From Guantanamo
plotSynopsis: Slate is asked to find escaped killer Paul Brewer and return him to his father before more people die. The retrieval becomes a three-sided hunt when another armed man is also looking for Paul, and a mistaken killing exposes a deeper deception about who is pursuing whom and why.

title: Crazy Old Carlo
plotSynopsis: Slate and Sailor run into Carlo, an eccentric fisherman who has sold his boat and started giving his money away because he believes someone is going to kill him. title: An Invitation to Death

title: A Backstabbing at Shannons Place
plotSynopsis: A man believed to be Joe Norman turns up alive after Norman has already been buried, then is stabbed at Shannonâ€™s Place. Slate and Sailor dig into the conflicting identities, the widowâ€™s story and a pending insurance payment, uncovering a fraud built around the wrong body and more than one murder.

title: Im Going To Die
plotSynopsis: Rhoda, an old friend of Slateâ€™s, is convinced that her mother killed her father and is now slowly killing her too. title: Man From Sumatra
plotSynopsis: A newly returned traveler tells Slate and Sailor about a Sumatran gold venture, then violence follows him into Havana. As Slate tracks a huge attacker, telegrams and the dead manâ€™s former partners, the story of a lost fortune becomes the center of a murder and double-cross.

title: Introduction to the OTRR
plotSynopsis: An Old Time Radio Researchers Group introduction explains the volunteer organization’s mission to preserve classic radio, improve and verify surviving recordings, correct dating and title errors, certify researched series, maintain logs and databases, and distribute completed collections freely rather than for profit.

title: The Oil Swindle
plotSynopsis: George investigates the Guaranteed Always Flowing Oil Development Company and is warned to stop asking questions, while Susan becomes the target of the promoters’ charm. Their jealousy briefly works against them, but the pair uncover the swindle, overpower the operators and turn the attempted con into another Morning Star exposé.

title: Bright Star Series Brief
plotSynopsis: A short overview of Bright Star identifies Irene Dunne as newspaper editor Susan Armstrong and Fred MacMurray as reporter George Harvey. It summarizes both stars’ screen careers, notes the program’s single-season run, and describes the series as a light comedy built around the pair’s rapport and newsroom conflicts.

title: Susan Runs for Mayor
plotSynopsis: A reform group recruits Susan to run for mayor, but George objects when crooked political figures appear on her slate. Susan ultimately uses a radio appearance to expose the machine’s corruption rather than protect her candidacy, helping an honest opponent win while George admits he is relieved she will not have mayoral kissing duties.

title: Fred Mac Murray Bio
plotSynopsis: This biographical feature traces Fred MacMurray from his Wisconsin upbringing and early music work through Broadway and Paramount films, including Double Indemnity, The Caine Mutiny and The Apartment. It also notes his Bright Star role as reporter George Harvey and his long television run as Steve Douglas on My Three Sons.

title: Hillsdale Becomes Mumdad
plotSynopsis: Susan’s work with children leads her and George into pretending to be parents while the Morning Star struggles with its own problems. The make-believe family produces fires, police trouble and other disasters, but George’s willingness to defend the children eventually earns him both journalistic praise and Susan’s affectionate approval.

title: Harry Von Zell Bio
plotSynopsis: This profile follows announcer and actor Harry von Zell from local radio in the 1920s to national announcing work with Bing Crosby, Eddie Cantor and Burns and Allen. It recalls his famous Herbert Hoover verbal slip, later film and television appearances, his role on The Burns and Allen Show, and his posthumous broadcasting-hall recognition.

title: Miss America Visits
plotSynopsis: An emergency landing brings Miss America to Hillsdale and gives George a glamorous story just as he and Susan are arguing over his future at the paper. Their professional and romantic maneuvering escalates into competing job offers and threatened departures before George decides that the Morning Star, and Susan, are where he wants to stay.

title: George the Informer
plotSynopsis: George’s sensational stories about gangster Joe Mentelli appear to come from a daring inside source, but Susan discovers that timid cashier Charlie Collins has been feeding him plots adapted from crime magazines. The fantasy becomes dangerous when Mentelli reacts to the articles, and the deception collapses once the magazine sources are exposed.

title: Irene Dunne Bio
plotSynopsis: This biography reviews Irene Dunne’s childhood music training, studies at Chicago Music College, transition into films, five Academy Award nominations and retirement from motion pictures in 1952. It also covers her Bright Star role as editor Susan Armstrong and her later charity, public-service and United Nations work.

title: The Crooked Carnival
plotSynopsis: George suspects the concessions at a visiting carnival are crooked even as Susan keeps winning prizes. His investigation leads him behind the midway, where he expects to expose another fraud but instead winds up confronting a loose lion and subduing it with a tent stake, turning his skepticism into the Morning Star’s biggest story of the day.

title: The Boxer
plotSynopsis: Susan champions middleweight contender Shock Powers while George distrusts the fighter’s publicity games. Shock privately admits that being hated is part of his box-office strategy, but his divided attention and overconfidence lead to a first-round knockout, giving George the last word and Susan a lesson in separating promotion from performance.

title: Dramatic Lessons
plotSynopsis: A retired actor persuades George to study dramatic technique, and Susan uses his theatrical ambitions to needle him. When real safecrackers break into the Morning Star, George’s bravado fails at first, but Susan tricks the robbers into the vault and the pair turn the crime into George’s most convincing dramatic performance.

title: French Dress Designer
plotSynopsis: A celebrated French designer arrives in Hillsdale and monopolizes Susan’s time while creating a wardrobe for her, leaving George openly jealous. George counters by befriending a talented local designer, and the rivalry ends when the Frenchman recognizes her ability and takes her to France to work with him.

title: George Covers Hillsdale Fire
plotSynopsis: Susan turns Pendleton Martin, a man associated with a major hotel fire, into a front-page hero despite George’s warnings about his character. Their argument sends George briefly to a rival paper, but Susan’s campaign collapses when police uncover evidence that Martin is actually the firebug who started the blaze.

title: George Coaches Hillsdale High
plotSynopsis: After ridiculing Hillsdale High’s football team in print, George is pushed into coaching it himself and clashes with the former coach. The coach’s daughter Sharon ultimately takes charge for the big game, combining what she learned from both men so that a victory can restore credit to each of them.

title: The Haunted House
plotSynopsis: George investigates a supposedly haunted house and stumbles into a counterfeit-money operation connected to gangster Joe Roberti. After George is knocked unconscious and Susan is drawn into the danger, the criminals are exposed and the Morning Star gets a major crime story out of what began as a ghost assignment.

title: Rodeo Star
plotSynopsis: Susan assigns George to cover rodeo star Bobby Brundage, and his lack of western experience quickly turns the assignment into a comic ordeal. George’s growing friendship with Bobby makes Susan jealous, but the visiting star ultimately pairs off with another Brooklyn-born admirer while George proves himself in the arena and returns to Susan.

title: Scientific Living
plotSynopsis: Susan tries to apply Dr. Lionel Hawker’s system of scientific living and romantic psychology, first on George and then on Hawker himself. George turns the method back on her with a jealousy scheme involving another woman, and the supposedly scientific experiment ends with Hawker headed for Alaska and Susan and George laughing at the formulas.

title: New Homemaker Page Editor
plotSynopsis: George hires attractive Marie Carroll to run a new homemaker page, and Susan becomes convinced that Marie’s domestic skills are also winning George. After Susan tries to compete at home, George reveals that his interest was journalistic: Marie is remarrying her former husband for the third time, giving the paper an exclusive story.

title: George's Old Flame
plotSynopsis: An old college flame arrives for a convention and quickly revives Susan’s jealousy, while Patience and Sammy try to keep the visitor from settling in at Susan’s house. Susan retaliates by producing an old sweetheart of her own, and the competing houseguests force Susan and George into a comic contest over who can make the other more jealous.

title: Aunt Sophia Plays Matchmaker
plotSynopsis: Susan’s visiting Aunt Sophia decides that Susan and George need help admitting their feelings. She engineers a string of jealous misunderstandings, including hiring a woman to pose as a wife, and the exasperated pair finally concede that the aunt has forced them to notice what they already feel for each other.

title: The Talking Parrot
plotSynopsis: George pays heavily for a parrot said to know the location of hidden treasure, and he and Susan spend days trying to make the bird reveal its secret. They eventually realize the “treasure” is not pirate gold at all but the parrot’s bond with a little girl and her grandfather, and George lets the bird return to them despite his lost investment.

title: Patience's Romance
plotSynopsis: Patience secretly places a lonely-hearts advertisement using Susan’s home address, alarming Susan and drawing George into an attempt to manage the responses. What looks like Patience seeking a husband turns out to involve a friend and a business proposition, and the confusion ends with Patience paid for her recipes and George rewarded with a special dinner.

title: Sammy and Shirley
plotSynopsis: Sammy’s romance with Shirley becomes confused when George mistakes Shirley’s older cousin for the girl Sammy has been seeing. Susan deliberately lets the misunderstanding grow until George is caught between the glamorous cousin and her jealous beau, after which Susan exposes the mix-up and enjoys George’s embarrassment.

title: Fight for Beaver Park
plotSynopsis: Susan leads the Morning Star against businessman Horace Briggs’s plan to replace historic Beaver Park, even after he threatens to withdraw valuable advertising. George helps keep the campaign alive until Briggs abandons the redevelopment and agrees to support improvements to the park instead.

title: Susan's Cousin Emily
plotSynopsis: Teenage cousin Emily arrives full of romantic fantasies and tales of a dangerous gangster boyfriend, prompting George to use psychology by pretending to fall passionately in love with her. The scheme puts George in genuine danger when real gangsters mistake him for a rival, and Susan has to pose as his domineering wife to help get him out safely.

title: Susan's Poetry
plotSynopsis: Susan’s secretly submitted poems are rejected, so George argues that modern poetry is easy and proves it by sending in a deliberately nonsensical poem that is accepted. Their rivalry carries them into a gathering of eccentric poets, where the experience convinces George that writing verse may be more dangerous than reporting the news.

title: A Flower for Susan
plotSynopsis: Susan receives roses from a mysterious admirer while George is assigned to entertain a visiting advertising buyer. Their attempts to hide their jealousy escalate into romantic counterplots, until each admits to manipulating the situation because neither wanted the other carried away by a rival.

title: Box Supper
plotSynopsis: At a charity box supper, Susan and George are separated from the partners they expected and end up dining with strangers Willie and Wanda. Each secretly exaggerates the stranger’s wealth to the other, accidentally encouraging Willie and Wanda toward marriage, while Patience and Sammy add to the chaos by landing in jail for speeding.

title: The Chorus Girl
plotSynopsis: George’s old friend Elwood brings chorus girl Sonny Knight into Susan’s house and creates the impression that George has a romantic past with her. Susan answers the misunderstanding with a performance of her own, and the pair finally expose Elwood’s meddling while admitting that jealousy has made the whole affair larger than it ever was.

title: The Society Burglar
plotSynopsis: George’s obsession with a mysterious society burglar makes him suspicious when Susan is seen with a well-dressed stranger around the time of another robbery. The supposed romantic mystery and the burglary investigation collide, but the actual crooks are caught and George’s jealous assumptions leave him more embarrassed than triumphant.

title: One Word Cablegram
plotSynopsis: A cryptic cable from Scotland sends Susan and George into a tangle involving a visitor, Scottish customs and repeated misunderstandings over an inheritance and romance. By the time the visiting relatives sort out who is marrying whom and who is going back to Scotland, George is left asking Susan for one favor he now understands perfectly: cook him some haggis.

title: Missing Childhood Sweetheart
plotSynopsis: A lonely visitor asks the Morning Star to help locate the girl he remembers loving in childhood. Susan and George discover that the woman he has idealized for decades is not what either expected, but their matchmaking finally reunites the old sweethearts and leaves George contemplating, then quickly retreating from, the lesson about not waiting too long.

title: George's Old Girlfriend
plotSynopsis: A letter from George’s past and Sammy’s trouble impressing a girlfriend create a chain of false identities at the Morning Star. When gangster Muggsy Crane storms in over an unfavorable story, George’s attempt to play editor gets him knocked out, and the resulting confusion leaves Susan once again holding the upper hand.

title: Susan's Cousin, Emily (Last Show)
plotSynopsis: Emily returns claiming an engagement to Peter Andrews, and Susan and George mistakenly assume she means a much older man. George tries to break the romance by pretending Emily has transferred her affection to him, only to discover that the fiancé is actually Peter Andrews Jr., leaving George and Susan to laugh over another needless intervention.

title: Operation In A Shack (1937-11-07)
plotSynopsis: Dr. Christian leaves Rivers End for a fishing vacation with Swampy and reaches a remote river shack to find young Jimmy unconscious with a ruptured appendix. The nearest hospital is about seventy miles away and Jimmy cannot survive the trip, while the doctor has neither surgical instruments nor proper facilities. Faced with almost certain death if he does nothing, Dr. Christian improvises an operating room in the shack, boiling water and using the knives and materials available to perform the emergency operation. Jimmy survives, and news of the feat brings Dr. Christian unexpected professional attention and the possibility of greater opportunities in the city. He ultimately remains in Rivers End, reminded that the ordinary patients who depend on their country doctor are the work he chose.

title: Steve Charlotte Story (1937-11-14)
plotSynopsis: After receiving national praise for one of her poems, Charlotte Dixon decides that ordinary life in Rivers End and marriage to dependable Steve are stifling her artistic future. She plans to divorce him and go to the city for a literary career, insisting that she no longer loves the commonplace husband she once chose. Dr. Christian sees that Charlotte is romanticizing freedom, so he recruits sophisticated Barbara Powell to make a convincing show of being interested in Steve. At the town picnic Charlotte's confidence in leaving evaporates as she watches Steve apparently fall for another woman. When she abandons the divorce and demands another chance, Steve carries the charade far enough to make her face what losing him would mean, then admits he loves only Charlotte. Dr. Christian reveals that Barbara's romance with Steve was arranged to give Charlotte something more real than poetry to think about.

title: Tanzy Story (1937-11-21)
plotSynopsis: Mrs. Tansy has spent years doing everything for a household of grown children and in-laws who love her but take her labor completely for granted. They plan a birthday supper in her honor without noticing that she will still be expected to cook it, clean up and continue waiting on everyone. When Christian sees how thoughtlessly they depend on her, he makes the family believe her heart requires complete rest and orders her to bed. Faced for the first time with cooking, housekeeping and supporting themselves without Mrs. Tansy, the family members are forced into responsibility: the unemployed son-in-law must work, the daughter has to use her business training, and the children learn how much their mother has quietly been doing. Mrs. Tansy improves while the household learns to function around her instead of through her. Christian later admits that she had not actually been ill; putting her to bed was his way of teaching the family what life would be like without her and of making them appreciate her before it was too late.

title: Susan The Opera Singer (1937-11-28)
plotSynopsis: Local singer Susan believes her great chance has arrived when famous opera star Sigrid Holmquist and impresario Otto Kaufman visit Rivers End. Desperate to be heard, Susan even asks Dr. Christian to keep Holmquist from singing at a charity concert when the star seems to be catching a cold, but he refuses to manufacture an opportunity for her. After Holmquist performs brilliantly, Dr. Christian explains that the star once struggled for years through rejection, poor jobs and relentless study before she was ready. Susan accepts that she still has work to do, and Holmquist warmly invites her to come backstage after the next concert, giving her encouragement without pretending success can be rushed.

title: Blind Boy Story (1937-12-05)
plotSynopsis: Dr. Christian saves a mysterious man who has taken poison and is determined to try again rather than face the disgrace and consequences waiting for him at home. Instead of turning him over to anyone, the doctor asks for a few more hours and takes him on an early-morning call to a poor farm family. There the man meets fourteen-year-old Robert, blind from birth with congenital cataracts, whose family has sacrificed for years to pay for an operation. Dr. Christian removes Robert's bandages and the boy sees his mother, his dog, his home and the dawn for the first time, declaring the world wonderful. Witnessing that joy gives the despairing man a new perspective. He abandons his plan to die and chooses to return home and face his troubles, while Dr. Christian compares life to a game that can be started again after a loss.

title: Mother in law Story (1937-12-12)
plotSynopsis: Wilma Parker and Howard Ross have repeatedly tried to marry, but Howard's devotion to his widowed mother keeps interfering. He has already sacrificed a promising job rather than leave Mrs. Ross, and another illness on their wedding day postpones the ceremony for a third time. The town begins to believe Mrs. Ross is deliberately preventing the marriage, and she finally admits to Dr. Christian that she does not want Howard to marry because she fears losing the son around whom she has built her life. Wilma feels humiliated and rejected, while Howard becomes too proud and angry to repair the break. During a heavy snowstorm Howard is working on a utility line when he slips and is seriously injured. With telephone lines down and Howard missing for hours, Wilma and Mrs. Ross are left together for seven agonizing hours, each fearing that the man they both love may die. Their rivalry gives way to honesty: Mrs. Ross admits she was wrong to treat Wilma as someone taking Howard away, and both realize there was room in his life for them both. Howard survives, and after the crisis the wedding finally takes place. Christian later observes that giving the two women time alone to talk accomplished what argument could not.

title: Young Fellow Who Stole An Auto (1937-12-19)
plotSynopsis: Danny returns to Rivers End for Christmas pretending to be a wealthy New York success, complete with expensive clothes and a car. When the car is identified as stolen, Dr. Christian learns that Danny had actually been working at a parking lot and, desperate to hide his failure and homesickness, took a customers car for what he intended as a short trip home. Dr. Christians testimony helps the court see the difference between a foolish, frightened mistake and a criminal career, and Danny is acquitted and decides to stay home and rebuild honestly.

title: Woman Who Runs Dress Store (1937-12-26)
plotSynopsis: Harriet Niles runs a successful dress shop in Rivers End and is raising her young daughter Toby in peace, but Harriet is living under an assumed name. She is actually Doris Fleming, widow of a notorious man who murdered one of her former admirers, was convicted and later died in prison. Dr. Christian helped Doris make a new start so Toby could grow up without carrying her fathers scandal. A self-righteous local man named John discovers the secret and insists that Harriet surrender her daughter, arguing that a child should not be raised by a woman with such a past. He pressures and effectively blackmails her until Harriet prepares to leave town and even considers giving Toby up. Dr. Christian investigates John in return and confronts him with what appears to be an official California report showing that he too served time in prison. Terrified of exposure, John confesses that he did spend five years in San Quentin and admits that bitterness over the woman involved in his own case has driven his crusade against Harriet. The report is actually from the state agriculture department; Dr. Christian needed only Johns confession. Rather than expose him, the doctor offers to help cure his resentment, while Harriet and Toby are allowed to keep their home and life in Rivers End.

title: Kidnapped Husband - Amos Spills the Beans (1938-01-02)
plotSynopsis: Henry Harris appears to have been kidnapped, drugged and released after a frightening ordeal, and the town treats him with new respect. Dr. Christian notices that the bottle used for the supposed knockout drops is actually an old prescription bottle he had given Henry months earlier. Confronted with the evidence, Henry admits that he staged the entire kidnapping because he was tired of being dismissed as his wealthy wife’s weak, dependent husband and wanted to prove that he had courage and importance of his own.

title: Auto Accident (1938-01-09)
plotSynopsis: On a snowy New Year's Eve, newly employed Dave Fenton is struck by a hit-and-run car outside the power plant and left with a dangerous brain concussion. Wealthy Marion Brooks soon admits that her own new coupe skidded at the same curve at about the same time, damaging its rear fender, and that she drove on because she was hurrying to a party. Convinced she may have hit Dave, Marion first looks for a way her money and position can protect her, but Dr. Christian forces her to face what the Fenton family would lose. By the time she decides to confess and help them, police report that another driver, Foster, has surrendered: the parked car at the curve was hit twice, and Marion caused only the earlier collision. The narrow escape leaves her changed even though she was not the hit-and-run driver.

title: Flood Story (1938-01-16)
plotSynopsis: Senator Conway offers Dr. Christian an important Washington appointment heading a national medical commission, with Judy to accompany him as secretary, and the opportunity is important enough that Christian seriously considers leaving Rivers End. Before he can decide, warm rain breaks an upstream ice jam and the river floods. Christian moves through the stricken area treating injuries and directing care while Judy, Jerry Turner and Senator Conway's son Bill throw themselves into rescue work. Bill's willingness to work beside everyone else changes jealous Jerry's opinion of his romantic rival. More importantly, the emergency makes clear just how completely the town depends on its doctor. Even Bill admits that taking Christian away would cost Rivers End something it cannot replace. Christian turns down Washington and decides that he and Judy will continue doing business at the same old stand, while Jerry and Bill agree to let the best man win where Judy is concerned.

title: Dog Story (1938-01-23)
plotSynopsis: Ten-year-old Tip finds a stray dog he names Jeff while his parents, Eleanor and Dick, are drifting toward a marital breakup. Eleanor believes Dick is involved with another woman, while Dick admits he has become infatuated and says the marriage is finished. Before the separation can harden, Tip falls through the ice on a pond and survives while Jeff dies in the same crisis. Their sons near loss and the dogs death force Dick and Eleanor to recognize how much they have taken for granted; they reconcile, later take Tip on a second honeymoon trip, and help him begin healing with a new puppy without pretending Jeff can be replaced.

title: The New Stove (1938-01-30)
plotSynopsis: After Charlie Lane dies, his adult children decide that their seventy-five-year-old mother should give up the modest house where she spent nearly fifty years and move into daughter Ella's modern, comfortable home. They mean well, but their efficiency removes everything that made Mrs. Lane feel useful and at home. She is served breakfast in bed, forbidden to help in the kitchen and surrounded by unfamiliar furniture, while she longs for her old carved bed, familiar kitchen, household work and the ordinary routines of her own place. Christian prescribes daily walks and later discovers that Mrs. Lane has secretly been walking back to the shuttered old house just to sit among the things she misses. The cold, damp visits leave her dangerously ill. Rather than keep treating only the illness, Christian tells the family that they have uprooted her identity along with her furniture. Against conventional caution he moves her back to the little brown house, warms it, restores the familiar surroundings and lets the family understand that independence and usefulness are part of her health. Mrs. Lane revives when she realizes she can stay there for good, and the family completes the homecoming with the kind of kitchen stove she wanted. Christian's cure is not modern comfort but restoring her desire to live in a place that still feels like her own life.

title: The Man With The Paralyzed Arm (1938-02-06)
plotSynopsis: A drifting young man calling himself Homer Moore arrives in Rivers End with one arm apparently paralyzed and a string of inconsistent stories about his past. His deep knowledge of music finally gives him away: Dr. Christian discovers that Homer is actually a composer and pianist whose career ended after an automobile accident. Homer had spent his life terrified that an injury would someday take away the hand he needed to play, and after the accident that fear became so powerful that he accepted the arm as permanently useless even though Christian can find no physical reason for the paralysis. To break the belief, Christian pretends to spill dangerous acid and cries for a towel. Homer instinctively grabs it with the supposedly useless hand. Christian reveals that the 'acid' was only distilled water and explains that the arm had remained physically sound. Freed from the fear that had trapped him, Homer can move his hand again and realizes he can return to music.

title: War Story (1938-02-20)
plotSynopsis: While playing checkers in Rivers End, Dr. Christian recalls an experience from his service as a medical officer during the First World War. In a village behind the lines he met a terrified young soldier everyone called Slim, who announced that he would desert rather than move to the front and challenged Christian to shoot him if he tried to leave. Instead of condemning him, Christian admitted that everyone was frightened and got Slim talking about the Indiana farm where he grew up and the farm of his own he dreamed of someday owning beside a river. Christian urged him to hold onto that picture strongly enough to carry him through the fear. Slim returned to his unit, was later brought into Christian's overcrowded dressing station badly wounded, and Christian defied orders limiting treatment in order to operate and give him a chance to live. Christian never learned what became of him. Years later in Rivers End, he is called to a newly purchased farm where a man named Catherwood is gravely ill from an infected cut that was neglected because he and his wife had spent nearly everything securing the farm. Under ether the patient relives the wartime encounter, revealing that he is Slim. Christian recognizes him and again uses the same hard-won dream of a farm by the river as something to fight for. Slim survives. Unable to pay much in cash, he settles the doctor's bill with firewood and eggs, and Christian tells Judy that the farm itself did more to pull the man through than any medicine he gave him.

title: Milk Racket Pt1 (1938-02-27)
plotSynopsis: A series of suspicious highway crashes has been wrecking milk trucks around Rivers End, and the latest collision kills a driver. Witnesses place young Bob Marvin on the truck that caused the fatal wreck, leaving him facing a manslaughter charge even though he says he was not driving and refuses to identify the man who was. Dr. Christian and attorney James Benson Clark discover that Bob's unusually well-paid job with the Farmers' Protective Organization may connect him to a protection racket that has been targeting milk dealers who do not cooperate. Bob is indicted and the case is rushed toward trial. Then a representative of the organization offers Dr. Christian first $20,000 and then $30,000 to leave the state before he can testify. Christian refuses, and the man answers with a direct threat that the doctor will never reach the witness stand, ending the first part with the racket openly moving against him.

title: Milk Racket Pt2 (1938-03-06)
plotSynopsis: As Bob Marvin's manslaughter trial approaches, Dr. Christian keeps digging into the Farmers Protective Organization behind a series of deliberately wrecked milk trucks. He learns that frightened dairymen have joined the organization simply to stop the attacks, confirming that the supposed protection plan is really a racket, and the men behind it increase their threats against him. During an emergency childbirth call, armed men arrive to take Dr. Christian away; he persuades them to let him save the mother and baby first, then keeps his word and goes with them, setting up the final confrontation in the next chapter.

title: Milk Racket Pt3 (1938-03-13)
plotSynopsis: The three-part milk-racket story reaches its conclusion with Dr. Christian kidnapped by the men behind the Farmers Protective Organization so he cannot testify in Bob Marvinâ€™s murder trial. While he is being held in a secluded house, one of the gang, Charles Moran, arrives badly wounded after violence involving a milk truck. Dr. Christian refuses to treat the injury as a simple patch-up and insists that Moran needs hospital care to survive. His captors finally allow him to take the wounded man in, costing Dr. Christian his chance to appear at the trial, but Bob is acquitted anyway when the prosecution cannot prove he was driving the truck connected with the killing. After Dr. Christian saves Moranâ€™s life, Moran repays him with a sworn confession describing the racket and identifying the people behind it. Dr. Christian then confronts the powerful attorney Mr. Clark, whose public defense of Bob had hidden his own connection to the organization. Clark destroys only a copy of Moranâ€™s statement before learning that the original is already with the district attorney. An officer waiting nearby arrests him, ending the racket and vindicating Dr. Christianâ€™s suspicions.

title: Story Of Prisoners Child (1938-03-20)
plotSynopsis: Seven-year-old Patty Elliott is gravely ill, with her mother dead and her devoted father Walt in prison for an old theft he voluntarily confessed to years after rebuilding his life. Convinced that medicine alone will not save the child, Dr. Christian races to the state capital and refuses to accept the normal timetable for parole, arguing that Walt's return is urgently part of Patty's treatment. After an exhausting overnight fight for his release, Dr. Christian brings Walt home. Patty, whom another doctor believed might not survive the morning, revives almost immediately once her father is beside her.

title: Story Of Windy The Truth Pills (1938-03-27)
plotSynopsis: Windy Smith's lifelong habit of telling outrageous stories makes him the easy suspect when money disappears from Clem Duke's store. Windy answers the accusation with an even wilder tale about armed gangsters, while Clem insists he must be guilty. Dr. Christian quietly turns the matter around with supposed truth pills that are nothing but sugar. Believing the medicine has forced honesty on him, Clem confesses that he took the money himself, lost it playing poker and blamed Windy because he was afraid to face his wife. Windy, who swallowed the same harmless pill, immediately launches into another impossible bandit story, proving that some habits are stronger than any imaginary cure.

title: Story Of Harry Monroe A Scarf (1938-04-03)
plotSynopsis: Judy's married friend Isabel Taylor feels trapped by quiet domestic life and secretly goes out with former beau Harry Monroe while her husband Kenneth is away. Harry has been drinking and drives his car into a ditch; frightened that he may be badly hurt, Isabel runs home and leaves behind a scarf she had borrowed from Judy. When the scarf is found in Harry's car, local gossip Edna assumes Judy was the woman with him. Judy claims the scarf rather than expose Isabel, even though the story could damage Judy's own reputation. Dr. Christian eventually gets the truth from her and turns the scarf into the solution. During a talk to Edna's club on first aid, he uses it to demonstrate an emergency sling and casually says that he himself left the scarf in Harry's car while treating Harry after the accident. The explanation protects Isabel, clears Judy without betraying her friend, and leaves Edna with no scandal to spread.

title: Landslide (1938-04-10)
plotSynopsis: A spring storm drives Jerry Turner and Jack Wilson into Echo Caverns, where Jerry crawls into a newly discovered passage just before a rockslide seals the opening behind him. Dr. Christian leads a difficult river rescue through darkness, rough water and motor trouble, but the rescuers discover that the passage has shifted and Jerry is no longer where expected. Dr. Christian enters the cave and finds Jerry, only for another slide to cut them off together. Their escape finally comes through a hidden route known by a reclusive local who has long guarded the caverns secrets, explaining the mysterious lights seen around the cave and bringing the trapped men safely out.

title: The Dishonest Boy (1938-04-17)
plotSynopsis: Russell Brandt steals his poor report card before his parents can see it and tries to shift suspicion onto Ira Nelson, his father's elderly longtime bookkeeper. The lie becomes dangerous because Mr. Brandt has already been considering dismissing Ira as no longer useful to the business. Dr. Christian questions Russell closely, catches the contradictions in his story and forces him to admit that he took the report card and falsely accused Ira. When Russell finally confesses, Dr. Christian reminds his angry father that honesty and courage are learned rather than automatic, and that Russell's lie did not create the father's willingness to discard a loyal old employee. The boy is held accountable, but his decision to tell the truth becomes the beginning of making things right.

title: Joe Perino (1938-04-24)
plotSynopsis: Dr. Christian is surprised one evening when Rivers End residents gather to introduce a successful visitor named Joe Perino, a man the doctor knew years earlier in Chicago. The meeting brings back the story of Joe as a delinquent boy arrested with a gang after a jewelry-store robbery. Although a judge is ready to send him to reform school, Dr. Christian argues that Joe has never had a fair chance, assumes responsibility for him and persuades the court to suspend sentence. He then convinces the very jeweler who was robbed to take Joe as an unpaid apprentice, even offering to guarantee any loss himself. The trust works. Joe learns the watch trade, eventually goes into business for himself and becomes successful. Now grown, he has tracked down the doctor who once believed in him and repays that faith on a scale no one expects: he donates $100,000 to build the modern Rivers End hospital Dr. Christian has long dreamed of, asking that it bear the doctors name.

title: Baby On Doorstep (1938-10-18)
plotSynopsis: An unidentified infant is left on Dr. Christian's doorstep with no note or label. Although several experienced mothers offer to adopt him, the bachelor doctor decides to keep the baby himself until the person with the strongest claim appears, and over the next six months he and Judy become deeply attached to the child. One day Lila Bronson, a woman Dr. Christian knew when she was younger, comes in with a sprained ankle. The doctor notices that her toes overlap in the same distinctive way as the baby's, and when she hears the child and asks to see him her emotional reaction confirms what he suspects. Lila has returned for the son she abandoned. Rather than accuse or shame her, Dr. Christian asks whether she would like to adopt the baby and raise him as her own, quietly restoring mother and child while admitting he knew that if he waited long enough the right person would come back.

title: Boy Loves Girl (1938-10-25)
plotSynopsis: Teenagers Hazel Miller and Bill are secretly in love and plan to marry when Hazel is eighteen, but their parents regard the relationship as childish and would separate them if they knew. Dr. Christian is aware of the romance and urges the adults to remember their own youth rather than treat the pair with contempt. After a disgruntled former employee exposes the secret, the parents react exactly as Hazel and Bill feared. The two run away to a mountain shack and, convinced they will be forced apart forever, begin talking about dying together like Romeo and Juliet. Hazel impulsively takes a pistol and shoots herself before Bill can stop her. Christian reaches the shack in time and finds that the bullet has only torn her side and the wound is not fatal. The near tragedy finally forces both families to take the young couple seriously. Their parents consent to an engagement, while marriage is postponed until Hazel and Bill are older and ready.

title: Dr Christian For Mayor (1938-11-01)
plotSynopsis: John Hewitt withdraws from the Rivers End mayoral race and decides that Dr. Christian should replace him, launching a draft movement before the doctor can refuse. The town embraces the idea so enthusiastically that Christian's office becomes campaign headquarters, civic groups demand promises for playgrounds, pensions, sidewalks, fountains and lower taxes, and his medical work is increasingly disrupted. Christian wants no part of politics, but Hewitt's supporters reinterpret every refusal to campaign as proof of his devotion to duty. At the public meeting Christian finally finds a medical way to cure the town of its political fever. He describes the costly demands being made on the next mayor and then makes the voters confront the fact that electing him would also mean giving up the doctor they rely on. The crowd quickly decides it needs Dr. Christian more as a physician than as a politician. Christian gives his support to the practical and experienced Hewitt, while the town names Christian honorary mayor as an expression of affection. He accepts the honorary title happily, having preserved both his practice and his friendship with the community.

title: Tony Donella (1938-11-08)
plotSynopsis: On a bitter night Dr. Christian answers a call to the cramped home of Tony and Rosa Donello and finds Rosa critically ill from a ruptured appendix. Rosa is terrified of hospitals because her sister died in one, and Tony has promised she will not be taken away. When the doctor insists that surgery offers her only chance, Tony pulls a gun and orders him to operate in the apartment instead. With Judy boiling water and improvising sterile conditions from whatever they can find, Dr. Christian performs the emergency operation there rather than abandon Rosa. She survives and is later recovering safely, while an overwhelmed Tony offers everything he has in gratitude. The doctor refuses a real fee and keeps one of Tony's barber tools as a souvenir.

title: The Accident (1938-11-15)
plotSynopsis: Dr. Christian attends the twenty-fifth anniversary celebration of admired former governor Charles Van Ness and his wife Carolyn, a couple everyone in Rivers End regards as an ideal marriage. Charlie leaves the party on a winter night and is killed when his car skids on a mountain road. After Christian brings the news home, Carolyn finally admits that the public image was false: she had repeatedly protected Charlie's reputation and hidden how unhappy their marriage really was. Returning to the crash scene, Christian finds that Charlie apparently swerved to avoid Cliff Peters, the town drunk, who is also found dead nearby. Everyone expects Cliff's wife Ellen to feel relieved to be free of him, but she remembers a very different man, a loving husband and father whose kindness the town never saw. The two deaths overturn Rivers End's easy judgments about both marriages and leave Christian reflecting on how little outsiders can truly know about another person's love.

title: Corner Stone (1938-11-22)
plotSynopsis: Fourteen-year-old Freddie Clemons dreams of becoming an aviator and secretly spends time at the local airfield with pilot Alec Skinner, alarming parents who still treat him like a child. After being punished for a forbidden flight, Freddie runs away in an airplane and crashes, then is ashamed to return home. Dr. Christian helps him understand that growing up means facing mistakes rather than escaping them, telling him that dreams are worth building only when they are given a sound foundation.

title: The Seeing Eye Pt1 (1938-11-29)
plotSynopsis: An automobile accident leaves accomplished young musician Peg Foster blind, and the pity of her mother and fiance Joe Hardy soon makes her feel helpless and incapable of the life she had planned. Dr. Christian argues that their loving dependence is doing more harm than the blindness itself and persuades Peg to attend the Seeing Eye school in Morristown, New Jersey. When the training becomes difficult and Peg wants to quit, he deliberately challenges her pride until she stays. She returns home independently with her guide dog Mara, able to travel on her own and ready to resume the active life, music and future she feared she had lost.

title: The Pirate Of Rivers End (1938-12-06)
plotSynopsis: A local historian's new manuscript about Rivers End begins exposing facts that respectable families would rather forget. Mrs. Sherman comes to Dr. Christian because wealthy Oscar Duban has learned that her son Brett was adopted and that Brett's natural father served time in prison. Duban uses the discovery to oppose Brett's engagement to his daughter Elaine, and Mrs. Sherman desperately asks Christian to conceal or falsify the truth. Christian refuses. Elaine, however, already knows Brett was adopted and still intends to marry him; Brett is proud of the parents who chose and raised him. Christian then turns the historian's research on Duban himself and discovers that the Duban fortune traces back to a notorious French pirate whose stolen property became the foundation of the family's standing. Faced with his own ancestry, Duban must admit that a person should not be judged by an ancestor's crimes. He drops his objection and gives Elaine and Brett permission to marry.

title: The Seeing Eye Pt2 (1938-12-13)
plotSynopsis: Blind pianist Peg Foster, now moving independently with her Seeing Eye dog Mara, begins giving music lessons and hopes to earn a teaching position at the McCary Institute of Music. Founder Dan McCary blocks the appointment solely because Peg is blind and even threatens to withdraw his financial support if the institute hires her. By chance, however, McCary hears Peg play beautifully at a pupil's home without realizing who she is or that she cannot see. After learning the truth, he admits that his assumptions were wrong and reverses his opposition, clearing the way for Peg's appointment. The job proves to Peg that she can support herself rather than be a burden, but she still hesitates over whether a blind woman has the right to marry Joe Hardy. Dr. Christian tells her that love, character and the life she and Joe can build together matter more than her blindness. Peg accepts Joe's proposal, with Mara ready to be part of the wedding.

title: Danny Gets Married (1938-12-20)
plotSynopsis: At Christmas, Dr. Christian watches nurse Goldie devote herself to Tony, a seriously ill boy in the Center City hospital, while young Dr. Danny Bradford quietly falls in love with her. Tony worries about what will happen to Goldie when he is no longer there for her and decides that Bradford is the man who ought to look after her. The adults hesitate to say openly what they feel, but Tony finally forces the question at the child's Christmas celebration, asking Goldie whether she wants Bradford as her Christmas present. She admits that she does. Dr. Christian later explains that Danny Bradford and Goldie were married the following Christmas Day, with Tony recovering slowly but steadily.

title: The Glamour Girl (1938-12-27)
plotSynopsis: Faith Denton fears that her husband Don is being drawn back to glamorous Brenda Baldwin, so Dr. Christian advises the quiet wife to remind Don that she can be exciting too. Faith transforms herself into Rivers End's new glamour girl, only to discover that Don dislikes the endless parties and begins seeking peace and sympathy from Brenda instead. The experiment reaches its breaking point when a snow-damaged roof begins collapsing during a children's program: Brenda panics, while Faith calmly plays a march and helps lead the children to safety before being injured herself. Seeing his wife's courage jolts Don back to what he nearly threw away, and Faith's recovery restores their marriage on firmer ground.

title: The Neediest Case (1939-01-03)
plotSynopsis: When Dr. Christian finds reclusive Ivy Fenner freezing and hungry in an unheated house, he treats her as Rivers End's neediest case and organizes food, fuel, blankets, medical care and small comforts she cannot afford. Ivy remains prickly and suspicious, especially whenever anyone goes near her old mattress. After her sudden death, the reason becomes clear: ten thousand dollars has been hidden inside it, making the supposed pauper a secret miser. At first the money appears destined for the state because she left no known will, until the telephone men produce a note Ivy wrote and had them witness when they installed her phone. It leaves her estate to the only good friend she believed she had, Dr. Paul Christian, giving him the chance to turn her hoarded money toward helping others.

title: Guest Of Honor (1939-01-10)
plotSynopsis: Riverâ€™s End prepares an elaborate medical-society dinner for visiting Sir Thomas Beaton, one of the worldâ€™s leading throat specialists, and Dr. Christian is assigned to meet the distinguished guest at the train. A fierce blizzard is already burying the roads, however, and Christian has another concern: Esther Denby, a seriously ill young woman living with her family at an isolated mountain farm. Instead of escorting Sir Thomas to his banquet, Christian persuades the irritated surgeon to carry his instruments and struggle with him through waist-deep snow to the Denby home. Once there, Sir Thomas realizes that Esther needs the very specialized treatment he can provide and performs the operation that may save her life. The two doctors miss the dinner entirely. Afterward, warming themselves over coffee, Sir Thomas admits that the exhausting detour has reminded him of something professional fame had allowed him to forget: a doctorâ€™s first obligation is to the sick person who needs him. He raises his own toast to Dr. Christian, the country doctor who made the celebrated guest of honor remember what it means to practice medicine.

title: Back To Youth (1939-01-17)
plotSynopsis: Forty-two-year-old Kent Lewis has lost his clothing business, cannot find work and has begun to believe everyone who tells him he is already old and finished. Dr. Christian pairs him with energetic seventy-year-old Grandma Nelson, whose appetite for hiking, exploring and adventure makes Kent feel young again and restores the confidence his business failure destroyed. Grandma's worried grandson Ted accuses the doctor of pushing her too hard, but she insists that age is largely a state of mind. The lesson becomes more complicated when Grandma returns alone to an abandoned house she wants to explore, falls asleep after lighting a fire and must be rescued when the house catches fire. Kent proves he is far from finished by helping save her, while Grandma admits that feeling young does not mean ignoring every physical limit.

title: Chains (1939-01-24)
plotSynopsis: Widowed Margaret Doyle Martin has spent years giving herself entirely to her grown daughters and grandchildren, who treat her devotion as a permanent obligation. On a train trip she meets widowed mining engineer Richard Bailey, falls in love and accepts his proposal, only to have her daughters shame and pressure her into giving him up. Dr. Christian recognizes that their possessiveness has chained Margaret to a life sentence of service and bluntly tells them that being a good mother does not cancel her right to happiness. Faced with Bailey waiting for her decision, Margaret finally chooses the man she loves; they marry and begin a new life together.

title: The Music Box (1939-01-31)
plotSynopsis: A wedding song causes elderly Miss Mary Loughkin to faint and finally reveal to Dr. Christian that she is really the once-famous opera singer Madame Lupina. Decades earlier in Moldavia she and Prince Carl fell in love, but public outrage over their romance threatened his throne and she left him, carrying only the music box he had given her. She spent the rest of her life in obscurity at Rivers End, and as she dies she asks Dr. Christian to tell Carl that she kept his music box and never forgot him.

title: Have A Heart (1939-02-07)
plotSynopsis: Nearly seventy-year-old Will Grannis has spent most of his life sheltered by his devoted sister Hattie because an illness in youth was believed to have left him with a dangerous heart condition. Dr. Christian runs a modern cardiograph and discovers that Will's heart is normal, turning what should be good news into the painful realization that decades of fear and restriction were unnecessary. Will responds not with bitterness but with a late-life revolt, traveling alone to a specialist and then across the country and beyond, spending his savings on the adventures he had always been denied. He eventually returns broke but delighted, telling Dr. Christian he packed more life into that year than many people manage in a lifetime.

title: Angel Unawarepr Snd At End (1939-02-14)
plotSynopsis: Rivers End's council wants the condemned shanties of Paradise Flats torn down, but Dr. Christian refuses to displace the poor families until the town provides decent replacement homes. Contractor Grimshaw dismisses the residents as worthless, singling out the simple-minded but goodhearted Duke Angel as proof that they do not deserve model cottages. When severe flooding comes, Christian and Judy try to cross the river to warn Mayor Hewitt that the bridge has washed out. Their boat carries them to Duke's flooded shanty, where Duke has remained behind with children rather than abandon his home. A floating log destroys the rowboat, leaving them stranded, and the mayor is still approaching the broken bridge. Duke, an exceptional swimmer whom the town has always underestimated, plunges into the icy, debris-filled flood and swims upstream far enough to stop the mayor's automobile, suffering a head injury in the effort. His courage forces Grimshaw and the town to reconsider their contempt. Paradise Flats is replaced by the model cottages Christian had sought, Duke receives a medal as Rivers End's hero, and even after moving into his new house he remains endearingly himself, asking whether he can build a packing-box shanty in the backyard because it would feel more like home.

title: Washington Had His Delaware (1939-02-21)
plotSynopsis: Unemployed and embittered Dan Smithers has little use for patriotic speeches until work on a Washingtons Birthday pageant forces him to study the real hardships behind the countrys founding. The history changes his outlook on freedom and responsibility just as he is trying to provide for his wife Marianne and their new baby. By the end, Dan has a job, a renewed sense of purpose, and a son born on Washingtons Birthday whom he hopes to name George.

title: Puppy Love (1939-02-28)
plotSynopsis: Blind Peggy Foster leaves her seeing-eye dog Mara with Dr. Christian while she is away, just as the doctor is again dealing with bitter recluse Mrs. Jackson. Since her husband's death years earlier, Mrs. Jackson has shut herself off from neighbors and grown openly hostile toward animals, while pets in the neighborhood have repeatedly disappeared or died. Mara gets loose, crosses near Mrs. Jackson's property and is later found desperately ill and barely able to move. Dr. Christian confronts Mrs. Jackson, who admits putting out poisoned meat to keep animals away and shows little concern for the harm she has caused. He forces her to understand that poisoning Mara is not merely hurting a dog but threatening the independence and freedom of the blind young woman who depends on her. Mara survives treatment. Shaken by Christian's words, Mrs. Jackson recognizes how thoroughly grief has turned her against the world, resolves to become a neighbor again, and volunteers to lead a community collection to buy Dr. Christian a dog of his own as a sign of Rivers End's affection.

title: A Bad Case Of Quarantine (1939-03-07)
plotSynopsis: Nine-year-old Patsy Robinson is recovering from measles just as her older brother Bud is preparing for a school dance with Merrily Hamlin. Bud soon comes down with the measles himself and must stay home, so visiting cousin Lester takes Merrily to the dance in his place. Lester proves such a good dancer that Merrily begins spending more time with him even after Bud recovers, leaving Bud jealous and convinced that the college-age cousin has stolen his girl. Patsy, feeling guilty for having given Bud the measles, quietly takes matters into her own hands when she realizes she is coming down with mumps. She carefully keeps everyone away except Lester, making sure he is the one exposed. Lester is quarantined until just before he is due to leave town, while Bud is sent to stay safely with the Hamlins. With Lester out of competition, Merrily makes clear that she really prefers Bud and plans to attend the basketball dance with him. Christian recognizes exactly what Patsy has done and rewards her protective little-sister plotting with an ice-cream soda.

title: Little Sweetheart (1939-03-14)
plotSynopsis: Polly Palmer returns to Rivers End and throws herself into raising money for Dr. Christian's children's clinic, rekindling the childhood hero-worship she has felt for him all her life. She breaks her engagement to Lee Morgan and mistakes Dr. Christian's gratitude and affection for romantic love, leaving the embarrassed doctor afraid that correcting her will humiliate her. Lee follows her home but, instead of forcing the issue, helps make the hospital campaign a success. Once the work is finished, Polly recognizes that Dr. Christian is the ideal she has always adored but Lee is the man who truly needs and belongs with her; she chooses Lee and asks Dr. Christian to attend their wedding.

title: Mr Meeks (1939-03-21)
plotSynopsis: Eleanor Meeks loves her husband Gregory but is embarrassed by his contentment with gardening, seed catalogs and time with their son. She wants the president of the family manufacturing company to become more ambitious and important, so Christian helps draw Gregory back into civic and business responsibilities. The change soon produces a much more serious problem. A government tent contract calls for twelve-ounce canvas, but the Meeks company has delivered eight-ounce material while charging for the heavier grade. Suspicion falls on Gregory, especially because his forceful secretary Doris Handen is the sister of a politically connected man long suspected of graft. Christian uncovers a forged factory order and tricks Doris into admitting that the Handens manipulated the order and used Gregory's inattention as cover; John Hewitt overhears the confession so it cannot simply be denied. At home Eleanor then confronts a second apparent scandal, the rumor that Gregory has spent night after night at Doris's house. Gregory admits the visits, but the explanation is absurdly innocent: Eleanor had forbidden his beloved seed catalogs around their own home, so he went elsewhere to read them. The crisis clears Gregory of both fraud and infidelity and leaves Eleanor facing the comic truth that trying to remake a harmless, contented husband nearly created the very troubles she feared.

title: Spring In The Air (1939-03-28)
plotSynopsis: With spring putting romance in the air, Judy Price confides to Dr. Christian that she is secretly engaged to young physician Ralph Gardner. Ralph is building his career with financial help from a disapproving uncle and has insisted that nobody know about the engagement until he is established. When he learns Judy has told Christian, he becomes angry, tells her to pretend they have broken up and stops seeing her openly. Judy believes he is working nights as hard as she is so they can marry sooner. Christian finally persuades the exhausted Judy to go out for dinner, where they unexpectedly find Ralph dancing with wealthy Laura Payson. Confronted outside, Ralph makes his choice plain: he intends to marry Laura and resents Judy questioning him. Judy is devastated, but Christian helps her see that losing a man willing to trade loyalty for money and position is not the end of love. He reminds her that, like spring itself, love can come around again.

title: Home Made Hero (1939-04-04)
plotSynopsis: Harvey Gibbons has postponed marriage to Agnes for years while supporting his widowed sister, her children and his mother, and he fears he cannot compete when Agnes's glamorous former sweetheart Mort Hallworthy returns. Agnes is swept up by Mort's confidence and travels with him on the same flight as Dr. Christian and Judy, but a violent storm strips away the glamour when Mort panics and Agnes sees the difference between swagger and dependable courage. Back in Rivers End, Harvey finds work that will ease his family burden, Agnes realizes whom she truly loves, and Harvey finally insists that they stop delaying and marry at once.

title: Doctor Doctor Come Quick (1939-04-11)
plotSynopsis: At the dedication of Riverâ€™s Endâ€™s new hospital, the town honors Dr. Christian by recalling one especially hectic day of his work. He first treats teenage Janet Hawker after she shoots herself superficially in a moment of despair over public humiliation at school, then gets her to admit she wanted people to understand how badly she had been hurt rather than truly wanting to die. He next comforts Mrs. Cochran, who believes her husband David has run away with his secretary Joan Summers, while also treating young Spike Morse after the boy is bitten by a dog he had been teasing. A report of a possible shortage at Davidâ€™s bank sends Dr. Christian racing to intercept David and Joan before they reach Chicago. He discovers that they are indeed running away together but that David knows nothing of any missing money. A radio bulletin then announces that cashier Elmer Clark has confessed to embezzling the funds.
