With the criminal suspicion removed, Dr. Christian persuades David and Joan to return to Riverâ€™s End rather than destroy their families and reputations, even inventing a harmless business-trip explanation for their absence. The dedication ceremony closes by recognizing that this mixture of medicine, counsel and community service is simply a normal day for Dr. Christian.

title: Once Around The Block (1939-11-01)
plotSynopsis: An evening walk around one Rivers End block reveals three households whose troubles are quietly connected. Kit McKenzie has just had a baby, but her husband George resents the new expenses because they have consumed the savings he hoped to use to buy the cottage they rent from Pete Williams. Pete, meanwhile, cannot emotionally let go of that cottage because it is tied to an old love and has become a shrine to his past; his wife Jennifer believes she can never compete with the memory and plans to leave him. The last stop is the mansion of elderly recluse Cordelia Bingham, whom the town believes to be a miser. Cordelia reveals that she has secretly given almost her entire fortune to charities around the world and has only $25,000 left, which she asks Dr. Christian to leave to one deserving person in Rivers End. Christian chooses the McKenzies' two-week-old baby. The legacy gives the young family the security to complete the purchase of Pete's cottage, removing the old house from Pete's life and giving Pete and Jennifer a chance to restore their marriage. The single walk around the block thus links a newborn child's future, a troubled marriage and the hidden generosity of a woman everyone had misjudged.

title: Bad Boy (1939-11-08)
plotSynopsis: Fifteen-year-old Ted Gallagher is caught with a gang after a nighttime jewelry-store break-in in which the watchman is shot. The town is ready to write Ted off as a bad boy, but Dr. Christian argues that the neglected youngster has never been given a fair chance. Judge Latimer places Ted on six months' probation under the doctor's supervision instead of sending him to reform school. Ted begins to flourish, showing unexpected skill caring for injured animals and an interest in medicine. Then, just before a birthday party arranged for him, Ted gets into a school fight with Buddy Melrose and Buddy dies. Ted admits striking him but refuses to explain the quarrel. Dr. Christian proves that Buddy had a congenital blood-vessel defect and suffered the fatal rupture before Ted's blow landed, clearing Ted of responsibility. A notebook finally reveals why Ted kept silent: Buddy had written a mocking poem about Dr. Christian, and Ted fought to defend the man who had believed in him.

title: Corn Gingerbread (1939-11-15)
plotSynopsis: Roy Davis grows jealous when Judy spends much of her time helping visiting author Clayton Grant research a book about Rivers End. Clayton is intelligent and charming, and he eventually tells Dr. Christian that he intends to marry Judy and take her away. The surprise is that his book, Corn and Gingerbread, uses Rivers End as an example of everything he believes is wrong with small-town American life and even proposes replacing familiar local landmarks. Judy rejects both his contempt for the town and his proposal, defending the memories and human ties he cannot measure, while Roy happily reclaims his place beside her.

title: Prelude To Thanksgiving (1939-11-22)
plotSynopsis: Teenager Katherine Anne 'Tanny' Gardner loves her mother but thinks the adults around her are hopelessly old-fashioned. A self-described tomboy, she is especially close to football star Randy Billings and resents glamorous newcomer Jean West. Randy first sides with Tanny's mother against Tanny riding on Bud Collins's motorcycle, then awkwardly tells Tanny that Jean has maneuvered him into taking her to the Thanksgiving football dance. Hurt and jealous, Tanny defiantly accepts Bud's offer of a motorcycle ride even as Randy tries to forbid it. Just after they start off, a truck skids around the corner and Tanny is badly hurt. She escapes internal injury but suffers heavy bruising and a broken arm. The accident forces Randy to admit that he had taken Tanny for granted and that jealousy and his own careless words pushed her toward Bud. As Tanny recovers, Randy chooses Thanksgiving dinner at her bedside over the dance, gives her his fraternity pin and makes clear that she is the girl he wants. Tanny, suddenly less certain that her mother's advice is obsolete, asks her mother what being in love feels like.

title: Mad Interlude (1939-12-06)
plotSynopsis: Successful businessman Hector Travis has worked without a real break for thirty years while his partner, wife and children continually add demands for money, possessions and plans. Suddenly he locks himself in his room, talks nonsense and behaves as though he has lost his mind, throwing both family and business into confusion. Dr. Christian eventually explains that Hector is not ill at all: completely worn down and unable to ask for rest any other way, he has been pretending to be crazy so the treadmill will stop. His family finally understands what their expectations have cost him and promises not to drive him that hard again.

title: No Crib For His Bed (1939-12-20)
plotSynopsis: Mary Bartlett is nearly penniless after her husband Ben leaves for Center City to find work soon after their baby's birth and sends only a single message in six weeks. Forced from her room and desperate to find him, Mary leaves the baby safely bundled at the bus station with a note asking someone to care for him while she walks into a Christmas snowstorm. Children from the church pageant discover the baby, while Dr. Christian travels to Center City and finds that Ben has finally secured steady work but was ashamed to write while he remained unemployed. On the return trip they find Mary collapsed in the snow and bring her back to Rivers End. The family is reunited at the Christmas pageant, where Mary discovers her own baby safe in the manger beneath the star of Bethlehem.

title: Love On A Diet (1939-12-27)
plotSynopsis: Dorothy Corbett breaks down after her daughter Margo, looking at an old photograph, innocently remarks that Dorothy used to be pretty. Dr. Christian discovers that years with domineering, jealous husband Dave have stripped Dorothy of nearly every pleasure and sign of individuality: she no longer goes out, dresses attractively or receives the affection she once knew. Treating the problem as emotional starvation rather than an ordinary illness, he and Margo restore Dorothy's hair, clothes and confidence and arrange harmless masculine attention from Arnold Darrow, who is actually Margo's fiancé. Dave returns unexpectedly, sees his transformed wife with Arnold and assumes an affair, even threatening divorce and blaming Dr. Christian. The doctor forces Dave to confront the truth that his possessiveness has nearly destroyed Dorothy. When Margo reveals Arnold belongs to her, Dorothy's collapse finally breaks through Dave's anger. He calls his wife by the old pet name 'Dolly' and resumes the tenderness he abandoned years earlier, giving her a reason to want life again.

title: None So Blind (1940-01-03)
plotSynopsis: Twelve-year-old Mary Dugan of Squatterstown is treated as the awkward, troublesome sister beside pretty Lillian and is finally thrown out of Mrs. Mudge's girls' club after another clash. Dr. Christian suspects that Mary's hostility is covering years of humiliation and notices something the adults around her have missed: an exceptional natural ear for music. He introduces Mary to blind pianist Peg Foster. Because Peg cannot judge the child by dirty clothes, looks or social standing, she responds to Mary's voice, personality and musical ability instead. Peg begins teaching her, protects her when Mrs. Mudge tries to shame her, and Mary rapidly develops into a gifted young pianist. After only a few months Mary performs publicly and wins a McCary Institute scholarship. When Mrs. Mudge suggests that some of the scholarship money can be diverted to buy things for Lillian, Christian and Peg make clear that the award belongs to Mary's education. The girl everyone dismissed as the ugly duckling finally has a future built on the talent others were too prejudiced to see.

title: There Is No Such Thing As Luck (1940-01-10)
sortKey: 0|1940-01-10|00062|there is no such thing as luck 1940 01 10
plotSynopsis: Wealthy fashion heir Henry Martin III comes to Dr. Christian miserable with his pampered business life and convinced that what he really needs is honest work on a farm. Christian pairs him with struggling farmer Tim Halsey and daughter Molly: Martin takes over the Halsey farm while the Halseys live in his Chicago apartment, with Martin also paying them a monthly allowance. The arrangement succeeds so well that Martin turns the farm into a profitable operation and wants to keep it, but after nearly a year the Halseys decide to return. When they refuse an extension, Martin threatens to sue Christian for $100,000 over the doctor's guarantee that he could remain. The dispute collapses when Molly reveals that she has used her time in Chicago to study fashion design. Her self-made clothes immediately impress Martin, who forgets the lawsuit and wants her for his firm. Soon afterward Molly writes that she and Martin plan to marry, leaving Christian amused that luck has solved a problem Martin insisted luck did not exist.

title: Stuff Of Heroes (1940-01-17)
plotSynopsis: Hospital handyman Hank Blevins has spent years letting his reckless brother Luke bully him and clean up after Luke's gambling debts. When Dr. Christian refuses to supply money for another rescue, Luke pressures Hank into stealing the hospital's valuable radium, arguing that no one will suspect him and that the theft will keep Luke out of jail. Hank gives in, but the theft leaves him miserable, especially after Dr. Christian explains that the radium is medically vital, registered and dangerous to anyone who mishandles it. Hank finally confronts Luke, takes the radium back and returns it to the hospital, earning a black eye in the struggle. Dr. Christian quietly lets the disappearance remain a secret and tells Hank that a man who can stand up for what is right after years of fear has the stuff that heroes are made of.

title: Revolt (1940-01-24)
plotSynopsis: Nineteen-year-old Bill and Helen arrive in Rivers End posing as brother and sister after running away from Minneapolis. Resentful of what he calls a system that keeps young people powerless, Bill plans to rob Dr. Christian's safe and pressures Helen to learn the combination, eventually threatening the doctor with a gun. Dr. Christian has already recognized their lies, found the police bulletin and quietly removed the cartridges from Bill's weapon. Confronted with how completely his rebellion has turned into crime, Bill abandons the robbery and decides to return voluntarily, face the consequences and then work honestly toward a future. Helen's mother is coming to take her home, and the two young people leave their marriage plans for a more responsible time.

title: Gypsy Love (1940-01-31)
plotSynopsis: On the eve of his wedding to Maria, gypsy prince Marko collapses with violent weakness that the camp believes is a black spell placed by Sarah, a woman who loves him and has vowed he will marry her or die. Maria secretly summons Dr. Christian despite the band's distrust of outside medicine. He notices that Sarah has been helping nurse Marko and tests the broth she gives him, discovering an obscure drug whose effects have been magnified by Marko's terror of the curse. Dr. Christian and the police stop Sarah before the dosing can become fatal. Marko recovers, Sarah is held until he is out of danger, and Dr. Christian returns to dance at Marko and Maria's wedding.

title: Stranger Things (1940-02-07)
plotSynopsis: Investment broker Joe Fletcher leaves thirty thousand dollars in bonds with town treasurer Harvey Ziegler, only to learn that Ziegler's safe has apparently been robbed. At the same time Joe's young son Alan suffers vivid recurring dreams containing details that seem to point toward the crime. With no conventional evidence, Dr. Christian uses the dream's clues to confront Ziegler, including a hidden compartment and an arm injury caused by the safe. Ziegler confesses to staging the robbery himself, leaving Dr. Christian unable to explain how Alan knew the truth except to acknowledge that some strange things remain beyond science.

title: My True Valentine (1940-02-14)
plotSynopsis: In 1925, seamstress Emily Cobb is engaged to Don Burns, a young man with a wild reputation who is trying to straighten out his life. After a machine-works robbery, watchman Joel Sims identifies one of the nearly identical Burns brothers before being shot to death. Don's brother Sandy is known to be away, leaving Don without an alibi, and Don is convicted despite insisting he is innocent. He refuses to let Emily tie her life to his and spends years in prison while she eventually builds a successful fashion business in Chicago. Fifteen years later Emily returns to Rivers End on Valentine's Day, torn over whether to marry a kind, successful man who loves her even though she still loves Don. At the same time Don returns after being cleared when the real killer confesses while already serving a life sentence on another charge. Emily decides before knowing Don is back that she cannot marry anyone else, and Dr. Christian reunites the two, suggesting that after all those lost years Valentine's Day is an appropriate day for their wedding.

title: I Cannot Tell A Lie (1940-02-21)
plotSynopsis: At a Washingtonâ€™s Birthday gathering in Riverâ€™s End, Dr. Christian quietly arranges a game in which each guest must answer an uncomfortable question truthfully. Young Barbaraâ€™s questions first expose small embarrassments, then reveal that newcomer Richard Flint lied about where he spent the previous night. Flintâ€™s jealous wife assumes he has been unfaithful, but the truth is more calculated: he has been pressuring Mrs. Browning, head of the parentsâ€™ organization, to help remove longtime school superintendent Mr. Randolph. Flintâ€™s supposed school-reform campaign is tied to his business interests with a school-equipment concern. When the scheme is exposed, a furious confrontation leaves Randolph wounded and gives him grounds for charges against Flint. Dr. Christian brokers a quiet settlement: Randolph will not press the matter if Flint and his wife leave Riverâ€™s End, and the guests agree to describe the commotion as part of a party game. Judy finally turns the truth game on Dr. Christian and makes him admit that he was the one who suggested it to Barbara in the first place.

title: Leap No More My Lady (1940-02-28)
plotSynopsis: Librarian Lucy Plum has spent years waiting on self-centered George Kegley, while the shy but dependable Stan Sherwood quietly cares about her. Dr. Christian and Judy push Lucy to stop arranging her life around George and deliberately let an engagement scheme go far enough to force everyone to show what they really want. When George plans an immediate wedding and a move away, Stan finally protests and admits he cannot bear to lose Lucy. Lucy realizes she no longer loves George, and the manufactured crisis clears the way for her and Stan.

title: Blossom Otoole (1940-03-06)
plotSynopsis: Years after young Claire Barnes ran away when her stern father refused to accept her love for Harry Hall, Dr. Christian learns that the now-elderly Barnes is dying and sends for the daughter he has never stopped missing. Claire returns as Blossom O'Toole, the stage name she adopted after leaving home. She admits to Christian that she and Harry never married and that her hoped-for theatrical success never came; Blossom is only a struggling second-rate actress. She is ashamed to let her father know how little came of the life she chose, but Christian persuades her to see him. At his bedside Claire allows the dying man to believe that she is happy and successful, giving him the comfort and pride he needs in his final moments. The reunion lets father and daughter make peace without forcing Claire to destroy the image that eases his death.

title: Angies Last Cure (1940-03-13)
plotSynopsis: Angie Hopper becomes an obsessive hypochondriac after buying a popular book of symptoms, diagnosing herself with one illness after another and keeping exhausted husband Fred constantly waiting on her. Dr. Christian sees that arguing with her fears will accomplish nothing. When Fred develops an ordinary ache, Angie immediately transfers all her attention to him, and Dr. Christian quietly encourages the reversal by giving Fred's harmless baldness the impressive name of a chronic glabrous condition. Caring for Fred cures Angie of her own imaginary diseases so completely that she throws the symptom book into the fire.

title: Spring Dance (1940-03-20)
plotSynopsis: Seventeen-year-old Bunn Williams, captain of the high-school basketball team, feels badly out of his depth at Sally Sans's sophisticated birthday dance. Convinced that wealthier Ken Carson and expensive gifts make his own dinner jacket, flowers and old-fashioned present look foolish, Bunn nearly gives up before telling Sally how he feels. Sally makes clear that the things he thought were embarrassments matter because they came from him, wears his flowers and agrees to be his girl. Their spring evening ends with Bunn wishing on the first star and Dr. Christian observing that his wish seems to have come true.

title: Visiting Lady (1940-03-27)
plotSynopsis: Rivers End goes overboard entertaining glamorous New York visitor Brenda Marsh, while Judy and the other townspeople exhaust themselves trying to prove how sophisticated the village can be. Brenda finally admits to Dr. Christian that she came to the country hoping to escape exactly this kind of social whirl and simply wants a chance to rest. During a drive, an out-of-control truck causes a serious crash that leaves Judy badly injured; Brenda keeps her head, gets Dr. Christian and Judy to help, and earns the town's respect as far more than an artificial society girl. Judy recovers, Roy's fright makes his feelings for her unmistakable, and Brenda's only remaining request is that Rivers End please stop giving parties for her.

title: Derelicts (1940-04-03)
plotSynopsis: Police bring alcoholic drifter Jim Martin into the hospital, where Dr. Christian discovers that the watch Jim guards so fiercely is one of the few things left from the life he lost. Jim was once the successful author of the popular Danny Dean children's books, but after an automobile accident killed his wife and son while he was driving, guilt destroyed his family life and his career and he drifted into drink. In the next room, an orphan boy named Les is recovering from pneumonia and happens to adore the Danny Dean stories. Christian brings the two together without initially revealing Jim's identity. Les's admiration draws Jim back into storytelling, and Jim begins writing again. When officials prepare to return Les to an institution, Jim finally recognizes that both of them have been living as derelicts without families. He races to the station, stops the boy from being sent away and announces that he will adopt Les, giving both of them a home and a new start.

title: Chicken Supreme (1940-04-10)
plotSynopsis: Dr. Christian receives an unwanted hen named Ella as payment from a poor patient and uses the odd gift while trying to help proud sisters Matilda and Lottie Tweedle find a useful occupation and a way to support themselves. At first the sisters intend to turn Ella into dinner, but failed attempts with a hatchet and then a shotgun leave them far too attached to the bird to kill her. Ella soon leads them into raising chicks, and what begins as sentiment becomes a serious poultry project. The women study feeding and breeding, rise early to care for the flock and devote themselves to building it properly. Their birds attract a buyer, and Christian helps them see how the operation can expand into a real business with more stock, runs, equipment and feed. The sisters gain work, independence and purpose. Their gratitude creates one last comic crisis when they decide the finest possible thank-you for Dr. Christian is to give him the best chicken in their flock, freshly killed.

title: Glamour (1940-04-17)
plotSynopsis: Thirteen years earlier, young widow Ellen McCarty asked Dr. Christian to find a home for her three-year-old daughter Glamour because Ellen intended to marry wealthy Carter Gaylord, who did not know the child existed. John and Evie Clark raised Glamour with Ellen's financial support. After Gaylord's death, Ellen returns to Rivers End and seeks custody of the now sixteen-year-old girl, promising wealth, travel and every social advantage. A judge leaves the final choice to Glamour. When Christian refuses to influence her, Ellen tries to force the decision by offering lifelong security to the Clarks if Glamour comes with her and threatening to withdraw every cent if she refuses. Glamour angrily chooses John and Evie and rejects the mother who abandoned her. The confrontation brings on another heart attack for Evie, and Ellen finally begins to understand that money and pressure cannot manufacture affection. Christian tells her that if she truly wants her daughter back in her life she must earn that relationship through patience and consideration. He suggests that Ellen build a summer cottage nearby, giving mother and daughter a chance to know each other gradually without uprooting Glamour from the family that raised her.

title: Riders On The Storm (1940-04-24)
plotSynopsis: Former test pilot Jim Waters has been grounded and emotionally shattered by an earlier accident that cost another man his life. With Dr. Christians encouragement he begins working again and builds a new plane, but his real test comes when a medical emergency on a remote island arises during a violent storm. Jim flies Dr. Christian through icing, poor visibility and mechanical trouble, risking his life to reach the patient and discovering that he can honor the life he lost by saving another rather than destroying himself with guilt.

title: Unfinished Business (1940-05-15)
plotSynopsis: Benjamin Stack has organized every minute of his marriage into a rigid schedule until his wife Maddie finally leaves, saying she has lived with a system instead of a man. Dr. Christian tries to help them reconcile, but even when Maddie asks only for spontaneity, Benjamin immediately tries to turn their life together into a modified timetable. After losing her again, his ordered world collapses so completely that he prepares to jump from a building. Dr. Christian talks him down by appealing to the one thing Benjamin still cannot abandon: an unpaid obligation, inventing a large medical bill that must be settled first. With the immediate crisis over, Dr. Christian recommends an unplanned road trip with Maddie, although Benjamin's first instinct is still to schedule every mile and meal.

title: Between Office Hours (1940-05-22)
plotSynopsis: Bruiser Burns, a wrestler and convicted killer being taken for psychiatric observation, badly crushes three fingers in a car door. Dr. Christian has no choice but to amputate the mangled fingers to save the arm. Months later Burns is judged criminally insane and escapes while being transferred from the asylum, convinced that Christian deliberately ruined his fighting career. He tracks the doctor to his office during the supposedly quiet gap between office hours and holds Judy while waiting to kill them both. Christian wakes from a nap, realizes the escaped man is inside, darkens the office and helps trip and overpower him. Even after Burns has tried to murder him, Christian notices something lodged in the man's inflamed eye and calmly removes it before the police arrive.

title: Ten Meter Romance (1940-05-29)
plotSynopsis: Albert Holly becomes lonely and despondent after his daughter Ethel marries and moves to the Philippines. Dr. Christian steers him toward amateur radio, and the ten-meter band gives Albert a new purpose: he can speak with Ethel across the ocean and eventually becomes a regular on-air friend of widowed operator Mrs. Winters. The nightly conversations cure the vague 'heart trouble' Albert had been complaining about and grow into a romance even though the two have never met face to face. When Ethel's family prepares to return closer to home, Albert decides to invite Mrs. Winters to Rivers End and ask her to marry him, with Dr. Christian coaching him to make the proposal as simply over the radio as he would make any other call.

title: Roughneck (1940-06-05)
plotSynopsis: Jockey Joseph Meadows is badly injured when thrown from his horse Roughneck and is left unable to move his legs. Another doctor expects permanent paralysis, but Dr. Christian believes Meadows may recover if he has a powerful enough reason to fight. Meadows' fourteen-year-old son Jimmy is determined to get Roughneck into the Memorial Stakes, the big race his father had been working toward before the accident. Christian takes Jimmy and the horse under his wing, reins in the boy's attempts to gamble for the entry fee and helps Rivers End raise the money by selling small shares in Roughneck. The approaching race gives Meadows a goal, and his rehabilitation progresses from a specially built walker to crutches. At the Memorial Stakes Jimmy rides Roughneck as the Rivers End entry. Roughneck wins by half a length, and in the excitement Meadows suddenly realizes he has risen to his feet without his crutches. The horse's victory becomes the final push in Meadows' own recovery.

title: Bensons Inventions (1940-06-12)
plotSynopsis: Buzz Benson is Rivers End's much-ridiculed school janitor and amateur inventor, better known for failed gadgets and pranks than for serious ability. Dr. Christian discovers that Buzz has a genuine interest in chemistry and quietly coaches him. When word spreads that Buzz has invented a revolutionary 'chemical motor' and that Christian plans to send him to New York, townsmen who had mocked Buzz suddenly call him a genius, argue that his discovery belongs in Rivers End and begin maneuvering for a share of the supposed fortune. Their enthusiasm grows into a public meeting built around developing the motor locally. Christian finally exposes the mistake: he never vouched for Buzz's chemical motor at all. The real achievement is a useful precipitation process Buzz discovered accidentally, and Christian has arranged for a pharmaceutical company in New York to give the young man a job where he can learn the business. By letting the rumor run, Christian reveals how quickly the town's contempt turned to self-interested praise once money seemed involved and makes the would-be backers confront how little they actually knew about the boy they had dismissed.

title: On Wings Of Song (1940-06-19)
plotSynopsis: Famous opera star Angela D'Nello returns to Rivers End, prompting Dr. Christian to remember the hometown moments that shaped her career. As a young singer she won a local music scholarship, and later, frozen by stage fright on an important opening night, Dr. Christian helped her find her voice by reminding her to sing as if she were back among the friends who first believed in her. Her bond with home is tested again when her mother becomes gravely ill while Angela is far away, making song the bridge that connects them across distance.

title: Suggestions For Divorce (1940-06-26)
plotSynopsis: Joan Lyman's jealousy has driven her marriage to Steve toward divorce, especially after she becomes convinced he is involved with his secretary. Dr. Christian tells Joan that her suspicion helped create the very estrangement she feared and urges her to become again the woman Steve originally loved. When Joan and Christian unexpectedly meet Steve and the other woman at a restaurant, Christian forces the situation into the open instead of letting either side retreat. A discussion of divorce arrangements turns into a revealing quarrel, and Steve's companion decides she wants no part of the marriage or its baggage. With the outside relationship ended, Joan and Steve finally admit their own faults and reconcile before the divorce is completed.

title: The Man Who Changed His Mind (1941-01-29)
plotSynopsis: Grocer Alex Johnson becomes furious when Dr. Christian quarantines his household after young Dickie contracts scarlet fever. Because Johnson runs a food store, the quarantine means he cannot simply live at home and continue working, and he declares that once the danger is past Christian will no longer be the family doctor. Weeks later the Johnson children play doctor in their backyard playhouse. They take real medicines from the house and give several pills and liquids to Dottie, then lock the playhouse as part of their game. When Christian learns what happened he breaks down the door, rushes the poisoned child to treatment and uses every antidote and stimulant he can while the family is being located. Johnson arrives still angry, believing Christian has interfered with his children yet again, only to discover the doctor is fighting to save his daughter. Dottie finally regains consciousness and passes the crisis. Faced with Christian's persistence and care despite having been dismissed, Johnson admits he was wrong, asks forgiveness and offers him a lifetime appointment as the Johnson family physician.

title: Sweethearts Protective Insurance (1942-09-16)
plotSynopsis: Violet Lindsley is hurt when she learns that her California-based fiancé Harry Davis has bought a novelty policy promising him cash and a Hollywood date if she jilts him. Dr. Christian jokes that hometown sweethearts ought to organize protection of their own, but Judy turns the joke into a real Hometown Sweethearts Protective Insurance Company and it quickly attracts members and national attention. Hollywood publicity man Pete Wade arrives with an offer to send the first genuinely jilted member to Hollywood for a screen test. Harry interprets Violet's participation as proof that she distrusts him and breaks their engagement, technically making her the first eligible claimant. Violet refuses the glamorous trip because she wants Harry rather than publicity. Pete stays to persuade her, becomes increasingly charmed by Violet and small-town life, loses his studio job and converts the publicity idea into a permanent national organization based in Rivers End. By the end his assignment has become personal: he introduces Violet as the future Mrs. Pete Wade, and the two leave to obtain their marriage license with Dr. Christian chosen as best man.

title: An Artist Comes To Town (1942-09-23)
plotSynopsis: When celebrated portrait painter Sylvia St. Vincent sweeps into Rivers End and demands the towns best doctor for an emergency, Dr. Christian discovers that the patient is her beloved dog rather than a person. After he successfully helps the animal, Sylvia insists on painting his portrait in gratitude. Dr. Christian accepts only on his own terms: instead of immortalizing him on canvas, he asks the famous artist to repaint an old table that belonged to his mother, and she turns the humble piece into a work of art.

title: On To Glory (1942-09-30)
plotSynopsis: Aunt Tanny has no serious physical disease, but she has convinced herself that her time has come and has arranged her final days as carefully as a performance, calling in relatives, revising her will and taking comfort in a fully paid burial policy that promises a proper funeral. Dr. Christian realizes that the attention and drama surrounding death have become more appealing to her than recovery. He secretly has the burial policy removed just as Tanny appears ready to make her grand exit. The shock of discovering that her carefully planned funeral is no longer assured immediately rouses her anger, energy and will to live. Dr. Christian tells her she has suffered a rare malady requiring exactly such a shock and reminds her of the husband, blind brother, nieces and friends who still depend on her. Tanny abandons her trip to glory and begins recovering.

title: The Case Of Tommy Holms (1942-10-07)
plotSynopsis: After attorney Gerald Fox deliberately crashes his car, he claims total amnesia just hours before a deadline for locating young Tommy Holmes, heir to a million-dollar estate. Dr. Christian becomes suspicious when Fox conveniently cannot identify the boy and discovers that Fox and the late mans business partner would profit if the heir is not confirmed in time. A supposed truth-drug injection is actually harmless distilled water, proving Fox has been faking his memory loss. Confronted, Fox identifies Tommy and signs the papers that secure the boys inheritance.

title: Black Magic (1942-10-14)
plotSynopsis: Dr. Christian recalls a case in which Molly became ill after an asparagus dinner and developed a startling black discoloration of her mouth and tongue. Her doctor blamed poisoned food, and attorney Jernigan prepared a damage suit against grocer George Pullos for selling bad asparagus. Asked to investigate for the defense, Christian learns that Molly has also been taking a prescribed beef, iron and wine tonic. He realizes the dramatic black coloring is not proof of food poisoning at all: compounds in the asparagus react with the iron in the medicine and form a dark, ink-like color. Christian demonstrates the effect on himself in court by eating asparagus and taking the same tonic. The supposedly mysterious 'black magic' is exposed as an ordinary chemical reaction, the case against Pullos collapses, and Jernigan disappears rather than continue the failed claim.

title: Miss Lizzies Burglar (1942-10-21)
plotSynopsis: Miss Lizzie surprises a burglar named Joe in her home, but instead of turning the injured man over to the police she nurses him back toward health. Joe, who boasts that he has avoided women all his life, becomes increasingly terrified that her kindness and concern mean she intends to marry him, and finally tries to escape before he is trapped. Dr. Christian is called into the absurd quarrel and discovers that both have misunderstood the other. Miss Lizzie has indeed been hoping to keep Joe, but not as a husband: what she desperately wants is a landscape gardener, and Joe happens to be one. The marriage panic collapses into a much more practical job offer.

title: Light On A Fallen Star (1942-10-28)
plotSynopsis: Navy test pilot Grant Hopper survives a fiery crash without major physical injury, but afterward becomes terrified of flame, smoke, sudden noises and even ordinary reminders of flying. His fear turns him bitter and withdrawn from wife Helen and young daughter Dodie, whose admiration for her once-fearless father only deepens his shame. Dr. Christian recognizes that Grant's real injury is psychological and looks for a way to reconnect him with the courage and responsibility he believes he has lost. When Dodie is endangered by a fire, Grant rushes into the flames to save her. The rescue breaks the grip of the crash on him, and Grant realizes that in going into the fire for his daughter he recovered the part of himself he thought had been destroyed.

title: The Storm (1942-11-04)
plotSynopsis: Discouraged after losing a patient he could not move to a properly equipped hospital, Dr. Christian broods over the money Rivers End lacks for specialists and better rural medical care. He falls asleep as a storm gathers and dreams that Dan Foster and his sister Blanche offer him a fortune to alter Blanche's face so she can impersonate a missing heiress and steal a million-dollar inheritance. The promised fee could finance nearly everything Christian has been wishing he could provide for his patients, making the temptation more dangerous than simple greed. He refuses the fraud, and Dan finally pulls a gun and threatens both Christian and Blanche unless the operation is performed. Christian still refuses. A crash of thunder wakes him before the gun can fire, and the dream leaves him reassured that limited resources do not excuse wrongdoing and that doing whatever good he can with what he has is still worthwhile.

title: Fields Of Corn (1942-11-11)
plotSynopsis: World War I veteran Jim Brown is terrified that his only son Howard will volunteer for the Air Corps and endure the horrors that killed Jim's friends and left him with years of nightmares. He even offers Dr. Christian a thousand dollars to declare the healthy young man medically unfit, but the doctor refuses. Howard agrees to stay on the farm for his father's sake, despite wanting to serve and despite the support of the girl he plans to marry. During a violent night storm, Jim is shaken by what he describes as a dream or vision in which the corn outside seems to become the comrades who died beside him in the last war, calling on him not to make their sacrifice meaningless. By morning Jim has changed his mind and gives Howard his blessing to do what he believes is his duty.

title: Bottled Up (1942-11-18)
plotSynopsis: A strange series of break-ins erupts around Riverâ€™s End as a desperate man searches drugstores and medical offices for bottles from a particular shipment. When he enters Dr. Christianâ€™s office and escapes with one bottle, the doctor notices that an identical bottle from the same delivery contains something hidden inside. He opens it and discovers a fountain pen with a rolled document concealed in its barrel. A call to the manufacturer reveals that a shipping clerk is suspected of stealing a valuable medical formula being prepared for the Army Medical Corps but had to be released for lack of evidence. Dr. Christian realizes the clerk hid the formula inside one bottle before shipment and is now frantically trying to recover the correct package after two similar shipments went to Riverâ€™s End. Police set a trap at another pharmacy and arrest him when he comes for the medicine. The hidden formula supplies the missing evidence, turning the local bottle-stealing mystery into a wartime case involving conspiracy against the federal government.

title: Antiques (1942-11-25)
plotSynopsis: The proud Proctor sisters live in an old family mansion filled with heirlooms, but bedridden Jane does not realize how badly their finances have collapsed. Her sister Libby has been quietly selling treasured family pieces one by one to keep the household going, even parting with a desk that had belonged to their father and grandfather. Dr. Christian recognizes the desk in an antique shop and understands why Libby refused to open the mansion for a Red Cross tour and why she has become increasingly desperate. Rather than expose the secret to Jane, he finds a way to give the house a useful new life: Mrs. Dawson, the wife of a serviceman, and her two children desperately need room while the husband is away. Christian persuades the Proctors to take the family in, giving Jane companionship and purpose, bringing children and life back into the mansion, and easing the pressure that had been forcing Libby to sacrifice the family's past piece by piece.

title: We Hold These Truths (1942-12-02)
plotSynopsis: Rivers End's civic leaders ask Dr. Christian to secure glamorous celebrities for a large War Bond rally, believing famous names are needed to push the local drive over the top. Christian agrees to provide 'stars,' but at the rally he explains that a town should not need show-business glamour to understand either the duty or the practical value of buying bonds. His guests are instead four servicemen: Sergeant Claude Baker, Corporal Stanley Winisaki, Private Streather and Private Swenson. Christian interviews them about their homes, backgrounds, reasons for serving and hopes for the future. One comes from a prosperous Boston family, another is the son of Polish immigrants, and the four different lives converge on ordinary ambitions, family, education and the constitutional liberty they are defending. By presenting them as the most important stars in America, Christian turns the rally from entertainment into a reminder of what the war effort is for. The example carries back into his own office, where he and Judy arrange to set aside ten percent of the practice's receipts and payroll for regular War Bond purchases.

title: Home Coming (1944-10-18)
plotSynopsis: Combat pilot Nicky returns to his wife Connie physically recovered but emotionally unable to bear being close to her, even though he knows he still loves her. Dr. Christian traces the estrangement to survivor's guilt over Nicky's wingman Skip, who died after Nicky's aircraft went out of control during their last combat. Nicky has convinced himself that if he had recovered control sooner he might have saved Skip, and a confused vision during his own crash has become proof in his mind that Connie would be better off without him. When Connie later appears to be in danger near a washed-out bridge, Nicky's immediate terror for her safety breaks through the emotional numbness. He finds her unharmed on the road, embraces her and finally accepts that his love for her never disappeared, a reunion Dr. Christian describes as another miracle worked by love.

title: Fame Before Folly (1944-10-25)
plotSynopsis: A widely reported rescue suddenly turns Dr. Christian from a quiet country physician into a national celebrity. Reporters, photographers, radio calls and even movie offers descend on Rivers End, and publicity man Scoop Gordon convinces himself that the doctor needs professional management. When Dr. Christian refuses to spend his time posing and endorsing products, Gordon secretly hires a close look-alike named Bottomley and manufactures photographs that appear to show the doctor promoting everything from baby products to girdles and dubious advice. The false publicity soon creates angry calls and absurd accusations from people who believe the endorsements are genuine. Confronted, Gordon admits the scheme, and Dr. Christian makes him hear the unglamorous truth behind the original rescue instead of the heroic legend Gordon wants to sell. The doctor returns to his patients, relieved to exchange manufactured fame for ordinary work.

title: The Substitute (1944-11-01)
plotSynopsis: Dr. Christian's overwork brings efficient nurse Agnes Spinney into the office as a temporary substitute for Judy. Spinney quickly reorganizes the office, changes long-standing suppliers, answers correspondence and assumes so many of Judy's duties that Judy feels she is being pushed aside. At the same time Judy is spending conspicuous hours with Lieutenant Tommy Bolton and helping shop for a wedding dress. Christian assumes Judy and Tommy are in love and decides that keeping Spinney will free Judy to marry and have a life of her own. Judy takes that decision as proof she has been replaced and walks out. At a community gathering Christian discovers that Tommy's real sweetheart is a blonde named Kay. Judy's secret errands with Tommy were actually helping him create a bust of Dr. Christian as the first memorial in Rivers End's new Hall of Humanity. Once the misunderstanding is cleared up, Judy returns to the office and Christian happily keeps his longtime partner beside him.

title: The Failure (1944-11-08)
plotSynopsis: Jeff Fowler has recovered from a long illness but is unable to return to his former work, leaving him desperate to prove he can support his wife Alice and their children through writing. He pours himself into poetry and serious manuscripts, suffers rejection after rejection and comes to see himself as a miserable failure. During a visit, Dr. Christian hears Jeff improvise a fantasy adventure for the children and notices how completely the story captures them. He recognizes that Jeff's natural gift is not the literary form he has been forcing, but the children's stories he tells with ease and imagination. With Jeff's permission Christian acts as his representative and has those stories prepared for publication. He then reminds Jeff that Hans Christian Andersen also pursued other literary ambitions before his fairy tales became his lasting achievement. A publisher accepts Jeff's first collection of Winky and Blinky adventures, and Jeff finally understands that reaching the hearts of children is his real vocation rather than a failure.

title: Younger Generation (1944-11-15)
plotSynopsis: Linda Munson learns that Lieutenant Alan Gibbons, the young man she had planned to marry before her mother objected that they were too young, has returned from war badly wounded and discouraged. She insists that she is old enough to decide where she belongs and goes to the military hospital with Dr. Christian. Alan is ashamed of his scarred face and has lost the will to continue treatment, but Lindas unwavering love convinces him that his future is not over. Their courage persuades the older generation, including Lindas mother, that the young people deserve more faith than they have been given.

title: Broken Melody (1944-11-22)
plotSynopsis: A little girl named Carol brings her injured dog to Dr. Christian and leads him to her ailing mother, who has separated from an ambitious musician husband after the strain of his career and their hard life damaged her health. When the father follows them to Riverâ€™s End, he sees how much his family has suffered, admits that music had become more important to him than they were, and asks for a chance to put his wife and daughter first. Dr. Christian helps the family reconcile and begin again.

title: Juliet Said It (1944-11-29)
plotSynopsis: Carol Tucker works as a nurse's aide while her husband, Sergeant Mark Tucker, serves overseas and her injured young brother-in-law Skip recovers in the hospital. Lonely and uncertain about Mark, Carol becomes fascinated by a glamorous visitor who presents himself as an RAF wing commander and former Russian prince. His stories and decorations impress the town, and after Mark is reported missing in action Carol begins to believe she may be falling in love with the supposed hero. Dr. Christian grows suspicious, especially after the man avoids a medical examination following an automobile accident. Skip's scrapbook of military decorations gives Christian the clue: the commander's claimed medal and the date he says he received it do not fit the actual history. Confronted, the impostor cannot produce proper papers and is taken by military police. Almost immediately a new War Department message reports that Mark is alive in a German prisoner-of-war camp and has been awarded the Silver Star for gallantry. Christian replaces the false hero at the town rally with the story of the real one, while Carol recognizes where her loyalty and love truly belong.

title: My Son (1944-12-06)
plotSynopsis: Bachelor engineer Peter Mallison has barely moved into the old Decatur mansion when his houseboy finds a three-month-old baby abandoned on the doorstep during a storm. A note from the desperate mother identifies the child as little Jim and asks whoever lives in the beautiful house to be good to him; a young woman found collapsed nearby soon dies, apparently leaving the baby alone in the world. Peter initially insists that family life has no place in his plans, yet he becomes deeply attached to the child. When no suitable Rivers End home can be found, arrangements are made to send Jim to an orphanage in Perryville. Peter realizes too late that he cannot let the boy go, races the train by car, reaches Perryville and takes Jim back from the accompanying nurse, declaring the child his son. His next problem is providing a motherly home. Judy declines Peter's proposal that she leave her work to help raise the boy, so she introduces him to Abby Westing, a capable woman who loves children. Abby moves in to care for Jim, and within weeks she and Peter are so obviously falling in love that Christian and Judy expect the new family to end in marriage.

title: Such Things Dont Happen (1944-12-13)
plotSynopsis: Mrs. Prince opposes her daughter Helen's marriage to recently discharged soldier Johnny Dodd because his family comes from the wrong side of the tracks, while proudly claiming descent from Revolutionary War hero Jonathan Jackson. Dr. Christian argues that Johnny's own service matters more than inherited social standing, but Mrs. Prince refuses to listen. Then Christian encounters Jonathan Jackson himself, apparently returned from the grave. The supposed family hero cheerfully dismantles the legend built around him: he was an ordinary man from an undistinguished family, his famous Revolutionary exploit was greatly exaggerated, and most decisively, he never married and therefore cannot be Mrs. Prince's ancestor at all. Christian brings Jonathan face to face with her. After hearing the truth from the man she has spent years glorifying, Mrs. Prince agrees to Helen and Johnny's marriage and promises them a proper wedding, while Jonathan disappears back into the night as mysteriously as he arrived.

title: The Fugitive (1944-12-20)
plotSynopsis: An escaped prisoner in German uniform is shot near Rivers End on Christmas Eve, forcing Dr. Christian to decide whether wartime hatred can change a doctor's duty. He treats the wounded man and assists a mysterious visiting surgeon through a delicate operation, insisting that a patient must be cared for regardless of uniform. The apparent enemy is then identified as an American serviceman who had escaped a German prison camp wearing enemy clothing. The unknown surgeon departs before he can be thanked, while Dr. Christian concludes that the war may justify fighting the enemy's ideas but not abandoning a physician's obligation to an individual life.

title: Wish On A Star (1944-12-27)
plotSynopsis: A rise in juvenile crime reaches Dr. Christian personally when a swaggering young tough named Joe comes to his office with a badly cut arm. Joe is trying to impress Judy Price with money, bravado and stories of easy living, but the doctor gradually learns that the cash comes from a gang involved in robberies. Joe wants out, yet the gangâ€™s hold and his fear of looking weak keep pulling him back. After an attempted holdup leaves him with a serious burn, Dr. Christian knows the police are already looking for a boy with exactly that injury. Joe begs the doctor not to turn him in because he wants Judy to remember him as someone worthwhile rather than as a criminal. Christian challenges him to prove that courage by surrendering voluntarily instead of waiting to be caught. Joe says an emotional goodbye to Judy, looks out at a star and makes his wish, then calls police headquarters himself and admits the holdup. Later Dr. Christian tells Judy that the judge recognized Joeâ€™s youth and voluntary confession, allowing him the chance to join the Navy and serve his country instead of simply disappearing into the criminal system.

title: The Queen Loved Herring (1945-01-10)
plotSynopsis: Nurse Nina Jones falls in love with wealthy Army Air Forces lieutenant Jimmy Bradley but is ashamed to let him meet the immigrant grandparents who raised her in their small delicatessen home. Jimmy's family has asked him to meet Nina's people before making a promise, and Nina becomes convinced that the contrast in background will end the romance. Dr. Christian sends Jimmy to the house anyway, where the grandparents welcome him with their own food, wine and traditions. To break Nina's obsession with pedigree, the doctor tells an elaborate story about disguised royalty whose queen prized an ordinary herring above jewels, then admits privately that the tale is nonsense that served a useful purpose. Jimmy sees the worth of Nina's family for himself, and he and Nina promise that when the bells of peace ring they will also be wedding bells.

title: And Not To Yield (1945-01-17)
plotSynopsis: Judy worries about a mysterious elderly man living quietly outside Rivers End with the devoted companion who has cared for him for years. The old man, once successful and well known, is now seriously ill and refuses help. Christian discovers that alcoholism destroyed his marriage long ago. His wife left with their young son Michael, and the ashamed father deliberately disappeared from the boy's life, believing that removing himself was the only decent thing he could still do. He later stopped drinking but remained too proud to seek forgiveness, following Michael's life only through photographs and clippings. Michael, now an Army lieutenant using his mother's surname Hill, has grown up believing his father simply abandoned him. Christian travels to Michael's camp and tells him the truth, arguing that older people can spend years paying inwardly for mistakes they made when they were younger. Michael at first refuses reconciliation, then changes his mind and returns to Rivers End. Father and son are reunited at the sickbed, and the old man's will to live returns with him. Their reconciliation closes with the lines from Tennyson that both remember: though weakened by time and fate, they remain strong in will 'to strive, to seek, to find, and not to yield.'

title: And A Little Child (1945-01-24)
plotSynopsis: Marina leaves her brilliant surgeon husband Tony Bartlett after success and money turn him cold, arrogant and unwilling to treat patients who cannot pay. Military service changes Tony: working beside compassionate doctors among wounded servicemen teaches him why medicine exists and what his ambition had cost him. Back in Rivers End he uses his skill to save the orphaned child Jamie, reunites with Marina, and the couple decide to adopt the child, beginning a new family around service and love rather than status.

title: Always Yours (1945-01-31)
plotSynopsis: After two years apart during the war, Gail Sloan breaks her engagement to serviceman Larry Warnock and becomes involved with older hospital doctor Graham, believing the distance has changed her feelings. Larry unexpectedly returns home suffering another attack of malaria and admits to Dr. Christian that losing Gail has left him with nothing to come home to. Meanwhile Graham pressures Gail into an immediate elopement across the state line. On the trip she realizes she has made a mistake, slips away from him at a bus stop and walks through the snow back to Rivers End. At Dr. Christian's office she and Larry finally speak honestly: he still wants a future with her, and she still loves him. Their reconciliation ends with Gail repeating the sign-off from Larry's wartime letters, 'always yours.'

title: The Shawl (1945-02-07)
plotSynopsis: Civil War veteran Arthur Colby dies after spending most of his long life trying to remember a single wondrous event that occurred after he was wounded at Gettysburg. In one final lucid moment he can almost tell Dr. Christian what happened, recalling a hospital, terrible cold and something he must leave behind, but he dies before naming it. Convinced there is a record in Colby's abandoned house, Christian and Judy search it at night. Beneath the bed they find an old trunk containing a shawl, Colby's faded uniform and his wartime diary. The final entries solve the mystery. On July 6, 1863, as the wounded Colby lay outside a hospital shivering while waiting for space inside, a tall man stopped, removed the shawl from his own shoulders, wrapped it around the soldier and spoke kindly to him. The man was Abraham Lincoln. The shawl Colby had struggled all his life to remember was therefore not a forgotten romance, as Judy first imagined, but a personal relic of Lincoln's compassion. Christian and Judy realize they have recovered both the historic object and the memory Colby had wanted preserved.

title: Golden Bells (1945-02-14)
plotSynopsis: Exhausted after a night with a sick child, Dr. Christian dozes in his office while worrying that he has promised a fresh story for a children's Valentine party. In his brief sleep he is summoned by a fairy from a second plane of existence and carried by magic carpet through a comic fantasy world of operators, trolls, fairies and strange rules to a golden palace where a young prince is in severe pain. Christian learns that the prince had visited the human world and eaten unripe apples. The court's mysterious magical illness turns out to be an ordinary stomachache, and a simple first-plane remedy quickly puts the prince right. The grateful fairy kingdom sends Christian home with a souvenir. He wakes after only a few minutes and tells Judy the whole impossible adventure as the new story for the children. Judy dismisses it as a dream, until Christian produces the physical souvenir he was given in the fantasy world.

title: George Washington Jenks (1945-02-21)
plotSynopsis: Twelve-year-old George Washington Jenks is mocked by classmates for his name, glasses and refusal to fight, but the boys do not know that rheumatic fever left him with a serious heart condition that forbids strenuous activity. When they stage another humiliating prank, George finally fights back, collapses from the strain and nearly dies. Dr. Christian explains to the ashamed boys that George has been fighting all his life against physical handicaps and that enduring them without complaint has taken more courage than any schoolyard brawl. George recovers to find his classmates waiting to welcome him back and asking him to manage their team, turning the name they once ridiculed into one they respect.

title: The Laughingest Family (1945-04-25)
plotSynopsis: Seven-year-old Mimi Peters has returned from wartime Europe after losing both parents and has passed through several foster homes without ever recovering the ability to laugh. Dr. Christian believes the traumatized child needs not another respectable placement but someone whose own suffering can create a genuine bond with her. At the same time, a young woman living in seclusion behind a black veil has withdrawn from the world because an accident scarred her face. Dr. Christian deliberately brings the two wounded lives together by arranging for Mimi to be lifted over the wall into the womanâ€™s garden. Mimi bluntly confronts the womanâ€™s shame, while the woman learns that Mimiâ€™s parents were killed in bombing and that the child believes her mother in heaven is waiting to hear her laugh again. Their defensiveness gives way to sympathy and affection. The woman removes her veil, decides to seek treatment for her scar and asks to adopt Mimi. Dr. Christian reveals that Mimiâ€™s supposed wandering into the garden was no accident, and the new family begins with both child and prospective mother ready to stop hiding from life.

title: This Is Where I Came In (1945-05-02)
plotSynopsis: Returning serviceman Perry Tate is preparing to marry Mary Mason when actress Vivian Hall produces an old letter in Perry's handwriting that reads like a proposal to her. Perry explains that years earlier, while helping Vivian prepare props for a stage play, he copied the romantic letter directly from the script as a joke and signed it. Vivian nevertheless intends to use the document as proof of a promise to marry and as publicity to revive her career. Dr. Christian confronts her with a copy of the play and gets Vivian to reenact the scene in which the heroine burns the letter. Carried away by her own performance, Vivian accidentally sets fire to the real document. Christian puts out the fire, but Perry's signature has burned away, destroying the leverage Vivian meant to use against his real marriage plans.

title: Excalibur (1945-05-09)
plotSynopsis: On a stormy night Dr. Christian tells Judy and Dick Foster a deliberately spooky story from a trip to Britain. He and two companions investigate a lake where local legend says Excalibur was cast away and is still guarded by the Lady of the Lake. A mysterious Lady Morgan in white seems to know more about their plans than she should, and when one of the men, Walker, makes a nighttime attempt to recover the sword, he dies in an accident that can be explained by a blow against the boat but leaves several uncanny details unresolved. Dr. Christian never tries again, leaving both the sword and the truth of the legend beneath the lake.

title: The Hero (1945-05-16)
plotSynopsis: Riverâ€™s End is preparing to dedicate a monument to wartime hero John Blake, who is believed to have died after going down during the war and is credited locally with a Distinguished Service Cross. On the day of the ceremony Dr. Christian discovers a starving, bearded drifter and recognizes him as the supposedly dead John. John explains that he actually survived with the help of French peasants, but after earlier trouble with his commanding officer he failed to report back to the Army. The medal story was a mistake involving another serviceman named John Blake, and shame kept him from returning to a mother and sweetheart who believed he had died honorably. Dr. Christian warns that simply walking into the dedication as he is would destroy the pride that helped his mother endure her loss. John decides instead to return to military authority, clear his record and earn his way home properly. At the station his former sweetheart Mary recognizes him despite his appearance. Learning what he intends to do, she promises to wait for him. The townâ€™s memorial ceremony goes forward, while the living John sets out to become the kind of man the monument already says he was.

title: Gentleman Of Mystery (1945-05-23)
plotSynopsis: Famous author Gerald Halsey returns to Rivers End after years abroad intending to sell the family toolworks, whose new industrial process is important to the war effort. Bitter, detached from his family and contemptuous of patriotism, he seems willing to sell to a suspicious foreign buyer even after his son and young engineer Nick warn him about the danger. Dr. Christian secretly stages a confrontation with an actor posing as the foreign agent, complete with a planted witness and blank cartridge. When the fake buyer threatens the family, Halsey finally fights to defend his son and the process, revealing courage and loyalty he had buried beneath years of cynicism; Dr. Christian keeps the ruse private while Halsey begins reclaiming his place in the family.

title: General (1945-05-30)
plotSynopsis: The elderly General Benjamin Gerard lives on wartime memories and meddles in the military letters received by his family, wanting to remain important while younger generations are away at war. After misplacing crucial letters and being harshly rebuked, he stages an apparent train accident so the family will fear losing him and appreciate him again. Dr. Christian quickly realizes the dramatic bruises are only ink, but lets the General keep his dignity rather than publicly exposing the ruse.

title: Diagnosis After Death (1945-06-06)
plotSynopsis: While Dr. Alexander Webb is temporarily covering Dr. Christian's practice, state senator Fredericks is found dead in the street after appearing to stagger like a drunk. The senator's widow Margaret privately threatens Webb, saying she heard him quarrel with her husband shortly before the death and will accuse him of murder unless he helps prevent an investigation that could expose family scandals. Webb had opposed the senator's plan to release and abandon his violently insane brother, giving Margaret a plausible motive to use against him. At the medical inquiry, needle scars first suggest that the senator may have been a drug addict, but Webb notices that the fresh injection was high on the right arm, an awkward place for the right-handed senator to inject himself. He concludes the senator was diabetic, that the marks came from insulin, and that a family member sometimes gave the arm injections. An excessive dose would also explain the senator's staggering before death as insulin shock rather than drunkenness. As Webb works through the evidence, Margaret breaks down and confesses that she deliberately gave her husband the fatal overdose because she hated him. Her attempt to coerce and frame Webb collapses under the medical evidence.

title: Jere To Liebe (1945-06-13)
plotSynopsis: With Dr. Christian away, Dr. Alexander Webb is drawn into the disappearance of visiting journalist Osgood, who had been seen anxiously studying an encyclopedia before vanishing to an abandoned quarry shack. Osgood is convinced that rapidly appearing red patches mean he has contracted leprosy and has isolated himself rather than expose his fiancee and the town. Webb traces the clue to the encyclopedia volume, examines him and finds that the terrifying self-diagnosis is completely wrong: after months of sparse wartime eating, rich food has triggered an extreme case of hives. The frightened reporter returns to Rivers End cured of both the rash and his imagined fatal disease, with his wedding merely postponed while he recovers.

title: The Lady The Wolf (1945-06-20)
plotSynopsis: While Dr. Alexander Webb is temporarily filling in at Rivers End, Judy Price keeps receiving bold telephone calls from Marine Lieutenant Jerry Mitchell, a stranger who has been told about her by a mutual friend. Webb dismisses Jerry as a telephone wolf and warns Judy against meeting him, but Jerry turns out to be a decent, lonely serviceman spending his last night of leave in town. Judy agrees to go dancing with him, leaving Webb with Jerry's unused concert tickets. Webb then telephones a woman he barely knows to offer the tickets and, in the process, gets himself invited to accompany her. Later Judy and Jerry run into Webb and his new companion at the concert, where Webb's attempt to pretend he is a classical-music expert quickly collapses. The comedy leaves Judy amused that the man who lectured her about telephone wolves has been caught in essentially the same sort of spontaneous romance himself.

title: Dr. Christian Award Winners of 1945 (1945-06-27)
plotSynopsis: This special broadcast steps away from the usual Riverâ€™s End drama to announce the winners of the 1945 Dr. Christian script competition. Jean Hersholt first reports on his just-completed trip to war-torn Europe and Denmark, then the program names eight prize-winning writers selected on merit from thousands of entries. The $2,000 first prize goes to Eleanor Tarshis of Forest Hills, New York; Joseph C. Cook and Dr. Simon G. Sacks of Duluth share the $1,000 second prize; James Boston of Cambridge receives the $500 third prize; and five additional writers receive $350 awards. The broadcast interviews several winners, including Tarshis in the studio and Cook and Sacks by remote connection from Duluth, discussing how they came to radio writing and developed their entries. The show closes by previewing upcoming broadcasts of the winning plays, making this episode a behind-the-scenes awards program rather than a fictional Dr. Christian story.

title: Always A Woman (1945-07-11)
plotSynopsis: Mike Taylor has waited for his fiancee to come home on leave from the Women's Army Corps, but when she arrives as a confident lieutenant he feels diminished by comparison and begins pushing her away. She interprets his defensiveness as rejection and prepares to leave Rivers End for good. Dr. Christian recognizes that Mike is not ashamed of her service; he is ashamed of how inadequate he feels beside it. He disables his own car and arranges for Mike to drive her on an out-of-town medical errand, giving them the private time neither has managed to ask for. The operation succeeds: she later telephones as Mrs. Michael Taylor.

title: Joyous Heart (1945-07-18)
plotSynopsis: Margaret Powers leaves the hospital convinced that her serviceman husband Hal has finally come home, only for Dr. Christian to discover that the bouquet she thought he brought was actually a telegram reporting him missing. He gently helps her face the shock without stripping away every source of hope. When fresh cigar ashes appear in Hals locked room, Margaret knows there is an ordinary explanation, but accepts them as the tangible sign she needs to believe he may still return, and the renewed hope restores her strength.

title: The Liar (1945-07-25)
plotSynopsis: Lydia Parker returns to Rivers End after years away and asks Dr. Christian for help with her twin sister Lucy. Lydia says Lucy has become a compulsive liar, inventing pointless stories about where she has been, what she has done and whom she has seen, and that the behavior has worsened since the death of Lucy's husband Emil. Christian listens carefully as Lydia describes their lifelong closeness and insists that Lucy is physically healthy but emotionally disturbed. He suggests rest and familiar surroundings and avoids directly challenging Lydia's account. Only after Lydia leaves again, supposedly taking Lucy to relatives in California, does the truth emerge: Lucy died of pneumonia in the spring of 1901, nearly forty years earlier, and Christian himself was a pallbearer at her funeral. Lydia never accepted her twin's death and has continued to live as though Lucy were beside her, creating new stories to explain her supposed activities. Because Lydia remains harmless and otherwise functions normally, Christian chooses compassion over a brutal confrontation with the fantasy, arguing that the lonely woman's private reality deserves understanding rather than ridicule.

title: The Legend Of Khorassam (1945-08-01)
plotSynopsis: While resting between calls, Dr. Christian is startled by a mysterious woman who brings an urgently ill companion, Moses, into his office. An emergency operation saves the man and removes an enormous pearl-like object that had been obstructing his airway. The strangers depart almost as mysteriously as they arrived, leaving Dr. Christian with an unexplained gift and a story that seems to echo an old legend; rather than destroy the mystery by investigating too closely, he chooses to let a little wonder remain.

title: Christmas Deferred (1945-08-08)
plotSynopsis: Six-year-old Ted Ward was gravely ill and unconscious through the previous Christmas, and his mother Ruth has never told him that the holiday passed while he slept. Ruth has also cut herself and Ted off from Rivers End, embittered by the disgrace and death of her husband Glenn after he took money from a bank and, she believes, was never given a chance to make restitution. When Dr. Christian learns that Ted is waiting for a Christmas he thinks is still ahead, he and newspaper editor Matt Redding decide to give it to him in midsummer. Matt publishes Ted's story and August 8 becomes a community Christmas, drawing gifts, letters, a tree and old neighbors who rediscover their own generosity. Christian deliberately shows Ruth how the project is healing other wounded people too, including an elderly craftsman who resumes making toys after losing his son in the war and former enemies who reconcile while baking Christmas cookies. Ruth's resistance finally breaks as she sees Ted brighten and the town answer bitterness with kindness. When Ted's grandmother tries to remove him from the excitement, Ted insists the celebration is helping him. Afterward he admits to Christian that he eventually realized it was August, not December, but continued the make-believe because the unusual Christmas was doing as much good for his mother and grandmother as it was for him.

title: Canine Justice (1945-08-15)
plotSynopsis: Young Teddy Douglas is devoted to Laddie, the family's discharged K-9 Corps dog whose wartime training makes him far more than an ordinary pet. Exploring an abandoned house that neighborhood children consider haunted, Teddy discovers a wanted jewel thief hiding there with stolen property. The fugitive catches the boy, ties him up and plans to leave him helpless while he escapes. Teddy warns that Laddie will come when called, and when the armed criminal threatens the dog, Laddie attacks and subdues him badly enough for the police to capture him. The thief survives and is identified as a man wanted in several cities, making Teddy eligible for a substantial reward. When officials then discuss destroying Laddie because he attacked a human being, Dr. Christian insists the dog used the training given him in war to save a child's life and help bring a dangerous criminal to justice, and vows to fight any attempt to punish him for it.

title: Leave It To Love (1945-08-22)
plotSynopsis: Randy Foster returns to Rivers End after losing both feet in combat. Army rehabilitation has taught him to use artificial feet confidently, he is preparing to return to work, and he wants an ordinary life rather than constant reminders that he is different. His wife Ellen, however, cannot stop protecting him, worrying over steps, drafts, traffic and every small exertion until her sympathy becomes suffocating. Randy asks Dr. Christian to help her see that he is capable, while Ellen separately complains that Randy refuses the special care she thinks he needs. Christian mischievously turns the situation around so that each begins treating the other as the fragile one. Randy fusses over Ellen, insists she rest and takes over the household, while Ellen experiences firsthand how oppressive excessive solicitude can feel. The scheme collapses when Christian and Judy arrive and learn the real reason Ellen has not been feeling well: she is pregnant. With a baby genuinely on the way, the couple's roles and worries find a more natural balance, and Christian admits that love and nature have solved the problem better than his meddling could.

title: Puff (1945-08-29)
plotSynopsis: Young Ted was blinded during a bombing in France that killed his family, and he insists that his beloved white poodle Puff still visits and guides him even though no one else can see the dog. X-rays reveal a treatable brain injury, but after successful surgery Ted still cannot see, leading Dr. Christian to suspect that fear and grief are blocking the recovery. When Ted's father, previously reported missing in action, unexpectedly returns, Ted finally uses his eyes and recognizes him. The father then tells how a mysterious white poodle led him safely through a German minefield, eerily echoing Ted's stories of Puff and leaving the dog's true nature unexplained.

title: Much To Do About Marty (1945-09-05)
plotSynopsis: Laurie Gary separates from her bandleader husband Marty after years of having their private life turned into material for his jokes, while Marty resents Laurie's increasingly determined effort to make him quieter, more dignified and socially conventional. Dr. Christian compares them to children in a tug of war and suggests that Marty stop pulling back for a while. Marty therefore gives Laurie exactly the refined husband she says she wants, trading his usual gags and show-business energy for quiet evenings, classical reading and restraint. The experiment makes both of them see what they have been demanding from the other. After Laurie gets a closer look at how difficult Marty's comic work really is, Marty promises not to exploit everything she says for a gag, and Laurie promises not to be so sensitive about the humor that is part of him. They reconcile without either having to become someone else.

title: Room Clerk (1945-09-12)
plotSynopsis: When Charlie Stutz, the room clerk on the three-to-eleven shift at Rivers End's United States Hotel, suffers a heart attack, Dr. Christian is summoned and sends him to the hospital. The hotel manager is away in Chicago and Alex, the next clerk, has not reported for work, leaving a lobby full of guests with no one to handle keys, mail, telephones or room problems. Bellboy George persuades Christian to take over the desk temporarily, with Judy helping, and the doctor quickly discovers that hotel work can be as chaotic as medicine. He sorts out wrong keys, confused guests and a drunken occupant while trying to find a room for a soldier's mother who has arrived late at night to meet her son when he comes home on furlough the next day. With every room occupied, Christian has the drunk guest moved to a warm cot in the furnace room under the pretense that the boys are hiding him from the police, freeing his room for the mother. Alex finally returns and, impressed that Christian kept the hotel running, relieves him. Christian and Judy are barely out the door when George calls them back because a woman in room 308 is having a baby, sending the exhausted doctor straight from his temporary job as room clerk back into his real profession.

title: Our Daughter Barbara (1945-09-19)
plotSynopsis: Laura Marshall is deeply devoted to her husband Steve and to Barbara, Steve's daughter from his first marriage, but a man from Laura's past threatens the family. Before coming to Rivers End, Laura had fallen in love with married Carl Gilbert and, after discovering he never intended to leave his wife, drove her car through a guardrail in despair. She recovered, began a new life and later married Steve. Months into that marriage, however, Laura angrily went out with Carl one night after quarreling with Steve because he would not leave an ill Barbara to take Laura on a trip. Carl later returns broke and demands $5,000. He still has Laura's old love letters and threatens to combine them with evidence of that night out to persuade Barbara's bitter maternal grandmother, who once lost a custody fight with Steve, to reopen the case by portraying Laura as an unfit stepmother. Unable to raise the money without Steve learning why, Laura turns to Dr. Christian. Christian brings Carl and Steve together and forces the blackmail into the open. Steve is initially shocked and Laura, believing he values her only as a mother for Barbara, prepares to leave. At that moment Steve recognizes that he loves Laura herself as much as ever. He stops her, forgives her, and they return home together to Barbara, while Carl's leverage disappears.

title: The Wolf Cried Navy Blue (1945-09-26)
plotSynopsis: Navy sailors Joe and Pip miss their train after Joe jumps off in Rivers End chasing a woman he mistakes for an old sweetheart. Dr. Christian and Judy invite the stranded sailors to dinner, where both men become increasingly interested in Judy and turn the evening into a comic rivalry full of boasting, flirting and misunderstandings. By the time they finally make the next train, the supposedly quiet town has given Judy exactly the kind of unexpected adventure she had been wishing for.

title: Love To Mama (1945-10-03)
plotSynopsis: Madeleine Renaldi's elderly mother lives for letters from her absent son Johnny, the troubled child she has always loved most. Mama believes Johnny escaped his criminal past, found honest work in California and is saving for a fur coat and a home where she can live with him. Madeleine knows the truth but protects the illusion: she reads the letters, destroys the evidence Mama should not see, goes hungry to buy the promised fur coat herself and lets Mama credit Johnny for everything. The truth finally arrives in a letter Mama brings to Dr. Christian to read aloud. Johnny has spent months in prison and is about to die in the electric chair. Realizing too late that Mama is hearing every word, Dr. Christian then explains Madeleine's sacrifice, including finding her praying in the snow for Johnny's soul. Mama understands that her daughter's supposed jealousy was love and courage, and chooses to keep sharing the comforting fiction with Madeleine rather than let the truth destroy what they have left.

title: Chain Letter (1945-10-10)
plotSynopsis: Dr. Christian and Judy argue over why people perpetuate chain letters, with Christian blaming fear and Judy believing money is the stronger motive.
