To test the question they send one to their financially struggling friend Tom Holland, whose advertising agency is close to failure. Tom himself despises chain letters, but his superstitious wife Bertha secretly sends copies in hopes of bringing him luck. One copy is addressed in Tom's name to Jack Douglas, the Old Silver cigarette representative whose account Tom desperately needs, even though Douglas has just declared that people who send chain letters are fools. Tom, Bertha, Christian and Judy scramble to recover the damaging letter. In the middle of the crisis, however, the repeated idea of a chain gives Tom the advertising hook he has been unable to find: a slogan linking chain smoking with Old Silver cigarettes. Douglas loves the campaign and awards Tom the major account, joking that he knew Tom was intelligent when Tom said he had thrown a chain letter away. The experiment nearly ruins Tom, but the chain letter accidentally supplies the idea that saves his business.

title: The Attic Stairway Murder Mystery (1945-10-17)
plotSynopsis: When wealthy Mrs. Parker is found dead at the bottom of her attic stairs, suspicion falls on her disabled housekeeper and former friend Mary Bignall, especially after Mrs. Parkers rings disappear. Dr. Christian learns that decades earlier Mrs. Parker had intercepted and switched letters between Mary and Ed Parker, then married Ed after an accident left Mary crippled. On the day of the death Mary finally found Eds original Valentine proving he had never rejected her; during their confrontation Mrs. Parker lost her balance and fell. Mary arranged the body and took the rings Ed had once meant for her, but Dr. Christian chooses to let the accidental death and Marys long suffering remain private.

title: Playboy (1945-10-24)
plotSynopsis: Pat Blair has always been Rivers End's charming, irresponsible playboy, and a damaged heart has kept him out of military service while his old schoolmate Bob Sims fights overseas. Gossip becomes especially ugly when Pat spends time with Bob's wife Lily, leading Bob to write Lily that she need not remain tied to him if she prefers Pat. Then Pat is injured in an automobile accident after trying to avoid blind Elizabeth Elliott as she crosses the street; Elizabeth suffers a broken hip and fears she will never walk again. Dr. Christian sends Pat to cheer her, and the supposedly selfish playboy devotes himself to her recovery. He helps arrange her settlement, sells securities left by his mother to pay part of it himself, tends her garden and becomes the one person who can make her laugh and believe she will walk. Bob returns on furlough just as Lily unexpectedly finds Pat coaching Elizabeth through her first steps. Lily angrily condemns Pat, but Elizabeth defends the friend she has come to know. The emotional confrontation makes Elizabeth forget her fear long enough to walk, while Bob finally hears Lily's explanation and recognizes how badly gossip and assumption distorted what happened. Christian's lesson is that Pat contains real generosity despite his faults, and that judging any of them by reputation alone misses the whole person.

title: Sterling Silver (1945-10-31)
plotSynopsis: As Rivers End's old opera house is about to be demolished, Dr. Christian remembers Sterling Silver, the melodrama actor who was his boyhood hero. The past suddenly becomes a real mystery when owner Sam Roberts is shot, valuable antique playbills disappear and one of Silver's ornate pistols is found at the scene. Sam believes the now-elderly actor attacked him over a thirty-thousand-dollar promissory note, but Dr. Christian cannot reconcile that accusation with the man he remembers. Returning to the dark theater with police, he traps the real thief, who had clubbed Silver, stolen one of his pistols, accidentally shot Sam and hidden both Silver and the stolen playbills among the stage props. Silver survives, the old debt is explained as an investment gone bad rather than a betrayal, and Dr. Christian gets one final chance to remember the theater as it was before demolition.

title: The Last Awakening (1945-11-07)
plotSynopsis: After a flood, scores of Rivers End residents suddenly fall into a deep, unnatural sleep, filling the hospital and provoking an airtight quarantine around the town. Dr. Christian notices that the victims are medically normal and traces the mystery to the waterworks, where Mayor Andrews personally tried to replenish a depleted chlorine supply. In the rush, cylinders of chloral were mistaken for chlorine; mixed into the water, the chemical formed chloral hydrate, effectively dosing the town with a powerful sleeping drug. Once the accidental contamination is identified, the terrifying epidemic is revealed to be a massive but temporary poisoning rather than a new disease.

title: The Long Lane (1945-11-14)
plotSynopsis: Gladys Brooks has built a new life with her young son Jackie and plans to marry Jerry Connor after years of separation from her husband Jeffrey. A War Department telegram suddenly reports that Jeffrey, long believed lost, has been found alive in China. Jackie is thrilled to learn that his father served in the war, while Gladys is forced to face feelings she thought were over. When Jeffrey returns, crippled but changed, he tells Dr. Christian that he had left Gladys because he believed he was selfish and useless, then found purpose fighting in China and learned to live for other people. Convinced Gladys loves Jerry, Jeffrey plans to leave rather than stand in her way. Gladys overhears him, realizes she still loves her husband, and asks his forgiveness. Jerry quietly withdraws as the separated couple reunites and Jackie gets his father back.

title: The Philandering Ghost (1945-11-21)
plotSynopsis: Recently discharged veteran John Talbot reopens his family's supposedly haunted old house, where the legend of his vanished great-uncle Mortimer soon becomes very lively. A flirtatious 'ghost' begins kissing frightened women, and John discovers that Mortimer has been wandering because of a promise made after losing the woman he loved. The supernatural visitor's matchmaking creates comic chaos but ultimately helps bring new affection into the lonely house, leaving John with the chance to replace the old haunting with life, love and laughter.

title: Retreat To Kindness (1945-11-28)
plotSynopsis: Former Rivers End troublemaker Jim Bradley returns as a successful, hard-edged reporter determined to write a sensational feature on psychiatrist Dr. Bob Patterson. Bradley plans to expose the violence and mental illness in Patterson's childhood home, including his father's commitment to an institution and young Patterson's own brief jailing after striking his father while defending his mother. Christian, Judy and Patterson argue that publishing every painful fact would serve gossip more than truth and would needlessly hurt Patterson's elderly mother, but Bradley prides himself on having no sentimentality and insists that hurting people is sometimes part of being a good reporter. Bradley has also returned to collect the diary his own mother left for him, sealed away after her death. Reading it changes him: his mother wrote of her love for Jim and of her gratitude to Patterson for helping her understand that Jim needed to leave Rivers End and make his own life, even though she longed to call him home. Confronted with the private compassion he had dismissed in others, Bradley abandons the article and tells Christian he is leaving with something more important, having made his own 'retreat to kindness.'

title: Girl Trouble (1945-12-05)
plotSynopsis: A cold December night brings Dr. Christian into what first looks like an attempted kidnapping. Wealthy schoolboy Johnny is found bound, gagged and nearly frozen on the Ramseysâ€™ porch, and the police assume a gang of boys must be responsible. Dr. Christian is less convinced. He sees that Johnny is under intense pressure from parents who buy him everything but give him little freedom, demand top school performance, control his food and schedule, and leave almost no time for ordinary play. Johnny also has a very obvious adolescent interest in the Ramseysâ€™ pretty daughter Marie. As the boy recovers, Dr. Christian establishes that the crude ropes and wire were no professional kidnapping tools and finally gets to the truth: Johnny staged the incident himself. Rather than punish a frightened and embarrassed boy, the doctor makes his parents recognize how their expectations helped drive him to such a desperate bid for attention. He persuades the police and family to let the matter die quietly, then asks Marie to help Johnny put the episode behind him by refusing to feed further gossip.

title: Susan Comes Marching Home (1945-12-12)
plotSynopsis: Riverâ€™s End welcomes home Army nurse Susan Anderson, who has survived wartime service and years in a Japanese prison camp. Susan has only thirty days of leave before returning to duty, and she has already decided what she wants most: to marry Hillary Dana, the shy lumber-mill owner she has loved since their school days. Hillary loves Susan too, but feels inadequate beside a decorated Army captain and is so painfully bashful that every attempt to propose collapses into comic disaster. Dr. Christian and Judy repeatedly try to coach him, but even a carefully rehearsed visit ends with a broken goldfish bowl and Hillary fleeing without his hat. Convinced he has made a fool of himself, Hillary retreats to a fishing cabin he had quietly begun building for Susan after wartime reports made him fear she would never come home. Susan finds him there, forces the truth into the open and accepts his clumsy proposal. Dr. Christian arrives with one more piece of good news: the Army is releasing personnel who spent more than sixty days in prison camps, so Susanâ€™s discharge will allow the couple to begin their life together without another separation.

title: The Little Carpenter (1945-12-19)
plotSynopsis: Dr. Christian is unexpectedly left to host an elegant Christmas party where old resentments and hidden scandals quickly surface. A wealthy man revives a decades-old grievance against the woman who rejected him when he was poor, her naval-officer son is exposed for borrowing valuable securities he could not repay, and another young man reveals that he and the officer are twin brothers separated in childhood, one adopted into privilege while the other grew up poor. The bitterness is interrupted by a poor boy asking to earn enough money for a set of carpenter's tools. His simple Christmas appeal changes the room: the overlooked brother offers the value of his art scholarship to cover the debt, the injured businessman chooses forgiveness and honest repayment, the officer's fiancée stands by him, and the adults begin reconciling. At dinner they discover that the little boy has quietly returned the money they gave him, completing the lesson in generosity.

title: Mission Accomplished (1945-12-26)
plotSynopsis: Ten-year-old Joni Love has taken seriously the last assignment her father gave her before he was killed during the war: look after her mother and make sure she is happy. Deciding that her lonely mother needs another husband, Joni first asks bachelor Dr. Christian to marry her. He gently declines but agrees to help. The better prospect turns out to be returning Major Miller, owner of the local radio station that Leslie Love has competently managed during his military service. Because their correspondence was signed simply 'Leslie Love,' Miller had assumed his wartime station manager was a man and initially has difficulty accepting that a woman has run the operation so well. Meeting Leslie quickly changes his attitude. Joni notices that her mother likes the younger major and that he likes both mother and daughter, and cheerfully shifts her matchmaking plan from Dr. Christian to Miller, satisfied that she is finally carrying out her father's mission to keep her mother from being alone.

title: What It Takes (1946-01-02)
plotSynopsis: A January blizzard strands Dr. Christian, Judy and a cross-section of strangers on an interurban bus. Among them are a wounded veteran disgusted by civilian complaining, a prisoner being returned under guard, a struggling musician, and a young mother whose undernourished baby urgently needs milk. Dr. Christian discovers that the mother is also clinging to the belief that her husband will come home, although the military telegram she carries reports him killed. As the stalled bus grows colder, the passengers who had been arguing and thinking only of themselves begin giving up coats, blankets, comfort and safety to protect the mother and child. Men set out through the storm for help, and even the prisoner, given a genuine opportunity to run, chooses not to escape. By morning the crisis has shown each of them what it takes to put another person's life ahead of his own grievances.

title: Curare (1946-01-09)
plotSynopsis: Former star aerialists Benning and Brown come to Dr. Christian with progressive weakness, dizziness and failing grip that have reduced them from the big time to a small circus. He warns them not to perform until the illness is understood, but they go on anyway and one falls from the trapeze. At the ring Dr. Christian notices clown Jojo drop a small bottle and connects it with the performers' rope-burned bare hands. Testing the equipment reveals that their trapeze ropes have been repeatedly dosed with curare, slowly poisoning the men through contact. Jojo confesses that he trained Benning and Brown, then grew bitter when they became stars while an injury ended his own aerial career. His elaborate revenge had been to destroy them gradually while pretending to remain their loyal friend.

title: Scandal In The Fourth Dimension (1946-01-16)
plotSynopsis: Professor John Boswell refuses to approve his daughter Betty's marriage to young Alec Dale because Alec intends to become an inventor after leaving the Army. Rather than argue directly, Dr. Christian tells Boswell an outrageous college story about Professor Erasmus Doke, his brilliant student Aloysius O'Flannigan and Doke's daughter Patsy. In Christian's tale, Doke's experiments with the fourth dimension leave him only partly visible. Aloysius understands the mathematics well enough to restore him, but will help only if Doke accepts his courtship of Patsy. Doke stubbornly refuses and tries to live half-invisible, producing classroom chaos, public panic and an absurd arrest in which police struggle with the visible and invisible halves of him. Humiliated, Doke finally gives in, Aloysius restores him, and the young couple's engagement follows. Boswell suspects Christian invented the whole story, but the lesson works: he admits he may have been too hard on Alec and agrees to reconsider rather than trying to stop the younger generation from choosing for itself.

title: Mr Sourpuss (1946-01-23)
plotSynopsis: Children's author and illustrator Elliott Kenyon returns from wartime service physically recovering from a bomber crash but emotionally shut down, hiding under another name and insisting that he can never write again. He finally tells Dr. Christian why: during his last mission over a French town, the bombing killed the mother of a little boy whose family later sheltered the wounded Elliott. The memory has made his old cheerful stories seem impossible and leaves him feeling unworthy of nurse Ann, who loves him. Time with Ann's young niece Candy begins to reopen the part of Elliott that could draw and tell stories, and he produces his first successful sketch since the war. Then Candy's father is killed in an accident overseas and the child runs away in grief. Elliott helps find her and reads the final letter her father left, urging Candy not to turn away from life because the world contains pain but to help make her own part of it worth living. The message speaks directly to Elliott's own guilt. By comforting Candy he finally accepts that he too must keep living, writing and loving, and he commits himself to a future with Ann and Candy.

title: Miss Minnie (1946-01-30)
plotSynopsis: After Dr. Christian persuades merchant J.D. Carter to give the formerly sheltered Minnie Marvin a job, Carter becomes convinced Minnie is trying to marry him. He secretly reads her diary, interprets every romantic entry as being about himself and grows so desperate to escape that he enlists in the Navy. Christian is less certain Carter has identified the right man. The truth arrives when Minnie announces that she is marrying James Sheldon, the postman she has loved for months. She also reveals that her father left her forty thousand dollars and that she has already bought the couple a home, but she kept the inheritance quiet because she wanted to work and wanted to know she was loved for herself rather than her money. Carter is left with a needless naval enlistment and the entire town's laughter at his vanity.

title: Requiem For A Hero (1946-02-06)
plotSynopsis: Father John Mulligan visits a condemned murderer who uses the same name and is wearing a unique family ring. The priest realizes the prisoner may be the infant son he believed lost at sea decades earlier, before he entered the priesthood. Dr. Christian questions the man, who claims the ring belonged to another rescued child named Eddie Graham and convinces Father John that Eddie, later a decorated serviceman killed in the South Pacific, was his true son. After the priest leaves comforted, Dr. Christian exposes the prisoner's deception: the man himself was the baby from the lifeboat and used an old photograph from the parcel to describe Father John's wife. Facing death, he chose to give his father a heroic son to remember rather than the shame of knowing a murderer was his child. Dr. Christian keeps the secret and tells him that his sacrifice was itself an act of heroism.

title: The Hoofer (1946-02-13)
plotSynopsis: Successful dancer Evangeline Moore returns to Rivers End exhausted and refuses ever to dance again. Years earlier she and her partner and fiancé Johnny 'Skeeter' Briggs were on the verge of a major stage break when he was inducted into the Army. Evangeline later toured for servicemen with the USO, but after Johnny's letters stopped she became convinced he was dead and finally collapsed into grief and self-pity. Dr. Christian traces Johnny and learns that he survived the war with a disabling injury. Believing Evangeline should not be tied to a helpless man, Johnny deliberately stayed silent while undergoing months of rehabilitation and dance practice. Dr. Christian arranges for Evangeline to attend a wounded-soldiers hospital show where Johnny makes his first public dancing appearance since his injury. The two reunite, discover that neither has stopped loving the other, and decide to dance together again.

title: The Girl With The Golden Gauntlets (1946-02-20)
plotSynopsis: Dr. Christian remembers Paris before the war, when his wealthy, aimless friend Steve became infatuated with the celebrated beauty Ariella, famous for never removing long golden gloves. Suspicious of her reputation and curious about the secret beneath the gloves, Steve and Dr. Christian trick Ariella into exposing hands that are badly deformed. Horrified by the cruelty of what he has done, Steve abandons his idle life and devotes himself to medicine, becoming a renowned plastic surgeon. Years later Dr. Christian reveals that the glamorous woman visiting Rivers End is Ariella herself, now Steve's wife, and that Steve's career was driven by his determination to restore the hands he once shamed her for hiding.

title: Forbidden Hill (1946-02-27)
plotSynopsis: Fourteen years after seven schoolchildren died from poison placed in a well at Cedar Hill, Margaret Anderson returns to Riverâ€™s End with her brother Roderick, the man who was blamed for the crime and committed to an asylum. Dr. Christian has always doubted that Roderick was insane, but the town still remembers him as a killer. Margaret repeatedly calls the doctor to the decaying house, while Roderick angrily tries to keep him away and appears to be threatening his sister. During a later visit Margaret serves Dr. Christian and Judy poisoned tea, but Roderick bursts in and knocks it from their hands, apparently attacking them. Laboratory testing confirms the poison and reverses the apparent roles. Dr. Christian concludes that Margaret, not Roderick, poisoned the children years earlier and is still dangerously disturbed. Roderick had understood his sisterâ€™s condition and silently accepted suspicion and confinement rather than expose her. His violent-looking intervention at Cedar Hill was actually another attempt to protect innocent people from her, finally giving Dr. Christian the proof needed to clear the man he never believed was insane.

title: One For The Money (1946-03-06)
plotSynopsis: Eighty-five-year-old Harriet Petticord summons her three young heirs and recruits Dr. Christian and Judy for a test of character. Although still wealthy, Harriet has Christian tell them that bad investments have left her penniless and that her house and belongings must be sold. Her grandniece Carol, a struggling actress and playwright, is prepared to help, while Carol's twin brother Bill cannot come because he is in the Army and sends his friend Private Frank Kennedy with a letter. Cousin Roger, Harriet's outwardly devoted favorite, immediately suggests putting her in an institution and is exposed as having secretly married the woman Harriet once disapproved of while continuing to check on Harriet's fortune through her lawyer. Harriet reveals the bankruptcy was a ruse, reduces Roger to a five-dollar inheritance, welcomes Carol and Frank into her home, and agrees to become the financial 'angel' for Carol's play.

title: Two Notes (1946-03-13)
plotSynopsis: Dr. Christian tells Judy about elderly neurologist Dr. Tuxbury, who has become convinced that his noisy upstairs tenant James Burton hates him and proudly describes what he believes is a perfect murder. Using a metronome and two repeated piano notes, Tuxbury claims he can exploit Burton's fear and heart response until the man's pulse races beyond endurance. The demonstration appears to work and Burton collapses, but the supposed victim has already recognized Tuxbury's growing paranoia and deliberately stages the reactions Tuxbury expects. No murder has taken place. Tuxbury is eventually confined to the state institution for the criminally insane, where he still reenacts his imaginary perfect crime for anyone willing to listen.

title: Man To Man (1946-03-20)
plotSynopsis: Young Nicky Marshall, grieving the recent death of his father, asks Dr. Christian to marry his widowed mother because he longs for a little brother or sister and believes a new father is the only way that can happen. Dr. Christian gently explains that no one can replace the father Nicky's mother still loves, then widens the boy's idea of family by showing him how children of different backgrounds can live as brothers and sisters in one world. The conversation becomes unexpectedly personal when Nicky's mother telephones with news Dr. Christian has not yet known: she is already expecting another child by her late husband. Nicky leaves overjoyed that he will have the brother or sister he wanted without replacing the father he still loves.

title: The Vagabond Veteran (1946-03-27)
plotSynopsis: Larry, a discharged fighter pilot, collapses in a Rivers End cafe convinced that recurring panic, suffocation and depression mean he is going insane. Dr. Christian recognizes a severe combat-nerves reaction rather than physical disease and brings Larry home instead of returning him to a hospital. Larry has no real home to return to, and the pressure and noise of a factory job after discharge only made his symptoms worse. Christian places him with the warm Santos family, where quiet routine and friendship with young Ted begin to restore him. A sudden startle in the garden makes Larry swing at Christian, terrifying him that he really is dangerous, but Christian refuses to give up on him. Later, while fishing with Christian and Ted, Christian falls into deep water. Larry reacts instantly, dives in and pulls him to safety without freezing or losing control. The emergency proves more convincingly than any reassurance that Larry's mind still functions under pressure. He accepts that he is recovering and agrees to stay with the Santos family, gaining the stable home and human connection he had been missing since the war.

title: The Devil That Calls In The Night (1946-05-15)
sortKey: 0|1946-05-15|00390|the devil that calls in the night 1946 05 15
plotSynopsis: Young widow Margie is living in the old Blackwood house with her baby, little Jeffrey, and the domineering Lucinda when she begins hearing the voice of her dead husband Jeff calling to her at night. The unseen voice, mysterious objects and other frightening incidents steadily convince Margie that she is losing her mind. Dr. Christian is called after elderly servant Amos runs from the house in terror and collapses dead, insisting that a devil is loose inside. Remembering the houses old speaking-tube system, the doctor suspects a very human explanation. He has Tom imitate Jeffs voice through the tube, and Lucinda reacts in a way that exposes the scheme. She admits that she has been whispering to Margie and planting reminders of Jeff, first to frighten her into staying and later in hopes of driving her insane or to suicide so Lucinda could become guardian of the child. Dr. Christian removes Margie and the baby from the house, supports her future with Tom, and warns Lucinda that he will reveal the entire story, including the circumstances surrounding Amos death, if she tries to interfere.

title: Two Loves Had Marian (1946-07-03)
plotSynopsis: Marian Douglas comes to Rivers End trying to find the soldier she remembers as David Rodell, a tall dark man she met at a New York servicemen's canteen and quickly fell in love with. Throughout the war she wrote to David Rodell overseas and fell even more deeply in love through his letters. When the real Rivers End David returned, however, he was shorter and blond, and Marian was so certain he was an impostor that she had him arrested for bothering her. Military records prove that the returning man is the genuine David and the man who actually received and answered Marian's wartime letters. Dr. Christian concludes that Marian has fused the real David's written personality with an idealized physical image formed around the stranger she first met. He recreates the emotional setting in which Marian originally fell in love, arranging a park encounter surrounded by butterflies. The memories finally join the real man to the feelings she already had for him. Marian recognizes David, the two marry the next morning, and Christian admits he helped the butterflies along with a little sugar water.

title: Spotlight On Grandma (1946-07-10)
plotSynopsis: Grandma Benson has spent years raising her daughter's children and keeping the Forbes household running, but realizes that the family now notices her mainly when a blouse needs mending or some other chore is unfinished. Dr. Christian suggests that she finally take a vacation and let them discover how much they depend on her. Grandma goes considerably further: after hearing of a wealthy man's old sweetheart, Marie Monahan, she stages a supposed kidnapping and leaves a ransom note claiming she is the missing heiress and needs old love letters to prove it. Her frantic family suddenly listens to every story about her younger days and searches the house in panic. When Grandma returns safely, Dr. Christian reveals that he knew the heiress story could not be true. The kidnapping was Grandma's own theatrical way of turning the spotlight on a woman her family had taken for granted.

title: The Norton Nose (1947-09-17)
plotSynopsis: A truck accident badly mangles young Pamela Norton's prominent family nose, and the reconstruction becomes a comic battle over identity. Pamela privately begs for a prettier nose, while formidable Aunt Augusta insists that the surgeon reproduce the ancestral Norton profile exactly from an old family miniature. Dr. Christian and the plastic surgeon refuse to turn Pamela into a museum piece and instead reconstruct a natural-looking nose suited to the young woman she actually is. The result helps free Pamela from years of embarrassment, and her romance with Mike Clancy moves toward marriage despite Augusta's outrage over the altered family landmark.

title: Cupids Boomerang (1947-11-26)
plotSynopsis: Dr. Christian agrees to help the painfully shy Dan tell Sarah that he has loved her for years. At a charity dance the bachelor-club members tease the doctor into promising that he will make the proposal for Dan. The plan backfires spectacularly: when Dr. Christian tries to explain that someone wants Sarah as his wife, she assumes he means himself and accepts before he can correct her. With the town already congratulating them, the doctor cannot bring himself to humiliate Sarah by admitting the mistake, while Dan is crushed. Dr. Christian and his friends then stage a fake fire at Sarahs house with a homemade smoke bomb. Believing the house is burning, Dan rushes inside, carries Sarah out and finally blurts out his real feelings. Sarah admits that she loves Dan too and breaks her mistaken engagement to Dr. Christian, who pretends to take the rejection bravely. Once safely unengaged, he swears off matchmaking when another woman immediately tries to arrange yet another romantic introduction for him.

title: Sammy Hits The Jackpot (1949-07-13)
plotSynopsis: Sammy La Coma, Riverâ€™s Endâ€™s irrepressible soda jerk, unexpectedly lands a logging contract and throws himself into the job despite everyoneâ€™s doubts about his experience. Working with capable logger Lucy, Sammy has to get a large shipment of logs to the river on schedule. A rival named Skilling repeatedly sabotages the operation, first damaging the road and later poisoning the crewâ€™s drinking water and tampering with a truck. Dr. Christian identifies the menâ€™s sudden illness as poisoning and helps keep the operation moving while Sammy catches Skilling at the truck and survives a rough fight with him. With drivers short and the deadline near, Dr. Christian and Lucy themselves help handle the heavy equipment so the last load reaches the river in time. Sammyâ€™s business gamble succeeds, but he considers the bigger jackpot to be Lucy, who kisses him after the final logs go in and then agrees to go to a movie with him.

title: Old Battle axe (1949-11-02)
plotSynopsis: After forty years in the classroom and several serious heart attacks, strict teacher Sarah Adams, known to generations of Rivers End children as 'Old Battle Axe,' retires and insists she never wants to see another child. Needing an inexpensive place to live after leaving the school cottage, she rents a room from Bruce and Jane Crandall, whose five-year-old son David is blind. Sarah immediately begins ordering the household around, correcting grammar, rearranging routines and disciplining David, but beneath the severity she becomes deeply involved in the family's future. She pushes Bruce to seek more education, offers to look after the house and David while his parents work, and quietly forms a powerful attachment to the boy. Christian tells the family that David's clouded corneas might be replaced if suitable healthy corneas become available. A dying man, Sam Dennis, has offered his eyes, but Sarah condemns the idea as interfering with Providence. When Sam dies, his relatives refuse permission and the opportunity is lost. Sarah then suffers another grave attack and understands that she herself is dying. Before her death she makes Christian promise that David will receive her own corneas, formally arranging the gift so no relatives can block it. The woman who had objected to David seeing through another man's eyes ultimately chooses to let him see the world through hers, revealing the love hidden beneath the fearsome reputation of Rivers End's 'Old Battle Axe.'

title: Love Is A Two sided Thing (1950-10-04)
plotSynopsis: Newly elected county attorney Grant Newman reopens a manslaughter case against Earl Carlson, unaware that Earl is his wife Eileen's estranged brother. Eileen has hidden her poor background and family from Grant, and the deeper truth is worse: she, not Earl, was driving when an old man was struck, while Earl took the blame to protect her and Grant's political campaign. Dr. Christian finds an eyewitness who proves the death was an unavoidable accident, clearing the driver, but Grant's attempt to dismiss the case makes him look corrupt. Eileen publicly tells the truth to protect her husband from that suspicion, and the crisis forces both spouses to recognize that love and marriage cannot remain one-sided.

title: Dont Look Down (1950-10-25)
plotSynopsis: While attending a medical meeting in New York, Dr. Christian is asked to help Joe Lance, a discouraged veteran who has reached a crisis after years of feeling trapped by a dull job, a troubled marriage and responsibility for his younger sister Audrey. Christian spends hours talking with Joe and gradually learns that beneath the despair he still wants the ordinary things he believes life has denied him: a real home, children, companionship and even simple pleasures such as fishing. Audrey's engagement removes one burden, but initially makes Joe feel even less needed. Christian refuses to deceive him and instead persuades the police to honor a promise allowing Joe time to reconsider. Joe finally comes back inside. His wife Emma, confronted with how selfish and distant their marriage has become, takes a risk of her own to reach him emotionally and promises that they will build the home and family he has wanted. Joe chooses to return with her. Audrey and Tim also prepare to marry, and Christian leaves New York with the family reconciled and looking forward rather than giving up.

title: The No Good (1950-11-29)
plotSynopsis: The school board dismisses poor, troublesome teenager Lem Tolan as a no-good boy unworthy of a scholarship, but Dr. Christian sees intelligence and possibility beneath his record of mischief. When the family workhorse Noble breaks a leg and Lem becomes physically ill from fear that his father will shoot it, Dr. Christian realizes that the boy needs responsibility more than punishment. He arranges treatment for Noble and makes Lem responsible for the horse's difficult recovery, with the boy working off the expense at the doctor's office. Months of patient care transform Lem's behavior and prove his character, and the same scholarship committee finally agrees that he deserves the educational chance Dr. Christian wanted for him from the start.

title: The Other One (1951-02-21)
plotSynopsis: Edward lies to police to protect his troubled brother Randolph, who is suspected in the death of schoolgirl Miriam Winslow. Dr. Christian patiently works past Edwards fierce family loyalty and uncovers a pattern of theft, secret spending and desperate attempts by Randolph to impress Miriam. Edward finally admits that Randolph met the girl wearing a hidden new jacket, tried to force an expensive necklace on her, and killed her when the encounter turned violent. Dr. Christian helps Edward understand that protecting his brother with lies will only deepen the damage, and that telling the truth is the only way to help both Randolph and their family.

title: The Runaway (1951-06-06)
plotSynopsis: College basketball player Adam reaches Rivers End frightened and on the run. He finally admits to Dr. Christian that he helped fix games at Midwestern University and fled because he believes the gambling syndicate behind the scheme has sent two gangsters after him. From his hotel room he points out one man watching the elevator and another sitting across the street, convinced they are waiting to follow him onto a lonely road and kill him. Dr. Christian tells Adam that escape will only deepen his trouble and persuades him to return to school, confess the basketball fix and accept the consequences. To get him past the men he fears, the doctor smuggles him from the hotel on a covered ambulance stretcher and puts him aboard the train. Only afterward does Dr. Christian reveal the irony: the supposed gangsters are ordinary Rivers End fixtures, one a longtime hotel-lobby reader and the other a harmless man who spends his days reading on a park bench. Adams guilty conscience turned strangers into pursuers, but the fear still pushed him toward the honest decision he needed to make.

title: Tonys Parcel (1953-12-23)
plotSynopsis: Tony, Rivers Ends hardworking street cleaner, finds a parcel containing money from a bank robbery. For a time he is tortured by the temptation to keep it and use it to improve life for his family and pay for his daughters musical training, but his conscience finally wins and he turns the money over to the police. The return earns him a substantial reward, and Tony uses part of it to make a Christmas gift to the childrens ward of the hospital.

title: Angela and Steven Kester (1950-02-01)
plotSynopsis: Concert pianist Angela Kester's obsessive fear of failure, rooted in her father's sacrifices and expectations, has progressed into paranoia toward her husband Steven. After she shoots herself, Kildare and Gillespie turn to a risky prefrontal lobotomy as a last resort, and the operation frees her from the obsessions that had overwhelmed her.

title: Marjorie Northrup (1950-02-08)
plotSynopsis: After an automobile accident forces the amputation of her right leg, Marjorie Northrup rejects her fiancé and refuses rehabilitation, convinced her life is ruined. Kildare brings in tennis player Evelyn Williams, herself an amputee, to show what recovery can look like, and Marjorie begins learning to walk again and face her future.

title: Benjamin Barkley (1950-02-15)
plotSynopsis: With Gillespie bedridden by influenza, Kildare takes over his irascible old patient Benjamin Barkley and diagnoses subacute appendicitis despite Gillespie's contrary opinion. Barkley refuses surgery until Kildare assigns an attractive surgical nurse who helps persuade him to consent, while Gillespie later turns the same tactic on Kildare when the younger doctor falls ill.

title: Rico Marchianos Dying Wife (1950-02-22)
plotSynopsis: Street violinist Rico Marchiano brings his wife Carmen to Blair after saving for treatment, only to learn her cancer is terminal because she arrived too late. Kildare and Gillespie maneuver around the hospital's financial restrictions to give her care, but Carmen dies; after Kildare delivers a healthy baby the next morning, Gillespie reminds him why doctors continue serving through both death and new life.

title: Vernon Pendleton - Hypochondriac (1950-03-01)
plotSynopsis: Wealthy hospital donor Vernon Pendleton insists that he is seriously ill even though repeated examinations show nothing wrong. Pressured to humor him, Kildare instead gives Pendleton an exhaustive stay in isolation filled with uncomfortable tests until the self-described invalid discovers how little he enjoys being a patient, curing the worst of his hypochondria.

title: Barbara Lane Dope Addict (1950-03-08)
plotSynopsis: Barbara Lane fakes barbiturate poisoning to get into Blair, where Kildare discovers that she is a morphine addict working with a supposed father to steal the hospital's narcotics. When the theft is thwarted and Barbara threatens to jump, Kildare promises to stand by her if she accepts treatment; she enters a sanitarium and begins fighting the addiction.

title: Caroline Shelley (1950-03-15)
plotSynopsis: Gillespie's young friend Caroline Shelley develops appendicitis while her separated parents are both away. A caretaker ignores medical orders and gives her castor oil, after which Caroline's appendix ruptures; Kildare performs emergency surgery, and the crisis helps bring her mother and father back together to make a home for their daughter.

title: Jane Dane New Cancer Treatment (1950-03-22)
plotSynopsis: Kildare prepares Blair's new betatron to treat Jane Dane's otherwise inoperable throat cancer. When two test guinea pigs die, the treatment is halted until their deaths are shown to be unrelated to the machine; Jane resumes the therapy and is later cured, validating the new approach.

title: Warren Jacksons Allergy (1950-04-12)
plotSynopsis: After insurance broker Warren Jackson attempts suicide while suffering from rashes, headaches and deep depression, Kildare suspects a physical cause rather than simple financial strain. Extensive testing finally traces his attacks to orris root in his wife's perfume, a wedding gift Warren himself had given her, and controlled injections begin building his immunity as his health and outlook recover.

title: Terry Murphys Hearing Problem (1950-04-19)
plotSynopsis: Fourteen-year-old Terry Murphy steals a revolver to impress boys who ridicule him as stupid, and a later apparent theft of a scalpel convinces Kildare something deeper is wrong. The scalpel incident proves Terry has misheard ordinary speech; testing reveals partial deafness from an obstruction in his ear, and a simple operation offers to restore his hearing and end the school failures and insecurity that fed his delinquency.

title: Philip Van Courts Amnesia (1950-04-26)
plotSynopsis: Philip Van Court disappears and is found with amnesia and a seemingly paralyzed arm. Under narcosynthesis he relives the wartime death of his best friend Paul, whose plane was shot down after Philip froze at his gun, and confesses his guilt over loving Paul's fiancée Irene. Learning that Irene had already broken the engagement before Paul's death frees Philip from the guilt, restoring both his memory and use of his arm, and he and Irene plan to marry.

title: Abandoned Baby (1950-05-03)
plotSynopsis: An ambulance driver discovers a malnourished baby named Jackie abandoned with a note asking Dr. Gillespie to care for him because his mother has nothing left to live for. As the child battles bronchial pneumonia, Kildare and police lieutenant Dan Riley trace the desperate mother, Eleanor Mason; Jackie survives, Eleanor regains hope, and Riley helps her find a home and work as the two begin planning a future together.

title: Kildares Old Girlfriend (1950-05-10)
plotSynopsis: Kildare reunites with Janet, the girl he loved before medical school, and briefly wonders whether devotion to medicine cost him another kind of life. When complications following influenza produce a fatal heart infection, every treatment fails and Janet dies; devastated, Kildare considers leaving medicine until Gillespie and Janet's younger brother remind him that one tragic loss can become the reason to save future lives.

title: Nurse Parker Resigns (1950-05-17)
plotSynopsis: After years of enduring Gillespie's insults, Nurse Parker finally resigns when he calls her incompetent. Gillespie's rigidly efficient replacement soon makes him appreciate Parker's judgment and flexibility, while Kildare exposes Dr. Carew's meddling in the change; Parker is called back, and after a brief spell of strained politeness, she and Gillespie return to their familiar bickering partnership.

title: Dr Carews Fat Wife (1950-05-24)
plotSynopsis: Dr. Carew asks Kildare and Gillespie to help his wife Angela lose twenty pounds so she can revive her old dance act at a benefit for Blair's new polio wing. A strict diet and exercise program tests Angela and wears down the doctors almost as much as their patient, but she reaches her goal, fits her old costume again and prepares to dance, leaving the exhausted physicians ready to celebrate with a lavish meal.

title: Dick Brennan Steals 5000 or 50000 (1950-05-31)
plotSynopsis: Young Dick Brennan admits taking $5,000 from an open safe after arriving in New York broke and unemployed, but the shop owner claims $50,000 was stolen and tries to pin the entire loss on him. Kildare realizes Dick was used as bait in a larger frame-up and, exploiting the owner's obsession with his health, helps obtain the truth under medication; the hidden money is recovered, while Dick accepts responsibility for the $5,000 he actually took and decides to return home to the farm.

title: Colonel Boregards Paralysis (1950-06-01)
plotSynopsis: Colonel Boregard arrives paralyzed from the waist down, and Kildare identifies a rare periodic paralysis associated with low potassium; potassium treatment gets him back on his feet. When the paralysis suddenly returns after he learns that his devoted daughter is secretly married and plans to leave, the new attack proves psychogenic, and Kildare uses the threat of losing her and his unborn grandchild to shock the proud colonel into walking again.

title: Gordon Mallorys Lead Poisoning (1950-06-08)
plotSynopsis: Construction worker Gordon Mallory develops lead poisoning and temporary paralysis in his wrists and hands even though he wears a protective mask. Kildare and Gillespie discover that he has spent years eating lunch beside crews spraying lead paint, absorbing fumes while unprotected, and a second worker is poisoned more acutely while burning painted metal; both men begin treatment and the contractor is pushed to adopt regular examinations and safer practices.

title: Glaucoma (1950-06-15)
plotSynopsis: Drake Simmons faces permanent blindness from glaucoma and sinks into despair after surgery cannot save his sight, eventually attempting suicide with ammonia. Kildare brings him together with Maria, a blind restaurant owner who built an independent life after losing her own sight; her blunt counsel helps Simmons stop mourning what he has lost and begin learning how to live in a new way.

title: Pricillas Broken Arm (1950-06-22)
plotSynopsis: A broken arm brings brilliant, abrasive teenager Priscilla Babcock to Blair, where Kildare realizes her cold scientific pose hides hurt and loneliness. She has been ridiculed and isolated at school because of her intellectual interests and was trying to run away; Kildare gets her mother to transfer her to the Rodman Academy, where she can pursue those interests among students closer to her own abilities and begin forming normal friendships.

title: Dr Gillespie Almost Gets Engaged (1950-06-29)
plotSynopsis: A pleasant evening with wealthy Millicent Forbes turns into a comic crisis when hospital gossip and newspaper interest convince everyone that Gillespie is about to marry her. Unable to stop the rumor without embarrassing Millicent, Gillespie turns to Kildare, who destroys the romantic illusion by revealing the doctor's decidedly unglamorous health regimen; Millicent decides they are better as friends and Gillespie escapes the supposed engagement.

title: Hunting Trip (1950-07-06)
plotSynopsis: Kildare and Gillespie's hunting vacation is interrupted when they reach a mountain town in the grip of a contagious throat epidemic among children. Kildare performs an emergency tracheotomy with his hunting knife, the doctors organize isolation and treatment until the outbreak is checked, and they also uncover young Dr. Bob Wheeler's long-hidden migraine condition; after treatment, Wheeler chooses to remain as the town's badly needed physician.

title: Dan Malloys Peptic Ulcer (1950-07-13)
plotSynopsis: Former outdoorsman Dan Malloy develops a peptic ulcer after years of being pushed into a desk-bound business and society life that leaves him frustrated and powerless. Kildare, Gillespie and Nurse Parker help him recognize what the strain is doing to him, and Malloy finally takes control, sells the company and moves with his wife to Cranberry Lake, returning to the active life both of them once enjoyed.

title: Mrs Stanfords Angina Pectoris (1950-07-20)
plotSynopsis: Mrs. Stanford's angina makes fright potentially deadly, and repeated appearances by a white-clad 'spirit' carrying a knife seem designed to terrify her into another attack. Kildare refuses to dismiss the visions as hallucinations and lays a trap, catching a woman in the household staging the ghostly visits for financial gain; the scheme is exposed before it can frighten Mrs. Stanford to death.

title: Buffalo Barnie Mc Clure (1950-08-10)
plotSynopsis: Wild West showman Buffalo Barney McClure lands at Blair with stomach trouble, and X-rays reveal that the missing dental bridge he has been searching for is lodged in his stomach. He refuses to let anyone pass an esophagoscope down his throat and backs the refusal with his six-shooter, so Kildare and Gillespie enlist his pride, his code of honor and Nurse Parker's admiration to get his consent; the bridge is removed safely, after which the irrepressible Barney leaves the hospital having also fleeced Dr. Carrou at cards.

title: Appendicitis Operation at Sea (1950-08-17)
plotSynopsis: A ship at sea reports a passenger with acute appendicitis, but rough water makes transfer impossible and there is no doctor aboard. Kildare first tries to guide former Navy medical corpsman Steve Nelson through the operation by radio, then takes a helicopter out to the ship when the improvised plan cannot safely continue; descending by rope ladder to the rolling deck, he performs the emergency operation in time and returns with the patient saved.

title: Carew Gets Medical Examiner Mixed Up (1950-09-07)
plotSynopsis: Dr. Carrou becomes obsessed with impressing visitors he believes can bring Blair money, while Kildare refuses to abandon an unconscious emergency patient simply to conduct a hospital tour. A chain of mistaken identities follows as Carrou and Gillespie give contradictory sales pitches to people they misunderstand, while Kildare treats the patient for a diabetic crisis; the joke turns on Carrou when that seemingly ordinary patient proves to be Mr. Ramsey, the wealthy donor whose approval he had been chasing all along.

title: Marion Lewis Teen Age Alcoholic (1950-09-14)
plotSynopsis: Seventeen-year-old Marion Lewis is brought to Blair dangerously intoxicated, and Kildare learns that drinking, sneaking out and a shoplifting episode have grown out of a bitter struggle with rigid parents who punish and restrict her without listening to her. He stalls her father's efforts to take her home, settles the shop's complaint, and finally brings both parents through the crippled children's ward to make them see that an emotional handicap needs patient help rather than punishment; the experience breaks through their stubbornness and the family leaves ready to start over together.

title: Sam Lubinski Has Spinal Paralysis (1950-09-21)
plotSynopsis: A workman is badly impaled by a broken iron ladder rung and survives emergency surgery, only to become suddenly paralyzed from the chest down afterward. Kildare suspects that a tiny fragment from the jagged metal has lodged beside the spinal column, but ordinary X-rays cannot find it; he brings in a portable wartime metal detector, locates the fragment near the dorsal spine, and a second operation removes it, allowing the patient to recover and walk again.

title: Mumpkins First Baby (1950-09-28)
plotSynopsis: Expectant father Willie Mumpkin turns his wife's first delivery into a hospital-wide comedy, camping around the maternity floor, reading scientific books aloud for prenatal influence, challenging hospital rules and worrying that the newborns will be mixed up. Kildare safely delivers Betty Jane's healthy baby while repeatedly steering Willie out of the staff's way, and the anxious new father finally leaves with wife and child intact after discovering that parenthood is less controllable than all his preparation suggested.

title: Eddie Jenkins and the Arsonist (1950-10-20)
plotSynopsis: Teenager Eddie Jenkins is burned in a waterfront gasoline fire and immediately becomes a suspect because he was found at the scene, although he insists he was sleeping beneath the pier and heard someone in the warehouse before the blaze. Kildare establishes that Eddie's headaches and truancy stem from poor eyesight, then realizes someone is trying to silence him when poisoned chocolates trigger violent convulsions; a recorded voice identifies the warehouse owner Maxon as the man Eddie heard, and when Maxon comes to the hospital with a gun, orderly Wayman knocks him down with a monkey wrench and ends the arsonist's attempt to kill the witness.

title: Ling Co Refuses Leg Surgery (1950-10-27)
plotSynopsis: Elderly Ling Co has a traumatic short circuit between an artery and vein in his leg that is overworking his heart and will soon kill him, yet he refuses the simple corrective operation because he believes living beyond his proper time would cost him dignity. Kildare's direct appeals fail, so Gillespie wins Ling's confidence as one old man speaking to another and lets him confront what his death would mean to his family, including a coming great-grandchild; Ling finally consents, the surgery succeeds, and his renewed appetite for life soon includes wagering with Gillespie over Chinese checkers.

title: Mr Bradleys Heart (1950-11-17)
plotSynopsis: Engineer Mr. Bradley ignores an angina warning and returns to his punishing work schedule until a coronary thrombosis brings him back to Blair in far worse condition. Tests reveal a dangerously weakened section of heart wall that is bulging with every beat and may rupture within days; Kildare chooses a risky operation, reinforcing the damaged area with a fascia graft, and Bradley survives with a new determination to retire to a quiet Vermont farm instead of gambling with a third attack.

title: Mr Kramer-Parker Needs a Hobby (1950-11-24)
plotSynopsis: Nurse Parker takes up painting as a hobby after one of her battles with Gillespie and becomes acutely ill after spending meals and spare time surrounded by oil paints, even dipping her brush into her coffee; Kildare recognizes mild lead poisoning. Her case supplies the clue to Mr. Kramer's puzzling new symptoms on top of chronic arthritis: his recently installed furnace recovers precious metal from jewelry sweepings by using litharge, or lead oxide, and has been slowly poisoning him as well; both patients begin treatment while Parker's much-ridiculed painting unexpectedly wins an art prize.

title: Lady Dunabees Annual Visit (1950-12-01)
plotSynopsis: Lady Dunabee returns for her annual stay at Blair complaining of a troublesome leg, and Kildare's X-rays reveal that a cracked lumbar disk is protruding into the spinal canal and causing her sciatica. Although the wealthy, strong-willed patient has heard many opinions in Europe and Dr. Carrou fears the consequences of operating on such an important guest, Kildare wins her confidence and performs the corrective surgery; she is soon walking without the old sciatic pain and celebrating her recovery with characteristic energy.

title: Arthur Morgan Needs Brain Surgery (1950-12-08)
plotSynopsis: Arthur Morgan is struck by a car and initially seems to have survived with a skull fracture, but a dilated pupil, rising pressure and prolonged unconsciousness reveal an extradural hemorrhage that will kill him without immediate brain surgery. His terrified wife refuses permission because her mother died from infection after a brain operation in 1919; with time running out, Kildare prepares and performs the lifesaving operation, while Gillespie later shows Mrs. Morgan how far modern surgery has advanced and obtains her consent, and Morgan recovers.

title: David Norton Has Pneumonia (1950-12-29)
plotSynopsis: Six-year-old David Norton develops severe pneumonia while his separated parents are fighting over custody, and Kildare brings both mother and father to Blair because the delirious child needs familiar voices as well as medical care. Their bitterness immediately turns the sickroom into another battleground, so the doctors force them to put David ahead of their grievances; as the boy passes the crisis and his fever finally drops, the parents rediscover their concern for each other and begin reconciling instead of using their son as part of the divorce fight.

title: Eddie Lazetti Kidnaps Nurse (1951-01-05)
plotSynopsis: Wounded payroll bandit Eddie Mazzetti is brought to Blair under guard after a robbery and murder, but he knocks out an officer, takes the man's gun and forces nurse Diana with him as he hides inside the hospital. Kildare realizes they are concealed in the pathology laboratory after Diana deliberately drops her nurse's cap as a clue; when Mazzetti cuts his hand on a broken specimen bottle and panics at the thought of leprosy, Kildare pretends to give him an emergency treatment but actually injects morphine, putting him to sleep so the police can retake him without Diana being hurt.

title: Dr Gillespies Testimonial Dinner (1951-01-12)
plotSynopsis: Blair's staff secretly plans a testimonial dinner for Gillespie's thirty-fifth anniversary, but scraps of overheard conversation make him suspect the hospital is preparing to retire him. Determined to prove he is still indispensable, he suddenly takes on extra cases, rises before dawn, bowls, walks stairs and displays so much forced vigor that his friends begin wondering whether he really wants to leave; at the supposed board meeting he finally learns the truth, receives the hospital's tribute and a commemorative watch, and gratefully admits that the frantic week has exhausted him more than ordinary work ever did.

title: Dr Conlon Quack (1951-01-19)
plotSynopsis: A cancer patient reaches Blair too late for effective treatment after spending months and her savings on Dr. Conlon's fraudulent 'electro-radonic' machine, prompting Kildare and Gillespie to expose him. Gillespie poses as an ordinary patient after three legitimate doctors document his healthy heart, and Conlon's machine confidently diagnoses serious cardiac disease and sells expensive treatments; the doctors reveal themselves and prepare a newspaper exposé backed by the contradictory records, then discover Conlon himself has a likely sarcoma and agree to operate only after he dictates a full confession of his swindling activities.

title: Joe Finleys Ulcer (1951-01-26)
plotSynopsis: Young route driver Joe Finley collapses with an ulcer driven by severe worry, and his employer then discovers $1,645 missing from Joe's receipts. Gillespie quietly replaces the shortage while Kildare looks for the pressure behind it, finding that Joe has been exhausting himself and his money caring for his chronically ill wife Lorraine; at Blair they discover she has been treated by fake physician Klaus Blackthorn, whose bogus credentials and dangerous care allowed her severe anemia to worsen. Kildare and Gillespie expose Blackthorn and call the police, Lorraine recovers under legitimate treatment, and Joe gets the chance to rebuild his health and career.

title: Oliver Van Meters Allergy (1951-02-02)
plotSynopsis: Oliver Van Meter suffers violent allergic attacks every Monday for three years, yet a change of location seems to make them vanish until a mailed Sunday newspaper reaches him a day late and the attack shifts to Tuesday. Kildare realizes the calendar pattern follows the paper rather than the place: Van Meter is allergic to the rotogravure ink in the Globe Bulletin's Sunday supplement, and avoiding that ink ends the mysterious weekly illness.

title: Anthrax Infection (1951-02-09)
plotSynopsis: After skinning an infected bear in the Adirondacks, John Breveton develops a rapidly dangerous illness that Kildare identifies as anthrax even though early laboratory tests fail to show the organism. Breveton's physician father stops the antiserum and threatens malpractice, but Kildare prepares for the wider outbreak he expects; when livestock begin dying with unmistakable signs, the father recognizes the error, treatment resumes, and doctors and veterinarians contain the outbreak while Breveton recovers.

title: Pete Cosloff Is Mentally Ill (1951-02-16)
plotSynopsis: House painter Pete Cosloff barricades himself with a gun in a kindergarten playhouse, convinced enemies are threatening a child inside, and Kildare goes in alone to keep the siege from turning deadly. Gillespie reconstructs Cosloff's wartime history and learns that invaders devastated his hometown and took the schoolchildren, including Pete's son; Kildare uses those memories to separate past from present, persuades Pete that his son is beyond harm and that he is now safe in America, and gets him to surrender for psychiatric treatment.

title: Buck Houston Cowboy Star (1951-02-23)
plotSynopsis: Cowboy star Buck Houston enters Blair with disabling sciatica that has no physical cause, and Kildare discovers the pain is tied to the older actor's resentment and guilt over living behind a manufactured Western hero persona. Instead of arguing him out of it, Kildare brings Buck into the overcrowded children's orthopedic ward, where a hopeless boy named Donnie recognizes his idol; Buck's promise of a ranch visit gives Donnie a reason to work toward recovery and restores Buck's own sense of purpose, and Buck funds an expansion of the children's ward.

title: David Coopers Burned Face (1951-03-02)
plotSynopsis: David Cooper survives a fiery airplane crash with severe facial burns, but when the bandages come off he rejects reconstructive surgery, withdraws from everyone and attempts suicide. Kildare learns that Cooper's wife is leaving for Reno because she believes he loves Elaine Dobson, the woman who survived the crash with him; after Kildare brings Elaine and Mrs. Cooper together and intercepts the wife at the airport, the misunderstanding is cleared up, Mrs. Cooper returns to David, and he chooses to live and begin facial reconstruction.

title: Edward Carltons Dog Bite (1951-03-09)
plotSynopsis: Edward Carlton is bitten by a boy's dog and within four days develops symptoms that seem like rabies, even though the incubation is suspiciously short and the dog shows no convincing disease. Kildare discovers that Edward's terrified mother has been reading about hydrophobia and feeding him every symptom, which he immediately reproduces, including apparent paralysis; he diagnoses pseudo-hydrophobia, spares the healthy dog from needless destruction, and reunites it with its devoted young owner while Edward begins treatment for his neurosis.

title: Amy Dickens Breaks Her Leg (1951-03-16)
plotSynopsis: Aspiring novelist Amy Dickens is recovering from two broken legs when she learns that boyfriend Paul has exaggerated a publisher's interest in her work to keep her spirits up, and the betrayal sends her into a slump that threatens her rehabilitation. Kildare and Gillespie make Paul face what he has done and push him to get publisher Floyd Emerson genuinely involved; Emerson reads Amy's manuscript, frankly tells her it is undisciplined but promising, offers her a future job where she can learn the craft, and Amy returns to her wheelchair, writing and recovery with her confidence restored.

title: Cathy Mortons Baby (1951-03-23)
plotSynopsis: Nineteen-year-old Cathy Morton brings her month-old son to Kildare and asks him to arrange an adoption, convinced that her inexperience makes her unfit to raise the child; she has even left her Marine husband Walter without telling him about the baby. Kildare and Gillespie stage an intentionally dreadful pair of prospective foster parents while tracing Walter, then force Cathy to face the finality of signing away her child. Her maternal resolve finally breaks through, Walter is reunited with her and meets his son, and the adoption papers are burned as the young family decides to stay together.

title: Joan Quinn (1951-03-30)
plotSynopsis: Gillespie grows suspicious when attractive nurse Joan Quinn temporarily works with Kildare, then snoops through Kildare's mail and convinces himself that the pair are romantically involved and that Kildare is leaving Blair for a Chicago post. Trying to keep him, Gillespie even doses himself with digitalis to produce alarming symptoms, but Kildare exposes the ruse and supplies the facts: Joan is an old friend whose wedding he attended, she married a medical student six months earlier, and Kildare has already rejected the outside job. Gillespie is prescribed a few days of genuine bed rest for his overwork and his meddling.

title: Gillespies New Suit for Henderson Award (1951-04-06)
plotSynopsis: As Gillespie prepares an important paper on antibiotic controls for the Henderson Award, Kildare and Parker become equally determined to replace the battered suit he has worn for years. With help from glamorous patient Susan Duchamp they maneuver him into buying new clothes, which he bitterly resists once he discovers the scheme. Gillespie does not win the Henderson prize, but he warmly applauds the deserving scientist who does, receives a special citation for his own paper, and later discovers that his reluctant wardrobe makeover has also earned him the assembly's designation as best-dressed doctor.

title: Yukon Joes Gold Mine (1951-04-13)
plotSynopsis: Nurse Parker and Dr. Carrou buy shares in Yukon Joe Moran's supposedly rich Moosehead Rock gold mine, only for Kildare and Gillespie to confirm that the land is real but the mine is worthless. When Joe refuses to return their money, Kildare persuades a newspaper editor to print a single fake special edition announcing a huge strike at Moosehead Rock; Joe sees the headline, panics and buys Parker's share back at full price. Carrou, however, secretly sees the same paper first and outsmarts himself by buying even more of the worthless property, leaving Parker rescued and Carrou holding the swindle.

title: Mysterious Hemophilia Patient (1951-05-18)
plotSynopsis: A secret patient admitted as John Smith proves to be Philip III, the former king of Corsonia who abdicated fifteen years earlier to make his country a democracy and has returned in disguise before a crucial plebiscite. Kildare and Gillespie find an operable cancerous growth obstructing his pylorus, but Philip is also a hemophiliac and may bleed to death if they operate; with only about two months to live otherwise, he accepts the extreme risk. After intensive preparation, rapid surgery and repeated transfusions he survives, the democratic side wins the Corsonian vote, Sarvo becomes president, and Philip is later appointed ambassador to the United States.

title: Dr Gillespies New Office (1951-05-25)
plotSynopsis: Dr. Carrou secretly replaces Gillespie's cluttered old office with an ultra-modern design while Kildare gets him out of town, but Gillespie returns furious because the old room and especially its rolltop desk hold decades of personal memories. He threatens to leave Blair, and Kildare retrieves the discarded desk from an auction only to discover that hidden inside were old love letters Molly Byrd wrote Gillespie when she was a student nurse. Once the letters are returned and Gillespie learns Molly kept his old letters too, his anger softens; with the cherished desk restored, he accepts the new office and soon boasts about its modern conveniences.

title: Pedro Maria and Rosie (1951-06-15)
plotSynopsis: During a desert vacation, Kildare and Gillespie are asked by Pedro and Maria to help their ailing burro Rosie, but Kildare soon develops acute appendicitis himself at the couple's remote shack. A flash flood cuts Gillespie off and leaves Kildare with only a short time before rupture, so with local anesthetic, a mirror and Maria handing instruments and standing ready with a stimulant, he performs his own appendectomy. Gillespie finally reaches the shack by helicopter and finds the appendix already removed in time, while the grateful couple later acquires a new burro and names it for one of the doctors.

title: Paul Bailey (1951-06-22)
plotSynopsis: Intern Paul Bailey misses ambulance duty and arrives smelling of liquor, prompting Blair to suspend him before anyone learns that he had collapsed after studying all night and his landlady revived him with brandy. He quits medicine and soon suffers a nervous breakdown, and Kildare discovers the deeper burden: years earlier Bailey accidentally killed his friend Billy in a hunting accident, chose medicine to make that loss mean something, and has driven himself mercilessly because his hometown expected him to fail like his father. Kildare and Gillespie give him one more diagnostic problem, and Bailey's wartime chest experience correctly challenges a mistaken tuberculosis diagnosis, proving both his ability and his desire to be a doctor; he returns to his internship.

title: Valerie and Walter Benton - Murder (1951-07-13)
plotSynopsis: Walter Benton, newly recovered from heart surgery and ready to leave Blair, falls seven stories to his death just after receiving $25,000 in cash and a valuable ring from the hospital safe. Because ambulance driver Wayman reaches the body first, suspicion falls on him when the money and ring are missing, and the ring is later planted to strengthen the case against him. Benton's estranged stepdaughter Valerie blames attorney Bill Walsh, but Kildare draws her out until she describes exactly how the killer could have entered disguised, robbed Benton and pushed him from the window; he then confronts her with evidence from the planted ring, and she pulls a gun while police listen in. Valerie is exposed as the killer who robbed and murdered her stepfather, and Wayman is cleared, with Dr. Carrou quietly revealed as the person who posted his bail.

title: Evelyn Briggs (1951-07-20)
plotSynopsis: On a fishing vacation near the Canadian border, Kildare diagnoses fellow guest Evelyn Briggs with diphtheria and insists that the Holiday Guest House be quarantined. Innkeeper Charlie Converse refuses, then hides Evelyn and makes her room appear unused because he is secretly sheltering Chuck Rivers, an FBI fugitive who has paid him to stay hidden until he can cross into Canada. Rivers and Converse force Kildare and Gillespie onto a train, but Kildare returns while Gillespie seeks county authorities; faced with an impending search, Converse admits that Evelyn is concealed in the attic. The doctors reach and treat the dangerously ill girl, while Kildare stalls Rivers long enough for the law to close in, turning their planned vacation into an emergency fight to stop both a criminal and a possible epidemic.

title: Robert Lane Intern Shirks Duties (1951-07-27)
plotSynopsis: Intern Robert Lane abandons a special hospital assignment and nearly costs a cardiac patient his life, yet refuses to explain where he has been, so Kildare covers for him while trying to discover the cause. A $5,000 life-insurance policy, a notebook of patients and a missing analytical spectroscope lead Kildare to the truth: Lane has been practicing medicine illegally on the side and pawned the hospital instrument for $300 because he is supporting his pregnant sister Margaret after her husband deserted her. Kildare brings him back to Blair as Margaret goes into labor, while Gillespie quietly retrieves the spectroscope and converts the $300 into a loan payable after Lane graduates. With the financial pressure exposed and his sister safely delivered of a son, Lane is able to return to his internship and continue toward becoming a doctor.

title: Alice Bradley Amnesia Victim (1951-08-03)
plotSynopsis: A well-dressed young woman arrives at Blair unable to remember her name or past, and Kildare diagnoses psychogenic amnesia rather than brain injury. She is identified as Alice Bradley, but the sight of her wealthy father Albert terrifies her; she later slips out in a nurse's uniform and is found at her mother's grave, where fragments of memory suggest that her mother died on a Swiss lake and that her father murdered her. Kildare and Gillespie learn that Alice recently found her late mother's diary accusing Albert, but Albert explains that his troubled wife went out alone in a canoe while he was away climbing with a group that included her brother George. Using a letter from Uncle George confirming the alibi and the truth about the accident, Kildare breaks through Alice's repression, restores her memory and reconciles her with her innocent father.

title: John Jock Todd (1948-05-02)
plotSynopsis: Mild-mannered Scotsman John Todd takes a post at an African trading station where bullying Captain Brock humiliates workers and repeatedly provokes him. When Brock beats Todd and prepares to punish a native boy, Todd finally fights back and exposes the supposedly fearsome captain as a coward; Brock is sent away, while Todd continues to insist that he is peace-loving and that his name is John, not the fighter's nickname Jack.

title: The Time Machine -Jeff Corey (1948-05-09)
plotSynopsis: Dr. Dudley takes Fowler in his time machine to the year 100,080, where they find a beautiful childlike people living above ground and predatory Morlocks below. When the Morlocks seize the machine, the men fight to recover it and escape back to 1948, but Wina is lost in the struggle, leaving Fowler with only a piece of her green silk as proof of the journey.

title: The Match (1948-05-16)
plotSynopsis: After accidentally killing camp boss Thorne in a fight, Billy Loring flees into the Canadian north and is finally captured by Sergeant Brokaw. A blizzard traps captor and prisoner together until Loring reveals that he has one match; the match appears to fail, but a spark catches and saves Loring beside a fire while Brokaw dies in the snow.

title: Leiningen Versus the Ants -William Conrad Jay Novello (1948-05-23)
sortKey: 0|1948-05-23|00042|leiningen versus the ants -william conrad jay novello (1948-05-23)
plotSynopsis: Plantation owner Leiningen refuses to flee when a vast army of ants approaches, trusting a network of defenses and his own intelligence. When the ants overwhelm the plantation, he runs through the swarm to close a floodgate, survives terrible bites, and floods the land until the ants are drowned.

title: Beau Geste (1948-06-06)
plotSynopsis: The disappearance of the Blue Water sapphire sends the Geste brothers into the French Foreign Legion, where their secret follows them to a brutal desert outpost under Sergeant Lejaune. After the fort's destruction and Beau's death, John eventually returns home with Beau's letter, which reveals that Beau stole only the imitation sapphire to protect Aunt Patricia after she had quietly disposed of the real stone for the estate's sake.

title: Country of the Blind -Paul Frees William Conrad (1948-06-27)
sortKey: 0|1948-06-27|00044|country of the blind -paul frees william conrad (1948-06-27)
plotSynopsis: After surviving a mountain fall, Nunez discovers an isolated valley whose people have been blind for generations and regard his sight as a defect. He falls in love with Medina-Sarote but refuses an operation to remove his eyes, escapes across the mountains, and eventually returns to civilization only to find that snow glare has left him blind.

title: A Tooth for Paul Revere (1948-07-04)
plotSynopsis: A farmer's painful tooth sends him to Paul Revere and, through a chain of comic circumstances, helps set events of the American Revolution in motion.

title: She (1948-07-11)
plotSynopsis: Two explorers reach a lost African city ruled by a beautiful immortal queen who believes one of the newcomers is the man she has awaited for centuries.

title: Habit (1948-07-18)
plotSynopsis: A combative sea captain recently jailed for assault sets out to prove himself by rescuing survivors during a hurricane, only to face a perilous medical emergency and more trouble.

title: The Man Who Would Be King -Ben Wright- -1 (1948-08-01)
sortKey: 0|1948-08-01|00048|the man who would be king -ben wright- -1 (1948-08-01)
plotSynopsis: Soldiers of fortune Daniel Dravot and Peachey Carnehan leave India determined to become kings in remote Kafiristan. Using military skill and the people's belief that they are more than ordinary men, they build a kingdom, but Dravot breaks their pact by deciding to take a wife. When the frightened woman bites him and draws blood, the people realize he is mortal and revolt. Dravot is killed, while the tortured Peachey eventually reaches the narrator carrying Dravot's mummified head and golden crown as proof that they truly became kings.

title: The Man Who Would Be King -Ben Wright- -2 (1948-08-01)
sortKey: 0|1948-08-01|00048|the man who would be king -ben wright- -2 (1948-08-01)
