title: An Uncontrolled Dog (1950-05-04)
plotSynopsis: Kathy brings home a stray dog, and Jim's efforts to remove the animal only create more trouble as the persistent pet keeps returning and upsetting the household and neighbors.

title: The Golf Challenge (1950-05-11)
plotSynopsis: Flush with confidence after a golf victory, Jim lectures the family about mind over matter, then finds his own philosophy tested when an ill-timed physical mishap threatens his next match.

title: Betty's Screen Test (1950-05-18)
plotSynopsis: Betty becomes convinced Hollywood stardom is within reach when a talent scout appears, sending the Anderson household into a frenzy before the situation proves less glamorous than she imagined.

title: Superstitious Folk (1950-05-25)
plotSynopsis: A day of supposed bad omens turns the Anderson household upside down as each family member reacts to superstition, including Jim, who insists he is the rational one.

title: Time For a New Car (1950-06-08)
plotSynopsis: Jim refuses to give up his aging automobile, but a simple repair becomes a chain of breakdowns and expenses that finally forces him to reconsider whether loyalty to the old car is worth it.

title: Father's Day Trip (1950-06-15)
plotSynopsis: The Andersons plan a special Father's Day, but Jim chooses a fishing trip instead; when both families join him, the outing ends with illness, lost gear, and the discovery that their prized fishing spot is actually a government fish hatchery.

title: A New Housekeeper (1950-06-22)
plotSynopsis: Jim hires a housekeeper to make the family look polished for his boss, but the eccentric helper creates far more disorder than she solves and threatens the very impression he hoped to make.

title: New Arrangements (1950-06-29)
plotSynopsis: Jim tries to accommodate several social commitments on the same evening, and his carefully arranged schedule collapses into a growing maze of conflicting plans and misunderstandings.

title: Vacation Arrives (1950-07-06)
plotSynopsis: The Andersons try to choose a destination for their summer vacation, but every family member has a different idea and the planning becomes more exhausting than the trip itself.

title: An Efficient House (1950-09-07)
plotSynopsis: Convinced the household needs businesslike organization, Jim introduces an efficiency system that quickly disrupts normal routines and proves that a family cannot be managed like an office.

title: Family Car Stolen (1950-09-14)
plotSynopsis: Jim is already battling a chaotic morning when the family car disappears, turning his rush to make an important appointment into a frantic search through the household's competing needs.

title: Who Has the Time (1950-09-21)
plotSynopsis: Conflicting clocks and schedules leave the Andersons arguing over what time it really is while an uncertain visit from Aunt Martha adds another layer of confusion.

title: The New Girlfriend (1950-09-28)
plotSynopsis: Bud's sudden interest in a new girlfriend collides with Betty's own romantic troubles, leaving Jim and Margaret caught in the middle of an unusually tangled family dinner.

title: Family Spending (1950-10-05)
plotSynopsis: Jim declares war on impulse buying, but his effort to teach the family restraint backfires when a favor for a colleague places him in an embarrassing buying predicament of his own.

title: The Skunk Must Go (1950-10-12)
plotSynopsis: Bud proudly brings home a supposedly deodorized skunk won in a raffle, and Jim's determination to get rid of it sends the Anderson home into predictable panic.

title: A Spooky Cemetery (1950-10-26)
plotSynopsis: Lost during a stormy Halloween night, the Andersons seek shelter near a cemetery and find their imaginations working overtime as an already unpleasant trip becomes increasingly eerie.

title: Too Many Problems (1950-11-02)
plotSynopsis: Jim tries to prepare for an important dinner, but one problem after another—from the children's mishaps to new community obligations—keeps expanding his list of crises.

title: The Bad Barbecue (1950-11-09)
plotSynopsis: Jim undertakes an ambitious backyard barbecue for important guests, only to watch the project go disastrously wrong before an unexpected turn rescues the meal.

title: Enterprising Kids (1950-11-16)
plotSynopsis: The Anderson children launch schemes to earn money, but their entrepreneurial efforts escalate into legal and family complications before producing a surprising payoff.

title: A Modern Thanksgiving (1950-11-23)
plotSynopsis: The children leave for separate Thanksgiving celebrations while Jim and Margaret stay behind, but each disappointing outing sends the family back home, where an improvised meal together becomes the holiday they really wanted.

title: Betty's French Teacher (1950-12-07)
plotSynopsis: Betty develops an intense crush on her French teacher, and Jim's attempt to manage the infatuation takes an unexpected turn when he discovers his own connection to the young man.

title: Father Becomes Ill (1950-12-14)
plotSynopsis: Jim tries to recuperate quietly from a cold, but the family's constant attention and a stream of well-meaning visitors make rest almost impossible.

title: Father Becomes Ill (AFRS) (1950-12-14)
plotSynopsis: Jim tries to spend a sick day resting in peace, but noisy children, mishaps, and aggressively helpful visitors turn his recovery at home into a more exhausting ordeal than going to work.

title: A Hans Christian Andersen Christmas (1950-12-21)
plotSynopsis: On Christmas Eve, Jim tells the family a story about Hans Christian Andersen, whose encounters with townspeople and his own storybook characters reveal lessons about love, faith, compassion, and the deeper meaning of Christmas.

title: Party Preparations (1950-12-28)
plotSynopsis: The Andersons' New Year's Eve preparations are disrupted when Jim wins a live turkey in a raffle, leaving the family to cope with an awkward prize while trying to get ready for the night.

title: Taking on City Hall (1951-01-04)
plotSynopsis: A dinner-table lecture about civic responsibility inspires Kathy to send the mayor a forceful letter in Jim's name, drawing him into a political dispute he never intended to start.

title: Missing Furniture (1951-01-11)
plotSynopsis: Jim enters a radio furniture giveaway on impulse, and the stunt leaves the Andersons facing the absurd prospect of a nearly empty house.

title: Redecoration Woes (1951-01-18)
plotSynopsis: Expecting wealthy dinner guests, the Andersons try to redecorate their living room cheaply; Jim's disastrous do-it-yourself paint job unexpectedly resembles the expensive fashionable style their guests already admire.

title: Sound Matchmaking (1951-01-25)
plotSynopsis: Jim and Margaret try to push cousin Louise and her longtime boyfriend toward marriage, but their matchmaking maneuvers produce confusion before the couple finally reaches a decision.

title: Jim Inherits a Ranch in Arizona (1951-02-01)
plotSynopsis: Jim learns he has inherited what appears to be a tremendously valuable Arizona cattle ranch, but the family's brief taste of being treated as rich ends when the property proves worth less than the taxes owed on it.

title: What was his Name (1951-02-08)
plotSynopsis: The family becomes preoccupied with solving a series of small mysteries, and Jim's determination to remember one elusive detail turns an ordinary evening into mounting frustration.

title: Orchid for a Lady (1951-02-15)
plotSynopsis: Valentine's Day becomes a neighborhood scramble when gifts and orchids are misunderstood, leaving Jim and the family trying to untangle who sent what to whom.

title: Always Tell Truth (1951-02-22)
plotSynopsis: Kathy promises to tell nothing but the truth on Jim's birthday, and her blunt honesty exposes uncomfortable secrets, embarrasses the adults, and wrecks his planned poker evening.

title: Rehearsing a Play (1951-03-01)
plotSynopsis: Jim reluctantly joins the children's Shakespeare production and discovers that his assigned part is nothing like what he expected, turning rehearsal into a comic lesson in literature and humility.

title: Being a Better Father (1951-03-08)
plotSynopsis: After reading a magazine article about fatherhood, Jim launches a determined campaign to become the best father he can possibly be.

title: Tax Interruptions (1951-03-15)
plotSynopsis: Jim lectures the children about procrastination while delaying his own tax work, and the contradiction catches up with him in a frantic night of paperwork and household disorder.

title: Stranded Strangers (1951-03-22)
plotSynopsis: After days of rain leave the Andersons complaining about their cramped, imperfect home, a stranded father and his children take shelter with them and give the family a renewed appreciation for what they already have.

title: Both Bosses Visit (1951-03-29)
plotSynopsis: An old love letter accidentally wins a contest on April Fool's Day, bringing reporters to the Anderson home and threatening to create serious trouble for Jim at work.

title: It Pays to Borrow (1951-04-05)
plotSynopsis: Jim bans borrowing and lending in the household, then watches the rule produce a cascade of complications that demonstrates how difficult his policy is to live by.

title: Carrot Costume Party (1951-04-12)
plotSynopsis: Jim's attempt to secure an important business deal becomes entangled with Betty's school production and an elaborate carrot costume that is impossible to keep out of the negotiations.

title: Anniversary Secret (1951-04-19)
plotSynopsis: The children and parents independently plan surprise anniversary celebrations for Jim and Margaret, and their secrecy causes the competing plans to collide in comic fashion.

title: Aunt Martha Visits (1951-04-26)
plotSynopsis: The family's plans for a baseball outing are derailed by the arrival of critical Aunt Martha, forcing everyone to juggle hospitality with the day they had intended to enjoy.

title: A Missing Salesman (1951-05-03)
plotSynopsis: Spring-cleaning chaos intensifies when the Andersons expect an important visitor and a missing salesman becomes the center of a string of misunderstandings.

title: Junk Around the House (1951-05-10)
plotSynopsis: To cure the family of bargain hunting, Jim buys an apparently useless object as a lesson, only for the purchase to take on surprising value and complicate his point.

title: Locked Out of the House (1951-05-17)
plotSynopsis: A simple attempt to leave for a tennis match becomes an ordeal of forgotten belongings, changed clothes, and finally the Andersons locking themselves out of their own house.

title: Anniversary Event (1951-05-24)
plotSynopsis: A tune Margaret hums convinces Jim she is dropping a romantic hint, and his effort to decipher it creates a chain of mistaken assumptions around their anniversary.

title: Going to New York (1951-05-31)
plotSynopsis: A promotion would require Jim to move the family to New York, forcing each Anderson to weigh personal ambitions and attachments before the decision takes an unexpected turn.

title: Father's Day Picnic (1951-06-14)
plotSynopsis: Jim expects a quiet Father's Day, but the family draws him into a huge community picnic where friendly recreation becomes an unexpectedly competitive athletic battle.

title: Mother Drives a Car (1951-06-21)
plotSynopsis: The family decides Margaret can learn to drive in a single day, and the crash course quickly becomes a chaotic test of everyone's patience and nerves.

title: Wedding Preparation (1951-06-28)
plotSynopsis: Betty announces plans for a sudden marriage to her artistic boyfriend, prompting a frantic family response and Jim's attempt to make the young couple confront the practical realities of married life.

title: Meaning of Freedoms (1951-07-05)
plotSynopsis: As the children argue about Independence Day, Jim uses a story from the American Revolution to show them that freedom carries sacrifice, responsibility, and meaning beyond a holiday celebration.

plotSynopsis: This Father Knows Best installment centers on “Saving Money to Buy a Boat,” the family situation identified in the transcribed episode index.

plotSynopsis: This Father Knows Best installment centers on “The Circus,” the family situation identified in the transcribed episode index.

title: A Diet Discussion (1951-09-20)
plotSynopsis: Jim embraces a strict new health diet and imposes it on the household, provoking mealtime rebellion until the family discovers an ironic truth behind his sudden enthusiasm.

title: Billiard Table (1951-09-27)
plotSynopsis: Jim gets an irresistible bargain on a used billiard table, but after tearing the felt he has to arrange a repair without Margaret discovering what happened.

title: The Rug (1951-10-11)
plotSynopsis: With Margaret’s birthday approaching, Jim buys a large surprise gift but discovers that hiding it from her until the celebration is harder than expected.

title: Gossip (1951-10-18)
plotSynopsis: A bout of careless talk teaches the Anderson family how quickly gossip can spread and how damaging it can become.

title: The Tie (1951-11-01)
plotSynopsis: A grotesque hand-painted necktie arrives with no sender identified, and the Andersons' attempts to discover who gave it to Jim create a series of uncomfortable and funny possibilities.

title: Fireside Chat 15
plotSynopsis: As war begins in Europe, Roosevelt recounts American efforts for peace, announces that the United States will remain neutral under existing law, and pledges to keep the country out of the conflict while insisting that neutrality does not require moral blindness to aggression.

title: Fireside Chat 26
plotSynopsis: Roosevelt addresses the wartime coal strike as a direct threat to military production. After describing the sacrifices of soldiers, industrial workers and farmers, he calls on miners to return to work under federal operation of the mines and argues that no group can place its interests above the war effort.

title: Fireside Chat 1
plotSynopsis: Roosevelt explains the banking emergency, why the national bank holiday was imposed, how banks will be examined and reopened in stages, and why restoring public confidence is essential to stabilizing the financial system.

title: Fireside Chat 9
plotSynopsis: In Part 1 of his March 1937 judicial address, Roosevelt argues that Supreme Court decisions have obstructed national economic policy and reviews the history of judicial review, constitutional powers and lifetime federal appointments before turning to the problem of aging judges.

title: Fireside Chat 16
plotSynopsis: In Part 1 of his May 1940 address, Roosevelt describes the humanitarian disaster spreading across Western Europe and urges support for relief. He then reviews American military preparedness, naval and army expansion, defense appropriations and the need to keep adapting to the rapidly changing methods of modern war.

title: Fireside Chat 25
plotSynopsis: After touring training camps and war factories, Roosevelt describes the United States as a single national fighting force. He focuses on manpower mobilization, the need to place workers where the war effort requires them, continued agricultural and industrial production, and the goal of a total victory that produces lasting peace.

title: Fireside Chat 27
plotSynopsis: Roosevelt points to the collapse of Mussolini’s Fascist regime and continuing Allied advances as evidence that the Axis is weakening. He reviews progress on the Russian and other fronts but warns against complacency, calling for sustained production and total victory over Germany, Italy and Japan.

title: Fireside Chat 20
plotSynopsis: In Part 1 of his February 1942 wartime report, Roosevelt compares the national struggle to Washington’s Revolutionary War hardships, rejects isolationism, explains the strategic importance of fighting across several theaters, and praises forces holding Japan at bay in the Philippines and Asia.

title: Fireside Chat 6
plotSynopsis: Roosevelt reviews industry and labor policy, the reorganization of the NRA, peaceful settlement of labor disputes, public works and the fight against permanent unemployment. He defends a broader idea of liberty that includes greater economic security for ordinary Americans.

title: Fireside Chat 31
plotSynopsis: Roosevelt tells Americans that the home front must continue producing weapons, paying taxes and buying war bonds while Allied forces press offensives around the world. He emphasizes that financing the war is a personal way for civilians to support those fighting and urges unrestricted participation in the war-bond drive.

title: Fireside Chat 19
plotSynopsis: Two days after Pearl Harbor, Roosevelt describes Japan’s attacks as part of a wider Axis assault and tells Americans to prepare for a long global war. He defends earlier aid to nations resisting aggression, calls for vastly expanded production, and says the United States must win both the war and the peace that follows.

title: Fireside Chat 29
plotSynopsis: On Christmas Eve, Roosevelt reports on his recent conferences with Allied leaders and discusses coordinated military strategy, the defeat of Nazi Germany and plans for a durable postwar peace. He closes with a Christmas message and prayer for American forces, prisoners, the wounded and the families waiting at home.

title: Fireside Chat 4
plotSynopsis: Roosevelt reports on the progress of recovery, discussing farm prices, the AAA, industrial employment under the NRA, purchasing power and monetary policy. He argues that commodity prices must rise while government credit and a sound currency are maintained.

title: Fireside Chat 22
plotSynopsis: In Part 1 of his April 1942 address, Roosevelt surveys the widening war and then turns to the home front, warning that inflation threatens the war effort. He introduces a comprehensive stabilization program covering prices, profits, wages, taxes, debt and the cost of living.

title: Fireside Chat 11
plotSynopsis: Roosevelt calls Congress into special session and argues for action on urgent national needs, including farm stabilization and long-range land and resource policy. He also discusses international instability and says the United States should actively pursue peace while avoiding the mistakes of the First World War era.

title: Fireside Chat 14
plotSynopsis: Roosevelt reviews the record of the 75th Congress, citing farm legislation, the Fair Labor Standards Act, investigations of monopoly, aviation reform, housing and support for smaller enterprises. He assesses the recession and urges voters to judge political candidates by constructive ideas rather than attacks.

title: Fireside Chat 10
plotSynopsis: In Part 2, Roosevelt explains his proposal to add a new federal judge whenever a judge over seventy declines retirement. He says the plan would speed justice, bring younger experience to modern social and economic questions, and restore balance among the branches of government.

title: Fireside Chat 13
plotSynopsis: In Part 2, Roosevelt details a renewed spending and lending program to create jobs, strengthen purchasing power and counter depression. He addresses the cost to the Treasury, cooperation with private business and the need for a government strong enough to protect both economic security and political liberty.

title: Fireside Chat 21
plotSynopsis: In Part 2, Roosevelt counters exaggerated rumors about Pearl Harbor losses, describes the scale of American war-production goals and industrial conversion, and calls for sacrifice, discipline and national unity as the country mobilizes for a long conflict.

title: Fireside Chat 23
plotSynopsis: In Part 2, Roosevelt spells out the sacrifices demanded by wartime stabilization, including higher taxes, limits on profits and incomes, price and rent ceilings, wage restraint, rationing and war-bond purchases. He closes by holding up military service and individual heroism as examples for civilians.

title: Fireside Chat 3
plotSynopsis: Roosevelt explains the New Deal recovery program as a coordinated attack on unemployment and collapsing purchasing power. He emphasizes the National Recovery Administration, shorter hours, higher wages, employer cooperation and collective action as the basis for industrial recovery.

title: Fireside Chat 2
plotSynopsis: Roosevelt reviews the first eight weeks of his administration, describing measures to stabilize banks, aid agriculture and homeowners, provide relief, restore credit and purchasing power, and begin a coordinated national recovery while warning against premature optimism and speculation.

title: Fireside Chat 18
plotSynopsis: After the German submarine attack on the USS Greer, Roosevelt describes the incident as deliberate aggression and argues that Axis control of the Atlantic would endanger the Western Hemisphere. He announces a more forceful naval defense of waters vital to American security.

title: Fireside Chat 7
plotSynopsis: Roosevelt presents the administration’s recovery program as a coordinated whole and explains the new federal work-relief effort, designed to replace direct relief with useful employment while relying on existing agencies and moving workers back toward private jobs when possible.

title: Fireside Chat 8
plotSynopsis: After touring drought-stricken states, Roosevelt describes farm families, livestock and communities devastated by drought. He outlines relief and long-term soil, water and land-use planning, and closes by linking Labor Day to the goal of economic as well as political freedom.

title: Fireside Chat 28
plotSynopsis: Roosevelt says recent Allied gains do not mean the war is nearly over and compares national cooperation to a community holding back a flood. He urges Americans to support the Third War Loan as a direct contribution to the fighting forces and a sign that the home front will not relax before victory.

title: Fireside Chat 12
plotSynopsis: In Part 1 of his April 1938 address, Roosevelt says the renewed business downturn requires aggressive government action. He links jobs, purchasing power and economic security to the survival of democratic institutions and argues that government cannot remain passive while unemployment rises.

title: Fireside Chat 30
plotSynopsis: Roosevelt celebrates the Allied capture of Rome and explains its military, political and symbolic significance while warning that Germany remains capable of resistance. He reviews the Italian campaign, rejects premature claims of final victory and praises Allied commanders and troops.

title: Fireside Chat 5
plotSynopsis: Roosevelt reviews the achievements of the 73rd Congress, including debt relief, securities regulation, reciprocal trade, housing, agricultural measures, communications regulation and monetary reform. He frames the administration’s work as a continuing program of relief, recovery and reconstruction.

title: Fireside Chat 17
plotSynopsis: In Part 2, Roosevelt calls for rapid modernization and expansion of defense production through American industry while arguing that the emergency does not require abandoning Social Security, conservation, collective bargaining or other domestic gains. He closes with an appeal for unity and peace.

title: Fireside Chat 24
plotSynopsis: Roosevelt argues that controlling inflation is essential to victory and presses Congress for action on the cost of living, wages and farm prices. He says he is prepared to use presidential powers if necessary and urges Americans to accept personal sacrifice rather than protect narrow economic interests.

title: Nineteen Eighty Four [Christo
plotSynopsis: Winston Smith works at the Ministry of Truth in a society watched by Big Brother and the Thought Police. Secretly disgusted by the Party's control of history and thought, he begins a forbidden relationship with Julia and discovers that private love can itself become an act of rebellion.

title: Nineteen Eighty Four [Christo
plotSynopsis: Winston and Julia try to move from private rebellion to active resistance by seeking the Brotherhood, but the Party's surveillance reaches them. Their defiance leads into the Ministry of Love and the threat of Room 101, where the regime sets out to destroy not just resistance but personal loyalty itself.

title: Homage To Catalonia
plotSynopsis: In 1936 Eric Blair leaves the village life he shares with Eileen and goes to Spain, determined not merely to report the Civil War but to fight fascism. He joins a badly equipped militia and enters a conflict whose confusion, hardship, and danger will reshape his political thinking and nearly cost him his life.

title: Homage To Catalonia
plotSynopsis: With the front stalled amid cold, bad weapons, and shortages, Eric is reunited with Eileen and returns to Barcelona to find the revolutionary atmosphere collapsing into conflict among the Left. Arrests, torture, and the detention of Georges Kopp convince the Blairs that they themselves are in danger and must escape Spain.

title: Keep The Aspidistra Flying — Part 1
plotSynopsis: Poet Gordon Comstock declares war on money and abandons a promising advertising career for deliberately low-paid work, convinced that poverty will preserve his integrity. Instead, his self-imposed deprivation corrodes his writing, friendships, and relationship with Rosemary until he is forced to decide whether rejecting ordinary security has become another form of self-destruction.

title: Animal Farm [Read by Bill Nighy]
plotSynopsis: Old Major's vision inspires the animals of Manor Farm to overthrow their human owner and build a society meant to belong to them. The pigs gradually take control, however, and Napoleon's rule transforms the revolution until the new rulers become increasingly indistinguishable from the humans they replaced.

title: Animal Farm [Tamsin Greig a & Toby J
plotSynopsis: Old Major's dream of an animal-run farm leads to rebellion and the expulsion of the humans. For a short time the animals believe they have created an equal society, but the educated pigs steadily concentrate power and Napoleon's leadership recreates the exploitation the revolution was meant to abolish.

title: Biographical Dramas Burma
plotSynopsis: After Eton and rejection by the girl he hopes to marry, young Eric Blair travels to Burma to join the Imperial Police. His experiences as an agent of empire profoundly unsettle him, helping drive his later rejection of imperialism and his decision to immerse himself in the lives of the poor after returning to England.

title: Biographical Dramas Dreaming
plotSynopsis: In 1938 Eric and Eileen Blair travel to Marrakech for Eric's health and so he can work on Coming Up for Air. The hostile reception to Homage to Catalonia and guilt over Spanish Civil War comrade Georges Kopp haunt the couple, while Eric dreams uneasily about England and his recent past.

title: Biographical Dramas Jura
plotSynopsis: In 1947, after Eileen's death, Eric Blair moves to the remote island of Jura with his sister Avril and young son. Seriously ill with tuberculosis, he tries to live off the land while pushing himself to complete the novel that will become Nineteen Eighty-Four.

title: Biographical Dramas Loving
plotSynopsis: The drama follows Eric Blair's difficult romantic life and, above all, the nine-year relationship with Eileen O'Shaughnessy that became central to both his private life and his development as George Orwell, amid his awkwardness, infidelities, and repeated attempts to reconcile intimacy with his work.

plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner secretly listen in on Cedric and a stranger, hoping to learn how Cedric acquired his unexpected money.

plotSynopsis: Lum organizes committees for the Pine Ridge premiere, but local personalities and autograph fever complicate his elaborate plans.

title: L&A 1942-05-04 (193) Apartment Idea Bad

plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner consider using Pine Ridge's $10,000 community fund for an old folks' home, a proposal whose appeal is partly tied to their own future comfort.

plotSynopsis: The partners discover that selling greeting cards also means coping with amateur poets and a growing collection of strange verse submissions.

plotSynopsis: Abner worries that his home is haunted while the men juggle baby-naming problems and other Pine Ridge obligations.

title: L&A 1942-07-27 (241) Coat-Of-Arms in Newspaper
plotSynopsis: After the coat of arms appears in a newspaper notice, Lum and Abner follow the new lead in hopes of identifying the baby's family.

plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner secretly organize a farewell party as Mousy gets ready to leave Pine Ridge for military service.

plotSynopsis: Pine Ridge gathers for Mousy's going-away celebration, mixing comedy with a sincere sendoff before his Army departure.

plotSynopsis: Lum's plan to have Cedric act insane in order to escape the engagement makes the wedding confusion even worse.

title: L&A 1942-12-31 (332) Patriotic Speech at Trial

title: L&A 1943-01-06 (335) Wimpy Foster Is Drafted
plotSynopsis: Wimpy Foster is drafted while the breach-of-promise case continues, creating an unexpected change in the defense's increasingly tangled strategy.

title: L&A 1943-01-07 (336) Winifred Elopes with Doctor

title: L&A 1943-01-11 (337) Grand Prize on Pinball
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner review Pine Ridge's latest oddities, including the recent elopement and the spectacular prize won by a local pinball player.

title: L&A 1943-01-12 (338) Club at Cedric's House

title: L&A 1943-02-25 (364) Lum Reads Etiquette Book

title: L&A 1943-03-01 (365) Pine Ridge Social Leader

title: L&A 1943-03-02 (366) Grandpap is Debutante

title: L&A 1943-03-09 (370) Club Learns About Etiquette
plotSynopsis: The Golden Era club receives a lesson in etiquette, giving its members new rules to misunderstand and debate.

title: L&A 1943-03-15 (373) Grandpap Doesn't Show Up

title: L&A 1943-03-31 (383) Better Dr Snide's Business

title: L&A 1943-05-03 (401) Synthetic Rubber Worthless
plotSynopsis: Tests reveal that the celebrated synthetic rubber is worthless, cutting short Lum's industrial dreams just as a new civic assignment arrives.

title: L&A 1943-05-04 (402) War Bond Staff Chairman
plotSynopsis: Lum's appointment to help lead the local War Savings Staff quickly inflates his sense of importance and complicates ordinary business at the store.

title: L&A 1943-05-12 (407) Neosho Doesn't Show
plotSynopsis: A planned war-bond event collapses when the featured mind reader fails to appear, forcing the organizers to improvise a substitute attraction.

title: L&A 1943-05-13 (408) Abner Subs for Neosho
plotSynopsis: Abner is pressed into impersonating the absent fortune teller for the war-bond drive, and the deception produces blackmail threats and identity confusion.

title: L&A 1943-05-19 (411) Lum's Troubles Known
plotSynopsis: Lum's romantic troubles become public and unexpectedly turn into the basis for a town-wide competition designed to sell more war bonds.

title: L&A 1943-05-20 (412) Selling Lots of War Bonds
plotSynopsis: The war-bond campaign sells heavily by turning Lum's future marriage into a public contest that he has little desire to win.

title: L&A 1943-05-25 (414) Relatives Arrive in Town
plotSynopsis: Relatives flood Pine Ridge to influence the war-bond wife contest, leaving Lum surrounded by family pressure and unwanted matchmaking.

title: L&A 1943-05-26 (415) Relatives Use Vacant Lot
plotSynopsis: The visiting relatives take over a vacant lot and create more disruption around the store while Lum's wife-election problem continues.

title: L&A 1943-06-01 (418) Lum Uses Psychology
plotSynopsis: Lum tries psychology to manipulate the results of the wife contest, but the supposedly clever strategy takes an ironic turn.

title: L&A 1943-06-02 (419) Mabel Melrose Shows Up
plotSynopsis: Lum attempts to flee the marriage contest just as the fictional candidate Mabel Melrose unexpectedly appears in person.

title: L&A 1943-06-03 (420) Mabel Wants to Claim Prize
plotSynopsis: The real Mabel Melrose demands the prize after winning the contest under the identity Lum invented, turning his escape scheme against him.

title: L&A 1943-06-08 (422) Lum in Love with Mabel
plotSynopsis: Facing marriage, a settlement or a lawsuit, Lum discovers that his feelings toward Mabel are changing in ways he did not expect.

title: L&A 1943-06-09 (423) Mabel, Surrealist Painter
plotSynopsis: Now smitten with Mabel, Lum tries to accommodate her career as a surrealist painter by finding an appropriately unconventional place for her work.

title: L&A 1943-06-14 (425) Artist in the Attic
plotSynopsis: Mabel's move into an attic and her eccentric art create household confusion while Lum helps organize an exhibit tied to war-bond sales.

title: L&A 1943-06-15 (426) War Savings Staff
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner build a War Savings Staff art event around Mabel's baffling modern paintings, leaving the organizers struggling to explain what the pictures mean.

title: L&A 1943-06-24 (432) Presiding over Art Sale
plotSynopsis: Lum presides over the art auction while his own secret engagement plan falters and Grandpap's simple painting becomes the unexpected attraction.

title: L&A 1943-06-28 (433) Lum Disgusted with Art
plotSynopsis: After his own art fails to impress, Lum swears off painting while Grandpap repeatedly boasts about the success of his traditional picture.

title: L&A 1943-06-29 (434) Lum and Mabel, Birdwatching
plotSynopsis: Lum tries to impress Mabel with his knowledge of rare birds, but the birdwatching expedition exposes just how shaky his expertise really is.

title: L&A 1943-06-30 (435) Lum Studies Correct Grammar
plotSynopsis: Lum studies grammar and tries to improve Abner's speech so he can appear more polished around Mabel, but Abner's literal mind resists every lesson.

title: L&A 1943-07-08 (440) How Mousey Was Wounded
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner investigate the story behind Mousy Gray's wartime wound, determined to learn how the returning soldier was actually injured.

title: L&A 1943-07-13 (442) Mabel Melrose Leaves Town
plotSynopsis: Lum misunderstands Mabel's request for help and convinces himself she is heartbroken and ready to run away with him just as she prepares to leave Pine Ridge.

title: L&A 1943-07-14 (443) Back to Business
plotSynopsis: With Mabel gone, Lum and Abner try to return to ordinary business until a missing telegram throws their War Savings Staff meeting into confusion.

title: L&A 1943-07-15 (444) Treasury Department Honors
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner fear a Treasury representative is coming to arrest them, unaware that the missing telegram explains a far more flattering reason for the visit.

title: L&A 1943-07-20 (446) Mousey and Old Blue at Club
plotSynopsis: Abner brings Old Blue to a men's club meeting after becoming obsessed with the idea of military service for his dog, creating canine chaos among the members.

title: L&A 1943-07-22 (448) Ellie Connors Escapes
plotSynopsis: A young runaway named Ellie Connors appears at the store looking for work just as a newspaper report reveals why authorities may be searching for her.

title: L&A 1943-07-26 (449) Don't Tell About Ellie
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner hide the escaped twelve-year-old from the marshal and wrestle with whether protecting Ellie is the right thing to do.

title: L&A 1943-07-28 (451) Ellie Will Go to Wisconsin
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner plan to get Ellie safely out of state, but the secrecy of the scheme and ordinary Pine Ridge nuisances complicate the escape.

title: L&A 1943-07-29 (452) Ellie Poses as Lum's Niece
plotSynopsis: Ellie poses as Lum's niece while the men try to send her away quietly, only for Squire Skimp and Abner's blunders to threaten the disguise.

title: L&A 1943-08-03 (454) Keeping Mary Entertained
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner try to keep the girl now known as Mary occupied and comfortable in her new identity, recruiting Cedric as an unlikely entertainer.

title: L&A 1943-08-04 (455) Who's Mary's Guardian
plotSynopsis: The men debate who should be Mary's legal guardian and whether her reform-school past must be reported, with Grandpap repeatedly derailing the decision.

title: L&A 1943-08-11 (459) Squire Suspicious of Mary
plotSynopsis: Squire grows suspicious of Mary while Abner manages the store and the complicated custody situation during Lum's absence.

title: L&A 1943-08-17 (462) Trailing Mary Around Town
plotSynopsis: Mary's probation places her under Uncle Henry's watch, forcing Lum and Abner to trail her and protect the secret of her past.

title: L&A 1943-08-18 (463) On Uncle Henry's Good Side
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner try to get on Uncle Henry's good side so Mary's probation will succeed, but their reconciliation scheme goes badly wrong.

title: L&A 1943-08-26 (468) Cedric Infects Everyone
plotSynopsis: Cedric's supposed illness spreads panic through the quarantined group until Lum and Abner discover that the case is not what everyone believed.

title: L&A 1943-08-31 (470) Story of Snorter the Pig
plotSynopsis: While Cedric recovers, his childish demands and habit of overhearing things make life difficult for Lum, Abner and everyone confined around him.

title: L&A 1943-09-01 (471) Getting Rid of Uncle Henry
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner search for a way to remove overbearing Uncle Henry from their affairs, but even a simple outing turns into another comic complication.

title: L&A 1943-09-02 (472) Report on the Reformatory
plotSynopsis: A damaging report threatens to send Mary back to the reformatory, prompting Lum and Abner to devise increasingly desperate ways to stop it.

title: L&A 1943-09-13 (477) President of School Board
plotSynopsis: Lum plots a campaign for school-board president, treating the local election as a chance to regain political standing in Pine Ridge.

title: L&A 1943-09-14 (478) Caleb Deciding Vote
plotSynopsis: Caleb becomes the critical vote in Lum's school-board campaign, and Abner's clumsy attempts to influence him endanger the whole plan.

title: L&A 1943-09-15 (479) Caleb Elected President
plotSynopsis: Lum's supposedly foolproof election strategy misfires and Caleb ends up president of the school board instead.

title: L&A 1943-09-22 (483) Paper for English Class
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner help Cedric prepare an English paper for high school, but turning his simple thoughts into acceptable schoolwork proves difficult.

title: L&A 1943-09-27 (485) Trade School Classes
plotSynopsis: Lum objects to the new board's emphasis on vocational training and gets into a literal-minded argument with Abner over what education should be.

title: L&A 1943-09-29 (487) Lum Leaves Town
plotSynopsis: Feeling forgotten and defeated, Lum disappears from Pine Ridge, leaving Abner worried about what has happened to his old partner.

title: L&A 1943-09-30 (488) Classified Ads
plotSynopsis: Abner and Grandpap place classified advertisements to locate the missing Lum, including a peculiar postscript meant to catch his attention.

title: L&A 1943-10-04 (489) Abner Rents Lum's House
plotSynopsis: Believing Lum may be gone for good, Abner rents his empty house to a widow who needs a place to live.

title: L&A 1943-10-06 (491) How to Get Widder Out
plotSynopsis: Lum returns to find a widow occupying his house and begins devising increasingly comic ways to persuade her to move out.

title: L&A 1943-10-07 (492) Ghosts
plotSynopsis: Lum tries to haunt his own home so the tenants will leave, only to learn that the elaborate ghost scheme may no longer be necessary.

title: L&A 1943-10-11 (493) Discuss a Movie Theater
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner plan a Pine Ridge movie theater and immediately clash over where it should be located and how they can possibly finance it.

title: L&A 1943-10-14 (496) Learn to Operate Projector
plotSynopsis: The new picture-show project hits a technical obstacle when Lum and Abner discover that operating the projection equipment is not as simple as they imagined.

title: L&A 1943-10-18 (497) Grandpap to Play Piano
plotSynopsis: Grandpap turns negotiations for a theater piano into a surprisingly hard bargain, forcing Lum and Abner to reckon with his business instincts.

title: L&A 1943-10-19 (498) Free Passes to Everyone
plotSynopsis: Lum gives away so many free theater passes that the generosity brings him into conflict with local authority before the doors even open.

title: L&A 1943-10-21 (500) Packing Suitcase for Trip
plotSynopsis: Abner packs for a simple training trip to the county seat and works himself into believing he has developed a serious illness.

title: L&A 1943-10-26 (502) Lum Buys The Vulture's Revenge
plotSynopsis: Lum buys a film called The Vulture's Revenge for the theater and discovers that acquiring motion pictures can become an expensive bidding contest.

title: L&A 1943-10-27 (503) Film Company President
plotSynopsis: Lum attempts to escape the bad film purchase but discovers that the movie company's salesman is much harder to outmaneuver than expected.

title: L&A 1943-10-28 (504) Mary's Problems in School
plotSynopsis: Mary's poor schoolwork and constant conversations with boys force Lum into an awkward attempt at a serious guardian-to-teenager talk.

title: L&A 1943-11-02 (506) Vote Name for Movie Theater
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner argue over advertising and other opening details while trying to choose a name for their new movie theater.

title: L&A 1943-11-03 (507) Squire to Be Third Partner
plotSynopsis: Squire Skimp demands a place as a third partner in the theater, threatening Lum and Abner's control of their new business.

title: L&A 1943-11-04 (508) Opening Competing Theater
plotSynopsis: When Lum and Abner refuse Squire's partnership demand, he threatens to open a competing theater and start a full-scale business war.

title: L&A 1943-11-09 (510) Squire Tricks Grandpap
plotSynopsis: Squire tricks Grandpap during the theater rivalry, leaving the old man out of work and Lum and Abner short of the help they expected.

title: L&A 1943-11-10 (511) Cedric Delivers Handbills
plotSynopsis: Cedric distributes handbills as Lum and Abner race toward opening day and discover a disturbing truth about Squire's competing plans.

title: L&A 1943-11-11 (512) Free Preview Tuesday
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner schedule a free preview in hopes of beating Squire to opening day, while Abner becomes far too absorbed in the feature film.

title: L&A 1943-11-15 (513) Rumors About Theater
plotSynopsis: Rumors and dirty tricks intensify the Pine Ridge theater war as both sides rush to attract customers first.

title: L&A 1943-11-18 (516) Squire's Theater Is Illegal
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner discover that an old ordinance may make Squire's upstairs theater illegal, giving them a legal weapon in the business feud.

title: L&A 1943-11-22 (517) Squire Arrested
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner move to have Squire arrested under the old theater ordinance while wrestling with whether using the law against a rival is fair.

title: L&A 1943-11-23 (518) Warrant on Squire
plotSynopsis: Justice Lum hesitates over serving the warrant on Squire, leaving Abner and Grandpap eager to enforce the ordinance themselves.

title: L&A 1943-11-29 (521) Squire Injured in Fall
plotSynopsis: Squire is injured during a busy night at Lum and Abner's picture show, turning the theater rivalry into a potential liability problem.

title: L&A 1943-11-30 (522) Writing Apologetic Note
plotSynopsis: Worried about Squire's fall, Lum and Abner write an apologetic note that may say far more about responsibility than they realize.

title: L&A 1943-12-01 (523) Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde
plotSynopsis: Lum tries to explain Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde to a confused, hypochondriacal Abner while the partners wait to see what Squire will do next.

title: L&A 1943-12-02 (524) Squire Sues for Damages
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner learn that Squire is suing them over his theater accident, transforming their guilty concern into fear of financial ruin.

title: L&A 1943-12-07 (526) Lum to Hire a Lawyer
plotSynopsis: Lum heads to the county seat to hire a lawyer for the lawsuit, but transportation trouble and Abner's advice make the legal mission difficult.

title: L&A 1943-12-08 (527) Things Don't Look Good
plotSynopsis: With the lawsuit looking disastrous, Abner waits anxiously for Lum while a confused long-distance call suggests they must recover damaging evidence.

title: L&A 1943-12-09 (528) Trying to Steal Note
plotSynopsis: Abner's attempt to retrieve an incriminating note from Squire turns into a botched break-in just as Lum returns with news about their case.

title: L&A 1943-12-13 (529) Squire Will Drop Charges
plotSynopsis: Squire's apparent willingness to drop one problem is overshadowed by the legal consequences of Abner's failed attempt to recover the note.

title: L&A 1943-12-15 (531) Wanting Squire's X-Rays
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner desperately seek Squire's X-rays, hoping the medical evidence will reveal something that can save them from the lawsuit.

title: L&A 1943-12-21 (534) Trying to Find Lum
plotSynopsis: Lum disappears during the trial, leaving Abner and Grandpap frantically trying to locate the man who may hold the key to their defense.

title: L&A 1943-12-23 (536) Lum Returns to Save the Day
plotSynopsis: Lum returns during the final phase of the case with evidence that changes the direction of the lawsuit against Squire.

title: L&A 1943-12-29 (539) Abner Sole Owner of Store
plotSynopsis: Lum urges Abner to sell the general store so the partners can put more money into the movie business, leaving Abner with sole ownership when the partnership splits.

title: L&A 1943-12-30 (540) Neither Lum Nor Abner Happy
plotSynopsis: After dissolving their partnership, Lum and Abner discover that neither is comfortable with the new arrangement or the loss of their old working relationship.

title: L&A 1944-01-03 (541) Everyone Against Abner
plotSynopsis: Abner struggles to run the store alone and find help, discovering that being the sole boss is less satisfying than he expected.

title: L&A 1944-01-04 (542) Lum's Theater Burns Down
plotSynopsis: Abner regrets leaving the theater venture just as Lum appears to be prospering, unaware that the picture show is about to suffer a disastrous fire.

title: L&A 1944-01-05 (543) Fire, Lum Loses Everything
plotSynopsis: Lum's uninsured picture show burns down, leaving him broke and too proud to admit how badly the loss has affected him.

title: L&A 1944-01-12 (547) Relationship Strained More
plotSynopsis: Working as Abner's delivery boy creates new resentment between the former partners as Lum finds ways to dodge chores and Abner struggles with the store books.

title: L&A 1944-01-13 (548) Lum Asks for a Raise
plotSynopsis: Lum turns his humiliating delivery job to his advantage by demanding a raise and maneuvering Abner into a position he did not expect.

title: L&A 1944-01-20 (552) Lum Trades Bogus Diamonds
plotSynopsis: Lum's imitation-diamond business collapses and a trade leaves him stuck with a barber chair, pointing him toward yet another unlikely profession.

title: L&A 1944-01-25 (554) Abner Thinks Lum Will Fail
plotSynopsis: Lum opens a barber shop inside Abner's store, wagers that he can make it succeed, and immediately provokes Pine Ridge's established barber.

title: L&A 1944-01-31 (557) Personalized Barber Mugs
plotSynopsis: With his new barber shop short on customers, Lum tries to attract business by offering personalized shaving mugs, creating a needlessly complicated promotion.

title: L&A 1944-02-01 (558) Lum Hires Customers
plotSynopsis: Lum pays local men to form a fake line outside his barber shop, but the stunt backfires and sends business toward his rival instead.

title: L&A 1944-02-03 (560) Shaves off Grandpap's Beard
plotSynopsis: A sleeping Grandpap becomes the victim of an ill-advised barber-shop makeover, and removing his familiar beard produces an unexpected shock.

title: L&A 1944-02-10 (564) Recruiting Book for Waves
plotSynopsis: Trying to escape his feud with Grandpap, Lum decides to join the Navy but badly misunderstands what the WAVES recruiting material is actually for.

title: L&A 1944-02-14 (565) Lum Invents Hair Tonic
plotSynopsis: Lum's continuing feud with Grandpap inspires a homemade hair tonic that appears to work far more dramatically than anyone anticipated.

title: L&A 1944-02-15 (566) Grandpap Mad at Tonic
plotSynopsis: Lum's fast-acting hair tonic and a wager with Grandpap create another round of trouble when the treatment works a little too well.

title: L&A 1944-04-04 (594) Cedric's Stenographer
plotSynopsis: Cedric's grand ideas about running the treasure company—including hiring a stenographer—force Lum and Abner to protect their investment from his extravagant management.

title: L&A 1944-04-11 (598) Car Breaks Down
plotSynopsis: The treasure-hunting party is stranded by automobile trouble and oppressive heat, turning the trip into a struggle over who will do the hard work.

title: L&A 1944-04-18 (602) Pawn Pinball Machine
plotSynopsis: After the failed treasure hunt, Cedric becomes convinced he is dying of a broken heart because he had to pawn his beloved pinball machine.

title: L&A 1944-04-24 (605) Mysterious Package Arrives
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner's worries about the Tennessee treasure expedition turn to excitement when an unexpected package arrives from their distant partner.

title: L&A 1944-04-26 (607) Using Worthless Old Coins
plotSynopsis: Lum returns with proof that their supposed treasure coins are worthless just after Abner and Cedric have committed money to an expensive purchase.

title: L&A 1944-05-01 (609) Lum Decides to Open Museum
plotSynopsis: Another disappointing batch of supposed buried treasure inspires Lum and Abner to turn the old objects into a museum instead.

title: L&A 1944-05-02 (610) Label Items in the Museum
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner prepare labels for their new museum collection, revealing that their ideas about history and proper curation are highly questionable.

title: L&A 1944-05-03 (611) Cedric Latest Date
plotSynopsis: Cedric borrows a supposedly historic coat from the museum while preparing for a special date, and the evening becomes unexpectedly awkward.

title: L&A 1944-05-04 (612) Lum Wants to Hire a Woman
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner debate hiring a woman to help operate the store and museum, with Abner's susceptibility to flattery complicating the decision.

title: L&A 1944-05-08 (613) Lum's Boring Museum Lecture
plotSynopsis: Lum tries to give a serious guided tour of the Pine Ridge museum, but his audience finds his high-culture lecture almost unbearably dull.

title: L&A 1944-05-11 (616) Is the Owl Alive or Not
plotSynopsis: Their investigation of a stuffed owl that keeps changing places becomes stranger when the supposedly lifeless exhibit appears to fly away.

title: L&A 1944-05-15 (617) Visit to Convalescent Lum
plotSynopsis: Abner's attempt to catch a museum thief ends with Lum accidentally struck on the head, leaving Abner scrambling to explain what happened.

title: L&A 1944-05-23 (622) Abner's Weird Behavior
plotSynopsis: Abner grows increasingly anxious as he tries to tell Elizabeth that his eccentric father is coming to Pine Ridge for another visit.

title: L&A 1944-05-25 (624) Phinus Peabody Arrives
plotSynopsis: Abner's eccentric father finally arrives in Pine Ridge and immediately throws Lum, Abner and the household into confusion.

title: L&A 1944-05-30 (626) 50th Wedding Anniversary
plotSynopsis: A golden-wedding-anniversary celebration is disrupted when Phinus Peabody's meddling turns a family occasion into comic chaos.

title: L&A 1944-05-31 (627) History of Peabody Family
plotSynopsis: Phinus launches into an exhausting account of Peabody family history for Cedric, and the rambling lesson leads toward an unusual outing.

title: L&A 1944-06-01 (628) Cedric and Phinus Take Trip
plotSynopsis: Abner struggles to obtain scarce gasoline for an urgent trip by Phinus and Cedric, only to learn the journey's purpose is surprisingly trivial.

title: L&A 1944-06-05 (629) Phinus Makes Elizabeth Nuts
plotSynopsis: Phinus's well-meant behavior creates turmoil at Abner's house until Abner asks Lum to help deal with his difficult father.

title: L&A 1944-06-06 (630) Odd Collecting Habit
plotSynopsis: Confusion over an expression leads Abner and Lum into a comic discussion of Phinus's peculiar habit of collecting unwanted objects.

title: L&A 1944-06-13 (634) Try to Find Job for Phinus
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner search for a suitable job to keep Phinus occupied, cycling through several impractical possibilities.

title: L&A 1944-06-14 (635) Job at Defense Plant
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner try to arrange an easy timekeeping position at a defense plant for elderly Phinus, only to encounter bureaucratic complications.

title: L&A 1944-06-15 (636) Tire Rationing Board Job
plotSynopsis: Another attempt to find employment for Phinus takes him to the tire-rationing board, where his interview does not go as expected.

title: L&A 1944-06-19 (637) Rich Stranger Arrives
plotSynopsis: The search for work for Phinus takes a surprising turn when he is seen with a wealthy stranger arriving in an expensive limousine.

title: L&A 1944-06-22 (640) The Story of Ponce De Leon
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner become suspicious of a visitor's interest in Grandpap's spring and connect the mystery, somewhat confusedly, with the Fountain of Youth.

title: L&A 1944-06-26 (641) BJ's Business Meeting
plotSynopsis: Lum is offended when he is excluded from a local business meeting and schemes to make himself appear essential to the gathering.

title: L&A 1944-06-27 (642) To Build Health Resort
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner enthusiastically back a plan to develop Grandpap's spring into a health resort, only to discover Grandpap strongly objects.

title: L&A 1944-06-29 (644) Taking Cedric's Picture
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner try to take a special photograph for Cedric to give his sweetheart before she leaves for Army service, with predictably clumsy results.

title: L&A 1944-07-03 (645) Grandpap Agrees to Resort
plotSynopsis: Lum begins maneuvering to become president of the proposed health-resort company just as Grandpap reveals a development that disrupts his plans.

title: L&A 1944-07-06 (648) Lum to Analyze Spring Water
plotSynopsis: Growing wary of the health-resort scheme, Lum and Abner decide to obtain an independent laboratory analysis of the spring water.

title: L&A 1944-07-11 (650) Results on Spring Water
plotSynopsis: The independent water analysis produces alarming results that cast the entire health-resort venture in a very different light.

title: L&A 1944-07-12 (651) BJ Webster Gets Analysis
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner pause before risking their savings after the spring-water reports they receive do not agree with one another.

title: L&A 1944-07-17 (653) Health Resort Riches
plotSynopsis: As Lum and Abner speculate about becoming wealthy through the resort, Grandpap makes an important announcement about the project.

title: L&A 1944-07-18 (654) BJ Webster Sole Owner
plotSynopsis: A legal question from Phinus occupies Lum and Abner while an apparently premeditated checkerboard offense becomes the day's unexpected problem.

title: L&A 1944-07-20 (656) Efficiency Measures at Work
plotSynopsis: Cedric introduces an efficiency idea at the war plant in hopes of earning a reward, only for the plan to produce an ironic consequence for him.

title: L&A 1944-07-24 (657) Grandpap to Sell Land
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner use a disguise while trying to invest in the resort and uncover a surprising development involving Grandpap's property.

title: L&A 1944-07-25 (658) Can't See Prez Spears
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner grow frustrated while waiting to see Grandpap, now acting as an important president and absorbed in a dubious meeting.

title: L&A 1944-07-26 (659) Putting up Screen Door
plotSynopsis: A supposedly simple attempt to install a screen door at the Jot 'Em Down Store turns into a string of comic mishaps.

title: L&A 1944-07-31 (661) Lum Serves Eviction Papers
plotSynopsis: As justice of the peace, Lum confronts the consequences of an eviction order that threatens Grandpap's farm for the sake of the resort development.

title: L&A 1944-08-01 (662) Grandpap Is Furious
plotSynopsis: Lum must somehow get eviction papers served on an enraged Grandpap while Pine Ridge's unreliable marshal is nowhere to be found.

title: L&A 1944-08-02 (663) Fiddle with Property Lines
plotSynopsis: New deputy Abner is given the unpleasant job of serving eviction papers on Grandpap and finds the assignment much harder than expected.

title: L&A 1944-08-03 (664) Briar Creek Ideas
plotSynopsis: Lum devises a questionable property-line and creek scheme intended to save Grandpap's farm and spring from Webster's development plans.

title: L&A 1944-08-08 (666) Abner Minds The Jail
plotSynopsis: In his new deputy-marshal role, Abner takes charge of the jail while his quarrel with Lum turns even routine business into a confrontation.

title: L&A 1944-08-09 (667) Abner Competes with Lum
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner's feud escalates until they literally divide the general store with a rope, bewildering anyone who tries to shop there.

title: L&A 1944-08-15 (670) Lum Traps BJ Webster
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner discover an obscure town ordinance and devise a plan to use it to place Webster under arrest.

title: L&A 1944-08-16 (671) BJ Webster Arrested
plotSynopsis: Deputy Abner attempts to arrest Webster for an antiquated traffic offense, carrying out the warrant in an unusually formal and comic fashion.

title: L&A 1944-08-21 (673) BJ Webster Pleads Guilty
plotSynopsis: Abner escorts Webster to court on the old traffic charge while Lum prepares to preside over a case central to their land scheme.

title: L&A 1944-08-22 (674) Buying Dillard Farm
plotSynopsis: The outcome of Webster's case becomes tied to a mysterious farm purchase, leaving Lum, Abner and Grandpap to sort out who now owns what.

title: L&A 1944-08-23 (675) Mailing Christmas Package
plotSynopsis: A Christmas parcel intended for a serviceman is repeatedly repacked as strict overseas mailing regulations make a simple errand increasingly absurd.

title: L&A 1944-08-24 (676) Helps Grandpap Move to Farm
plotSynopsis: Abner helps Grandpap and Aunt Charity settle onto their new farm, prompting a comic argument over work, chores and idleness.

title: L&A 1944-08-28 (677) Divert Creek to Property
plotSynopsis: Lum and Abner secretly discuss rerouting a creek to benefit Grandpap's land, but a nosy youngster repeatedly threatens to expose the scheme.

title: L&A 1944-08-29 (678) Won't Have to Change Creek
plotSynopsis: A legal loophole may let Lum and Abner recover Grandpap's spring without moving the creek, though keeping the plan quiet proves difficult.

title: L&A 1944-08-31 (680) Telling Lum About Charges
plotSynopsis: When embezzlement charges are filed against Lum, deputy Abner faces the painful responsibility of arresting his closest friend and business partner.

title: L&A 1944-09-06 (683) Lum Is Miserable
plotSynopsis: While jailed for embezzlement, Lum struggles to create the proper atmosphere of suffering for the autobiography he has decided to write.

title: L&A 1944-09-07 (684) Inflation Play (Repeat)
plotSynopsis: Still in jail, Lum organizes an amateur play warning about inflation, and the production quickly becomes another Pine Ridge comedy of errors.

title: L&A 1944-09-13 (687) Everyone Working on Case
plotSynopsis: Lum and his friends crowd together to prepare his embezzlement defense, with their frantic brainstorming eventually reaching a plea of insanity.

title: L&A 1944-09-14 (688) Squire to Take Lum's Case
plotSynopsis: Lum's approaching trial changes direction when Squire agrees to become his defense lawyer, giving Abner new hope for the case.

title: L&A 1944-09-20 (691) Situation Looks Hopeless
plotSynopsis: Witnesses in Lum's misuse-of-funds trial offer a confusing mixture of damaging and comic testimony, making his defense look increasingly bleak.

title: L&A 1944-09-27 (695) Lum Appreciates Everything
plotSynopsis: After his trial, Lum returns to the store determined to live quietly and work hard, but his new humility is soon tested.

title: L&A 1944-10-03 (698) School Board President
plotSynopsis: Lum claims the public wants him to become school-board president until Abner discovers where that supposed groundswell of support really originated.

title: L&A 1944-10-04 (699) Ignore Board Prez Lum

Mama distrusts him, invents a relative connected to the mining experts and police in Australia, and watches the promoter flee rather than let her verify his story.

title: Yetta's Lesson
plotSynopsis: Yetta complains about the family's apartment, car, neighborhood and plain dinner until Papa learns that a large customer check may fail and force him out of business. Mama calmly shows how they could manage with less, and when the check proves good, she uses the scare to teach Yetta how quickly ordinary comforts become precious when they seem about to disappear.

title: Jake Buys a New Car
plotSynopsis: When Jake brings an automobile salesman home, the family immediately quarrels over what kind of new car he should buy and criticizes his driving. After the daughters admit they were selfish and rude, Jake reveals he has already bought a new roadster, leaving everyone to argue cheerfully over who will use the rumble seat.

title: Planning an Afternoon Party
plotSynopsis: Mama prepares an elaborate bridge luncheon full of obligatory guests, prizes, special linens and social rules, including an invitation to the relentlessly boastful Mrs. Fink. When Mrs. Fink arrives bragging about her wealth, Mama calmly recalls her much humbler past and advises that people who have truly grown accustomed to money do not need to talk about it constantly.

title: Engagement Announced
plotSynopsis: On a Sunday morning, Mama and Papa complain about their daughters sleeping late and worry about Sidney's uncertain employment. Sarah then announces that she and Sidney became engaged the night before and plan to marry in four weeks, sending the household immediately into wedding, trousseau and job-planning mode.

title: Sidney Goes to Work for Jake
plotSynopsis: Newly working in Jake's business, Sidney alarms him by selling merchandise the factory does not even make and pushing for a much larger operation. Jake finally learns Sidney has ordered new machinery, leased two more floors and committed the firm to becoming a full-scale uniform manufacturer.

title: Red Uniform Profit
plotSynopsis: Jake is furious over a batch of bright red uniforms he assumes Sidney has made without a buyer. Sidney reveals they were a special order for a South American presidential guard, produces a certified check and a large profit, then announces prospects for thousands more uniforms.

title: Where's Sidney
plotSynopsis: Jake and Sam desperately need Sidney for an urgent Washington sales meeting but cannot locate him anywhere in Philadelphia. After fruitless calls to hotels and the telegraph office, Mama reasons that at dinnertime Sidney will be eating and successfully finds him at a restaurant through a relative's connection.

title: One Hundred Seventy Five Dollar Dress Bargain
sortKey: 0|9999-99-99|00017|one hundred seventy five dollar dress bargain
plotSynopsis: Shopping for Sarah's trousseau, Mama refuses to accept a department store's $175 price for an evening dress even while Sarah begs her not to bargain. When Mama recognizes a relative who works as the store's buyer, he reduces the same dress to $95, proving that her determination to haggle was worth the embarrassment.

title: Making the Wedding List
plotSynopsis: Mama and Sarah work through the enormous invitation list for Sarah's wedding, adding relatives, business acquaintances and social obligations while Mama supplies running commentary on each one. The task becomes a long lesson in marriage and in-laws as Mama warns Sarah that family complications begin as soon as the wedding is over.

title: Sidney's Visit at Night
plotSynopsis: Jake and Mama cancel an evening visit and settle in for cards, only to have Sarah and Sidney drop by just as Jake gets comfortable. Mama exposes Jake's afternoon pinochle games at the office, but Jake answers by revealing Sidney's late-night crap games to Sarah, sending Sidney home and leaving Jake free to take off his collar and shoes again.

title: Sara Is Jealous
plotSynopsis: Sarah becomes furious after learning that Sidney took a red-haired girl dancing while he was away in Philadelphia, and their argument grows until they ask Mama to decide who is right. Mama tells them both they are wrong, warns Sidney to consider his fiancee's feelings and Sarah not to risk their happiness over a few dances, and the couple reconciles under her practical marriage advice.

title: Honeymoon in Europe Rumor
plotSynopsis: As Sarah's wedding approaches, Papa hears Sidney telling a customer he may spend months in Europe and panics that the uniform business will be left in his hands. Sidney finally explains that the Europe story was only a bluff to force the customer to place an order and that the honeymoon will be just a short motor trip.

title: Mrs Fink Told Off
plotSynopsis: During the final days before Sarah's wedding, boastful Mrs. Fink belittles the Blooms' money, looks and family standing until Mama finally throws her out and fiercely defends Jake and the girls. Jake initially claims he would have ignored the insults, but becomes just as furious when he hears that Mrs. Fink also slighted Sarah.

title: Blank Checks
plotSynopsis: The day before Sarah's wedding, the Bloom home is overwhelmed by deliveries, telephone calls, expensive clothes, forgotten invitations and last-minute errands. Jake objects to nearly every new expense but keeps writing checks until Mama reaches the one request he dislikes most of all: several signed blank checks for her to fill in later.

title: The Day Before the Wedding
plotSynopsis: On the eve of Sarah and Sidney's wedding, the family is exhausted by fittings, relatives, honeymoon plans and endless last-minute details. Amid worries over the cost, Jake reveals that he has bought Sarah a new car simply because he wants to do one extravagant thing for his oldest daughter's wedding, and the household braces for the ceremony ahead.

title: The Wedding Day Arrives
plotSynopsis: Sarah's wedding day becomes a household scramble over a missing veil, ill-fitting clothes, flowers, food, the wedding cake, the rabbi and an absent bridegroom. Sidney finally arrives, the last-minute crises settle enough for everyone to take their places, and the ceremony is ready to begin.

title: Another Engagement
plotSynopsis: With Sarah and Sidney's wedding finally over, Mama and Papa sit up late reviewing the celebration, the relatives and the mountain of expenses. Just as they begin to enjoy the thought that life can return to normal, the family gets another surprise: Yetta announces that she is engaged.

title: New Furniture
plotSynopsis: As Yetta's wedding plans begin, Mama argues that the ceremony must be held at night so working friends can attend and enjoy it. The discussion turns to replacing the family's old furniture, and Mama uses pride, appearances and a well-timed reminder of one of Jake's old girlfriends to get him moving toward the furniture stores.

title: Yetta and Harold Elope
plotSynopsis: The Blooms and Finks discuss an elaborate wedding for Yetta and Harold, including hundreds of guests, orchestras, food and entertainment, while Mama argues for a simpler affair. Their plans become pointless when Sidney finally reveals that Yetta and Harold have already eloped to Greenwich.

title: Out of Honeymoon Money
plotSynopsis: After Yetta and Harold marry without the planned large wedding, the family learns that the newlyweds are in Greenwich with too little money for a honeymoon because Harold is determined not to ask his father for help. Papa agrees to finance the trip, while the family also learns that Harold plans to support himself by joining Sidney in the Bloom business.

title: Harold Becomes a VIP
plotSynopsis: After Yetta and Harold return from their honeymoon, Mama warns that adding another son-in-law to the knee-pants factory may strain Jake's patience. Jake decides Harold should learn the business from the bottom instead of getting a flashy executive office, only for Sidney to arrive with new company stationery naming Harold vice president in charge of sales.

title: Should Papa Retire
plotSynopsis: Mama visits the modernized factory and defends Jake's attachment to the old knee-pants business while the family debates fancy offices and new ways of working. The discussion ends with Sidney and Harold telling Jake that, now that they can handle the business, they think he should retire.

title: Papa Wants a Vacation
plotSynopsis: With Sidney and Harold urging Papa to retire from the knee-pants business, Mama tries to convince him that after years of work he needs a real vacation and can trust the younger men for a while. Jake finally agrees to take several weeks off, only to discover Mama has already bought tickets for Yellowstone Park.

title: Travel Plans Changed
plotSynopsis: Mama and Papa begin planning the Yellowstone vacation for which Mama has already bought tickets, until Mrs. Fink visits and boasts about her travels. Learning that Mrs. Fink has never been to Hollywood gives Mama a new target, and she abruptly tells Sarah to exchange the Yellowstone material because the Blooms are going to Hollywood instead.

title: Should Sam Retire
plotSynopsis: While Jake prepares for a Hollywood vacation, his partner Sam complains about the factory's new gadgets and the changes brought by Sidney and Harold. After Mama explains why she wants Hollywood and Jake reassures himself that Sam can keep the boys in line, Sam arrives with worse news: Sidney and Harold are trying to persuade him to retire too.

title: First to Hollywood
plotSynopsis: As Mama and Papa prepare for their own Hollywood trip, the family gives them an early farewell dinner and new luggage. The celebration takes an unexpected turn when Harold rushes off to say goodbye to his own parents, who are leaving for Hollywood the very next morning.

title: Grandparents Soon
plotSynopsis: Mama gives up trying to beat Mrs. Fink to Hollywood after learning the Finks will arrive there first, deciding that competing with her is foolish. Sidney and Sarah then reveal that Mama and Papa will soon be grandparents, giving Mama the one happy distinction she can enjoy before Mrs. Fink after all.

title: Mr Greenville's Offer
plotSynopsis: A businessman named Mr. Greenville visits the Blooms and offers to buy the entire knee-pants factory so he can expand his own operation. Papa cannot bring himself to answer immediately, and Mama slips away in tears because selling the business would mean closing a piece of the life they struggled together to build.

title: Eighty Thousand Dollar Price
plotSynopsis: When businessman Mr. Grenville offers to buy the Blooms' factory, Jake and Sam initially decide they cannot part with the business. Mama discovers from a magazine that Grenville is actually an executive of a major uniform manufacturer, so she tells Jake to quote an enormous $800,000 price to scare him away; Grenville accepts, leaving Jake astonished and free to retire and take a leisurely drive to Hollywood.

title: The Hollywood Trip Begins
plotSynopsis: After Jake and Sam sell the factory for $800,000, Mama changes the Hollywood trip from train travel to a leisurely drive and gets the reluctant Jake packed for retirement. As Mama and Papa finally leave, their daughters and sons-in-law surprise them by announcing that they are all coming along.

title: The Bridge Game
plotSynopsis: At a Michigan hotel, Mama decides that playing bridge with the other guests is part of taking a proper vacation, even though Jake barely knows the game. Paired against experienced strangers, Jake blunders into a six-spade contract and only then learns they are playing for ten cents a point.

title: Indian Trouble
plotSynopsis: While driving through Arizona, Mama and Papa take a wrong road, become separated from the children and panic when a group of Indians appears to chase them. The pursuers turn out to be performers in a movie being shot in the desert, and the Blooms' intrusion ruins the take and leaves Papa facing the director's complaint about the costly disruption.

title: In the Pictures
plotSynopsis: During the family's Hollywood vacation, Mama insists that Papa accompany her on a tour of a movie studio, where the unfamiliar jargon and production routines leave him baffled. Watching the day's rushes brings the biggest surprise when Mama and Papa discover that Sidney and Harold have already managed to get themselves into the pictures.

title: Papa Buys In
plotSynopsis: Sidney and Harold secretly prepare to persuade Papa to invest in the movie business, believing he will soon become restless on vacation, while the daughters worry that he and Mama deserve a rest. When the family finally raises the subject, Papa surprises everyone by revealing that he has already bought what he believes is a small interest in a Hollywood movie company.

title: Sidney and Harold Are Also In
plotSynopsis: Jake proudly believes he has beaten Sidney and Harold into the movie business by buying an interest in Excelo Pictures on his own. When he visits the studio, however, he discovers Sidney's name being painted on an office door and realizes the two sons-in-law are already involved there as well.

title: A Controlling Interest
plotSynopsis: Papa is already furious that Sidney has installed himself in the movie company when another surprise arrives: a contract Papa thought bought only a share of the studio is examined closely. Sidney discovers that Papa actually purchased the controlling interest, making the bewildered Jake the big boss of Excelo Pictures.

title: Getting Used to It
plotSynopsis: The morning after learning that he accidentally bought the entire Excelo Pictures Corporation, Jake would rather stay in bed than face his new business. Mama talks him into getting up and learning the ropes, and Jake works himself into a determined rush to reach the studio before Sidney until Sarah reminds him that it is Sunday.

title: Learning the Ropes
plotSynopsis: Jake struggles with flashing telephone lines, secretaries and Hollywood jargon while Sidney and Harold try to run his new studio like seasoned executives. Their effort to shield him from unannounced visitors backfires when the persistent unnamed woman they keep waiting outside turns out to be Mama, who cannot understand why her own husband suddenly needs her name before she can see him.

title: A Quiet Evening at Home
plotSynopsis: Jake plans a peaceful evening at home with his shoes off and the newspaper, but Mama fills the night with comments about his socks, weight, relatives and an old girlfriend. After repeatedly trying and failing to read even one article in peace, Jake decides that going out to a movie will be more restful than staying home.

title: Marsha Valle's Temper Tantrum
plotSynopsis: Excelo's temperamental star Marsha Valle refuses her current story and threatens to walk out, putting the delayed production in danger. Mama arrives with a letter from New York that reveals the glamorous actress's Bronx identity, giving the Blooms exactly the leverage needed to bring the crisis under control.

title: Back to Normal
plotSynopsis: With Marsha Valle's threatened walkout settled, the family gathers for supper and credits Mama with saving the studio from losing its biggest star. Mama uses the incident to remind everyone that movie-business glamour and new interests should not make them forget where they came from or that they are still one family.

title: One Hundred Suits of Armor
plotSynopsis: After Sidney's purchase of a hundred suits of armor leaves Jake furious and sore from being trapped inside one, Sarah urges Mama to modernize Papa's clothes so he looks more like a Hollywood executive. Jake tries to put the armor fiasco behind him, only to lose his appetite when Sidney announces that the evening's movie is The Iron Horse.

title: One Hundred More Arrive
plotSynopsis: Determined to rid Excelo Pictures of one hundred unwanted suits of armor, Jake arranges to sell them off even at a loss and goes to the prop department to watch them leave. His relief vanishes when a delivery truck arrives with one hundred more suits of armor that Sidney has just purchased.

title: A Super Picture
plotSynopsis: Papa is furious that Sidney has bought another hundred suits of armor, leaving the studio with two hundred seemingly useless costumes, and he threatens to sell the movie company. Sidney and Harold then reveal that the armor inspired them to write a large costume picture for Marsha Valier, turning Papa's supposed disaster into the basis for a super production.

title: Movie Premier
plotSynopsis: Mama and Jake head to their first Hollywood premiere but leave an unopened letter at home and battle crowds, parking fees and poor seats without seeing much of anything. After they return exhausted, Sidney calls and reveals that the special-delivery letter they ignored contained the tickets that would have admitted them properly.

title: Mama Is Homesick
plotSynopsis: Surrounded by Hollywood excitement and the plans for the studio's big picture, Mama admits that she is homesick for New York and the quieter life she and Papa once knew. Papa offers to go back for her sake, but their talk reminds her that home is where the family is, and she stays involved even while discovering that owning the company does not automatically put Papa's name in the screen credits.

title: Yascha Bloomakoff
plotSynopsis: Frustrated that everyone else receives screen credit, Jake decides his own name should appear prominently on the new picture and Mama enthusiastically agrees. Sidney arrives with an advance poster, but the promised credit shocks Jake because Hollywood has renamed him 'Yascha Bloomakoff.'

title: New Name Accepted
plotSynopsis: Sidney decides Jake Bloom needs the more impressive screen-business name Yasha Bloomacoff, but Jake resents giving up the name he built his life and business under. Mama reminds the family what Jacob Bloom's name and signature have meant to them, even as Jake gradually begins to warm to the fancy new version.

title: Shooting Gallery
plotSynopsis: A reluctant Jake joins the family for a Sunday trip to an amusement park and is talked into proving his skill at a shooting gallery. He misses badly while Mama unexpectedly hits every target and wins a prize, and the outing gets even worse for him when the family enters a dark attraction and comes out without Papa.

title: Papa's Dancing Partner
plotSynopsis: Driving home from a banquet, Mama jealously accuses Papa of dancing too many times with the wife of an important film exhibitor and of enjoying her resemblance to an old flame. Papa insists the dances were strictly business, but the quarrel follows them all the way to bed, where a late-night call about the woman gives Mama's suspicions one more comic jolt.

title: Sara Is Jealous
plotSynopsis: Sarah becomes jealous after seeing Sidney with movie star Marsha Vallier when he had said he was too busy to have lunch with her. Sidney explains that the meeting was strictly business about Marsha's part in a new picture, and the misunderstanding quickly blows over.

title: New Neighbors
plotSynopsis: Mama postpones Papa's supper while she watches new neighbors move in, first admiring their belongings and then inventing suspicions from every new thing she sees.
