By the time the move is finished she has changed her mind again and plans to invite them over, remembering how hard it can be for newcomers with an accent to make friends.

title: Movie Plot Problem
plotSynopsis: Sidney and Harold struggle to repair a movie plot in which the heroine returns late after riding away on horseback, but every excuse they invent contradicts scenes already filmed. Mama casually suggests that the girl took the wrong road because Halloween pranksters turned a road sign around, giving the boys the solution they need just before their deadline.

title: Sara Has Twins
plotSynopsis: Papa, Sidney and Harold wait anxiously for news while Mama is with Sarah, passing the time with pinochle and worrying despite Mama's attempts to stay practical. Telephone calls finally bring the news that Sarah has delivered twins, a girl and a boy, leaving Mama and Papa overwhelmed with joy at becoming grandparents.

title: Going to the Hospital
plotSynopsis: Mama and Papa hurry to the hospital to see Sarah and the newborn twins, where Sidney sneaks Papa toward the nursery for an early look. Papa confidently identifies two babies through the glass as his grandchildren and argues with Sidney about it, only for Mama to reveal that Sarah's twins are actually in the room with their mother.

title: Getting to Sleep
plotSynopsis: Exhausted new grandparents Mama and Papa try to get a full night's sleep, but they keep waking one another over the twins, household noises, a late sandwich and imagined trouble. A middle-of-the-night call from Sidney briefly sends Mama into alarm before she learns the baby is fine, leaving Papa desperate for the uninterrupted sleep he cannot get.

title: Shopping for a New Suit
plotSynopsis: Mama insists that Papa needs a new suit for the twins' naming celebration and drags him through a department store. Papa becomes distracted by the store's free food samples and the pair argue over styles and shopping until the store begins closing before their errand is properly finished.

title: Picking Baby Names
plotSynopsis: Mama and Papa wait for Sidney and Sarah to help choose names for the newborn twins, while Jake campaigns for Nathan in honor of his grandfather. When the parents favor other family names, Mama proposes drawing the boy's name from a hat and secretly writes Nathan Morris on every slip so Papa's favorite name will be chosen.

title: Naming Party
plotSynopsis: As the Blooms prepare their apartment for the twins' naming party, Papa tries to steal time with the babies while Sidney insists on following childcare rules from a book. The preparations unravel when Mama burns Papa's new trousers while ironing them just as the guests begin arriving.

title: The Fortune Teller
plotSynopsis: Sarah persuades a skeptical Mama to visit a Hollywood fortune teller who claims he can reveal facts without being told anything. Mama challenges his questions and vague predictions at every turn, and the only useful revelation comes when the visit reminds her that she left potatoes cooking on the stove at home before the psychic charges them five dollars.

title: Arthur S Mollington
plotSynopsis: At the studio commissary, Mama and Papa meet Arthur S. Mollington, an extra who grandly describes himself as a serious stage actor temporarily lending art to the movies. Mama notices that beneath the boasting he eagerly accepts food and plainly needs steady work, so she asks Papa to find him a job.

title: Almost Caught at Pinochle
plotSynopsis: Papa, Sidney and Harold spend office time playing pinochle until Mama and Sarah unexpectedly arrive, forcing them to hide the cards and invent a story about discussing a new picture. The women appear to leave without discovering the truth, but Mama doubles back just as the men are ready to resume the game.

title: To the Restaurant
plotSynopsis: After Mama rearranges the apartment, Jake is recruited to put the furniture back instead of going out to eat. While moving a lamp they open an old trunk and happily reminisce over family keepsakes until a photograph from Jake's courting days revives an old grievance and makes a restaurant suddenly seem like the safer choice.

title: The Magician's Show
plotSynopsis: A family trip to the theater begins with Jake enduring constant backseat driving from Mama, Sarah and Sidney. During the magician's act, Mama volunteers to be hypnotized but keeps arguing with every suggestion and refuses to become drowsy, while the performer finally discovers that Jake has fallen asleep in the audience instead.

title: Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollar Super Picture
sortKey: 0|9999-99-99|00076|two hundred fifty thousand dollar super picture
plotSynopsis: Papa corners Sidney and Harold for the final cost of Excelo's completed super picture, but the boys keep evading the figure while explaining the extra actors, locations, costumes and production work. Mama tries to keep Papa calm until they finally admit the picture will cost about $250,000, leaving him stunned into silence.

title: Sneak Preview
plotSynopsis: Papa dreads the sneak preview of Excelo's expensive new picture, convinced that a failure will make him look foolish and waste a fortune. Mama and the children try to steady him, and by the time they leave for the theater Papa privately tells Sidney that even if this picture fails, they will spend the money necessary to make a good one next time.

title: Retirement
plotSynopsis: After the expensive Excelo picture receives encouraging reaction at its preview, Papa admits that Sidney and Harold may be capable of running the studio and announces that he may finally retire and take a real vacation with Mama. The resolution lasts only until bedtime, when he suddenly remembers to set the alarm so he can get to work early the next morning.

title: Wuthering Heights (1944-10-22)
plotSynopsis: Heathcliff and Catherine grow up bound by an intense love that is broken when Catherine chooses the security of marriage to Edgar Linton. Heathcliff returns wealthy and embittered, but neither revenge nor years apart can extinguish his bond with Catherine. After Catherine dies following their final reconciliation, Heathcliff spends the rest of his life longing for her and eventually dies calling to her spirit, suggesting the lovers are reunited beyond death.

title: Beloved Enemy (1944-10-29)
plotSynopsis: During the Irish conflict of 1921, rebel leader Dennis Reardon and English aristocrat Helen fall in love even as their countries stand opposed. Reardon joins negotiations in England and returns home urging his followers to accept a treaty and build Ireland through peace rather than vengeance. A dissident shoots him during a public address, but the wound is not fatal, and Helen joins him as he looks toward both a peaceful future and a life together.

title: My Favorite Wife (1944-11-05)
plotSynopsis: Nick Arden has his long-missing wife Ellen declared legally dead and immediately marries Bianca, only for Ellen to return after seven years stranded on an island. Nick struggles to undo the new marriage while hiding Ellen’s return, then becomes jealous when he learns she shared the island with handsome Stephen Burkett. A bewildered judge annuls Nick’s second marriage, confirms Ellen as his lawful wife and sends the reunited couple home together.

title: Penny Serenade (1944-11-12)
plotSynopsis: As Julie prepares to leave her husband Roger, a stack of records carries her back through their courtship, marriage, financial struggles and the loss of a pregnancy that leaves them unable to have a child. They adopt a little girl, Trina, and build a family around her, only to lose her to sudden illness years later. Their shared grief nearly breaks the marriage, but Julie and Roger reconcile just as the adoption agency offers them a chance to take in a three-year-old boy.

title: Scarlet Pimpernel (1944-11-19)
plotSynopsis: Sir Percy Blakeney hides his work rescuing victims of the French Revolution behind the mask of a foolish English dandy, even from his wife Marguerite. Their marriage is strained by Percy’s belief that she betrayed an aristocratic family, while Chauvelin blackmails Marguerite by threatening her brother. When she discovers Percy is the Scarlet Pimpernel and follows him to France, the couple outwit Chauvelin, rescue the threatened fugitives and reconcile.

title: Mr and Mrs Smith (1944-11-26)
plotSynopsis: Married couple David and Ann Smith learn that a jurisdictional technicality means their marriage was never legally valid. David assumes Ann will simply marry him again, but his handling of the news infuriates her, and his friend Jeff begins courting her while David grows increasingly jealous. After comic battles over whether they still belong together, new legislation validates the original marriage and the Smiths happily reconcile.

title: Jane Eyre (1944-12-03)
plotSynopsis: Governess Jane Eyre falls in love with the brooding Rochester at Thornfield Hall, only to discover at their attempted wedding that his mentally ill wife Bertha is still alive and hidden in the house. Jane leaves rather than become his mistress. She later returns after Bertha has set Thornfield ablaze and died in the fire, finding Rochester blinded but alive, and chooses to stay as his wife and become his eyes.

title: Hold Back the Dawn (1944-12-10)
plotSynopsis: European refugee George Iscovescu is stranded in Mexico waiting for permission to enter the United States when he plans a marriage of convenience to American schoolteacher Emmy. The scheme changes when he genuinely falls in love with her, but its discovery drives Emmy away and she is badly hurt in a crash. George crosses the border illegally to reach her, and an immigration inspector ultimately gives the reformed George a chance to enter legally and reunite with his wife.

title: Elizabeth the Queen (1944-12-17)
plotSynopsis: Queen Elizabeth and the Earl of Essex are bound by love but divided by pride, ambition and the demands of the English throne. Essex defies the queen during the Irish campaign, returns with armed supporters and is imprisoned for treason. In their final meeting both admit their love, but Essex warns that pardoning him would only renew his challenge to Elizabeth’s authority, and he accepts execution so that she may continue to rule.

title: A Stable in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania (1944-12-24)
plotSynopsis: Two lonely, cynical clubmen spend Christmas Eve listening to a mysterious waiter recount a modern Nativity-like story from Bethlehem, Pennsylvania. A stranded Mary and Joseph take refuge in a stable, where a trucker, a doctor, a lawyer, a merchant and policemen rally around the birth of their child while pursuing a stolen star sapphire. When the clubmen learn no such waiter was on duty, the story leaves them newly aware of charity, companionship and the spirit of Christmas.

title: Random Harvest (1945-01-07)
plotSynopsis: An amnesiac former soldier known as Smithy escapes an institution, falls in love with Paula and builds a quiet married life with her. An accident restores his identity as wealthy Charles Rainier while erasing his memories of Paula and the years they shared. Paula later returns to his life without revealing the full truth, waiting for his memory to return, and their long separation finally ends when familiar places unlock the past and Smithy recognizes her again.

title: Smilin' Through (1945-01-14)
plotSynopsis: Elderly John Carteret raises his niece Kathleen while remaining haunted by the memory of his beloved Moonyeen, who was killed on their wedding day by jealous Jeremiah Wayne. When Kathleen falls in love with Wayne’s son Kenneth, John tries to prevent history from repeating itself because of his hatred of the Wayne family. He finally blesses the young couple’s marriage, then dies peacefully in his garden as he sees Moonyeen waiting to lead him away.

title: Rebecca (1945-01-21)
plotSynopsis: The shy second Mrs. de Winter arrives at Manderley feeling overwhelmed by the memory of Maxim’s glamorous first wife Rebecca and by Mrs. Danvers’s devotion to her. When Rebecca’s sunken boat and body are recovered, Maxim’s past comes under renewed scrutiny and Rebecca’s cousin accuses him of murder. A doctor’s evidence that Rebecca had an incurable disease provides a motive for suicide, and with the threat lifted the new Mrs. de Winter claims Manderley as her home and looks toward a future with Maxim.

title: Beautiful Dreamer (1945-01-28)
plotSynopsis: The drama follows songwriter Stephen Collins Foster from youthful ambition in Pittsburgh through popular success, marriage and the financial hardships that his music cannot overcome. As poverty separates him from his wife Jeannie and their child, Foster writes on but dies in New York at thirty-eight with only thirty-eight cents. The closing narration contrasts his personal failure with the enduring American life of songs such as Beautiful Dreamer.

title: Reap the Wild Wind (1945-02-11)
plotSynopsis: In 1830s Key West, spirited Loxi Claiborne is drawn to sea captain Jack Stuart while lawyer Stephen O’Jay investigates dangerous salvage practices among the Florida reefs. A storm exposes Jack’s plan to ground his own vessel so he can profit from the valuable cargo through a staged salvage claim. Faced with the truth, Loxi rejects Jack and realizes that the steadier Stephen is the man she loves.

title: Intermezzo (1945-02-18)
plotSynopsis: World-famous violinist Holger Brandt falls in love with gifted young pianist Anita Hoffman and leaves his wife and daughter to tour with her through Europe. Their musical and romantic partnership brings intense happiness, but Anita comes to believe that their love has no rightful future at the cost of Holger’s family. She quietly leaves to accept a scholarship, and Holger returns home, preserving the affair as a bittersweet intermezzo in his life.

title: The Highwayman (1945-02-25)
plotSynopsis: A romantic outlaw rides by moonlight to meet Bess, the landlord’s daughter, until soldiers seize her and bind her in the window as bait for his return. Unable to escape, Bess reaches the trigger of a musket and shoots herself to warn him as he approaches. The highwayman learns of her death, rides back in fury and is killed on the road, while the closing legend imagines the lovers’ ghosts meeting again on moonlit nights.

title: Rendevous at Mayerling (1945-03-11)
plotSynopsis: Crown Prince Rudolf of Austria and young Marie Vetsera fall deeply in love, but imperial duty, Rudolf’s marriage and the Habsburg court make a life together impossible. Ordered to end the affair, Rudolf promises that a final meeting at Mayerling will be their last. Knowing they cannot have the ordinary home and family they imagine, Rudolf and Marie choose to die together at dawn, believing they will find the freedom and peace denied them in life.

title: The Pirate of Orleans (1945-03-18)
plotSynopsis: Pirate Jean Lafitte is offered money and a pardon to help the British capture New Orleans, but he instead sides with Andrew Jackson and helps defend the city during the War of 1812. After the victory, Lafitte tries to return to the freedom of the sea rather than settle into domestic life with the woman who loves him. She secretly joins his ship, and the pirate finally accepts that his adventures will now include a wife as well as a crew.

title: Till We Meet Again (1945-03-25)
plotSynopsis: In Nazi-occupied France, young convent novice Sister Clotilde becomes involved in helping an American officer escape with vital underground papers. Their journey teaches the sheltered novice about love, marriage and the life outside her religious calling, but she keeps her promise to return after the officer reaches safety. When the Gestapo threatens her with a fate worse than execution, a companion intervenes violently rather than let the Nazis take her, while the rescued officer carries her memory home.

title: Love Story of Elizabeth Barrett and Robert Browning (1945-04-01)
sortKey: 0|1945-04-01|00024|love story of elizabeth barrett and robert browning (1945-04-01)
plotSynopsis: Invalid poet Elizabeth Barrett meets Robert Browning under the controlling shadow of her father and slowly discovers that Browning’s admiration has become a love she returns but is afraid to trust. After nearly losing him, Elizabeth reveals an honest love letter she had never meant him to see. They decide they can no longer be separated and plan to leave her father’s house together for marriage and a new life in Italy.

title: A Man Named Jones (1945-04-08)
plotSynopsis: In Imperial Russia, American naval hero John Paul Jones falls in love with Princess Anna Korakina despite the objections of Empress Catherine and Prince Nassau. Jones and Anna secretly marry before he leaves to fight for Russia, but Catherine sends Anna away. After returning victorious, Jones crosses Russia searching for his wife, finally finding Anna and their young son at a convent and promising to take them home to Virginia.

title: Intoduction to the OTRR
plotSynopsis: An Old Time Radio Researchers Group introduction explains the organization’s volunteer preservation work, the move from transcription discs and tape to digital formats, efforts to correct misdated or poorly encoded files, and its process for researching, certifying and freely distributing accurate old-time radio series.

title: Matinee Theater Audio Brief
plotSynopsis: This short series history explains that Matinee Theater grew out of Dangerous Assignment as a CBS Sunday-afternoon dramatic anthology, broadened its range from classics to biographical and contemporary stories, starred Victor Jory with rotating female leads, ran from October 1944 through April 1945, and was sponsored by the Vick Chemical Company.

title: Victor Jory Bio
plotSynopsis: A brief biography of Victor Jory traces his Yukon birth, Coast Guard boxing and wrestling background, stage and Broadway work, 1930 Hollywood debut, long film and television career, notable roles including Gone with the Wind and The Shadow, his work as a playwright, and his Hollywood Walk of Fame recognition.

title: A Sweet Scent of Mystery
plotSynopsis: A woman comes to Slade convinced that her daughter was murdered rather than lost through ordinary circumstances. His investigation follows the daughter's death and the clues surrounding the perfume associated with the case.

title: Passage to Tangiers
plotSynopsis: Two unusual clients in Morocco hire Slade to help search for a valuable treasure, sending the private investigator into a dangerous hunt through Tangiers and the Moroccan desert.

title: Pattern for a Frame
plotSynopsis: While helping a congressman investigate a racketeer and political corruption, Slade is framed for murder. With the evidence apparently airtight, he has to expose the setup while facing the police case against him.

title: The Secret Grey Man
plotSynopsis: At Morro Bay, Slade becomes involved with an old Army friend who is now working as a secret agent. A wartime vow connecting several men, danger at the 'Glass House,' and a sinking yacht pull the detective into the espionage mystery.

title: Who Killed My Penpal?
plotSynopsis: Eccentric millionaire Polly Smith sends Slade to Los Angeles to learn what happened to one of her pen pals. The search leads him to the people around the missing correspondent and into a murder case tied to the unusual correspondence.

title: A Case of Murder
plotSynopsis: The widow of a man who has been shot asks Slade to make the corpse disappear. The bizarre request puts him inside a murder case in which the people involved expect a private detective to help conceal the crime.

title: Find Julie Rayton
plotSynopsis: Slade is hired to investigate the disappearance of Julie Rayton, a pharmacist's assistant who has vanished under suspicious circumstances, and begins tracing what happened to her and why she disappeared.

title: The Incredible Dr. Lintz
plotSynopsis: Slade is kidnapped from the highway by the wife and father of a man who was executed after Slade's testimony helped convict him. The abduction forces him to confront a family that holds him responsible for the man's death.

title: Melody Ranch - I Hate to Say Goodbye 47-06-29 (1947-06-29)
sortKey: 0|1947-06-29|00028|melody ranch - i hate to say goodbye 47-06-29 (1947-06-29)
plotSynopsis: Gene opens with 'I Hate to Say Goodbye to the Prairie' and later recalls a ranch-versus-ranch rodeo competition decided by the saddle-bronc event. His draw, a paint horse later known as Skyball Paint, seems almost tame in the chute and then explodes into a violent bucking ride that throws Gene and costs his ranch the contest. Gene later acquires the horse and stages repeated attempts by skilled riders to stay aboard; after others, including the boastful Blackie, are quickly thrown, Gene finally rides the paint for eleven seconds, wins the prize money and earns the horse himself.

title: Melody Ranch - San Fernando Valley 2 48-09-19 (1948-09-19)
plotSynopsis: After singing 'San Fernando Valley,' Gene tells of going undercover in Silver City as a Ranger investigating Jake Berdyck, a powerful local criminal accused of swindling and terrorizing residents. Gene takes a job inside Berdyck's operation, watches him hide incriminating material in a safe, and summons other Rangers before trying to obtain the evidence. Berdyck's men discover Gene, but the Rangers arrive during the ensuing fight, secure enough evidence to break the organization and put Berdyck in jail. The program then returns to western music and its closing announcements.

title: Melody Ranch - Here Comes Santa Claus 48.12.21 (1948-12-21)
plotSynopsis: Gene Autry hosts a Christmas edition of Melody Ranch four days before Christmas, opening with 'Here Comes Santa Claus' and filling the broadcast with holiday music, comedy and seasonal talk. The dramatic portion centers on young Susan, who still believes in Santa Claus, and her embittered grandfather, who dismisses Christmas traditions and tries to discourage her belief. Gene and the ranch gang protect Susan's faith, and by the end her grandfather admits that he had lost something important himself and recovers enough Christmas spirit to prepare for Santa's visit.

title: Melody Ranch - Lonesomest Cowboy 2 49-09-17 (1949-09-17)
plotSynopsis: Gene opens with 'The Lonesomest Cowboy' before recalling the trial of longtime country doctor James Reardon, charged with involuntary manslaughter after operating on Clyde Martin without permission while Martin's wife was away. Gene testifies to the doctor's years of service, and medical evidence later shows that the patient's tumor was so advanced that he would have died within twenty-four hours regardless of treatment. The jury finds Reardon not guilty, and Gene closes the story with a tribute to country doctors and the sacrifices they make for their communities.

title: Melody Ranch - Ragtime Cowboy Joe 50-09-30 (1950-09-30)
plotSynopsis: Gene opens this Melody Ranch broadcast with 'Ragtime Cowboy Joe' and mixes music and comedy with a western story about old prospector Caleb Hooten, whom Gene once found panning for gold with his mule Clarence. When Caleb later disappears, Gene checks the county claims office and finds that the Sandy Creek ground has supposedly been filed by another man; because the filing is dated on the state's Admission Day holiday, when the government office would have been closed, Gene realizes the claim is fraudulent. He uses Johnny Bond and a newly filed mining claim as bait to trap the swindlers, clears up Caleb's disappearance and property fraud, and ends with more western music and the Melody Ranch signoff.

title: Melody Roundup - Dixie Cannonball 51-02-05 (1951-02-05)
plotSynopsis: This Armed Forces Radio Service Melody Roundup opens with Gene Autry singing 'Dixie Cannonball' and continues as a compact western music-and-comedy program. The cast trades jokes, performs additional songs, and turns one member's claimed twenty-third birthday into an extended comic routine and novelty birthday song about his age and lack of presents. Gene closes the musical portion with 'When the Snowbirds Cross the Rockies' before the AFRS signoff.

title: Melody Ranch - Hair of Gold 56-01-29 (1956-01-29)
plotSynopsis: Gene opens with 'Hair of Gold' and later recalls finding Pedro Chavez mortally shot in Redstone Canyon. Pedro manages to say 'Ringo,' leading Gene and Pat to the abandoned Ringo mine, where someone knocks down timbers in an attempt to trap and kill them; Champion helps bring rescuers to the site. Records show Pedro held the old mining claim, and ore samples reveal that he had discovered uranium. Gene then exposes attorney Ransom, whom Pedro had consulted about the claim, as the man who murdered Pedro to steal the mine and tried to kill Gene and Pat to hide the crime.

title: Gene Autry Interview - by Don Owens 60-07-04 (1960-07-04)
plotSynopsis: This short surviving Don Owens interview clip introduces Gene Autry as a veteran figure in country and western music. Owens notes that Autry had been making records since the late 1920s and emphasizes how his recordings crossed from the country field into popular music long before such crossover success became common. The available recording is only a brief excerpt rather than a complete interview.

title: Gene Autry Interview - by Merv Griffin 70-11-26 (1970-11-26)
plotSynopsis: Merv Griffin interviews Gene Autry and Pat Buttram about Autry's long career in western entertainment. They joke about Autry's flashy stage clothes, discuss the several horses named Champion, recall Roy Rogers and the Sons of the Pioneers, and talk about rodeo appearances and stunt work. Autry also discusses his recording success, including the extraordinary continuing sales of 'Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer,' while the conversation ranges across western performers and Hollywood trick riders.

title: Gene Autry Interview by Charles Collingwood 1960
plotSynopsis: Charles Collingwood visits Gene Autry and his wife at their North Hollywood home for an informal filmed interview. Gene discusses his Newhall ranch, his collection of Western memorabilia and the telegraph key that recalls his railroad work, and says he made roughly one hundred motion pictures plus about ninety-five half-hour television films. He remembers wanting to become a major-league ballplayer as a boy, comments on the lasting appeal and heavy production of Westerns, and, with his wife, talks about his reading habits, interest in current affairs and home life.

title: Gene Autry Interview - by Merv Griffin 1971
plotSynopsis: In this short Merv Griffin interview clip, Gene Autry discusses his ownership of the California Angels, horses and riding, and his long motion-picture career. He recalls making large numbers of films for Republic and Columbia, mentions an earlier picture with Jane Withers, says his final film work was around 1959, and notes that he had not been singing much in recent years. The conversation is an informal retrospective on his performing and business life rather than a Melody Ranch drama.

title: Gene Autry Interview - by Mike Douglas 1967
plotSynopsis: In this Mike Douglas interview, Gene Autry looks back on beginning in radio and records in 1927, becoming an early singing cowboy in motion pictures, and making his first film work in the mid-1930s. He discusses his later business interests in radio and television stations and hotels, credits railroad work with teaching him responsibility and bookkeeping, and talks about his trademark equipment and recording career. The conversation closes with the story of how his wife persuaded him to reconsider and record 'Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer,' which became a multimillion-selling hit.

title: Gene Autry Interview - by Steve Allen 1970
plotSynopsis: In this Steve Allen program excerpt, Gene Autry reminisces about the early Chicago radio world, including WLS performers, recording sessions and entertainers he knew during radio's earlier decades. The conversation ranges through memories of old broadcasting personalities and the way radio stars could be famous without being visually recognized, with Gene contributing anecdotes from his own years in the medium. It is an informal historical conversation rather than a Melody Ranch drama.

title: Melody Ranch - Be Honest with Me
plotSynopsis: Gene Autry opens this Melody Ranch broadcast with 'Be Honest With Me,' mixes songs and ranch-house banter with memories from his career, and presents a western story about rancher Mullins facing foreclosure on a $10,000 bank loan before his cattle are ready for market. Gene contacts cattle buyer Gabe Lawford and arranges an early appraisal and purchase that supplies the needed cash, then helps expose the men who were trying to force Mullins out of his ranch. The program closes with more western music, including 'Melodies from the Sky,' and the usual Melody Ranch signoff.

title: Melody Ranch - Bloom Is on the Sage 1
sortKey: 0|9999-99-99|00008|melody ranch - bloom is on the sage 1
plotSynopsis: Gene opens with 'When the Bloom Is on the Sage' and the broadcast mixes songs and ranch comedy with a domestic mix-up that begins when an old friend asks Gene to look after his sister Sally. The ranch hands eagerly expect a young woman, but the arrival instead involves a baby and turns the household upside down with arguments over who should care for the child and a later visit from relatives. The confusion is eventually straightened out, and a fresh telephone request to take care of another friend's sister produces an immediate comic refusal before the musical close.

title: Melody Ranch - Bloom Is on the Sage 2
sortKey: 0|9999-99-99|00009|melody ranch - bloom is on the sage 2
plotSynopsis: Gene opens with 'When the Bloom Is on the Sage' and later receives a letter from his friend Steve Williams asking to borrow $5,000. The letter contains a false memory of a hunting trip they never took, so Gene sends a cashier's check while investigating and discovers that another man is collecting Steve's registered mail. Steve has actually been held by Joe Conway, who gambled away money belonging to the ranch owner and forced Steve to write the request when the owner announced his return. Gene notices the deliberately capitalized words 'every,' 'six' and 'words,' reads every sixth word as a hidden message giving Steve's location, frees him and exposes Conway's scheme.

title: Melody Ranch - Bloom Is on the Sage 3
sortKey: 0|9999-99-99|00010|melody ranch - bloom is on the sage 3
plotSynopsis: This Melody Ranch broadcast mixes western music and Thanksgiving comedy with a story about a young girl who is kidnapped just before the holiday and held for a $5,000 ransom. Gene Autry studies the ransom note, follows a clue connected with a temporary diner worker, and trails a man carrying a turkey to a remote cabin on Black Bear Mountain. Gene rescues the child, who has charmed her nervous captors into telling stories and planning Thanksgiving dinner, and the program closes with a holiday-minded musical blessing.

title: Melody Ranch - Cowboy Blues
plotSynopsis: Gene opens with 'Cowboy Blues' and recounts searching for a missing man whose earlier mineral research pointed to valuable deposits in the area. At a boarding house Gene is knocked unconscious, tied and blindfolded, then hauled away in a truck, but he memorizes clues from the route and later retraces them with a local official who claims to be helping. Near the hideout that official turns a gun on Gene and reveals his own part in the scheme to obtain the missing man's mineral information. Gene survives the betrayal with help from Johnny, the conspirators are subdued, and the missing man is found tied in a back room and freed.

title: Melody Ranch - Dear Hearts and Gentle People 1
sortKey: 0|9999-99-99|00012|melody ranch - dear hearts and gentle people 1
plotSynopsis: Gene opens with 'Dear Hearts and Gentle People' before telling about elderly cowboy Billy, who insists he and his horse Dynamite can still handle a cattle drive. The younger hands tease him and Gene initially assigns him to the chuck wagon, but when a storm threatens to scatter the herd Billy rides out and helps turn the cattle. Gene and Pat later find him injured at the bottom of a draw, still more worried about Dynamite than himself. Gene offers him a permanent job, but Billy decides he has proved what he needed to prove and returns home to his wife, his garden and a quieter life.

title: Melody Ranch - Dear Heats and Gentle People 2
sortKey: 0|9999-99-99|00013|melody ranch - dear heats and gentle people 2
plotSynopsis: This Melody Ranch broadcast opens with 'Dear Hearts and Gentle People' and develops a comic family story around Mike Connors, a tough, gun-toting, quick-tempered woman whose daughter Ruth is coming to visit. Worried that Ruth will be ashamed of her, Mike lets Gene and the others coach her into acting like a refined 'lady,' producing an elaborate false persona and plenty of comedy. The deception proves unnecessary: Ruth tells Mike she is proud of her real hard-talking, gun-toting mother and loves her exactly as she is, bringing the mother and daughter together before the musical close.

title: Melody Ranch - Dixie Cannonball
plotSynopsis: Gene opens with 'Dixie Cannonball' before recalling how he took a job with Mark Gentry, a rancher being squeezed by powerful banker Red Watson and ordered to pay $10,000 almost immediately or lose his property. Gene uses his reputation with a Star City cattle buyer to obtain a $10,000 cash advance against Gentry's herd, allowing Gentry to pay the bank. When bank man Steve Nolan is later found dead, Watson's men try to frame Gentry for the killing. Gene exposes the setup by showing Watson and the sheriff knew details they should not have known, then lets a United States Marshal listening by telephone hear their admissions and arrests them.

title: Melody Ranch - Dixie Canonball 2
plotSynopsis: This Melody Ranch program opens with 'Dixie Cannonball' and comic talk about stocks, dividends and get-rich schemes before turning to a western story about ranchers whose water supply has been cut off by a privately built dam. Gene investigates the water rights and learns that a recent flood shifted the river channel onto state land, giving him a legal way to defeat the attempted water monopoly. He secures the state-land position and has the obstruction blown up, restoring the creek to the valley, before the broadcast returns to music and the closing signoff.

title: Melody Ranch - Down Yonder
plotSynopsis: Gene opens with 'Down Yonder' before the show turns to comedy about Pat's new detective ambitions and a cattle-rustling case. Rustlers burn the Hastings ranch barn as a diversion and drive off the herd; Pat's homemade camera trap photographs one of the thieves, but the local sheriff tries to seize and destroy the evidence because he is part of the racket. Gene confronts the sheriff and his accomplice, has a U.S. marshal called in, and exposes the protection scheme before the program returns to western music.

title: Melody Ranch - Down Yonder 2
plotSynopsis: After opening music and vacation comedy, Gene tells the story of a young man, Eddie, who seems to straighten out but is secretly drawn back into crime by older ex-con Riley Curtis. The pair steal an $18,000 payroll and retreat to an abandoned mine, where Riley plans to kill Gene with dynamite. Eddie turns against Riley and pulls the fuse in time to save Gene; he receives three years for his part while Curtis gets ten, and a later letter says Eddie has finally gone straight for good.

title: Melody Ranch - for Me and My Gal 2
sortKey: 0|9999-99-99|00018|melody ranch - for me and my gal 2
plotSynopsis: This Melody Ranch broadcast mixes music and comedy with a story in which Gene searches for a missing Ranger friend and follows a tip to a bar where a concertina player is connected with the disappearance. Gene is captured and learns that international crook Duvall is holding his friend while running a racket that smuggles immigrant labor into the United States with false citizenship papers and then exploits the newcomers. A woman from the group turns against Duvall because of his treatment of her people, helps arm Gene and the Ranger, and enables them to confront and overpower the smugglers for the immigration authorities.

title: Melody Ranch - Four Leaf Clover
plotSynopsis: Gene opens with 'I'm Looking Over a Four Leaf Clover' before a story about a dangerous livestock disease spreading into the cattle of Chief Silver Eagle's community. The chief rejects Gene's warning and modern veterinary methods, trusting traditional protection instead, so Gene seeks help from the chief's college-educated son Charlie. Charlie tries to bridge the two viewpoints but becomes gravely ill after eating meat from an infected steer; with a fever around 105 degrees his heart briefly stops and the medicine man believes he has died. A doctor gives Charlie an emergency injection and revives him, giving the chief direct evidence of the value of modern medicine while the broadcast returns to music.

title: Melody Ranch - Gay Ranchero
plotSynopsis: After the opening music, Gene recalls driving about 320 cattle toward a river crossing controlled by a reclusive landowner. A man claiming to be the hermit's nephew says the old man drowned, produces a will leaving him the property and suddenly demands two dollars a head to cross. Gene becomes suspicious and checks the land records, discovering that the supposed will bears a written signature even though the hermit had always signed his deed with an X because he could not write. The 'nephew' is exposed as having kidnapped the living hermit and forged the inheritance so he could profit from passing cattle herds; he ultimately receives a life sentence, and Gene gets the herd across the river.

title: Melody Ranch - Gold Cant Buy Love
plotSynopsis: After the opening song, Gene receives a coded poem from imprisoned bank robber Ben Curlin. Two criminals who intercepted the message believe it reveals where more than $60,000 in unrecovered robbery money is hidden; they let Gene work on the cipher, then seize and beat him trying to learn the answer. Gene decodes references to Halloween, an old deserted house and a substitution of the letter W for B, which points him to the well at old man Larkin's place. The criminals confront Gene and Johnny there, but are overpowered, the hidden money is recovered from the well, and the men are taken to the sheriff.

title: Melody Ranch - Heart as Big as Texas 2
sortKey: 0|9999-99-99|00023|melody ranch - heart as big as texas 2
plotSynopsis: Gene opens with 'Heart as Big as Texas' before becoming involved in a train holdup that local officials intended as a staged frontier stunt for visitors. The joke turns real when live ammunition appears, a man is killed and rodeo treasurer Finley loses a satchel containing $10,000 in prize money. Gene traces the switch to conductor George Davis, who knew Finley would be carrying the cash, positioned himself beside him to identify the target and signaled the engineer to slow the train early so two real masked robbers could board under cover of the planned fake holdup. Gene confronts Davis with the stolen money and disarms him by bluffing about the loads in his own shooting-act guns, exposing the inside job.

title: Melody Ranch - Heart as Big as Texas 50.09.
sortKey: 0|9999-99-99|00024|melody ranch - heart as big as texas 50.09.
plotSynopsis: Gene opens with 'Heart as Big as Texas' before taking responsibility for a troubled youth named Mike who otherwise faces reform school. Gene gives him work, a room and increasing trust, and after weeks of resistance Mike begins to respond. Gene then deliberately entrusts him with $50 as a test. Mike runs away, buys a railroad ticket toward Capital City, but changes his mind at Silver Springs and walks back to the ranch with the unused money. Gene tells him that returning was the proof he needed and closes the story by invoking Kipling's 'If' as a lesson in becoming a man.

title: Melody Ranch - Honey Im in Love with You
sortKey: 0|9999-99-99|00026|melody ranch - honey im in love with you
plotSynopsis: The broadcast opens with 'Honey, I'm in Love with You' and then tells a western crime story about a robbery gang that repeatedly seems to vanish after each job. A marked bill from the Red River payroll robbery leads Gene and the sheriff to former ranch hand Joe Fallon, and a later Sagebrush robbery sends Gene following fresh wheel tracks to a hiding place near the river. There he discovers the gang's trick: it is essentially a man-and-woman team, with the woman disguising herself as a harmless grandmother while they change from horseback escape to a buckboard. Gene captures the pair, ending their disappearing act, and the show closes with more cowboy music.

title: Melody Ranch - Hot Digidy Final Show
plotSynopsis: This is the farewell Melody Ranch broadcast, with the cast mixing familiar songs and comedy with tributes to Gene Autry as he retires from the regular radio series. Gene reflects on the performers who became stars in their own right, thanks the Melody Ranch family for their loyalty, and recalls nearly seventeen years of radio broadcasts and the fans who kept the program going. The company closes with affectionate farewells, western standards including 'Home on the Range,' and a final 'Back in the Saddle Again' signoff.

title: Melody Ranch - I Tipped My Hat 1St Half 1949
sortKey: 0|9999-99-99|00029|melody ranch - i tipped my hat 1st half 1949
plotSynopsis: This surviving first-half fragment opens with Gene Autry singing 'I Tipped My Hat and Slowly Rode Away.' The recording then moves through Doublemint advertising and light ranch-house comedy, including Pat Buttram joking about an embarrassing name mix-up, before another chewing-gum commercial. The available audio ends during this early portion rather than preserving a complete dramatic story.

title: Melody Ranch - Idaho
plotSynopsis: Following the opening song 'Idaho,' Gene investigates why cattle on young Betty Carson's ranch are mysteriously dying. Dead grass beside the ranch's salt blocks leads to laboratory tests showing that the blocks were poisoned with arsenic made tasteless in the salt. Gene discovers that Betty's guardian, Uncle Dan Carson, has been pretending to be crippled; he is poisoning the herd to force a sale before Betty turns twenty-one because a new railroad spur will make the property highly valuable. A distinctive footprint from Dan's leg brace helps expose the deception, and his attempt to silence Gene and Betty ends with him being taken for prosecution.

title: Melody Ranch - Im an Old Cowhand 1
plotSynopsis: Gene opens with 'I'm an Old Cowhand' and later finds a runaway boy named Joe who says he wants to become a cowboy. Joe admits that his parents are always busy and that his father never seems to have time for him, so Gene gives him shelter while quietly learning enough to contact the family. Joe's parents come to the ranch, recognize how neglected he has felt and promise him more time and attention, and Gene reunites them. A later letter reports that the family is doing well and that Joe, now older and still visiting Gene, is about to begin high school.

title: Melody Ranch - Im an Old Cowhand 2
plotSynopsis: After 'I'm an Old Cowhand,' Gene tells of hiring a huge ranch hand calling himself Bill Collins and discovering that he is former strongman Moose Mallory. When a utility-company safe containing $15,000 is carried off, Moose disappears and later returns to surrender, but Gene suspects another person is behind the crime. A hidden letter leads him to Moose's former manager, who has blackmailed Moose for years by threatening to accuse him of deliberately killing boxer Billy Garcia in a bout that was actually accidental. Gene forces the blackmailer to admit the scheme, clearing up why Moose committed the robbery under pressure.

title: Melody Ranch - Ive Got Spurs
plotSynopsis: Gene opens with 'I've Got Spurs' before the program moves into a western mystery in which he is framed for the shooting death of Art Richards. A gun connected to Gene and an earlier boundary dispute make him the obvious suspect, but a sympathetic sheriff gives him a chance to investigate; at Richards's ranch Gene finds a torn railroad ticket showing that Art's brother Sam had secretly traveled from Rock Springs just before the killing. Gene then uses Art's personal effects in a bluff that makes Sam reveal knowledge only the killer should possess, leading to Sam's confession and Gene's exoneration. Music and a requested western number for a serviceman in Japan round out the broadcast.

title: Melody Ranch - Lonesomest Cowboy 1
plotSynopsis: Gene sings the cowboy blues before recounting a case in which criminals disguise themselves as Native Americans to frame Chief Whitebird's people for robberies. After a stolen bracelet is planted at a murder scene, one of the chief's men is arrested and local hostility rises. Gene recognizes the setup, organizes watchers around town, and catches the disguised criminals during a bank robbery, exposing one supposed Indian as a blond white man and clearing the tribe of the crimes.

title: Melody Ranch - Lonesomest Cowboy 3
plotSynopsis: After the opening cowboy song, Gene recounts searching for a missing man whose earlier mineral research pointed to valuable deposits in the area. At a boarding house Gene is knocked unconscious, tied and blindfolded, then hauled away in a truck, but he memorizes clues from the route and later retraces them with a local official who claims to be helping. Near the hideout that official turns a gun on Gene and reveals his own part in the scheme to obtain the missing man's mineral information. Gene survives the betrayal with help from Johnny, the conspirators are subdued, and the missing man is found tied in a back room and freed.

title: Melody Ranch - Memories
plotSynopsis: After opening with songs about memories, Gene tells a stormy-weather story that begins when a single-engine airplane crashes near Melody Ranch and the pilot disappears. The aircraft is tied to a Central City bank robbery in which $50,000 and securities were taken and a guard was killed, so Gene, Pat and Sheriff Dillon organize a large search through the rain-soaked hills. Gene eventually confronts and subdues the fugitive robber, and the story ends with the storm breaking and a rainbow appearing before the broadcast returns to western music.

title: Melody Ranch - My Adobe Hacienda
plotSynopsis: The broadcast opens with 'My Adobe Hacienda' and develops into a ranch story in which a young woman becomes involved with Johnny and then warns Gene that cattle rustlers are planning to hit the herd. Gene prepares a reception for the thieves, but the arriving 'sheriff' and his men are themselves part of the rustling outfit. Gene recognizes the impostor because he already knows details only someone who had inspected the night herd could know, turns the trap on the criminals, and exposes the woman as their inside accomplice before the program returns to music.

title: Melody Ranch - Old Fashioned Hoedown
plotSynopsis: Gene opens with 'Old Fashioned Hoedown' before telling how, as treasurer of the Cattlemen's Association, he was carrying about $3,500 in livestock-show receipts to the bank when two masked men robbed him and one shot him. A quick body movement turns the shot into a flesh wound, and despite the injury Gene follows a fresh torn matchbook clue left after a rainstorm to trace the robbers. At the final confrontation he uses a gun concealed in the sling on his wounded arm to surprise and capture the men, recovering from the holdup before the broadcast returns to music.

title: Melody Ranch - Old Fashioned Hoedown Copy 2
plotSynopsis: Gene opens with 'Old Fashioned Hoedown' before telling how, as treasurer of the Cattlemen's Association, he was carrying about $3,500 in livestock-show receipts to the bank when two masked men robbed him and one shot him. A quick body movement turns the shot into a flesh wound, and despite the injury Gene follows a fresh torn matchbook clue left after a rainstorm to trace the robbers. At the final confrontation he uses a gun concealed in the sling on his wounded arm to surprise and capture the men, recovering from the holdup before the broadcast returns to music.

title: Melody Ranch - Old Time Religion 1
plotSynopsis: Gene opens with 'Old Time Religion' before a story about ranchers being squeezed by Cody Bennett, who controls a crucial water source and charges excessive prices. Gene pretends to join Bennett, dams his own stream and deliberately makes friends think he has betrayed them so Bennett will trust him. After learning Bennett is tied to the suspicious death of former landowner Larkin, Gene uses a staged newspaper front page and a hidden sheriff to convince Bennett that another witness has been silenced. Feeling safe, Bennett boasts that he killed Larkin with a crowbar and fabricated a family relationship with a phony birth certificate to inherit the property, giving the sheriff the confession needed to arrest him.

title: Melody Ranch - Old Time Religion 2
plotSynopsis: Gene opens with 'Old Time Religion' before retelling the case of country doctor James Reardon, charged with manslaughter after operating on Clyde Martin without permission from the patient's absent family and losing him during surgery. Gene testifies to Reardon's years of selfless service, while medical evidence establishes that Martin's tumor was so advanced he would have died within about twenty-four hours regardless and that surgery was his only chance. The jury returns a not-guilty verdict, allowing Reardon to return to his practice, and Gene closes with a tribute to country doctors and more music.

title: Melody Ranch - Old Time Religion 3
plotSynopsis: Gene opens with 'Old Time Religion' before recalling a ranch job where he and Johnny share quarters with an abrasive hand named Brant. After Brant notices the ranch payroll being placed in owner Jeff Marlow's bedroom safe, Marlow is shot dead and the payroll disappears; Brant vanishes, leaving his pocket knife by the empty cash box. Gene tracks him to Mother Miller's cabin, where Brant is holding Miller at gunpoint. Gene realizes Brant is there because Miller claims he has just read a letter from his daughter, even though Gene knows Miller cannot read or write. Gene and Miller overpower Brant and take him in for the murder and robbery.

title: Melody Ranch - Ridin to Tennessee
plotSynopsis: Gene opens with 'Ridin' to Tennessee' and a reminiscence about western travel before telling how neighboring ranchers Charlie Clayton and Clem Carter nearly turn a simple accident into a feud. A broken fence mixes more than 300 cattle carrying identical brands, leaving the men unable to separate their herds and increasingly angry over ownership. Each ultimately gives his share to his child, only to learn that Bert and Sara have already been secretly married for a month, making the mixed herd their joint property and ending the quarrel. The older men return to settling their unfinished checker match instead.

title: Melody Ranch - San Antonio Rose 1954
plotSynopsis: After 'San Antonio Rose,' Gene joins former sheriff Tom Dillon in investigating a truck and trailer heard carrying foreign passengers near the border. The new sheriff, Miller, dismisses the concern but receives a coded telephone message; Gene verifies the call, deciphers the numbers as a route, junction, date and time, and stakes out the rendezvous. There he and Tom catch Miller and his partners collecting money for another group of people being smuggled into the country, with the passengers themselves providing the evidence. Miller is arrested and Tom Dillon returns to the sheriff's office.

title: Melody Ranch - San Fernando Valley 1
plotSynopsis: Gene sings 'San Fernando Valley' and then tells the story of how he came to own Champion. He takes on a difficult, nearly unrideable horse and gradually wins enough trust to ride him, only for the animal to disappear with other horses soon afterward. Gene follows the trail through wild-horse country and uncovers a horse-stealing scheme, confronts the thief and recovers the animal. He closes by explaining that Champion never left his side after that and, though older now, remained one of his closest companions.

title: Melody Ranch - Shes My Sunflower
plotSynopsis: After Gene sings 'She's My Sunflower,' cattle losses and an advertisement from a supposed eastern syndicate offering to buy local ranches create panic among area ranchers. Gene's investigation leads toward a poisoned-water scheme and a false trail meant to implicate another man. He takes assayer Frank Parker across the desert, then tricks him with ordinary water by claiming it came from the poisoned spring; Parker's panic makes him confess that he put the poison there. Ed Thompson, Parker's boss and head of the cattlemen's association, is exposed as the man behind the scheme, which was intended to weaken the ranchers and push them toward selling, and both men are headed for jail.

title: Melody Ranch - Sioux City Sue 1954
plotSynopsis: Gene opens with 'Sioux City Sue' before a cattle-drive story in which Johnny is lured into a roulette game by Maisie at the Silver Dollar and unwittingly reveals where the herd is camped. Maisie later warns that rustlers plan to scatter the herd and offers to fetch the sheriff, but the arriving 'Sheriff Jenkins' and his men are themselves part of the rustling gang. Gene catches the fraud when the supposed sheriff already knows there are exactly three cowboys riding the night herd, information he could know only by scouting the camp. Gene disarms the impostors, sends for the real sheriff and captures Maisie when she returns, exposing her as the gang's inside contact.

title: Melody Ranch - South of the Border 12Th Anniversary Show
sortKey: 0|9999-99-99|00051|melody ranch - south of the border 12th anniversary show
plotSynopsis: This twelfth-anniversary Melody Ranch broadcast looks back over Gene Autry's years on the program through songs, memories and comedy. Gene, Pat Buttram and the cast revisit popular numbers and career moments from 1939 through the late 1940s and into 1950, including songs associated with Autry's films and major hits such as 'Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer.' Rather than presenting a western drama, the show functions as an anniversary retrospective and musical survey of the program's past twelve years.

title: Melody Ranch - Teardrops from My Eyes 1
plotSynopsis: The broadcast opens with 'Teardrops From My Eyes' and comic banter about Pat's hopeless budgeting before turning to a cattle-rustling story. Pat rigs a homemade camera trap to photograph whoever is stealing stock and finds a matchbook clue pointing toward Waverly; Gene follows the trail and discovers that the local sheriff is part of the rustling racket. When the sheriff tries to buy Gene off with a share of the operation, Gene has a U.S. marshal listening by telephone and uses the attempted bribe to expose the scheme. The show closes with additional western music and its regular signoff.

title: Melody Ranch - Teardrops from My Eyes 2
plotSynopsis: The broadcast opens with 'Teardrops From My Eyes' before Gene recalls working as a deputy U.S. marshal on a border-smuggling case involving stolen X25 medicine. The ring moves the drug into Mexico and gradually dilutes it for black-market sale, while corrupt insiders arrange for small packages to be hidden beneath Gene's own saddle so he will unknowingly carry them across the border. Gene recognizes that supposedly secret information about his contacts could only have come from inside the investigation, turns the scheme back on the conspirators, and exposes the local collaborator who then tries to kill him before being captured.

title: Melody Ranch - Till 1
plotSynopsis: This Melody Ranch broadcast opens with 'Till' and later tells a crime story about robbers who repeatedly vanish along Ridge Rock Road after striking businesses in town. Gene and the sheriff canvass the ranches, then use a townwide stakeout and Champion's speed to follow the bandits after another robbery. The trail leads to the supposed home of elderly Grandma Brian, where Gene uncovers the trick: one member of the gang is using an old-woman disguise and the hideout to change appearance and escape pursuit. Gene captures the pair and the show closes with more western music.

title: Melody Ranch - Till 2
plotSynopsis: The program opens with 'Till' and develops into a story about a scheme to steal Champion. A supporting ranch hand is lured by a forged letter into what looks like a friendly card game with professional crooks and loses Gene's horse as the stake. Gene checks with the supposed sender, learns no letter was ever written, and realizes the whole game was arranged to get Champion. The thieves leave their hotel and move the horse by rail in a numbered stock car, but Gene follows the transportation trail, exposes the frame-up and recovers Champion before the musical close.

title: Melody Ranch - Tweedle O Twill
plotSynopsis: This Melody Ranch broadcast mixes music and comedy with the story of Ben Carter, the son of a late minister who had expected him to continue the unfinished church and ministry. Bitter that his father gave everything to others and died leaving debts, Ben decides to abandon the church and leave town. A robber named Rocky Sims later forces Ben to hide him and a bag containing about $5,000 stolen from a local exchange; after Sims is killed, the money remains missing and Gene realizes Ben knows where it is. Gene reminds him of his father's favorite warning about gaining the world and losing one's soul, and by Sunday Ben has changed course and is in the pulpit preaching from his father's scripture instead of running away with the money.

title: Melody Ranch - When Payday Rolls Around
plotSynopsis: Gene opens with 'When Payday Rolls Around' and then gets caught between neighboring ranchers Buck Dean and Miss Hawkins, whose long-running feud involves survey lines, a barn, a concrete feed lot and access to water. Each has used property boundaries to get even with the other, and a dry spell makes the dispute more serious when Hawkins needs water for her ranch. Gene maneuvers the situation so Buck sees that continuing the feud will only cost both of them more. Buck finally offers her all the water she needs if she will stop trying to make him move his barn again; Hawkins accepts, the two call a truce, and the program returns to music with the quarrel finally settled.

title: Melody Ranch - When Youre Smiling
plotSynopsis: After opening with 'When You're Smiling,' Gene tells of Aunt Martha's plan to build a boys' ranch in memory of her late husband, born Gus Salvatore and later known as Alexander Haynes, who had grown up poor and without parents. Martha knows she has only about a year to live and is determined to finish the ranch in time, so Gene rallies roughly fifteen men to help the carpenters complete the work. The final board is nailed in place on January 10 and the ranch is dedicated the next day. Martha dies on January 13, exactly a year after receiving her prognosis, but the finished ranch continues giving hundreds of boys the better chance she and her husband wanted for them.

title: Melody Roundup - Old Fashioned Hoedown
plotSynopsis: This Melody Roundup recording is a compact western music-and-comedy program rather than a dramatic episode. Gene Autry opens with 'Old Fashioned Hoedown,' the cast trades light banter, and the musical set includes trail and cowboy numbers such as 'Come a Ti Yi Yippee Yi Yay,' 'That's My Home' and a closing song about the trail at twilight. The program ends with the regular roundup invitation and signoff.

title: Melody Roundup - Sunny Side of the Rockies
sortKey: 0|9999-99-99|00061|melody roundup - sunny side of the rockies
plotSynopsis: This Armed Forces Radio Service Melody Roundup opens with Gene Autry singing 'On the Sunny Side of the Rockies' and stays focused on western music and comedy rather than a dramatic story. A comic guest spins exaggerated tales about his big-city adventures, including cars on sidewalks, a circus target job and an enormous ranch whose cattle he jokes are counted by their feet. The musical program continues through novelty and sentimental numbers including 'Carolina Moon' and 'My Adobe Hacienda' before the AFRS signoff.

title: Melody Roundup - When Payday Rolls Around
plotSynopsis: This Armed Forces Radio Service Melody Roundup opens with Gene Autry singing 'When Payday Rolls Around' after the troupe's return home from a nine-week trip. The program is built around western songs and comedy rather than a dramatic story, including an extended routine in which Johnny is taught to drive and creates chaos with the car. The broadcast continues with more music, jokes and a cowboy-classic segment before the AFRS signoff.

title: Melody Roundup - You Stole My Heart
plotSynopsis: This Melody Roundup broadcast opens with Gene Autry singing 'You Stole My Heart' and combines western and popular songs with comedy from the supporting cast. A major comic routine has one performer boast that he took part in the California Gold Rush of 1849, producing a string of deliberate impossibilities and anachronisms as the others puncture his tall tale. Gene later sings 'South of the Border,' and the program closes with an Armed Forces Radio Service signoff.

title: Return to Huxley (1946-11-05)
plotSynopsis: Huxley College quietly hires Shayne after a series of frightening incidents targeting female students, hoping to avoid scandal. When Agnes is murdered with football laces, evidence points toward football player Gill Packard, but Shayne notices that brilliant student Quincy Baldwin is always too conveniently helpful. A second attack using tennis strings exposes Quincy, who admits he staged the crimes and murders as a psychological experiment to prove his superiority and manipulate everyone around him.

title: The Case Of The Judge Is Shot (1947-10-14)
sortKey: 0|1947-10-14|99999|the case of the judge is shot 1947 10 14
plotSynopsis: Judge Storman secretly summons Shayne, then a murder investigation spreads through the judge's political circle as people connected to an old enemy named Winters begin dying. Shayne discovers the supposedly finished Winters affair is still driving the killings and that the murderer has been living behind another identity; a failure to disguise his handwriting helps expose him before he can complete the revenge campaign against Estelle.

title: Case Of Anthony Carrell (1948-07-15)
plotSynopsis: Shayne investigates a New Orleans family terrified of Anthony Carrell, a legendary voodoo figure said to have survived since the early nineteenth century and to destroy anyone who defies him. Members of the Carrell clan kill to preserve the fear, but when Shayne fights his way into the room where the immortal man is supposedly hidden he finds it empty, proving the family has kept a dead man's legend alive for generations as a weapon of control. This earlier dated recording is preserved separately from the later Man Who Lived Forever version.

title: Case Of The Blood Stained Pearls (1948-07-29)
plotSynopsis: A frightened old sailor and a trail of violence pull Shayne into the hunt for a bag of legendary pearls believed to be worth a fortune. After murder and repeated attacks, Shayne traps the killer by pretending to throw the jewels into a fire; the desperate attempt to save them exposes the man who killed for the treasure. Shayne had substituted fake pearls before the test, leaving the real historic jewels intact for a museum.

title: Case Of The Phantom Gun (1948-08-06)
plotSynopsis: A woman hires Shayne to learn why her husband Dick Kenny is staying out at night, but the trail leads to blackmail rather than another woman. Kenny is murdered and ballistics point to Shayne's own gun even though it was traveling through the mail; Shayne proves the bullets were first fired through his gun and then reused through a larger smooth bore, exposing Jasper and Judith de Vaal's blackmail-and-murder conspiracy. This original dated recording is preserved separately from the later 1949 version.

title: Case Of The Hate That Killed (1948-08-13)
plotSynopsis: Shayne is drawn into a family poisoned by years of hatred after Mark Sanderson becomes convinced someone is trying to kill him. Deaths and poisoned brandy point back to patriarch Gregory Lawson, whose malice was arranged to keep reaching his heirs even after his own death, while lawyer Holmesby knows the will leaves him everything if the family is wiped out and tries to keep Shayne from disturbing the plan. Fingerprint evidence on the poisoned containers finally breaks the scheme.

title: The Case of the Grey Eyed Blonde (1948-08-20)
sortKey: 0|1948-08-20|00009|the case of the grey eyed blonde 1948 08 20
plotSynopsis: Grey-eyed Helen hires Shayne to make what she calls a final blackmail payment, but the errand is a frame: Shayne is shot and wakes up accused of a $62,000 robbery with only hours to clear himself. He tracks Helen through a hotel and a planned midnight flight to Havana, uncovering her partnership with Frank in the robbery and her plan to run away with the money; when Shayne exposes that betrayal, Frank turns his gun on Helen and the scheme collapses in the ensuing struggle.

title: The Case Of The Generous Killer (1948-09-04)
plotSynopsis: A mysterious passenger from the Star of Bermuda sends Shayne a $100 bill through an intermediary, beginning a chain of unusually generous payments, stolen identification and murder. The man first believed to be Victor Groz is not Groz at all, and the real Groz begins eliminating people who can expose the identity switch. Shayne survives the setup and finally catches Groz after the killer tries to close the last loose end while moving in disguise.

title: Model Murder (1948-09-11)
plotSynopsis: Jonathan Franklin hires Shayne to find runaway heiress Mary Ann Shevney before her twenty-fifth birthday, when she is due to inherit eight million dollars. Shayne follows her trail from a modeling agency to New York and discovers Franklin has arranged for a killer to follow him, locate Mary Ann through his investigation and murder her before she can claim the inheritance. This original dated recording is preserved separately from the later 1949 version.

title: Pursuit Of Death (1948-09-18)
plotSynopsis: Shayne meets Shirley after she nearly walks into traffic and becomes convinced someone is stalking and trying to kill her. Threatening incidents and suspicious people seem to support her fear, but the pattern eventually reveals a mind turning against itself: Shirley murdered her husband Stanley, strangling him with a gold mesh necklace and hiding his body near the Mississippi, then repressed the crime until guilt broke through as a terrifying persecution delusion.

title: The Crooked Wheel (1948-09-25)
plotSynopsis: Mexico City casino owner RamÃ³n Pachito hires Shayne to learn who is repeatedly beating his roulette tables. Shayne uncovers a crooked-wheel scheme built around a manipulated ball, with casino employee Mark Hagan and Gabby able to steer winning numbers; the racket turns murderous when Gabby joins Hugo and Drool in a double-cross, leaving Shayne to survive the gunplay and expose the rigged operation.

title: Wandering Fingerprints (1948-10-02)
plotSynopsis: Inventor Ziegler claims he can transfer fingerprints and tries to force Shayne into a blackmail racket by planting Shayneâ€™s prints at a robbery scene. He boasts that he framed accused murderer Al Metcalf the same way, but Shayneâ€™s investigation shows Metcalf really is guilty and exposes Zieglerâ€™s supposed fingerprint transfer as a trick using planted objects and stolen prints, turning the scheme back on its creator.

title: Case of the Purloined Corpse (1948-10-09)
plotSynopsis: Wealthy, widely hated Josiah DeLacey hires Shayne after the corpse of his supposedly dead son Ezekiel disappears from Cypress Grove Cemetery. The search leads through DeLacey's home for homeless girls, another murdered body and the deaths of people protecting family secrets; Shayne finally learns Ezekiel was alive and killed his father to get the inheritance, while Cleo and Penelope moved Josiah's body into their own vault and Penelope sent the ransom note as part of the deception.

title: Case Of The Left Handed Fan (1948-10-16)
plotSynopsis: Actress Christina Bancroft hires Shayne after a campaign of threats leaves her frightened and surrounded by jealous admirers. When Frank Harper, the man she loves, is murdered backstage, Christina gives Shayne a false clue about a ring on the killerâ€™s left hand; the clean murder weapon proves that story impossible, and Shayne forces her to admit she killed Frank out of jealousy when she believed he loved another woman.

title: Deadly Dough (1948-10-23)
plotSynopsis: A nervous waterfront character hires Shayne to move a suitcase from a station locker, using him as a decoy in a hunt for money from an old bank robbery. Ex-con Dan Bascom, former accomplice Ed Ferris and others threaten and double-cross one another over the missing $100,000, but when the real suitcase is finally recovered the cash is in obsolete large-size bills from 1931, making the deadly fortune almost impossible to spend.

title: Case Of The Popular Corpse (1948-10-30)
plotSynopsis: Clarissa Howard hires Shayne to find her missing niece Joan Lawson, but other men are hunting Joan too and the case becomes a contest of tails, threats and false identities. Shayne eventually proves Clarissa has been stealing from Joanâ€™s estate and killed her when Joan discovered the theft, then hired another woman to pose as Joan and confuse the investigation.

title: Case of the Bayou Monster (1948-11-06)
plotSynopsis: Shayne is hired to stay at the Forsythe family estate in the bayou, where an old legend says a werewolf-like creature kills one member of each generation. After a dog is torn apart and the creature attacks, Shayne exposes the monster as Paul Forsythe wearing a hidden family mask and iron claws; Paul revived the legend so he could kill his wife Amy, gain control of her fortune and free himself from a marriage he hated.

title: Case Of A Problem in Murder (1948-11-13)
plotSynopsis: Shayne is drawn to a rain-soaked house and a missing $50,000 while Inspector LaFever is investigating a man believed to be Frank Carter. After run-ins with Carterâ€™s partners Diana and Caesar, Shayne realizes the client calling himself Barrington is actually Carter, who murdered the real Barrington, switched identities and tried to take the money for himself while cutting his partners out.

title: The Case Of The High Priced Twins (1948-11-20)
sortKey: 0|1948-11-20|00021|the case of the high priced twins 1948 11 20
plotSynopsis: Linda Oldham and estate manager Arthur Jeffrey hire Shayne to find the Bronig Twins, two rare coins supposedly worth $35,000 that vanished with her uncle's secretary Wilkerson. Shayne recovers the coins after Wilkerson is murdered, only to learn they are worthless; the real inheritance clue is written in white ink beneath the lining of their red leather case and points to a safe-deposit key, while Jeffrey's attempt to seize that secret exposes his role in the theft and murder.

title: The Case Of The Carnival Killer (1948-11-27)
plotSynopsis: A carnival dancer named Diane secretly hires Shayne, but he soon finds a young woman believed to be Diane strangled. At the carnival he discovers Diane has a twin sister, turning the murder into an identity puzzle among the performers. Shayne ultimately exposes fortune teller Carlotta, whose jealousy over Jimmy drove the attack; the twins' resemblance caused her first murderous move to strike the wrong sister, and she keeps killing once she realizes the mistake.

title: Constant Companion (1948-12-04)
plotSynopsis: A nervous little man called Shorty hires Shayne to hide him and help locate Big Ed Lasky, only for Shayne to discover Shorty is an escaped prisoner wanted for murder. Shorty insists he was framed and wants Laskyâ€™s confession; Shayne eventually hears Lasky admit the setup, clearing Shorty, but must stop the exhausted fugitive from turning vindication into revenge murder.

title: The Eager Victim (1948-12-09)
plotSynopsis: Claude Janik offers Shayne $1,000 to kill him and leaves a statement absolving the detective, but Janik later turns up murdered with the same gun and Shayne's fingerprints on it. Shayne learns the office visitor was an impostor who used the bizarre suicide offer to put Shayne's prints on the weapon, then killed the real Janik with an accomplice after securing a cash settlement, creating a frame that nearly sends Shayne down for murder.

title: Borrowed Heirloom (1948-12-11)
plotSynopsis: Clarence Drake hires Shayne to protect a hidden collection of jewelry he claims his late first wife bought as family heirlooms, even though he is now nearly broke. Shayne learns the story is backwards: Drake is a compulsive thief, his first wife spent her money keeping him out of trouble, and the jewels were stolen merchandise she had asked a friend to return. Drake turns violent when the truth comes out, and the jewelry is ultimately sent back to its rightful owners.

title: The Corresponding Corpse (1948-12-16)
plotSynopsis: A Havana businessman hires Shayne after receiving an urgent letter from his friend Julian, even though everyone in New Orleans insists Julian died two years earlier. Shayne uncovers a blackmail scheme in which Val Dain has been imitating Julianâ€™s handwriting, while the client himself admits he killed the real Julian years before; the confrontation ends with Val Dain shot and Shayne stopping the client before another murder.

title: The Mail Order Murders (1948-12-23)
plotSynopsis: William Kinsella hires Shayne after receiving a mailed death list naming himself and three other people. As names on the list begin dying, Shayne traces all four to a past murder and theft on Capri and discovers Kinsella was the killer they hired and then cheated; he placed his own name on the list to deflect suspicion while hunting down the people who double-crossed him.

title: The Phantom Neighbor (1948-12-30)
plotSynopsis: Anne Griffin wakes Shayne with a late-night call claiming she has killed a man, and soon becomes the prime suspect in gambler Lyle Metcalfâ€™s murder. Shayne follows the gambling connections and a witness who tries to exploit what he saw, then proves Anneâ€™s boyfriend Harris crossed an air shaft into Metcalfâ€™s apartment, committed the murder, knocked Anne unconscious and planted the gun in her hand to frame her.

plotSynopsis: In Miami, Shayne is pulled into an investigation of heroin being pushed to high-school students and the violence surrounding the narcotics trade. The trail leads through a candy-store connection to dealer Rosiella and addicted teenager Ralph, whose dependence has already brought his family tragedy; Shayne finally gets Ralph to turn against the dealer and helps break the ring while the boy faces the difficult work of escaping his addiction.
