title: Number 13 (1950-03-06)
plotSynopsis: Randy Stone is held up by an elderly former professor, then discovers the man is trying to prove a roulette system with borrowed money. The system builds a fortune, but after the professor dies his wife carries out one final promised bet and loses it all when the wheel lands on number 13, ending the obsession that had consumed him.

title: Old Blind Pop (1950-08-07)
plotSynopsis: Randy befriends a blind street musician who has spent years avoiding his daughter Vicki while pretending he is still successful. Vicki has been writing home with a lie of her own, claiming a glamorous ballet career, and Randy brings father and daughter together so both can finally admit the truth and discover that neither failure nor disability has changed their love for each other.

title: Gunner's Last Fight (1950-08-14)
plotSynopsis: Randy tries to help boxer Gunner Evans after gamblers rough him up for refusing to throw a fight. The pressure becomes more dangerous when Randy discovers that Gunner's own wife is working with the men trying to control the bout.

title: Doctor's Secret (1950-08-21)
plotSynopsis: Sent to Joliet to cover an execution, Randy meets Dr. Graham, an alcoholic physician whose son is about to die in the electric chair. Graham's tortured behavior convinces Randy that the doctor carries a deeper guilt connected to the crime, and Randy pushes toward the secret before the execution becomes irreversible.

title: Old Home Week (1950-09-04)
plotSynopsis: On a short vacation at Paradise Lake, Randy rescues Pat Torrance from the water and immediately suspects there is more to her apparent drowning. His attempt to sort out what happened puts him in the middle of a bitter tangle involving a husband, an ex-wife and former girlfriends with motives of their own.

title: The Hunter Becomes the Hunted (1950-09-11)
plotSynopsis: Escaped condemned prisoner John Galt kidnaps Randy and the district attorney who prosecuted him, insisting that he was wrongly convicted. Rather than simply fleeing, Galt forces the two men into his desperate attempt to uncover the evidence he believes can prove his innocence before the law catches up with him again.

title: Wanna Buy a Story (1950-09-18)
plotSynopsis: A frightened young woman named Mary Callahan offers Randy information about the murder of notorious gambler Marty Crain, but demands five hundred dollars for the story. Randy refuses to buy news, then follows her lead anyway and uncovers the hatred, revenge and manipulation behind both the murder and Mary's attempt to sell its secret.

title: A Case of Butter (1950-09-25)
plotSynopsis: Randy learns that a large shipment of butter may be contaminated with typhoid and has already entered distribution. With public health at stake, he races to trace the dangerous shipment before more people can eat it and become ill.

title: The Kenny Day Amnesia Case (1950-10-06)
plotSynopsis: Randy meets an injured, confused Kenny Day, whose memory has stopped years in the past. Clues in Kennyâ€™s wallet and a matchbook lead Randy to the life Kenny has forgotten, including his pregnant wife, and a desperate race through a house fire ends at the hospital where Kenny learns both his wife and newborn son are safe.

title: Einar Pierce (1950-10-13)
plotSynopsis: While vacationing near Duluth, Randy is drawn into the hunt for escaped prisoner Einar Pierce and discovers that an entire community is helping hide him. Their purpose is not to free Einar permanently, but to give his dying mother and family one last chance to see him before he voluntarily walks out to the waiting police.

title: The Doctor's Daughter (1950-10-27)
plotSynopsis: Jerry Karn has been shot in the head and will die unless a skilled brain surgeon operates, but the surgeon refuses to save him. Randy discovers that Jerry was in love with the doctor's daughter and digs into the family history behind the refusal while trying to get the operation performed before it is too late.

title: The Black Cat (1950-11-03)
plotSynopsis: On a rainy night Randy investigates the killing of Nick Corby in a rundown neighborhood where suspicion quickly centers on a strange black cat and the eccentric people around it. He has to separate superstition and neighborhood fear from the human motive behind Corby's death.

title: The Slasher (1950-11-10)
plotSynopsis: A knife attacker known as the Slasher is terrorizing women across Chicago. Randy Stone follows the clues toward artist Rick Bennett, whose unsettling interest in women with scars makes him a prime suspect as Randy tries to stop another attack.

title: Big John Mc Masters (1951-03-04)
plotSynopsis: Former Prohibition gangster Big John McMasters is released from prison and is soon shot, pulling Randy into the old man's hidden past. Randy uncovers blackmail, loyalty and family secrets, then decides that telling the whole story in print would hurt innocent people more than it would serve the truth.

title: Juke Box Romance (1951-05-18)
plotSynopsis: Randy investigates an unusual romance involving a dwarf newsdealer and Julie, a woman who works as a live operator for a wired jukebox service. A store robbery pulls their strange courtship into Randy's night beat and reveals that the romance is tied to more than music requests.

title: Fear (1951-05-25)
plotSynopsis: Randy receives an anonymous threatening letter and gradually becomes convinced that someone intends to kill him. As fear begins shaping how he sees every encounter, he has to identify the source of the threat before panic makes him an easier target.

title: Will of Mrs Orloff (1951-06-01)
plotSynopsis: After poor scrubwoman Martha Orloff dies, Randy discovers that she left behind a bankbook containing fifty thousand dollars. His search for Stanley Orloff turns a routine obituary into a mystery about where the money came from and who is entitled to it.

title: The Search for Fred (1951-06-08)
plotSynopsis: Randy must find a man named Fred after learning that he has been bitten by a rabid dog without realizing the danger. The search becomes a race against time because Fred needs treatment before the infection can become fatal.

title: Sanctuary (1951-06-22)
plotSynopsis: Five-year-old Jody Letterin is taken into a church bell tower by a frightened man who threatens to kill him if police close in. Randy realizes that the crowd, searchlights and armed response are feeding the man's need for attention, and argues that giving him true sanctuary may be the safest way to bring the child down alive.

title: Byline For Frank (1951-06-29)
plotSynopsis: A dying newspaperman named Frank asks Randy to help him finish a story connected to the event that destroyed his career. Randy follows the old reporter's last lead, trying to uncover the truth and restore meaning to Frank's final byline.

title: Antonio's Return (1951-07-13)
plotSynopsis: Randy becomes involved with a gravely ill woman who is determined to find her missing husband before she dies. Her search for Antonio leads Randy through old relationships and unanswered questions about why the man vanished and whether he can still be brought back to her in time.

title: Mr. and Mrs. Carothers (1951-10-06)
plotSynopsis: An elderly Illinois couple asks Randy to help them enjoy one grand splurge in Chicago. Their sudden determination to spend freely seems cheerful at first, but Randy senses that the Carothers are hiding a more serious reason for treating the night as if it may be their last chance.

title: Lost Souls (1951-11-16)
plotSynopsis: Randy meets Ruth, a frightened woman who believes a female figure from her past is somehow following her from city to city and reaching her by telephone. As Randy protects her and tests whether anyone is really pursuing her, the haunting is traced to unresolved guilt and trauma from Ruth's childhood, giving her a chance to seek help instead of continuing to run.

title: Five Days off for Christmas (1951-12-21)
plotSynopsis: Ordered to take five days off for Christmas, Randy realizes he has no one to spend the holiday with. When a boy carrying an envelope for him is struck by a car, Randy searches for the boy's mother and is drawn into a story that gives his lonely Christmas unexpected meaning.

title: Expectant Father (1951-12-28)
plotSynopsis: Randy gets caught up in the nerves of expectant father Ben Troy while Ben's wife is about to have their baby. Ben becomes so frantic over the birth that Randy winds up managing the anxious husband almost as much as the real medical emergency.

title: Gusher James (1952-03-07)
plotSynopsis: Randy investigates the claim of a convicted murderer who insists that the killing for which he was blamed was actually committed by Gusher James, a wealthy and influential oil man. The accusation sends Randy against money and power as he tries to determine whether the prisoner's story is a last desperate lie or the truth.

title: The Jockey Brothers (1952-05-29)
plotSynopsis: Randy is pulled into a bitter rivalry between jockey brothers Ben and Keeney Clark. Ben fears his reckless younger brother's return to racing, while Keeney believes Ben is trying to protect his own fading career, and the conflict drives the brothers toward a dangerous reckoning on the racetrack.

title: Reformer (1952-06-26)
plotSynopsis: Benjamin Tusher, a farmer from rural Illinois, arrives in Chicago determined to reform a corrupt political machine without violence. Randy watches Tusher confront the city's entrenched interests with an almost disarming belief in goodwill and love, and discovers that the simple approach is more effective than anyone expects.

title: The Old Itch (1952-07-03)
plotSynopsis: Randy falls for Kit Gaynor, a talented roving reporter who seems ready to trade constant travel for a life with him in Chicago. Just as Randy begins to believe she might stay, Kit's old urge to move on returns and forces both of them to confront what settling down would cost her.

title: Flight from Fear (1952-07-31)
plotSynopsis: Randy notices that veteran printer Dutch Hildebrand has deliberately removed part of reporter Gil Lovett's story before publication. The missing material leads Randy to a gifted young swimmer and a secret serious enough to draw the FBI into the case, turning a newsroom oddity into a Cold War investigation.

title: His Name Was Luke (1952-08-14)
plotSynopsis: Randy encounters Julie Bronson, a skilled young pickpocket who urgently needs a large amount of money. Her desperation leads him to a man named Luke and into the dangerous reason Julie believes stealing is her only way out.

title: The Man With The Red Hair (1952-08-21)
plotSynopsis: On his night off, Randy meets a woman in a bar and joins her on a strange late-night tour of Chicago. Her mood changes sharply whenever a red-haired man appears, and Randy gradually learns that the night's ritual is tied to a deeply personal anniversary she has been unable to leave behind.

title: Ellen (Bomb on a Plane) (1952-09-04)
plotSynopsis: A call to the Chicago Star warns that a bomb is aboard an airliner. Randy cannot dismiss it as a crank call, so he races to protect the passengers and identify who planted the explosive before the threatened flight ends in disaster.

title: Larry the Understudy (1952-09-11)
plotSynopsis: Randy investigates young dancer Larry Wilson after a racketeer becomes determined to buy his services and Larry abruptly walks away from a promising theatrical break. The mystery ends at a rectory, where Randy learns Larry has chosen a different calling entirely: he is leaving show business to enter the seminary and become a priest.

title: Policy Wheel Racket (1952-09-18)
plotSynopsis: Randy investigates after Brother James, the organist at a Skid Row mission, is beaten and someone throws a hand grenade into the mission. The violence points toward a policy gambling racket and forces Randy to uncover why a charitable refuge has become a target.

title: The Bug Killings (1952-09-25)
plotSynopsis: A mentally disturbed killer admits murdering three women but insists he did not commit a fourth similar slaying. Randy takes the denial seriously and investigates whether the latest victim belongs to a different crime hidden behind the earlier murders.

title: Obsession Synopsis
plotSynopsis: An audio overview of Obsession, summarizing the series or collection for listeners.

title: Compartment B, Car 92 (AFRS) (aka Paranoia, Death House Express)
sortKey: 2|00002|compartment b, car 92 (afrs) (aka paranoia, death house express)
plotSynopsis: While being transported to prison by train, a convict overpowers and kills the officer guarding him. When a woman enters their compartment, the murderer forces her to help free him from the handcuffs before he makes a dangerous attempt to escape and assume the dead officer's identity.

title: The Blackout Killer
plotSynopsis: Aboard an ocean liner, Judith Webster meets an attractive stranger just as word spreads that the notorious Blackout Killer may be hiding on the ship. The man's false name and his suspicious interest in the coffin Judith is escorting make her wonder whether the killer is much closer than she imagined.

title: Murder Deferred (aka Second Best)
plotSynopsis: Norton Roberts believes the woman he loves is leaving him for another man and hires someone to kill his rival. When she later admits that the other romance was only a ruse and agrees to marry Norton, he desperately tries to cancel a murder contract that has already passed into unknown hands.

title: Hunting Party (aka Holiday House) (AFRS)
plotSynopsis: A buyer arrives to take possession of the Holiday mansion after Mrs. Holiday supposedly killed her husband by accident during a hunting party. When her doctor has her committed before the buyer can speak with her, suspicious prescriptions and a bullet still left in the gun suggest that the accepted story of the shooting is false.

title: Cousin Charlie (AFRS)
plotSynopsis: Jake Crowley has embezzled ten thousand dollars and must replace it before investigators arrive. When wealthy Cousin Charlie unexpectedly visits carrying exactly that amount in cash, Jake and his wife decide that killing their inconvenient relative may solve their financial problem.

title: The North Wind (AFRS)
plotSynopsis: A rough sailor is accused of murder, leaving the woman who loves him to decide whether she believes in his innocence. To stand by him, she must overcome her own deep fear of the sea and go to him despite the danger.

title: A Question of Personality (AFRS)
plotSynopsis: A police detective recovering from a nervous breakdown returns to duty, only to kill his own police chief. In a bizarre turn, he is then placed in the position of investigating the very murder he committed.

title: The Silver Cord (AFRS)
plotSynopsis: Sarah wants a life of her own, but the older woman who raised her continually uses illness and guilt to keep her at home. When Sarah considers marriage, her guardian reveals a disturbing claim about madness in the family in a final effort to prevent her from leaving.

title: The Hangman
plotSynopsis: A poor painter marries a woman he believes is wealthy, only to discover that she is nearly as broke as he is. Faced with the collapse of his expectations, he begins devising a dangerous plan to obtain the money the marriage failed to provide.

title: Summer Evening (AFRS)
plotSynopsis: A commercial artist loses the advertising job he never truly wanted and spends the evening confronting what comes next. At home with his wife, memories of their life together and his unrealized artistic ambitions force him to reconsider what he values.

title: Surrender Is Farewell (AFRS)
plotSynopsis: A man's sister refuses to accept his new marriage and repeatedly interferes in the couple's life, using increasingly underhanded tactics in an effort to break them apart.

title: Dynamite
plotSynopsis: A California truck driver begins hauling explosives because the dangerous work pays far better than ordinary freight. Encouraged by a spirited waitress he wants to help, he keeps taking riskier loads until his pursuit of money places both his future and his life in danger.

title: Wind Song
plotSynopsis: Anne Mason is bored by the safe, predictable future offered by her longtime suitor when she meets the restless traveler Brad Evans. Her attraction to Brad and his freedom forces her to choose between security and the uncertain life—and love—she has always imagined beyond her small town.

title: Amnesia (aka The Stranger) (AFRS)
plotSynopsis: An amnesiac named Robin is hired to impersonate a woman's long-missing love, but the deception collapses when he discovers that he really is the missing man. Recovering his identity also means confronting the fact that before losing his memory he had been blackmailing the woman's father.

title: Tailored for Murder
plotSynopsis: Hector accepts an expensive imported coat and hat from a hitchhiker, only to learn that the clothing links its wearer to a murder. His best chance at an alibi depends on Phyllis, the girl who had persuaded him to borrow her father's car and then abandoned him for a party.

title: David and Laura
plotSynopsis: Laura is devastated when her husband David dies in a drunken car crash after another woman claims they had been carrying on an affair. A dreamlike encounter with David later forces Laura to reconsider what she believes about his death and their marriage.

title: Clinging Hate (AFRS)
plotSynopsis: Aviator Ted Jordan's life becomes dominated by a corrosive hatred that reaches into his marriage, his relationship with fellow pilot Wade McCrary, and the people around their airport. The obsession grows against a background of dangerous flying and stormy weather.

title: Solitary Genius
plotSynopsis: The drama frames the troubled life and imagination of Edgar Allan Poe through compressed dramatizations of his work, including The Raven and The Fall of the House of Usher, blending biography with the dark creations that came to define him.

title: Ebb Tide
plotSynopsis: After losing a patient, a doctor abandons both his medical practice and his marriage and heads for the South Seas, retreating into alcohol rather than facing the failure that has consumed him.

title: Little Man of Destiny (aka Napoleon Bonaparte)
plotSynopsis: A dramatic biographical portrait follows Napoleon Bonaparte, the ambitious military leader whose consuming drive for power and greatness carried the 'little colonel' toward domination of much of Europe.

title: The Peacock Screen (AFRS)
plotSynopsis: An Obsession collection or drama item identified as “The Peacock Screen (AFRS).”

title: Kiss Of Kismet
plotSynopsis: During a Himalayan expedition, Grace falls in love with Clive despite being married to an overbearing husband and decides to leave her marriage. Clive is then lost in a mountain slide, and Grace's grief becomes an obsession as a mysterious monastery seems to draw her toward the possibility of hearing him again.

title: Blood Bath (Marie Antoinette)
plotSynopsis: An Obsession collection or drama item identified as “Blood Bath (Marie Antoinette).”

title: Eternal Spring
plotSynopsis: An Obsession collection or drama item identified as “Eternal Spring.”

title: Cry Vengeance
plotSynopsis: In the Belgian Congo, two criminals murder a kindly old Dutchman who is beloved by nearly everyone around him—including the animals. The killing sets in motion the story's promised cry for vengeance.

title: Faith is the Evidence
plotSynopsis: A drifter staying with a kindly minister rejects the idea that the meek are blessed. Circumstances then give the skeptical hobo an unexpected opportunity to deliver a sermon of his own and confront the philosophy he dismissed.

title: Case Of The Living Dead (Egyptian Curse w Elliott Lewis)
sortKey: 9|case of the living dead (egyptian curse w elliott lewis)
plotSynopsis: On their honeymoon in England, investigator Bill Christopher and his wife Pat are asked to prevent another death among the archaeologists who opened the tomb of Pharaoh Amon Ra-Tep. Six members of the expedition have already died mysteriously, and a scarab ring offered by an Egyptian servant appears to connect the victims.

title: Raised From The Dead (aka Strange Obsession, Terrible Obsession, Mary Anderson) (AFRS)
sortKey: 9|raised from the dead (aka strange obsession, terrible obsession, mary anderson) (afrs)
plotSynopsis: A criminal gang fakes a prisoner's death to break him out so he can reveal where stolen loot is hidden. Once he draws the map, members of the group begin dying one by one, leaving the surviving conspirators to wonder who is eliminating them.

title: Shadow of Huntley House (aka On The Wild Sea) (AFRS)
sortKey: 9|shadow of huntley house (aka on the wild sea) (afrs)
plotSynopsis: A woman sees a chance to steal her twin sister's newly inherited fortune by murdering her and taking her place. After her husband helps dispose of the body, she kills him too, hoping to erase the last person who knows about the substitution.

title: Todd Branson's Old House (aka A Long Chance)
sortKey: 9|todd branson's old house (aka a long chance)
plotSynopsis: A dying gangster leaves his house to a fellow criminal, who arrives and assumes the dead man's identity to take possession. He finds a woman already living there and the two begin imagining a new life together, but a visit from the real owner's uncle threatens to expose both impostors.

title: The Palm Beach Story (1944-10-29)
plotSynopsis: Broke inventor Tom Jeffers and his wife Gerry love each other, but Gerry decides their marriage is holding Tom back and heads for Palm Beach to get a divorce and find a rich backer for his inventions. On the way she attracts millionaire John D. Hackensacker III, while his flirtatious sister becomes interested in Tom after he follows Gerry south. The romantic mix-up forces Tom and Gerry to admit they still belong together, undoing Gerry's plan to solve their financial troubles by marrying money.

title: True to Life (1944-11-12)
plotSynopsis: Successful radio writers Link Ferris and Fletcher Marvin are hunting for believable material when Link becomes involved with the struggling Porter family and secretly turns their everyday troubles into a popular serial. Link helps father Pop get a raise and grows close to daughter Bonnie, but the deception becomes harder to hide as Fletcher also pursues her. When Bonnie learns how much of her family's life has gone on the air, Link finally drops the pretense and wins her by proposing for real.

title: Vivacious Lady (1944-11-19)
plotSynopsis: Shy biology professor Peter Morgan impulsively marries nightclub singer Francey in New York, then brings her home to the conservative college town where his formidable father is university president. Afraid to reveal the marriage, Peter passes Francey off while his old fiancée, his suspicious father and a household full of misunderstandings close in. A spectacular quarrel and family crisis finally force the truth into the open, and Peter and Francey at last get the honeymoon their secret marriage has delayed.

title: Clarence (1944-11-26)
plotSynopsis: The wealthy Wheeler household is full of quarrels: Mr. and Mrs. Wheeler are jealous and unhappy, daughter Cora is infatuated with an unsuitable man, son Bobby is troublesome, and governess Violet Penny is caught in the middle. Clarence, an unassuming former soldier hired as a handyman, quietly sees through everyone's problems and uses patience and humor to straighten out the family. His own romance with Violet emerges along the way, leaving the household far more settled than when he arrived.

title: Take a Letter Darling (1944-12-03)
plotSynopsis: Advertising executive A.M. MacGregor hires artist Tom Verney as her male secretary because his charm can help her manage difficult male clients and their jealous wives. Tom accepts only to earn money for a painting trip to Mexico, but the unusual arrangement becomes personal as the two fall in love while insisting they are too independent for romance. After jealousy and a breakup expose how strongly they feel, MacGregor gives up her emotional defenses and chooses to go to Mexico with Tom.

title: Lucky Partners (1944-12-17)
plotSynopsis: Strangers Jean Newton and David Grant become 'lucky partners' after a chance meeting leads them to share a sweepstakes ticket and agree to spend any winnings on a trip together. Their innocent bargain alarms Jean's fiancé and grows increasingly romantic as Jean and David travel toward Niagara Falls. When the pair wind up before the same judge who knew of their arrangement, the legal comedy ends with the judge pushing them toward the permanent partnership they have both come to want: marriage.

title: Bachelor Mother (1944-12-24)
plotSynopsis: Department-store clerk Polly Parish is mistakenly believed to be the mother of an abandoned baby and cannot convince her employer, David Merlin, that the child is not hers. David first forces her to care for the infant, then becomes increasingly involved with both Polly and the baby while his father enthusiastically assumes he has become a grandfather. After escalating misunderstandings over the child's parentage, David realizes he loves Polly and proposes, happily accepting the ready-made family he still believes is hers.

title: Room Service (1944-12-31)
plotSynopsis: Shoestring producer Gordon Miller has housed his entire cast in a hotel run by his brother-in-law while desperately waiting for financing for a new play. When the hotel chain's hard-nosed executive arrives demanding payment, Gordon and his company invent illnesses, deaths and other increasingly wild excuses to keep their rooms and protect young playwright Leo Davis's show. Their schemes finally collide with a visiting senator and potential sponsor, and the play is saved when the supposedly disastrous production wins the backing it needs.

title: The Lady Eve (1945-01-07)
plotSynopsis: Cardsharp Jean Harrington falls for wealthy, naive snake expert Charles Pike aboard ship, but he rejects her when he discovers she has been working a con with her father. Determined to get even, Jean reinvents herself as the aristocratic Lady Eve Sidwich and returns to Charles's life under an assumed identity, making him fall for her a second time. Her revenge gives way to genuine love, and after another round of deception and separation, Jean and Charles reunite without Charles ever fully grasping that both women were the same person.

title: Nothing but the Truth (1945-01-14)
plotSynopsis: Young stockbroker Bob Bennett wagers that he can tell nothing but the truth for twenty-four hours, putting $10,000 at stake just as he is surrounded by clients, friends and his boss's family. Absolute honesty quickly turns a weekend gathering into chaos as Bob blurts out opinions and secrets he would normally soften or conceal, including his feelings for the boss's daughter Gwen. A last-minute argument over the clock seems to cost him the bet, but a corrected time proves he has won both the money and Gwen.

title: The Show-Off (1945-01-21)
plotSynopsis: Aubrey Piper is a tireless braggart whose grand claims and meddling exasperate the modest Fisher family, especially after he marries daughter Amy. His boasting repeatedly lands him in trouble, including an arrest that costs the family precious savings, but his shameless confidence unexpectedly becomes useful when he confronts lawyers handling Joe Fisher's invention. Aubrey bluffs them into a much better deal, leaving the family forced to admit that their impossible show-off has finally done something worthwhile.

title: Appointment for Love (1945-01-28)
plotSynopsis: Playwright Andre Casall marries dedicated doctor Jane Alexander expecting a conventional home life, only to learn that Jane intends to keep her own apartment, hospital schedule and professional independence. Their attempt at a carefully organized marriage produces jealousy, missed meals and mounting frustration as Andre feels more like an appointment than a husband. A jealous confrontation finally breaks through their rules, and Jane happily allows Andre to drag her back into the shared married life both have been avoiding.

title: My Favorite Wife (1945-02-04)
plotSynopsis: Nick Arden has his wife Ellen legally declared dead after years missing at sea and immediately marries Bianca, only for Ellen to return alive from the shipwreck. Nick cannot find a way to tell his new bride, while Ellen disguises herself as an old family friend and becomes jealous when she learns another survivor shared her island exile. The mounting deception returns everyone to court, where the legal tangle is untied, Bianca abandons the marriage, and Nick is restored to Ellen, his very much alive favorite wife.

title: A Girl a Guy and a Gob (1945-02-11)
plotSynopsis: Dorothy Duncan is engaged to respectable Stephen Herrick when exuberant sailor Coffee Cup enters her life and becomes a disruptive new friend. Coffee Cup's rough charm, Navy buddies and impulsive schemes repeatedly throw Dorothy and Stephen's courtship into confusion, and for a time he seems ready to compete for her himself. Realizing Dorothy truly loves Stephen, Coffee Cup steps aside, arranges and pays for their wedding, and heads back to duty after making sure the couple finally marries.

title: The Milky Way (1945-02-18)
plotSynopsis: Mild-mannered milkman Burleigh Sullivan accidentally proves he can handle himself against middleweight champion Speed McFarland, inspiring manager Gabby Sloan to turn the reluctant milkman into a boxing attraction. Gabby arranges bouts intended to manufacture Burleigh's reputation, but Burleigh's innocence and unexpected success keep complicating the scheme while romances develop around both fighters. By the end, Burleigh's rise has transformed the group, and he looks forward to marriage and a future far removed from the prizefighting world he never really wanted.

title: You Cant Ration Love (1945-02-25)
plotSynopsis: On a wartime college campus, shy chemistry student Johnny Simpson becomes the subject of a campaign to turn him into a glamorous romantic commodity, complete with slang lessons and girls competing for his attention with ration points. The makeover works so well that Johnny becomes almost too popular, forcing Ann Jordan to admit that her interest in improving him has become love. Their feud collapses into a comic wedding, proving that affection is the one thing the campus cannot successfully ration.

title: Standing Room Only (1945-03-04)
plotSynopsis: Businessman Lee Stevens and his new secretary Jane Rogers travel to overcrowded wartime Washington seeking an important government contract but cannot find a hotel room. Jane solves the problem by getting them hired as a supposedly married cook and butler in a private home, forcing Lee to conduct business while maintaining their domestic disguise. Visiting executives, mistaken identities and household chaos nearly wreck the deal, but Lee lands the contract and realizes that the secretary who engineered the adventure is also the woman he loves.

title: The Magnificent Dope (1945-03-11)
plotSynopsis: Success-school promoter Rockingham Conway expects national publicity when small-town Tad Page wins his contest, only to discover that Tad is perfectly happy without ambition, status or wealth. Conway tries to remake him into a model graduate while secretary Claire Harris shows Tad the big city, but Tad's contentment exposes how artificial Conway's philosophy of success really is. The experiment overturns Conway's plans and brings Tad and Claire together, with Tad choosing love and his own simple values over the life Conway designed for him.

title: A Lady Takes a Chance (1945-03-18)
plotSynopsis: Molly Truesdale heads west on a bus trip and becomes entangled with rodeo cowboy Duke Hudson, a confirmed bachelor who prefers horses to marriage. A missed bus strands Molly in Duke's rough little town, where quarrels, jealousy and reluctant attraction keep drawing them together despite Duke's resistance. When Duke is hurt after another fall from his horse, Molly's fear for him finally strips away their defenses and the two admit they are in love.

title: Brewsters Millions (1945-03-25)
plotSynopsis: Monty Brewster learns that he can inherit a huge fortune only if he first spends a smaller fortune within a fixed period and finishes with nothing to show for it, without explaining the condition to anyone. He throws extravagant parties, makes reckless purchases and deliberately bad investments, only to watch his money-making instincts and good luck repeatedly increase his wealth instead. His apparent irresponsibility nearly costs him Peggy, but Monty finally satisfies the will, reveals the truth and gains both the inheritance and the woman he loves.

title: The Major and the Minor (1945-04-01)
plotSynopsis: Fed up with predatory men and unable to afford full train fare home, Susan Applegate disguises herself as a twelve-year-old girl and winds up sharing a compartment with Major Philip Kirby. The masquerade follows her to his military academy, where cadets pursue her, Philip's suspicious fiancée complicates matters, and Susan quietly helps Philip toward the active military service he wants. Back in Susan's hometown, Philip finally meets her as an adult woman, recognizes the truth, and the two discover that their unlikely deception has turned into romance.

title: A Slight Case of Murder (1945-04-08)
plotSynopsis: Former bootlegger Remy Marko goes legitimate after Prohibition and discovers that respectable business is harder than crime: his brewery is losing money, his beer is terrible, and foreclosure threatens. At home, old gang associates, a police-officer suitor for his daughter and a group of wanted criminals turn the household into comic chaos. When the fugitives become worth substantial reward money, Remy's financial crisis disappears almost as suddenly as it began, while he grudgingly accepts the policeman his daughter loves.

title: The Nervous Wreck (1945-04-22)
plotSynopsis: Chronic hypochondriac Henry Smith travels west convinced that every ache is fatal and that exertion may kill him. Instead he becomes entangled with Sally, a rough local bully and a series of situations that repeatedly force him to act more bravely than he believes possible. Henry finally knocks out the dangerous man everyone fears, only to learn the supposed bully is wanted outlaw Charlie the Gap; the reward makes Henry a local hero, though one sneeze is enough to restore his old medical panic.

title: Scatterbrain (1945-04-29)
plotSynopsis: Country girl Judy is discovered almost by accident and brought to Hollywood by studio publicity men who hope to turn her rustic personality into a screen sensation. Studio chief J.R. Russell doubts her, and her first dramatic test appears to confirm his fears, but Judy's natural comic energy and musical talent win over the camera in spite of every attempt to control her. The studio claims the success as its own discovery, while Judy remains cheerfully herself and the men around her scramble to keep up.

title: Hired Wife (1945-05-06)
plotSynopsis: Businessman Stephen Dexter faces a legal attack that could seize everything he owns, and his lawyer finds one loophole: if Stephen marries and places the assets in his wife's name, the creditors cannot reach them. Stephen plans to marry glamorous Phyllis, while efficient secretary Kendall Browning organizes the rescue and becomes the practical woman he actually depends on. As the scheme unfolds, Stephen discovers Phyllis is interested in his fortune while Kendall truly loves him, turning the hired marriage arrangement into a genuine one.

title: She Loves Me Not (1945-05-13)
plotSynopsis: Nightclub dancer Dolores Lopez becomes mixed up in dangerous trouble and is hidden at Princeton by students Paul Lawton and Buzz Jones. To keep her presence secret, the boys disguise her and invent explanations that grow increasingly impossible as the dean, Paul's sweetheart Midge and publicity people close in. The attempt to hide Dolores eventually becomes public spectacle, but the students survive the scandal, Paul and Midge remain together, and Dolores's dramatic apology becomes one last publicity event.

title: Boy Meets Girl (1945-05-20)
plotSynopsis: Hollywood writers Benson and Law seize on pregnant studio waitress Susie as the answer to their latest story problem, then turn her baby Happy into a wildly successful screen attraction. Their meddling makes Susie's private life part of the studio machine, especially when star Larry Toms decides marrying Susie would give him control of Happy. The writers recruit English extra Rodney as part of another scheme, only to discover he genuinely loves Susie; after the confusion clears, Rodney and Susie are free to build a real family while the writers move on to their next racket.

title: June Moon (1945-05-27)
plotSynopsis: Small-town lyricist Fred Lane rides to New York dreaming of Tin Pan Alley success and meets practical Edna Baker on the train. In the city he teams with an experienced songwriter, chases publishers, gets distracted by glamorous Lucille and discovers that the music business is less romantic than he imagined. After disappointments strip away his Broadway fantasies, Fred meets Edna again on the train and chooses the honest connection he nearly overlooked instead of continuing to chase success at any cost.

title: Having a Wonderful Crime (1945-06-03)
plotSynopsis: Newlyweds Jake and Helene Justice cannot stop playing amateur detective, so criminal attorney Michael J. Malone reluctantly joins their honeymoon trip after a magician mysteriously disappears during his act. At a lakeside lodge, Jake and Helene find the magician Fred King dead inside a trunk that has been mistakenly delivered to Malone's room. Malone traces the killing to hotel manager Winslow, who murdered King while trying to recover a $50,000 check and then offers Malone money to stay quiet; instead Malone exposes the crime and once again solves the case his friends dragged him into.

title: Tom Dick and Harry (1945-06-10)
plotSynopsis: Telephone operator Janie is courted by three very different men: practical Tom, wealthy and sophisticated Dick, and impulsive mechanic Harry. Unable to decide, she becomes engaged to all three and dreams through what marriage to each man might actually be like. Janie finally chooses Dick as the sensible answer, but his kiss leaves her unmoved; when Harry kisses her, the missing spark is obvious, and she runs off with the least practical man because he is the one she truly loves.

title: Cupcakes 1
plotSynopsis: A bakery-industry spot recommends packaged frosted cupcakes as an easy school-lunch dessert or after-school snack, emphasizing freshness, convenience and the extra energy a sweet treat can provide children.

plotSynopsis: Jell-O presents a recipe for golden apricot pie made with orange Jell-O, cooked dried apricots, sugar, a baked pie shell and whipped cream, selling the dessert as a colorful new family treat.

plotSynopsis: CBS promotes an upcoming Bing Crosby Show as a family program mixing music and comedy, mentioning Crosby, John Scott Trotter and Ken Carpenter and inviting listeners to tune in Wednesday night.

title: Roma Wines 5

title: Chase Sanborn Coffee 1
plotSynopsis: During wartime coffee rationing, Chase & Sanborn argues that each scarce cup should deliver maximum flavor, describes its coffee as a blend of finer beans, and asks shoppers to spend their ration coupons on the brand even if stores are temporarily sold out.

title: L and M Cigs 1
plotSynopsis: L&M promotes its Miracle Tip filter with celebrity testimonials and claims the filter gives an easy draw, fuller flavor and less nicotine, urging smokers to follow the growing trend toward the brand in regular or king size.

title: Dutch Cleanser 2

title: Rexall 4
plotSynopsis: A Rexall druggist explains how company research helped develop a medicated adhesive plaster intended to stick securely while irritating skin less, using that example to argue for the testing behind Rexall's broader line of drug products.

title: Autolite D
plotSynopsis: A Christmas-themed comedy exchange promotes Auto-Lite spark plugs for smoother performance, quicker starts and fuel savings, stressing that the plugs are engineered as part of a complete ignition system and are available in standard or resistor types.

title: Ironized Yeast 2
plotSynopsis: Ironized Yeast tablets are marketed to people who feel pale, weak or run down, with the ad linking some such symptoms to iron deficiency, describing the product as an iron tonic with brewer's yeast, and advising listeners that other causes should still be discussed with a doctor.

title: Lux F
plotSynopsis: Lux Toilet Soap promotes its facial routine as Hollywood-style complexion care, claiming widespread use by leading screen stars and citing tests in which many users' skin became softer and smoother.

title: L and M Cigs 2
plotSynopsis: A jingle-driven L&M commercial calls switching brands a 'red letter day' and sells the cigarettes on a combination of richer-tobacco taste and the white Miracle Tip filter.

title: NP 27
plotSynopsis: NP27 is promoted as a two-part athlete's-foot treatment: a liquid advertised for penetrating infected areas, relieving itch and pain and encouraging healthy tissue, plus a powder intended to guard against reinfection.

title: Jello 7 Magic
plotSynopsis: Jell-O compares making dessert to easy kitchen magic, emphasizing the product's versatility and fruit flavors including strawberry, raspberry, cherry, orange, lemon and lime.

title: Chesterfield Q
plotSynopsis: Chesterfield presents its regular and king-size cigarettes as the product of decades of tobacco research and promotes them on quality, taste and mildness.

title: Marlboro
plotSynopsis: A roughly half-minute, music-dominant recording contains no consistently intelligible spoken product copy across repeated exact-audio decodes.

title: Maxwell House 3
plotSynopsis: Instant Maxwell House is advertised as combining the brand's 'good to the last drop' flavor with instant preparation, no pot or grounds, and claimed savings compared with ordinary brewed coffee.

title: Adam Hats
plotSynopsis: During a Dr. Weird program break, a comic dialogue shifts from mystery to men's style and promotes Adam hats for their shape, finish and color, presenting the brand as an affordable way to look well dressed.

title: Lux 1
plotSynopsis: A Paramount casting director discusses the unusual demands of movie casting and says performers need good screen presence and complexions, leading into a Lux Toilet Soap endorsement tied to studio beauty care.

title: Lux 6
plotSynopsis: Actress Ella Raines describes her daily Lux soap facial routine of working up a lather, rinsing warm and then cold, while the commercial presents Lux as an easy route to softer, smoother skin and popular screen-star complexion care.

title: Pet Milk 1
plotSynopsis: Pet Evaporated Milk encourages mothers to keep children on the product through weaning from bottle to glass, claiming its nutritional qualities help support teeth, bones and steady growth throughout childhood.

title: Wrigleys 3
plotSynopsis: Wrigley's Spearmint chewing gum is promoted for its mint flavor and refreshing quality, with the ad suggesting that chewing it can help listeners feel fresh, alert and ready for work or recreation.

title: Chesterfield T
plotSynopsis: A very short cigarette spot uses a question-and-answer setup followed by an 'ABC' mnemonic praising the cigarette's mildness and taste.

title: NBC 3 Chimes
plotSynopsis: A very short recording consists of a brief sequence of resonant musical chimes, with no intelligible speech.

title: Rambler 1
plotSynopsis: Rambler promotes its compact car as roomy enough for six while still easy to handle and park, stressing economy, resale value, adjustable seating, reclining seats and available air conditioning as evidence of advanced design and careful workmanship.

title: Lipton Noodle 1
plotSynopsis: Lipton's Noodle Soup Mix is presented as a quick modern substitute for hours of homemade soup preparation, promising chicken flavor and tender egg noodles from a package emptied into boiling water.

title: Chesterfield U
plotSynopsis: A short Chesterfield announcement promotes the brand's premium-quality regular and king-size cigarettes and closes by identifying Chesterfield with the Dragnet program.

title: Chesterfield J
plotSynopsis: A Chesterfield spokesman says more king-size smokers are changing to the brand, arguing that its tobacco quality, taste and mildness distinguish both the regular and king-size versions.

title: Lucky Strike 1
plotSynopsis: Lucky Strike cites a Crossley poll of tobacco auctioneers, buyers and warehousemen to claim that knowledgeable tobacco professionals prefer the brand, using that survey to reinforce its 'fine tobacco' advertising theme.

title: Velveta 1
plotSynopsis: Kraft promotes Velveeta as an economical, nourishing cheese food that can be used in snacks, sandwiches, cheese sauces and inexpensive hot main dishes, emphasizing versatility as a way to stretch meals and leftovers.

title: Lux A
plotSynopsis: A Paramount-focused promotional segment discusses young actress Joan Taylor and the film Here Comes the Groom before shifting to complexion care, where Lux Toilet Soap is recommended through Hollywood-star examples and a simple warm-rinse, cold-splash facial routine.

title: Clipper Craft Coats 3
plotSynopsis: Clippercraft advertises suits, topcoats, sport jackets and tropical clothing on styling, durability, comfort and comparatively low prices, explaining that a cooperative buying plan among more than a thousand stores helps support the value claim and naming participating New York-area retailers.

title: Signal Oil F
plotSynopsis: The audio is a Roma Wines commercial urging listeners to serve wine with meals, naming sherry and burgundy, emphasizing California production and low per-glass cost, and closing with Roma's claim to be America's largest-selling wines.

title: Cheerios 1
plotSynopsis: Cheerios is promoted as an oat cereal that helps provide strength and energy, using the recurring phrase 'He's feeling his Cheerios' to connect the breakfast cereal with an active start to the day.

title: Cheerios 2
plotSynopsis: A sports-themed Cheerios commercial uses the 'go power' slogan to sell the ready-to-eat oat cereal, highlighting its O-shaped form, milk pairing and claimed contribution of vitamins, protein and minerals to an energetic breakfast.

title: Lux H
plotSynopsis: A brief retail-shopping announcement urges listeners to visit grocers for a week of special values and specifically notes that Lux Flakes and Lux Toilet Soap are among the products widely offered at promotional prices.

title: Spam 4
plotSynopsis: A short Spam commercial asks listeners to remind the household shopper to buy a can, presenting the canned meat as convenient and easy to serve either cold or hot.

title: Pepsodent 2
plotSynopsis: Pepsodent toothpaste is advertised around a foaming cleanser ingredient, with claims that its bubbles remove mouth film and leave teeth feeling cleaner and the mouth fresher; the spot also asks shoppers to bring an empty tube to the drug counter.

title: Fatima - Step
plotSynopsis: Fatima lays out a step-by-step case for its king-size cigarettes, stressing brand quality, a distinct flavor and aroma, mildness, and a blend of Turkish and domestic tobaccos.

title: Bromo Quinine
plotSynopsis: Bromo-Quinine cold tablets are promoted as a multi-ingredient remedy for several common cold symptoms, with the advertisement contrasting the product with single-action remedies and emphasizing its inclusion of quinine, other medicines and vitamin C.

title: Du Pont Chemistry 3
plotSynopsis: DuPont describes a household silver-polishing tool that uses neoprene rubber because of its resistance to polish oils and chemicals and lack of sulfur, presenting the product as an example of new businesses enabled by DuPont materials research.

title: Autolite 8
plotSynopsis: Auto-Lite urges motorists to winterize their cars and check spark plugs before cold weather, promoting standard and resistor-type Auto-Lite plugs for dependable starting and smoother engine performance and describing the resistor design as capable of a wider spark gap.

title: Goodyear Rubber Cement
plotSynopsis: Goodyear explains how wartime scarcity of natural rubber led its researchers to develop a synthetic rubber-to-metal cement for engine mounts, describing the material's role in isolating aircraft vibration and its use under heavy strain in airplanes and tanks.

title: Ford 1
plotSynopsis: An NBC continuity announcement previews upcoming drama, concert and variety programming before turning to a Ford automobile testimonial, where an owner praises the car's handling, comfort and value and listeners are invited to test-drive the new model at a dealer.

title: Fatima Cigs 3
plotSynopsis: Fatima promotes its king-size cigarettes on tobacco quality, mildness, flavor, aroma, manufacturing and package appearance, emphasizing a blend of Turkish and domestic tobaccos and repeatedly framing quality as the brand's distinguishing feature.

title: Chesterfield 8
plotSynopsis: Chesterfield uses laboratory comparisons and a long-term doctor-observation claim to market its regular and king-size cigarettes on quality, nicotine level and alleged lack of adverse nose, throat and sinus effects among a group of smokers.

title: Exlax 3
plotSynopsis: Ex-Lax is advertised as a gentle overnight laxative intended to help restore regularity, with the spot emphasizing doctor and consumer confidence and describing the chocolate-flavored medicine as effective without harsh upset.

title: Equitable Insurance 4
plotSynopsis: The Equitable Society explains its Assured Home Ownership plan, combining a first mortgage with life insurance and a growing cash fund, and promotes the arrangement as a way to pay off a mortgage early while protecting a surviving widow from inheriting the debt.

title: Ironized Yeast
plotSynopsis: Ironized Yeast tablets are promoted for people who feel tired and pale, with the ad linking some cases to iron-related nutritional anemia and claiming the tablets can help build red blood cells, strength and energy.

title: American Way
plotSynopsis: A public-information message argues that America's economic system is a fundamental part of the 'American way,' urges listeners to understand and improve it, and offers a free booklet titled The Miracle of America before returning to Tales of the Texas Rangers.

title: Signal Oil D
plotSynopsis: Signal Gasoline uses sound imagery from The Whistler to ask listeners to picture the brand's black-and-yellow traffic-signal logo, then promotes Signal gasoline, lubricants and independently operated dealers as dependable wartime car care.

title: Chesterfield 5
plotSynopsis: Chesterfield markets its regular and king-size cigarettes as a blend of high-quality tobaccos, repeatedly advertising taste, satisfaction and low nicotine as reasons smokers should switch to the brand.

title: Pabstead Cheese 2
plotSynopsis: A cheese-food commercial offers serving ideas from cream soup and eggs with cheese sauce to pear salad, apple pie and other dishes, presenting the product as a versatile ingredient that can appear throughout an entire meal.

title: Del Monte Catsup 2
plotSynopsis: Del Monte Catsup is promoted for a distinctive flavor the ad attributes to pineapple vinegar combined with ripe tomatoes, spices and herbs, with listeners urged to use it to brighten otherwise plain foods.

title: Blue Coal 2
plotSynopsis: Blue Coal is marketed as a dependable hard-coal heating fuel that requires less furnace attention and provides steady heat, with the ad stressing Pennsylvania sourcing, laboratory testing and the ability to locate dealers through the classified directory.

title: L and M Cigs 9
plotSynopsis: A short L&M cigarette spot uses the slogan 'Live modern' and promotes the brand's Miracle Tip filter on claims of richer taste, cleaner smoking and easier draw.

title: Ford 2
plotSynopsis: Ford ties a National Safety Council campaign to dealer service, urging motorists to have brakes, lights, steering and tires checked before summer driving and emphasizing Ford-trained mechanics, approved methods and genuine parts.

title: Roma Wines 6
plotSynopsis: Roma Wines uses an imagined dinner in Ecuador to portray the California wine as an American product appreciated abroad, then contrasts that prestige with its low domestic cost and promotes Roma as an inexpensive everyday wine for meals and entertaining.

title: Roma Wines 7
plotSynopsis: Roma Wines emphasizes bouquet, body and taste, describing California grapes, traditional winemaking skill, reserve wines and Burgundy and Sauterne varieties as reasons the brand offers good value and broad popularity.

title: Autolite A
plotSynopsis: An Auto-Lite message following Suspense promotes the company as a major maker of automotive electrical equipment and directs motorists to Auto-Lite service stations or their car dealers for trained electrical service and original factory parts.

title: GM Guardian Maintenance
plotSynopsis: Edgar Bergen and Charlie McCarthy use a comic mishap to promote General Motors Guardian Maintenance, presenting GM-trained dealer mechanics as the place for lubrication, repairs and appearance service on GM cars and trucks.

title: Hallo Shampoo
plotSynopsis: A sung shampoo jingle repeats a 'hello/halo' refrain and says the product glorifies the listener's hair.

title: Kraft 2
plotSynopsis: Kraft Dinner is promoted as a quick macaroni-and-cheese meal that cooks in about seven minutes, combining tender macaroni with Kraft grated cheese for an easy, strongly flavored family dish.

title: Ford 4
plotSynopsis: Ford promotes its new car on comfort, performance and economy, highlighting the midship ride, cushioned front seat and available V-8 or six-cylinder power while urging shoppers to test-drive the car before buying.

title: Dash Soap 1
plotSynopsis: Dash granulated soap is advertised as a value product that produces abundant long-lasting suds, cleans washable fabrics including colors, and costs less per ounce because the package contains more soap than competing brands.

title: Dodge
plotSynopsis: A comic exchange compares the feeling of being in love with the smoothness of Dodge's 'Airglide' ride, then promotes the 1936 Dodge on comfort, styling and a comparatively low factory price.

title: Chesterfield 4
plotSynopsis: Band leader Ray Anthony and his wife are cited as Chesterfield smokers in a testimonial-style spot that presents the brand as popular with younger adults and promotes its regular and king-size cigarettes for taste and mildness.

title: Lux 5
plotSynopsis: Lux Flakes offers a mail-in Gone with the Wind brooch promotion, describing the jewelry's simulated stones and antique-style setting and instructing buyers to send a large-box opening tab plus fifteen cents for the brooch and access to matching pieces.

title: Autolite 4
plotSynopsis: A very brief Auto-Lite announcement tells listeners that battery dealers can be found in the classified telephone directory under the batteries listing.

title: Jello 4
plotSynopsis: Jell-O promotes new butterscotch, chocolate and vanilla puddings as quick, easy desserts with homemade-style flavor and texture, encouraging shoppers to buy several packages and try all three varieties.

title: Life Buoy 3
plotSynopsis: Lifebuoy soap links hard work and warm weather with perspiration and body odor, urging daily baths or showers with the soap and promoting its lather as a way to wash away grime, perspiration and odor while leaving the user refreshed.

title: Autolite C
plotSynopsis: A comic Auto-Lite spot promotes the Stay Full battery's large liquid reserve and fiberglass retaining mats, claiming it needs water only a few times a year and lasts longer than batteries without those features.

title: Signal Oil E
plotSynopsis: A Whistler break promotes Signal gasoline during wartime rationing by emphasizing mileage, telling listeners that drivers who track fuel use report going farther with the brand.

title: L and M Cigs 4
plotSynopsis: L&M uses a 'Live modern' theme to promote its Miracle Tip filter, claiming the filtered cigarette delivers richer taste, cleaner smoking and an easier draw.

title: Camel 8
plotSynopsis: A wartime Camel message acknowledges that the brand can be difficult to find despite high production, promises that tobacco quality will not be reduced, and urges smokers to keep asking for Camels for their mildness and full flavor.

title: Chesterfield D
plotSynopsis: Chesterfield cites a college survey, chemical analyses and a doctor-observation claim to market its regular and king-size cigarettes on premium quality and alleged mildness and safety.

title: Autolite 9
plotSynopsis: Auto-Lite promotes its factory parts and service stations as a coordinated way to maintain a car's electrical system, highlighting spark plugs, batteries and ignition components and directing motorists to trained service outlets.

title: Signal Gas 2
plotSynopsis: Signal Ethyl gasoline is advertised as a spring tonic for older or newer cars, with claims that the premium fuel improves acceleration, hill climbing and resistance to engine pinging.

title: Chesterfield E
plotSynopsis: A short Chesterfield spot stresses decades of tobacco research, a claimed favorable record with smokers, high quality and low nicotine while selling the brand on taste and mildness.

title: Chesterfield N
plotSynopsis: Chesterfield summarizes a six-month medical observation of regular smokers and uses the reported lack of adverse ear, nose, throat and sinus findings to promote its regular and king-size cigarettes.

title: Boy Scouts
plotSynopsis: A brief Boy Scout Week announcement notes that communities and parents across the country are observing the occasion and links scouting with adventure.

title: Equitable Insurance 3
plotSynopsis: The Equitable Society tells the story of a shoe salesman whose career and income rise over time to illustrate a flexible life-insurance plan designed to expand as a policyholder's earnings and family responsibilities grow.

title: Lipton 2
plotSynopsis: Lipton Tea is promoted as a breakfast ritual, with the commercial emphasizing its amber color, aroma and brisk flavor as a lively way to start the day.

title: Exlax
plotSynopsis: Ex-Lax is advertised as a gentle overnight laxative intended to restore regularity, with the spot emphasizing effectiveness, doctor and consumer confidence, and a chocolate-flavored dose described as close to natural acting.

title: Lucky Strike 4
plotSynopsis: Lucky Strike promotes its cigarettes on the quality of the tobacco, claiming a smooth smoke from first puff to last and citing the preferences of tobacco auctioneers, buyers and warehousemen as evidence for the brand's L.S.M.F.T. slogan.

title: Palmolive Soap
plotSynopsis: Palmolive Soap promotes a large cash-prize '49 Gold Rush' contest, asking entrants to finish a short sentence about why they like the soap and mail it with a Palmolive wrapper for a chance at thousands of prizes.

title: Haleys MO
plotSynopsis: Haley's M-O is marketed as a combination of mineral oil and milk of magnesia for people dealing with both irregularity and acid indigestion, with the ad stressing its two kinds of relief and gentle action.

title: Cresta Blanca
plotSynopsis: A very short Cresta Blanca brand tag spells out the wine name and repeats it as a compact musical or spoken identification.

title: Signal Oil 4
plotSynopsis: Signal Ethyl gasoline is promoted as a premium fuel worth a few extra pennies, with the ad claiming stronger acceleration, smoother hill climbing and better overall driving performance.

title: Crisco
plotSynopsis: A brief Crisco tag identifies the shortening as all-vegetable and digestible and encourages listeners to keep cooking with it.

title: Lux G
plotSynopsis: A grandmother-and-granddaughter dialogue promotes Lux Flakes for delicate rayon garments, claiming repeated Lux washing helps preserve color and appearance and urging users to launder fine clothing after each wearing.

title: Swan Soap 2
plotSynopsis: Swan Soap is promoted for bath use through its rich 'beauty lather,' with the ad emphasizing gentle cleansing, easy rinsing and a smooth, fresh after-bath feeling.

title: Life Buoy 1
plotSynopsis: A short Lifebuoy message recommends buying the soap for daily baths or showers, promoting its lather for washing away dirt and perspiration and leaving the user feeling extra clean.

title: NBC 7 Convention
plotSynopsis: NBC explains how it plans to cover the Democratic National Convention with hundreds of newsmen and technicians, promising speeches, delegate interviews, off-guard candidate moments, behind-the-scenes political activity and explanatory reporting.

title: Lipton 1
plotSynopsis: Lipton Tea is sold on its brisk flavor, lively character and popularity, with the commercial presenting a cup of Lipton as a source of everyday refreshment and contentment.

title: Colgate Shaving 3
plotSynopsis: The recording contains a December 7 remembrance and Victory Loan appeal urging listeners to buy and hold war bonds, followed by a plug for Bill Stern's Esquire article 'Doctors, Our Miracle Men.'

title: Lucky Strike 2
plotSynopsis: Lucky Strike promotes its cigarettes as a fine-tobacco product associated with relaxation and feeling at one's best, reinforcing the pitch with the L.S.M.F.T. slogan and a claim that tobacco-industry experts prefer the brand.

title: Lux 8 Song
plotSynopsis: Lux Flakes is promoted as a gentler dishwashing soap through a domestic scene about rough hands and a comparison test in which Lux-washed hands are said to remain softer and smoother because the product contains no harsh alkali.

title: Haleys MO 1
plotSynopsis: Haley's M-O promotes a newly flavored version of its laxative, describing the product as a combination intended to address both irregularity and acid stomach upset and emphasizing its gentle action for adults and children.

title: Quaker Yukon Model 1

title: Community Chest 1

title: Colgate Shaving Cream

title: Autolite B
plotSynopsis: Auto-Lite promotes its Stay Full battery by listing an extra-large liquid reserve, extra electrical capacity and fiberglass insulation as features intended to reduce watering needs, provide starting power and extend battery life.

title: Alka Seltzer

title: Turtle Wax 1

title: CBS Radio 3
plotSynopsis: CBS Radio touts results from a broadcasting poll in which its programs and personalities won numerous first-place honors, naming Jack Benny, Eve Arden, Bing Crosby and Doris Day before returning listeners to Gunsmoke.

title: CBS Radio 2
plotSynopsis: A brief CBS Radio continuity announcement promotes the network's weekday daytime dramatic serials and invites listeners to tune in on Monday before returning to Gunsmoke.

title: Jello Chocolate Pudding
plotSynopsis: Jell-O introduces a chocolate pudding powder intended to make an old-fashioned-style dessert by cooking the mix with milk in a double boiler, emphasizing simple preparation, low cost and six servings per package.

title: Post Toasties 1

title: Rio Grande Gas 1
plotSynopsis: Rio Grande gasoline cites use by police, fire, ambulance and other municipal fleets in California as an endorsement, promoting the fuel for starting, acceleration, mileage and reserve power.

title: Signal Battery
plotSynopsis: Signal dealers warn that older cars and limited wartime driving can leave batteries undercharged, offering free battery inspections and promoting Signal-spec replacement batteries with a stated guarantee of up to two years.

title: Quaker Oats 1
plotSynopsis: Quaker Oats is promoted as a hot breakfast cereal for active children, with a jingle and claims that oatmeal supports growth and endurance for sports and school activities.

title: Lava Soap
plotSynopsis: Lava Soap asks users to write in with their favorite uses while promoting the product for quickly cleaning heavily soiled hands and claiming it can remove housework grime in a short washing time.

title: Glocoat Wax
plotSynopsis: A short 1949 Glo-Coat commercial promotes a newer self-polishing floor wax as brighter than earlier versions and recommends it for linoleum floors.

title: Coleman
plotSynopsis: Coleman promotes a limited-time oil- and gas-heater sale with a lower purchase price, claimed fuel-cost savings and a free 32-piece glassware set, urging customers to visit a dealer before winter.

title: Signal Oil 9
plotSynopsis: During gasoline rationing, Signal promotes its Go Farther gasoline on mileage, saying the wartime formula retains high-energy components and adds other high-mileage hydrocarbons to help drivers stretch fuel stamps.

title: Dupont
plotSynopsis: A DuPont science feature describes two products: an N2-based rat poison sold in branded compounds with safety cautions, and a precision blasting timer designed to fire charges in controlled delays to reduce vibration and improve blasting efficiency and safety.

title: Elgin American
plotSynopsis: A Christmas shopping commercial presents Elgin American compacts, cigarette cases, dresser sets, simulated pearls, lighters and other accessories as stylish last-minute gifts, emphasizing design, craftsmanship and value.

title: Swan Soap 4
plotSynopsis: Swan Soap promotes its floating bath bar and 'super cream' blend for a rich lather that cleans gently, rinses away thoroughly and leaves skin feeling fresh and smooth.

title: Anacin
plotSynopsis: Anacin is promoted as a pain and headache remedy containing multiple pain-relieving ingredients, with the commercial claiming faster and more complete relief than a listener's usual single remedy and offering a money-back guarantee.

title: CBS Radio 1
plotSynopsis: CBS Radio cites a poll of hundreds of critics and editors to claim that its programs won more top honors than all competing networks combined, using the survey to reinforce the network's reputation for high programming standards.

title: Kraft 4 Malted 1
plotSynopsis: A Kraft promotion explains how to make a chocolate-flavored malted drink at home by mixing Kraft malted milk with chilled milk, emphasizing its flavor, convenience and nutritional value.

title: Prell 1
plotSynopsis: A Prell cream-shampoo commercial promotes radiant, manageable hair, dandruff removal and concentrated economy, using testimonial-style endorsements from both women and men.

title: Fatima Cigarettes
plotSynopsis: A holiday-season Fatima cigarette advertisement recommends cartons as Christmas gifts and repeatedly stresses the brand’s long-cigarette format, Turkish and domestic tobacco blend, extra mildness, flavor and aroma.

title: Kraft 3
plotSynopsis: A Kraft Dinner commercial presents its boxed macaroni and cheese as a quick seven-minute meal, emphasizing tender macaroni, Kraft grated cheese and the likelihood that diners will ask for seconds.

title: Emz Chlorophyl 1
plotSynopsis: An ENNDS chlorophyll-tablet advertisement claims internal chlorophyll can combat breath, body and other personal odors, demonstrates the pitch with an onion-odor test and offers a money-back guarantee.

title: Chesterfield A
plotSynopsis: A Chesterfield cigarette spot urges listeners to try the brand on claims of high tobacco quality, low nicotine, mildness and satisfaction, promoting both regular and king-size versions.

title: Signal Oil 1
plotSynopsis: A Signal gasoline commercial ties fuel economy to engine efficiency, arguing that the company’s Go Farther gasoline delivers both strong performance and improved mileage.

title: Lux E
plotSynopsis: A Lux Toilet Soap promotion recommends the new bath-size bar as a beauty bath, highlighting creamy lather, performance in hard water and a long-lasting floral fragrance.

title: Blue Coal 4
plotSynopsis: A Blue Coal advertisement urges homeowners to order the laboratory-tested hard coal, promising dependable heat, less furnace attention and strong value for home heating.

title: Rexall 2
plotSynopsis: A Rexall family-druggist message promotes the company’s broad line of drug products, using Rexall Milk of Magnesia as an example of a mild, smooth product the affiliated pharmacists confidently recommend.

title: Dristan 1
plotSynopsis: A Dristan commercial presents its three-layer decongestant tablet as relief for cold and sinus congestion, describing claimed effects on swollen membranes, pain, fever, allergy symptoms and breathing passages.

title: NBC 5
plotSynopsis: An NBC network promotion previews upcoming comedy, drama and crime programming, including Dean Martin and Jerry Lewis, Red Skelton, Truth or Consequences, Theatre Guild on the Air and Dragnet.

title: Chesterfield 2
plotSynopsis: A Chesterfield cigarette jingle and sales pitch claims the brand is more perfectly packed for an easy draw, fuller tobacco flavor, mildness and greater smoking satisfaction.

title: Way Cold Tabs
plotSynopsis: A Four-Way Cold Tablets advertisement featuring William Bendix claims rapid relief from common cold symptoms including aches, headache, fever, upset stomach and irregularity.

title: Alka Seltzer Plop Plop
plotSynopsis: An Alka-Seltzer jingle uses the familiar “plop, plop, fizz, fizz” refrain to promote the effervescent tablets for fast relief of an upset stomach and headache after overeating.

title: RCA 2
plotSynopsis: An RCA Victor promotion links the anniversaries of professional baseball leagues with watching games on television and advertises the company’s available 19-inch television sets and improved picture reception.

title: Pepsi Cola 1
plotSynopsis: A light comic Pepsi-Cola spot describes the drink as light, refreshing and suitable for picnics or parties, then closes with the “Be Sociable” theme and a reminder to buy an extra carton.

title: Exlax 2
plotSynopsis: An Ex-Lax advertisement cites qualities doctors reportedly want in a laxative and promotes chocolate Ex-Lax as effective, gentle, close to natural acting and suitable for overnight relief of constipation.

title: Spam 6
plotSynopsis: A Spam commercial recommends serving the canned pork-and-ham product baked as an easy dinner centerpiece, describing its preparation, flavor and a playful story about baked Spam winning a suitor.

title: Equitable Insurance 2
plotSynopsis: An Equitable Society life-insurance spot follows an ambitious worker whose promotions allow his flexible insurance plan to expand with his income, emphasizing low initial cost and increasing family protection.

title: Gulf 2
plotSynopsis: A Gulf commercial promotes Gulflex registered lubrication as a method of extending automobile life, describing model-specific service, multiple specialized lubricants and supporting tests, while also mentioning Gulf oils and gasoline.

title: Fitch
plotSynopsis: A multi-product Fitch advertisement promotes coconut-oil shampoo for clean, manageable hair, no-brush and brush shaving creams for comfortable shaves, and a dandruff-remover shampoo backed by a guarantee.

title: Chesterfield M Dragnet
plotSynopsis: A Dragnet-linked Chesterfield message invokes the program’s emphasis on facts and cites a medical report about smokers before urging listeners to choose regular or king-size Chesterfields.

title: Lipton 3
plotSynopsis: A Lipton Tea commercial recommends ending meals with the brand’s tea, stressing its brisk, lively flavor and popularity among tea drinkers.

title: Tide Soap 1
plotSynopsis: A Tide detergent advertisement repeatedly claims Tide produces cleaner laundry than any soap, citing laboratory comparisons and everyday examples such as overalls and towels.

title: Camel 7
plotSynopsis: A wartime Camel cigarette message addresses shortages, says production has increased, and insists the brand will continue using properly aged tobaccos to preserve its familiar mildness and full flavor.

title: Colgate Shaving 2
plotSynopsis: A Colgate Lather Shaving Cream commercial explains how its moist, fine-textured lather softens and supports whiskers for a close, comfortable shave, followed by the closing of Bill Stern’s sports program.

title: Ford 3
plotSynopsis: A Ford Dealers commercial uses an owner testimonial to promote the 1954 Ford’s durable finish, fuel economy, low maintenance costs and resale value, then invites listeners to test-drive the car.

title: Signal Gas 1
plotSynopsis: A Signal Ethyl gasoline spot tells drivers to try the premium fuel if their cars start slowly, accelerate poorly or ping on hills, arguing that gasoline quality determines vehicle performance.

title: Quaker Oats 5
plotSynopsis: A Quaker Puffed Rice and Puffed Wheat promotion emphasizes the cereals’ gun-puffed crispness and nut-like flavor while teasing a forthcoming 3-D space-flight-to-the-moon premium offer.

title: Pepsodent 1 Part
plotSynopsis: A partial Pepsodent toothpaste commercial cites a family preference test and promotes its Irium foaming action for cleaner breath, brighter teeth and removal of dulling film.

title: Lux 4
plotSynopsis: A Lux Toilet Soap dramatization links an attractive complexion with romance and Hollywood beauty, recommending regular cleansing with Lux before makeup and at bedtime.

title: Contadina Tomato Paste
plotSynopsis: A short sung jingle repeatedly asks who puts “a great tomato” in a small can before identifying Contadina tomato paste.

title: Johnson Wax 1
plotSynopsis: A Johnson’s Glo-Coat advertisement recommends the self-polishing floor wax for brightening kitchens, stressing that it needs no rubbing, protects linoleum and leaves a durable shine.

title: Raleigh
plotSynopsis: A Raleigh cigarette advertisement cites purported scientific tests comparing nicotine and tar levels with other leading brands and promotes the cigarette as smoother, better tasting and safer to smoke.

title: Mutual Kid Shows
plotSynopsis: A Mutual network promotion invites children and families to weekday afternoon programming featuring fantasy adventures and Western songs, presenting the block as imaginative entertainment for young listeners.

title: Old Spice 1
plotSynopsis: A Father’s Day Old Spice advertisement suggests several Shulton grooming gifts, including after-shave lotion, cologne, deodorant and boxed sets at different prices.

title: Parkay 2
plotSynopsis: A conversational Parkay margarine commercial describes a neighborhood of good cooks who use the product for spreading and cooking, emphasizing taste, nutrition, economy and availability in yellow quarter-pound sticks.

title: Wildroot 1
plotSynopsis: A Wildroot Cream-Oil commercial advises men to check their appearance before work and promotes the hair dressing for neat hair, relief of dryness and loose dandruff, and its lanolin-containing, alcohol-free formula.

title: Spam 3
plotSynopsis: A Spam advertisement recommends baking the canned pork-and-ham product as an easy family dinner, describing its flavor and preparation and ending with a playful romantic rhyme.

title: Schlitz 1
plotSynopsis: A Schlitz beer commercial tells a humorous story about a reluctant guest who enjoys a family gathering after discovering a shared interest in fishing and tasting Schlitz, ending with the brand’s familiar fame claim.

title: Fitch Shampool 1
plotSynopsis: A very brief Fitch shampoo slogan urges listeners to “use your head,” save their hair and use Fitch shampoo.

title: Signal Oil A
plotSynopsis: A Signal Premium Compounded Motor Oil advertisement compares modern cars with modern lubricants, claiming the oil’s additives clean deposits, guard bearings, resist thinning and foaming, and do more than simply lubricate.

title: Johnsons Glocoat 2
plotSynopsis: A Johnson’s Glo-Coat commercial explains that the self-polishing floor finish needs no rubbing or buffing, dries to a hard shine, protects linoleum and simplifies floor care.

title: L and M Cigs 6
plotSynopsis: An L&M filter-cigarette spot promotes the brand’s white “miracle tip,” filtration and tobacco blend, claiming superior taste, mildness and flavor.

title: Tums 1
plotSynopsis: A short Tums advertisement recommends the antacid tablets for acid indigestion, heartburn and gas and mentions several package sizes and prices.

title: L and M Cigs 8
plotSynopsis: An L&M cigarette commercial urges listeners to “live modern,” promoting the filter’s claimed richer taste, cleaner smoke and easier draw.

title: Vaseline 2
plotSynopsis: A Vaseline-sponsored Dr. Christian program announcement reminds listeners that the annual script competition is nearing its deadline and invites suitable listener-written scripts for a $2,000 award.

title: Household Finance Corp

title: Colgate Shaving 5

title: International Sterling
plotSynopsis: An International Sterling advertisement stresses that its sterling-silver prices have remained unchanged since 1944, promotes the Spring Glory pattern and frames the silverware as finely crafted, lasting beauty.

title: Frigidaire 1

title: Del Monte Catsup 1

plotSynopsis: A short quiz-style Anchor Hocking spot contrasts famous authors’ real names with their better-known pen names before presenting Anchor Hocking as a famous name in glass.

title: Tums 2
plotSynopsis: A Tums antacid commercial promotes the tablets for quick relief of acid indigestion, emphasizes their safety and lack of acid rebound, and lists several package sizes and prices.

title: Clipper Craft Coats 1

plotSynopsis: A mysterious thousand-dollar deposit appears in Novak's bank account just as he is hired to meet a man arriving by ship and collect a playing card—the Jack of Clubs. A corpse and smuggled microfilm turn the strange errand into an espionage-and-murder case.
