title: Oyster Shucker at the Fifty Fathoms (1953-10-06)
plotSynopsis: Rocky’s oyster-shucking job turns dangerous when he opens a dozen special oysters and finds valuable stolen pearls hidden inside. The restaurant is part of a smuggling route in which pearls arrive offshore, are planted in oysters and delivered to a wealthy diner, while waiter Ferdinand works to keep the operation hidden. Rocky survives an attempted disposal at sea, exposes Ferdinand, recovers the pearls from the diner’s meal, and learns that Iris, the waitress he has been courting, is an undercover U.S. Customs agent.

title: Double Indemnity (1953-10-13)
plotSynopsis: Rocky answers a chauffeur ad, is knocked unconscious and wakes in a wealthy household where everyone insists he is Steve Crandell, husband of Laura and holder of a large life-insurance policy. He learns that the household is trying to use him as a substitute corpse in a double-indemnity scheme devised by the real Steve, Laura and their accomplices. At a cliffside staged suicide, Laura loses her nerve and police intervene, exposing the disguised man as the real Steve and the insurance plot.

title: The Shipboard Jewel Robbery (1953-10-20)
plotSynopsis: Working as a steward aboard a luxury liner, Rocky gets caught in the theft of Lady Harkness’s jewels and is framed for the murder of ship’s doctor Harper. The jewels had been mixed into the plaster cast on Rocky’s injured arm so they could pass through a shipwide search, but the doctor’s plan to X-ray the cast threatened to expose them. Rocky identifies nurse Helen and her partner Larry as the thieves, with Helen also responsible for killing Harper, and the captain overhears enough of her confession to clear Rocky and recover the jewels.

title: Pint-Sized Payroll Bandit (1953-10-27)
plotSynopsis: A nine-year-old boy named Mickey walks into Rocky’s all-night diner carrying a shoebox that really contains $50,000 from a payroll robbery. Rocky tries to protect the runaway child and return the marked money, but gunmen connected to Mickey’s father pursue them and repeatedly try to recover the cash. Mickey ultimately takes the money to police himself, Rocky survives the gangsters’ attempt to kill him, and the boy is left safely with his aunt instead of the father he fears.

title: Messenger for Death (1953-11-10)
plotSynopsis: Rocky earns a hundred-dollar messenger fee delivering a mysterious package for fashion artist Laura Chandler, only to be knocked out and lose it. He learns Laura was drugged at a party and made to believe she had shot a red-haired woman, part of a blackmail scheme built around the gun in Rocky’s package. When the supposed victim is later murdered for real with Laura’s weapon, Rocky traces the setup to Laura’s secretary Eve and exposes the frame before Laura can be arrested for the killing.

title: Some Cat's Killed the Canary (1953-11-17)
plotSynopsis: Rocky fills in on bass at a jazz club and soon finds singer Evie Johnson murdered in a hotel room while Dolores, the drugged ex-wife of musician Johnny Lament, is being framed for the crime. The corpse disappears, but Rocky discovers Johnny hid it in a bass case and murdered Evie because she learned he was dealing narcotics. The investigation also exposes club manager Quaid and musician Bugsy as part of the drug operation, and police recover Evie’s body before the gang can dispose of Rocky.

title: Murder on the Aisle (1953-11-24)
plotSynopsis: Rocky is hired to keep an alcoholic drama critic in his theater seat and instead finds him murdered during the performance. A producer, playwright and Rocky all have motives or opportunity, while magazine editor Porridge even confesses in an attempt to protect actress Miss Carter. Rocky’s discovery of a blonde bobby pin beneath the seat exposes Carter’s brunette disguise; the critic had been threatening to have her deported, and she killed him before trying to silence Rocky backstage.

title: Murder Among the Statues (1953-12-01)
plotSynopsis: Rocky’s handyman job in a bargain statuary shop turns deadly when owner Oliver Bates is murdered and several people hunt for one seemingly worthless plaster figure. After kidnappings and a wild drive to a wealthy collector’s estate, the statue breaks open to reveal an ancient Aphrodite by Praxiteles hidden beneath the plaster. The payoff exposes Bates’s assistant as his killer and the collector as part of the theft-and-sale scheme.

title: Murder on the Midway (1953-12-08)
plotSynopsis: Rocky befriends hungry eight-year-old Billy at a carnival and is suddenly accused of kidnapping him when the boy disappears inside a midway attraction. Chasing Billy through the carnival, Rocky discovers the boy deliberately ran away from his guardian to reunite with his mother, a carnival worker who had lost custody after her husband’s family convinced a court she was unfit. After another brief disappearance and frantic chase, the guardian relents and Billy is allowed to live with his mother.

title: Companion to a Chimp (1953-12-15)
plotSynopsis: Rocky takes a paid-companion job and discovers his charge is Godfrey, a valuable chimp at the center of a publicity stunt that turns into a real kidnapping. When promoter Marty Bunsen is murdered, Rocky is framed while gangster Harry tries to turn the fake ransom scheme into a payoff and pin the killing on him. Police arrive before Harry can finish Rocky, and Godfrey is recovered after one last comic escape.

title: The Plot to Murder Santa Claus (1953-12-22)
plotSynopsis: Rocky takes a Christmas job as a department-store detective and temporary Santa, then finds the regular Santa murdered after a recent $8,000 pearl robbery. A threatening note and a missing doll point to an inside accomplice who had used Santa to hide the stolen pearls, then stabbed him when he would not reveal where they were. Rocky survives a gunfight among the toy displays, captures the killer and discovers the missing pearls inside the child’s doll, earning its young owner the reward.

title: The Prize Fight Fix (1953-12-29)
plotSynopsis: Rocky is mistaken for prizefighter Luis Gandolfo and forced into a bout that gamblers expect Gandolfo to throw. Instead the opposing fighter is poisoned, upsetting the fix and producing a fortune in unexpected winning bets, while the real Gandolfo later turns up strangled in Rocky’s closet. Rocky uncovers Loopie Monsoon and Stanley’s double-cross, only for bookmaker Mike Mitchell to seize their winnings and prepare to kill everyone involved; police intervene before Mitchell can finish the cleanup.

title: On the Trail of a Killer (1954-01-05)
plotSynopsis: Rocky becomes suspicious of the polished Brock after Rocky’s old friend Ellie dies in what was ruled an accident and Brock quietly claims she actually killed herself. Following clues that Brock may have profited from similar deaths before, Rocky deliberately follows him west and pushes until the man makes a move. Brock tries to throw Rocky from the back of a train, but police alerted by Sergeant Finger are already aboard and arrest him.

title: The Rodeo Murder Mystery (1954-01-12)
plotSynopsis: Rocky takes an errand job with a rodeo and is quickly blamed when the show’s aging owner is murdered. The cowboys lock him in a stall to await their own rough justice, but Rocky escapes with help from an educated mule and keeps investigating. He discovers that Ringo hired a gunman to kill the old man so he could take over the financially troubled show, and the same gunman confirms the arrangement before Ringo tries to silence everyone. Rocky stops him and locates the $45,000 the owner had hidden to save the rodeo.

title: The Museum Murder (1954-01-19)
plotSynopsis: While conducting a sightseeing tour at a museum, Rocky finds a red-haired woman’s body hidden in an Egyptian sarcophagus, only to have it vanish before police arrive. Her missing purse and letters lead Rocky deeper into the museum after hours, where curator Deans reveals himself as part of the crime and prepares to kill Rocky and hide him as a mummy. Sergeant Finger finds the woman’s body in Deans’s office and arrives in time to stop the curator before Rocky becomes another exhibit.

title: Hollywood or Boom (1954-01-26)
plotSynopsis: Rocky accepts a lucrative job driving a truckload of explosives to Hollywood and discovers the cargo is camouflage for fugitive Mike the Butcher, who is hiding inside with stolen postal money. Mike murders Rocky’s partner and tries to use Rocky and a redheaded passenger as disposable cover while double-crossing his own gang. The passenger turns out to be a postal agent, and after a dangerous showdown around the explosive truck, Mike is stopped and the stolen money recovered.

title: The Football Fix (1954-02-02)
plotSynopsis: Pro quarterback Jerry Brady hires Rocky after fixer Addison pressures him to throw a championship game, but the case becomes a murder investigation when coach Pat Casey is killed and conflicting sightings place Brady in impossible locations. Rocky uncovers an escaped identical twin whom Jerry has secretly been hiding, a double that has scrambled the alibis and been used throughout the scheme. Addison’s betting operation collapses during the final confrontation, and the surviving players are left to answer for the fix and the killing.

title: The Football Fix (AFRTS) (1954-02-02)

title: The Catskills Cover-Up (1954-02-09)
plotSynopsis: Filling in as social director at Mama Greenspan’s Catskills resort, Rocky stumbles over a nervous guest, a missing fortune and several people searching for Larry Greenspan. After being slugged and chasing a suitcase of cash that has been hidden inside blintzes, Rocky faces gunman Bugsy while the supposed secretary Gloria takes control of the money. Gloria then reveals she is a U.S. Treasury agent, the cash is recovered for the government, and Larry’s part in helping expose the scheme may even earn him a commendation.

title: One Husband Too Many (1954-02-16)
plotSynopsis: Seductive Lulu Ann offers Rocky $5,000 to kill wealthy lawyer Perry Shane, then admits she already has another living husband, ex-con Marvin. Rocky warns Shane and learns Marvin believes Lulu Ann wants Perry dead for his money, but Lulu Ann is actually maneuvering to remove both men who stand between her and that fortune. When Marvin prepares to kill Rocky, Sergeant Finger shoots the gun from his hand; Perry begins annulment proceedings, Lulu Ann is taken in, and Rocky earns a job as Shane’s process server.

title: A Sitting Duck for Death (1954-02-23)
plotSynopsis: Escaped killer Carl ‘the Grinder’ vows to murder the three men who sent him to prison, making Rocky the bait in former prosecutor Harry Bowman’s plan to draw him out. Bowman’s scheme backfires when his own disguise gets him killed, leaving Rocky to face the real Grinder. Rocky survives the attack and finds one last trap, a bomb hidden in a ballot box, barely throwing it clear before it explodes.

title: Honor Among Thieves (1954-03-02)
plotSynopsis: Working for attorney Perry Shane, Rocky helps a doctor whose son Stan is addicted to heroin and appears to be stealing and selling narcotics from his father’s practice. Rocky discovers that Miss Carroll has been supplying the boy, using his forged signatures to obtain drugs while running the real sales herself. A staged payoff and hidden microphone draw out her confession that she intends to take $100,000 and flee, clearing Stan for treatment instead of leaving him to carry her crimes.

title: The Twice-Murdered Man (1954-03-09)
plotSynopsis: Rocky reunites with childhood friend Sammy, now an actuary, whose joking use of probability seems to identify businessman Crispy as a murderer before any crime has been proved. Crispy admits choking a woman who was blackmailing him, but the victim survived that attack and was later stabbed with a paper knife. Blood on Sammy’s sleeve and knowledge he should not possess expose the truth: the woman was Sammy’s fiancée, he learned she had been blackmailing other men, killed her himself and tried to make Crispy’s earlier assault carry the blame.

title: Psychological Murder (1954-03-16)
plotSynopsis: Rocky is drawn into the wealthy Bigelow household after Jane Bigelow becomes convinced she is going insane and will eventually murder her husband. The threats and violent episodes turn out to have been planted by Bigelow, a disgraced former psychologist who uses hidden voices and staged incidents to reinforce fears inherited from Jane’s mother. Rocky exposes the conditioning before Bigelow can kill him and blame Jane, revealing that the husband’s real motive is her money.

title: Rocket Racket (1954-03-23)
plotSynopsis: Rocky answers an ad seeking an unattached man for dangerous experimental work and is recruited by a foundation supposedly preparing a revolutionary rocket flight. Snooping inside the ship, he finds painted canvas, studio props and dynamite instead of spacecraft equipment: the promoters have taken millions from a wealthy backer and plan to blow up the fake rocket with Rocky aboard. Rocky escapes by switching clothes with a guard and survives the explosion, then proves the fraud with debris from the phony craft.

title: Boarding House Doublecross (1954-03-30)
plotSynopsis: Rocky rents a room in a violent boarding house and meets Gerald Kinsey, who insists he and his wife Helen had occupied the same room until the landlady and her son suddenly denied ever seeing them. Rocky discovers Helen imprisoned in a backyard shed and learns that she and Gerald are themselves jewel thieves, while the boarding-house pair are trying to steal their loot. A shooting and a garbage-can escape end with police identifying Gerald as a wanted jewel robber and hauling the surviving conspirators away.

title: Stagecoach (1949-01-09)
plotSynopsis: A mixed group of passengers crosses dangerous Arizona country by stagecoach while Geronimo's Apaches threaten the route. title: The Exile (1949-01-23)
plotSynopsis: With England ruled by Cromwell, the future Charles II lives in exile in Holland, hiding his identity while loyal supporters wait for a chance to restore him. During his wandering he finds shelter and work with Katie, whose practical life at her inn and farm offers him a peace far removed from courts and civil war, and the two fall in love. Charles is eventually drawn back into the royal cause when supporters and enemies converge on his refuge, forcing him to fight for both his life and his claim. After the immediate danger is defeated, word arrives that a new free Parliament has invited him to return to England as king on terms that include the freedoms he demanded. Katie knows he belongs to his people rather than to her alone, and they part with a final promise of enduring love as Charles leaves to reclaim the throne.

plotSynopsis: David and Ann Smith learn that a legal technicality means their three-year marriage was never valid. David assumes they will simply marry again, but Ann is furious when he treats the situation casually and decides to make him earn her back. She begins seeing David's law partner Jefferson, whose courtly Southern manners give David a very real rival. The contest follows them to a winter resort, where Ann stages one last attempt to make David give up on her and David refuses to be driven away. Their jealousy finally exposes that neither wants anyone else, and the Smiths reconcile as a couple all over again.

title: Hired Wife (1949-02-06)
plotSynopsis: Efficient secretary Kendall Browning secretly loves her boss, cement-company owner Stephen Dexter, but spends every spring watching him fall for another glamorous woman. When a rival company threatens to tie up every asset Stephen owns, his lawyer proposes a temporary marriage so the business can be transferred into a wife's name until the legal danger passes. Stephen wants model Phyllis Walden, but Kendall's attempt to arrange that marriage goes wrong and she ends up becoming Stephen's legal wife herself. Once Kendall controls the company she stops behaving like a compliant secretary, and the resulting battle finally makes Stephen see her as the woman she has always been. Their business marriage becomes real, and Stephen asks her to marry him just before remembering that they already are.

title: Magnificent Obsession (1949-02-13)
plotSynopsis: Reckless millionaire Robert Merrick nearly drowns, and the emergency equipment used to save him is therefore unavailable when beloved physician Dr. Hudson suffers a fatal accident. Hudsonâ€™s widow Helen resents Robert for the loss, and Robertâ€™s careless attempt to force a reconciliation contributes to another accident that leaves her blind. In Paris she learns his identity but also recognizes the man he has become; fearing that marriage to a blind woman would burden him, she leaves. Six years later Robert returns as a physician, performs the difficult operation himself, and Helen opens her eyes to light, with the promise that her sight will continue to return.

title: The Prisoner of Zenda (1949-02-20)
plotSynopsis: Englishman Rudolf Rassendyll arrives in Ruritania and, because he is nearly identical to King Rudolf, is forced to impersonate the monarch after the king is drugged and kidnapped by the ambitious Black Michael. While carrying the deception through court and falling in love with Princess Flavia, Rassendyll learns the real king is imprisoned at Zenda Castle. He helps rescue the king and defeats the plot, then gives up both the throne and Flavia because her duty is to her country and its rightful ruler.

title: The Night Has a Thousand Eyes (1949-02-27)
plotSynopsis: Stage mind-reader John Triton begins as a fraud in 1929, working with his fiancÃ©e Jenny and friend Whitney Courtland, until his act suddenly becomes real and he starts seeing events before they happen. A tampered clock gives everyone false relief before the real hour strikes and oil executive Gilman attacks Jean over missing business options. Triton intervenes, saves her, and dies beside a marble lion, fulfilling the final vision he had already recorded in his diary.

title: A Foreign Affair (1949-03-06)
plotSynopsis: Congresswoman Phoebe Frost arrives in occupied Berlin to investigate the conduct of American troops and quickly focuses on nightclub singer Erika von Schlütow, a former Nazi whose protection appears to reach inside the U.S. Army. The couple retreats to Peggyâ€™s family home in Bloomington, where Chuckâ€™s pride makes unemployment harder to bear than poverty itself. Reconciled and expecting a child, they endure the Depression together until work and music begin to return. Years later, Chuck is again leading an orchestra, with Peggy beside him as the life they nearly lost comes full circle.

title: The Perfect Marriage (1949-03-20)
plotSynopsis: On their fifth anniversary, successful husband and wife Dale and Jenny Williams realize that their supposedly perfect marriage has gone flat and that familiarity has replaced romance. Talk of separation becomes serious when old flames Gloria and Gil reappear, giving each spouse reason to suspect the other has already moved on. The jealousy they thought had vanished returns with force, and both discover that they still care far more than they admitted. After comic attempts to provoke one another collapse, Dale and Jenny shut out their would-be alternatives, celebrate their anniversary after all, and rediscover the marriage they nearly abandoned.

title: Suddenly Its Spring (1949-03-27)
plotSynopsis: Husband-and-wife lawyers Peter and Mary Morley return from wartime service after years apart only to discover that distance, pride and unspoken hurt have left their marriage close to divorce. As they divide the possessions in their apartment, each old object brings back a memory and exposes the misunderstandings they never discussed, including their grief over not having a child and the possibility that they could have adopted. A broken music box begins playing after being shaken, giving them an obvious metaphor for their own marriage. Mary finally dismisses the other man, and she and Peter abandon the divorce and reconcile.

title: The Ghost Breakers (1949-04-03)
plotSynopsis: Radio personality Larry Lawrence becomes entangled with Mary Carter and follows her to a supposedly haunted castle on a Cuban island she has inherited. The real prize is a rich silver deposit, and Montgomery and his partners have been using the supernatural legend to frighten Mary away and keep control of it. Their conspiracy collapses in a gunfight with police, leaving Mary wealthy and Larry insisting that the ghosts were tricks, just before one final unexplained scare undercuts his certainty.

title: Music for Millions (1949-04-10)

Fred and Alâ€™s daughter Peggy fall in love, but Al insists Fred end the relationship while he is still married. After Fred loses his drugstore job defending Homer and other veterans, he pushes Homer to trust Wilma rather than sacrifice their future out of fear. At Homer and Wilmaâ€™s wedding, Fred reveals that Marie is divorcing him and that he has found new work. Peggy accepts the difficult life ahead, and Fred realizes the best years of his life may still be in front of him.

title: The Skys the Limit (1949-04-24)
plotSynopsis: Decorated fighter pilot Jerry Burton comes home on leave and, tired of being treated as a public hero, hides his identity while enjoying New York as an ordinary man. He falls for magazine photographer Jean, but his evasiveness and apparently aimless behavior make her believe he is wasting his life while editor Phil also hopes to marry her. Jerry cannot tell her that his leave is ending and that he is returning to combat. Phil sends Jean to photograph departing fighter pilots, and at the airfield she finally discovers who Jerry really is. They confess their love just before his transport takes off, with Jean promising to wait for him until the war is over.

title: The Trouble with Women (1949-05-01)
plotSynopsis: Reporter Kate Farrell writes a sensational article about psychology professor Gilbert Sedley that leaves her newspaper facing a major libel suit, including the claim that he believes in hitting women. To manufacture proof, Kate enrolls in Sedley's class under cover and repeatedly tries to provoke him into striking her. Instead the combative experiment turns into romance, and the escalating deception finally spills into court, where psychology, hypnosis and Kate's real feelings undo the scandal she set out to create.

title: Its a Wonderful Life (1949-05-08)
plotSynopsis: George Bailey has spent his life sacrificing his own ambitions to help the people of Bedford Falls through the family building-and-loan. On Christmas Eve, an $8,000 shortage leaves him facing disgrace and possible arrest, and in despair he wishes he had never been born. Clarence, an angel hoping to earn his wings, grants that wish and shows George a grim alternate Bedford Falls in which his brother died young, his mother does not know him, Mary never married, and many people George once helped were left far worse off. Realizing how deeply his life is woven into the lives of others, George begs to live again. Restored to his family, he learns that the townspeople he helped for years have raised more than enough money to cover the loss, and the sound of Christmas chimes tells him Clarence has earned his wings.

title: Hold Back the Dawn (1949-05-15)
plotSynopsis: Romanian confidence man and former gigolo Georges Iscovescu is stranded in Mexico waiting years for an immigration quota number that will let him enter the United States. When an old acquaintance explains that marriage to an American offers a quicker route across the border, Georges sets his sights on Emmy Brown, a trusting American schoolteacher whose station wagon has broken down nearby. He marries Emmy intending only to use her for immigration, while Anita, another woman from his past, waits for him to complete the scheme. During a honeymoon trip Georges unexpectedly falls genuinely in love with his wife. Anita later tells Emmy the truth about the wedding and Georgesâ€™s past, and a devastated Emmy leaves. When Georges has a sudden vision that she has been hurt in an automobile accident, he crashes the border to reach her hospital bedside, sacrificing his chance of legal entry. His devotion restores Emmyâ€™s will to live, and the immigration inspector who followed him chooses not to report the crossing, leaving Georges and Emmy together as a real husband and wife.

title: Her Husbands Affair (1949-05-22)
plotSynopsis: Margaret Weldon loves her ambitious husband Bill, but his confidence repeatedly outruns his judgment, especially when he throws himself into the inventions of an eccentric professor. A new cream is promoted as a hair remover, only to produce the opposite result and leave its test subjects sprouting alarming amounts of hair. With lawsuits and the governor furious, Margaret recognizes that the failed remover is actually a potentially valuable hair restorer and turns the disaster into a commercial opportunity. Bill resents her habit of rescuing his schemes and makes her promise to stop interfering, but almost immediately the professor arrives with another accidental invention, a fluid that preserves flowers indefinitely. Bill forgets every lesson he has just learned and eagerly launches the next venture with Margaret at his side.

title: Trade Winds (1949-05-29)
plotSynopsis: Private detective Sam Wye is sent across the Pacific to bring back fugitive Kay Kerrigan, who believes she murdered playboy Tommy Broome after he drove her sister to suicide. Sam falls for Kay and spots a crucial contradiction: Kay remembers shooting Broome in the heart, but he died from a bullet to the head, and a pair of black antelope gloves at the scene were not hers. Sam gathers the women linked to Broome and uses the gloves as bait; Mrs. Cornell claims them and finally admits that Kay's gun held blanks and that her husband Walden killed Broome after Kay left. With the confession secretly witnessed, Kay is cleared and Sam's pursuit ends in marriage rather than arrest.

title: The Killers (1949-06-05)
plotSynopsis: When hitmen murder former boxer Swede Anderson without resistance, the investigation works backward through his life to explain why he simply waited for death. Swede had fallen in with Big Jim Colfax's gang, joined a major robbery, double-crossed the others for the stolen money and fled with Kitty, only to be betrayed and stripped of the cash himself. Years later the old crime catches up with him, leaving Swede convinced there is nowhere left to run.

title: Mr Blandings Builds His Dream House (1949-07-01)
plotSynopsis: Advertising executive Jim Blandings is tired of cramped New York apartment life and decides that moving his family to the country will solve everything. Instead, the supposedly simple dream house becomes an escalating chain of surveys, architects, contractors, wells, unexpected construction costs, and new emergencies that push the project far beyond its original budget. Jimâ€™s work suffers at the same time because he cannot find a slogan for the Wham ham account, while his friend Billâ€™s constant helpfulness around Muriel gives Jim one more thing to worry about. Just when Jim is ready to believe the entire venture was a mistake, the familyâ€™s housekeeper casually supplies the winning Wham slogan, a contractor returns an overcharge, and Jim realizes that despite the expense and aggravation he truly does love the house. Asked whether he would do it all again, he admits that he probably would.

title: The Big Clock (1949-07-08)
plotSynopsis: George Stroud works inside the vast Janoth publishing organization, where his domineering boss has built an empire ruled by schedules, deadlines, and the enormous clock in the company lobby. After Janoth kills Pauline York, the woman Stroud had also been seeing, Stroud discovers that the unidentified man the company has ordered him to hunt is himself. Forced to direct the investigation, he uses the companyâ€™s own research machinery while desperately keeping his identity hidden and gathering evidence against Janoth. He finally turns the trap by accusing Janothâ€™s aide Steve Hagen; Hagen breaks and reveals that Janoth actually killed Pauline. Janoth tries to flee, falls into the buildingâ€™s generator machinery, and is electrocuted, ending both the murder hunt and his obsessive control of the clock.

title: Yellow Sky (1949-07-15)
plotSynopsis: After a bank robbery, outlaw leader Stretch and his exhausted gang cross a deadly desert and reach the abandoned mining town of Yellow Sky. There they find only an old prospector and his fiercely independent granddaughter Mike, who are secretly working a rich gold claim. The gang quickly turns on its hosts and on itself over the treasure, while Stretch, increasingly drawn to Mike, tries to keep the others from simply taking everything. Greed splits the outlaws into rival factions, and Dude and Lengthy move to seize the gold for themselves. Stretch survives the final gunfight, returns his gun to Mike, and declares that he is through with the life that brought him there. With the dangerous members of the gang gone, he asks Mike and her grandfather to let him remain in Yellow Sky.

title: Casbah (1949-07-22)
plotSynopsis: Master thief Pepe le Moko is safe from arrest only while he remains inside the maze of Algiers' Casbah. His love for visiting Gaby gives Inspector Slimane the weakness he has been waiting for: Slimane falsely tells Gaby that Pepe is dead and arranges her departure, knowing Pepe will leave the Casbah to reach her. Pepe walks into the trap at the airport as Gaby's plane leaves for Paris, losing the sanctuary that had kept him beyond the law.

title: Saigon (1949-07-29)
plotSynopsis: After the war, pilot Larry Briggs learns that his badly wounded friend Mike Perry has only a few months to live. Larry and Pete Rocco decide not to tell Mike and instead take a lucrative flying job in the Orient so they can fill his remaining time with adventure. Their employer, Alex Maris, turns out to be a wanted war profiteer, and his secretary Susan Cleaver is carrying a briefcase containing roughly half a million dollars. Mike falls for Susan while Larry distrusts her, then Larry seizes the money and tries to force her away from Mike before the scheme destroys him. The groupâ€™s flight into Indochina draws police attention, Maris catches up with them, and the criminal plot collapses in violence. Pete is killed, Mike dies from his condition, and Maris is shot. With the money recovered and the police satisfied, Larry and Susan leave Saigon together, both chastened by the lives lost around them.

title: Fort Apache (1949-08-05)
plotSynopsis: At remote Fort Apache, experienced Captain Kirby York understands that Cochise and his people have left the reservation because corrupt Indian agent Meacham has cheated and abused them. York risks an unarmed mission into Apache country and persuades Cochise to return for peace talks after promising fair treatment. The fortâ€™s rigid commander, Colonel Thursday, ignores both Yorkâ€™s warning and Cochiseâ€™s grievances, treats negotiation as humiliation, and orders the Apache back under Meachamâ€™s authority. Thursday then dismisses Yorkâ€™s warning of an ambush and leads the regiment into a narrow pass, where nearly the entire command is destroyed. Wounded, Thursday refuses rescue and dies with his men. When Cochise approaches the remaining wagons, York keeps his promise and meets him unarmed; Cochise returns the regimental flag. The regiment is later rebuilt, carrying forward the names and memory of the men who died.

title: Jezebel (1949-08-12)
plotSynopsis: Proud New Orleans belle Julie Marsden repeatedly tests and humiliates her fiancé Pres Dillard until her defiance destroys their engagement. When Pres later returns married to Amy, Julie tries to reclaim him and provokes jealous rivalries that end in a fatal duel. A yellow-fever epidemic then strikes New Orleans and Pres falls gravely ill. Realizing the damage her selfishness has caused, Julie asks Amy to let her accompany Pres to the deadly quarantine island because she knows the local conditions and can fight for his survival. Amy agrees, giving Julie a final chance at redemption through sacrifice rather than possession.

title: Love Crazy (1949-08-19)
plotSynopsis: Steve and Susan Ireland expect to celebrate their wedding anniversary quietly, but a meddling mother-in-law and a series of innocent-looking encounters with another woman convince Susan that Steve is unfaithful. When she pushes ahead with a divorce, Steve seizes on a lawyerâ€™s suggestion that a legally insane husband cannot be divorced immediately and begins pretending to be mad. The scheme becomes much less funny when doctors actually declare him insane and place him under Susanâ€™s custody, forcing Steve into increasingly frantic attempts to escape and explain himself. A jammed elevator finally brings Steve, Susan, and the other woman together long enough for the truth to come out. Susan realizes the supposed affair was innocent, her anger collapses, and the two reconcile instead of divorcing.

title: Appointment for Love (1949-08-26)
plotSynopsis: Successful playwright Andre marries independent doctor Jane, only to discover that she intends marriage to preserve two separate people rather than merge them into one household. She takes an apartment several floors above his so each can continue working and living independently, leaving Andre baffled and increasingly jealous. Both begin manipulating appearances and outside admirers to prove that jealousy really does matter, turning the apartment building into a comic battlefield. After the games finally expose how much they actually want each other, the pair abandon their experiment in detached marriage and reconcile.

title: Apartment for Peggy (1949-09-02)
plotSynopsis: Retired professor Henry Barnes, convinced that age has made him useless, rents his attic to veteran student Jason Taylor and Jason's energetic pregnant wife Peggy during the postwar housing shortage. Peggy draws Barnes back into life, persuading him to organize classes for veterans' wives and reminding him that knowledge matters only when it helps people. After Peggy loses her baby, guilt and financial pressure drive Jason to abandon school for a better-paying sales job, and Peggy prepares to leave as well. Believing he has lost the people who gave him purpose, Barnes takes what he thinks are sleeping pills, only for Peggy and the returning Jason to discover the tablets were harmless. Jason chooses teaching again, Peggy stays, and Barnes realizes he is needed after all.

title: The Human Comedy (1949-09-09)
plotSynopsis: Teenager Homer Macauley works as a bicycle messenger in wartime Ithaca, carrying the small joys and devastating news of his neighbors while his older brother Marcus serves overseas. Through school, family and the telegraph office, Homer learns that becoming a man means recognizing both difference and shared humanity. Elderly telegrapher Willie Grogan dies at his desk just as the message arrives that Marcus has been killed in the war. Before Homer can bring the telegram home, Marcus's wounded Army friend Tobey arrives in Ithaca, saying Marcus made him part of the family. Homer tears up the death notice and welcomes Tobey into the Macauley home as the living piece of his brother that has returned.

title: Whispering Smith (1949-09-16)
plotSynopsis: Railroad detective Luke 'Whispering' Smith returns to Medicine Bend and discovers that his old friend Murray Sinclair has crossed from questionable salvage into organized theft, sabotage and train robbery with Rebstock's gang. Smith tries to pull Murray back for the sake of the woman they both care about, but Murray kills Rebstock, turns on Smith and refuses every chance to surrender. Their friendship ends in a final armed confrontation in which Smith is forced to shoot the dying Murray after Murray draws on him one last time.

title: Dont Trust Your Husband (1949-09-23)
plotSynopsis: Advertising man Vince repeatedly comes home late claiming business with a mysterious Mr. Frazier, only for his wife Paula to discover that Frazier is a woman and suspect an affair. Trying to prove that jealousy works both ways, Vince encourages handsome stranger Claude Kimball to flirt with Paula, not realizing Kimball is a wealthy tobacco executive who begins taking the assignment seriously. The scheme escalates into threats of divorce, competing romances and a badly timed confession until the real business client appears and the manufactured jealousy collapses. After one final comic misunderstanding with a hired admirer, Vince and Paula reconcile.

title: Pride of the Yankees (1949-09-30)
plotSynopsis: The story follows Lou Gehrig from a powerful Columbia ballplayer into a Yankees rookie, his romance and marriage with Eleanor, and the long run of durability that earns him the name the Iron Man. As his consecutive-game record and fame grow, unexplained weakness finally forces him from the lineup and doctors diagnose the fatal illness that will bear his name. At Yankee Stadium, surrounded by teammates and fans, Gehrig refuses self-pity and calls himself the luckiest man on the face of the earth before walking away from baseball to a final ovation.

title: The Senator Was Indiscreet (1949-10-03)
plotSynopsis: Vain but spectacularly inept Senator Melvin G. Ashton decides that his growing publicity proves the country wants him for president, while his press agent Luke Gibson struggles to contain the damage and marry sharp-tongued columnist Poppy McNaughton. As Ashton's accidental popularity grows, everyone around him worries about the private diary in which he has recorded years of political secrets and indiscretions. Poppy finally gets hold of the diary and sends it toward the newspapers just as Ashton convinces himself the White House is within reach. Realizing publication will destroy him, the senator abruptly abandons the presidential campaign and starts dreaming instead of being summoned to lead somewhere as remote as Outer Mongolia.

title: Criss Cross (1949-10-10)
plotSynopsis: Armored-truck driver Steve Thompson cannot let go of his former lover Anna, even after she marries gangster Slim Dundee. When Slim discovers them together, Steve invents an armored-car robbery to explain the meeting and secretly plans to use the heist to escape with Anna. The robbery kills an old guard and leaves Steve wounded, while Slim survives and sends gunman Vincent to finish him. Steve bribes Vincent to take him to Anna, only to discover that her promises were driven by money and self-preservation. Slim arrives at the hideout as Anna turns back to Steve for protection, and the final confrontation ends in gunfire just as police close in. Steveâ€™s detective friend Pete can only tell him that Anna was poison and that some men have to learn the truth the hard way.

title: Pitfall (1949-10-17)
plotSynopsis: Insurance investigator John Forbes is bored with the routine of suburban marriage when his work brings him to Mona Stevens, who received expensive gifts bought with money embezzled by her imprisoned boyfriend. John should simply recover the property, but attraction leads to a brief affair that he hides from his wife Sue. Private detective MacDonald, already obsessed with Mona, discovers the relationship and begins threatening both John and Mona. After the embezzler is released, the jealous and increasingly violent chain of events reaches Johnâ€™s home, where John kills the armed man in self-defense while Mona shoots MacDonald. John finally tells the police and then Sue the whole truth. Sue considers leaving him but decides that one terrible lapse should not automatically erase an otherwise good marriage, and the couple agree to try to rebuild what his deception damaged.

title: Love Letters (1949-10-24)
plotSynopsis: During the war, Captain Alan Quinton writes deeply personal love letters for his less articulate friend Roger Morland to a young woman named Victoria. Alan falls in love with the unseen recipient through his own words, but Roger returns home, marries Victoria, and later tells her that the letters were never his. After Roger is found stabbed to death, Alan comes home convinced that Victoria killed him and eventually meets an amnesiac young woman known as Singleton, not realizing she is Victoria herself. The two fall in love while Alan struggles with the knowledge of her past. Returning to Meadow Farm finally restores the missing truth: Victoriaâ€™s guardian, Beatrice Remington, killed Roger after he struck Victoria, and Victoriaâ€™s shock erased her memory. Cleared of the murder and reunited with the man who truly wrote the letters she loved, Victoria and Alan can finally claim the relationship that began before they ever met.

title: Remember the Night (1949-10-31)
plotSynopsis: Lee Leander is arrested for stealing a diamond bracelet just before Christmas, and prosecutor John Sargent has the case postponed until after the holidays rather than risk a sympathetic jury. Feeling responsible for leaving her jailed over Christmas, John arranges bail and discovers that Lee has nowhere worth returning to, so he takes her along to his own family home. The warmth of Johnâ€™s mother and aunt gives Lee a glimpse of the honest life she never had, and she and John fall in love on the trip back to New York. At trial John quietly tries to give her every possible chance, but Lee refuses to let his love compromise his duty. She pleads guilty, accepting that she must pay for what she did. John promises to stand beside her through sentencing and whatever prison term follows, while Lee hopes that if he still wants her afterward they can begin together on equal terms.

title: Body and Soul (1949-11-11)
plotSynopsis: Charlie Davis rises from neighborhood boxer to champion, but success ties him to promoter Roberts and a corrupt fight business that treats fighters as disposable assets. After an opponent with a known brain injury dies following a rigged bout, Charlie finally understands the human cost of the racket, even as Roberts arranges for him to throw his own title fight. Given $60,000 to bet against himself, Charlie instead fights to win, rejecting the fix and Roberts' control. He leaves the ring bruised but morally free, reunited with Peg and declaring that Roberts can no longer take anything from him.

title: The Uninvited (1949-11-18)
plotSynopsis: Rick Fitzgerald and his sister Pamela buy an old seaside house despite its reputation for ghostly sobbing and unexplained cold. The mystery deepens when young Stella Meredith, whose mother supposedly died falling from the nearby cliff, is drawn compulsively to the house and nearly goes over the same precipice. Rick investigates the old Meredith household and learns of Mary Meredith, her husbandâ€™s Spanish model Carmel, and a long-buried scandal. The accepted story says Carmel was the dangerous rival, but the hauntings reveal the opposite truth: Stella is actually Carmelâ€™s daughter, and Mary Meredith was the jealous woman who tried to kill the child and died at the cliff. Carmelâ€™s spirit finally reaches Stella with love and peace, while Rick confronts the malevolent apparition of Mary and drives it from the house, ending the haunting and freeing Stella from the false history of her birth.

title: Spiral Staircase (1949-11-25)
plotSynopsis: Traumatized by witnessing her parents' deaths, Helen has been unable to speak for years and works in the Warren household while a killer stalks women he considers physically imperfect. During a storm, suspicion seems to point toward volatile Steven Warren, but Helen discovers that the apparently respectable professor is the murderer and that he has deliberately used Steven's presence to divert suspicion. Trapped in the house and targeted because of her muteness, Helen races up and down the spiral staircase trying to reach Mrs. Warren's gun. Mrs. Warren finally shoots the killer, and the shock breaks Helen's silence: she is able to telephone Dr. Perry herself and speak for the first time since childhood.

title: All My Sons (1949-12-02)
plotSynopsis: Manufacturer Joe Keller has built his life around providing for his family, but his son Chris discovers that Joe knowingly allowed defective aircraft cylinders to be shipped during the war and let partner Herbert Deever take the blame. Twenty-one pilots died, and Joe insists he did it to protect the business for his sons. A letter from missing son Larry reveals that Larry learned of his father's crime and deliberately went to his death because he could not live with the shame. Joe finally understands that the dead airmen were 'all my sons' too. Moments later a gunshot from the house tells Chris that his father has killed himself.

title: Call Northside 777 (1949-12-09)
plotSynopsis: Chicago reporter McNeil reopens the case of Frank Wiecek, imprisoned for the murder of a policeman after an identification by speakeasy owner Wanda Skutnik. What begins as a human-interest story driven by Frank's mother's long campaign becomes a search for evidence that the conviction was wrong. McNeil finally finds a newspaper photograph showing Skutnik with Frank before the date she swore she first saw him; an enlargement reveals the date on a newsboy's paper as December 22. The proof establishes perjured identification testimony and wins Frank his freedom after years in prison.

title: The Affairs of Susan (1949-12-16)
plotSynopsis: Susan's prospective husband tries to understand the woman he plans to marry by questioning the men who knew her before him. Ex-husband Roger remembers an innocent country girl, writer Bill recalls an intellectual companion, and Westerner Mike describes an adventurous outdoor woman, leaving the fiancé wondering which Susan is real. The answer is that each man saw the side of her that his own expectations brought out. After the newer suitors step aside, Roger returns and admits that he was too impatient to understand the young woman he married. Susan realizes she still loves him, and the divorced couple reunites.

title: Miracle on 34th Street (1949-12-23)
plotSynopsis: Macy's hires kindly Kris Kringle as its department-store Santa, but Kris insists that he really is Santa Claus and gradually wins over practical Doris Walker, her skeptical daughter Susan and lawyer Fred Gailey. When Kris is committed and his sanity becomes a courtroom issue, Fred defends him by turning the question of Santa Claus into a legal test, while the Post Office's delivery of thousands of letters addressed to Santa gives the judge a way to recognize Kris without deciding the impossible. Susan and Doris regain their faith, and Kris quietly guides the three toward the Cape Cod house Susan has wished for.

title: One Way Passage (1949-12-30)
plotSynopsis: Escaped convict Dan Hardesty, being returned to San Quentin to face execution, meets terminally ill Joan Ames aboard a Pacific liner. Neither initially reveals the death sentence hanging over them, and they fall in love while trying to crowd a lifetime of happiness into the voyage and a day ashore in Honolulu. At San Francisco Joan discovers Dan is the prisoner, runs after him for one final goodbye and dies as he is taken toward the death house. On New Year's Eve in Acapulco, their doctor watches two cocktail glasses mysteriously break with their stems crossed in the X Dan and Joan used to mark their happiest moments, suggesting they have found each other after death.

title: Magic Town (1950-01-06)
plotSynopsis: Public-opinion expert Rip Smith discovers that the small town of Grandview is a mathematical mirror of the entire United States: its population, politics, income, religion, and voting patterns match national averages almost perfectly. Facing failure in his polling business, Rip secretly moves in as an insurance man and uses Grandview as a shortcut for national surveys. He also falls for local newspaper editor Mary Peterman, who is fighting for civic improvements and initially believes Rip has joined the town in good faith. Once his secret is exposed, national publicity turns Grandviewâ€™s status into a commercial craze, and the townspeople begin selling their opinions as if they were infallible. Their first self-conscious poll is spectacularly wrong, the boom collapses, and the town is humiliated. Rip then asks one final question: what does the average American do after making a mistake? Grandview answers by rebuilding together, proving its value not as a magic oracle but as a community capable of correcting itself, while Rip and Mary reconcile.

title: Tomorrow Is Forever (1950-01-13)
plotSynopsis: Lieutenant John MacDonald is horribly wounded and reported dead at the end of World War I. Believing his shattered body and face would only destroy the life of his young wife Elizabeth, he lets her think he died and builds a new identity as Austrian chemist Erik Kessler. Elizabeth, pregnant with Johnâ€™s child, eventually marries her kind employer Larry Hamilton and raises her son Drew in a loving home. More than twenty years later Kessler comes to work for Larry and quietly meets the son he never knew, just as another war is beginning. Elizabeth gradually recognizes John beneath the altered face and confronts him with their old memories, but he refuses to reclaim her, insisting that Larry is now her true husband and that the past must remain past. He brings Drew home after the boy tries to leave for Canada to enlist, then tells Elizabeth to let their son follow his conscience. Kessler dies the next morning, leaving Elizabeth to understand that his final act of love was to protect the life she built without him.

title: Mr Lucky (1950-01-20)
plotSynopsis: Professional gambler Joe Adams takes over a gambling ship and agrees to use it for Dorothy Bryant's wartime relief fundraiser, initially seeing the charity as just another angle. Dorothy's trust and love push Joe toward a life that is 'good and right and straight,' but his former partner Zepp tries to steal the night's receipts and forces Joe at gunpoint to carry the money away. Joe turns the tables, returns the entire bag to Dorothy's organization, and later sails for Greece with food and medical supplies. After his ship is reported torpedoed, Dorothy believes him dead until Joe unexpectedly returns to the pier, where the two reunite and Joe jokes that he has finally used up all the luck he ever had.

title: It Had to Be You (1950-01-27)
plotSynopsis: Wealthy young sculptor Vicki Stafford is preparing to marry the respectable Oliver Harrington when a dashing man named George suddenly steps out of her imagination and begins disrupting the match. George insists that he is only a figment created from Vickiâ€™s dreams and that his purpose is to keep her from marrying the wrong man. As Vicki falls in love with him, childhood photographs reveal the real source of the fantasy: George looks exactly like Johnny Blaine, the little boy Vicki adored years earlier. George understands that Vicki is not meant for a dream at all but for the real Johnny, and arranges one last interruption of the wedding by calling the fire department. Fireman Johnny Blaine arrives, Vicki recognizes him instantly, and George disappears with his mission complete as the two childhood sweethearts rediscover each other.

title: The Sea Wolf (1950-02-03)
plotSynopsis: After a ferry disaster, writer Humphrey Van Weyden and a young woman named Ruth are rescued by the sealing schooner Ghost, commanded by the brutal and intellectually formidable Wolf Larsen. Larsen rules his crew through fear, mocks compassion and religion, and refuses to let his unwilling passengers leave, forcing Van Weyden to confront a philosophy built entirely on strength and survival. As the voyage worsens, Larsen begins suffering violent headaches and periods of blindness, while his abused crew grows mutinous. An attack by Larsenâ€™s brother leaves the Ghost sinking and the crew gone. Van Weyden gets Ruth away in a lifeboat, then returns for supplies and finds Larsen alone, blind, and waist-deep in rising water. Larsen tries to keep Van Weyden with him so he will not die alone, but cannot stop his escape. The sinking captain is left reciting scripture, finally receiving the one thing he had never asked of anyone before: company at the edge of death.

title: This Thing Called Love (1950-02-10)
plotSynopsis: Business statistician Anne Collins returns from a whirlwind marriage in Rio convinced that romance should be managed scientifically. When her mining-engineer husband Tice comes home after three months away, Anne announces that they will test her new marriage theory with a four-month platonic trial, separate rooms and an intellectual rather than emotional relationship. Tice is appalled but plays along, while Anneâ€™s carefully organized experiment produces jealousy, misunderstandings and escalating schemes. Needing financing from family-minded Peruvian investor SeÃ±or de Estro, Tice falsely implies that Anne is expecting a baby, forcing both spouses deeper into comic deception. Their arguments make it increasingly obvious that neither statistics nor rules can contain their attraction. Anne finally abandons the experiment and rewrites her theory around the emotional reality of marriage, concluding that a wife sometimes needs to be kissed rather than analyzed.

title: Its in the Bag (1950-02-17)
plotSynopsis: Flea-circus operator Fred Floogle learns that his murdered Uncle Trumbull supposedly left him $300,000 hidden in one of a set of chairs that were sold at auction. Fred and his family chase the chairs from owner to owner while criminals and the uncle's lawyer Jefferson T. Pike pursue the same prize. The final chair exposes Pike as the uncle's killer and preserves the evidence against him, but Fred's hoped-for cash fortune turns out to be something else entirely: Trumbull's $300,000 is tied up in a murder story he wrote called Its in the Bag.

title: The Paleface (1950-03-03)
plotSynopsis: The governor sends Calamity Jane undercover to stop renegade Preston from smuggling rifles and dynamite to hostile Indians. To maintain her cover she joins a wagon train and marries timid dentist Painless Peter Potter, who believes he has suddenly become a legendary frontier gunfighter whenever Jane secretly shoots from behind him. Painless basks in his accidental reputation while Preston mistakes him for the government agent and targets him for death. Captured by the Indians, Painless finally learns that his new wife is really Calamity Jane and that all of his miraculous marksmanship was hers. The pair escape in Prestonâ€™s wagon, accidentally setting off the dynamite shipment and destroying the contraband before it reaches the Indians. With the mission complete, Jane admits she loves Painless, although another assignment immediately threatens their long-delayed honeymoon.

title: Portrait of Jenny (1950-03-10)
plotSynopsis: Struggling artist Eben Adams meets the mysterious Jennie in Central Park and discovers that each time she reappears she has aged years while almost no time has passed for him. Loving her transforms his work, and her portrait becomes the painting that finally gives his art life. Eben learns that Jennie belongs to another time and died in a New England storm, then races to the lighthouse where her fate is repeating. He reaches her but cannot defeat the great wave that takes her again. Years later, after Eben's own death, the story closes with the suggestion that the two have finally crossed time to reunite.

title: Champion (1950-03-17)
plotSynopsis: Midge Kelly is a poor, angry drifter who discovers that boxing may be his way out of a life in which he feels like a nobody. Trainer Tommy Haley sees talent in him and helps turn him into a contender, but success feeds Midgeâ€™s ambition faster than his character. He discards people when they no longer serve him, threatens former lover Grace, abandons loyal relationships and even refuses to leave training when his dying mother calls for him. By the time he reaches the championship, his brother Connie sees how thoroughly the fight business and Midgeâ€™s hunger for status have corrupted him. In a savage title defense against Johnny Dunne, Midge is beaten nearly senseless but refuses to let Tommy throw in the towel. He rallies, knocks Dunne out and hears the crowd finally cheering his name, only to collapse moments later and die. Connie bitterly gives the reporters the conventional line that Midge went out like a champion, even though the victory has cost him everything.

title: Chicago Deadline (1950-03-24)
plotSynopsis: Chicago reporter Ed Adams finds a young woman named Rosita dead of tuberculosis in a cheap hotel room and becomes obsessed with the address book she leaves behind. Working backward through its names, Ed discovers that Rosita had crossed paths with gamblers, wealthy financier G. G. Temple, gangster Sully Wellman, Blackie Franchot, John Spangler and others whose lives were damaged by the same violent circle. Temple had once struck Rosita and, believing he had killed her, relied on Sully to dispose of the body. Rosita was actually alive, and Spangler hid her until his unwanted advances drove her away again. Sully later killed Blackie and Spangler, used the secret to terrorize Temple into suicide, and tries to make Ed his fourth victim when the reporter finally reconstructs the chain. Belle Dorsett shoots Sully before he can kill Ed. Wounded and hospitalized, Ed knows he has finally met Rositaâ€™s funeral deadline: her story will be printed, and a woman who died almost unnoticed will at least be understood.

title: The Dark Mirror (1950-03-31)
plotSynopsis: Identical twins Ruth and Terry Collins frustrate a murder investigation because police cannot prove which sister was with Dr. Peralta when he was stabbed. Psychologist Dr. Scott studies the twins and discovers that gentle Ruth is innocent while Terry is a paranoid personality driven by jealousy and capable of murder. Terry tries to impersonate Ruth and eliminate the people closing in on her. Police finally trap her by faking Ruth's death, provoking Terry into revealing herself. Ruth survives, Terry is taken for psychiatric treatment, and Scott promises Ruth that they will wait for the day her sister can recover.

title: The Fighting O Flynn (1950-04-07)
plotSynopsis: Irish soldier of fortune Oâ€™Flynn returns home in 1797 and becomes entangled in a conspiracy tied to Napoleonâ€™s planned intervention in Ireland. His path repeatedly crosses Lady Benedetta, whose distrust gradually gives way to admiration as Oâ€™Flynn uncovers evidence that Lord Sedgemouth is working with the French and preparing a signal that will allow Bonaparteâ€™s forces to land. Branded a traitor and nearly executed, Oâ€™Flynn survives long enough to reach the fortress where the signal is to be sent. He scales the walls, defeats Sedgemouth in a sword fight, and prevents the rocket from being fired, leaving the French fleet waiting offshore for a signal that never comes. At dawn he returns wounded but victorious, and Benedetta finally admits that she no longer intends to resist him.

title: It Happens Every Spring (1950-04-14)
plotSynopsis: College chemistry professor Vernon Simpson accidentally creates a substance that makes baseballs behave impossibly around wooden bats. Keeping his discovery secret, he joins a major-league club under an assumed identity and becomes a sensational pitcher whose baffling delivery carries the team toward the pennant while his university colleagues and sweetheart wonder where he disappeared. When the chemical supply runs out, Vernon believes his career is finished, only to discover in the final game that he can still pitch well without it. He returns to the university with baseball earnings, his scientific future restored, and his romance intact.

title: A Kiss in the Dark (1950-04-21)
plotSynopsis: Concert pianist Eric Phillips unexpectedly becomes owner of the Cleopatra Arms apartment house and initially sees its tenants and problems as annoyances distracting him from his career. Model Polly Haynes and devoted manager Willoughby gradually force him to see the people behind the property, especially after he learns Willoughby ruined himself financially trying to care for the building and its residents. Eric begins using his money and influence to solve their problems instead of escaping them, restores Willoughby as manager for life, and discovers that his growing concern for the tenants is inseparable from his love for Polly.

title: Rope of Sand (1950-04-28)
plotSynopsis: Mike Davis returns to South Africa two years after being tortured by the diamond syndicate, determined to recover a cache of stones he hid in the forbidden desert. Syndicate men Martingale and Vogel use dancer Suzanne Renaud to win Mike's confidence and learn the location, but Suzanne falls in love with him and secretly tries to keep him alive. Mike gives her a map, then discovers it was passed to Vogel and believes she betrayed him. After surviving another attempt on his life, Mike recovers the diamonds. The final confrontation exposes Vogel as a killer and Martingale manipulates events so Vogel dies rather than share the fortune. Martingale then reveals Suzanne surrendered the map only to protect Mike, and Mike leaves Africa with both the diamonds and the woman he nearly misjudged.

title: When My Baby Smiles at Me (1950-05-05)
plotSynopsis: Burlesque partners Skid Johnson and Bonnie Kane marry and build an act together, but Skid's Broadway success, drinking and involvement with dancer Sylvia Marco pull him away from Bonnie and eventually break up their partnership. Bonnie tries to move on while Skid's career and health collapse under alcohol, leaving him barely able to perform. When she finds him failing backstage, Bonnie returns to the act, holds him up through the number and reveals that she never married the wealthy rancher who courted her because she still loves Skid; the pair reunite onstage and off.

title: Butch Minds the Baby (1950-05-12)
plotSynopsis: Paroled safecracker Big Butch is trying to stay straight when gangster Harry the Horse recruits him for one more job. Butch agrees only because widowed Susie O'Neill and her baby Michael desperately need money, and the robbery becomes farcical when he has to mind the baby at the same time. After the safe is blown, Butch tries to return a stolen check so its owner will avoid tax trouble and so Michael can win a promised baby-contest prize. His parole officer discovers the scheme, but recognizes that Butch's motive was to help Susie rather than enrich himself. Butch still expects to answer for the crime, yet walks away feeling that for once he has come out on top by doing something for someone else.

title: Miss Grant Takes Richmond (1950-05-19)
plotSynopsis: Inexperienced secretary Ellen Grant is hired by Dick Richmond's real-estate office without realizing that the business is largely a respectable front for illegal bookmaking. Taking the company at face value, Ellen enthusiastically proposes an affordable housing development and is put in charge, forcing Richmond and his partners to turn their fake operation into a real construction project to protect their cover. Her chaotic management creates comic disasters, but the houses become genuine and worthwhile. Ellen's faith in Richmond pushes him away from the racket, and the scheme that began as camouflage ends by giving him a legitimate business and a romance with the secretary who accidentally reformed it.

title: Flamingo Road (1950-05-26)
plotSynopsis: Carnival dancer Lane Bellamy leaves the road behind and tries to build a respectable life in a small Southern town, but political boss Sheriff Titus Semple decides she is unsuitable for deputy Fielding Carlisle and uses his power to drive them apart. Lane later marries businessman Dan Reynolds and enters the world of local politics, where Semple's machine keeps tightening its grip. As corruption and personal revenge collide, Semple comes to Lane's home armed and threatens her. She kills him in self-defense, the grand jury clears her, and the collapse of Semple's political machine gives Lane and Dan a chance to start over on Flamingo Road.

title: She Wouldnt Say Yes (1950-06-02)
plotSynopsis: Psychiatrist Susan Lane meets irrepressible cartoonist Michael Kent, creator of the mischievous Nixie, and is immediately irritated by his determination to turn every encounter into a romance. Their feud follows them onto a train, through Susanâ€™s treatment of an emotionally troubled young woman, and into a string of schemes in which each tries to prove the other is the one behaving irrationally. Susan insists she is too disciplined and well balanced to fall in love, while Michael keeps forcing her to confront the feelings she is trying to diagnose away. When jealousy and a rival blonde finally push Susan past her professional defenses, she admits that she loves Michael and asks him to marry her. He briefly needles her by walking away, then returns with lilacs, and Susan happily accepts the emotional disorder she had spent the story trying to cure.

title: Mr Blandings Builds His Dream House (1950-06-09)
plotSynopsis: New York advertising executive Jim Blandings and his wife Muriel flee their cramped apartment for what looks like an idyllic Connecticut farmhouse, only to learn that the old house must be torn down and their affordable country dream rebuilt from scratch. Construction costs explode through rock blasting, a vanishing water supply, an endlessly deep well and one expensive surprise after another until Jim's planned $10,000 home becomes a roughly $48,000 ordeal. At the same time he is under pressure to invent a new slogan for the Wham Ham account. Household worker Gussie casually supplies the winning line, saving Jim's job, and after all the grief, debt and jealousy, Jim admits that if he had to do it over again he would still build the dream house.

title: The Strange Love of Martha Ivers (1950-06-23)
plotSynopsis: As a child Martha Ivers kills her domineering aunt while Walter O'Neil witnesses the crime, and their later testimony helps send an innocent man to his death. Years afterward Martha controls Iverstown and is trapped in a bitter marriage to Walter when childhood friend Sam Masterson unexpectedly returns. Martha and Walter fear Sam knows their secret, but Sam reveals he left before the killing and never witnessed it. Martha tries to draw Sam back into her life and ultimately urges him to remove Walter, but he refuses to become part of their guilt and walks away. Left together with the truth and their hatred, Martha and Walter bring their destructive marriage to a fatal end.

title: Shadow of a Doubt (1950-11-09)
plotSynopsis: Young Charlie Newton is thrilled when her adored Uncle Charlie visits the family in Santa Rosa, but clues from two investigators and a newspaper story make her realize he is the wanted 'Merry Widow Murderer.' She keeps silent to protect her mother while trying to force him to leave, and Uncle Charlie responds by attempting to kill her, including trapping her in a garage filling with exhaust. Their final struggle ends with Uncle Charlie dead, while the family believes his death was accidental. Charlie alone is left with the knowledge that the charming uncle she worshiped was a serial killer.

title: Lifeboat (1950-11-16)
plotSynopsis: Survivors of a ship torpedoed in the Atlantic crowd into a lifeboat, joined by Willi, a German from the U-boat that sank them. The Americans and Britons argue over whether to trust him, but gradually surrender navigation and survival decisions to the calm, capable sailor. They discover too late that Willi has hidden water and supplies, deceived them about their course and is steering them toward a German vessel; after the injured Gus dies and Willi's betrayal becomes undeniable, the survivors turn on and kill him. Forced to row and think for themselves, they are finally spotted during a naval battle and expect rescue. When another young German sailor climbs aboard with a gun, they disarm rather than kill him, ending with the unresolved question of what war requires people to become.

title: Cluny Brown (1950-11-23)
plotSynopsis: Free-spirited Cluny Brown has an inconvenient passion for plumbing that her uncle considers improper for a young woman, and she is sent into domestic service at an English country estate to learn her place. There she meets refugee professor Adam Belinski, another outsider who recognizes how badly Cluny fits the rigid social rules around her. Cluny tries to become respectable by accepting the attentions of conventional pharmacist Mr. Wilson, but her impulse to repair the plumbing during his mother's formal party proves that she cannot turn herself into the woman he expects. Wilson recoils, while Belinski offers Cluny a life where her impulses are part of who she is rather than a disgrace. She leaves with him, becoming Mrs. Belinski and trading a prescribed place in society for an uncertain but shared future.

title: Mrs Mike (1950-11-30)
plotSynopsis: Boston-raised Kathy O'Fallon marries Mountie Sergeant Mike Flanagan and follows him into the isolated Canadian North, where she must learn to live with brutal cold, cultural differences, scarce supplies and Mike's responsibility for everyone in his enormous district. The hardships gradually become part of their shared life until an epidemic sweeps the settlement. Despite Mike's efforts and the eventual arrival of serum, their baby dies, and Kathy, overwhelmed by grief, decides she cannot survive the North and leaves. Mike transfers back to his old post believing he has lost her. Kathy ultimately turns back after seeing another frontier family recover from the loss of a child, telling Mike that they cannot let the North defeat them and that, together, they will keep fighting it.

title: My Favorite Wife (1950-12-07)
plotSynopsis: After seven years missing at sea, Ellen Arden returns home on the very day her husband Nick has finally had her declared legally dead and married Bianca. Ellen tries to reclaim her place without immediately shattering the children or the new marriage, while Nick desperately searches for a legal and emotional way out of the absurd situation. Matters get worse when Nick learns Ellen spent the shipwreck years on an island with another man, provoking a new round of jealousy and concealment. The complications finally collapse under the truth, Bianca is released from the mistaken marriage, and Nick and Ellen reunite as husband and wife.

title: The Lady Gambles (1950-12-14)
plotSynopsis: Newspaper wife Joan Booth accompanies her husband David to Las Vegas and treats casino gambling as harmless vacation excitement. A small win and the attention of casino manager Corrigan awaken a compulsion she cannot control; soon she is borrowing money, chasing losses, lying to David, and choosing the tables over her marriage. Her addiction carries her from respectable casinos to private games and eventually to the bottom, where she is found beaten and nearly destroyed after a year away from her husband. David refuses to abandon her and works with doctors to uncover the fear, resentment, and family wounds feeding the obsession. A final emotional confrontation with her sister Ruth forces Joan to face the truth instead of escaping into gambling. When David reaches for her, Joan finally reaches back, accepts his help, and leaves with him determined to begin again.

title: Miracle on 34th Street (1950-12-21)
plotSynopsis: When the Santa hired for Macyâ€™s Thanksgiving parade is found drinking, a kindly old man named Kris Kringle takes his place and soon becomes the department storeâ€™s most convincing Santa. Kris insists that he truly is Santa Claus, winning the trust of practical-minded little Susan while challenging the skepticism of her mother Doris. Lawyer Fred Gailey believes in Kris and also hopes to break through Dorisâ€™s guarded outlook. After store psychologist Sawyer helps have Kris committed to Bellevue, Kris deliberately fails his examination in despair, but Fred persuades him not to give up and takes his case to court. The judge demands authoritative proof of Krisâ€™s identity, and the case turns when the Post Office delivers nine truckloads of letters addressed simply to Santa Claus, effectively recognizing Kris as their proper recipient. The case is dismissed. Susan and Doris both affirm their belief, while Kris quietly points Fred toward a Cape Cod cottage that could give Fred, Doris and Susan the family home Susan has wished for.

title: Alias Nick Beal (1950-12-28)
plotSynopsis: Idealistic district attorney Joseph Foster is desperate to convict racketeer Hanson when mysterious Nick Beal offers him the evidence he needs. Each favor draws Foster deeper into compromise: forged books win the case, political influence carries him toward the governor's office, and Beal plants glamorous Donna Allen beside him while gradually isolating him from his wife and conscience. Foster finally realizes Beal's bargains amount to a claim on his soul. After resigning the governorship rather than serve the corrupt interests that elected him, Foster is still bound by a written contract requiring him to follow Beal. Reverend Garfield places the agreement inside a Bible, which Beal cannot take, breaking his hold. Foster is saved, while Beal withdraws to wait for other people willing to make the same bargain.

title: Prince of Foxes (1951-01-04)
plotSynopsis: In Renaissance Italy, soldier and artist Andrea Orsini serves the ruthless Cesare Borgia, who values Andreaâ€™s wit and deceit as much as another manâ€™s sword. Borgia sends him as ambassador to the mountain city of CittÃ  del Monte so he can undermine its ruler, Count Marc Antonio Varano, from within. Instead, Andrea comes to admire Varanoâ€™s honor and falls in love with his wifeâ€™s kinswoman Camilla, turning against Borgia when conquest threatens the city. After CittÃ  del Monte resists, Andrea is captured and condemned; Borgiaâ€™s lieutenant Don Esteban blinds him and leaves him as a warning. Andrea slowly recovers his sight in secret and organizes an uprising through a hidden entrance to the castle. He frees Camilla, kills Esteban in a duel, and helps the people retake the city, choosing resistance to Borgia and a future with Camilla over the cynical service that once made him a prince among foxes.

title: Ivy (1951-01-11)
plotSynopsis: Ambitious Ivy Lexton wants a richer life than her husband Jim can provide and secretly carries on with doctor Roger Gretorex while setting her sights on millionaire Miles Rushworth. She steals poison from Roger's dispensary and murders Jim, allowing suspicion to fall on Roger, who confesses rather than expose the woman he loves. As Roger's execution approaches, a witness finally admits seeing Ivy take the poison and the police uncover both motive and evidence. Roger is reprieved, Miles rejects Ivy after learning what the police know, and the fortune-teller's prophecy that has haunted Ivy closes in on her. With nowhere left to run, Ivy calls Detective Lieutenant Martin and says she will be waiting for him.

title: The Big Lift (1951-01-18)
plotSynopsis: American airmen Hank and Danny are sent into the Berlin Airlift, flying food and supplies into a city cut off by the Soviet blockade. Hank is openly suspicious of Germans after the war, while Danny becomes romantically involved with Frederica, a young German woman whose ruined city and uncertain future awaken his sympathy. Their experiences gradually force both men to look beyond wartime labels and confront what occupation, defeat, and democracy mean in everyday life. Danny proposes to Frederica, only to discover a letter revealing that she has been using him as a path to the United States while planning to reunite with another man there. Hurt, he breaks off the marriage. Hank, meanwhile, learns from Gerta that democracy includes the freedom to challenge authority, and both airmen leave Berlin with a more complicated understanding of the people they had first judged so simply.

title: Spellbound (1951-01-25)
plotSynopsis: Psychoanalyst Constance Peterson falls in love with the newly arrived Dr. Edwards, then discovers that the man is an amnesiac impostor who cannot remember his own identity and fears he may have murdered the real Edwards. Constance follows him when he flees and, with her old mentor Dr. Brulov, uses his dreams and phobias to recover the buried memories behind his guilt. He finally remembers that he is John Ballantine, an Army veteran whose childhood trauma came from accidentally causing his brotherâ€™s fatal fall, and that Dr. Edwards died during a skiing trip at Gabriel Valley. A bullet in Edwardsâ€™s body seems to condemn John after all, but Constance interprets the final symbols in his dream and realizes that retiring hospital chief Dr. Murchison had followed Edwards to the resort and shot him. She confronts Murchison, talks her way past his gun, and calls the police, clearing John and freeing the couple to marry.

title: Take a Letter Darling (1951-02-01)
plotSynopsis: Advertising executive A.M. MacGregor hires artist Tom Verney as her male secretary, expecting him to provide the social charm that helps her handle conservative male clients. Tom resents being treated as a decorative employee, but the two become increasingly dependent on one another while wealthy Southern client Jonathan Caldwell complicates matters by courting Mac. Tom's outrageous parting gift finally blows up Mac's expected match with Caldwell, and when she realizes Tom is leaving for Mexico she abandons the business-first pose and admits she is in love with him.

title: Lucky Jordan (1951-02-08)
plotSynopsis: Self-centered racketeer Lucky Jordan is drafted into the Army and immediately looks for a way around service, only to become entangled with a stolen briefcase containing sensitive military plans. At first Lucky treats the papers like any other commodity and considers selling them for a fortune, while Jill tries to make him understand that the war and the country's survival affect even a man who believes only in himself. Rival gangsters and enemy agents pursue the plans, forcing Lucky to use the same street instincts that built his criminal career to recover and protect them. By the end, his cynicism has given way to a reluctant sense of responsibility, and he chooses his country over the payoff he once wanted.

title: Dark Victory (1951-02-15)
plotSynopsis: Wealthy, reckless Judith Traherne learns that a brain tumor has left her only a short time to live, even though surgeon Frederick Steele initially tries to shield her from the full prognosis. Anger and fear drive Judith back toward drinking and self-destruction, but her love for Fred finally gives her a reason to face death rather than flee from it. They marry and build a quiet life together, knowing that sudden blindness will signal the end. When that moment comes, Judith insists Fred leave on an important medical trip so he will remember her courage instead of watching her die. She says goodbye, arranges for a friend to care for him, lies down alone with his pillow beside her, and meets death without fear, calling that courage their victory over the dark.

title: No Minor Vices (1951-02-22)
plotSynopsis: Pediatrician Perry Ashwell casually dismisses artist Octavio Quaglini's work as junk, inspiring the flamboyant painter to teach the smug doctor a lesson in emotion.
