Octavio insinuates himself into Perry's home and marriage, deliberately stirring jealousy by charming Perry's wife April and making Perry believe his secure domestic life may not be so secure after all. The comic scheme ultimately makes Perry and April recognize how much they need one another, while Octavio leaves satisfied that he has finally learned how to suffer and has shaken the doctor out of complacency.

title: A Foreign Affair (1951-03-01)
plotSynopsis: Iowa congresswoman Phoebe Frost arrives in occupied Berlin to investigate the morals of American troops and quickly discovers evidence that nightclub singer Erika von SchlÃ¼tow, a former Nazi favorite, is being protected by an American officer. That officer is Captain John Pringle, who has been supplying Erika with food and favors while keeping her off labor details. To divert Phoebeâ€™s investigation, John romances the prim congresswoman, only to find himself genuinely falling for her. Military intelligence then orders him to continue seeing Erika as bait for her fugitive Nazi lover, Hans Otto Birgel. Erika exposes Johnâ€™s double life to Phoebe just as the trap closes. Birgel emerges at the nightclub and tries to kill John and Erika, but military police shoot him first. Once Phoebe learns that John was acting under orders, the pair reconcile, while Erika is finally taken away to a labor detail.

title: Bachelor Mother (1951-03-08)
plotSynopsis: Department-store clerk Polly Parish finds an abandoned baby and is mistaken for its mother, a misunderstanding that follows her back to work when the foundling home and her employers decide she must accept responsibility for the child. Store heir David Merlin becomes personally involved in Polly's predicament and gradually falls in love with her, while his father becomes convinced the baby is David's own secret son. By the time Polly can explain that she is not the mother at all, David no longer cares: he publicly claims the child as his, declares that he and Polly are marrying that night, and only then learns she still has one final surprise about the baby's true parentage.

title: Thelma Jordan (1951-03-15)
plotSynopsis: Assistant district attorney Cleve Marshall, unhappy at home and drinking after hours, meets the mysterious Thelma Jordan when she comes to the district attorneyâ€™s office about supposed break-ins at the home of her wealthy aunt Vera. Cleve begins an affair with her, unaware that Thelma and her lover Tony Laredo have been planning to rob Vera. When Vera catches Thelma at the safe, Thelma shoots her and then calls Cleve, who becomes trapped into destroying evidence and helping construct her alibi. Cleve later prosecutes the very case he has compromised, and Thelma is acquitted. After the trial Tony returns to claim Thelma and her inheritance, while Cleve finally forces the truth into the open. Thelma admits killing Vera and admits Cleve was meant to be the useful man inside the law, but she also reveals that her feelings for him became real. She leaves with Tony, deliberately drives their car into a crash, and gives a final confession that protects Cleve from being exposed as her Mr. X. Cleve loses his law career, but survives with the possibility of repairing his life with his wife Pamela.

title: The Great Lover (1951-03-22)
plotSynopsis: Freddie Hunter, an insecure scoutmaster sailing for Europe with his boys, tries to remake himself into a sophisticated ladies' man after meeting a beautiful Duchess and her gambling father. His attempts at high-stakes poker and romance put him in the path of a mysterious card-table murderer, and Freddie soon becomes the chief suspect and has to hide while the ship searches for him. The real killer is Dabney, who plans to murder Freddie and the Duchess and make their deaths look like another disappearance. Freddie and his unlikely canine ally expose and subdue Dabney, clearing Freddie's name and leaving him free to pursue the Duchess as the ship reaches shore.

title: Next Time We Love (1951-03-29)
plotSynopsis: Young journalist Chris Tyler and actress Sicily marry for love, but their careers repeatedly pull them apart. Chris's foreign assignments and professional setbacks leave Sicily supporting their child through a rising stage career, while loyal friend Tommy remains in love with her and offers the steadier life Chris cannot provide. Years of separation finally bring Chris and Sicily to talk of divorce, with Chris claiming he no longer loves her and urging her toward Tommy. Sicily refuses to believe him and discovers the truth when Chris collapses: he has been hiding a serious illness in a sanitarium because he did not want to burden her. Their love survives the years of missed chances, and Sicily retires at the height of her career to remain with Chris for whatever time they have left together.

title: The Damned Dont Cry (1951-04-05)
plotSynopsis: Ethel Whitehead escapes a life of poverty by remaking herself as the sophisticated Lorna Hansen Forbes, but every step upward draws her deeper into George Castleman's criminal organization. Ambition, luxury and divided loyalties cost her the people who once mattered to her, while her relationship with Castleman's rival Nick Prenta turns the underworld power struggle personal. After Nick is killed, Ethel finally turns against the racket and gives the full story to a newspaperman so other desperate women will understand the price of taking her path. Castleman comes for her in the final confrontation; Ethel is wounded, but his attempt to silence her is stopped and she is left to face what her ambition has cost.

title: Hired Wife (1951-04-12)
plotSynopsis: Cement-company owner Stephen Dexter faces a legal maneuver that could freeze his business and property. His lawyer suggests a technical escape: marry immediately, transfer everything to his wife, and divorce later. Stephen intends to marry glamorous Phyllis Walden, but his indispensable secretary Kendall Browning, who has long hidden her love for him behind strict efficiency, ends up becoming the temporary wife instead. Once Kendall controls the property, she proves far better at protecting the company than Stephen expected and refuses to surrender her new position on command. Their supposedly businesslike marriage becomes a comic battle involving Phyllis, a suspicious creditor, a chaperone, and Stephenâ€™s growing jealousy. After the company is saved, Stephen finally realizes that the woman he cannot run his business without is also the woman he loves, only to be reminded that he and Kendall are already married.

title: Humoresque (1951-04-19)
plotSynopsis: Brilliant but hard-edged society woman Helen Wright becomes fascinated by gifted young violinist Paul Boray and uses her money and connections to help his career, even as their attraction grows into an affair. Paul rises to concert fame while Helenâ€™s marriage collapses, and her husband eventually agrees to a divorce. Yet Helen comes to understand that Paulâ€™s deepest commitment is not to any woman but to his music, and that her own drinking, restlessness, and need to escape would eventually damage the life he has built. After speaking with Paulâ€™s longtime friend Gina and his mother, Helen refuses Paulâ€™s plan to abandon his career and run away with her. She ends their relationship instead, telling him that music is in his bones and that he cannot escape the genius that has taken possession of his life.

title: Jackpot (1951-04-26)
plotSynopsis: Bill and Amy Lawrence seem to strike it rich when Bill wins a radio jackpot made up of thousands of dollars in merchandise, only to discover that the prizes create a huge income-tax bill and almost no cash to pay it. Bill desperately tries to sell everything from soup to watches, loses his job in the process, and nearly wrecks his marriage when Amy mistakes artist Hilda Jones's secret portrait of her for evidence of an affair. A recovered $5,000 payment for a lost prize gives the family enough to meet the tax crisis, Bill lands an even better job, and the couple finally escapes for a vacation. When another giveaway program calls, they refuse to answer and want nothing more to do with jackpots.

title: Captain from Castile (1951-05-03)
plotSynopsis: Young Spanish nobleman Pedro de Vargas defies the Inquisition after its cruel chief, Diego de Silva, falsely accuses his family of heresy and tortures Pedroâ€™s young sister to death. With help from peasant Juan Garcia and the devoted Catana, Pedro escapes prison, kills de Silva in a duel, gets his parents to safety, and flees Spain. Rather than hide in Europe, he joins HernÃ¡n CortÃ©sâ€™s expedition to the New World, where he and Catana marry. Pedro later protects CortÃ©sâ€™s treasure and is nearly framed and hanged when conspirators steal precious jewels through a secret passage. He exposes the thieves, survives the expeditionâ€™s internal betrayals, and resumes the march toward Montezumaâ€™s realm with Catana beside him, choosing the uncertain new world over the old life he can no longer return to.

title: No Time for Love (1951-05-10)
plotSynopsis: Sophisticated magazine photographer Katherine Grant is assigned to photograph the sandhogs building a tunnel under the river and immediately clashes with rough, self-confident worker Jim Ryan. After Ryan is injured protecting her during a construction accident, Kate hires him as a model and sets out to prove that his swagger, manners and physical appeal are completely incompatible with her cultured life and her relationship with wealthy Henry Fulton. Every attempt to make Ryan look ridiculous only makes Kate more attracted to him, while Ryan refuses to be reshaped into the kind of man she thinks she should want. When Kate finally stops treating her feelings as an experiment, she chooses Ryan openly, leaving Henry and her carefully designed ideas about romance behind.

title: Rogues Regiment (1951-05-17)
plotSynopsis: American intelligence agent Whit Corbett enters the French Foreign Legion in Indochina to identify Nazi war criminal Martin Bruner, whose face and identity have disappeared among thousands of former soldiers. Working with French agent Lili and Colonel Mauclaire, Corbett follows a trail of gunrunning, forged papers and hidden money. Dying Legionnaire Heinrich finally reveals that the man called Riker is Bruner. Corbett tracks him to Saigon, where Bruner tries to escape with a forged passport, a fortune hidden in platinum tools and Lili as a hostage. Corbett overpowers him and brings him back alive; the story closes with Bruner executed for his war crimes.

title: Back Street (1951-05-24)
plotSynopsis: Ray and Walter fall deeply in love, but a missed meeting and circumstance leave Walter married to Corinne while Ray becomes the hidden woman in his life. For twenty-five years she accepts a back-street existence so Walter can keep his family, children and rising banking career, even refusing to demand the divorce that would make their relationship public. When Walter dies after years of divided loyalties, Ray is left alone with the memory of the life they might have shared and dies soon afterward with his final words still in her heart.

title: Beyond Glory (1951-05-31)
plotSynopsis: Combat veteran Rocky Gilman enters West Point after World War II and becomes a symbol of the Academy's honor system during a congressional investigation, only to have opposing counsel expose an old accusation that Rocky disobeyed orders in Tunisia and caused Captain Daniels' death. Rocky himself believes the charge because combat trauma has distorted his memory, and he refuses to defend his reputation. A psychiatrist and fellow veteran finally reconstruct the battle and prove that Rocky was knocked unconscious by a tank blast during the critical minutes and could not have committed the alleged disobedience. Vindicated, Rocky graduates from West Point with his faith in himself and the Academy restored.

title: The Gunfighter (1951-06-07)
plotSynopsis: Notorious gunman Jimmy Ringo comes to town hoping for one quiet meeting with estranged wife Peggy and the young son who barely knows him. His reputation makes peace almost impossible: crowds gather, three brothers hunt him for revenge, and young would-be gunfighters dream of becoming famous by killing him. Marshal Mark Strett buys Jimmy enough time to see Peggy and arrange a possible future reunion, but as Ringo leaves, swaggering Hunt Bromley shoots him from ambush. Dying, Ringo falsely says he drew first so Bromley will escape the law, then condemns him to the same life he hated: forever watching for the next young gun who wants fame by killing the man who killed Jimmy Ringo.

title: The Ghost Breakers (1951-06-14)
plotSynopsis: Radio crime-buster Larry Lawrence is hired by Mary Carter, who has inherited Black Island off Cuba and the ominous Castillo Maldito. The castle is reputed to be haunted, but Larry follows Mary to the island despite gangsters, warnings, and a very convincing zombie. Inside the castle the pair discover that the supernatural effects are being manufactured to frighten Mary away from a valuable mine on the property. Montgomery and his confederates are behind the ghostly tricks, while Frenchy Duvall closes in from another direction. The rival villains finally shoot each other, the police take control, and Mary keeps the mine. Larry leaves Cuba rich enough to joke about financing her television career, still insisting there are no such things as ghosts even after everything they have seen.

title: DOA (1951-06-21)
plotSynopsis: Accountant and notary Frank Bigelow walks into a police station to report a murder, his own. While on a trip to San Francisco, someone slipped a lethal luminous poison into his drink, leaving him only days to live. Frank spends those final hours tracing the reason for his murder to a notarized bill of sale involving stolen iridium, a dead man named George Reynolds, and businessman Eugene Phillips. Each clue leads deeper into blackmail, murder, and an effort to silence anyone connected with the document. Frank finally identifies Halliday as the man who poisoned him at the Fisherman club and kills his own murderer in a final confrontation. After completing his statement to the police, Frank collapses and dies; the official report is marked with the grim abbreviation D.O.A., dead on arrival.

title: The Lady Takes a Chance (1951-06-28)
plotSynopsis: New York bank teller Molly J. Truesdale spends her savings on a fourteen-day guided tour of the West, expecting scenery and a brief escape from her orderly life. At a rodeo she literally catches cowboy Duke Hudkins when a bronco throws him, and the chance meeting turns into a romance. Molly abandons part of her scheduled tour to travel with Duke and his friend Waco, discovering that life with a cowboy means rough roads, horses, camp food, and a man who is far more comfortable making decisions than discussing feelings. Their attraction repeatedly collides with Mollyâ€™s independence and Dukeâ€™s stubbornness, and she finally returns to New York convinced the adventure is over. Duke follows her there, sweeps her back onto the same western bus route, and announces that they will marry when the bus reaches Phoenix. Molly protests every step of the way, but this time she willingly takes the chance on him.

title: Only Yesterday (1951-07-05)
plotSynopsis: In World War I, young Mary Lane secretly marries soldier Jim Emerson just before his regiment is sent overseas. Mary soon learns she is pregnant and moves to New York, where she gives birth to their son while waiting for Jim to come home. But a wartime concussion leaves Jim with shell shock and large gaps in his memory, including his marriage to Mary, and she raises their son without him while sending unsigned New Year greetings year after year. On the eve of the 1929 crash they meet again as strangers and are instinctively drawn to each other, though Jim still cannot place her. Years later, as Mary is dying, a final letter reaches Jim and restores the missing truth. He comes to her bedside, recognizes the love he lost, and meets their son at last, beginning the father-son relationship Mary had waited years to make possible.

title: The Fugitive (1951-07-12)
plotSynopsis: In a Latin American country where religion has been outlawed, a hunted priest moves secretly among the poor, trying to continue his ministry while the authorities close in. Fearful and imperfect, he nevertheless risks capture to hear confessions, celebrate Mass, and bring comfort to people who still depend on him. A police lieutenant determined to eradicate the old faith takes hostages and pursues him relentlessly, while Maria Dolores and others help the priest hide. The priest is finally captured after answering what he believes is a dying manâ€™s call and is sentenced to death. Before the firing squad he asks Maria to tell his village to keep faith, insisting that killing him will kill only a man and that someone else will carry the faith forward. Even the lieutenant is shaken by the execution and retreats to drink, unable to erase what the priest represented.

title: Remember the Night (1951-07-19)
plotSynopsis: Assistant district attorney John Sargent prosecutes shoplifter Lee Leander just before Christmas, then delays the case when he realizes a holiday jury may acquit her out of sympathy. Feeling guilty about leaving her jailed over Christmas, he arranges bail and, learning she grew up near his own Indiana home, takes her along for the holiday. John's warm family gives Lee the first real sense of belonging she has known, and she and John fall in love. He even offers her the chance to remain across the Canadian border, but Lee refuses to damage the career he worked so hard to build. Back in court John subtly tries to lose the case, so Lee stops him by pleading guilty. Before sentencing he asks her to marry him; she chooses to serve her time first, certain that if he still wants her afterward they can begin honestly and as equals.

title: Stairway to Heaven (1951-07-26)
plotSynopsis: RAF pilot Peter Carter should die when he jumps from a burning aircraft without a parachute, but a celestial mistake lets him survive long enough to meet and fall in love with American radio operator June. When heaven's messenger returns to correct the error, Peter appeals for the right to keep the life he was accidentally given. On earth, neurologist Frank Reeves diagnoses a brain condition and prepares Peter for surgery; in Peter's other reality, Reeves serves as his advocate before a heavenly court. June proves the depth of their love by offering her own life for Peter, and the court grants the appeal. Peter survives the operation with a new date of death far in the future and the chance to live the life he and June nearly lost.

title: Caged (1951-08-02)
plotSynopsis: Young widow Marie Allen enters womenâ€™s prison for taking part in a forty-dollar robbery committed with her late husband and discovers she is pregnant soon after arrival. Frightened and determined to serve her time cleanly, she is caught between humane superintendent Ruth Benton and brutal matron Evelyn Harper, whose corruption and cruelty help turn prison into a school for crime. Marie gives birth behind bars, but when neither her mother nor the institution can legally keep the baby for her until parole, the child is placed for adoption. A friend dies after being denied release, Harperâ€™s abuse hardens Marie further, and professional criminals begin offering her an easier path outside. By the time parole finally comes, Marie rejects an honest job arranged for her and chooses a criminal connection instead, trading her wedding ring and innocence for the promise of real diamonds and fast money. Benton orders her file kept active, certain the system that helped harden Marie will soon bring her back.

title: Wuthering Heights (1951-08-09)
plotSynopsis: Cathy and the orphan Heathcliff grow up together at Wuthering Heights with a fierce love that neither can escape, but Cathy's desire for position leads her to marry the gentler, wealthier Edgar Linton. Heathcliff returns after years away with money and bitterness, using Edgar's sister Isabella and ownership of Wuthering Heights as instruments of revenge while Cathy is torn between the life she chose and the man she still loves. Their reunion comes too late: Cathy dies after Heathcliff reaches her, and he begs her spirit to haunt him rather than leave him alone. Years later, witnesses see Cathy and Heathcliff together on the moors, suggesting the lovers finally found each other beyond death.

title: The Ghost and Mrs Muir (1951-08-16)
plotSynopsis: Widowed Lucy Muir moves with her daughter into Gull Cottage despite warnings that the seaside house is haunted by its late owner, the irascible Captain Daniel Gregg. Lucy refuses to be frightened away, and when money troubles threaten her home, Daniel dictates his colorful sea memoir, Blood and Swash, while she puts it on paper. Their unusual partnership deepens into love, but Daniel urges Lucy to live among the living. She falls for writer Miles Fairley, only to discover that he is already married. Daniel, believing he is standing in the way of her earthly life, has already made her think their years together were only a dream. Lucy grows old at Gull Cottage with only fragments of those memories, and when she finally dies Daniel returns, restores her youthful spirit, and takes her with him into the afterlife.

title: The Velvet Touch (1951-08-23)
plotSynopsis: Broadway star Valerie Stanton kills her controlling producer Gordon Dunning during a struggle after he threatens to destroy her chance to leave him and marry Michael Morrell. Valerie hides her role while Gordon's former lover Marian Webster falls under suspicion, then Marian's despair ends in suicide and deepens Valerie's guilt. During rehearsals for a new play built around a staged suicide, Valerie can no longer sustain the performance of innocence and finally gives herself up to Captain Danbury.

title: Mother Is a Freshman (1951-08-30)
plotSynopsis: Widowed Abigail Fortitude Abbott is nearly broke but must keep her daughter Susan at Pointer College, so she exploits an old family scholarship by enrolling there as a freshman herself. Abby soon falls for English professor Richard Michaels, only to discover that Susan has a serious crush on the same man and sees her own mother as a rival. Abby prepares to give Richard up for her daughter, but Susan finally accepts that Richard loves Abby and steps aside, allowing Abby and Richard to plan their marriage.

title: Broken Arrow (1951-09-07)
plotSynopsis: Prospector Tom Jeffords comes to believe peace is possible between white settlers and the Chiricahua Apache and earns the trust of Cochise. Jeffords helps bring General Howard to negotiate a three-month armistice and later a treaty based on Apache equality and security on their own land. During the peace effort Jeffords marries Apache woman Sonseeahray, but renegade whites led by Slade ambush them and kill her. Grief-stricken Jeffords wants revenge, yet Cochise refuses to let either bad whites or bad Indians destroy the agreement. The armistice holds, and Sonseeahray's death becomes part of the sacrifice that seals a lasting peace.

title: Raffles (1951-09-14)
plotSynopsis: Gentleman thief A.J. Raffles wants to abandon crime for Gwen, but old friend Bunny's desperate financial trouble pulls him into one final burglary. At Lord Melrose's house Raffles plans to steal a valuable emerald necklace, only to find another burglar already in Lady Melrose's room. Raffles overpowers the intruder and takes the jewels himself, then repeatedly outmaneuvers Inspector Mackenzie while Gwen realizes the truth about the man she loves. When Scotland Yard finally identifies Raffles as the amateur cracksman, he admits it, returns the emeralds and directs Lord Melrose's promised reward to Bunny. Raffles escapes before arrest, but risks one last visit to Gwen to tell her he loves her before disappearing through the window.

title: No Man Of Her Own (1951-09-21)
plotSynopsis: Pregnant and abandoned Helen Ferguson survives a train wreck in which newlywed Patrice Harkness and her husband are killed. Because the Harkness family had never met Patrice, Helen is mistaken for the dead woman and accepts the identity so her child can have a secure home. She falls in love with Bill Harkness, but former lover Stephen Morley discovers the fraud and blackmails her. When Morley is later found murdered, Helen and Bill each try to take responsibility, while Bill's dying mother leaves a confession meant to protect them. Police prove Morley was already dead when Helen fired at him and reveal that his actual killer has been caught, finally freeing Helen to keep the life and family she had feared losing.

title: Waterloo Bridge (1951-09-28)
plotSynopsis: During the First World War, dancer Myra and officer Roy Cronin meet during an air raid on Waterloo Bridge and quickly fall in love. After Myra is told Roy has been killed, poverty and despair drive her into a life she is ashamed to reveal when Roy unexpectedly returns alive. He still wants to marry her, but after confessing the truth to his understanding mother, Myra decides she cannot let Roy carry her past and leaves him for the last time; years later Roy remembers her on Waterloo Bridge with the good-luck charm she returned to him.

title: Retribution (1979-02-05)
plotSynopsis: A husband and wife manufacture a phony western gold strike by planting ore, promoting a worthless mine and selling shares to eager townspeople. They intend to disappear after taking the money and even plan to destroy the workings so no one can prove the fraud. Instead, the blast exposes an enormous real vein of gold. The swindlers then discover that by selling every share they also gave away their rights to the land, leaving the investors owners of the genuine bonanza. Rather than share the fortune, the pair are left facing punishment and menial work at the very mine they tried to use as a fraud.

title: And Baby Makes Four (1979-02-06)
plotSynopsis: After nearly ten years of marriage, Joe and Elizabeth Bentley separate just as a five-year-old Vietnamese-American boy named Joey is about to arrive through an adoption arrangement they began together. Although their marriage appears finished, neither can bear to abandon the child, so they agree to continue with the adoption long enough to give him a home. Joey quickly bonds with both of them and turns their planned separation into an increasingly absurd argument over which parent would get custody. By the time Joe and Elizabeth admit they still want each other, Elizabeth has one more surprise: she is pregnant, making their repaired family four.

title: Hostages (1979-02-07)
plotSynopsis: During a violent hostage standoff, a separated police officer's wife realizes the crisis has put her directly in the path of her unstable husband. Years on the force have left him paranoid and violent, and she believes he is using the confrontation to eliminate her and other people he sees as enemies. A hostage's staged medical emergency moves one gunman toward surrender, but the officer intervenes despite the stand-down; the standoff ends in gunfire and his death while outsiders continue to regard him as a devoted husband and hero.

title: Hildy (1979-02-08)
plotSynopsis: Illustrator Edward Gaskin and his wife Joan adopt a dog named Hildy shortly before their elderly dog Sam dies. One snowy morning Edward runs for a train and crashes into a steel girder, suffering a severe head injury that leaves his right side paralyzed and initially robs him of speech. Back home he grows bitter, resents Joan for working, rejects friends and even contemplates suicide because he believes his life and career are finished. Joan finally confronts his self-pity, and Edward begins trying to rebuild his life, drawing with his left hand and accepting help. Hildy repeatedly places a ball in Edward's useless right hand and nudges the arm through the same motion. One day he unexpectedly holds and throws the ball, and soon he can lift a fork with that hand. Edward credits Hildy's persistence with helping give him his life back.

title: The Choosing (1979-02-09)
plotSynopsis: After an emergency landing in an authoritarian African country, six Americans are imprisoned by dictator Mandu Rana. They are first told all will be executed, then informed that only one must die and that they themselves must choose the victim. Rejecting a random drawing, they hold a grim trial in which each person argues for the value of his or her life. The group discovers that wealthy Franklin P. Butler is an arms dealer who has supplied weapons to conflicts like the one around them. Elderly Mr. Rosen volunteers to die, but Butler tries to buy both Rosen and the others. When the final vote ties between Rosen and Butler, Elizabeth chooses Butler, who is taken away for execution. Rosen then dies naturally, leaving the survivors to face the bitter irony that Butler may be shot with weapons he helped sell.

title: Leavin' Cheyenne (1979-02-12)
plotSynopsis: As the era of the great cattle drives fades, older trail cook Samuel and young wrangler Ross find themselves out of work and camping outside Cheyenne. Ross is nursing a head injury from a saloon fight caused by a woman and a confidence trick, while Samuel tries to teach him that pride, honor and gunplay mean something different off the trail than they did in the old cattle outfits. Their argument exposes the widening gap between Ross's romantic image of the West and Samuel's hard-earned realism. When Samuel decides to return to town for a battered frying pan that has been his companion for nineteen years, Ross insists on going with him because Samuel is his friend. Their uneasy loyalty becomes the thing that survives as the old trail life disappears.

title: Should Old Acquaintance Be Forgot (1979-02-13)
plotSynopsis: Middle-aged newlyweds Fred and Margaret discover after their impulsive marriage that each has left behind a long-standing almost-fiancé: Jane in Fred's case and Tom in Margaret's. Jealousy and old habits complicate the honeymoon as the former partners remain very much in their lives, but the awkward foursome gradually rearranges itself. Jane and Tom become attracted to one another and leave together on a South Seas cruise, while Fred and Margaret accept that their wounded egos are part of the adjustment and settle into the comic work of learning how to live together.

title: The Thirteenth Governess (1979-02-14)
plotSynopsis: Private investigator Harry Holiday is hired by Valerie Robeson after her husband Matt is shot from a rooftop while following one of thirteen identically dressed governesses through a park. The same elaborate setup is repeated with a man calling himself Teddy Ward, who is then killed in the same place. Holiday discovers that Teddy was actually Valerie's brother Larry, believed dead for two years, and that the governesses and baby carriages are part of a blackmail money exchange. Zachary West had caused a fatal hit-and-run, was blackmailed by Larry, and tried to kill him by sinking his boat. Larry survived under a new identity, while Matt later became involved in the payoff scheme and grew greedy. Disguised with altered hair, mustache and contact lenses, Zachary murders both blackmailers. Holiday exposes the disguise, corners Zachary with the rifle evidence and takes him in.

title: This Home Is Dissolved (1979-02-15)
plotSynopsis: Tony and Louise Corder take responsibility for two elderly sisters whose memory loss and confusion have made living alone increasingly dangerous. Finding safe care proves harder than expected as relatives, a guardian and government procedures complicate every attempt to move them, while one interested party appears more concerned with controlling their money than their welfare. The couple finally arrange a suitable home and move the women despite the emotional strain. The story closes by framing their painful decision against the larger, often unseen problem of neglecting elderly people who can no longer safely care for themselves.

title: Climb (1979-02-16)
plotSynopsis: Mountaineers Jack Shields and Dan Hunt are high on a dangerous rock face when a piton tears loose and Jack falls, suffering a head wound that leaves him unable to see through the blood and bandages. Retreat is no longer practical, night and violent winds are approaching, and no rescuers are nearby, so Dan guides the blinded Jack across the technical face toward a route that can take them to the summit. Near the top Dan himself gets into trouble, and Jack refuses to abandon him. Working by touch, trust, and each other's directions, they reach the summit after sunset, realizing that in the final stretch both men effectively completed the climb blind.

title: Final Fall (1979-02-19)
plotSynopsis: Elderly North Woods recluse Andy Fritzen, a former lumberjack of mixed Ojibwe heritage, is offered ten thousand dollars by the government for the land around his isolated cabin. Andy refuses to regard the property as his to sell, insisting that he is only its caretaker and that it belongs to his mother's people. A drinking trip during a blizzard leaves him snow-blind, hospitalized and furious at the institutions trying to manage his life; even an attempt to mail the check back ends with a brief arrest because he carries no identification. Andy finally returns the money, watches his friend Clarence prepare to marry and move away, and chooses to remain in the regrown forest, accepting his own part in having once cut it down and finding meaning in watching the land heal.

title: The Troublemaker (1979-02-20)
plotSynopsis: An electronics company hires an outside troubleshooter to fix a management team whose three senior executives blame one another for every problem. Instead of smoothing things over, he deliberately needles each man, exposing a martini-soaked decision maker, an overbearing ego and a boss whose temper drives away employees. His provocations finally give the three executives a common enemy and force them to unite in defense of one another. Once the chairman fires the apparent troublemaker, the consultant reveals that getting the team to stop fighting each other and work together was the real assignment.

title: The Ouija Spells Murder (1979-02-21)
plotSynopsis: Ellie and her friends casually experiment with a Ouija board while their city is terrorized by a serial killer known as the sidewalk slasher. The board produces messages telling them to find the killer, go to Clover Heights and contact the police. Following the clues leads them to a house already connected with a legitimate suspect and to the alley where the latest victim was found. Police Lieutenant Connors appears to take their strange story seriously and escorts the women through the investigation, but later reveals himself as the murderer when he hides in their car and threatens them with a knife. Their friend Bill arrives in a cab at the crucial moment, and the driver tackles Connors before he can escape. Safely home, the group is amazed that the Ouija board led them first to the crime scene and then to the actual killer, but their promise to stop using it lasts only until another ominous message begins to spell itself out.

title: I Want Him Dead (1979-02-22)
plotSynopsis: After his young son Billy is killed when he rides his bicycle into the path of Robert Trenton's car, George Green becomes consumed by the belief that Trenton was drunk and escaped justice. His obsession with revenge drives away his wife and daughter and costs him his job, until he takes a gun to Trenton's home intending to kill him. Trenton reveals that he has an inoperable brain tumor and that what looked like drunkenness was a seizure; Billy's death was an unavoidable accident. Confronted with the truth and with a man already facing death, George puts away the gun and calls his wife to say he is coming home.

title: Then There Were None (1979-02-23)
plotSynopsis: The crew of the spaceship Omega lands on a seemingly alien world after finding signs of a civilization that does not appear on their charts. Explorers are killed by enormous spider-like and reptilian creatures, violent 'earthquakes' and sudden torrents of water, leaving Commander Austin Baker and two women to abandon the ship and search for shelter. They encounter gigantic ants and discover an immense sneaker, suggesting the planet's inhabitants are colossal. The final scene shifts perspective to an ordinary suburban backyard: the mysterious floods are lawn sprinklers, the sneaker belongs to a child, and the tiny spacecraft is mistaken for one of his toys, revealing that the explorers have been struggling through a familiar world at miniature scale.

title: The Afro-Westerner (1979-02-26)
plotSynopsis: Joseph Jenkins Roberts leaves Liberia for Wyoming Territory in 1875, carrying family stories of grandparents who had escaped American slavery and a determination to experience the West for himself. In Laramie he befriends a reporter, a boarding-house keeper, a Chinese businessman and Shoshone people, learns to ride and gradually sheds his tenderfoot status. After returning from a family visit with an inheritance, he chooses to work as a cowboy before using the money to buy land and cattle. He eventually marries Moon Feather and builds a ranching life with her, raising six Afro-Indian children near the country his grandparents once knew.

title: Care and Feeding of a Sex Symbol (1979-02-27)
sortKey: 0|1979-02-27|00017|care and feeding of a sex symbol (1979-02-27)
plotSynopsis: Hollywood talent agent Harry Silverman is under pressure to find a client who can revive his own flagging fortunes when he notices Susie, an actress whose looks have made her a sex symbol but have kept people from taking her acting seriously. Susie is used to agents treating her as an object and is suspicious of Harry's offer to represent her. He brings her home to meet his wife and children, trying to prove that his interest is professional, while discovering that Susie's appetite, family, pet cheetah and astrological adviser make managing her anything but simple. Harry nevertheless becomes convinced that there is a real performer behind the image and promises to build publicity around her without losing sight of her acting ambitions. After her astrologer warns that their signs are incompatible, Susie decides to take the chance anyway and signs Harry's management contract, giving both of them a possible new start.

title: Wanda (1979-02-28)
plotSynopsis: A teenage patient named Jane insists that she has a sister named Wanda, even though her family and medical records say no such sister exists. Psychiatrist Crane Shaker follows Jane's memories instead of treating them only as a delusion, tracing them to two sisters named Jane and Wanda Webber who died in an automobile accident eighteen years earlier. Jane recognizes their graves, former home and details she should not know, and confronting that earlier tragedy finally ends her obsession with finding Wanda.

title: The Long Night (1979-03-01)
plotSynopsis: Cleaning woman Anna Kauffman, security guard Ernie Mottrano, and young office worker Bonnie Albus are trapped overnight in a stalled elevator. With no immediate way out, Anna tells how she survived Auschwitz, Ernie admits that guilt from Vietnam has poisoned his life, and Bonnie confesses that as a lonely college student she briefly lived with a violent cult led by a man later exposed as a mass murderer. Anna insists that remembering evil must be joined by forgiveness, forgiving Ernie and urging him to forgive himself; the three emerge from the night changed enough that, when help finally arrives, they choose to wait and leave the elevator together.

title: The Mc Guffey Connection (1979-03-02)
plotSynopsis: Narcotics agent Arnold McGuffey goes to East Africa under cover of running a small school while awaiting word on an opium shipment intended for the heroin trade. The supposed cover operation becomes real as local adults learn to read, write and master practical skills, and McGuffey becomes increasingly determined to give them a genuine education. He renames the school Equatorial University and organizes diplomas, a multi-faith blessing and a graduation ceremony while a female contact keeps him informed about the rerouted shipment. By the end, the drug mission is still ahead of him, but the school has become far more than a disguise.

title: The Lady and the Outlaw (1979-03-05)
plotSynopsis: English traveler Isabella Bird arrives in the Colorado Rockies determined to recover the freedom and health she never found in a sheltered life. Against local warnings, she chooses notorious Rocky Mountain Jim Nugent to guide her up Longs Peak, the dangerous summit she has set her heart on reaching. During the climb Jim proves capable and protective, while confiding the losses, drinking and violence that turned him into a feared outlaw, and Isabella comes to see the troubled man beneath his reputation. They survive the difficult ascent and return to civilization, where Jim even attends a social gathering in her honor and restrains himself when challenged. Isabella then resumes her travels, leaving behind a man briefly restored to the better self she had recognized in him.

title: Oh, Brothers! (1979-03-06)
plotSynopsis: Brothers Carl and Jerry Bernaschi both become interested in Mary Ann and quickly turn her into the latest subject of their lifelong rivalry. Each takes her out, tries to impress her and warns her about the other's faults, while Mary Ann watches their competition with growing amusement. When the brothers finally demand to know which of them she prefers, she reveals that neither one is her choice. She has fallen for the story's narrator, Stanley Perinaschi, whose running commentary has placed him closer to the action than the brothers realized. A year later Mary Ann and Stanley are happily married and expecting a child, while Carl and Jerry remain bachelors but are about to become honorary uncles.

title: Carmilla (1979-03-07)
plotSynopsis: In Vienna after the First World War, Amy befriends the beautiful and mysterious Carmilla, whose face matches the woman from a terrifying vision Amy experienced as a child. Carmilla becomes intensely attached to her while Amy grows weak, suffers strange nighttime sensations and develops a small mark on her throat. An old family portrait reveals Carmilla's exact likeness to Countess Karnstein, and a visiting general describes how a similar young woman preyed upon his own daughter. A doctor orders that Amy never be left alone, and the adults trace the mystery to the Karnstein tomb. There they identify Carmilla and the long-dead countess as the same vampire and destroy her while Amy lies barely alive. Amy recovers, but years later the memory of Carmilla still frightens and haunts her.

title: No Greater Dream (1979-03-08)
plotSynopsis: Biochemist John Sanderley and his terminally ill scientist wife Mary decide to use her approaching death to test whether the human soul can exist apart from the body. They build a sealed glass chamber with a single outlet leading to a vial, hoping to isolate whatever leaves Mary at death and then establish communication with it. When Mary dies, John sees a luminous form emerge from her, change shape and enter the vial. His colleagues can identify no known element or ordinary atomic substance in the strange glow. John later receives the cryptic message '4W' before the light leaves the vial. In hospital ward 4W, a woman has just delivered a stillborn boy, but the infant suddenly begins to move. The episode leaves the implication that Mary's departing life force has found a new body.

title: The Tough Guy (1979-03-09)
plotSynopsis: Traveling Americans Frank and Susan Mallory fall into the hands of a modern pirate band in Southeast Asian waters, where they also meet cynical gunrunner Harry Bennett. Pirate leader General Kant-Kim wants Bennett's weapons and holds the Mallorys as leverage. Harry bargains with him by promising a shipment of guns and inventing a tempting cigarette-smuggling trawler to draw the pirates away. When the general insists on keeping Susan as a hostage, Harry secretly takes Frank away only long enough to circle back by dinghy, overpower the remaining guards and rescue her. The three escape under fire, with Harry wounded but still joking that survival comes from being pragmatic rather than heroic.

title: Powder River Policy (1979-03-12)
plotSynopsis: A worn former soldier finds a badly wounded preacher beside an overturned wagon and brings him into a Wyoming town whose residents are more interested in betting on whether the stranger will live than in helping him. Drawing on hard-earned battlefield experience, the old soldier takes control, removes the bullet and refuses to accept the common belief that the preacher is doomed. He learns that the wounded man was carrying money to build a church and was traveling to marry a woman already waiting in town, then brings her to his bedside to give him another reason to fight. When the preacher revives enough to speak, the old soldier also recognizes that the weapon carried by Dokes matches the kind that fired the bullet and helps expose the shooting. His unexpected competence earns him a place and steady work in the town.

title: Where Guardian Angels Fear to Tread (1979-03-13)
plotSynopsis: Michael McLeod, an impulsive guardian angel with a weakness for earthly fun, is sent down to help Kate McCall, an exotic dancer whose life and career have become increasingly chaotic. Taking human form, Michael becomes involved with Kate and her manager Teddy, repeatedly bending heavenly rules as he tries to protect her and keep her out of trouble. Instead of maintaining the detachment expected of a guardian angel, he falls in love with her. His superiors eventually recall him and make clear that he cannot continue crossing the line between guardian and mortal. Michael chooses to give up his angelic powers and memory so that he can return to earth as an ordinary man. Kate does not understand where he has been, but the two are reunited and begin their relationship again without the supernatural complications.

title: Going Home (1979-03-14)
plotSynopsis: After Lydia Stevens is struck by a taxi in New York, she awakens in a hospital with no memory of the accident and is told she was lucky to survive. Back home, sculptor Alexander Pluto begins calling from the Cornwall farmhouse where Lydia spent childhood summers, claiming that her spirit appears there and insisting that she return. He eventually brings her to the eerily unchanged house, shows her a marble Persephone modeled on her, and reveals a childhood world that seems to exist around them. When Lydia finally remembers the crash, Alex says her return has been delayed since the accident; the closing narration strongly implies that Lydia actually died and has been drawn back to an afterlife shaped by her happiest childhood place.

title: Sometime Every Summertime (1979-03-15)
plotSynopsis: A brief island romance is retold from three points of view: an outside observer, young elevator operator Mary, and advertising man Clem Waldron. During two carefree vacation weeks Clem becomes infatuated, proposes marriage and convinces himself the feeling is love, while Mary takes his attention seriously but refuses to move faster than her values allow. Back in the city, differences of class and background that seemed invisible on vacation suddenly matter to Clem, and he realizes with shame that he is a snob; after a transfer he never calls her again. Mary later marries someone else but continues to remember Clem and that summer, while Clem can no longer even remember her name.

title: The Wrath of ZEUS (1979-03-16)
plotSynopsis: In 2057, the Zeus 5 computer controls the world's weather and has transformed deserts, agriculture and daily life. When unscheduled rain causes a deadly Los Angeles flood and huge typhoons threaten Japan, officials initially fear that the system itself has begun to malfunction. Their investigation instead shows that the computer has been deliberately given destructive instructions. Technician John Campbell finally admits that he manipulated Zeus because he believed its power should be used boldly and that he was capable of ruling through it. He is arrested, but the crisis leaves the World Council with a harder problem: shutting Zeus down is no longer practical because civilization has been rebuilt around the weather system and has become dependent upon it.

title: The Female of the Species (1979-03-19)
plotSynopsis: Entomologist Prudence Hastings arrives with a forged letter from the governor and persuades the Texas Rangers to send Ranger Chet Gearing with her to the headwaters of Salado Creek, supposedly to collect grasshoppers. Her real purpose is to recover one hundred thousand dollars in stolen gold for her husband, escaped killer Cody Bancroft. Bancroft and fellow fugitive Davey Gross murder a ranch couple on their way to the cache, then reunite with Prudence, capture Chet and leave him tied over an ant hill to die. Chet survives long enough to join the pursuing Rangers, and a gunfight and chase destroy the gang: Gross is killed, Prudence dies after Bancroft throws her from their overloaded horse, and Bancroft is captured with the recovered gold.

title: Getting Drafted (1979-03-20)
plotSynopsis: During World War II, American war correspondent Hanley Finn is already working in New Guinea when he learns that he has somehow been drafted into the Army despite earlier being turned down for a commission. Sent through Brisbane for induction, he bounces through a comic maze of billets, dispensaries, ambulances and physical examinations because no one quite knows how to process a civilian who has already been overseas. After finally passing his physical, Finn unexpectedly receives a commission as a second lieutenant and emergency orders to Sixth Army headquarters. His new assignment sends him straight back to Finschhafen, the same New Guinea post where he first learned he had been drafted.

title: Mushrooms, Darling (1979-03-21)
plotSynopsis: George Avery has spent years trapped in a miserable marriage and decides to kill his wife Bella with poisonous mushrooms so he can be free for his younger lover. An expert amateur mycologist, George deliberately includes deadly amanita among the mushrooms he serves Bella, avoids eating them himself, and watches her die in what appears to be an accidental poisoning. His plan seems successful until the observant Mr. Tobias confronts him with evidence that George cultivated the poisonous fungi in his cellar. Tobias then reveals that he is himself an experienced murderer who has killed eleven people. Instead of taking money, he calls the police, explaining that George's eventual execution will let Tobias count one more death as his own.

title: An Honest Man (1979-03-22)
plotSynopsis: New York cabdriver Lou Marino finds a briefcase containing $200,000 left by two passengers just as his son Bobby is hospitalized for serious intestinal surgery and the family is struggling financially. Although the money could solve nearly every problem they face, Lou refuses to spend it and insists on finding its owners himself. He eventually traces the men and returns the full amount, becoming a reluctant public hero. The promised reward turns out to be only $200, and the attention makes it harder for Lou to work, but ordinary people moved by his honesty begin mailing the family money. Because many of the gifts have no return addresses, Lou finally cannot send them all back, leaving his stubborn honesty rewarded by strangers rather than by the wealthy owners of the briefcase.

title: The Mercenaries (1979-03-23)
plotSynopsis: Veteran mercenary Colonel Fest is hired by commercial interests to overthrow President Andre Bocar of Mondunga, the ruler Fest himself helped install a year earlier. With only a small force, Fest combines infiltration, a fake foreign-aid offer, a seized radio station and promises of back pay and bonuses to turn the army and presidential guard without a conventional battle. The coup succeeds and a former president returns, but the new regime immediately begins planning executions and proves no more principled than the old one. Fest is unconcerned: he demands the rest of his fee, the defense ministry and a share of the saffron business, making clear that money, not liberation, has driven the operation from the start.

title: Ace-in-the-hole (1979-03-26)
plotSynopsis: Newly released prisoner Zeb Hamilton is trying to start over when a lame horse leads him to the isolated Jamison farm. His former gang leader Kurt Fanner has escaped and followed Zeb to recover money they buried after the robbery that sent them both to prison, trapping Zeb, Wilbur Jamison and Wilbur's niece Marcy under gunfire. Zeb and Marcy fall in love while trying to survive, and Fanner is finally stopped. The danger is not over when a lawman decides to steal the recovered money and eliminate the witnesses, but the scheme fails; Zeb returns the money to the bank and decides that Marcy, not the hidden cash, is his real ace in the hole.

title: The Terrible Dream of Mister Glitch (1979-03-27)
plotSynopsis: Arnold Glitch goes to his bank expecting an ordinary transaction and is stunned when its computer insists that he has no account and, worse, that official records say he is dead. His attempt to prove that he exists becomes a nightmare in which computerized institutions reduce identity, work and personal freedom to whatever their records say is true. He finally awakens back at the bank, relieved to learn that the computer error declaring him dead has been corrected. The relief is short-lived: the bank now accepts that Arnold is alive, but its computer still insists that he never had an account there.

title: Cajun Death (1979-03-28)
plotSynopsis: Anthropologist Deborah Simms comes to the Louisiana bayou town of Mercy to research local folklore and the stories surrounding her late grandmother, Marie 'Mamrie' Simms, whom residents feared as a loup-garou witch. Townspeople soon suspect Deborah has inherited the same powers and blame her for bad crops, empty fishing nets and other misfortunes. After a pregnant woman gives birth to a stillborn child shortly after Deborah visits the family, an angry mob pursues her into the swamp. Deborah escapes by boat with her tape recorder while the hunters follow. In the darkness they encounter strange lights, frightening animal sounds and the unmistakable voice of Mamrie warning them never to harm her family again. The mob flees and Deborah returns safely. Her recorder has malfunctioned, however, and when asked whether the supernatural voice somehow came from her, Deborah can only say she honestly does not know.

title: First Star Tonight (1979-03-29)
plotSynopsis: Television star Lisa Chadwick is already questioning the career and identity she built around fame when she is asked to help Marilyn Todd, a struggling young actress threatening to jump from a studio ledge. Marilyn initially sees Lisa as proof that stardom would solve everything, but Lisa admits that success left her empty enough to attempt suicide herself. Their conversation shifts from rescue to the question of whether either woman believes her life has value apart from Hollywood approval. Marilyn finally comes in from the ledge after realizing she wants to live, and Lisa recognizes that she needed the encounter too, admitting that she no longer knows whether the television persona she fought to protect is the life she wants.

title: The Flight of the Starbird (1979-03-30)
plotSynopsis: Balloonist Gloria Travis prepares the Starbird for a competitive flight with instructor Chad and her sixteen-year-old niece Sally nearby. Determined to gain an advantage, Chad maneuvers Sally into the basket and launches before Gloria has knowingly approved the plan. He then pushes the flight toward the mountains despite an approaching storm, forcing the balloon to climb into thin air and eventually carrying it beyond the mountains and out over the Pacific. As the exhausted crew tries to descend, Sally catches Chad pulling the wrong line before he can open the balloon's rip panel. The Starbird survives long enough for help to reach them, and Sally's quick observation proves crucial to bringing the reckless flight to a safe end.

title: Conspiracy at the Golden Gate (1979-04-02)
plotSynopsis: In early 1861 San Francisco, secessionists plan to pull California out of the Union, seize the federal mint and Presidio, and divert the state's gold to the new Confederacy. Shipping man Toby Kingston is drawn into the plot and assigned to assist a mysterious colonel whose knowledge of mines and gold transport makes him essential. Toby's friend Bill Sweeter and the colonel's daughter Emily complicate his loyalties, especially when Emily reveals that she had been falsely told her father was dead. As the attack approaches, Toby and Bill help warn Union General Johnston and arrange for father and daughter to escape together. Secessionist leader Hastings discovers the betrayal and holds them at gunpoint, but the colonel overpowers him. Watching the reunited pair sail away, Toby realizes that he has chosen the Union and is grateful California has not been torn away from it.

title: As You Wish (1979-04-03)
plotSynopsis: Chicago factory worker Eddie Meagan buys an old lamp at a yard sale and discovers a genie who grants him five wishes. Eddie quickly learns that careless wording has consequences: offhand remarks count as wishes, and wishing never to work again leaves him fired rather than rich. His wife sells the lamp to raise money for their son Larry's birthday present, forcing Eddie through a frantic search to recover it while police and other complications gather around him. After using a wish to make everyone forget the trouble surrounding the lamp, Eddie spends his last real wish on the finest piano in the world for Larry. His family is delighted, and soon afterward a friend unexpectedly brings word that Eddie has been offered a better factory job. Eddie ends up happier through family and ordinary good fortune than through the selfish wishes he first imagined.

title: Improvisation (1979-04-04)
plotSynopsis: Struggling actor Tom needs money before his pregnant wife gives birth, and his unusual ability to use yoga to make himself appear dead gives his actor friends a dangerous idea. They propose reinstating his life-insurance policy, faking his death, obtaining a false certificate and substituting a dummy before burial so his wife can collect the proceeds. Their elaborate improvisation unravels amid a locked mortuary, a damaged dummy, suspicious professionals and a farcical legal confrontation. The fraud never becomes the easy solution they imagined. Instead, the mortician offers Tom legitimate flexible work driving a hearse, a job he can leave when acting work appears, giving him a practical way to support his family without pretending to die.

title: A Matter of Priorities (1979-04-05)
plotSynopsis: After her father's funeral, Abby expects to sell the family home and radio station and return quickly to her writing career in Los Angeles. Her plans change when longtime housekeeper Maria disappears and Abby discovers that she is pregnant by station manager John Travis, who had taken advantage of her during the months she cared for Abby's ill father. Looking more closely at the station, Abby also discovers that Travis has been abusing his position and draining value from the business. She fires him, takes the house off the market, and commits herself to Maria, the coming baby, and the station. After helping Maria reconnect with the young man who loves her, Abby realizes that staying home and accepting these new responsibilities is the right priority for her as well.

title: A Short History of Bac Ha (1979-04-06)
plotSynopsis: After American soldiers kill the prized water buffalo of a Vietnamese village elder, relations between the nearby village of Bac Ha and an American firebase begin sliding toward open hostility. Private Eckstein, who has built trust with local villagers, persuades his commanders to let him enter Bac Ha alone and unarmed rather than turn the dispute into another combat operation. He meets the elders, acknowledges that he cannot justify the soldiers' act, and works out restitution in the form of replacement buffalo. The settlement appears to offer a rare escape from the cycle of retaliation, but on a return visit Eckstein is killed. The elder carries his body back to the firebase and tells the Americans that those responsible for the killing have lost the village's support. Grieving on both sides, the elder and the commander agree that the village gates will reopen and that future trouble should be met first with conversation.

title: Out in Colorado (1979-04-09)
plotSynopsis: Labor organizer Mother Mary Jones enters the Colorado mining strike zone despite orders barring her from Trinidad and is repeatedly arrested for refusing to stay away from the striking miners and their families. General Chase and the state militia try deportation, confinement and intimidation, but Jones treats every arrest as another chance to expose the power being used against workers; even after weeks held in isolation, she continues writing and challenging the soldiers guarding her. Released and warned never to return, she instead heads to Washington to testify before the House Mines and Mining Committee about conditions in Colorado. While she is there, the Ludlow Massacre destroys the miners' tent colony and kills women and children. The strike is lost, but the drama closes by placing that defeat within the longer labor struggle Jones continues for the rest of her life.

title: Fontaine Harris, Le Baron De Paree (1979-04-10)
plotSynopsis: In 1929, small-time con men Fontaine Harris and Vernon abandon a failing high-speed-car racket when talking pictures suggest a richer scam. They recruit a French hotel worker, give him a glamorous screen identity and create a nonexistent motion-picture company that attracts would-be stars and investors in Kansas City. Moving on before the fraud is exposed, they take the operation toward Chicago and become entangled with gangsters who want in on the movie business. The scheme collapses into another escape, but their companion Millie comes away with a fortune in real bootlegging money. Newly flush, the group decides to refund the Kansas City investors and head west to try its luck in Hollywood.

title: The Ham That Cried Wolf (1979-04-11)
plotSynopsis: Michael Hammond, a citizen-band radio enthusiast known for outrageous stories, overhears men planning to kill Governor Charles Dawson shortly after his inauguration. Because Michael has spent years telling tales no one believes, the police initially dismiss his warning, forcing him to keep monitoring the conspirators himself. He uncovers their radio handles, timing and plan to enter the governor's office, then identifies one of the men by voice at the state capital. The authorities have quietly taken his information seriously and use him to help trap the conspirators before the assassination can occur. The governor cannot reveal the operation publicly while the wider conspiracy is still being investigated, but he deputizes Michael as a special agent for citizen-band communications. Back at his radio club, Michael finally proves at least part of his story by calling the governor directly on the air.

title: My Hero (1979-04-12)
plotSynopsis: Newly promoted network employee Cathy Applebee falls for celebrated foreign correspondent David Jeffries, who claims he is dying of cancer and uses the story to persuade her to move in and care for him. In private David boasts that the illness is a scam, while at home he belittles Cathy, pressures her to abandon her own work, and invokes his supposed condition whenever she resists him. After the deception is exposed and David loses his position, he tries to charm Cathy into persuading her boss to rehire him. Cathy refuses both the relationship and the favor, telling him that pity cannot sustain love and that his deeper sickness is the way he manipulates people.

title: The Curse of Princess Chiestry (1979-04-13)
plotSynopsis: A black-cat pendant with emerald eyes is taken from the ancient tomb of Princess Chiestry, and a trail of strange deaths follows the stolen treasure. Decades later Kevin buys the necklace secondhand as a fifth-anniversary gift for his wife Nancy. When the stone cat touches her bare skin, Nancy collapses into a catatonic state. An expert explains that a wizard cursed the cruel princess by trapping her spirit inside the pendant, where it can escape by possessing a living woman. Kevin, Nancy and an elderly man who once entered the tomb return to Egypt hoping to replace the necklace in its original chamber. Nancy, already under the princess's influence, leads them through the tomb. The old man dies while still clutching the pendant, Kevin finds Nancy transformed into Princess Chiestry, and the tomb begins collapsing. Kevin survives, but the cursed necklace disappears again, leaving him to warn that it may surface in another jewelry shop.

title: The Duke of Nevers (1979-04-16)
plotSynopsis: In 1885 San Francisco, wealthy Harry Penrod is alarmed when his daughter Gertie returns from Europe married to Charles Jules Francois, a penniless Frenchman who calls himself the Duke de Nevers and commander of the Legion of Honor. Charles lives by an elaborate code of aristocratic honor, refuses an offered business partnership and never touches a large sum Mrs. Penrod places within his reach. His downfall comes when he tries to help a young couple by pledging property he does not own as bail, leading to his arrest for false statements and fraud. Investigation shows the historic Nevers line has been extinct for generations, and Charles privately admits to Gertie that he was born poor in Paris and married her under false pretenses. Sentenced to five years at hard labor, he nevertheless refuses to abandon the noble identity he has created for himself, insisting to the end that he is the Duke de Nevers.

title: Hizzoner Hamlet (1979-04-17)
plotSynopsis: Successful actor Ben Gamble abruptly quits his long-running television role because he wants to experience something real instead of living through scripts. A publicity opportunity makes him honorary mayor of a small town, where he discovers a genuine political fight between redevelopment-minded Mayor Brinniger and city attorney Brad Nelson, who says the mayor's plans hide corrupt land deals. Ben first treats the job like another part, then joins Nelson's effort to force the issue into public view. He deliberately lands in jail while his actress wife stages a public appearance that brings reporters and television crews to town, giving the corruption story the attention it lacked. After the political adventure is over, Ben admits that real life is harder and less entertaining than acting. His old series writes him back into the show as a ghost, and he happily returns to the studio.

title: The Old Boy (1979-04-18)
plotSynopsis: Professor Charles Grayson is horrified when his newborn son begins growing at an impossible rate. Remembering an earlier accident involving radiation from a cyclotron, Charles concludes that his exposure somehow altered the genes passed to the child. He hides the boy from his wife Ellen and from outsiders as the child races through infancy, childhood, adulthood and old age in a matter of days. By roughly the eighteenth day the son is already an old man, weak and near the end of his life. Ellen finally discovers him, accepts that he is their child, and brings him back into the house. Two days later he dies peacefully in his mother's arms, having lived an entire lifetime in only a few weeks.

title: The Season of Glad Songs (1979-04-19)
plotSynopsis: Fifty-year-old Mildred has grown used to being treated as an outsider because she is unmarried and older than most of her coworkers. Her life changes when she begins seeing fifty-two-year-old Jim, whose companionship makes work and daily life feel lighter, and he soon asks her to marry him. Coworkers tease them and wedding businesses make Mildred painfully conscious of her age until she nearly calls off the ceremony, convinced that other people see their marriage as ridiculous. Jim reminds her that their love is real regardless of what strangers think. Mildred regains her confidence, and the story ends at their wedding with a reading from the Song of Solomon celebrating spring, renewal, and a love whose time has finally come.

title: Bruja (1979-04-20)
plotSynopsis: Young Dolores wants a modern life of college, dancing and friends, not the destiny her family says was chosen for her by an old shaman and the Jaguar warrior tradition. Her great-aunt Dona Lola begins teaching her the ancient practices of a bruja, and strange encounters gradually convince Dolores that the powers are real. Rival warlocks move to destroy her before those abilities fully mature. When they attack, Dolores relies on the lesson that harming another is ultimately harming oneself, and the violence turns back on the attackers, forcing her to accept that the old tradition she resisted is now part of her life.

title: Abilene (1979-04-23)
plotSynopsis: Mayor Joseph McCoy, desperate to restore order to cattle-boom Abilene, hires Civil War veteran and scout James Butler Hickok as marshal after other lawmen have failed. Hickok moves quickly against the violent saloons and crooked gambling, closing the back room at the Bull's Head and making an enemy of proprietor Phil Coe. Coe answers by inflaming the Texas cattlemen against the new 'Yankee' marshal and organizing a mob to run him out of town. Hickok refuses to be driven off, while his allies seek help from the town's farmers, and the confrontation ends in gunfire that shows how difficult it will be to impose law on Abilene's violence.

title: Here's Morgan (1979-04-24)
plotSynopsis: A Henry Morgan comedy-revue edition built from a sequence of satirical sketches rather than one continuous story. Morgan opens by joking about canned television laughter and promising a live audience, then moves through parody commercials, a spoof all-news radio station, breakfast-cereal advertising, and a deliberately overstuffed old-time radio mystery. Later segments include an interview with a man claiming an endurance record and a 'Little Journeys' visit to the home and souvenir business of fictional singing idol Melvin Presby. The program closes in the same sketch-comedy format, with Morgan and the ensemble using radio, advertising, celebrity culture and show-business conventions as their targets.

title: The Sabbatical (1979-04-25)
plotSynopsis: Distinguished professor Melville Pauli eagerly accepts a year-long cultural-exchange appointment in Vienna, but leaving the familiar routines of home triggers a growing terror he cannot explain. Homesickness becomes disorientation, compulsive thoughts and episodes in which he feels that the people and places behind him have ceased to exist; after he wanders Vienna accosting strangers, his wife Corinth tries to arrange their return without humiliating him. A bureaucratic cancellation of the program gives them a face-saving way home, yet even on the return voyage Mel feels the same dread. He resumes his university career and functions normally for years, but the fear he discovered in himself never truly leaves him.

title: Baby, Baby (1979-04-26)
plotSynopsis: Recently separated decorator Julie is still emotionally dependent on her estranged husband Barry when she becomes involved with self-absorbed screenwriter Rick and then learns she is pregnant with Barry's child. Rick's attention fades as the pregnancy becomes more real, while Julie's friend Carol pushes her to stop measuring love by whether someone takes care of her. Julie finally confronts Rick, accepts that he is absorbed in his own career, and prepares to face motherhood without either man. Six months after giving birth to a daughter with Carol coaching her through labor, Julie meets Rick again as a more confident, independent woman and decides for herself whether he has any place in her life.

title: The Odyssey of the Vigilant (1979-04-27)
plotSynopsis: The surveillance ship Vigilant encounters an unknown craft and its crew vanishes, leaving Captain Adam Bricker, Lieutenant Eve Kramer and Chief Stone prisoners of an alien power. Their captors, the Alveons, kill the rest of the crew and select the three humans as expendable warriors in a campaign against the Zaborians. After a failed escape, the prisoners are sent into battle, where Chief Stone reveals that he is descended from refugees who escaped a world the Alveons destroyed thousands of years earlier, making Adam and Eve descendants of his people. Stone dies helping defeat their enemies, and the Alveons, satisfied with the result, allow Adam and Eve either to return home or remain on the small planet where the battle occurred. They choose to stay, name the world Earth after the ancestral planet that was destroyed, and become the implied beginning of a new human population there.

title: Henry 'Box' Brown (1979-04-30)
plotSynopsis: Enslaved Richmond laborer Henry Brown resolves to escape after enduring the brutality of slavery and arranges with a white accomplice and Northern abolitionists to ship himself to freedom inside a wooden crate. To create time for the attempt he deliberately injures his hands so he will be excused from work, then is nailed into the box with only a little food, water and air holes. During the 350-mile journey he is repeatedly turned upside down, jolted, dropped and nearly suffocated as the crate travels by wagon, train and steamer. After about twenty-seven hours the box reaches Philadelphia, where abolitionists open it and find Henry alive. He emerges a free man and becomes known as Henry 'Box' Brown.

title: Guess Who's Coming to California (1979-05-01)
plotSynopsis: Greg and Lois Edwards hope for a quiet California summer while their children are away, but their old friends Harry and Thelma Newman arrive as self-invited house guests. The Newmans fill every day with tourist plans, gambling, cemetery visits, dubious real-estate schemes and constant commotion, leaving Greg and Lois desperate for peace without wanting to hurt their friends. Greg reluctantly agrees to accompany Harry on a sales trip for desert property, but before they can go a small earthquake shakes the house. Terrified, Harry and Thelma immediately flee California for home. Greg and Lois finally celebrate having the house to themselves, only to receive a call announcing that Lois's mother is arriving the next day.

title: Miniatures (1979-05-02)
plotSynopsis: Wealthy Matilda Winston controls her grandson Claude through his trust fund while devoting herself to a valuable collection of miniature objects and dolls. Claude discovers that dog groomer Anna has been stealing miniatures from wealthy clients and uses that secret when Matilda announces plans to leave her fortune to her dog and place Claude's reduced share in trust. He forces Anna to enter Matilda's house at a chosen time so she can be framed for murder, then kills Matilda hours earlier and later reports that he caught Anna fleeing after strangling her. His scheme initially fits Anna's record as a thief. But Dr. Hartness notices that Matilda's smashed miniature clock stopped at 2:10 and that her body is already cool near eight o'clock, evidence that directly contradicts Claude's story and begins to expose the frame-up.

title: The Other Grandmother (1979-05-03)
plotSynopsis: After the grandmother who raised him dies, young Alex searches his late father's papers and discovers that another grandmother, Lucinda, may still be alive. He finds her in a state hospital, where she has spent roughly forty-five years after typhoid fever, poverty, an absent husband and lost records during the Depression left her institutionalized despite a nurse's belief that she was not mentally ill. Alex and his mother bring Lucinda home, but his grief makes him try to fit her into the place occupied by the grandmother he lost. During a month together, Lucinda gently establishes a different relationship with him. While flying a kite, she teaches Alex that loving something does not mean holding it forever, helping him let go of the past enough to accept the grandmother who is now part of his life.

title: Anne Bonny's Gold (1979-05-04)
plotSynopsis: Newlyweds Ralph and Queenie Quince sail to a Caribbean island with what Ralph believes is an authentic Anne Bonny treasure map. After rescuing worldly adventurer Harry Bennett from the sea, they enlist his help, unaware that Skipper Sampson and his men are watching the hunt and intend to steal the treasure once it is found. Harry discovers the plot, sabotages and sinks the gang's launch, and leaves the would-be thieves stranded while Ralph keeps working through the map's clues. Their digging appears to fail until Harry notices that the map is dated July 22, 1718: the clue depends on the sun striking a specific spot on that same date each year, so their February search was hundreds of feet off. The three plan to return on July 22, confident they finally know where Anne Bonny's gold is buried, while Harry asks only for the chance to pocket a few doubloons when it is uncovered.

title: The Lovers (1979-05-07)
plotSynopsis: Rough frontiersman Simon Guthrie returns to town and eventually marries Eve Mitchell, who begins teaching him to read and write while they build a future together. Their new life is threatened when the jealous Ward Hutton arrives armed and Eve is shot during the confrontation. Ward is jailed, but Eve's blood loss and later pneumonia leave her close to death while Simon keeps working on the house they planned. She survives, and the story closes with Simon bringing her to the finished home and the two rocking chairs waiting on its porch.

title: Here's Morgan Again (1979-05-08)
plotSynopsis: A Henry Morgan comedy revue built as a sequence of satirical sketches rather than one continuous story. Morgan's material sends up beauty-pageant judging, government committees, foreign travel and casino conventions, then turns to absurd celebrity-magazine interviews with invented personalities whose names, marriages and public images become the jokes. Andy Griffith hosts the broadcast, while Morgan and the ensemble use deadpan misunderstandings, wordplay and deliberately ridiculous social commentary throughout.

title: The Assassin (1979-05-09)
plotSynopsis: A counter-terror operation in Athens tracks a committee preparing to murder an elderly chief justice and his wife. Surveillance agent Charles Holland and police position cameras, marksmen and observers around the hotel while the hired assassin waits across the street with a machine pistol. The attack still exacts a terrible price: the justice and his wife are killed, a security man and bystanders are wounded, and the gunman escapes hurt. Holland then uses the conspirators' effort to hide the wounded assassin to bring the killer and the committee members together in one hotel room, giving police the chance to take the group at once.

title: Overnight Guest (1979-05-10)
plotSynopsis: Young ex-Navy veteran Steve Corey comes to Hollywood dreaming of becoming an actor and meets Vicki Lipton in an acting class.
