Broke and homeless, he becomes Vicki's temporary houseguest until her insistence that he take responsibility for himself finally sinks in. Steve leaves an apology, finds work, repays what he owes and begins studying law. Vicki eventually tracks him to a night-shift gas-station job, where they discover that growing apart long enough to change has also made them ready to admit they love each other.

title: Milwaukee Deep (1979-05-11)
plotSynopsis: Coast Guard officer Tom Sims investigates a string of vanished pleasure boats after an abandoned yacht is found drifting near the Milwaukee Deep. His trail leads from the Gulf Coast to a remote development in the Yucatan, where he discovers the missing boats are being used to carry enormous Mayan idols out to sea. The developer is removing the statues because strange tremors and accidents seem to follow his efforts to disturb the ancient site. Sims and a companion escape their captors and seize their boat, but the final idol appears to summon a huge wave and stop the engines until it is swept overboard into the deep, after which the boat immediately moves again.

title: Bull Story (1979-05-14)
plotSynopsis: Texas rancher Ned and wealthy neighbor Leland carry on an old family feud that flares after Ned's prize Aberdeen Angus bull, Boo, wins a third straight fair ribbon. Leland covets Boo and needles Ned about money, land and Ned's son Bobby, who has recently quit football. During a violent storm Boo escapes, and Bobby follows him to an abandoned oil rig where collapsing steel traps and badly injures his leg. Ned needs Leland's winch truck to free him, but Leland initially tries to exploit the emergency by demanding Boo in exchange. Ned refuses because Boo now belongs to Bobby. Bobby's courage eventually shames Leland into helping with the rescue, and Bobby prevents Ned from turning the feud into murder. By the end, Ned's family decides not to sell the ranch, Boo remains Bobby's, and they prepare to face Leland again at the next fair.

title: A Very Nice Couple (1979-05-15)
plotSynopsis: Steve Montgomery's endless succession of hobbies and half-started careers strains his marriage to successful radio performer Connie, especially after he drags home a huge piece of granite and announces that he is becoming a sculptor. As Connie spends more time with an admirer and Steve moves from one new pursuit to another, the couple separates and Steve is left miserable. Then a magazine representative looking for Steve's photography sees the untouched granite and mistakes it for striking surrealist sculpture, offering thousands of dollars for it as well as a steady staff photography job. Connie returns with the news, and Steve cares far more about having his wife back than about his accidental artistic success.

title: The Nightmare (1979-05-16)
plotSynopsis: Janice is tormented by a recurring dream in which a red pickup crosses a highway divider, crashes into her car and kills her while 'As Time Goes By' plays on the radio. Her fear deepens when her mother reveals that she dreamed of Janice's father's grave shortly before his death, and ordinary red trucks and snatches of the song begin to feel like warnings. Janice withdraws from school and driving until a psychiatrist persuades her that the nightmare reflects anxiety and guilt rather than fate. Determined to reclaim her life, she finally drives alone to meet her husband and watches in terror as a red pickup approaches, swerves and safely passes. She reaches him convinced the danger is over, and they plan a weekend drive to Carmel, but the episode closes with 'As Time Goes By' playing again on the radio.

title: Mister Chan (1979-05-17)
plotSynopsis: Mr. Chan, an elderly Chinese tailor in New York, has spent decades measuring the people around him as carefully as he measures cloth. Memories of famine, disease and family loss in China mingle with his observations of impatient customers, changing generations, condescension and a society increasingly driven by money and possessions. He takes quiet pride in craftsmanship and independence, rejecting both petty extortion and well-meant attempts to organize his life for him. One night, alone in his shop and reflecting on the world he has watched change around him, he smells smoke from a growing fire. Part of him wants to flee while another part remains still, and he becomes unable to make himself move. After the blaze, an ambulance crew carries his body from the gutted shop, leaving those outside to confront how little they really understood the old tailor whose life had unfolded among them.

title: Country of Fear (1979-05-18)
plotSynopsis: American graduate student Ruth Rodriguez is arrested while backpacking through an authoritarian South American country after she tries to help a badly beaten man. Secret police isolate and torture her, demanding a false espionage confession that the regime hopes will help secure forty million dollars in U.S. military aid. Her traveling companion, local allies and journalists obtain evidence of her imprisonment, forcing officials to prepare her release while trying to blame everything on Captain Salcido. Ruth sees through the cover-up, and Colonel Mendez offers Salcido's execution in exchange for her silence. She refuses to kill him, reasoning that a living witness to the regime's betrayal can expose the system more effectively, and leaves with the arriving American consul and her friends.

title: The Legend (1979-05-21)
plotSynopsis: Hardware dealer Ned Austin becomes an unwilling Western celebrity after newspaper publicity transforms him into a legendary retired gunfighter. At first Ned resents the attention, though his business prospers and politicians begin imagining a public career for him. The legend becomes dangerous when three real gunmen arrive to kill Ned and claim the fame for themselves. Ned decides to face them rather than endanger the town, but his friend Billy cleverly points out that only one killer can receive credit and that three men shooting Ned together would only enlarge the legend. The gunmen turn on one another, Ned survives without becoming a killer, and he finally begins to enjoy the advantages of his heroic reputation.

title: Here's Morgan Once More (1979-05-22)
plotSynopsis: A Henry Morgan comedy revue made up of separate satirical sketches rather than one continuous story. Morgan and the cast move through jokes about children and television advertising, doctors chasing publicity with increasingly absurd medical claims, a mock continuing serial called Detergent, and a routine built around an adult-book shop, along with additional short comic pieces. The program relies on Morgan's dry delivery, wordplay and social satire, with each segment standing on its own instead of contributing to a single plot.

title: A Test of Love (1979-05-23)
plotSynopsis: Wealthy industrialist Paul Cunningham suspects that his wife Lisa values his fortune more than she values him, so he arranges a fake kidnapping to test her. Instead of trying to save Paul, Lisa and her lover Roberto stall the ransom demand and ultimately tell the supposed kidnappers to kill him so she can inherit. They then discover that Paul's newly revised will, which would have left Lisa almost everything, was never signed and that the earlier valid will gives most of his estate to charities while leaving her only an allowance. Paul appears alive with his attorney and investigators, revealing that the kidnapping and murder were staged and recorded. He tells Lisa that if she had tried to save him he would have signed the generous will, and adds that he is terminally ill, so her greed has cost her the fortune she might soon have inherited.

title: Muncy's Mob (1979-05-24)
plotSynopsis: Professional golfer Pat Muncie begins an important tournament playing well, but headaches and dizzy spells give way to confusion, angry outbursts and violent behavior that shocks his wife Sharon, his caddy and the gallery known as Muncy's Mob. After Pat assaults people on the course, the case reaches court, where his friend Dr. Theodore Bassett argues that the sudden personality change must have a physical cause. A court-ordered examination reveals a subdural hematoma caused by a seemingly minor bump to Pat's head before the professional rounds began. Surgery succeeds, the assault case is dropped and the PGA welcomes him back. Months later Pat returns to competition and caps his recovery by holing an eagle on the eighteenth hole to win.

title: The Lone Voyager (1979-05-25)
plotSynopsis: When veteran sailor Ian Janis collapses on the eve of a planned round-the-world voyage, his daughter Jessica takes his yacht Adventure to sea and decides to complete the journey for him. She reaches Australia alone, where naval architect David Flynn helps repair the boat while arguing that she is risking her life by continuing. Jessica presses on, learns that her recovering father is proud of her, and survives the most dangerous stages of the voyage, including Cape Horn. When she finally returns home to a waiting fleet, her father and David are there to greet her. Having proved she can make the voyage alone, Jessica realizes she no longer needs to live as though she must do everything alone.

title: Neither Snow Nor Rain (1979-05-28)
plotSynopsis: In a remote mountain community, aging postmaster Cyrus Huddleston learns that Washington intends to close the tiny post office because it handles too little mail. Desperate to preserve both the community gathering place and his daily contact with widow Mildred, whom he secretly loves, Cyrus begins manipulating the mail situation and eventually burns correspondence he does not want delivered. Matters become more tangled when Mildred wins $50,000 through a mailed sweepstakes and starts receiving letters from wealthy Pittsburgh businessman Harris Hughes, who proposes marriage. Jealous Cyrus accuses Hughes of fortune hunting, only to be caught with burning mail and threatened with prosecution. The post office closes despite his efforts, but Cyrus receives a suspended sentence and finally marries Mildred. She admits she never intended to marry Hughes and used the situation to make Cyrus finally declare himself.

title: The Strange Affliction (1979-05-29)
plotSynopsis: Ned Keesey's wife Jane suddenly develops a bizarre condition that makes nearly everything she says come out in rhyme. Doctors, therapists and assorted cures fail to stop it, and the tendency even seems briefly contagious when people around her begin rhyming too. Jane's brother Harry eventually convinces the couple to treat the condition as a rare talent instead of an illness, and publicity turns Jane into a national curiosity with lucrative television opportunities. On the night of a major interview, however, Jane abruptly discovers that she can speak normally again. The public assumes she was a fraud and her show-business plans collapse, but Jane and Ned realize that the cure they originally wanted has finally arrived and that they still have each other. The closing joke comes when the interviewer himself starts speaking in rhyme.

title: A Leading Case (1979-05-30)
plotSynopsis: In 1890s San Francisco, Cordelia Botkin begins an affair with newspaperman John Dunning, whose wife and child are living with her family in Dover, Delaware. When Dunning decides to end the relationship and return to his wife, Cordelia becomes desperate. A package of poisoned candy sent east kills Dunning's wife and her sister, and investigators trace the arsenic purchase and other evidence back to Cordelia. Her trial then raises a novel jurisdiction question because the poison was mailed from California but the deaths occurred in Delaware. The California court rejects the defense challenge, Cordelia is convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life imprisonment, making the case a lasting legal precedent.

title: The Great March (1979-05-31)
plotSynopsis: A young woman joins a committee trying to stop an American fascist group from marching through town and becomes close to Jan, an older married man whose memories of fascism and wartime camps make the issue deeply personal. When the courts establish that the march is protected by the First Amendment, the committee searches for a response that will oppose the group without denying the same freedom it claims to defend. They decide the strongest protest is to ignore the march. The woman also ends her relationship with Jan rather than injure his wife and daughter, while Jan resolves to carry the renewed joy he found with her back into his family life.

title: Mc Guffey's Hong Kong Connection (1979-06-01)
plotSynopsis: Drug-enforcement agents Arnold McGuffey and Miss Tawawa travel to Hong Kong to break a heroin-smuggling route, beginning with an airline emergency in which Tawawa helps land a jet after the flight crew is incapacitated. McGuffey dismisses her suspicion that a doll factory is part of the operation, but she takes a job there and discovers that selected dolls are packed with heroin. McGuffey finally follows the same trail, walks into the smugglers' trap and is rescued when Tawawa ignores his order to stay behind. The Hong Kong police take the traffickers, and McGuffey is forced to admit that his partner's hunch was right before their boss assigns the pair to another narcotics case in Hollywood.

title: A Poor Orphan Girl (1979-06-04)
plotSynopsis: In 1896, a nearly seventeen-year-old girl takes a job waiting tables so she can earn enough money for a wedding dress and marry local sheriff Harvey. On her first day, aging outlaw Rooster Redleg hides in her room, holds her at gunpoint and forces her to conceal him while Harvey and a posse search town. Once she realizes the famous outlaw is less murderous legend than shabby fugitive, fear gives way to fascination. Desperate for money and adventure, she even proposes joining Rooster as his partner so they can rob together and make their names famous. Rooster refuses and tries to escape, only to be recognized outside. The girl remains behind, returns to her supper shift, and Harvey tells her they will talk afterward about their future together.

title: Quartette in Nothing Flat (1979-06-05)
plotSynopsis: Recently released criminals Al and Sid recruit lock expert Waxy and getaway driver Madame Olga for an absurd plan to hijack a DC-10. They dismantle realistic plastic toy guns so Olga can carry the pieces through airport security, reassemble them aboard the plane and seize the aircraft, forcing pilot Henderson to fly east while the Air Force gives chase. The scheme unravels over the Atlantic when fuel runs low and the crew makes a blind landing in heavy fog. At first the gang mistakes the sheep outside for strange creatures and imagines it has reached another world, only to learn that it has landed in Sussex and is surrounded by British troops. The men finish the adventure in prison, Olga and Henderson end up together, and Al immediately begins dreaming up a new robbery inside the institution meant to reform him.

title: A Whisper in My Ear (1979-06-06)
plotSynopsis: Physicist Peter Farrow joins celebrated scientist Miles Baxter to build a machine capable of sending a person's mind through time while leaving the body behind. Baxter covets Peter's work and his wife Kate, and when Peter becomes the first human test subject a power failure leaves his body conscious but apparently empty. Miles urges Kate to institutionalize him, believing Peter's mind is trapped beyond reach. Instead Peter begins projecting his thoughts across time directly into Miles's mind and reveals that Miles deliberately cut the power to steal the invention and Peter's life. Kate cannot hear the voice, so Miles's terrified argument with the unseen Peter makes the saboteur appear to be the one who has lost his sanity.

title: A Sense of Pride (1979-06-07)
plotSynopsis: After Calvin Black loses his janitorial job, medical bills consume the savings he and his wife Mahalia have left, and the elderly couple is eventually evicted. Too proud to ask for help, they begin living by riding Chicago elevated trains day and night, leaving only for meals and necessities. Their fortunes change when a motorman becomes incapacitated and Calvin fights his way to the controls of a runaway train and brings it to a stop. News coverage reveals both his heroism and the couple's homelessness. The transit authority honors them, job offers pour in, and the Gracious Fellowship they had recently visited promises them a furnished home, restoring both their security and their sense of dignity.

title: White Out (1979-06-08)
plotSynopsis: Ski patrol captain Skip Blanchard warns resort owner Haverly that a whiteout is moving into Keyhole Basin and urges him to shut down the lifts, but the warning is ignored. Two inexperienced women, Lisa and Cindy, are carried to an expert slope just as the storm closes in and leaves them stranded in freezing wind and near-zero visibility. They attempt to descend through the trees while the patrol tracks their route. When the sky finally begins to clear, the women unknowingly ski onto an avalanche field just as rescuers reach them and the slope breaks loose. The patrol gets them through the slide alive, and afterward the women are ready to confront Haverly about the resort's safety practices.

title: Cottonwood (1979-06-11)
plotSynopsis: A young buffalo hunter called Cottonwood helps Deputy U.S. Marshal James Blodgett capture murderer Ed Smith and then stays in town, helping build a church and falling in love with Blodgett's daughter Marjorie. Cottonwood has spent ten years hunting the wooden-legged man he remembers from the wagon-train massacre that killed his parents, and just as he decides to abandon vengeance for a life with Marjorie he discovers that man is Blodgett. The marshal admits he rode with the killers as a frightened youth but says he took no part in the massacre and secretly carried six-year-old Cottonwood to safety afterward. Cottonwood lowers his rifle, accepts the truth, and marries Marjorie in the church he helped build.

title: Last Resort (1979-06-12)
plotSynopsis: Struggling comedian Benny Milton signs with the mysterious Mr. Deville and suddenly receives the career he has always wanted: packed rooms, effortless laughs, money and expensive gifts. When Benny becomes uneasy and tries to end the relationship, Deville reveals that the success was never free. During a drive in a powerful new car whose brakes will not work, Deville identifies himself as the Devil and demands Benny's soul as payment. Benny dies in the crash and awakens in what looks like a miserable old Catskills resort. Deville explains that this is Benny's personal hell, where the comedian is sent back onstage to perform forever for an audience he can never escape.

title: The Perfect Hostess (1979-06-13)
plotSynopsis: Wealthy Samson Cuthbert, trapped in a failing marriage to society-perfect Margery, secretly discusses having her killed while he is away on a western business trip. The hired killer's attempt fails, and family friend Dr. Woolsey uncovers enough of the scheme to test Samson with a false telegram announcing Margery's death. When Samson returns and finds his wife alive and sincerely offering to rebuild their marriage, he interprets her presence as torment and kills her himself. At the evening dinner party he continues speaking to Margery although none of the guests can see her, leading Woolsey to realize what has happened and send for the police.

title: A Piece of Flesh (1979-06-14)
plotSynopsis: A television network searching for a ratings hit decides to revive the career of William Trevor, a once-famous actor who vanished from public life and has been destroyed by alcoholism. Producer Jan North tracks him from a skid-row hotel to a secluded ranch, where a doctor gets him through withdrawal while the network prepares makeup, contracts and a carefully staged comeback meeting. Trevor gradually recognizes that returning to stardom would mean rebuilding the same identity that helped trap him in the first place. When the network executive treats him as a commodity rather than a person, Trevor cancels the meeting and chooses the uncertain work of finding a new life instead.

title: American Family Robinson (1979-06-15)
plotSynopsis: Affluent businessman John Robinson sells his company and suburban home and moves his wife, children and elderly father to an isolated island in hopes of rebuilding the family life that success has hollowed out. Most of the family embraces the adventure, but teenage Brad resents losing his friends and comforts and remains determined to leave. The Robinsons repair an old house, build a new home, plant a garden and learn the dangers of the island, while John's father forms a bond with Brad. A volcanic eruption suddenly tears through their new life, destroying much of the work they have done. Brad risks himself to help his grandfather and promises to rebuild the ruined garden, then realizes he no longer wants to be sent away. The disaster breaks down the hostility between father and son, and the family decides to remain together on the island and begin again.

title: Incident at Red Butte (1979-06-18)
plotSynopsis: Overland stage boss Russell has built a frontier legend by keeping his Wyoming division running through outlaw country, but the men around him begin to see the brutality behind his reputation. Jenny tries to escape him, and young Seth initially refuses to believe her stories until he watches Russell execute suspected horse thieves without trial and nearly burn a cheating hay seller alive. Seth finally defies Russell, helps a stranded family and prepares to leave with Jenny. Russell forces a gun confrontation, and Seth shoots him, concluding that whatever good man Russell may once have been was lost long before the final showdown.

title: The Advancement of Vern Berwick (1979-06-19)
plotSynopsis: Vern Berwick is a thirty-two-year-old auto-parts clerk whose extraordinary memory has always seemed more odd than useful. After taking a speed-reading course, he begins absorbing entire libraries and his instructor realizes that his ability is far beyond ordinary intelligence. Vern's rapidly developing mind attracts government attention, and he is eventually selected for an interstellar mission to Andromeda. He accepts even after learning that relativity means only a few years will pass for him while decades pass on Earth, so everyone he knows will be gone when he returns. On launch, however, the ship's computer surprises him by reproducing the familiar nagging voices of his parents, giving the newly advanced Vern an absurd reminder of the home he thought he was escaping.

title: Anniversary (1979-06-20)
plotSynopsis: A group of young people staying in an isolated house begin hearing voices, music and violent disturbances from a locked area they cannot explain. Their attempts to escape only deepen the mystery, and they eventually learn from a neighbor that the house belonged to singer Evelyn Dinell and her husband and manager John D'Costa, who died there in a murder-suicide. The date is exactly one year after their deaths, and the visitors realize that what they have witnessed is the dead couple's restless spirits reenacting the fatal events on their anniversary.

title: Who's Who (1979-06-21)
plotSynopsis: Aging playwright James Markham, increasingly isolated since his wife's death and a string of failed plays, agrees to help young novelist Toni adapt her book That Festive Summer for Broadway. Their collaboration becomes a clash over generations, love and the meaning of the story, and a rehearsal of a love scene briefly blurs the difference between acting and genuine feeling. Toni later learns from veteran actress Margaret Mason that Markham's supposedly busy social life is largely a pose. After another quarrel Toni leaves, while Markham finishes a draft that adds a deeply felt suicide scene for the novel's older father. Toni, her boyfriend Al and Margaret fear Markham may be acting out the scene and rush to his apartment, only to discover that the apparent gunshot was a champagne cork and that he is drunk but alive. Toni returns to the play determined to replace its despair with life, she and Al reconcile, and Markham himself reaches toward a new beginning with Margaret.

title: A Briefcase of Trouble (1979-06-22)
plotSynopsis: A boatman named Peter is hired to help recover a missing briefcase in a coastal jungle region torn by armed revolution. His clients insist the case contains sensitive political papers, but after capture, escape and a dangerous return to the hiding place, Peter becomes convinced they are lying. A gunpoint confrontation confirms the deception, and the opened briefcase reveals papers concealing a fortune in high-grade rubies. Peter and his companion turn the tables on the conspirators, keep the gems and head away together in search of whatever lies beyond the next horizon.

title: Old Bones (1979-06-25)
plotSynopsis: Two young dirt-bike riders encounter an elderly desert caretaker named Josh, who helps them after one rider badly injures his leg. During the night they hear Josh talking about a buried treasure called Nuggets and assume he has hidden gold nearby. One rider becomes increasingly greedy and violent while the other leaves to get a truck for the injured man. After Josh is bitten by a rattlesnake and dies, the surviving riders dig beside the barrel cactus where he directed them. Instead of gold they uncover the bones of an animal that had been named Nuggets, realizing that Josh's buried treasure was a beloved companion from his past. They bury Josh, mark his grave, and leave the desert with a very different understanding of what he had valued.

title: A Weekend Pass (1979-06-26)
plotSynopsis: At Fort Gordon in 1964, Army cook Conroy Rafael, known as Steel, receives a pile of back pay and turns a two-day pass into an increasingly chaotic weekend with several buddies. Drinking, clubs, unexpected hospitality and one detour after another keep the soldiers away from post until Monday, when the narrator realizes the group has gone absent without leave. His friends scramble to cover for him, while Steel escapes serious trouble largely because an officer's wife still needs one of his recipes. The comedy takes a bittersweet turn when Steel reveals that he is about to ship out for Vietnam; the narrator later recalls that he survived the war and eventually opened a successful restaurant in the Virgin Islands.

title: A Game of Cat and Mouse (1979-06-27)
plotSynopsis: Nineteen-year-old Bo Henshaw escapes from a psychiatric hospital and goes on the run, while his father Matt and brother Davey race the police to find him first. Matt distrusts the institution and insists that the family should handle Bo themselves, even after learning that Bo has killed a woman and stolen a car. Knowing Bo's obsession with automobiles, they trace him toward a county fair and speedway, where he imagines he can become a race driver. Bo obtains a gun and threatens officers when they corner him, forcing an officer to shoot him. Matt then seizes the gun and holds the police at bay rather than allow medical help. Bo dies from his wound, and Matt calls for revenge, but Davey finally refuses to continue the cycle, returns the officers' weapons and accepts that more violence or running away will change nothing.

title: The Hamster Caper of Curtis Cleever (1979-06-28)
plotSynopsis: Curtis Cleever and Louise want to marry but Curtis refuses to do it until he has achieved financial independence. His answer is Love for Sale Enterprises, a hamster-breeding business built on the animals' rapid reproduction. The venture quickly outruns his calculations: the hamsters multiply through the apartment, hibernate when the heat fails, chew or escape from delivery boxes, and leave customers chasing animals that were supposed to arrive neatly packaged. With his get-rich plan collapsing into comic chaos, Curtis finally realizes that waiting for perfect financial security has become its own trap. He proposes that he and Louise stop postponing their lives and make the following week their own Independence Day by getting married.

title: Shah-nama (1979-06-29)
plotSynopsis: Two trusted museum couriers carrying the priceless Persian Shah-nama back to Tehran arrange to steal it by cooperating with hijackers and a wealthy collector. Their plan turns violent when undercover Scotland Yard Inspector Fenton identifies the criminals and is killed after the aircraft is forced down and burned. A female Scotland Yard sergeant traveling under cover follows the thieves with the aircraft captain, while one of the young couriers begins to regret entering the scheme. At the collector's remote farmhouse the couriers themselves are betrayed and threatened with death, escape, and eventually join the pursuing officer and captain. The captain takes the collector's small plane, recovers the manuscript, radios authorities to arrest the collector and his daughter, and flies the Shah-nama back toward safety.

title: The Panther (1979-07-02)
plotSynopsis: A young frontier woman traveling home through a forest ignores warnings that a large panther has been killing livestock in the area. As darkness closes in and the animal stalks her, she takes refuge in an abandoned house, only to have the panther force its way inside. She retreats upstairs and finally into the attic, dragging a heavy trunk across the trap door while the animal repeatedly hurls itself against the weakening barrier. Just as her strength and the hinges are giving out, help arrives below. More than a century later, her descendant remembers the ordeal whenever he drives past the modern highway interchange built over the site where his great-great-grandmother fought for her life.

title: Here Comes the Bride - Again (1979-07-03)
plotSynopsis: Roger Carmichael and his wife Susan brace themselves when Roger's glamorous mother Elaine announces that she has left her latest husband, Walter, and is coming to Los Angeles. Elaine quickly plunges into another round of romance and adventure, while Roger worries that her restless search for novelty will upset the family yet again. By the end, Elaine admits she is tired of maintaining a perpetually youthful image and decides she wants to enjoy her sixties instead of starting over with another man. Walter arrives ready to reconcile, and Elaine turns a farewell celebration into yet another wedding, choosing to marry him again on the spot.

title: Melissa (1979-07-04)
plotSynopsis: Fourteen-year-old Melissa Baker and her mother move to a quiet California seaside town after the death of Melissa's father, only to become the center of a community panic. Melissa does not attend school because she possesses extraordinary knowledge and says that figures such as Albert Einstein and Leonardo da Vinci communicate with and teach her. A school inquiry cannot agree whether her experiences are psychic, psychological or supernatural, while one hostile official brands her evil and public fear grows into threats against the family. Melissa and her mother refuse to flee, and more than a hundred local young people gather at their home to protect her. Their insistence that no one can name any harm Melissa has actually caused forces some of the adults to confront how fear of difference, rather than Melissa herself, created the crisis.

title: Billy D. Burton (1979-07-05)
plotSynopsis: Gifted jazz trumpeter Billy D. Burton repeatedly sabotages a brilliant career through heroin, erratic performances and an inability to accept the demands placed on him. Friends, lovers and manager Doris keep trying to pull him back while critic Leo Leather chronicles both the flashes of genius and the disasters, including missed concerts, an aborted European tour and behavior that steadily destroys Billy's professional standing. Billy marries a woman who shares his drug use, later enters a six-month rehabilitation program, but relapses almost immediately and continues losing work. Near the end of his life he spends several weeks away from the public pressure, practicing seriously and reaching a new maturity in his playing. Before he can make the comeback others are waiting for, he dies after a sudden attack, leaving those who heard his final work convinced that he had at last begun to find himself in his music.

title: Vienna Three and Four (1979-07-06)
plotSynopsis: English businessman Fred Carson arrives in Vienna to negotiate a large doll purchase and is seized by intelligence men who insist he is the spy known as Vienna Three. After escaping, he takes refuge with airline stewardess Agnes Brown, while freelance operative Harold Cox closes in on a microdot containing the names of more than a thousand American agents in West Germany. Fred eventually reveals that the mistaken identity was no mistake: he really is Vienna Three, the genuine microdot is in his possession, and he and Agnes have arranged its sale while using earlier operatives as decoys. Cox boasts that he killed Vienna One and arranged the fatal crash that killed Vienna Two. Fred then reveals that Vienna Two was his daughter. The final confrontation leaves Fred wounded, and he sends Agnes to escape through Vienna's sewers while he remains behind.

title: Katie Mac Beth (1979-07-09)
plotSynopsis: Drifter Toby Hibbert takes work at the McBeth ranch and begins an affair with Katie McBeth while her husband Alex is away. Katie's elderly father-in-law Ramsey discovers the relationship and attacks Toby, but after Toby escapes wounded, Ramsey dies under circumstances Katie later admits were her doing. When Alex returns and confronts the lovers, Toby restrains him while Katie kills him, and they hide his body deep in the wine cellar. Their secret unravels as Toby's guilt grows and another woman exposes what she knows; Toby finally confesses and leads the sheriff to Alex's body. Katie is convicted and sentenced to hang, but after giving premature birth in the prison hospital she dies from internal bleeding before the execution can take place.

title: Jack and the Energy Crunch (1979-07-10)
plotSynopsis: A satirical fairy tale sends Jack Jr. from energy-dependent Yo-Huppetsville on a quest after the village exhausts its oil. Guided by a talking avocado, he encounters a nature-loving witch, an energy corporation, a giant and a wizard who finally gives him a magical orb providing limitless energy. Jack returns a hero but turns the new power source into a monopoly, raises prices, crushes opposition and becomes the same kind of energy tyrant he once challenged. The wizard returns, takes back the orb because Jack abused it, and leaves him facing the renewed crisis and the public consequences of having confused control of energy with ownership of it.

title: The Girl on the Billboard (1979-07-11)
plotSynopsis: Television and recording star Lydia Ward returns to her hometown with husband Derek Smith and their young son Wally, only to be confronted by former lover Emory Downs, Wally's biological father, who now wants custody. Wally is kidnapped, Derek is implicated when Emory dies after a fight, and Lydia's pharmacist father is then suspected when poison is found in Emory's medicine. Derek traces the timing of the poison to Emory's home, where Emory's abused wife admits that Emory arranged the kidnapping and planned to flee with the boy and their money; she poisoned him to stop him. Police recover Wally safely in Los Angeles, clearing Lydia's family and ending the visit with the child on his way home.

title: Spring Cleaning (1979-07-12)
plotSynopsis: While wealthy Mrs. Perry is away, longtime housekeeper Harriet is left to complete the spring cleaning under the eye of the woman's resentful daughter-in-law Darlene. Harriet's daughter Jane, a college student, is meanwhile involved with an older man she knows as Pete, who avoids meeting her family and speaks of a cottage where they can be alone. When Jane visits the Perry house with her mother, she discovers that Pete is actually Herb Perry, Darlene's married husband. Herb denies any real affair and claims Jane has built a fantasy around a few conversations, but details he shared with her make the explanation increasingly difficult to accept. Darlene cancels a dinner party and takes Herb home for a private reckoning. To protect herself from Mrs. Perry's criticism, she agrees not to report Harriet's drinking if Harriet says nothing about the scandal. The house is restored to order before Mrs. Perry returns, though the family's hidden problems remain.

title: Two Faces of Evil (1979-07-13)
plotSynopsis: Celebrated astronaut Jason Tucker and his clone, Joe Van, fly to the deep-space station Janus II to recover a failed robot computer. Jason believes Joe Van is to remain behind, while Colonel Frank Cain has secretly ordered the clone to strand Jason and return alone. After Joe Van follows that order, Cain claims the clone went rogue and pushes to lead a heroic rescue. Major Stoddard insists on questioning Joe Van, exposing Cain's scheme to recreate an earlier mission failure, vindicate himself, and discredit the clone program. Jason is recovered, Cain is removed for psychiatric examination, and Joe Van recommends Stoddard to lead the program with a better balance of emotion and efficiency.

title: Punishment and Crime (1979-07-16)
plotSynopsis: Former sheriff Ed Pettigrew recalls the mystery of identical-seeming brothers Jubal and Jidiah Siluto, one gentle and one vicious, after a stranger is found shot beside their isolated house. Evidence points to Jidiah, yet his supposed sickroom is empty and Jubal insists that his brother has escaped. Pettigrew eventually learns that the brothers were not twins at all: years of buried rage over Jidiah's betrayal and destruction of Jubal's fiancée fractured Jubal's mind, and he had been unconsciously living as both personalities. The murdered stranger is the real Jidiah, returned after fifteen years and killed by Jubal; convicted of murder but judged already deeply punished, Jubal is committed to an institution for the criminally insane.

title: The Crown Jewels of Grandomir (1979-07-17)
plotSynopsis: Alfred Grant lives an ordinary American life while concealing from girlfriend Jill Gordon that he is the exiled king of tiny Grandomir. Three aging royalists still maintain a government-in-exile around him and dream of restoring him to the throne, while revolutionaries in Grandomir struggle with their own bankrupt regime and send agents to recover the royal crown jewels. Jill initially thinks Alfred's story is an elaborate joke until the exiles and the jewels prove otherwise. Alfred finally decides that he wants Jill and a private life more than a kingdom, and the couple swear that they will never claim the throne. A letter then arrives from Alfred's sister, who has already signed his abdication for him, overthrown the revolutionaries' arrangement by restoring the monarchy, and plans to crown herself queen. Relieved, Alfred and Jill celebrate while the old royalists transfer their loyalty to the new queen.

title: The Joke's on Guess Who (1979-07-18)
plotSynopsis: Decorated war veteran Will Hinchcliff arranges a fake alley mugging so he can disarm the supposed attacker and prove his courage to his wife Judy. The practical joke collapses into real violence, leaving Judy and the man hired to play the mugger dead. As police and friends try to make sense of the disaster, Will's guilt exposes a deeper motive: he has never reconciled surviving the war while so many of his friends died, and happiness has felt like something he did not deserve. What was meant to make him look heroic instead destroys the life he was trying to prove worthy of.

title: Survival (1979-07-19)
plotSynopsis: Bank vice president Cliff Grant promotes ambitious protégé John Hogan, only to find himself competing with the younger man when the executive vice presidency opens. Cliff's wife Melissa, frustrated by her husband's reluctance to play office politics, secretly feeds John inside information and pushes him to campaign aggressively for the job, eventually revealing that she intends to divorce Cliff and make a future with John if he wins. Faced with the personal cost of the ruthless climb he has embraced, John abruptly resigns before his board interview and disappears. Cliff receives the promotion while Melissa quietly returns home, leaving him unaware of how close both his career and marriage came to being taken from him.

title: The Visit (1979-07-20)
plotSynopsis: Peter Ratner and his wife Laurie use a European trip as cover for a dangerous visit to Zantburg, where Peter's mother has remained since she sacrificed her own escape years earlier so her husband could flee with their infant son. Peter finds her and plans to take her to the West, but the local chief constable becomes suspicious of the American couple, arrests them, dismantles their van and tries to force them to identify a supposed local traitor. Peter's mother intervenes, helps them escape custody and joins their flight across the countryside. Evading searchers, the three find a concealed route leading across the border, where an ally has prepared new papers, money and tickets home. The rescue succeeds because strangers and family members alike decide that having the ability to help also creates a reason to act.

title: Uncle Zora Comes to the Pig Festival (1979-07-23)
sortKey: 0|1979-07-23|00121|uncle zora comes to the pig festival (1979-07-23)
plotSynopsis: A Nebraska town's annual pig festival becomes the stage for a comic battle with Carrie Woodruff, a domineering gossip whose accusations threaten widow Dorothy Griffith and the young people around her. Dorothy's colorful visiting Uncle Zora Miller joins the effort to distract, expose, and finally stand up to Carrie as family secrets and romantic misunderstandings spill into public. When Melinda Jane's planned marriage to Freddie Baker is revealed, the town closes ranks against Carrie's meddling and forces her to apologize publicly to Dorothy, her daughter, and Zora. Restored to the festival, Zora promptly turns the victory into a business opportunity by asking to sell his patent medicine.

title: Fontaine Harris in Hollywood (1979-07-24)
plotSynopsis: Fontaine Harris, Vernon Crawley, Millie and their companions head for California with money left from their earlier adventures and discover that their invented connection to the motion-picture business can be turned into something real. In Hollywood, members of the group stumble into studio work and Fontaine studies the shaky finances of a company struggling to meet payroll and keep production moving. Rather than merely bluff his way through the situation, he buys a controlling seventy-five percent share of the studio for $20,000. When the former owner announces plans to begin another silent Western the next morning, Fontaine calmly reminds him who now owns most of the company and says that the first order of business will be making changes.

title: The Ransom (1979-07-25)
plotSynopsis: Honest plumber Toby McVay idly sketches a supposedly foolproof kidnapping plan after working at the estate of wealthy Mrs. DePaultry, only to let his small-time hustler friend talk him into carrying it out. They abduct her and demand millions, then discover that her fortune is tied up in assets that cannot be converted to cash without attracting police attention. Toby improvises again, releasing her on her word that she will conceal their identities and later pay $100,000. She keeps the first half of the bargain but returns to announce that a promise made under duress does not require her to hand over cash. Instead, she has bought a $100,000 life-insurance policy naming the kidnappers as beneficiaries. If they want the money, they will have to murder the woman they just freed, turning their perfect crime into one final absurd dilemma.

title: Reunion (1979-07-26)
plotSynopsis: Fred Heming and Gwen unexpectedly meet again thirty-five years after a youthful romance ended when Gwen failed to reach the train that carried Fred away. As they compare memories, she finally explains that her car ran out of gas after her young brother secretly siphoned fuel, while Fred admits he had taken her absence as rejection and allowed their letters and lives to drift apart. Now widowed and divorced, they spend several days rediscovering the ease they once had together while also confronting the families and disappointments that shaped them in the intervening years. Fred asks Gwen to leave with him and gives her a second version of their old test: meet him at the airport if she wants a future together. Encouraged by her daughter to choose happiness, Gwen arrives in time, and the couple decides not to lose another chance.

title: The Value of a Hunch (1979-07-27)
plotSynopsis: A sheriff becomes suspicious of Sutherland's supposedly therapeutic drug-rehabilitation ranch after strange nighttime activity and a group of men who remind him of a violent California cult. Weeks of surveillance reveal odd tire tracks, military-style trucks and an offshore ship, convincing him that something large is being smuggled ashore. When an amphibious craft finally lands, the sheriff expects weapons but discovers crates packed with high-grade marijuana instead. A raid arrests twelve men and seizes more than thirteen million dollars worth of drugs, though Sutherland escapes in the confusion. Hours later the fugitive unknowingly hitches a ride with the sheriff, pulls a gun, and surrenders only after the lawman bluffs that a hidden weapon in the car is aimed at him.

title: Trooper Lopez (1979-07-30)
plotSynopsis: After a Butterfield stage is ambushed near Fort Bowie, survivor Lopez warns the Army that outlaw Joshua Lucas is operating in the territory. Sergeant Major Michael Hawks initially distrusts him, but the larger danger emerges when Lucas targets two new Gatling guns being moved secretly in a medicine-show wagon. Lopez proves his loyalty as the soldiers work to keep the weapons from being used in an ambush against their own troops. In the final attack the Army avoids Lucas's trap, defeats the gang, and takes Lucas, but Lopez is mortally wounded. As he dies, the men who doubted him acknowledge him as a trusted friend and brother.

title: Baldie (1979-07-31)
plotSynopsis: Bern becomes obsessed with his thinning hair just as he and his wife leave on a Nevada vacation with friends. After meeting a performer with an impressive head of hair, Bern eagerly waits for a promised carton of a product he thinks will restore his own. When it arrives, he rubs an entire tube into his scalp, only to wake up completely bald. At the manufacturer he learns that the carton was sent by mistake and the product was actually a depilatory meant to remove hair. To everyone's surprise, Bern decides he likes his new look, especially after learning the Lions Club now prefers him as master of ceremonies, and he jokes about completing the resemblance to Telly Savalas.

title: Voodoo Lady (1979-08-01)
plotSynopsis: Blind neighborhood spiritual healer Miss Rabbit uses powders, bones, prayer and powers she has learned to treat with caution after earlier arrogance cost her sight. A desperate mother asks her to save a nine-month-old son whose unexplained condition is steadily killing him, and Miss Rabbit agrees even after being warned that such an intervention may demand a terrible price. The child suddenly recovers, leaving the doctors unable to explain the change. When grateful neighbors return to thank Miss Rabbit, they find her mysteriously gone, leaving the cost of the miracle unanswered.

title: Writer's Block (1979-08-02)
plotSynopsis: Successful novelist Alex returns to his parents' home exhausted from publicity and hoping for quiet, only to be persuaded into leading a writing workshop he once attended. Most of the members spend more time performing the role of writer than actually writing, until newcomer Patience Webbersbee reads a sentimental children's story about a pigeon afraid of heights. Alex knows the story is poor but, attracted to Patience, softens his criticism while the group praises it. The dishonesty begins to trouble him so badly that he develops the writer's block of the title just as his relationship with Patience deepens. He finally tells her directly that the story is badly written and needs real work. Hurt, she leaves, but after rereading it objectively she returns and admits he was right. With honesty restored between them, Alex's block breaks and their romance resumes.

title: Absent Minded Professor
plotSynopsis: A Soviet defector's revelations lead British intelligence to a physicist suspected of passing atomic secrets to a global spy ring.

title: Bankof England Robbery
plotSynopsis: Two American criminals launch an audacious 1873 forgery operation against the Bank of England and trigger an international manhunt.

title: Black Market Murder
plotSynopsis: The killing of a notorious black marketeer reveals Polish deserters tied to organized crime and another murder.

title: Blodie Belgium
plotSynopsis: A dismembered body discovered in wartime London sends Scotland Yard and a forensic expert into a difficult murder inquiry.

title: Bonefroma Voice Box
plotSynopsis: A skeleton recovered from bomb ruins must be identified before police can trace the killer who used the Blitz as cover.

title: Brothers Staunton
plotSynopsis: The unusually close bond between two brothers ends in shocking violence when one tries to escape a mercenary marriage.

title: Bucketsof Blood
plotSynopsis: A severed head found near the Thames points investigators toward a woman with a violent and complicated past.

title: Burkeand Hare
plotSynopsis: Two Edinburgh immigrants turn murder into a business by killing victims and selling their bodies for anatomical study.

title: Captain X
plotSynopsis: A Polish officer accused of murder faces a wartime London trial shaped by conflicting testimony and crucial physical evidence.

title: Charles Piece
plotSynopsis: Master criminal Charles Peace commits murder and uses disguises to evade police until his long-hidden crimes finally catch up with him.

title: Counterfeiter
plotSynopsis: The program examines how counterfeit coins were made, distributed, and detected through several historic criminal cases.

title: Dr Ruxton Axe Killer
plotSynopsis: The investigation of Dr. Buck Ruxton reveals the brutal 1935 murders and dismemberment of his wife and maid.

title: Family Soliciter
plotSynopsis: A respected solicitor is tried for poisoning his wife, but the apparently straightforward prosecution contains a major surprise.

title: Fence
plotSynopsis: Scotland Yard examines the hidden criminal economy of fences who profit by receiving and redistributing stolen property.

title: Florence Maybrick
plotSynopsis: A sensational poisoning trial places a wife at the center of a case that remains clouded by disputed evidence and public controversy.

title: Frederick Stewart
plotSynopsis: A burglar's casual lie about a garage that does not exist gives detectives the clue needed to find him after a fatal crime.

title: General Charles Lewardaka Death In The Wood
sortKey: 2|018|general charles lewardaka death in the wood
plotSynopsis: The murder of a general's wife disrupts a quiet country community and produces a baffling investigation with tragic consequences.

title: George Smith
plotSynopsis: George Joseph Smith's repeated 'Brides in the Bath' murders reveal the pattern that eventually exposes and condemns him.

title: Great Gold Robbery
plotSynopsis: A criminal mastermind develops an elaborate plan to steal a valuable gold shipment traveling by rail between London and Paris.

title: Greeneyed Monster
plotSynopsis: A glamorous woman is tried for killing her young lover after jealousy erupts during a quarrel in her London apartment.

title: Henri Perot
plotSynopsis: An ambitious waiter murders his way toward wealth until the crimes and identities of his past finally lead police to him.

title: Henry Fauntleroy
plotSynopsis: A talented banker resorts to increasingly massive forgeries to save his institution and finance his lifestyle, ending at the gallows.

title: Hunted Hunter
plotSynopsis: A dismembered body on Hankley Common forces Scotland Yard to identify the victim before it can methodically track the murderer.

title: Saved By APiece Of Paperaka Identifications
plotSynopsis: Multiple eyewitnesses identify a man as a murderer, yet investigators struggle with an alibi that may prove them wrong.

title: Jackthe Ripper
plotSynopsis: The story follows a barber and publican who poisons several wives while considering whether he may also have been Jack the Ripper.

title: Jimthe Penman
plotSynopsis: The elaborate frauds of master forger Jim the Penman are traced through the clever schemes that eventually bring him down.

title: Justa Matchstickanda Duster
plotSynopsis: A discarded trunk containing gruesome evidence begins a painstaking Scotland Yard effort to identify both victim and killer.

title: Kindly Doctor
plotSynopsis: A Victorian doctor repeatedly faces accusations of murder and bigamy as disputed medical evidence surrounds a wealthy woman's death.

title: Ladyin Distress
plotSynopsis: A woman with a scandalous history is murdered and suspicion falls on her husband, though the evidence leaves room for doubt.

title: Lady Isa Crook
plotSynopsis: Several cases illustrate resourceful female criminals—and the women detectives whose work ultimately defeated them.

title: Lessonin Love
plotSynopsis: A naive woman's devotion to a deceitful lover collapses into desperation and murder when his true nature is exposed.

title: Liverpool Bank Fraud
plotSynopsis: A bank accountant's enormous embezzlement confession reveals how gambling losses and blackmail destroyed his respectable life.

title: Lucky Murderer
plotSynopsis: A taxi driver's puzzling murder reaches court, where a strange twist of fate determines whether the convicted killer is executed.

title: Murder Most Foulaka Mrs Voisson
plotSynopsis: Wartime investigators use forensic work to unravel the gruesome dismemberment murder of a woman in London.

title: Murder Without Motive
plotSynopsis: A woman and her lover are prosecuted for her husband's carefully planned murder, reconstructed through a chilling series of letters.

title: Murderers Letter
plotSynopsis: A Victorian Glasgow doctor goes on trial after the suspicious deaths of both his wife and mother-in-law.

title: Music Murderanda Mackintosh
plotSynopsis: The still-debated 1931 killing of Julia Wallace becomes a murder puzzle whose evidence divided investigators and the public.

title: Neville Heath
plotSynopsis: A charming impostor leaves a trail of brutality and murder across England before police finally capture and execute him.

title: Nurse Waddingham
plotSynopsis: An ambitious nurse poisons patients she hopes to inherit from, intending to finance her dream of owning a nursing home.

title: One Man Too Many
plotSynopsis: A love triangle ends in a fatal shooting and murder trial, but the precise truth of the night remains uncertain.

title: Perfect Detective
plotSynopsis: Jonathan Wild rises as a celebrated thief-taker while secretly operating as a powerful criminal mastermind before his empire collapses.

title: Poisoner
plotSynopsis: A respected solicitor and wartime major is accused of poisoning his eccentric wife and trying to kill a business associate.

title: Romantic Murderer
plotSynopsis: A quiet doctor's secret affair and difficult marriage lead investigators to his wife's sudden disappearance and murder.

title: Ronald Vivian Light
plotSynopsis: An ex-soldier's chance meeting with a young bicyclist becomes crucial after the woman is found murdered soon afterward.

title: Rootof All Evil Money
plotSynopsis: An insurance inquiry into a supposedly stolen pearl necklace uncovers deception and financial desperation in a prominent household.

title: Servant Problem
plotSynopsis: A dangerous domestic servant kills her employer and attempts to hide the body, setting off a grim police investigation.

title: Smoke Clingstothe Hair
plotSynopsis: An insurance fraud built around a fatal fire seems carefully planned until one subtle physical clue destroys the deception.

title: Storyof Walter Miller
plotSynopsis: A ruthless bricklayer pursues money and a better life through two murders and a desperate crime spree before capture.

title: Theftofthe British Crown Jewels
plotSynopsis: Colonel Thomas Blood attempts one of history's boldest robberies by trying to steal the Crown Jewels from the Tower of London.

title: Witchcraft Law
plotSynopsis: A celebrated medium and associates face a 1944 prosecution under Britain's old Witchcraft Act after a police sting.

title: Crime On The Railway
plotSynopsis: A survey of ingenious railway thefts shows how organized gangs and opportunists preyed on Britain's rail system.

title: Mightier Than The Sword
plotSynopsis: The history of forgery and confidence crime is explored through notable cases and artifacts preserved by Scotland Yard.

title: Fiction Is Stranger Than Truthaka Reginald Sidney Buckfield
sortKey: 8|fiction is stranger than truthaka reginald sidney buckfield
plotSynopsis: An amateur writer suspected of murder accidentally describes incriminating details of the real crime in a fictional story.

title: Jean Pierre Vaquier The Dapper Frenchmanaka Battalier
sortKey: 8|jean pierre vaquier the dapper frenchmanaka battalier
plotSynopsis: A charming Frenchman's holiday affair ends in a suspicious death at an English country inn and a murder investigation.

title: Scalesof Justiceaka Robert Wood
plotSynopsis: An artist's murder trial turns on unusual evidence, including a peculiar sketch left on a postcard.

title: Accurate Spelling Is Essential
plotSynopsis: Coincidences, a sharp-eared postal clerk, and a criminal's spelling mistakes expose an otherwise carefully hidden murder.

title: Murder At Moat House Farm
plotSynopsis: A newly married woman disappears from an isolated Essex farm, prompting police to uncover what happened behind the farmhouse walls.

title: The Communist Menaceclcut
plotSynopsis: At the request of his station owner and the FBI, Chuck Morgan reads a pro-Communist script on the air and is publicly fired. The dismissal is a cover that lets him infiltrate the Communist Party organization in Los Angeles and try to identify the person directing it.

title: Luke Larsons Murder
plotSynopsis: Chuck learns that a light-heavyweight bout involving Luc Larson may be fixed, but before he can prove the setup Larson is found murdered in his apartment. The suspicious fight becomes the starting point for Chuck's investigation into the killing.

title: Mark Adams Murder
plotSynopsis: Respected stockbroker Mark Adams is found badly beaten and shot on a lonely road off Mulholland Drive. Robbery does not explain the murder, and the victim's spotless public reputation leaves Chuck searching for the hidden part of Adams's life that could supply a motive.

title: Marijuana Mystery
plotSynopsis: Carol Curtis follows an anonymous tip about a large marijuana shipment expected to cross the border at Calexico. Chuck dismisses the tip at first, but Carol is soon arrested and framed as a smuggler, forcing him to investigate the people behind the setup.

title: Queenies 10000 Dollar Alibi
plotSynopsis: Queenie O'Rourke appears unexpectedly in Chuck's apartment, insists that he was with her on the previous Friday, and leaves him ten thousand dollars to support the false alibi. Chuck sets out to discover what happened that night and why Queenie needs his name badly enough to pay for it.

title: Prisoners Of The Revolution
plotSynopsis: Chuck and Carol travel to South America to cover a revolution and discover that Chuck is an uncanny double for the country's ousted president. The resemblance puts the reporter directly into the political danger he came only to cover.

title: The Tennant Jewels Stolen
plotSynopsis: A diamond valued at roughly half a million dollars disappears, throwing Mrs. Tennant into panic. Chuck senses that the circumstances of the theft do not fit together and remains on the scene to uncover what really happened to the jewel.

title: Baby Betsys Mother
plotSynopsis: A woman who adopted Betsy at birth and has raised her for five years comes to Chuck for help after another woman appears claiming to be the child's biological mother and demanding custody. Chuck becomes involved in determining what lies behind the sudden claim.

title: The Black Hand
plotSynopsis: A frightened man tries to give Chuck an anonymous tip about a gangland shooting. Before the information can be safely used, the man's daughter is kidnapped, turning the attempted tip into a case of intimidation and organized-crime pressure.

title: Trixies Bank Heist
plotSynopsis: Police ask Chuck to impersonate a nationally known bank robber so he can get close to a violent female bank robber and her associate. The undercover role places him inside the criminals' confidence while the police try to break the gang.

title: Gladstone Smith Murder
plotSynopsis: Gladstone Smith, an apparently ordinary city tax auditor with a respectable family life, is murdered and his face is smashed beyond recognition. Police ask Chuck to look into why someone with no obvious criminal connections would be killed so brutally.

title: Displaced Into Danger
plotSynopsis: Displaced person Jan Darvis complains to police that someone is forcing him to pay protection money and is then beaten to death. Chuck investigates a blackmail and extortion operation preying on displaced people in Los Angeles.

title: Lonely Hearts Club Of Doom
plotSynopsis: Lonely, wealthy Amos Bugsby answers a personal advertisement and marries widow Ellen Cutler after meeting her protective brother. When Bugsby later claims that his new wife and her brother tried to kill him, he turns to Chuck for help.

title: The Kidnappers New Shoes
plotSynopsis: Chuck's old fishing friend Fred Michaels learns that his young son Ricky has been kidnapped. The abductors demand fifty thousand dollars in cash and jewels and specifically order that Chuck deliver the ransom, putting him directly into the kidnapping case.

title: Eddie Flores Frame-UP
plotSynopsis: A young couple is found brutally murdered in a car off Mulholland Drive, and a young man discovered near the scene runs away. He later asks Chuck to help prove that he did not commit the killings, drawing the reporter into a case built around evidence that appears to frame him.

title: Hollywood Love Triangle
plotSynopsis: Powerful Hollywood producer Roger Van Rim is arrested for arson, and Chuck's pursuit of the story draws him into the romantic triangle surrounding the producer. The Hollywood scandal becomes more than a simple arson report as Chuck investigates the relationships behind it.

title: Mr Hendricks Mines Of Murder
plotSynopsis: Gold-mine speculator John Hendricks is operating an old mine near Las Vegas where three men have died in only a few months. Chuck becomes suspicious when he learns that each dead worker carried substantial insurance from which the mining operation benefited.

title: The Wetback Murders
plotSynopsis: After Chuck and Carol return from Mexico, a murdered man is discovered in the trunk of their car. The death connects them to a Border Patrol investigation of a human-smuggling operation whose organizers appear to know patrol movements and have already left multiple victims dead.

title: ASpy Ring In June
plotSynopsis: An espionage suspect who had been accused of passing aircraft information escapes custody, but the man later recaptured may only be a decoy. Because Chuck has interviewed the real suspect before, investigators enlist him to help expose the substitution and lead them toward the actual spy.

title: Quintion Mc Cleans Fortune
plotSynopsis: Carol's suitcase is accidentally switched with another passenger's luggage on her return from New York. Inside the wrong case she finds a large amount of cash and half of a map connected to the Quentin McLean fortune, sending Chuck and Carol into a dangerous search for what the map leads to.

title: The Clueless Crime Spree
plotSynopsis: Los Angeles is hit by a growing series of crimes that seem to leave no usable clues. Chuck becomes fascinated by the unusual lack of evidence and tries to discover the common explanation behind the seemingly clue-free crime spree.

title: The Sniper
plotSynopsis: A sniper has killed several people at random from dark alleys, leaving police without a motive or identity. The killer begins telephoning intended victims before striking—and then calls Chuck to tell him that he is next.

title: Naomi Needs An Operation
plotSynopsis: Hospital patient Tom Edwards offers Chuck information about a dangerous racket, but only on the condition that Chuck broadcast the story even though Edwards believes doing so will cause his own murder soon afterward. Chuck must decide how to use the information while trying to understand the threat.

title: Subversive Activities
plotSynopsis: Chuck sees a newspaper photograph of a man running for mayor of a nearby city and believes he recognizes the candidate as someone previously convicted of subversive activity under another name. He travels to investigate whether the promising politician is really the man from the older case.

title: Death On The Tracks
plotSynopsis: Chuck receives a tip that a death on a remote stretch of the Southern Express railroad was not the accident authorities believe it to be. He and Carol drive to the isolated railroad settlement to investigate the possibility of murder.

title: The Light
plotSynopsis: Government scientist Joe Stanley, who had been working on a secret hydrogen-bomb project, dies along with dozens of others in a plane crash. Because it is one of several similar air disasters in a short period, Chuck begins to suspect that the crashes may not be accidental.

title: Audition and Sales Presention (1946-01-15)
plotSynopsis: An audition or sales-presentation recording associated with Strange Wills, identified in the archive as “Audition and Sales Presention.”

title: The Mad Concerto (1946-06-08)
plotSynopsis: Young pianist Nadia Winter inherits a ten-million-dollar fortune only under conditions that keep her unmarried and isolated. Probate lawyer John Francis O'Connell falls in love with her, but Nadia chooses the inheritance and the life of confinement attached to it, with consequences that unfold over many years.

title: Alias Doctor Svengali (1946-06-15)
plotSynopsis: Dying Philip Martin tells O'Connell that what appeared to be a suicide attempt was actually an effort to kill him and rewrites his will to accuse his wife and psychiatrist Dr. Cosmo. O'Connell investigates a doctor whose music and hypnotic influence seem to give him dangerous power over his patients.

title: Black Interlude (1946-06-22)
plotSynopsis: Wealthy Francis Blair despises his son Paul because both men love the same woman and cuts Paul from his will while vowing that his hatred will continue after death. When Blair dies, Paul's guilt and fear deepen into psychological collapse, leaving O'Connell to confront what may be a haunting—or the destructive force of the father's revenge.

title: The Lady and the Pirate (1946-06-29)
plotSynopsis: In 1724 an ancestor of John Francis O'Connell sails for the Carolinas on a secret mission to help capture pirate Black Richard Templeton. The voyage becomes complicated by Lady Ruth's fascination with the outlaw, leading to an adventure that ends with one of the strangest wills O'Connell's family has ever handled.

title: Prince of Broadway (1946-07-06)
plotSynopsis: Broadway agent Harry McNeil discovers and develops young Gertrude Pulaski into singing star Judy Morrison, then falls in love with her. When contractual obligations threaten her future, McNeil makes a legal sacrifice that leaves O'Connell caught between professional duty and the feelings of the two people involved.

title: Treasure to Starboard (1946-07-13)
plotSynopsis: A will made aboard the treasure ship Toledo in 1703 eventually places clues to its lost cargo in the hands of O'Connell's friends Paul and Jean more than two centuries later. Their expedition to recover the sunken jewels becomes a race against rival German treasure hunters.

title: One Shining Night (1946-07-20)
plotSynopsis: Disgraced scientist Professor Don Borgia leaves O'Connell instructions concerning his daughter Nina, whose childhood behavior suggests the same fascination with fear, cruelty, and forbidden experimentation that destroyed her father's reputation. As Nina grows older, O'Connell must discover whether she has inherited more than Borgia's name.

title: Midnight on the Moor (1946-07-27)
plotSynopsis: While traveling through Scotland, O'Connell becomes involved with Sir Walter McClanahan, who is determined to learn who murdered his son. The investigation across fog-covered moors grows increasingly frightening as the dead man's father vows that even death will not stop him from exposing the killer.

title: Seven Flights to Glory (1946-08-03)
plotSynopsis: Dying industrialist Lucy Witherspoon offers her son Bob a choice in her will: inherit the family empire by running it for years, or take a small sum and go to Paris to pursue his dream of becoming a painter. Bob chooses art over wealth, a decision that reshapes his career and his relationships.

title: The Girl from Shadowland (1946-08-10)
plotSynopsis: Professor Lucifer Nicolai's diary reveals experiments intended to separate mind from body and send human consciousness backward through the light waves that preserve the past. Young Alice experiences King Arthur's court and then attempts a journey to ancient Egypt, where a malfunction turns the experiment dangerous.

title: Madman's Diary (1946-08-17)
plotSynopsis: Professor Lucifer Nicolai's diary describes experiments that separate the mind from the body and allow young Alice to experience scenes from the distant past. This surviving program is a repeat or alternate presentation of the same story circulated as The Girl from Shadowland.

title: Emeralds Come High (1946-08-24)
plotSynopsis: Burlesque star Patsy 'Bubbles' Moran unexpectedly inherits a prospector's map to a rich emerald mine in Colombia. O'Connell joins her and experienced guides on a jungle expedition to find the treasure and survive the dangers surrounding it.

title: Emily (1946-08-31)
plotSynopsis: The story follows a remarkable violin named Emily from its creation in eighteenth-century Cremona through generations of famous musicians, war, and theft. O'Connell eventually becomes involved in tracing the instrument after its journey through Nazi-occupied Europe and trying to return it to its rightful owner.

title: Margin for Love (1946-09-07)
plotSynopsis: Tim Ryan is convicted of murder and sentenced to the electric chair despite insisting he was knocked unconscious at the crime scene. A dying woman's confession gives O'Connell evidence that Ryan may be innocent, forcing a desperate race to stop the execution before time runs out.

title: They Met in Monte Carlo (1946-09-14)
plotSynopsis: In Monte Carlo, O'Connell helps fellow American Dick Marlowe meet Hungarian beauty Carla Lux. Their immediate romance collides with Carla's politically connected fiancé and agents of the German Reich, turning a casino encounter into a dangerous attempt to escape the country.

title: The Girl in Cell 13 (1946-09-21)
plotSynopsis: Collector Charles Ashbrooke decides to entrust the priceless paired rubies known as the Tears of the Madonna to O'Connell so they can be returned to the place from which they were stolen centuries earlier. Before the transfer is completed Ashbrooke is murdered, and the gems' violent history becomes part of the investigation.

title: So Deep the Stream (1946-09-28)
plotSynopsis: Playwright Frank Warner leaves his son a trunk of rejected plays and the challenge of staging them when the world is ready. The son's devotion to his father's work costs him love and friendship as success arrives, forcing him to decide whether artistic ambition has taken him away from the people the plays were meant to serve.

title: The Miser's Gold (1946-10-05)
plotSynopsis: Eccentric old miner Nick possesses ten sacks of gold but despises the three relatives who once schemed to take it from him. Knowing death is near, he asks O'Connell to construct a will that disposes of the fortune while also delivering a final lesson to his greedy family.

title: East of Hudson's Bay (1946-10-12)
plotSynopsis: Headstrong socialite Angela Nelson inherits a vast ranch in the remote country east of Hudson Bay and travels north to claim it. Guided through the dangerous Quebec wilderness by Pierre, she discovers that the strange bequest may also change the direction of her personal life.

title: Autograph Girl (1946-10-19)
plotSynopsis: Movie star Peter Braten meets fan Angel Dare on the same day he signs a new will and impulsively marries her. Angel's initial lack of interest in Hollywood soon gives way to an obsessive push into a film career, turning their romance into a darkly comic struggle with fame.

title: Penthouse Orphan (1946-10-26)
plotSynopsis: Confirmed bachelor Felix Grayson inherits money on the condition that he care for a distant French relative called Baby Babette. He expects a child, but the new dependent who arrives is an eighteen-year-old woman, creating romantic and comic complications in his carefully ordered life.

title: Singapore Liz (1946-11-02)
plotSynopsis: O'Connell travels to Singapore searching for Marilyn Webster, beneficiary of a million-dollar will, and becomes fascinated by the notorious woman known as Singapore Liz. His search for the missing heiress becomes entangled with Liz's story and the dangerous world around the port.

title: Crosswinds (1946-11-09)
plotSynopsis: Condemned killer Patrick Malone escapes death row while O'Connell is handling the affairs of Margaret Levering, heir to a steamship company. Their paths converge aboard a vessel bound for South America, where romance, inheritance, and the fugitive's presence create a dangerous voyage.

title: Dance Director (1946-11-16)
plotSynopsis: Wealthy Margo Davis can inherit her father's ten-million-dollar estate only after earning her own living for a full year. Forced outside the privileged world she knows, she enters theatrical life and learns what work, money, and independence actually mean.

title: Death Is My Destiny (1946-11-23)
plotSynopsis: Gangster Lefty Light dies clutching a strange handwritten bequest naming waitress Kitty Ledderby as heir to everything he owns. O'Connell and a crime reporter try to decipher why a notorious criminal would leave his estate to a woman he barely knew and what the cryptic final message reveals.

title: The Killer and the Saint (1946-11-30)
plotSynopsis: Identical twins David and Don Kerwin meet again at their father's funeral: David is a convicted bank robber and safecracker nearing parole, while Don works at a bank and is engaged to the woman both brothers love. After David's release, a new series of bank robberies makes their identical appearance central to suspicion and deception.

title: Portsmouth Square (1946-12-07)
plotSynopsis: In 1906 San Francisco, young Lily Marcelle arrives at the rough Barbary Coast establishment run by Horseshoe Harry while searching for her shanghaied brother. Harry gives her work as a pianist and unexpectedly supports her musical ambitions, turning their meeting into an unusual romance stretching from Portsmouth Square to the city's high society.

title: 00 Introduction to the OTRR
plotSynopsis: An introductory audio feature for the Strange Wills collection.

title: 01 Strange Wills Series Synopsis
plotSynopsis: An audio overview of Strange Wills, summarizing the series or collection for listeners.

title: 02 William Warren Bio
plotSynopsis: An audio biographical feature on William Warren, included with the Strange Wills collection.

title: 03 Howard Culver Bio
plotSynopsis: An audio biographical feature on Howard Culver, included with the Strange Wills collection.

title: 04 Lurene Tuttle Bio
plotSynopsis: An audio biographical feature on Lurene Tuttle, included with the Strange Wills collection.

title: 05 Lloyd Del Castillo
plotSynopsis: A Strange Wills collection feature identified as “05 Lloyd Del Castillo.”

title: Robert E. Lee (1953-10-04)
plotSynopsis: The drama imagines Robert E. Lee accepting Winfield Scott and Abraham Lincoln's offer to command the United States Army at the beginning of the Civil War instead of ultimately leading Confederate forces, then explores history from that altered decision.

title: Earl of Essex [followed by NBC News] (1953-10-11)
plotSynopsis: The episode explores an alternate history in which the Earl of Essex succeeds in his plot to depose Queen Elizabeth I, rather than seeing the rebellion fail as it did in actual history.

title: The Burr-Hamilton Duel (1953-10-18)
plotSynopsis: The drama reverses the fatal Burr-Hamilton duel, imagining Alexander Hamilton killing Aaron Burr and surviving the encounter, then considers how American history might have changed with Hamilton still alive.

title: Escape of Marie Antoinette (1953-10-25)
plotSynopsis: The episode imagines Marie Antoinette successfully escaping during the French Revolution and avoiding execution by guillotine, using that escape as the point from which its alternate history develops.

title: Lincoln's Consular Service (1953-11-01)
plotSynopsis: The drama imagines Abraham Lincoln obtaining the foreign consular post he wanted in 1841 and leaving the United States, diverting him from the political path that in real history eventually led to the presidency.

title: Benedict Arnold (1953-11-08)
plotSynopsis: The episode asks what might have followed if Benedict Arnold's treason had succeeded and he had managed to turn the American stronghold at West Point over to the British during the Revolution.

title: Caesar and Cleopatra (1953-11-15)
plotSynopsis: The drama imagines Julius Caesar marrying Cleopatra VII of Egypt, using that political and personal union as the altered event from which a different course of ancient history unfolds.

title: Germany Invades the Rhineland (1953-11-22)
plotSynopsis: The episode imagines France responding with military force when Adolf Hitler remilitarizes the Rhineland in 1936, rather than allowing the German move to stand, and explores the consequences of confronting Hitler at that earlier moment.

title: Battle of Quebec (1953-11-29)
plotSynopsis: The drama reverses the 1759 Battle of Quebec, imagining the French defeating the British and retaining Quebec rather than losing the decisive contest for control of New France.

title: Our Neighbor in Alaska (1953-12-06)
plotSynopsis: The episode imagines Russia never selling Alaska to the United States in 1867, leaving Russian territory on the North American continent and exploring the historical consequences of that radically different relationship.

title: Alexander the Great (1953-12-13)
plotSynopsis: The drama imagines Alexander the Great surviving the illness that killed him in 323 BCE and continuing his campaigns in Asia, extending the conqueror's life beyond the age of thirty-two.

title: America's First Secret Weapon (1953-12-20)
plotSynopsis: The episode imagines David Bushnell's Revolutionary War submarine Turtle successfully destroying British warships, turning the experimental one-man submersible into an effective American secret weapon.
