Nick discovers the relatives are genuine and the 'professor' is the fraud: the real Wainger died in Czechoslovakia, and the impostor killed Irwin to escape exposure when the government expected him to produce a submarine detector.

title: Wandering Corpse (aka Missing Corpse, Wedding Anniversary, Lonesome Bear) (1943-10-10)
show: The Adventures of the Thin Man
sortKey: 0|1943-10-10|00002|wandering corpse (aka missing corpse, wedding anniversary, lonesome bear) (1943-10-10)
plotSynopsis: Nick and Nora's anniversary is derailed when a wealthy man's coffin turns out to be empty and his poisoned body appears in a hotel room. Nick reconstructs an elaborate corpse-switch meant to pass off a natural death for the murder and exposes Bellows, who killed the husband so he could marry the widow after she inherited.

title: Nora Is Drugged (aka Mysterious Meow) (1944-10-06)
show: The Adventures of the Thin Man
plotSynopsis: After Nora vanishes and returns with drugged, fragmented memories, Nick finds Bill Martin's body and a second murder tied to Nora's lost evening. The clues show Joan drugged Nora to manufacture an alibi, killed her husband for insurance, used Martin as an accomplice, then murdered him to silence him.

title: COT All American Menace (AFRS Globe Theater) Upgrade (1944-12-01)
show: The Adventures of the Thin Man
sortKey: 0|1944-12-01|00008|cot all american menace (afrs globe theater) upgrade (1944-12-01)
plotSynopsis: Nick and Nora investigate the murder of blackmailer Alistair Fort after football star Plunger Belson and Joan Winslow appear entangled in his files. Fort's cache includes evidence against several people, but Nick traces the decisive prescription and apartment visit to Olga, exposing her as Fort's killer and as the woman whose earlier poisoning secret he had been exploiting.

title: COT Boogie Woogie Murder (AFRS Myst Phs) (1945-02-09)
show: The Adventures of the Thin Man
plotSynopsis: A record-shop mystery draws Nick and Nora into the deaths around musician Martin Curtis and a frightened young woman named Pat. Someone has manipulated threatening letters, guns and a staged confrontation; Nick proves Oliver engineered the scheme, using blanks to make Pat believe she had killed and then murdering the real victims himself.

title: Cot Moon Murder (1945-11-25)
show: The Adventures of the Thin Man
plotSynopsis: Nick and Nora find a body hidden beneath a freshly repaired Fifth Avenue excavation, along with a moon emblem linking the victim to gambler Ellsworth Gilton and a bizarre blackmailing 'moon' cult. After surviving staged threats and sorting the cult's crimes from the murder, Nick exposes Gilton: he killed Patsy Tonelli after Tonelli was hired in a dispute over the racket.

title: Passionate Palooka (1948-07-06)
show: The Adventures of the Thin Man
plotSynopsis: Heavyweight challenger Adam 'Bomber' is too heartsick over his missing dog JoJo to focus on the championship bout, so Nick and Nora investigate the apparent dog-napping. The trail points to girlfriend Lulu, who hid JoJo; the dog is recovered before the fight, though Bomber still loses in the ring and later reconciles with Lulu.

title: Haunted Hams (1948-07-13)
show: The Adventures of the Thin Man
plotSynopsis: A country visit lands Nick and Nora among an amateur acting troupe and a suspicious barn fire, and Nora catches the acting bug. As rehearsals are repeatedly disrupted, Nick finally admits he secretly engineered the animal invasions to ruin Nora's confidence because he feared stardom would take her away; the couple abandons theatrical ambitions after opening night.

title: Leo Is on the Air - 1936 - After the Thin Man (Mentioned at 12 M)
show: The Adventures of the Thin Man
sortKey: 0|9999-99-99|00010|leo is on the air - 1936 - after the thin man (mentioned at 12 m)
plotSynopsis: MGM presents a year-end musical review of hit songs from 1936 films, moving through numbers associated with studio releases before introducing 'Smoke Dreams' as a prospective 1937 hit. The closing segment promotes After the Thin Man, naming returning stars William Powell and Myrna Loy, author Dashiell Hammett and director W.S. Van Dyke.

title: Fred Allen Jimmy Durante (1950-11-05)
plotSynopsis: Tallulah Bankhead's early Big Show broadcast features Fred Allen, Jimmy Durante, Mindy Carson, Frankie Laine, Ethel Merman, Danny Thomas and other guests. Alongside comedy and songs, Jose Ferrer performs a dramatic scene from Cyrano de Bergerac before the company returns to the variety-show finale.

title: Groucho Marx Fanny Brice (1950-11-12)
plotSynopsis: Tallulah Bankhead's Hollywood Big Show features Groucho Marx and Fanny Brice with Jane Powell, Hanley Stafford, David Brian, John Agar and other guests. The broadcast moves between sharp show-business comedy, Baby Snooks material, songs and ensemble exchanges before the closing musical sequence.

title: Eddie Cantor Mindy Carson (1950-11-19)
plotSynopsis: Tallulah Bankhead presides over a crowded variety bill with Eddie Cantor, Mindy Carson, Perry Como, Jimmy Durante, Jose Ferrer and Bob Hope. The guests trade jokes about show business and one another between musical performances and comedy sketches, ending with the full company sign-off.

title: Fred Allen Ed Wynn Jack Carson (1950-11-26)
plotSynopsis: Tallulah Bankhead leads a Big Show edition with Fred Allen, Ed Wynn and Jack Carson, combining extended comedy routines, songs, telephone and show-business gags, and ensemble sketches across the 90-minute broadcast.

title: Fred Allen Phil Silvers (1950-12-03)
plotSynopsis: Tallulah Bankhead hosts Fred Allen and Phil Silvers with Margaret Truman, Mindy Carson, Joan Davis, Douglas Fairbanks Jr., the Sons of the Pioneers and others. Much of the comedy centers on Truman's visit and radio careers, with songs and ensemble bits filling out the broadcast.

title: Clifton Webb Jimmy Durante (1950-12-10)
plotSynopsis: Tallulah Bankhead welcomes Clifton Webb and Jimmy Durante on a full Big Show bill that also includes Mindy Carson and pianist Joe Bushkin. The broadcast alternates comic sparring, songs and a longer acted sketch, then previews the Actors Company feature joining the program.

title: Bob Hope Phil Harris (1950-12-17)
plotSynopsis: From Los Angeles, Tallulah Bankhead hosts Bob Hope and Phil Harris alongside Louis Armstrong, Deborah Kerr, Frankie Laine, Dean Martin and Jerry Lewis. The program mixes Hollywood comedy banter, musical numbers and guest sketches before the company closes the show together.

title: Jimmy Durante Robert Merrill (1950-12-24)
plotSynopsis: Tallulah Bankhead hosts a Christmas Big Show with Jimmy Durante, Robert Merrill, Margaret O'Brien, Bert Lahr, Ed Wynn, Edith Piaf and other guests. The holiday broadcast mixes comedy and music with Christmas material and a closing tribute dedicated to American service members around the world.

title: Vivian Blaine Jose Ferrer (1950-12-31)
plotSynopsis: For a New Year's Eve edition, Tallulah Bankhead hosts Vivian Blaine and Jose Ferrer with Sam Levene, Ken Murray, Margaret O'Brien, Gloria Swanson, Fran Warren and others. The program combines holiday comedy, music and an extended acted scene adapted from Accent on Youth before the New Year closing.

title: Fred Allen Danny Thomas (1951-01-07)
plotSynopsis: Tallulah Bankhead hosts Fred Allen and Danny Thomas with Phil Baker, Edward G. Robinson, Fran Warren, Marlene Dietrich and other guests. The 90-minute broadcast mixes comic exchanges, guest songs and acted scenes before a company finale.

title: Louis Calhern Jack Carter (1951-01-14)
plotSynopsis: Tallulah Bankhead hosts Louis Calhern and Jack Carter with Jimmy Durante, Martha Raye, Florence Desmond and Fran Warren. The program alternates character comedy, songs and acted routines, including extended British-character and show-business bits before the ensemble close.

title: Fred Allen Eddie Cantor (1951-01-21)
plotSynopsis: Tallulah Bankhead hosts Fred Allen and Eddie Cantor with Portland Hoffa, Judy Holliday and other guests. The program moves among topical comedy, character routines, songs and ensemble scenes before the cast joins the closing number.

title: Ray Bolger Gary Cooper (1951-01-28)
plotSynopsis: Tallulah Bankhead hosts Ray Bolger and Gary Cooper with Danny Kaye, Rudy Vallee, the Delta Rhythm Boys and other performers. Alongside comedy and music, Cooper joins a substantial dramatic scene adapted from A Farewell to Arms before the broadcast returns to variety material and the company finale.

title: Fred Allen Robert Cummings (1951-02-04)
plotSynopsis: Tallulah Bankhead hosts Fred Allen and Robert Cummings with Lorraine Day, Judy Holliday, Frankie Laine and other guests. The 90-minute program mixes show-business and baseball comedy, songs and acted sketches before the company closes the broadcast together.

title: Groucho Marx Judy Garland (1951-02-11)
plotSynopsis: Tallulah Bankhead hosts Groucho Marx and Judy Garland from Hollywood with the Andrews Sisters, Joan Davis, Gordon MacRae, Dean Martin and other performers. Comedy and songs dominate the program, followed late in the broadcast by a solemn reading of Abraham Lincoln's letter of condolence to a bereaved mother.

title: Fred Allen Jack Carson (1951-02-18)
plotSynopsis: Tallulah Bankhead hosts Fred Allen and Jack Carson on a broadcast that also features Portland Hoffa, Dennis King and the West Point Choir. A trainload of audience members from New England becomes part of the running comedy as songs and sketches fill out the program.

title: Jack Haley Paul Kelly (1951-02-25)
plotSynopsis: Tallulah Bankhead hosts Jack Haley and Paul Kelly with Uta Hagen, Judy Holliday, Robert Merrill, Olsen and Johnson and Monty Woolley. The 90-minute show combines songs, character comedy and extended routines, including jokes about transferring visual stage and television comedy to radio.

title: Fred Allen Clive Brook (1951-03-04)
plotSynopsis: Tallulah Bankhead hosts Fred Allen and Clive Brook with Portland Hoffa, Ethel Merman, Margaret Truman, Herb Shriner and other performers. The broadcast blends comedy and songs with a substantial dramatic scene before returning to guest banter and the ensemble close.

title: Bob Burns Jimmy Durante (1951-03-11)
plotSynopsis: Tallulah Bankhead hosts a 90-minute Big Show variety broadcast featuring Bob Burns, Jimmy Durante, Evelyn Knight, Celeste Holm and other guests, with comic exchanges, musical performances and ensemble routines built around the visiting stars.

title: Fred Allen Phil Baker (1951-03-18)
plotSynopsis: Tallulah Bankhead hosts Fred Allen and Phil Baker with Eddie Cantor, Eddie Fisher, Ella Fitzgerald, Jan Peerce and other guests. The 90-minute show mixes comic routines, songs and quiz-show parody before the cast closes with a round of farewells.

title: Judy Holliday Carmen Miranda (1951-03-25)
plotSynopsis: Tallulah Bankhead's Easter Sunday Big Show features Judy Holliday and Carmen Miranda with Jimmy Durante, Rex Harrison, Don Cornell, Jackie Miles, Lily Palmer and other guests. Comedy and songs include Miranda's Brazilian-style number, while the closing portion makes a direct Easter appeal for the American Red Cross.

title: Groucho Marx Bob Hope (1951-04-01)
plotSynopsis: From Hollywood, Tallulah Bankhead hosts Groucho Marx and Bob Hope with Joan Davis, Ben Johnson and other guests. The show combines Hollywood comedy, music and ensemble routines, with a more serious literary reading set to orchestral music in the middle of the broadcast.

title: Fred Allen Vivian Blaine (1951-04-08)
plotSynopsis: Tallulah Bankhead hosts Fred Allen and Vivian Blaine with Jimmy Durante, Portland Hoffa, Rudy Vallee, Jane Morgan and other guests. Comedy and songs give way near the close to Ralph Bunche's remarks on democracy, the United Nations and an honor being presented to Bankhead.

title: Eddie Cantor Jack Carson (1951-04-15)
plotSynopsis: Tallulah Bankhead hosts Eddie Cantor and Jack Carson with Martha Raye, Eddie Arnold, Olivia de Havilland and other guests. The 90-minute program combines topical comedy, character routines, songs and ensemble sketches, including baseball-themed comedy late in the broadcast.

title: Fred Allen Portland Hoffa (1951-04-22)
plotSynopsis: Tallulah Bankhead hosts Fred Allen and Portland Hoffa with Joan Davis, Judy Holliday, Dennis King, Lisa Kirk, Herb Shriner and Fran Warren. The show combines illness and show-business comedy, songs and sketches, and closes with a large patriotic reading celebrating American regions, industry and national union.

title: Jimmy Durante Milton Berle (1951-04-29)
plotSynopsis: Tallulah Bankhead hosts Jimmy Durante and Milton Berle with Rosemary Clooney, Ethel Merman, Frank Lovejoy, Gordon MacRae and other guests. The show mixes songs, guest comedy and Bankhead's running efforts to control her temper, along with new-sponsor jokes before the customary company finale.

title: Fred Allen Georgie Jessell (1951-05-06)
plotSynopsis: For the season finale, Tallulah Bankhead welcomes Fred Allen, Georgie Jessel, Groucho Marx, Ginger Rogers, Margaret Truman, Portland Hoffa and others. The broadcast mixes comedy and music with jokes about the season ending, then closes with Bankhead thanking the cast, crew and audience before the summer break.

title: George Sanders Bea Lillie (1951-09-30)
plotSynopsis: Broadcast from London's Palladium as part of NBC's silver-anniversary celebration and its relationship with the BBC, Tallulah Bankhead hosts George Sanders, Beatrice Lillie and a large British-American guest roster. The program mixes transatlantic comedy, music and guest banter built around Bankhead's return to London.

title: Jimmy Durante Jack Carson (1951-10-28)
plotSynopsis: This shorter Armed Forces Radio presentation of The Big Show has Tallulah Bankhead hosting a half-hour segment with Jack Carson, Jimmy Durante and other performers. It combines Carson's comedy with a darker acted vignette about a father hunting the man who attacked his daughter, then returns to comedy and the company sign-off.

title: Richard Eatham Joe Frisco (1952-03-09)
plotSynopsis: Tallulah Bankhead hosts Richard Eatham and Joe Frisco on a later Big Show edition with a large comedy-and-music cast. The broadcast includes an extended dramatic scene about a hard-nosed show-business figure explaining why genuine talent survives rejection, then returns to songs, comedy and the closing chorus.

title: The 22 Caliber Pistol
plotSynopsis: A woman accused of killing her lover faces a trial in which the physical evidence and her own account produce an unexpected result.

title: A 32 Caliber Bullet
plotSynopsis: Scotland Yard follows the history of one bullet to connect jewelry-store robbers with a killer.

title: The Bath Tub
plotSynopsis: A serial bigamist murders wives for their money by drowning them until police expose how the scheme worked.

title: The Bloodstained Brick Bat
plotSynopsis: A handyman's visit to a suburban house ends in a savage attack that reveals jealousy and hidden domestic tensions.

title: The Brass Button
plotSynopsis: A brass button found near a murdered woman points investigators toward the killer inside a nearby military camp.

title: ACan Of Weedkiller
plotSynopsis: A wife's sudden death divides an English village and produces a murder trial with an uncertain truth.

title: The Canvas Bag
plotSynopsis: Investigators identify a dismembered victim and uncover a betrayal connected to a seemingly ordinary canvas bag.

title: The Car Tire
plotSynopsis: The killing of a police constable during a stolen-car case is solved through parts stripped from the vehicle and one surviving tire.

title: AClaw Hammer
plotSynopsis: A con man posing as a workman murders an elderly woman, but the weapon and his distinctive habits lead police to him.

title: The Door Key
plotSynopsis: A mysterious key found with a murdered traveling salesman becomes Scotland Yard's route into the case.

title: The Faded Tartan Scarf
plotSynopsis: A distinctive tartan scarf becomes the crucial evidence tying a career criminal to murder.

title: Four Small Bottles
plotSynopsis: A wealthy older man's chloroform poisoning brings suspicion onto his young wife and a clergyman.

title: Glass Shards
plotSynopsis: A fatal burglary leaves shattered glass and a missing bracelet as the clues investigators must reconstruct.

title: The Hammerhead
plotSynopsis: A missing-person inquiry turns into a murder case after dismembered remains reveal a family secret and the weapon used.

title: The Jack Handle
plotSynopsis: A wartime romance between an American soldier and a British accomplice descends into violent crime in blackout London.

title: The Khaki Handkerchief
plotSynopsis: The murders of two girls are solved through forensic evidence and observations made by children.

title: ALady's Shoe
plotSynopsis: A bride's disappearance exposes her husband's suspicious behavior, forged documents, and evidence supplied by a loyal dog.

title: The Mandolin String
plotSynopsis: A single instrument string helps police connect two supposedly accidental deaths to a deliberate crime.

title: The Notes
plotSynopsis: A series of killings marked by the same taunting phrase sends an inspector after an unexpected murderer.

title: The Old Wooden Mallet
plotSynopsis: A burned car and charred body expose a salesman's double life and his attempt to stage his own death.

title: The Pair Of Spectacles
plotSynopsis: Police trace a missing young woman's final movements to a chicken farmer who becomes central to her murder investigation.

title: The Pink Powder Puff
plotSynopsis: A faded powder puff becomes the small piece of evidence that helps expose a manipulative serial killer.

title: The Post Card
plotSynopsis: A postcard marked by a distinctive rising-sun drawing becomes a vital clue in a brutal murder.

title: The Sash Cord
plotSynopsis: A Brighton theater murder reveals a scheme involving gambling debts, deception, and a stagehand's death.

title: AService Card
plotSynopsis: A car's maintenance record helps investigators reconstruct a young man's progression from robbery to killing his own parent.

title: ASilencer
plotSynopsis: A Scotland Yard inspector hunts an unseen gunman terrorizing residents of a new suburban development.

title: The Spotted Bedsheet
plotSynopsis: Blood on a bed sheet and an open porthole turn a woman's disappearance from an ocean liner into a shipwide murder inquiry.

title: The Tan Shoe
plotSynopsis: A bloodstained tan shoe exposes the murderer of a trusted colliery paymaster killed aboard a train.

title: The Telegram
plotSynopsis: Investigators study a telegram in detail after a young woman's new job leads her into a killer's trap.

title: ATrunk
plotSynopsis: A trunk containing dismembered remains at Charing Cross sets London police on a painstaking identification and murder inquiry.

title: The Walking Stick
plotSynopsis: Suspicious deaths in a Glasgow doctor's household bring him under investigation and eventually onto a murder charge.

title: The Wool Jacket
plotSynopsis: A baby's wool jacket preserved in the Black Museum introduces the disturbing criminal case associated with it.

title: Drug Ring Pt 1-2 (1940-05-15)
plotSynopsis: The Blue Beetle attacks a narcotics ring after a movie star's suicide note says drugs have become her master. Dan Garrett is machine-gunned during the investigation and nearly dies, but Dr. Franz gives him an experimental formula that produces a rapid recovery and lets him resume the case. Following the weapon and the traffickers to a waterfront warehouse, the Blue Beetle rescues the police commissioner's kidnapped daughter, breaks up the dope ring and then lets the police receive public credit for the arrests.

title: Sabotage-Liquidation Pt 1-2 (1940-05-17)
plotSynopsis: The Blue Beetle uncovers an international sabotage ring targeting new American military aircraft and moves to break up the operation.

title: Murder for Profit Pt 1-2 (1940-05-22)
plotSynopsis: After wealthy investment broker James Ridley dies during an operation, the Blue Beetle suspects his death was arranged so conspirators could profit from the stock-market panic. He searches the Ridley home and uncovers documents linking Ridley's partner Cochran and a corrupt doctor to the scheme, but is captured when the plotters move to silence everyone who can expose them. With help from Dr. Franz and the doctor's imprisoned intern, the Blue Beetle escapes, overpowers the conspirators and leaves the murder-for-profit ring for the police and district attorney.

title: Blasting the Dynamite Gang Pt 1-2 (1940-05-24)
plotSynopsis: A dynamite gang bombs the city, disables power and exploits the resulting chaos for widespread robbery while the mayor's son is kidnapped. The Blue Beetle survives capture by the Octopus, is freed with the boy's help, chases the mastermind by motorboat, saves him from drowning, and leaves the gang for police.

title: Invisible Ghost Pt 1-2 (1940-05-29)
plotSynopsis: A slot-machine racket tries to force crooked gambling devices into local businesses, while Dr. Franz gives the Blue Beetle an experimental coating that can make him temporarily invisible. Using the formula, the Blue Beetle infiltrates the gang's supposed haunted-house headquarters, survives a trap that drops him into an underground stream and returns unseen to terrify the racketeers into surrendering. He leaves the prisoners for Mannegan, who still has no idea that Dan Garrett and the Blue Beetle are the same man.

title: Death Rides on Horseback Pt 1-2 (1940-05-31)
plotSynopsis: A masked horseman wages a murder campaign against police officers in the city park, and the Blue Beetle discovers that the killings are part of a political conspiracy meant to discredit the current police administration. Captured in the killer's underground base, he refuses to join the scheme and escapes a flooding cell with remote help from Dr. Franz. He frees reporter Joan Mason, defeats the killer, exposes the businessman behind the conspiracy and leaves the evidence and prisoners for the police.

title: Death Strikes from the East Pt 1-2 (1940-06-05)
plotSynopsis: The Blue Beetle investigates an extortion racket terrorizing Chinatown under the name of the Purple Dragon. The gang forces merchants to buy through its organization and kidnaps a city markets commissioner and his daughter in an attempt to stop official action against the scheme. The Blue Beetle traces the operation to wealthy importer Tony Rondos, survives an attempt to kill him and breaks up the gang at its Chinatown stronghold, giving the threatened merchants the chance to turn on the men who had intimidated them.

title: Sea Serpent Pt 1-2 (1940-06-07)
plotSynopsis: A supposed sea serpent drives swimmers away from a resort after victims die with paired puncture wounds. The Blue Beetle discovers that corrupt lifeguards are injecting swimmers with cobra venom through twin hypodermic needles to create snake-bite marks and sustain the scare; he rescues Joan Mason, captures the operators, and exposes the scheme.

title: Frame-Up Pt 1-2 (1940-06-12)
plotSynopsis: The Blue Beetle races to save an innocent man from execution while uncovering a conspiracy involving a ruthless loan shark and a corrupt official.

title: Spirits Dont Talk Pt 1-2 (1940-06-14)
plotSynopsis: A fatal seance draws the Blue Beetle into a spiritualist racket that uses fraud, fear and murder to exploit its victims.

title: Thoroughbreds Always Come Through 1-2 (1940-06-19)
plotSynopsis: After jockey Buddy Winston dies suspiciously, the Blue Beetle investigates a betting scheme built around swapping and repainting similar horses so the gang can manipulate races and odds. The conspirators also frame a stable worker, but the Blue Beetle uses Dr. Franz's portable television apparatus to capture their incriminating conversation and turn the evidence over to police.

title: Smashing the Arson Ring Pt 1-2 (1940-06-21)
plotSynopsis: A wave of fires at vacant or heavily insured properties leads the Blue Beetle to professional arsonists using naphtha. After two witnesses are kidnapped and Garrett is nearly buried in a sand barge, he escapes, reaches the gang leader's yacht, rescues the captives, and breaks the waterfront arson ring.

title: Rounding Up the Payroll Bandits Pt 1-2 (1940-06-26)
plotSynopsis: A string of payroll robberies appears to depend on inside information. The Blue Beetle discovers that respected philanthropist Benjamin Jarvis uses his mission as cover to coerce parolees into robberies by threatening to send them back to prison; Dr. Franz records the confrontation, Jarvis is exposed, and the payroll racket collapses.

title: Crime Incorporated Pt 1-2 (1940-07-03)
plotSynopsis: A nationwide syndicate frames the Blue Beetle by using impostors to commit crimes in his name, forcing him to clear himself while attacking the organization.

title: Saved by a Hair Pt 1-2 (1940-07-10)
plotSynopsis: A gang exploits parolees by threatening to send them back to prison unless they help with robberies and other crimes. When policeman Joe Riley is killed and Commissioner Donnelly's daughter Helen is kidnapped, the Blue Beetle follows the racket through a cafe owner, a crooked lawyer and a farmhouse hideout. He rescues Helen, turns the surviving gang members over to police and exposes the blackmail operation, with the lawyer's carefully dyed black hair becoming the clue that helps identify him during the final confrontation.

title: Finesse in Diamonds Pt 1-2 (1940-07-17)
plotSynopsis: The disappearance of the Bannisters' half-million-dollar diamond necklace produces two convincing fakes and leaves social secretary Lucy Ridgeway jailed. The Blue Beetle uncovers insurance investigator McCaffrey's double-cross, retrieves the genuine necklace before the thieves can sail for South America, and clears Lucy after Mr. Bannister confirms the real stones and says his wife has confessed.

title: Sabotage Incorporated Pt 1-2 (1940-07-24)
plotSynopsis: After a munitions executive is murdered, the Blue Beetle races to expose saboteurs planning to destroy an important military shipment.

title: Smashing the Restaurant Racket Pt 1-2 (1940-07-31)
plotSynopsis: The Cosmopolitan Restaurant Owners Association pretends to protect eateries but uses phony labor trouble, violence and intimidation to extort restaurant owners and finance a political machine. The Blue Beetle infiltrates the racket, escapes a burning building with reporter Joan Mason, uses her documents to expose Danford as the power behind it, and helps stop his attempted flight after the gang's killers are intercepted.

title: Two Rackets in One Pt 1-2 (1940-08-07)
plotSynopsis: Two protection rackets squeeze trucking and poultry businesses that refuse to join their associations. After a truck driver is killed and banker Williamson is murdered by a bomb, the Blue Beetle traces both schemes to brothers Julio and Nick Martinell and finds evidence that Williamson had threatened to expose them. He pursues the gang beyond the city, survives an attack during the chase and helps bring in Nick, whose confession also implicates bribed politicians who protected the rackets.

title: Underworld Goes Underground Pt 1-2 (1940-08-14)
plotSynopsis: Reginald Dunlap's tunnel project suffers suspicious accidents that threaten his construction contract. The Blue Beetle infiltrates the job, survives an attempt to kill him through rapid decompression, learns that insiders plan a staged tunnel disaster, and gets warnings out in time to save the workers and expose the sabotage.

title: Dancing Ghost of Rocky Hill Pt 1-2 (1940-08-21)
plotSynopsis: A coded plea draws the Blue Beetle to Gray Crags Manor, where a young heiress named Rosalie is being kept under close control while supposed ghosts dance in the windows. He discovers that the haunting is produced mechanically to conceal a counterfeiting operation and an inheritance scheme, tips the sheriff to the counterfeit money, and rounds up the men behind the deception.

title: Whale of Pirates Folly Pt 1-2 (1940-08-28)
plotSynopsis: A perfume peddler leads the Blue Beetle to a smuggling operation bringing untaxed perfume, liquor and other contraband from the West Indies. The apparent whale seen offshore proves connected to the racket's concealed submarine method of landing cargo, and the Blue Beetle follows the smugglers from a warehouse to their coastal base. He survives being trapped and thrown into the water, then helps police seize the submarine cargo and arrest the surviving members of the ring.

title: Asylum of Doctor Drear Pt 1-2 (1940-09-04)
plotSynopsis: The disappearance of a prominent banker leads the Blue Beetle to a sinister asylum and a scheme driven by greed and deception.

title: Jewel Mystery of Channel Island Pt 1-2 (1940-09-11)
plotSynopsis: Sent to Channel Island to investigate jewel thefts at the Bonair Hotel, Dan Garrett learns that the stolen gems are being moved away from the island rather than kept at the hotel. As the Blue Beetle he secretly tags the jewels for his radio locator, follows their carrier-pigeon route to a mainland hideout, and catches the gang receiving the stones while allowing Mannegan to take official credit.

title: Origin Story
plotSynopsis: The Blue Beetle investigates a citywide drug racket after a movie star's death and the grave wounding of a fellow police officer.

title: Alley Cat (1971-09-17)
plotSynopsis: John’s marriage explodes when his hard-drinking wife Linda admits she married him for money, has emptied his bank account and intends to throw him out. In fury he repeatedly calls her a cat, and the suggestion becomes horrifyingly literal as Linda changes into a great snarling feline creature. John hides her from the world, kills a doctor who wants to report the transformation, and when a neighbor discovers the animal he chooses a final, desperate use of his gun rather than let anyone take Linda from him.

title: Neanderthal (1971-09-24)
plotSynopsis: After an automobile plunges over a cliff, Jeffrey and his companions awaken injured in a prehistoric landscape and encounter an actual Neanderthal hunter. Realizing they have somehow fallen backward through time, the modern travelers discover that reason and civilized manners are useless against brute force. Jeffrey, a diplomat who has always despised weapons, finally uses the gun he carries to kill the attacking caveman and keep the group alive in a world tens of thousands of years before their own.

title: Revolt of the Worms (1971-10-01)
plotSynopsis: A researcher retreats to the country after experimenting with powerful growth hormones, only to discover that discarded chemicals have soaked into the soil and transformed ordinary earthworms into gigantic creatures. The worms kill those around him and multiply until their enormous bodies churn beneath and across the land. Trapped in his house as the monsters lift its foundations, he realizes that his attempt to escape the troubles of the modern world has created an even greater threat.

title: Where Are You (1971-10-08)
plotSynopsis: Newlyweds Michael and his wife visit New York and suddenly discover that the Empire State Building, Times Square and eventually the entire city have been abandoned in the middle of ordinary life. With no radio broadcasts and no sign of humanity, they wonder whether mankind has been removed after exhausting divine patience with war and cruelty. Facing a silent world together, they decide that if they have been left to begin again, they must build their new life around the principle of treating others as they would wish to be treated.

title: Mr Freak (1971-10-15)
plotSynopsis: Paul has hidden from society because a badly deformed face has taught him to expect ridicule and rejection. He befriends a blind young woman who knows him only through his voice and kindness, and their closeness deepens as she prepares for an operation that may restore her sight. Convinced that seeing him will destroy her affection, Paul nearly kills himself, but she finds him first, looks directly at the face he hates and tells him that she loves him in the light as she did in darkness.

title: Gravestone (1971-10-22)
plotSynopsis: Three young women on a winter holiday wander through an old burial ground and accidentally trample and dance on a grave. One is struck by a rock that seems to fly from the cemetery, and mounting disturbances convince the terrified women that a poltergeist has been angered by the desecration. During the night two of them are drawn back through the snow to the grave, where rescuers find them strangely dancing over it as the supernatural attacks begin again.

title: Ancestor (1971-10-29)
plotSynopsis: A young woman held by three criminals prays for help while her captors wait for another killer to arrive and dispose of her. An unseen presence identifies itself as an ancestor who has returned in her agony, and the gangsters begin dying from arrows fired by no visible hand. Police finally find all three men dead and rescue the shaken captive, who repeatedly names Philippe de Martevard, an ancestor in her family who lived more than eight centuries earlier.

title: Nature Study (1971-11-05)
plotSynopsis: A Sunday nature-study group hikes into an isolated canyon, where accidents begin killing its members one by one. The survivors gradually reveal that each has secretly committed murder, including a woman who poisoned the friend she saw as a romantic rival. By nightfall the apparent accidents look less accidental, and the last man is left alone with the bodies as an advancing shadow calls out the crimes of the dead and comes to claim him as well.

title: Big Mr Little (1971-11-12)
plotSynopsis: After a drunken mixture, an ordinary little man discovers that whatever destructive thing he wishes aloud immediately happens, from a falling elevator to fatal accidents. A doctor proves the power can also work for good when a wish restores a blind newsdealer’s sight, but the newly empowered man instead plans to blackmail governments and industrial leaders by threatening death. The doctor and his wife pretend to cooperate until they turn the man’s own failure to respect them against him and end his reign before he can impose himself on the world.

title: No Escape (1971-11-19)
plotSynopsis: Condemned prisoner Rogan is obsessed with revenge against Mark Street, the man he says betrayed him and caused the death at the center of his case. He escapes death row through flooded sewers, murdering a fellow prisoner during the flight, only to learn that Street has already died. Rogan goes to Street’s grave determined to follow him into death if necessary, and there the boundaries between the living and dead collapse as the murder victim’s spirit returns and the old vengeance continues beyond the grave.

title: Vacation with Death (1971-11-26)
plotSynopsis: A family rents an elegant country house for an implausibly low price, despite the strange behavior of its elderly caretaker and their young son’s uneasiness. The boy begins witnessing spectral scenes of a mother and daughter being murdered twenty years earlier, and the visions expose the caretaker as the killer who now intends to silence the new witnesses. As he turns his gun on the family, the long-dead victims intervene through the house’s ghostly music and finally take their revenge.

title: The Hole (1971-12-03)
plotSynopsis: College student Ray Stewart imagines a chemical solvent that feeds on everything it dissolves and grows stronger as it consumes the earth. His experiment becomes an expanding pit that swallows buildings, bores miles downward and threatens to tear the planet apart while terrified crowds blame its creator. The apocalypse abruptly gives way to a mundane tragedy: a watchman finds Ray dead after sleepwalking across campus and diving headfirst into an empty swimming pool, revealing the bottomless hole as his final nightmare.

title: Live Forever (1971-12-10)
plotSynopsis: A man terrified of death is carried in a vision into a future where science has made human beings effectively immortal. Instead of paradise, he finds an overcrowded society dominated forever by the same ancient people, while younger generations have no work, authority or purpose. A group of frustrated young immortals recruits him into assassinating their elders to make room for themselves, and the horror sends him back to his own time newly convinced that death is necessary for life and renewal.

title: Going Down (1971-12-17)
plotSynopsis: Ernie takes his wife Emma deep beneath the city into service tunnels and sub-basements, secretly intending to kill her and then himself. Their plan is overtaken by something far stranger when a blind creature from beneath the earth begins stalking them through the dark. Ernie finally confesses why he brought Emma there, sends her away to recover the note that would make him look like her murderer, and stays behind to draw the creature toward himself so she can escape.

title: Balance Sheet (1971-12-24)
plotSynopsis: A young Corday heir reaches her family’s isolated island and discovers the true source of its wealth: for more than three centuries, generations of workers have been conditioned to surrender freedom in exchange for lifelong security at the family factory. Horrified, she tries to shut the machines down and teach the workers to live as independent human beings, but they resist the very freedom she offers. When the old caretaker abandons her on the island, she is left among the workers determined to begin the harder task of teaching them what freedom means.

title: House Is Haunted (1971-12-31)
plotSynopsis: After cheating an Australian bushman out of a valuable diamond and killing him, Alec Riverton returns home haunted by the dead man’s warning that he will die on the third day. The victim’s voice begins speaking through strangers around Alec, including a cab driver, waiter and finally his doctor, driving him deeper into terror. On the third day Alec panics when the doctor approaches with a sedative, sees the murdered man in his place and collapses dead as the prophecy appears to complete itself.

title: Official Killer (1972-01-07)
plotSynopsis: Samuel Jones has spent years as the state’s official hangman, taking pride in carrying out hundreds of executions. After hanging a young prisoner, he is confronted by the man’s mother and learns that the condemned youth was his own son. The shock unleashes a nightmare procession of the relatives of people he has executed, all seeming to pursue him through the streets, until the terrified hangman barricades himself indoors and kills himself before the imagined mob can reach him.

title: The Hungry One (1972-01-14)
plotSynopsis: Astronomer Russell Adams and his wife Diane watch a meteor shower when one object crashes near their home. From the meteor grows a huge bodiless head, an alien intelligence that can speak with them and regards human beings as food. When it draws Diane toward itself, Russell attacks and destroys the creature, only to look up and see more meteorites streaking toward Earth, suggesting that the first hungry visitor may have been only the beginning.

title: Three Thousand Dollars (1972-01-21)
plotSynopsis: A sailor named Swenson wins three thousand dollars in a sweepstakes and happily plans to use it for the little farm he has dreamed of buying for his wife and children. His friend Tony, a hard-bitten deep-sea diver obsessed with money, dismisses that modest dream and soon accepts a dangerous dive for a share of a million dollars in sunken gold. Beneath the sea Tony hears the voice of a dead sailor calling to him; when the crew finally hauls up his line, Tony is gone and only a gold bar is tied where he should have been.

title: The Chest (1972-01-28)
plotSynopsis: Harold brings home a heavy brass-bound chest bought cheaply at auction, despite his family’s anger over the purchase. When they force it open, the inside is stained with old blood, and soon the chest seems to move and strike on its own: Harold’s son is found dead beneath its lid and his wife disappears upstairs after confronting it. Left alone, Harold attacks the advancing chest with an axe, while a later revelation identifies it as the very chest in which a murderer once concealed a young woman’s body.

title: Paris Macabre (1972-02-04)
plotSynopsis: Two young Americans in Paris stumble into a strange nighttime gathering filled with people who seem to belong to another century. An old woman reveals that the dancers are victims of the guillotine who return for a single night and need a living head so one of their own can remain. One of the friends is taken and appears again as a headless figure, while the other flees into the street from a nightmare whose boundary with reality is never fully explained.

title: Rocket from Manhattan (1972-02-11)
plotSynopsis: A spacecraft crew returns toward Earth decades after atomic power was supposed to guarantee permanent peace. From orbit they watch old hatreds erupt into global war as nuclear weapons escalate beyond control, while the scientist who once promised peace admits that humanity learned nothing from its earlier terror. A hydrogen chain reaction finally burns away the planet’s atmosphere, leaving the crew circling a dead Earth with only a few hours of life-support remaining.

title: Hollywood Visitor (1972-02-18)
plotSynopsis: Fading Hollywood star Madeline Kay visits the English coastal home of her financial adviser Charles and bluntly tells his wife that she intends to take him away from her. Local fishermen try to warn Charles that something dangerous is moving in the water, but he dismisses them and takes Madeline out by boat. A gigantic octopus-like creature attacks; the fishermen rescue Charles and the others, but the monster finally coils an arm around Madeline and drags her into the sea, turning the story’s warning about retribution into a literal ending.

title: Cemetary (1972-02-25)
plotSynopsis: Veteran newspaper columnist Sam Roberts is dismissed by ruthless new publisher Jay Rogers Bridge just before the pension he has spent decades earning. Soon afterward Bridge’s own arrogance drives away his chauffeur on a lonely night, and a mysterious stranger leads him into the family cemetery and toward the graves of those whose lives his decisions have damaged. The next morning a proof sheet inexplicably appears announcing that Bridge has committed suicide in his family mausoleum, complete with a signature from the dead columnist.

title: Speed (1972-03-03)
plotSynopsis: A private detective investigates a spree of impossible daylight robberies and hit-and-run deaths and discovers a scientist whose chemical can accelerate body and mind dozens of times beyond normal human speed. The detective joins him, and together they use the drug for theft, murder and dreams of controlling the country. Their stronger final concentrate works too well: their life processes accelerate without limit, and in moments their bodies race through an entire lifetime, aging them to death before their conquest can begin.

title: Shrinking People (1972-03-10)
plotSynopsis: Explorer Peter Strensky learns that his wife Ellen plans to leave him for John and pretends to arrange a civilized divorce. Instead he poisons John, imprisons Ellen and uses a South American shrinking technique to turn both lovers’ bodies into doll-sized trophies for his lectures. Fleeing England with the preserved pair hidden in a trunk, Strensky begins hearing their voices, throws them overboard and is finally dragged into the sea by the tiny figures he thought he had destroyed.

title: Citizenship-Insurance Racket (aka-Political Racket) (1938-05-05)
plotSynopsis: Ward boss Joe Desmond preys on new immigrants by selling them expensive life-insurance policies as if they were fast-track citizenship papers, then uses a city official to place the victims on public jobs and strengthen his political machine. When witnesses become dangerous, murder follows; the Green Hornet turns Desmond's own murder weapon and frightened lieutenant Nelson against the organization, producing a confession that exposes the insurance-citizenship fraud and the killings behind it.

title: The Crooked Bridge (1938-05-24)
plotSynopsis: Grand-jury investigator James Conway is ready to expose a protected gambling ring when the mob kidnaps his daughter Paula and demands his evidence. The Hornet poses as one of the abductors, follows the trail to Dick Sloughkin's Seven-Eleven club, prevents the gang's plan to kill father and daughter in a staged bridge accident, and helps Conway bring trusted police in on a raid that recovers Paula and the evidence.

title: Phony Insurance Advisor (1938-11-01)
plotSynopsis: Duke and Webster pose as independent insurance advisers and persuade policyholders to replace sound policies with arrangements that benefit the racketeers while costing victims more in the long run. When they mistakenly decide a man named Lund is the Green Hornet, they try to blackmail him for $50,000; police overhear the attempted squeeze, giving them the blackmail case and the evidence needed to expose the insurance racket.

title: There Was a Crooked Man (1939-04-06)
plotSynopsis: Grand-jury investigator James Conway returns with evidence capable of smashing a protected gambling ring, only to reverse himself after his daughter Polly is kidnapped and held as leverage. The Green Hornet penetrates the syndicate behind the gambling houses, disrupts the coercion of Conway and preserves the evidence needed to expose the protection network rather than letting the kidnappers dictate the investigation.

title: Not a Drop Worth Drinking (1939-05-09)
plotSynopsis: An illness outbreak is used to frighten the city into buying an expensive new water-filtration system, while city chemist Fox produces tests that seem to prove the water is contaminated and discredits Dr. Holmes for saying otherwise. The Hornet and Holmes uncover the fraud, replace the samples with pure distilled water, and a public retest still shows contamination, proving Fox rigged his reagents and exposing the graft behind the scare.

title: The Ghost Who Talked Too Much (1939-05-30)
plotSynopsis: The Green Hornet targets a bogus spiritualist who exploits grieving clients while steering them into a fraudulent investment scheme.

title: Words and Music (1939-06-01)
plotSynopsis: The Green Hornet goes after a nationwide music-publishing swindle and forces the racketeers to make restitution to the people they cheated.

title: Charity Takes It on the Chin (1939-06-06)
plotSynopsis: The Green Hornet investigates a welfare-fund theft scheme in which crooked insiders exploit pre-signed charity checks to siphon money from the city’s needy.

title: Trouble Hits the Trolleys (1939-06-08)
plotSynopsis: Britt Reid, acting as the Green Hornet, uncovers a businessman’s scheme to sabotage public transportation for his own profit.

title: Not One Cent for Tribute (1939-06-13)
plotSynopsis: The Green Hornet devises a trap to break a powerful gas-station protection racket and bring its violent leader down.

title: Justice Wears a Blindfold (1939-06-15)
plotSynopsis: A judge is pressured by a racketeer through blackmail, and the Green Hornet intervenes before corruption can dictate the outcome.

title: Money Talks Too Loud (1939-06-20)
plotSynopsis: The Green Hornet moves against bookmaking interests trying to buy legislative support for a bill legalizing horse-race gambling.

title: Pink Lemonade and Tan Bark (1939-06-22)
plotSynopsis: A protection racket preys on circuses and other traveling shows, using hired toughs to cause damage unless owners pay Fenders for protection. Britt frames three of Fenders's muscle men for a staged burglary, then uses their anger over withheld pay to make them expose the whole setup in front of witnesses, allowing the police to break the extortion ring.

title: Bait for a Two-Timer (1939-06-27)
plotSynopsis: After a corrupt construction job collapses, Britt deliberately plants a false Sentinel story about missing fire-sprinkler equipment to identify the newspaper leak feeding information to the rival Clarion and to panic the officials behind the building graft. The Green Hornet then traps inspector Hudson and his partner inside another building, using smoke and the working sprinklers to force a signed confession that exposes the construction racket without killing them.

title: Pavement Condemned (1939-06-29)
plotSynopsis: Contractor Brande Meyer lets a street-paving strike drag on while merchants lose business and face financial ruin, positioning himself to profit from the distressed property. The Green Hornet obtains evidence tying Meyer to the scheme and forces him to settle the strike, return the money involved and put the paving crews back to work before the Sentinel publishes the story.

title: Put It on Ice (1939-07-04)
plotSynopsis: The Green Hornet investigates and exposes a plan to sabotage a meatpacking business and ruin its owner.

title: Disaster Rides the Rails (1939-07-06)
plotSynopsis: A rigged poker game aboard a train ends in murder, drawing the Green Hornet into a case built on deception and false accusations.

title: The Devil's Playground (aka-Carnival) (1939-07-11)
plotSynopsis: After an accident on the Devil’s Dipper roller coaster, the Green Hornet works to expose the contractors hiding evidence that the dangerous ride was knowingly left unsafe.

title: War on the Waterfront (1939-07-18)
plotSynopsis: Shipowner Jensen's loading operation is crippled by suspicious accidents and a strike while someone demands $5,000 to make the trouble stop. Although union leader Trask appears responsible, the Green Hornet discovers that Trask's aide Wolf is really working for Slickby, the supposedly neutral head of the arbitration board. The Hornet follows the river payoff and turns it into evidence that exposes Slickby's extortion scheme and clears Trask.

title: House and Home (1939-07-20)
plotSynopsis: A deadly fire draws attention to unsafe tenements owned by Macklin, but a corrupt building inspector keeps the slum properties from being condemned. When ordinary legal pressure fails, the Green Hornet forces the issue and gets the suppressed inspection papers into police hands; the records prove the buildings were unfit and expose Macklin's arrangement with the inspector.

title: Murder by Accident (1939-07-27)
plotSynopsis: Promoters of a fraudulent old-age pension campaign skim most of the contributions, and when collector Hurley threatens to expose them they have him killed and the death staged as an accident. The Hornet steals their payroll records, identifies the hired killer and lets the conspirators' fear turn them against one another, effectively delivering the murderer to police.

title: Bait for a Burglar (1939-08-01)
plotSynopsis: Respected philanthropist Gilmore is secretly the 'big shot' behind a burglary ring, using fence Crocker to move stolen property. Britt turns his own apartment and valuables into bait, and a concealed photograph plus the criminals' conversation gives police the evidence to expose Gilmore, Crocker and the receiving operation.

title: A Racket in the Ring (1939-08-03)
plotSynopsis: Struggling fighter Danny Cannon is drawn into a crooked boxing scheme in which his manager disguises him as the supposedly foreign 'Pampas Panther' and manipulates betting around the match. The Green Hornet gets Cannon out before the bout, lets the real fighter take the ring and turns the corrupt manager and boxing commissioner against each other until their fixed-fight racket is exposed.

title: The Lawyer Beats the Law (1939-08-08)
plotSynopsis: Crooked attorney Sturgis repeatedly keeps racketeer Moroni beyond the reach of the law by manufacturing alibis and manipulating evidence. The Green Hornet turns the criminals' own murder weapon and distrust against them, forcing Sturgis into an incriminating confrontation with Moroni and Jigger that police overhear, ending the lawyer's career as an officer of the court and exposing him as an accessory to their crimes.

title: Lightning Hits a Shakedown (1939-08-10)
plotSynopsis: Political operator Fargo secretly causes power failures so he can attack the private light company, promote a city takeover and shake down company president Porter. The Green Hornet traces the sabotage to Fargo's hired man Scadron and stages a confrontation with blank cartridges that makes Scadron confess the power-plant attack in front of witnesses, destroying Fargo's racket.

title: Money in the Meter (1939-08-15)
plotSynopsis: Wakeman controls the city's taxi business through inflated charges, finance-company traps, blacklisting and intimidation of independent drivers. The Green Hornet uses threatened cabbie Potsy as bait, arranging for police to catch Wakeman and his gunmen breaking into the driver's room with intent to kill him, giving the law the charge needed to unravel the larger taxi racket.

title: A Racket Robs the Cradle (1939-08-17)
plotSynopsis: A child-actress publicity machine built around Honey Bancroft becomes entangled in a staged disappearance and a manager's exploitative contracts. The Green Hornet returns the child safely, turns the supposed kidnapping back on the adults using it for publicity and destroys the contracts that bound Honey and other youngsters to the same arrangement, ending the cradle-robbing racket.

title: A Rake-Off on the Job (1939-08-22)
plotSynopsis: Employment agent Croll collects ten-dollar deposits from desperate job seekers, while employer Quentin briefly hires and then fires them so the two men can split a steady stream of fees. The Green Hornet uses one of the cheated applicants to bring the partners together, gets them arguing openly about the scheme, and leaves police with a live witness and the admissions needed to break the employment racket.

title: The House That Jack Built (1939-08-24)
plotSynopsis: Builders are being forced to pay protection to Carlotti's organization, which uses fires and bombs against anyone who refuses. The Green Hornet infiltrates the racket, empties the explosive from a bomb planted in a new house and detonates a harmless charge nearby; the intact bomb, complete with the planter's fingerprints, gives police the evidence to break the gang.

title: Numbers Make a Racket (1939-08-29)
plotSynopsis: Numbers boss Tobin has Dootcher murdered and uses innocent cab driver Potsie as the fall guy, while the racket continues behind layers of intimidation. Britt proves the cab was manipulated, then the Hornet corners Tobin and his men and deliberately gets Tobin talking while a policeman listens from the fire escape, producing the confession that clears Potsie and smashes the numbers operation.

title: Ripe for the Taking (1939-09-05)
plotSynopsis: Franklin's Farm by Proxy scheme sells worthless rocky acreage as future apple orchards and locks victims into years of maintenance charges. The Green Hornet plants a fake geological report suggesting oil on the land, tricking Franklin and his partner into buying the acreage back from their customers at inflated prices before learning there was never any oil and they are stuck with the worthless property.

title: Courtroom Racket (1939-09-07)
plotSynopsis: Court official Cole decides to expose Robertson's racket of forcing state court employees to kick back part of their salaries, but Robertson intercepts him before he can reach the Sentinel. The Green Hornet tracks the conspirators to their hideout, prevents Robertson's men from murdering Cole, and leaves him alive to give reporters the facts that finally break the courtroom extortion scheme.

title: State Institution Racket (1939-10-26)
plotSynopsis: The Sentinel investigates politician Murchison's control of state institutions and the ease with which people can be confined without meaningful review. Undercover reporter Sherman obtains records of graft at Rock Ridge, only to be branded a dangerous escaped lunatic when the racket discovers him. The Green Hornet preserves the records and leaves Murchison's organization exposed to police, helping clear the way for reform.

title: Cash on the Parking Lot (aka-The Parking Lot Racket) (1939-10-31)
sortKey: 0|1939-10-31|00389|cash on the parking lot (aka-the parking lot racket) (1939-10-31)
plotSynopsis: The Green Hornet sets a calculated trap for operators of a parking-lot protection racket and turns their own methods against them.

title: Test Stamps a Swindle (aka-Research Racket, Phony Testing) (1939-11-09)
sortKey: 0|1939-11-09|00392|test stamps a swindle (aka-research racket, phony testing) (1939-11-09)
plotSynopsis: A bogus testing laboratory sells its approval while pressuring manufacturers and allowing unsafe products to carry reassuring test labels. After bad tires and appliances expose the danger, the Green Hornet pits the laboratory operators against a manufacturer they have blacklisted and arranges for police to find the checks and records proving the testing-and-blackmail racket.

Joe Desmond runs a fraud that takes money from immigrants by promising citizenship papers and instead saddling them with costly insurance, while corrupt associates provide alibis for his other crimes. When Andrew Melvin looks ready to crack, Desmond has him murdered and staged as a suicide; the Hornet later interrupts an attempt to plant Melvin's murder weapon on another accomplice, provoking the man into exposing Desmond and the racket.

title: The Smuggler Signs His Name (aka-The Smuggling Racket) (1939-11-25)
sortKey: 0|1939-11-25|00396|the smuggler signs his name (aka-the smuggling racket) (1939-11-25)
plotSynopsis: The Green Hornet uncovers a smuggling operation that hides behind diplomatic privilege to move illicit goods.

title: Waiters Union Racket (1939-12-21)
plotSynopsis: An honest waiter leading a revolt against corrupt union boss Catra is fatally struck down just as the membership begins to challenge the racket. The Sentinel keeps pressure on the union while the Green Hornet follows Catra's accomplices to the hidden union funds. Police recover the money and get testimony tying Catra and his partners to the theft and the reformer's death.

title: Finneys WPA Racket (1940-01-04)
plotSynopsis: WPA official Davidson extorts kickbacks from men desperate for relief jobs, while politician Finney discovers the scheme and demands a fifty-percent cut. When anonymous Sentinel informant Meekon is murdered to keep him quiet, the Hornet captures the killer Dutch and delivers him to police, where his confession exposes Davidson, Finney and the WPA racket.

title: Graft in the Courtroom (aka-Courtroom Racket) (1940-02-14)
plotSynopsis: Court official Cole decides to expose Robertson's racket of forcing state court employees to kick back part of their salaries, but Robertson intercepts him before he can reach the Sentinel. The Green Hornet tracks the conspirators to their hideout, prevents Robertson's men from murdering Cole, and leaves him alive to give reporters the facts that finally break the courtroom extortion scheme.

title: Advice for a Price (aka-Snavley, the Crooked Politician) (1940-02-21)
sortKey: 0|1940-02-21|00420|advice for a price (aka-snavley, the crooked politician) (1940-02-21)
plotSynopsis: The Green Hornet targets a fraudulent insurance-advice racket that charges victims for information they could obtain freely, while the gang claims to know the Hornet's secret identity.

title: The Tricky Tankers (aka-Robertson's Gas Racket) (1940-03-04)
plotSynopsis: The Green Hornet attacks Robertson’s gasoline racket after a train wreck is used to shift blame onto the masked vigilante.

title: Income from Immigrants (aka-Ligget's Citizenship Racket, Walter's Union Racket) (1940-03-06)
sortKey: 0|1940-03-06|00424|income from immigrants (aka-ligget's citizenship racket, walter's union racket) (1940-03-06)
plotSynopsis: The Green Hornet targets a racket that uses stand-ins to cheat citizenship exams, then blackmails vulnerable immigrants with the fraud the racket itself arranged.

title: Salesman in Short Pants (aka-Child Labor Racket) (1940-03-11)
plotSynopsis: The Green Hornet goes after Grafton’s child-labor scheme, which exploits children by putting them on the streets selling handkerchiefs.

title: Parole Plays the Wrong Policy (aka-Michael Parole Board Racket) (1940-03-13)
sortKey: 0|1940-03-13|00426|parole plays the wrong policy (aka-michael parole board racket) (1940-03-13)
plotSynopsis: A political fixer named Michael uses his influence over the parole board to release men for a racket controlled by businessman Leggett. When one of the paroled men becomes dangerous, he is murdered with a rifle; the Green Hornet plants the conspirators' own recorded conversation where police can hear it, making Michael and Leggett turn on each other and confess the parole racket and killing.

title: One Goes Out as Two Go in (aka-Property Tax Racket) (1940-03-18)
sortKey: 0|1940-03-18|00427|one goes out as two go in (aka-property tax racket) (1940-03-18)
plotSynopsis: The Green Hornet uncovers a property-tax-office check-kiting scheme after corrupt supervisors frame an innocent employee for their theft.

title: Murder in the Offing (aka-Trust Fund Racket) (1940-03-20)
plotSynopsis: A trust-fund scheme turns deadly when Palmer and his partner Michael murder Grayson and try to keep the stolen money and blame away from themselves. The Green Hornet plays the partners against each other, leaves Palmer's written statement where police will find it, and lets each man accuse the other until both admit their roles in the murder and robbery; the recovered money is returned to the insurance company that paid Grayson's claim.

title: Graft in the Hospital (aka-The Hospital Racket) (1940-03-25)
plotSynopsis: Political appointees Johnson and Leggett turn General Hospital purchasing into a kickback racket, taking money from supplier Robertson while Dr. Wakefield is threatened and pushed out for opposing them. The Green Hornet forces the conspirators together at Robertson's place and leaves police the supplier's double-entry ledger showing every hospital charge and payoff, giving investigators the hard evidence needed to smash the racket.

title: Accidents on Purpose (aka-Phoney Accident Racket) (1940-05-20)
plotSynopsis: A ring of professional claimants stages pedestrian accidents, throwing themselves in front of cars and using crooked legal help to collect damages from frightened motorists. The Sentinel's investigation draws retaliation, but the Green Hornet keeps pressure on the group until one member talks; police then move on the organizers and the false-injury racket collapses.

title: Sins of the Father's (aka-Carling Tells All, Tilson's Gift Racket) (1940-05-22)
sortKey: 0|1940-05-22|00444|sins of the father's (aka-carling tells all, tilson's gift racket) (1940-05-22)
plotSynopsis: A corrupt politician decides to confess and expose his associates when he realizes his own son is following the same criminal path.

title: A Copyright on Chiselling (aka-The Writer's Racket) (1940-05-27)
plotSynopsis: A so-called writers' bureau flatters amateur authors, charges them fees for 'polishing' manuscripts and guarantees publication only by printing tiny excerpts in its own magazine. After Axford is taken in, the Green Hornet submits a previously copyrighted story under another name, creating a trap in which the scammers' own publication violates the real author's copyright; the threatened lawsuit turns the law they exploited against them and forces restitution for victims.

title: Murder Seeks Its Victim (aka-Crandall and the Murder Ring) (1940-06-05)
sortKey: 0|1940-06-05|00448|murder seeks its victim (aka-crandall and the murder ring) (1940-06-05)
plotSynopsis: Crandall, a witness who can expose a murder ring, is being hidden by a rival newspaper while an imported gunman searches for him. The Green Hornet traces both sides to the hideout, disables the killers and leaves Crandall in a position where cooperating with police is his safest choice; Crandall then agrees to tell everything he knows about the racket.

title: Sales Make a Swindle (aka-Sales Tax Racket) (1940-06-12)
plotSynopsis: The Green Hornet pursues evidence that the state sales-tax commissioner has cooked the books and diverted a large sum from public funds.

title: Witness a Murder (aka-The WPA Graft Racket) (1940-06-17)
plotSynopsis: The Green Hornet takes on politician Finney and a graft scheme exploiting the W.P.A., using the murder case to expose the corruption behind the racket.

title: Insane and Able (1940-06-19)
plotSynopsis: The Daily Sentinel and the Green Hornet expose the head of a mental hospital who has turned the institution into a source of state-treasury graft.

title: Smoke Without Fire (1940-06-24)
plotSynopsis: Police chief Ritter boasts that organized gambling has been wiped out, but the Sentinel suspects he is protecting Frankie's reopened gambling operation. The Green Hornet engineers a smoke-and-fire alarm that brings firefighters and police into the joint before its equipment can be hidden, leaving the gambling evidence in place and exposing the protection racket Ritter had been covering.

title: Prescription Filled (1940-08-28)
plotSynopsis: Neighborhood druggist Ferris is threatened into joining Mr. Big's Big Four racket. The Green Hornet removes Ferris before the gang can act against him and uses the resulting search to expose a Big Four meeting place to police; several racketeers are captured, but Mr. Big's identity remains unresolved.

title: Needy Family Racket (1940-09-18)
plotSynopsis: When the Sentinel checks on families it helped the previous Christmas, Britt notices a disturbing pattern: several households are suddenly comfortable, and in every case the husband has gone to prison after confessing to a crime. The trail leads to ex-convict Spencer, whose men are secretly making weekly payments to the prisoners' families; the Green Hornet follows the payoff system and exposes the racket that has been buying men's willingness to take prison sentences for others.

title: Votes for Sale (1940-10-09)
plotSynopsis: The Green Hornet fights a vote-buying and election-fraud operation in an effort to keep a local election honest.

title: The Highway That Graft Built (1940-10-16)
plotSynopsis: A highway corruption scheme escalates to murder, leading the Green Hornet to expose the politician profiting from the graft.

title: Wrong Money Means Jail (aka-Smashing the Counterfeiting Ring) (1941-05-17)
sortKey: 0|1941-05-17|00504|wrong money means jail (aka-smashing the counterfeiting ring) (1941-05-17)
plotSynopsis: The Green Hornet breaks up a counterfeiting operation that uses young boys to circulate the gang’s bogus money.

title: Suicide for a Shake Up (aka-Murder at the Market) (1941-05-24)
sortKey: 0|1941-05-24|00505|suicide for a shake up (aka-murder at the market) (1941-05-24)
plotSynopsis: A protection gang extorts fruit and vegetable dealers, demanding regular payments and bombing businesses that refuse. Britt uses a legitimate insurance survey as cover to learn which merchants are being threatened, while the Green Hornet follows the collection chain back toward the racketeers; the gang's own weapons, payoffs and witnesses finally give police enough to smash the market-protection operation.

title: Man Wanted - for What (1941-06-21)
plotSynopsis: A disoriented man named Braley wanders near the Sentinel repeating fragments about a moon, a tree and a shooting, then disappears after being poisoned and removed from the hospital. Britt realizes Braley witnessed Hazelton's murder and is slowly recovering his memory; the Hornet tracks the killers, keeps Braley alive long enough to remember, and the recovered witness identifies Protowski as the murderer.

title: Walkout for Profit (Mr X 1 of 4) (1941-06-28)
plotSynopsis: The Green Hornet investigates a manufactured wildcat strike controlled by a hidden criminal organizer and works to rescue a reporter taken by the scheme’s operators.

title: Money for Mr X (Mr X 2 of 4) (aka-Murder for Mr X) (1941-07-05)
sortKey: 0|1941-07-05|00511|money for mr x (mr x 2 of 4) (aka-murder for mr x) (1941-07-05)
plotSynopsis: Cain and Bragg run a numbers racket under the shadow of the mysterious Mr. X, cheating bettors and collecting payoffs through a hollow-tree drop. When victim Mori steals the money, the Green Hornet forces him to return it, plants the cash to make Cain suspect Bragg of a double-cross, and lures the pair back to the drop; police capture Cain and Bragg and break their racket, while Mr. X slips away to continue the larger battle.

title: Murder Across the Boards (Mr X 3 of 4) (1941-07-12)
plotSynopsis: A murder and a plan to fix a major horse race draw the Green Hornet into a gambling syndicate’s operation.

title: Bid and Asked (1941-08-16)
plotSynopsis: The Green Hornet confronts a contractor who uses violence to manipulate city bidding and protects a woman willing to testify against him.

title: Paroles for Sale (1941-08-23)
plotSynopsis: The Green Hornet investigates and dismantles a racket that corrupts the parole system for profit.

title: Racket on the River (1941-09-06)
plotSynopsis: City officials boast that illegal gambling has been wiped out, but reopened games are secretly operating under a protection arrangement. The Green Hornet traces the protection scheme and engineers a raid before the operators can dump or hide their gambling equipment. Police catch the games in operation and obtain the evidence needed to expose the officials and gamblers behind the racket.

title: Hot Guns for Sale (1941-09-13)
plotSynopsis: The Green Hornet searches for the insider in the police department who is putting confiscated crime guns back on the street.

title: Reservoir for Murder (1942-02-07)
plotSynopsis: After a newly built reservoir fails, the Green Hornet investigates the collapse and uncovers a scheme intended to frame a senator.

title: Charity Takes It on the Chin (1942-02-28)
plotSynopsis: The Green Hornet exposes a crooked charity operation while clearing an innocent man who has been framed for embezzlement.

title: Invasion Plans for Victory (1942-05-23)
plotSynopsis: The Green Hornet deliberately takes blame for murder and robbery as part of a plan to keep vital Allied invasion information out of enemy hands.

title: A Slip of the Lip (1942-05-30)
plotSynopsis: After a sailor’s careless disclosure compromises wartime information, the Green Hornet races to stop saboteurs from destroying a convoy ship.

title: Murder Traps a Rat (1942-09-19)
plotSynopsis: A woman’s false murder confession leads the Green Hornet into an investigation of a larger counterfeiting operation.

title: Last Words Mean Sabotage (1942-09-26)
plotSynopsis: The Green Hornet uncovers a sabotage plot aimed at destroying a vital power dam.

title: Torpedo on Wheels (1942-11-21)
plotSynopsis: With his secret identity endangered, the Green Hornet must stop a plot aimed at destroying an important convoy of war materials.

title: Sabotage Finds a Name (1942-11-28)
plotSynopsis: A murdered man’s final clue puts the Green Hornet on the trail of saboteurs planning to destroy the wartime transport ship Mariana.

title: The Corpse That Wasn't There (1943-03-07)
plotSynopsis: A lost letter leads Britt Reid to a corpse that disappears before police arrive, sending the Green Hornet into a mystery built around the vanished body and a hidden criminal plot.

title: The Unseen Watchman (1943-05-30)
plotSynopsis: Enemy agents target radar expert George Wallace, first trying to bomb his home and then murdering a captured accomplice before he can talk. The Green Hornet infiltrates the spy ring and makes its leaders believe he will deliver Wallace for a $50,000 payoff, then turns the planned kidnapping and interrogation into a police trap that saves Wallace and leaves the agents in custody.

title: Sentinel of Death (1943-06-06)
plotSynopsis: A mysterious explosion at the Redding munitions plant is traced not to machinery but to specially treated newspaper copies that burst into flame after they dry. A newsboy has unknowingly been distributing the sabotaged editions, leading the Green Hornet back to the enemy laboratory that prepared them. He frees the boy and leaves the agents, chemicals and treated papers for police.

title: The White Ticket (1943-06-13)
plotSynopsis: A murdered chauffeur's white membership ticket gives Britt a path into a covert sabotage organization headed by Melchior. The Green Hornet reproduces the ticket, infiltrates the group and learns Melchior has been holding evidence over his agents to force their obedience; the resulting raid exposes the sabotage ring, solves the chauffeur's murder and frees a woman the gang had abducted to protect its secrets.

title: Rats of a Feather (1943-06-20)
plotSynopsis: A family is sickened after eating meat tied to a black-market operation, leading Britt toward dealers who profit from uninspected and illegally diverted supplies. The Green Hornet pressures the racketeers into betraying one another and guides police to a warehouse full of illicit meat, where the records and conspirators expose the scheme.

title: The Reward Claimers (1943-06-27)
plotSynopsis: Spy Nicky Barsetti, posing as engineer Marvin Redcliffe, murders a man and passes the body off as the Green Hornet so he can collect the Sentinel's $25,000 reward while stealing military blueprints for the Axis. The real Hornet turns up alive, exposes the fake death, recovers the plans and traps Barsetti and his accomplice in front of a police inspector.

title: Yankee Dollars (1943-07-04)
plotSynopsis: Reporter Lowry's chance encounter with a frightened young woman leads into a German espionage network operating in the city. The Green Hornet breaks up the cell, recovers its code material and more than fifty thousand dollars, then has the enemy money anonymously divided between the Red Cross and the USO.

title: Going Out of Business (1943-07-11)
plotSynopsis: A clandestine organization summons members to secret meetings by hiding coded numbers in store advertising, and Paul Coleman is killed after becoming entangled with the group. The Green Hornet traces the code to Booker's store, locates the hidden meeting room in its basement and tips the FBI, which raids the gathering and captures Booker and the organization he controlled.

title: Traitor's Reward (1943-07-18)
plotSynopsis: Reporter Ed Lowry uncovers evidence that influential J.D. Stanley is not merely corrupt but working with German agents. Stanley arranges for a submarine to attack an American destroyer and tries to suppress the evidence, but the Hornet breaks up the sabotage plan, delivers documents proving Stanley's treason, and leaves the conspirators to face the authorities.

title: Dead Men Talk (1943-07-25)
plotSynopsis: Enemy agents try to stop Judge Callow's grand-jury investigation by making his son Dan believe he has killed a man, then using the supposed murder to force the judge's resignation. The Green Hornet reconstructs the frame-up, compels one of the conspirators to reveal it and leaves evidence that frees Dan, keeps Callow on the investigation and brings the FBI down on the ring.

title: Backfire (1943-08-01)
plotSynopsis: A man calling himself Sleede and claiming to represent the Department of Justice persuades Britt Reid to stage a society party with the Bradley jewels as bait for the Green Hornet. Britt suspects a trap, has Kato follow Sleede and discovers the scheme is tied to a criminal and espionage ring; the Hornet turns the false setup back on its organizers, recovers the jewels and leads police and federal agents to Kessner's hideout.

title: Official Business (1943-08-08)
plotSynopsis: Enemy agents kidnap test pilot Stan Mercer after he flies a secret high-performance aircraft and try to force him to reveal its capabilities. Britt uses a deliberately provocative Sentinel story to flush the kidnappers into trying to silence reporter Lowry, follows their move as the Green Hornet, and reaches the hideout in time to free Mercer and turn the espionage gang over to federal authorities.

title: Long Distance (1943-08-15)
plotSynopsis: Photographer Clicker Binney returns from the South with pictures of small war-production plants, and the murder of a nightclub waiter points toward men tied to a sabotage plot. During a major storm, the Hornet and Clicker use a long-distance line to warn a Southern power plant that its emergency switch has been wired to explosives, preventing the blast and helping expose the conspirators.

title: The Murder Gas (1943-08-22)
plotSynopsis: After two associates of scientist Dr. Lockhart die in apparent suicides involving samples of his new gas, the Green Hornet learns enemy agents are trying to force the secret formula from the remaining scientists. He warns Lockhart, sets a trap at the doctor's house and turns the stolen gas against the conspirators, leaving police an enemy agent and the evidence behind the murders and espionage plot.

title: Gasoline and the Hornet (1943-08-29)
plotSynopsis: Sanders undercuts competing gasoline stations with altered double-compartment tank cars that conceal good fuel while other gasoline is sold through his chain, and his records point to tax fraud as well. The Green Hornet uncovers the tank-car trick and Sanders's attempted bribery, giving investigators the evidence needed to move against the operation.

title: Axford Rises to Shine (1943-09-05)
plotSynopsis: A drugstore is supplying illegal drugs to young people, and a fatal automobile crash convinces Michael Axford that the traffic must be stopped. The Green Hornet helps funnel the operation toward a police roundup while Axford pressures dealer Daniels into identifying the people behind the distribution ring.

title: The Knot (1943-09-12)
plotSynopsis: Rudolph pays Dr. Mead to fake the escape of disturbed patient Dexter so the man can be used as a scapegoat during the theft of confidential Allied shipping charts. When the Green Hornet discovers Dexter hidden at Rudolph's home, Rudolph and enemy agent Kurt try to shift the planned theft onto the Hornet instead. The scheme collapses, and police recover Dexter, the charts and evidence tying Rudolph, Mead and Kurt to the conspiracy.

title: Detour to Justice (1943-09-26)
plotSynopsis: German-born aircraft worker Pete Rader is framed for treason by his Nazi brother Carl, who exploits their family ties while working with a spy ring. Britt Reid arranges for the Green Hornet to stage Carl's escape from custody, follows him to his contacts, and forces the conspirators to produce evidence clearing Pete before police arrive.

title: The Green Hornet Goes Underground (1943-10-03)
plotSynopsis: A German saboteur is landed by submarine with orders to delay American aircraft production. His cell exploits a legal dispute over a war-housing project and plants explosives in a new water main serving an airplane factory; the Hornet penetrates the underground route, cuts the detonator wires, exposes the sabotage group and leaves their money to aid servicemen's families.

title: Fire Blitz (1943-11-21)
plotSynopsis: Escaped criminal Three-Fingers O'Malley helps a Nazi scientist hijack special paper, chemically treat it into artificial leaves and scatter them from a stolen plane so they ignite as they dry and start coordinated forest fires. Gail Manning traces the leaves to the spy's novelty shop, and the Green Hornet rescues her before the shop is burned with her inside, leaving the sabotage leader for police.

title: Diamond in the Rough (1943-11-28)
