show: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
plotSynopsis: The Vogons finally reach Nano, leaving Thor—newly offered a contract to become the planet's god—as the group's best hope of stopping the destruction.

title: First Show (1932-05-02)
plotSynopsis: In his first paid network appearance, Jack introduces himself as master of ceremonies alongside George Olsen's orchestra and Ethel Shutta. He jokes about his new radio job, needles the musicians and performers, introduces songs and specialty numbers, and works Canada Dry plugs into the comedy.

title: Review of 1932 (1933-01-01)
plotSynopsis: The New Year's program welcomes 1933 with Father Time, resolutions from Jack and the cast, and a comic review of personalities and events from 1932. The retrospective turns figures such as Amelia Earhart into exaggerated guest-style sketches rather than offering a serious year-in-review.

title: Bertha the Sewing Machine Girl (1933-01-22)
plotSynopsis: Jack opens with topical jokes and mock-news material before the orchestra takes over for a musical interlude. The second half shifts into a deliberately old-fashioned melodrama parody, with the cast playing exaggerated family and romantic scenes while repeatedly breaking the action for jokes about the dialogue, timing and performance. Music and sponsor material frame the comedy throughout.

title: Mary Does She Done Him Wrong (1933-03-31)
plotSynopsis: The cast spoofs She Done Him Wrong, with Mary in the Mae West-style lead and Jack as the mission worker opposite her. The familiar Bowery setup becomes a vehicle for flirtation, tough-guy jokes and cast interruptions before the show returns to its sponsor close.

title: Guest Edward G. Robinson (1933-04-21)
plotSynopsis: Jack mixes Chevrolet-contest promotion, movie-business boasting and musical numbers before welcoming Edward G. Robinson. Their exchange plays on Jack's inflated screen ambitions and Robinson's tough-guy image, and Jack closes by joking that he hopes the guest will buy the picture rights to the evening's comedy.

title: Sherlock Holmes and King Kong - Part 2 (1933-06-02)
plotSynopsis: Jack continues the Mr. X mystery as a Sherlock Holmes parody, with Watson and Mary helping him sift clues. King Kong becomes a suspect after being found with Mary, but the investigation takes another turn and the murder remains a comic puzzle.

title: Who Killed Mr. X (1933-06-09)
plotSynopsis: The show opens with a comic replay of a major boxing match and then returns to the running mystery of Mr. X's death. Jack, Mary and the detectives chase increasingly absurd clues, take the investigation into the air and end with the murder still unsolved for another installment.

title: Last Show of the Season - Mary's Birthday - All-star Party (1933-06-23)
sortKey: 0|1933-06-23|00048|last show of the season - mary's birthday - all-star party (1933-06-23)
plotSynopsis: For the season finale and Mary's birthday, the program turns into a crowded comic party. A stream of celebrity names and impersonation-style arrivals overwhelms Jack's preparations, after which the cast says goodbye for the summer.

title: Uncle Tom's Cabin (1933-12-10)
plotSynopsis: The cast mounts a broad period parody of Uncle Tom's Cabin, using Uncle Tom, Simon Legree and other melodrama figures as the basis for jokes and commercial interruptions. The recording contains racial stereotypes and exaggerated dialect typical of the era's burlesque treatment of the story.

title: Miniature Women (1934-02-11)
plotSynopsis: The cast presents its own two-act version of Little Women. Mary plays Jo while Jack takes the wealthy young man next door, and the familiar March-family situations, illness and courtship are turned into broad Benny-style jokes and romantic misunderstandings.

title: Don't Live Right (1934-02-18)
plotSynopsis: Jack opens with birthday banter and jokes about being told he does not live right, then moves through cast exchanges and listener-mail comedy. After the musical material, the program turns into a comic murder-mystery scene in which Jack and the others rush to a reported killing, encounter police, and are questioned among suspects over the victim, a knife and conflicting stories.

title: My Life as a Floorwalker in Omaha (1934-02-25)
sortKey: 0|1934-02-25|00047|my life as a floorwalker in omaha (1934-02-25)
plotSynopsis: Jack reenacts an episode from his supposed former life as a department-store floorwalker in Omaha. Customers, clerks and elevator-floor announcements become a string of jokes as he tries to prove that his store career ended through no fault of his own.

title: Duel in the Graveyard (1934-03-04)
plotSynopsis: Jack trades insults with the cast, reads a fan letter about becoming a master of ceremonies, and eventually faces a mock duel in a graveyard. The confrontation is played for farce as weapons are chosen, tombstones inspire jokes, and the supposed danger collapses into another gag.

title: Haunted House - Request Letter from John Dillinger (1934-03-11)
sortKey: 0|1934-03-11|00043|haunted house - request letter from john dillinger (1934-03-11)
plotSynopsis: After Jack and the cast trade insults about his on-air appearance, a test of courage pits him against Frank Black over a night in a haunted house. A coin toss sends Jack inside, with the others following to heighten the scares, before he ends by insisting he knew the frightening setup was a joke.

title: An Arizona Western - Play of the Golden West (1934-03-18)
sortKey: 0|1934-03-18|00042|an arizona western - play of the golden west (1934-03-18)
plotSynopsis: After jokes about Jack's sanity and the cast's various obsessions, the program turns to a comic Western set on Jack's Arizona ranch. Jack and the gang discover their cattle have been taken and play out an exaggerated frontier adventure full of mock toughness and deliberately absurd cowboy business.

title: Guest Alois Havrilla - the Eternal Triangle (1934-04-01)
plotSynopsis: On Easter Sunday Jack trades seasonal jokes with the cast and hears Mary's latest poem before guest Alois Havrilla joins the program. The featured blackout, 'The Eternal Triangle,' casts Havrilla as the husband, Mary as the wife and Jack as her lover, and the broadcast closes the Chevrolet series.

title: First Show of Season - Broadcast from Ebbett's Field, New York (1941-10-05)
sortKey: 0|1941-10-05|00026|first show of season - broadcast from ebbett's field, new york (1941-10-05)
plotSynopsis: For the season opener, Jack nervously rehearses before airtime and complains about the script before the reunited cast turns to the World Series. The broadcast moves to Ebbets Field, where Dodgers-Yankees arguments, hot-dog vendors and Jack's confusion around the game provide the main comedy.

title: Hollywood Bound (1941-10-12)
plotSynopsis: Still broadcasting from New York, Jack and the cast trade jokes about their theatergoing, hotel life and the end of their stay before turning toward the trip back to California. The impending return to Hollywood becomes another frame for jokes about Jack's vanity and economy.

title: On the Train to Los Angeles (1941-10-19)
plotSynopsis: The cast travels west by train after the New York broadcasts, filling the trip with compartment, dining-car and travel jokes. Jack looks ahead to California while Phil, Mary and Dennis needle him about accommodations, money and their return to Hollywood routines.

title: Dive Bomber (1941-10-26)
plotSynopsis: After banter about Phil Harris's night school and Jack's film career, the cast stages a parody of Dive Bomber. Jack insists on playing the doctor role, assigns the others parts, and turns the aviation-medical drama into a string of comic experiments, insults and production mishaps.

title: Halloween (1941-11-02)
plotSynopsis: The cast gathers at Jack's house in Halloween costumes before heading out for the night. After jokes about Dennis's costume, Phil's night school and household mishaps, Jack leads the gang into Halloween pranks and winds up tormenting an irritated neighbor from outside the house.

title: Football Game (1941-11-09)
plotSynopsis: Jack boasts about starting a new film with Carole Lombard and director Ernst Lubitsch while the cast punctures his movie-star ego. He then prepares the annual football sketch, only to be distracted when Phil brings in Brooklyn Dodgers manager Leo Durocher, extending the sports jokes beyond the staged gridiron.

title: He Fumbled the Ball (1941-11-16)
plotSynopsis: After joking about NBC's anniversary and the cast's radio careers, Jack mounts a football comedy as 'Flash Benny,' coach of Flatfoot College. He assigns the gang positions, boasts about his own high-school football past, and turns the gridiron setup into a broad parody of coaching and college athletics.

title: Thanksgiving Day Dinner (1941-11-23)
plotSynopsis: The cast gathers at Jack's home for Thanksgiving dinner, where his stinginess and household arrangements become the main joke. Mary, Phil, Alice and the others trade insults around the table as the supposedly festive meal turns into a typical Benny argument.

title: Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde Part One (1941-11-30)
sortKey: 0|1941-11-30|00017|dr jekyll and mr hyde part one (1941-11-30)
plotSynopsis: The cast's usual teasing gives way to the first half of a comic Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde adaptation. Jack's scientist experiments with a transformation formula, becomes an aggressive Hyde, and uses the change as an excuse for slapstick threats and running jokes aimed at the cast and Fred Allen.

title: Mr. Hyde and Mr. Jekyl - Part 2- Program Interrupted for News of Pearl Harbor (1941-12-07)
sortKey: 0|1941-12-07|00014|mr. hyde and mr. jekyl - part 2- program interrupted for news of pearl harbor (1941-12-07)
plotSynopsis: Jack returns to the Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde parody begun the previous week, with the cast ribbing his performance and repeating the transformation routine. The comedy is interrupted by live war bulletins reporting Japanese actions in Shanghai and developments following the attack on Honolulu.

title: Horseradish - a Ride in the Maxwell - Christmas Shopping (1941-12-14)
sortKey: 0|1941-12-14|00027|horseradish - a ride in the maxwell - christmas shopping (1941-12-14)
plotSynopsis: Opening with wartime news and Jack's appeal to buy defense bonds, the program shifts into Christmas-season comedy. Jack works through a gift list, argues over borrowed household items and Rochester, and goes shopping with his characteristic penny-pinching while the cast turns holiday errands into running gags.

title: The Christmas Tree (1941-12-21)
plotSynopsis: With Christmas approaching, Jack plans to leave the studio early so the gang can help with his tree. Holiday banter, a special-delivery interruption and jokes about gifts lead into the trip home and the cast's attempt to get Jack's Christmas preparations in order.

title: Jack Talks About His Christmas Party (AFRS) (1941-12-28)
plotSynopsis: The cast reviews Jack's stingy Christmas party, ridiculing his dinner of celery and supposed turkey while Jack tries to defend himself. Rochester then bargains for New Year's Eve time off, and the holiday comedy gives way near the close to a wartime patriotic bit invoking Allied leaders.

title: Jack Celebrates New Year's Eve at the Biltmore Bowl (1942-01-04)
sortKey: 0|1942-01-04|00003|jack celebrates new year's eve at the biltmore bowl (1942-01-04)
plotSynopsis: The program reenacts the cast's New Year's Eve, beginning with Jack getting dressed at home and quarreling with Rochester over missing cuff links. At the Biltmore Bowl, Jack fusses over paper hats, the waiter, Phil's orchestra and the bill before the night ends with his sleepy ride home.

title: From March Air Field (Inc) (1942-01-11)
plotSynopsis: Broadcast from March Field, the show is tailored to the servicemen in attendance. Jack jokes about aviation and the trip, Mary reads a poem for the soldiers, the cast trades military-themed gags, and Jack interviews an exceptionally large sergeant before the rushed close.

title: Carol Lombard Dies - All Music (1942-01-18)
plotSynopsis: Jack does not take part in the regular comedy following Carole Lombard's death. The broadcast is instead devoted largely to music, with Mahlon Merrick's orchestra, chorus, the Sportsmen Quartet and Dennis Day carrying a subdued replacement program before the usual closing commercial material.

title: The Frightwig Murder Case Part 1 (1942-01-25)
plotSynopsis: The program launches a comic murder mystery after socialite Homer J. Frightwig is found dead in his den. Jack reviews a houseful of suspects, questions the victim's wife and turns detective conventions into gags, but the case is deliberately left for continuation.

title: The Frightwig Murder Case Part 2 - Humphrey Bogart (1942-02-01)
sortKey: 0|1942-02-01|00009|the frightwig murder case part 2 - humphrey bogart (1942-02-01)
plotSynopsis: The Frightwig murder spoof resumes with Humphrey Bogart joining the cast and insisting on taking command of the investigation. Jack and Bogart argue over who will be captain while the suspects and clues are revisited in a deliberately hard-boiled, comic style.

title: Fred Allen Moves to Sunday Nights (1942-02-08)
plotSynopsis: Fred Allen's move to Sunday becomes the running target of the program. Jack feuds with his cast and sound man, Don stages an elaborate Jell-O commercial scene, and Jack ends by proposing a mock organization of Sunday performers devoted to fighting Allen's 'low comedy.'

title: Jack Goes to the Movies on Birthday (1942-02-15)
sortKey: 0|1942-02-15|00004|jack goes to the movies on birthday (1942-02-15)
plotSynopsis: On Jack's birthday, Rochester and the cast secretly organize a surprise party and struggle to keep him at home long enough for the guests to arrive. Jack keeps trying to leave for the movies, including a showing of Sergeant York, while everyone invents excuses to delay him.

title: From the Presidio in San Francisco (1942-02-22)
plotSynopsis: Broadcast from the Presidio in San Francisco, Jack spars with Mary over Fred Allen and with Phil over hotel expenses while playing to the soldiers in attendance. The location also becomes part of a deliberately strained Jell-O commercial built around repeated references to Sausalito.

title: Jack Is Mad About the Academy Awards (1942-03-01)
sortKey: 0|1942-03-01|00028|jack is mad about the academy awards (1942-03-01)
plotSynopsis: Jack spends the show sulking over the Academy Awards, insisting that politics rather than talent kept him from winning and comparing himself to Gary Cooper. The cast relentlessly mocks his wounded pride, even inventing a melodramatic suicide attempt with the Maxwell, while Jack keeps defending his screen career.

title: From San Diego Marine Base (1942-03-08)
plotSynopsis: From the Marine Corps base at San Diego, the cast jokes about the drive south, military life and Jack's makeshift tire experiment. Mary delivers a Marine-themed poem, and guest Joan Bennett joins Jack for film and romance jokes as the servicemen remain central to the broadcast.

title: How Fred Allen Became a Comedian - Jack Talks About Lending Fred $10 (1942-03-15)
sortKey: 0|1942-03-15|00029|how fred allen became a comedian - jack talks about lending fred $10 (1942-03-15)
plotSynopsis: Jack hears that members of his cast have been offered work on a rival beauty-clay program and treats everyone as a traitor until loyalties are sorted out. He then answers Fred Allen's version of show-business history with a mock biography of Jack Benny, racing through his childhood, violin lessons, wartime years and vaudeville career to continue their feud.

title: Jack and Phil Play Golf - Jack Plants a Victory Garden (1942-03-22)
sortKey: 0|1942-03-22|00015|jack and phil play golf - jack plants a victory garden (1942-03-22)
plotSynopsis: Springtime sends the cast outdoors: Phil brags about planting a Victory garden with tomatoes, beans and radishes, while Jack insists on another round of golf despite a disastrous earlier match. The gang reconstructs that outing and needles Jack about his game, clothes and refusal to pay off a bet.

title: The Minstrel Show with Doc Benny (1942-03-29)
plotSynopsis: The cast stages a period minstrel-show parody built around Doc Benny's troupe, combining songs, banjo material, stock comic exchanges and a closing Romeo and Juliet spoof. The recording includes racial caricature and stereotyped dialect associated with the historical minstrel format.

title: Don Won't Read Jack's Jell-O Commercial (1942-04-05)
plotSynopsis: Jack's Easter-program banter centers on his bargain suit and a suspenders mishap, while a quarrel sends Don Wilson out to sulk. Mary receives a special-delivery letter from home, and Jack previews his new 'Try and Get It' quiz while continuing the Fred Allen feud.

title: 'Try and Get It' Quiz Show (1942-04-12)
plotSynopsis: Broadcast from Camp Haan, the show mixes military-camp banter with Jack's new quiz format, in which contestants including Myrtle and Phil Harris answer increasingly expensive questions while Jack tries to keep his promised cash prizes under control.

title: Don Writes a Jell-O Play (1942-04-19)
plotSynopsis: The show opens shortly before airtime in the drugstore across from NBC, where Jack spars with Mary and the gang over food, money and show business. The talk shifts to Jack's new picture with Ann Sheridan and Dennis's wish to visit the set, then to chaotic travel plans for the following week's San Francisco broadcast.

title: Jack Hawkins Revenge (1942-04-26)
plotSynopsis: From the new NBC studios in San Francisco, the broadcast eventually presents 'Jack A. Hawkins' Revenge,' a Gold Rush comedy set in 1849. Jack plays hard-bitten gambling-house operator Jack A. Hawkins, whose threats, gunplay and schemes over newly discovered gold turn the frontier melodrama into slapstick.

title: Cast Visits Jack at Warner Brothers Studio (1942-05-03)
sortKey: 0|1942-05-03|00025|cast visits jack at warner brothers studio (1942-05-03)
plotSynopsis: The cast visits Jack at Warner Bros., where he boasts about his dressing-room arrangements and gives them a tour of the picture he is making. The studio visit leads to jokes with Ann Sheridan and other film personnel, including teasing over Jack's romantic behavior and his performance on the set.

title: Jack Thinks He's Going to Be Fired - Broadcast from Mather Field, San Francisco (1942-05-10)
sortKey: 0|1942-05-10|00001|jack thinks he's going to be fired - broadcast from mather field, san francisco (1942-05-10)
plotSynopsis: Broadcast from Mather Field, the show mixes Mother's Day and Army Air Corps jokes with Jack's mounting fear that a sponsor executive plans to fire him. Mary accompanies him to the meeting, where his melodramatic panic collides with the executive's much more favorable news.

title: Jack Imitates Fred Allen - Broadcast from the Santa Ana Air Base, California (1942-05-17)
sortKey: 0|1942-05-17|00021|jack imitates fred allen - broadcast from the santa ana air base, california (1942-05-17)
plotSynopsis: Broadcast from the Santa Ana Air Base, the program combines service-camp banter with jokes about Fred Allen and a mock lesson on bombardiers, bombsights and bombing procedure. The military setting drives the comedy while the cast plays to the personnel stationed there.

title: Jack Announces a New Sponsor - Phil Becomes a Father (1942-05-24)
sortKey: 0|1942-05-24|00008|jack announces a new sponsor - phil becomes a father (1942-05-24)
plotSynopsis: Broadcast from Camp Callan, Jack announces that next season the show will leave Jell-O for another General Foods product, Grape-Nuts Flakes, prompting jokes about how he can build a new opening catchphrase. Phil Harris also celebrates his newborn daughter and insists she is already destined to become a musician.

title: Last Show of Season - a Cavalcade of 8 Years with Jell-O (1942-05-31)
sortKey: 0|1942-05-31|00024|last show of season - a cavalcade of 8 years with jell-o (1942-05-31)
plotSynopsis: In the final Jell-O broadcast, Jack opens with wartime gasoline-conservation jokes and then looks back over eight years with the sponsor. The cast revisits earlier routines and characters, including a Shangri-La parody, before giving Jell-O a farewell and closing the season.

title: The Redhill Sisterhood
plotSynopsis: Loveday Brooke is called to Redhill after police suspect a small religious sisterhood of helping a gang rob country houses. Working from observation rather than appearances, she clears the sisters, follows clues involving the neighborhood's electrical system and a deliberately planted false trail, and helps trap landlord John Murray and the real burglary gang.

title: Mr Bovey's Unexpected Will
plotSynopsis: Florence Cusack becomes involved in an eccentric inheritance contest in which Henry Bovey's fortune in gold sovereigns is to go to the claimant whose body weight most nearly matches the treasure. When the gold is stolen and violence follows, she links rival Campbell Graham to a coining gang, discovers the melted sovereigns hidden in disguised form, and breaks the conspiracy behind the robbery and murder.

title: The Golden Slipper
plotSynopsis: Society detective Violet Strange is asked to stop a series of jewel thefts surrounding a circle of inseparable young women. A lost golden slipper, her own marked jewelry and careful observation let her expose the deception; the case then reveals Violet's private motive for detective work, earning money to support the gifted older sister her father disowned after she married against his wishes.

title: The Law and the Lady
plotSynopsis: Soon after marrying Eustace Woodville, Valeria learns that he used another name because his first wife died by poison and a Scottish jury returned the unresolved verdict 'not proven.' Refusing to accept the stain on him, she reconstructs the old case, questions witnesses including the eccentric Dexter, and finds a final letter showing that Sarah took her own life; Valeria and Eustace choose compassion over a public vindication that would destroy the dead woman's memory.

title: Too Many Crooks (1951-08-03)
plotSynopsis: Harry is summoned to Budapest by banker Fekity, who says his bank is about to be robbed. Harry discovers an elaborate tunnel scheme involving his old acquaintance Lulu, the Coralli gang and bank employee Fodor, but every participant plans to double-cross the others. Fekity himself intends to steal the bank's money and blame the robbers, while Lulu expects Harry to help her escape with the entire haul. Harry locks Lulu and the tunnel gang below the flower shop, then anonymously tips police to Fekity as he walks out of his own bank carrying the money. The police arrest Fekity and the gang, while Harry positions himself to collect the various rewards offered for stopping the robbery and capturing the wanted crooks.

title: See Naples and Live (1951-08-10)
plotSynopsis: In prewar Naples, Harry plans to steal a valuable emerald locket worn by wealthy Mrs. Donaldson and cuts his dangerous partner Rubio out of the deal. Harry engineers an introduction to Mrs. Donaldson and her hired companion Amy Collins, then becomes genuinely attracted to Amy while arranging to drug Mrs. Donaldson and remove the locket during a moonlit visit to Pompeii. Rubio interrupts and tries to take the jewel, but police arrive and arrest him, leaving Harry looking like the hero who saved Mrs. Donaldson. Amy has seen enough to understand Harry's real purpose and quietly ends their budding romance. Harry loses both the emerald and Amy, receiving only a modest reward for his apparent bravery.

title: Clay Pigeon (1951-08-17)
plotSynopsis: Harry returns to New York and becomes entangled with gangster Cato, who possesses incriminating photographs that can be used to blackmail Governor Hadley into granting valuable concessions. Harry appears to join Cato and demands half the deal, but at the governor's office Cato turns violent and Harry stops him during an attempt on Hadley's life. Harry keeps the damaging negatives long enough to make the governor worry that the blackmail has merely changed hands. Later, alone in a dark alley, he burns the photographs rather than exploit them, proving more honest than anyone expected.

title: Ticket to Tangier (1951-08-24)
plotSynopsis: A personal advertisement lures broke Harry from Paris to Tangier, where Patsy admits she placed the notice and paid his fare. Her late husband was involved in heroin smuggling and left a large shipment hidden in an empty villa; Patsy wants Harry's contacts to sell it. An armed former associate arrives for the drugs, but Harry disarms him as police close in. Patsy flees and is later arrested for her husband's murder, while Harry retrieves the hidden bundle. Refusing to traffic the actual narcotics, he dumps the heroin into the Bay of Tangier and sells seven packages of confectioners' sugar to the waiting gangsters for $50,000, keeping only the prayer rug that had wrapped the shipment.

title: Voodoo (1951-08-31)
plotSynopsis: Stranded in Haiti, Harry learns that the lost jeweled scepter of national hero Henri Christophe is still secretly guarded by local believers. He pressures his friends Fancy and Greek into revealing enough of the secret to sell the information to wealthy Sam Talkin, putting all of them in danger. A voodoo ceremony ends with Talkin dead and Fancy and Greek marked for sacrifice because the scepter has been betrayed. Harry interrupts the ritual, admits that he was the one who sold the secret, and frees his friends at gunpoint. He then pauses during their escape to steal the scepter himself and later sells it to a collector in Brussels.

title: Bohemian Star (1951-09-07)
plotSynopsis: Harry learns that jewel thieves are after the Bohemian Star, a huge diamond, and tries to get into the deal himself. The thieves kidnap and drug him, planning to keep him quiet until they can escape with the stone, but Harry turns the tables and takes possession of the diamond. When Scotland Yard officers reveal they have been hidden nearby listening, Harry immediately presents himself as the honest man who recovered the jewel for its rightful owner. He returns the Bohemian Star for a reward, later admitting that the visible tip of a policeman's shoe behind a curtain had a great deal to do with his sudden honesty.

title: Love Affair (1951-09-14)
plotSynopsis: Seeking an oil fortune in an oil-rich Saudi Arabian city, Harry meets nineteen-year-old American Marion and is quickly drawn into a romance while political and oil-concession intrigue swirls around him. When danger closes in, Harry helps Marion flee under false passports, traveling as husband and wife and treating the escape as his first marriage. Her large supply of cash makes the arrangement look even better to him. In Vienna, FBI agent George Harris catches them and reveals that Marion had shot and killed her wealthy husband at the hotel before attaching herself to Harry as a way out of the country. The serial numbers on the husband's recently cashed banknotes led authorities to her. Marion is taken back for trial, leaving Harry to admit that this time he was the one who had been used.

title: Rogue's Holiday (1951-09-21)
plotSynopsis: After a profitable swindle in New York, Harry sails for England and targets a wealthy woman he believes to be an aristocrat traveling with an extraordinarily valuable string of pearls. She eventually gives him the pearls as security for a $10,000 loan, and Harry leaves believing he has acquired a fortune. A London fence then tells him the pearls are imitations and the supposed noblewoman is Doris Jones, a confidence artist from Clapham. Harry's loss has one final twist: the $10,000 he gave her was counterfeit. When they meet again later, each recognizes the other's trick with no hard feelings.

title: Work of Art (1951-09-28)
plotSynopsis: In wartime Buenos Aires, Harry becomes interested in an art collection belonging to a woman connected with a wealthy Nazi munitions manufacturer and decides to steal a supposed Rubens. He slips back into her gallery after a dinner party and escapes with the painting, only to learn from a fence that it is merely a well-made copy worth about $100. Harry realizes he has been used in an insurance scheme: the fake was insured as an original, and his theft gives its owner a convincing loss while leaving him exposed as the burglar. A sympathetic contact buys the worthless copy and helps Harry leave the country. Harry later learns that the deception also helped preserve the woman's reputation while she secured a divorce and a new marriage.

title: Operation Music Box (1951-10-05)
plotSynopsis: In London, Harry meets a woman searching antique dealers for three music boxes purchased during a specific period. He learns that one of them contains a hidden fortune in jewels and steals her list so he can find it first. Harry tracks down the owners, breaking into a collector's flat and destroying music boxes as he searches, only to discover that the crucial third box has already been given away to charity. At an orphan institution he arrives just as officials dedicate a new wing. A child had accidentally dropped the donated box, exposing its secret compartment and jewels; the gems were sold to finance the building. Harry can only listen as the intact music box is played at the ceremony, his hoped-for fortune permanently beyond reach.

title: Golden Fleece (1951-10-12)
plotSynopsis: Harry takes a job as captain of Nadia's yacht by using forged master's papers, despite having almost no nautical experience. With a real sailor covering for him, he discovers the vessel is carrying explosives and an enormous secret shipment of gold to China, where Nadia's father, a powerful warlord, awaits it. After reaching China, thieves seize the yacht and Harry joins the pursuit. During the final fight Nadia and Harry escape as the explosive-laden ship and its fortune are lost at sea, reportedly taking half a billion dollars in gold with it. Harry later tries to sell an investor the location of the wreck as a salvage opportunity, only to discover his audience is the colony's chief of police and be ordered out of town.

title: Blue Bride (1951-10-19)
plotSynopsis: Operating from Bordeaux, Harry arranges a large counterfeit-currency deal while rival Baras closes in on him. To distract the opposition, Harry cultivates Baras's bride Sofia, while the endlessly helpful Professor Saint-Pierre keeps blundering into the scheme. Harry eventually flees with a suitcase full of bogus notes and is nearly stopped by police; Saint-Pierre's innocent testimony briefly convinces them Harry is only an eccentric scholar. Moments later an old man finds the spilled suitcase and displays the counterfeit money, sending Harry running from Bordeaux with the police siren behind him.

title: Every Frame Has a Silver Lining (1951-10-26)
plotSynopsis: Harry follows a seemingly respectable family because a valuable picture in a silver frame appears to offer a profitable opportunity, only to discover that Helen and her supposed relatives are part of an opium-smuggling ring. Harry and Helen temporarily join forces, tie up the others and wait for the money, with Helen proposing that they become permanent partners. When police arrive, Harry switches sides without hesitation, claiming he forced Helen to reveal the gang and directing the officers to the smugglers and their drugs. He collects the government reward and later insists that he opposed narcotics on principle, while admitting the size of the reward made honesty particularly attractive.

title: Mexican Hat Trick (1951-11-02)
plotSynopsis: A dying pickpocket's confession reveals that Vicente Coelio was wrongly accused of murder seventeen years earlier and that affidavits proving his innocence were hidden somewhere in León. Harry offers to recover the evidence for Coelio's family and travels there with Coelio's daughter Alicia, hoping to collect a large fee. He discovers that the ragged beggar shadowing them is actually Vicente, still alive and searching for the same papers. The strange change in a church bell's tone leads Harry to the affidavits hidden around its clapper. Alicia fights the beggar without realizing he is her father, and Harry later keeps Vicente's identity secret, returns the proof that clears him, and leaves León before his feelings for Alicia can keep him there.

title: Art Is Long and Lime Is Fleeting (1951-11-09)
sortKey: 0|1951-11-09|00015|art is long and lime is fleeting (1951-11-09)
plotSynopsis: Harry buys a worthless painting and plans to sell it to two wealthy Brazilian women as a valuable masterpiece. A suspicious rival keeps him under watch while Harry arranges a five-million-franc sale and risks having the picture examined by an art expert. When a thief grabs the canvas, Harry chases him and deliberately lets the picture burn in a street fire, apparently destroying the evidence. The expert later admits he knew it was a fake all along but chose to spare Harry public embarrassment, leaving Harry with the sale intact and a warning about trying the same trick again.

title: In Pursuit of a Ghost (1951-11-16)
plotSynopsis: In a Central American country on the edge of revolution, Harry is drawn into the hunt for a rebel leader who has escaped with about a million dollars. A beautiful woman later offers to help Harry steal the money from the fugitive in Havana and flee with it, but Harry recognizes the setup and warns the man instead, causing the woman to be arrested when she searches his hotel room. Harry then escorts the fugitive and the cash aboard his yacht, where government forces spring the real trap. The mild Englishman Harry met at the beginning reveals himself as the country's police captain and explains that he planted the clues Harry followed, using him to recover the citizens' money and draw the revolutionary leaders into the open. Harry is released with exactly the money he brought into the country, which is nothing.

title: Horse Play (1951-11-23)
plotSynopsis: Harry creates an elaborate fake betting club in Paris to swindle wealthy American Harris into wagering on a supposedly fixed horse race. The staged telephones, cashiers and track information convince Harris to put up $28,000, but the scheme goes wrong when Harry's partner Janine mistakenly buys a win ticket instead of the intended safer bet and the horse runs second. Harry then stages Janine's shooting with blanks and fake blood, terrifying Harris into fleeing France because he believes he is implicated in murder. Before Harry can enjoy the money, real police raid the bogus club and seize almost everything. He escapes prison but is left with only a tiny fraction of the planned score.

title: 3 Farthings for Your Thoughts (1951-11-30)
plotSynopsis: Harry joins Helen Barrett in a hunt for the £20,000 stolen by her imprisoned husband Bill. Bill has hidden the clue in three farthings and a letter referring to Beethoven; a maid and Bill's former partner Baxter are after the same money. After Bill is killed and Baxter corners Harry and Helen, Harry overpowers him and realizes the final clue points to Beethoven's 'Fury Over a Lost Farthing' among Bill's music records, where the money is hidden. The police arrive before Harry can profit, and his false pose as a bank-insurance investigator gets him deported instead.

title: The Third Woman (1951-12-07)
plotSynopsis: During the war, Corporal Harry Lime is dressed as a civilian colonel and sent by Allied intelligence to learn why agent Brunell is withholding the true location of a German underground rocket factory. In Istanbul, Harry discovers that the Germans are holding Brunell's younger sister Julie inside their embassy and using her to force false reports. Harry promises to free Julie in exchange for the real factory information. He enters an embassy reception, overpowers an armed guard, finds Julie and escapes with her through a window into firemen's rescue nets arranged in advance. Brunell provides the intelligence, although Harry later learns another agent had already supplied enough information for an air raid on the factory.

title: An Old Moorish Custom (1951-12-14)
plotSynopsis: In North Africa, Harry falls for De Rouge, granddaughter of wealthy Armand Deluge, while rumors of a Barbary-pirate treasure attract a gang led by Mario and the mysterious El Sikina. Harry and De Rouge are captured and forced to lead the gang to a coastal cave containing old chests and gold dust. The criminals celebrate with wine stored beside the treasure, only to collapse because Deluge had deliberately poisoned it for anyone who came looting in his absence. Harry saves De Rouge and escapes, but the romance ends with her goodbye rather than the fortune he imagined.

title: It's a Knockout (1951-12-21)
plotSynopsis: Harry and several confederates lure wealthy Stan Pierce into a supposedly fixed boxing match in Havana. After convincing Pierce that the result is certain, they take his $45,000 wager and stage a fighter's apparent death with blanks, fake blood and a bogus doctor, frightening Pierce into fleeing Cuba before he can demand his money back. The elaborate swindle works until Harry opens the money satchel and discovers that Jenny, the woman who helped hook Pierce, has disappeared with the proceeds. Her note leaves Harry to explain the loss to the rest of the gang, turning one of his neatest confidence games into a double cross on himself.

title: Two Is Company (1951-12-28)
plotSynopsis: In Sicily, Harry meets wealthy grocery heir Gus Schmidt, whose fiancée Emily Hickenlooper loves him but rejects the unromantic grocery life. Harry enlists notorious bandit Batzini in a staged kidnapping meant to let Gus rescue Emily dramatically, while Harry extracts ransom checks and runs up additional gambling debts from the participants. Harry separately manipulates Gus, Emily and Emily's father so each believes the other is in danger. The plan unravels when a real romantic rival, Alfredo, appears with a gun and Gus knocks him down. Emily chooses Gus, and Harry runs before the victims can stop him. He escapes with several large checks, only to admit they are worthless because he cannot safely stay long enough to cash them.

title: Cherchez La Gem (1952-01-04)
plotSynopsis: Harry becomes involved in a hunt for about $75,000 in hidden jewels in Honolulu, with a rival named Brissie willing to use a gun to get them first. Harry survives the pursuit and gets the jewels into a car, only to learn that Moana wants no part of the fortune because it came from her late stepfather and could bring scandal on her family. At a cliff she deliberately lets the car roll into the Pacific with the jewels still inside. Harry manages to grab only a half bottle of Scotch from the back seat and is left with a kiss instead of the money.

title: Hand of Glory (1952-01-11)
plotSynopsis: Trying to lie low in rural England, Harry accepts an invitation from Helen to stay with her twin uncles, retired scientists obsessed with discovering the secret of making gold. Their laboratory research turns out to include an occult recipe for a 'hand of glory' requiring material from a murdered stranger and a hanged man. Harry realizes the uncles intend to kill a wandering tramp and then murder Harry so the two bodies will supply what they need. The plan collapses before Harry can become their victim, leaving the uncles themselves dead in the laboratory. A newly discovered will leaves their fortune to Helen rather than their gold-making foundation, and Helen chooses to remain with her inheritance instead of leaving with penniless Harry.

title: Double Double Cross (1952-01-18)
plotSynopsis: Harry falls for Louise and agrees to work with her and Pierre as an airborne courier, parachuting packages between France and England for a thousand pounds a trip. On a later run, Pierre pushes Harry from the plane while Louise has anonymously tipped Scotland Yard that Harry will be landing with a large amount of illegal currency. Police are indeed waiting, but their search finds that every carefully sealed packet contains only brown paper. Louise and Pierre had also replaced the money in an effort to cheat Harry, so their two betrayals cancel each other out and leave him with nothing incriminating. Harry walks free and concludes that war is less dangerous than romance.

title: 5000 Pengoes and a Kiss (1952-01-25)
plotSynopsis: In postwar Hungary, singer Helena Bana hires Harry to get her across the closed border for 5,000 pengoes and a kiss. Rival fixer Zama betrays the scheme to the police, forcing Harry and Helena through barbed wire, patrols and gunfire. Harry finally holds a police inspector at gunpoint long enough for Helena to cross into Austria, while he stays behind and bargains away his automobile to buy his own escape. Helena later becomes a success abroad, but Harry remembers that even after collecting his promised kiss she dedicated a song to him about a rascal better off dead.

title: Dark Enchantress (1952-02-01)
plotSynopsis: In Algiers, Harry is drawn into a blackmail scheme involving the glamorous Magda Polarese and the mysterious Charles Bonquera. Detective Mike Nolan finally exposes the central trick: Magda and Charles are the same person, using a masculine disguise to blackmail women and her female persona to manipulate men. Harry helps turn the tables as the scheme collapses and Magda is taken into custody. A grateful Claremont gives Harry $5,000, which Harry surprisingly donates to the convent whose sisters had helped protect a young woman caught in the affair, while insisting Nolan keep the charitable gesture quiet to protect Harry's reputation.

title: Earl on Troubled Waters (1952-02-08)
plotSynopsis: Harry joins Robinson in a scheme to move a large sum of money across the Channel and winds up carrying £29,000 while a troublesome boy named Ronald keeps noticing more than Harry would like. Harry takes control of the cash and leaves Ronald guarding Robinson, hoping to slip ashore with the money. Instead, Ronald brings officials and proudly identifies both the smuggler and Harry as the man who stopped him. Harry instantly recasts himself as an anti-smuggling hero, turns over £5,000 as the recovered money and quietly keeps the other £24,000 hidden in his billfold. Ronald gets the praise while Harry gets the profit the boy never knew existed.

title: Dead Candidate (1952-02-15)
plotSynopsis: Harry tries honest business by taking the Bazzo soft-drink concession in the tiny Mediterranean republic of Malini, only to be pulled into a thoroughly dishonest election. Local political bosses treat him as a supposed Washington connection while opponents are eliminated, promises of democracy are staged for effect, and even the timing of a candidate's death becomes campaign strategy. Quarantined with Malinian measles, Harry watches much of the intrigue from the sidelines as Susie brings news. The whole scheme is finally swept aside when outside power Frieza intervenes and declares Malini liberated, putting Harry on an outbound plane and convincing him never to go straight again.

title: It's in the Bag (1952-02-22)
plotSynopsis: Aboard the Orient Express, Harry talks a Greek traveler into buying a bundle of Yugoslav banknotes at a steep discount, then secretly tips border police that the man is carrying counterfeit money. The scheme briefly lands Harry in jail as well, until officials verify the notes and apologize. Back on the train, a veiled woman and her accomplice steal the suitcase containing Harry's cash by nesting it inside a larger bag and throwing the larger case from the train in a tunnel. Their plan backfires when the bag knocks the waiting accomplice unconscious. Police recover the money and identify the pair as dangerous agents, but instead of returning Harry's cash they confiscate it and reward his supposed heroism with a medal.

title: Hyacinth Patrol (1952-02-29)
plotSynopsis: During a stop near the Panama Canal, Harry befriends American sergeant Tiger Dolan and becomes entangled in suspicions about an officer secretly meeting an enemy contact. With help from Rita, a local girl, Harry confirms that an espionage ring is using a hidden communications post to coordinate an attack intended to cripple the canal and its dam. The agents capture Harry and Dolan and prepare to kill them while signaling an offshore carrier and its bombers. Rita has already gone for help, however, and Dolan's Hyacinth Patrol arrives in time to storm the hideout. The spy network is rounded up, the attack is stopped and the enemy carrier is destroyed before the canal can be bombed.

title: Turnabout Is Foul Play (1952-03-07)
plotSynopsis: In Bern, Harry overhears German industrialist Hans Croft and a fixer discussing plans to obtain confidential Western European reconstruction information. Harry joins a counter-scheme involving official Bill Foster, who supplies convincing but false plans. Croft entrusts £30,000 to Harry during the deal, and Harry prepares matching envelopes so he can secretly keep the cash. Croft's daughter Frieda, who has fallen for Harry, learns the truth and insists the tainted money should go to a refugee organization. Harry switches the envelopes on her, but Frieda notices and switches them back. From his departing train Harry reads her note explaining that she loves him but cannot become the wife of another criminal, while the full £30,000 goes to the refugees.

title: Violets, Sweet Violets (1952-03-14)
plotSynopsis: In Marseille, Harry becomes involved with black-market operator Griffo and a warehouse packed with contraband, including weapons and aircraft parts. An elderly violet seller becomes an unwilling link in the transaction while occupation authorities close in on the network. Harry is arrested and accused of participating in the trade, but offers to clear himself by delivering Griffo and exposing the ring. After tracing Griffo to a boat and subduing him in a violent struggle, Harry turns him over to the authorities. The black-market organization is broken up and Harry is cleared of that charge, although the French prefect strongly suggests that he leave on the next boat.

title: Faith, Lime, and Charity (1952-03-21)
plotSynopsis: On a train to Agra, Harry meets a woman calling herself Mrs. Halley, who tells him that a mission orphanage has burned and wealthy Lady Edith might donate £5,000 to rebuild it. Harry decides to collect the money himself, but the supposed missionary is actually a confidence woman who intends to take the cash and kill him with the help of Mustafa. Harry escapes by exploiting her fear of snakes, only to be found by police with the money in his coat. Because his testimony finally gives them a case against the woman, Lady Edith believes Harry was her innocent agent and makes him publicly present the real mission with the £5,000, earning him a foundation stone naming Harry Lime as a philanthropist.

title: Pleasure Before Business (1952-03-28)
plotSynopsis: In Venice, Harry recruits experienced accomplice Joan Willoughby to help rob Count Delaverobia's valuable jewels. Joan gains the count's confidence and learns where the jewels are kept, but during the setup she falls in love with him. When Harry breaks into the palace and opens the safe, Joan stops him from taking the jewels and admits the scheme. The count forgives her and announces that they will marry, even inviting Harry to be best man. Harry leaves Venice before the wedding, but not entirely empty-handed: on his way out of the palace he steals a small Tintoretto painting worth more than £2,000.

title: Fool's Gold (1952-04-04)
plotSynopsis: Harry is recruited into a plan to hijack a valuable gold shipment in the Middle East and fly it to India for a huge black-market profit. He, Clancy and Singh pose as travelers and mechanics, divert the shipment onto a cart, load the heavy crates into their plane and escape with what Harry believes could bring nearly a million dollars. The operation begins to unravel when Professor Solomon and Filoura recognize what is happening and alert contacts ahead. Harry races the stolen cargo toward a buyer named Parenda, only to discover Parenda is already cooperating with police. Clancy and Singh are arrested and Harry's dream of a fortune collapses into a modest reward for supposedly helping recover the gold.

title: Man of Mystery (1952-04-11)
plotSynopsis: Billionaire Gregory Arkadin hires Harry to investigate Arkadin's own past, claiming that he remembers nothing before waking in Zurich in 1927 with a large sum of money. Harry traces him back to a Warsaw criminal gang and learns that Arkadin was once Arthur Boggs, one of the surviving members. As Harry locates former associates, they begin turning up dead, including two people strangled near Havana. Harry realizes Arkadin has been eliminating everyone who can expose his past. To protect himself, Harry tells Arkadin's daughter Raina what he has discovered. Faced with his daughter knowing the truth, Arkadin sets his private plane on automatic control and jumps from it to his death, leaving the aircraft to fly on empty.

title: The Painted Smile (1952-04-18)
plotSynopsis: On holiday in Sicily, Harry reunites with circus clown Antonio Vega, an old friend who secretly finances his daughter's education through emerald smuggling. Vega shows Harry the fortune he has saved for the girl and asks him to protect it if anything happens. His daughter unexpectedly arrives and learns the truth about her father while local public-safety officials close in on the smuggling operation. At the circus, Vega's jealous lover Lola deliberately switches cages during his animal act, sending a genuinely vicious cat at him instead of the trained one. Harry exposes the switch and Lola's motive, revealing that the danger was an attempted murder born from jealousy rather than an accident.

title: Harry Joins the Circus (1952-04-25)
plotSynopsis: A photograph convinces Harry that fugitive Nazi official Hans Hessel may still be alive under a new identity, and the search leads him into a traveling circus. A young performer has spent years hunting Hessel because his mobile gas chambers killed her father, while the clown Gico behaves increasingly suspiciously. Harry follows Gico into a remote mountain mine and discovers that the clown is Hessel. Harry becomes trapped underground, and the same young woman who vowed to kill Hessel crawls into danger to place dynamite that will free Harry. She then learns Gico is the man she has hunted, but her rescue effort gives him a chance to escape through the opened tunnel, leaving vengeance unresolved.

title: Suzie's Cue (1952-05-02)
plotSynopsis: In Vienna, Harry teams with the broke Countess Suzie and her associate Carl to steal a wealthy baron's valuable necklace. Suzie supplies the safe key, Carl distracts the baron at the front door, and Harry enters by the balcony and takes the jewels. Suzie then convinces Harry that Carl plans to double-cross them, so Harry confronts Carl at gunpoint and takes possession of the necklace. Police arrive moments later, arrest Carl and recover the jewels. The inspector reveals that Carl really is a respected aristocratic former officer and not the treacherous impostor Suzie described. Suzie admits she invented the story and tipped off police so Carl would be removed, leaving Harry free for her instead of receiving a share of the robbery.

title: Vive Le Chance (1952-05-09)
plotSynopsis: Harry joins a Paris confidence scheme aimed at wealthy American traveler Henry Weatherstone. A young woman poses as the impoverished heir to a family treasure, and Harry's accomplices provide a planted jewel case, a fake government clerk and a map supposedly revealing where the ancestral fortune was buried. Harry and Weatherstone each put up a million francs to buy the case, then follow the map to an empty chest. Harry later learns that Weatherstone was running his own counter-swindle with the woman and tries to recover the money at gunpoint. He gets Weatherstone's million francs back, only to discover afterward that the woman has picked his pocket and taken it from him in turn.

title: Elusive Vermeer (1952-05-16)
plotSynopsis: After an English country-house burglary, Harry learns that a valuable Vermeer is still missing even though police have recovered the rest of the stolen property. Hoping to sell the painting for about $150,000, he traces it through an unsuspecting family and buys the apparent old daub for £50 from a woman who has no idea what it is worth. Harry heads for his wealthy buyer with the picture under his arm, only to find Scotland Yard closing in from both directions. He instantly claims he was bringing the recovered Vermeer to the police. The story saves him from arrest, but his hoped-for fortune shrinks to the £500 insurance reward.

title: Murder on the Riviera (1952-05-23)
plotSynopsis: While smuggling American cigarettes along the Riviera, Harry encounters Danielle beside a car containing her dead husband and helps her dispose of the vehicle before taking her along. Danielle claims the dead man owed her fifteen million francs, but her shifting story leaves Harry unsure whether she murdered him for the money. As they prepare to flee by train, police arrive after tracing Harry's cigarette truck. Danielle panics, grabs a gun and shoots Harry in the shoulder before officers disarm her. Police say her final account is that she tried to hold her husband at gunpoint for money and killed him when he grabbed for the weapon. Harry survives but is arrested for cigarette smuggling and sent from the hospital toward jail.

title: Pearls of Bohemia (1952-05-30)
plotSynopsis: Harry takes a job promoting young American dancer Melody Johnson and discovers she is being followed because she possesses the stolen Pearls of Bohemia. An Italian operative trails her on behalf of their true owner, Count Paul of Bohemia, who wants the gems recovered quietly. On the voyage to Alexandria, Harry learns the Count keeps an imitation duplicate set for public appearances. He swaps the genuine pearls for the convincing copies, arranges for the real jewels to go back to the Count, and sells the duplicate set to the pursuing agent for 2,000 Egyptian pounds. Harry then helps Melody clear her gambling debts and enjoys the proceeds of a trick that lets the Count keep both his pride and his real pearls.

title: A Night in a Harem (1952-06-06)
plotSynopsis: Harry decides millionaire oilman Sam Cord is the perfect mark and gets drawn into a supposed oil concession in a tiny Red Sea kingdom. Princess Laila, a supposed geologist and competing interests make Harry believe he can earn ten percent of a $100 million deal, while palace intrigue sends him through disguises, threats and a six-hour wait in the royal harem. He finally learns he was being used to drive up the option price: the alleged oil expert was an actor and there was no oil. His grand commission disappears, leaving Harry to admit that this time the sucker was himself.

title: Blackmail Is a Nasty Word (1952-06-13)
plotSynopsis: Harry becomes vulnerable to a counterfeiting charge when young Heidi threatens to swear that she saw him pass bogus money unless he helps bring her father out from behind the Iron Curtain. With help from fixer Mama Regent, Harry works on the escape while stumbling into the secret of French politician Givolle. Givolle had collaborated with the Nazis under a false identity and later rebuilt a respectable political career; gangsters had already used that secret for protection. Harry unknowingly frightens him with what sounds like another blackmail threat, and Givolle eventually kills himself. Harry later meets Heidi safely reunited with her father and agrees never to use that particular nasty word again.

title: The Professor Regrets (1952-06-20)
plotSynopsis: An old acquaintance tells Harry that a respected professor preparing to leave for an important American post has been meeting secretly with a known Soviet agent. Harry tests the story by posing as the professor's replacement contact, copying the identification signals used during clandestine boat meetings. The professor accepts Harry as a Russian operative and incriminates himself, but Harry has no witnesses and his own reputation makes officials reluctant to believe him. He takes the evidence to the professor's longtime mentor, who has regarded the man almost as a son. Confronted with proof of the betrayal, the older man ultimately shoots the professor and prepares to answer to the police, leaving Harry to reflect on the cost of exposing the traitor.

title: The Hard Way (1952-06-27)
plotSynopsis: Trying to go straight, Harry accepts $1,000 to fly a wealthy man's troublesome young niece to a finishing school in Switzerland. The girl secretly turns the trip into a kidnapping scheme of her own, hoping Harry will demand a huge ransom from her uncle so she can take the money and marry her fiancé. Harry wants no part of the plan and lands at the remote farm of his old associate Mo while deciding what to do. Mo mistakes the situation for a real abduction and is horrified that Harry has broken his promise to stay legitimate. Harry returns the girl to her uncle, who is determined to get her safely to school. The episode ends with one final complication: during her stay at the farm she stole $60,000 of counterfeit money from Mo.

title: Paris Is Not the Same (1952-07-04)
plotSynopsis: Harry returns to Paris and rekindles feelings for the wife of a mild-mannered man while joining a scheme that dilutes expensive perfume and resells the doctored bottles to unsuspecting buyers. When the operation begins to unravel, the husband learns enough about Harry's criminal involvement and offers him 50,000 francs to leave Paris permanently and sign a confession that can be turned over to police if he returns. Harry accepts but decides that merely leaving will not end the woman's attachment to him. After an accident leaves another man dead with his face crushed beyond recognition, Harry plants his own identification on the body and lets Paris believe Harry Lime is dead. Much later the grateful husband tells the very-much-alive Harry that the apparent death finally ended his wife's grief and restored their marriage.

title: Honeymoon (1952-07-11)
plotSynopsis: In Sicily, Harry reconnects with ex-gangster Plucky Mariello and meets photographer Kathy, who is determined to make her career with pictures of notorious bandit Thomasino. Her cameras become dangerous evidence as criminals, police and Harry maneuver around one another. At a railway station, police set an ambush for Thomasino while Kathy positions herself for photographs of the killing. The bandit dies in the gunfire, but Harry ends up with the camera containing the valuable images. Instead of selling the pictures back or exploiting them, he throws the camera onto a passing train, destroying Kathy's scoop and spoiling one of the few decent acts he has ever committed.

title: The Blue Caribou (1952-07-18)
plotSynopsis: Near San Marino, Harry meets Jennifer, an American whose valuable blue caribou figurine has been stolen from her hotel. His search leads to an antique shop connected with Louis de Julio and managed by a man Harry recognizes as a former black-market operator. Harry discovers that valuable pieces from cheap lots entrusted to the shop have been quietly diverted and sold to an accomplice, and the missing blue caribou is among them. After a confrontation with the men involved, Jennifer recovers the figurine. Harry gets no profit from the case and instead spends his borrowed Swiss francs taking Jennifer skiing.

title: Greek Meets Greek (1952-07-25)
plotSynopsis: In Greece, Harry becomes involved with a woman whose shifting stories conceal a scheme to deliver crates of weapons to killers. After gunfire, false identities and an escape through back streets to a waiting ship, Harry and his companion complete the delivery and collect the final payment. She then reveals the real double cross: the machine guns may be genuine, but the ammunition she supplied does not fit them because she refuses to help the buyers kill anyone. Their accomplice Gregor does not survive the surrounding treachery, while Harry and the woman divide the blood money and briefly consider a partnership before discovering they are too much alike to trust each other.

title: The Lives of Harry Lime Audio Synopsis
sortKey: 0|9999-99-99|00016|the lives of harry lime audio synopsis
plotSynopsis: A short history of The Lives of Harry Lime explains that Harry Alan Towers produced the British series with Orson Welles reprising his Third Man role in stories set before the film. It describes the gunshot-and-zither opening, Harry's career as a con artist across 52 episodes, the BBC's purchase of only part of the run, and the later short-story collection based on scripts. It also notes that several radio plots supplied material Welles later expanded in Mr. Arkadin.

title: Orson Welles Audio Brief
plotSynopsis: A biographical overview of Orson Welles traces his rise from the Federal Theatre Project's all-Black Macbeth and The Cradle Will Rock through the founding of the Mercury Theatre, his radio work as The Shadow, the Mercury Theatre on the Air and the War of the Worlds broadcast. It continues through Citizen Kane, wartime and political work, later acting and independent-film struggles, major career honors, and his final projects before his death in 1985.

title: King of the County (1938-04-18)

title: The Price of Wool (1938-04-20)

title: Murder of Pony Express Rider (1938-04-22)

title: Toll Booth at Eagle Pass (1938-04-25)

title: Trap for a Gambler (1938-04-27)

title: Mine Claim Scheme (1938-05-02)

title: The Bart Colt Gang (1938-05-04)
plotSynopsis: A calculating outlaw plans to frame an honest sheriff and his brother while robbing two towns, leaving the Lone Ranger to unravel the double scheme.

title: Billy Garrett Kidnapped (1938-05-06)
plotSynopsis: A boy is taken for ransom by an outlaw gang, and the Lone Ranger must overcome both the kidnappers and an inept sheriff to bring him home.

title: Ammunition for the Indians (1938-05-09)
plotSynopsis: Traitors plot to sell army ammunition to Chief White Bear, and the Lone Ranger sets a trap to identify the men supplying the weapons.

title: Bob Mc Alister Framed for Murder (1938-05-11)
plotSynopsis: A young man faces execution for a murder and robbery he did not commit, sending the Lone Ranger after the evidence that can expose the real killer.

title: New-Fangled Justice (1938-05-13)
plotSynopsis: A smooth-talking schemer plans to marry for money and eliminate anyone in his way, but the Lone Ranger begins uncovering the design behind the apparent romance.

title: No Worse Enemy (1938-05-16)
plotSynopsis: A divided wagon train becomes vulnerable to an outlaw raid, and the Lone Ranger tries to reunite the travelers before their internal quarrel destroys them.
