title: Episode 9
show: The Lord of the Rings (BBC Radio)
plotSynopsis: Faramir’s men capture Frodo and Sam in Ithilien, and careful questioning reveals their connection to Boromir and eventually the truth of the Ring. Faramir refuses the temptation that overcame his brother, spares Gollum after the creature is caught at the forbidden pool, and allows the travelers to continue. In Gondor, Pippin offers his service to Denethor as the city prepares for the coming war.

title: Episode 5
show: The Lord of the Rings (BBC Radio)
plotSynopsis: After escaping Moria without Gandalf, the Fellowship reaches Lothlórien, where Galadriel tests their hearts, offers counsel and gifts, and resists the temptation to take the Ring herself. The company departs by river while Gollum shadows them. Boromir finally tries to seize the Ring from Frodo, prompting Frodo to decide he must continue alone until Sam discovers his plan and refuses to be left behind.

title: Episode 10
show: The Lord of the Rings (BBC Radio)
plotSynopsis: Faramir brings Denethor news of Frodo’s mission and is sent back toward the fighting as Gondor’s defenses weaken. Frodo, Sam and Gollum enter the secret pass above Minas Morgul, where Gollum leads them into Shelob’s lair. Shelob strikes Frodo down, Sam drives her off and takes the Ring believing Frodo dead, then learns from Orcs that Frodo is alive and follows them into the tower to rescue him.

title: Episode 6
show: The Lord of the Rings (BBC Radio)
plotSynopsis: Boromir dies defending Merry and Pippin from the Orcs, leaving Aragorn, Legolas and Gimli to pursue their captured companions across Rohan. Merry and Pippin escape into Fangorn and meet Treebeard, while Frodo and Sam force the pursuing Gollum to guide them toward Mordor. The three hunters enter Fangorn as well and are astonished to find Gandalf returned, now clothed in white.

title: Episode 3
show: The Lord of the Rings (BBC Radio)
plotSynopsis: Strider leads the hobbits out of Bree after the Black Riders strike at the inn, but the Nazgûl catch them on Weathertop and Frodo is wounded by a Morgul blade. As the poison works inward, Strider presses toward Rivendell and Glorfindel helps Frodo escape the pursuing Riders at the Ford. Frodo awakens safely in Elrond’s house, reunites with Bilbo, and the Council begins assembling the history and danger of the Ring.

title: Episode 7
show: The Lord of the Rings (BBC Radio)
plotSynopsis: The Ents decide to march against Isengard while Gandalf brings Aragorn, Legolas and Gimli to Edoras, where Théoden is freed from Wormtongue’s influence and rides to war. As Saruman’s forces pour into Rohan, Théoden’s people take refuge at Helm’s Deep and prepare for a massive assault. At the same time Frodo and Sam continue east with Gollum, conserving their dwindling food as the road to Mordor grows harsher.

title: Episode 2
show: The Lord of the Rings (BBC Radio)
plotSynopsis: After escaping Saruman’s imprisonment at Isengard with the help of the eagle Gwaihir, Gandalf races to recover lost time. Meanwhile Frodo, Sam, Pippin and eventually Merry leave the Shire, repeatedly sense or evade the Black Riders, and make their way to Bree. There Strider warns them of the danger, while Butterbur finally produces the urgent letter Gandalf had entrusted to him months earlier.

title: Episode 1
show: The Lord of the Rings (BBC Radio)
plotSynopsis: Bilbo’s eleventy-first birthday ends with his sudden disappearance and reluctant surrender of the ring to Frodo. Seventeen years later Gandalf returns with the truth: the ring is Sauron’s One Ring, Gollum has betrayed the names Baggins and Shire, and the Nazgûl are searching for it. Frodo resolves to leave the Shire while Gandalf rides south seeking counsel and aid.

title: Episode 13
show: The Lord of the Rings (BBC Radio)
plotSynopsis: With the war over, the Fellowship finally separates and the hobbits return north, only to find the Shire damaged and dominated by Saruman’s remaining influence. They help their own people reclaim and restore it, while Sam uses Galadriel’s gift to heal the land and begins a life with Rosie. Frodo, still wounded by what he endured, eventually departs from the Grey Havens with Bilbo, Gandalf and the Elven Ring-bearers, leaving Sam to return home.

title: Episode 11
show: The Lord of the Rings (BBC Radio)
plotSynopsis: Frodo and Sam escape the tower and begin the exhausting march across Mordor while war engulfs Gondor. At Minas Tirith, Denethor’s despair ends in his death, Théoden falls in battle, and the Witch-king is defeated as the Rohirrim and Aragorn’s arriving forces turn the Battle of the Pelennor Fields. Afterward Aragorn tends the wounded, and the captains decide to march on the Black Gate to draw Sauron’s attention away from the Ring-bearer.

title: Episode 8
show: The Lord of the Rings (BBC Radio)
plotSynopsis: After the victory at Helm’s Deep, Gandalf and Théoden confront Saruman at ruined Isengard and reject his attempts to persuade them. Pippin’s encounter with the palantír exposes him to Sauron, while Aragorn receives the Grey Company and a summons toward the Paths of the Dead. Far to the east, Frodo and Sam reach the Black Gate, abandon a direct entry into Mordor, and follow Gollum toward a more secret route.

title: Episode 12
show: The Lord of the Rings (BBC Radio)
plotSynopsis: Sam helps the nearly exhausted Frodo climb Mount Doom while the captains of the West confront Sauron’s forces at the Black Gate. At the Crack of Doom the Ring is finally destroyed, Sauron falls and Mordor collapses around the hobbits, who are rescued by the Eagles. Frodo and Sam awaken to victory, and the episode carries the story through Aragorn’s coronation, the renewal of Gondor and the farewells that begin the journey home.

title: Episode 4
show: The Lord of the Rings (BBC Radio)
plotSynopsis: Frodo freely accepts the task of carrying the Ring toward Mordor, and the Fellowship sets out from Rivendell. A brutal attempt to cross Caradhras fails, wolves attack in the night, and the company reluctantly enters Moria. Deep underground they discover Balin’s tomb and a record of the dwarves’ destruction just as drums sound in the deep and Orcs close on the chamber.

title: Birthday Cards (1946-09-03)
plotSynopsis: Mel tries to drum up business by mailing flattering birthday cards to dozens of townspeople. The scheme backfires when he discovers every card also promises a gift under separate cover, leaving him facing the cost of nearly a hundred presents and scrambling to undo his own publicity stunt.

title: Efficiency Expert (1946-09-10)
plotSynopsis: Betty persuades Mel to adopt an efficiency expert’s system at the fix-it shop, but the spotless new arrangement makes every needed part impossible to find. With a customer demanding her missing zipper, Mel restores the shop’s old disorder and immediately finds it, proving that his chaotic filing system was efficient in its own peculiar way.

title: The Cake Contest (1946-09-17)
plotSynopsis: Mel’s attempt to avoid embarrassment over baking a cake turns into a full-scale county-fair contest, complete with putty holding his entry together and Zookie trying to dispose of competing cakes. When the rival YWCA cake is destroyed, Zookie’s enthusiasm for Mel’s entry helps win him the domestic-science cup, exposing the secret he was trying to hide from Betty.

title: Mel Tries to Fix a Water Heater (1946-09-24)
sortKey: 0|1946-09-24|00037|mel tries to fix a water heater (1946-09-24)
plotSynopsis: Mel takes on repairs at the Colby house, but garbled telephone instructions send Uncle Rupert and Zookie into a demolition spree involving doors and windows. Mr. Colby is briefly delighted by one accidental improvement, only to learn that repairing the new damage may take six months.

title: Muscle Man Contest (1946-10-01)
plotSynopsis: Mr. Colby enters Mel in a strength contest against district manager Lionel Owens and secretly orders Mel to lose so Owens will remain confident in his job. Uncle Rupert and Zookie unknowingly rig the meter so Mel wins spectacularly, forcing Mel to reverse the trick and restore Owens’s confidence before Colby is promoted into the punishing job he was trying to avoid.

title: Sally and Marylou (1946-10-08)
plotSynopsis: Mel secretly agrees to repair Mr. Cushing’s fishing rod, Sally, and boat, Mary Lou, but overheard references to the two names convince Betty and Mr. Colby that he is seeing other women. A photograph and Cushing’s explanation finally reveal the innocent truth behind both ‘girls’ and rescue Mel from another romantic disaster.

title: Postmans Ball (1946-10-15)
plotSynopsis: Mel wants to take Betty to the Postman’s Ball, but Mr. Colby insists she help entertain a visiting sardine-company executive. Discovering the guest is a fellow Zebra, Mel helps Colby through a checker game that accidentally impresses the visitor enough to secure a valuable sardine order, winning Betty permission to go out even though Mel’s tickets are for the wrong Saturday.

title: Songwriter (1946-10-22)
plotSynopsis: Mr. Colby reveals a secret ambition to become a songwriter and asks Mel to use his supposed show-business connections to get a singer to hear his new tune. Mel manages to bring the performer in, only for her to recognize Colby’s ‘original’ song as music she already knows, collapsing both men’s artistic pretensions.

title: Community Chest Show (1946-10-29)
plotSynopsis: Mel organizes a Community Chest benefit at the local auditorium, combining musical entertainment with Zookie’s wildly confused pageant about Columbus. The amateur show nearly gets away from him, but the evening succeeds and raises support for the community campaign.

title: The New Radio (1946-11-05)
plotSynopsis: Mel insists on repairing Mr. Colby’s brand-new radio and promptly ruins it. He hides behind the set and impersonates broadcasts to conceal the damage until Colby catches him, but Mel’s deciding vote on Colby’s admission to the Zebra lodge gives him just enough leverage to survive the disaster.

title: Lodge Invitation (1946-11-12)
plotSynopsis: When Mr. Colby is initiated into Mel’s lodge, Mel dons a dress and wig to play flirtatious Lulu Belle while the other Zebras stage a jealous husband with a shotgun. The prank works until Colby discovers who is under the costume, turning Mel’s chance for revenge into another reason for his prospective father-in-law to chase him.

title: The Astrologer (1946-11-19)
plotSynopsis: When Mr. Colby prepares to sell his supermarket and move away, Mel discovers the buyer relies on an astrologer before making decisions. Zookie diverts the real mystic while Mel poses as a Maharaja with a crystal ball, sowing enough doubt to stop the deal and keep Betty in town even though Colby throws him out again.

title: Thanksgiving Party (1946-11-26)
plotSynopsis: Mel hosts a Thanksgiving party to improve relations with Mr. Colby, but the guests discover there is no turkey because Mel quietly gave it to an orphanage and serves salami instead. When an orphan arrives to thank him and exposes that Colby forgot his own annual turkey donation, Colby drops his anger and welcomes Mel to the table.

title: The Elopement (1946-12-03)
plotSynopsis: Mel wants to elope with Betty but loses his nerve after an earlier attempt sends Zookie into Mr. Colby’s hands. He visits a psychiatrist for courage, adopts an exaggerated tough-guy personality and marches back to the Colby house, where the doctor winds up treating the entire family instead of producing a wedding.

title: Christmas Present (1946-12-10)
plotSynopsis: Unable to match Willie Murdoch’s expensive Christmas gift for Betty, Mel disguises himself as an elderly woman to win a $40 bottle of perfume in Mr. Colby’s supermarket contest. The masquerade collapses on the air, but after Colby throws both Mel and Willie out, Betty understands how far Mel was willing to go to find her a present.

title: Christmas Shopping (1946-12-17)
plotSynopsis: Betty’s shifting Christmas wishes send Mel back to the department store again and again to exchange earrings, a compact, a bracelet and other gifts. When the store demands approval from several earlier customers, Mel tries to impersonate them all at once, only to be exposed just as Betty changes her mind yet again.

title: Mel Plays Santa Claus (1946-12-24)
plotSynopsis: Mel’s promise to play Santa for Mrs. Bradley’s young son makes Betty think he is secretly seeing another woman. He keeps the promise anyway, turning up in costume with presents, and the misunderstanding clears when Mr. Cushing and Mr. Colby join the Christmas party, leaving Mel and Betty reconciled after a generous holiday gesture.

title: Zebra of the Year (1946-12-31)
plotSynopsis: At the Zebra lodge’s New Year’s Eve meeting, Mel stages a comic pageant reviewing the events of 1946 before the members elect their Zebra of the Year. Every member initially votes for himself, but a stray ballot breaks the tie in Mr. Colby’s favor and makes him the lodge’s newly honored Zebra.

title: The Broken Caruso Record (1947-01-07)
plotSynopsis: Mel breaks Mr. Colby’s treasured Caruso and Galli-Curci records and tries to conceal the disaster by hiding with Professor Pachnik behind a curtain and impersonating the singers. The counterfeit concert is exposed, but banker Grimes finds the evening amusing enough to help replace the damaged records.

title: Foreign Relatives (1947-01-21)
plotSynopsis: When Mr. Colby needs a bank loan, Mel and Professor Pachnik stage an elaborate parade of invented foreign relatives in hopes of impressing banker Grimes. The deception collapses, but Grimes turns out to be an amateur actor who enjoys Mel’s performance enough to approve the loan, keeping Betty’s family from moving away.

title: Masquerade Ball (1947-01-28)
plotSynopsis: At the lodge masquerade, Mel tests Betty’s devotion by courting her in a succession of disguises, including a French count and a tough gangster. Betty sees through much of the act, but Professor Pachnik’s separate Russian disguise wins genuine attention from her, leaving Mel more jealous than reassured when the masks come off.

title: Bettys Suitors (1947-02-04)
plotSynopsis: Trying to make himself look like Betty’s best marriage prospect, Mel and Zookie parade a succession of ridiculous rival suitors before Mr. Colby. The scheme only reinforces Colby’s hostility, and he tells Betty she may marry any of the fake candidates except Mel, leaving the couple engaged in spirit if not with her father’s approval.

title: Mels Birthday (1947-02-11)
plotSynopsis: Facing bankruptcy and an auction of his fix-it shop on his birthday, Mel pretends to disappear so he can discover how much his friends really care. He returns in disguise to hear the auction, only to learn that everyone knew he was alive and the sale was part of an elaborate surprise birthday celebration.

title: The Missing Slice of Bread (1947-02-18)
plotSynopsis: When a loaf bought by Zookie is missing one slice, Mel becomes obsessed with finding a bread thief and even suspects Mr. Colby. After a blow to the head he dreams an elaborate Bugs Bunny courtroom trial, then learns the missing slice was part of a bread-company promotion rather than a crime.

title: Vaudeville Team (1947-02-25)
plotSynopsis: Mr. Colby’s chance to head the Zebra lodge entertainment committee depends on proving he can put on a show, but he refuses to perform cheap vaudeville. Mel fills the gap with celebrity impersonations and an old-fashioned comedy routine, winning over the visiting lodge official and securing Colby the post he wanted.

title: Councilman Colby (1947-03-04)
plotSynopsis: Mr. Colby’s hopes for a city-council seat are endangered when Mel accidentally reveals that he shot a pheasant out of season. Mel then discovers Mayor Quimby committed the same offense, giving everyone reason to forget the matter and allowing Colby to become a councilman, with Mel drafted as his unwanted assistant.

title: The Art Critic (1947-03-11)
plotSynopsis: Mr. Colby leaves Mel two paintings to clean and tells him he may sell the worthless one for extra money. Mel manages to sell the valuable painting to banker Grimes instead, then spends the rest of the day trying to recover it before Colby discovers the mistake.

title: Two Loves Has Mel (1947-03-18)
plotSynopsis: An accidental proposal leaves Mel engaged to both Betty and Cousin Dottie. He tries to make Dottie abandon him by portraying himself first as a dangerous criminal and then as a hopeless weakling, but every scheme increases her interest until her mother arrives and finally puts an end to the unwanted engagement.

title: Miss Ugga Ugga Boo (1947-03-25)
plotSynopsis: Jealous after misunderstanding Betty’s dealings with Hartley Benson, Mel urges the Zebra lodge to elect Cousin Dottie in its annual beauty contest. The vote ends in a tie, his South American delegate disguise fails to settle it, and a rerun judged by Hartley ends with Hartley outrageously crowning himself the winner.

title: April Fools (1947-04-01)
plotSynopsis: Mel’s April Fool prank convinces Mr. Colby he has inherited a fortune, prompting Colby to start giving away the supermarket’s stock. Mel disguises himself as an English lawyer to undo the damage, only for Colby to expose the trick and retaliate with a fake shooting before Mel receives a suspiciously well-timed call claiming he has actually won a car and cash.

title: Easter Egg Hunt (1947-04-08)
plotSynopsis: To impress Mr. Colby, Mel offers a $100 reward for the person who finds his advertising egg, then panics when the costly egg lands in Colby’s supermarket. He disguises himself as a farmer and finally stages a banana-armed egg robbery, but Colby drops the eggs in the commotion, ending the contest at the price of one ten-cent banana.

title: Society Party (1947-04-15)
plotSynopsis: Determined to prove he belongs at a society party, Mel disguises himself as a flamboyant Italian impresario and crashes the gathering with Professor Pachnik. His critique of Mrs. Grimes’s singing nearly ruins everything, but banker Grimes finds the impersonation hilarious and declares that Mel has rescued an otherwise boring evening.

title: Literary Discussion (1947-04-22)
plotSynopsis: Determined to prove he belongs in high society, Mel attends Mrs. Grimes’s literary discussion while Mr. Cushing hides outside with an encyclopedia and feeds him answers through the window. The ruse is exposed, and Mel happily retreats to a checker game with Mr. Colby, grateful to be back among people who expect less scholarship.

title: James Mason Movies (1947-04-29)
plotSynopsis: After a James Mason movie fires Mel’s theatrical ambitions, he tries to turn himself into a sophisticated actor and becomes entangled in plans for a play built around the famous star. When Mason cannot appear and Mel’s own writing and acting are judged hopeless, he gives up the stage and returns to the fix-it shop.

title: Oil Stock (1947-05-06)
plotSynopsis: Mel gets tangled in dubious Sunnyville Oil stock and tries to keep Mr. Colby from losing money with the same promotion. After a series of disguises and a staged report that oil has been discovered on the property, Mel makes Colby believe the shares are suddenly valuable enough to rush over and buy Mel’s stock back.

title: Supermarket Journal Editor (1947-05-13)
plotSynopsis: Before a Supermarket Journal interview, Mr. Colby assumes the editor will be impressed by foreign education, so Mel poses as an eccentric professor and invents a grand academic past for him. The editor actually admires self-made men and attended the same trade school as Colby, so Mel’s confession unexpectedly creates a bond and earns him a little goodwill with Betty’s father.

title: Trial Separation (1947-05-20)
plotSynopsis: Mel and Betty try a temporary separation so each can date other people, but neither likes the experiment. Mel eventually enters a get-acquainted club in a Spanish disguise and runs into Betty and Mr. Colby, who recognizes him but decides that compared with the club’s other Romeos he prefers an old-fashioned jerk like Mel after all.

title: The French Interior Decorator (1947-05-27)
plotSynopsis: After Zookie leaves Mr. Colby’s supermarket in a decorating disaster just as a buyer is considering the property, Mel disguises himself as French interior decorator Pierre Eclair and tries to sell the color scheme as high style. The act almost works until he gives himself away, sending Colby after him and Betty back to thoughts of eloping.

title: To Rent a Summer Cottage (1947-06-03)
plotSynopsis: When Hartley Benson beats Mel to a summer cottage Mr. Colby wants to rent, Mr. Cushing suggests that Mel exploit the owner’s love of sailors by posing as an old sea captain. The nautical disguise wins the cottage back for Colby until Hartley exposes the imposture, turning Mel’s success into another chase.

title: The Chinese Philosopher (1947-06-10)
plotSynopsis: Mr. Colby depends on a famous Chinese philosopher to appear at graduation exercises, but Zookie’s bungling at the station sends the real guest back out of town. Mel takes the philosopher’s place, improvising absurd proverbs and ceremonial wisdom long enough to save Colby’s program.

title: Show at the Market (1947-06-17)
plotSynopsis: Mr. Colby fires Mel as master of ceremonies for the supermarket show after deciding his jokes are terrible and gives the job to Hartley Benson. When Hartley drives the audience toward a rival store, Mel takes over, discovers the crowd loves his corny material and saves the evening along with Colby’s business.

title: The Missing Bread Slices (1947-06-24)
plotSynopsis: When a loaf bought by Zookie is missing one slice, Mel becomes obsessed with finding a bread thief and even suspects Mr. Colby. title: Romance of Rosey Ridge (1944-11-28)
show: The Mercury Theatre on the Air
plotSynopsis: After the Civil War, former Union soldier and schoolteacher Henry Bowen wanders into a community still divided by hatred between former Yankees and Confederates. When masked bushwhackers terrorize the area, Henry defends the family and kills two attackers. One is wearing gray beneath his disguise and the other blue, proving that cruelty belongs to neither former side alone. Lissie Ann's father finally accepts the lesson, and Henry and Lissie Ann decide to remain together at Rosy Ridge.

title: The Plot to Overthrow Christmas (1944-12-19)

plotSynopsis: The fiends of Hell decide that Christmas must be destroyed and draw lots to choose an assassin, sending Nero to the North Pole to kill Santa Claus. title: Secret Life of Walter (1944-12-26)
show: The Mercury Theatre on the Air
plotSynopsis: During an ordinary shopping trip, Walter Mitty repeatedly escapes his timid everyday life through elaborate heroic fantasies. Each fantasy is abruptly punctured by traffic, shop clerks or some other small embarrassment. title: Harold Peavy's Fast Cow (1945-01-09)

title: Heart of Darkness (1945-03-13)

Marlow removes the dying Kurtz from the interior, but Kurtz does not survive the return journey. Back in Europe, Marlow visits the woman who loved Kurtz and cannot bring himself to tell her what he witnessed, preserving her idealized memory rather than exposing the darkness he found.

title: Miss Dilly Says No (1945-03-20)

title: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (1945-03-27)

title: The Diamond as Big as the Ritz (1945-04-03)

title: Anything Can Happen (1945-04-24)

title: Mercury Summer Theater 1946-09-13 (15) King Lear (1946-09-13)

title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes - the Adventure of the Missing Submarine Plans (1939-11-06)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes

plotSynopsis: Government clerk Cadogan West is found dead on an Underground train roof with some, but not all, of Britain's secret submarine plans in his pocket. Holmes traces the missing papers to spy Hugo Oberstein's house beside the railway and lures Colonel Valentine Walter there with a coded advertisement. Walter admits stealing the plans; West followed him, confronted Oberstein, was killed, and was placed on the train to make him look guilty, while Holmes uses Walter to recover the remaining secrets.

title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes - the Case of the Retired Colourman (1940-03-11)

Amberley had trapped the pair in a sealed room and killed them out of jealousy, then concealed their bodies in an old well and fabricated the elopement and robbery. Exposed by Holmes and Lestrade, Amberley is taken away and ultimately ends his life in an asylum.

title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes-The Copper Beeches (1940-10-06)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
sortKey: 0|1940-10-06|00028|the adventures of sherlock holmes-the copper beeches (1940-10-06)
plotSynopsis: Governess Violet Hunter accepts a strangely lucrative post at Copper Beeches where she must cut her hair, wear a blue dress and sit where she can be seen from outside. Holmes realizes the Rucastles are using her to impersonate Mr. Rucastle's imprisoned daughter and deceive the young woman's suitor. Hunter helps uncover the locked West Wing, the daughter escapes, and Rucastle's own savage dog turns on him when the scheme collapses.

title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes-The Mystery of Mrs.Warrens Key (1941-12-07)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
sortKey: 0|1941-12-07|00046|the adventures of sherlock holmes-the mystery of mrs.warrens key (1941-12-07)
plotSynopsis: Mrs. Warren's secretive lodger and a chain of coded signals draw Holmes into the affairs of Italian fugitives hunted by the violent Red Circle. The supposed lodger is connected to Emilia and Gennaro Lucca, who have been hiding from gang leader Gorgiano after refusing his demands. Gennaro finally confronts and kills Gorgiano, and Holmes reconstructs the signals and mistaken identities that had concealed the couple's desperate attempt to escape the gang.

title: The Adventure of the Missing Bloodstains (1944-05-15)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: A political murder seems calculated to implicate a rival statesman, but Holmes is troubled by the absence of the blood that should have marked anyone who handled the stabbed victim. A washed towel and Holmes's chemical test expose an accomplice who tried to erase the missing stain. Professor Moriarty admits arranging the killing to destroy a threatened political coalition, then attempts to dispose of Holmes and Watson in an overheated steam room, but they escape his trap.

title: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes-The Adventure of the Superfluous Pearl (1944-05-22)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
sortKey: 0|1944-05-22|00021|the new adventures of sherlock holmes-the adventure of the superfluous pearl (1944-05-22)
plotSynopsis: A society gathering erupts when a valuable pearl necklace apparently loses its jewels and Holmes agrees to search the guests. The case turns on a numerical impossibility: when the necklace is restored it contains 106 pearls although the original strand held only 105. Holmes uses the extra, or superfluous, pearl to expose the deception behind the theft and return the genuine property to its rightful owner.

title: The Book of Tobit (1945-03-26)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: Holmes courts Diana Beckworth while investigating a murderer who sends warnings under the name Asmodeus. He stages a wedding, using Mycroft in disguise as the clergyman and a deliberately worthless handwritten will, to make Diana believe she has secured Holmes and his estate. Diana tries to stab him after the ceremony and is exposed as the killer; the marriage was never valid, and the supposed Reverend Wheeler is left to answer questions about his own part in the plot.

title: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes-The Amatuer Mendicant Society (1945-04-02)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
sortKey: 0|1945-04-02|00049|the new adventures of sherlock holmes-the amatuer mendicant society (1945-04-02)
plotSynopsis: Holmes and Watson infiltrate an exclusive society of beggars and discover that its leaders are anarchists exploiting mendicant disguises to move freely around London and prepare an attack during the coming Jubilee. Their cover blown, the detectives are bound beside a timed bomb while one conspirator, Lady Bradley, turns against the murder plan. Holmes has already arranged for police to surround the headquarters, cuts himself free with a concealed blade, and traps the society with evidence of attempted murder and conspiracy.

title: The Viennese Strangler (1945-04-09)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: A blackmailer is strangled in a Vienna lodging house, and a second victim, a Chinese actor, is killed after apparently witnessing the first crime. Holmes narrows the suspects by the strangler's long fingernails and by hairs left in a closet, then disguises himself as the dead actor to frighten the guilty woman into confessing. She had killed the blackmailer and removed the papers he held over her, then murdered the witness to protect herself.

title: The Notorious Canary Trainer (1945-04-23)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: A criminal named Wilson appears to confess to murder and then shoots himself from a pier, while his missing victim and a pair of dead canaries deepen the mystery. Holmes discovers Wilson had planned a fake suicide with blank cartridges so he could disappear after abandoning his old identity. His wife secretly replaced the blanks with live ammunition, killing him for real, and Holmes proves she loaded the gun by matching her fingerprints and secures her confession.

title: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes-The Unfortunate Tobacconist (1945-04-30)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
sortKey: 0|1945-04-30|00045|the new adventures of sherlock holmes-the unfortunate tobacconist (1945-04-30)
plotSynopsis: Three tobacconists are murdered in succession in the same East End waterfront shop, leading Holmes to suspect the premises rather than the victims. The latest proprietor stages a threatening note and a fake attack on himself, but Holmes catches the performance and finds a secret passage running from the shop toward the river. The shop is exposed as the headquarters of an espionage ring using foreign ships and waterfront access to move agents and information, and its proprietor is unmasked as the organizer.

title: The Purloined Ruby (1945-05-07)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: An actress is watched by a man whose family has spent generations seeking a legendary giant ruby, and Holmes becomes involved when her jewel disappears. The chase leads to a darkened theater where the recovered ruby is planted as bait and Holmes is fired upon from hiding. The attacker is Professor Moriarty, concealed under a theatrical identity; he has killed a man who discovered his secret and set the stage trap for Holmes, while the recovered stone proves valuable but is not the legendary treasure the lifelong seeker hoped to find.

title: In Flanders Field (1945-05-14)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: During a First World War entertainment behind the lines, Holmes investigates a disappearance and a shot fired with a German pistol. He proves that General Morley's own brother Maitland has been spying for the enemy and attempted to kill Holmes before crossing to the German lines. Holmes arranges for Maitland to carry identifying evidence that makes the Germans believe they have captured Sherlock Holmes, turning the traitor's escape against him while preserving the coming Allied operation.

title: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes-The Paradol Chamber (1945-05-21)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
sortKey: 0|1945-05-21|00025|the new adventures of sherlock holmes-the paradol chamber (1945-05-21)
plotSynopsis: A supposedly revolutionary scientific chamber and the murder of a woman lure Holmes and Watson into an airtight metal room. Professor Moriarty reveals that the invention and its victims were bait for Holmes and seals the detectives inside to die as their oxygen runs out. Holmes survives because he had ordered the Baker Street Irregulars to report if he failed to return; Mary Watson and the authorities reach the chamber in time, while Moriarty's murdered accomplice remains evidence of the trap.

title: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes-The Limping Ghost (1945-09-03)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
sortKey: 0|1945-09-03|00031|the new adventures of sherlock holmes-the limping ghost (1945-09-03)
plotSynopsis: A Scottish castle is haunted by a limping armored ghost just as an American claimant threatens the succession. After the American is murdered, Holmes proves the haunting was manufactured: the supposedly worn ancestral armor had merely been rearranged, while the killer used a modern suit to create the apparition. Nolan committed the murder to ensure his sister's fiance would inherit the title and estate, but Holmes baits him into repeating the ghost performance and springs the trap.

title: Colonel Warburton's Madness (1945-09-10)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: Colonel Warburton suffers violent, seemingly insane attacks whenever he hears a mysterious whistle, and dogs that react to the same sound are killed. Holmes demonstrates that a specially made ultrasonic whistle is triggering Warburton's hypersensitive hearing and that the dogs were destroyed because they could expose the trick. The culprit is Warburton's niece Ellen, who feared he would favor the young African woman Nada in his estate plans and tried to make him appear insane so a new will could be invalidated.

title: The Case of the Out of Date Murder (1945-09-17)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
sortKey: 0|1945-09-17|00002|the case of the out of date murder (1945-09-17)
plotSynopsis: Holmes visits museum curator Evan Whitlow after a body apparently dating from 1777 is found perfectly preserved in lime caves, but an anachronism in the dead man's supposed diary proves the corpse is modern. The victim is the long-missing George Clavering, whose disappearance had left his wife unable to move on with her life. Whitlow confesses that he killed George out of love for George's wife, then tried to pass the body off as an ancestor from the eighteenth century; jealousy deepened when he realized she loved George's brother Harry instead.

title: The Eyes of Mr. Leyton (1945-09-24)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: American businessman Wayne Layton and his English rival Cholmondeley both approach Holmes over control of a valuable San Pedro concession, each fearing the other will use violence. Layton is later found fatally stabbed after entering a Limehouse hideout, and his dying attempt to name his killer sounds like 'Mandalay.' Holmes tracks the opium-addicted Cholmondeley, tricks him into believing Layton survived, and obtains a confession that he stabbed his rival to secure the concession; the dying word was Holmes's clue to the unusual pronunciation of Cholmondeley's name.

title: The Problem of Thor Bridge (1945-10-01)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: Grace Dunbar is accused of murdering Maria Gibson after the dead woman is found at Thor Bridge clutching a note from Grace and Grace's revolver is discovered in her wardrobe. Holmes notices damage beneath the bridge parapet and recreates the crime with Watson's revolver tied to a heavy stone. Maria Gibson killed herself and rigged the gun to be pulled into the water after firing, then planted the matching revolver in Grace's room and arranged the note so that her husband's governess would be blamed.

title: The Vanishing Elephant (1945-10-08)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: A sacred white elephant disappears on the eve of an important festival, and Holmes discovers that the animal was secretly killed, cut into pieces and removed while an elephant call was sounded to preserve the illusion that it still lived. The reigning Maharaja is then murdered with poison placed in his eye drops and the elephant keeper is killed to prevent him from revealing the truth. Holmes confronts the Maharaja's brother, now the new ruler, as the man with the motive, medical knowledge and opportunity to commit both murders; beyond the reach of ordinary local law, he is ultimately threatened with the same legendary succession ritual he exploited.

title: The Great Gandolfo (1945-10-22)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: A magician's cabinet illusion depends on twin sisters secretly exchanging places, but one twin is found murdered after a performance and the other disappears. Holmes learns that the dead woman had been working as a spy for the Great Gandolfo and wanted to quit after realizing Holmes was investigating him. Gandolfo killed her because she could expose him; Holmes locates the surviving twin, reconstructs the cabinet trick and closes in on the magician while Mycroft independently identifies the suspended cabinet as the hiding place used in the espionage scheme.

title: Murder by Moonlight (1945-10-29)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: On a ship bound for Cavarati, Holmes and Watson secretly protect the returning Rani after the ship's doctor is killed and threats point toward an assassination plot. At a party the Rani is poisoned with arsenic even though her official taster samples everything first. Holmes realizes the taster has been fed increasing doses for a year until he became immune, allowing the same poisoned food to pass safely through him; the conspirator who prepared him also killed the doctor and admits the goal was to prevent a white Rani from ruling Cavarati. The assassin flees as the ship reaches Cavarati waters but is shot by the Rani.

title: The Fifth of November (1945-11-05)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: James Stewart tells Holmes that his cousin Falconbridge is plotting against him amid Guy Fawkes Day tunnels, gunpowder and disguises. Holmes discovers Stewart himself rented the neighboring house, planted the supposed conspiracy clues and tried to build a case that Falconbridge meant to kill him, so that Stewart could shoot his cousin and claim self-defense. The scheme collapses when Holmes substitutes an unloaded revolver and exposes the planted dagger; Stewart flees across the rooftops carrying a Guy Fawkes dummy and dies after the strain and excitement overwhelm him.

title: The Speckled Band (1945-11-12)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: Helen Stoner fears she will die as her sister did after hearing strange nighttime music in a bedroom with a dummy bell rope, a ventilator into Dr. Roylott's room and a bed fixed to the floor. Holmes and Watson keep watch and see a venomous snake crawl through the ventilator and down the rope toward the bed. Holmes strikes it with his cane, sending it back through the opening, where it bites Roylott instead; the 'speckled band' is revealed as the snake Roylott trained with a whistle to murder his stepdaughters.

title: The Case of the Double Zero (1945-11-19)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: At a Riviera casino, heavily losing gambler Roger Gilbert arranges a fake shooting to frighten his wife and dramatize his losses, using red ink to make himself appear dead. Casino director Chevrey discovers the deception, plants a roll of banknotes on Gilbert and then shoots him for real because he is in love with Gilbert's wealthy wife. Holmes exposes him when Chevrey claims an alibi for a murder whose time had never been established; the bullet holes through the planted money confirm that Chevrey handled Gilbert before firing the fatal shot.

title: The Case of the Accidental Murderess (1945-11-26)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: Watson initially fears Alice Markham may be repeating the suspicious history of her first marriage after a series of apparent accidents surrounds her second husband Jeffrey. Holmes reverses the suspicion and shows that Jeffrey Markham engineered the pattern himself: he had previously caused the death that enriched Alice, poisoned her first husband Dangerfield, and is now trying to kill Alice while making each attack look accidental. Markham also fires the second rifle shot that wounds Holmes while Alice is shooting at the same moment, and the accumulated evidence sends him to the gallows.

title: Murder in the Casbah (1945-12-03)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: Holmes travels to Algiers to find Douglas Milton, the long-missing heir to the Montrevor estate, and locates a man in the Casbah who claims the name. After violence surrounding his companion Aisha, Holmes gets the supposed heir to the British consulate and deliberately has him swear a legal statement to his identity. Holmes then reveals that he is an impostor and deserter: the real Milton was a painter with a trained eye for color, while this man cannot distinguish red from green. The Foreign Legion closes in as the false Milton tries to escape, ending a scheme built on impersonation, forgery and perjury.

title: A Scandal in Bohemia (1945-12-10)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: The King of Bohemia hires Holmes to recover a compromising photograph of himself with Irene Adler before it can threaten his forthcoming marriage. Disguised as a clergyman, Holmes stages a street disturbance and false fire alarm to make Irene reveal where she keeps the photograph. Irene recognizes him, however, follows him in disguise and leaves England with her new husband, Godfrey Norton. She takes the incriminating photograph with her but promises never to use it against the king, leaving Holmes a different portrait and the lasting memory of the woman who outwitted him.

title: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes-The Second Generation (1945-12-17)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
sortKey: 0|1945-12-17|00029|the new adventures of sherlock holmes-the second generation (1945-12-17)
plotSynopsis: In retirement, Holmes is approached by Miss Norton, Irene Adler's daughter, who persuades him and Watson to recover a filigree box from the home of a wealthy collector by claiming it contains compromising letters. During the burglary the collector's butler tries to exploit the situation, steal valuable jewels and kill Holmes and Watson while blaming the intruders. Holmes survives, discovers that Miss Norton used him as a cat's-paw and that the box concealed the stolen Kippenja emerald, and returns the gem. Out of regard for Irene Adler he spares the young woman, but arranges for the filigree box itself to be restored to its owner.

title: The Night Before Christmas (1945-12-24)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: On Christmas Eve, Lord Widdickham asks Holmes for help after receiving an extortion note threatening the valuable presents at his family celebration unless a large payment is made. Holmes recognizes the disguised handwriting as that of one of Professor Moriarty's trusted associates and realizes the thieves are using the holiday crowds and Santa Claus disguises to move unnoticed. The gang follows Watson and Mrs. Hudson and becomes entangled with Watson's sack of children's gifts, but Holmes traces the criminals to a nearby house, surrounds them with police and his street helpers, and recovers the stolen valuables. He then directs part of the reward toward the children caught up in the case.

title: The Strange Case of the Iron Box (1945-12-31)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
sortKey: 0|1945-12-31|00008|the strange case of the iron box (1945-12-31)
plotSynopsis: For generations the Dunbar family has waited to open an iron box of gold on the New Year's Eve before the heir's twenty-first birthday, a delay stretched to eighty-four years because Sir Walter Dunbar was born on February 29. Holmes suspects the box is too light and helps Sir Walter stage a disappearance so the younger Ian Dunbar can force it open. Inside is only an old Murdoch-family IOU proving that the lawyers' ancestor took the gold long ago. Holmes then finds a false bottom containing an unpublished manuscript by Sir Walter Scott, a treasure worth more than the missing sovereigns and enough to rescue the family's hopes.

title: The Strange Case of the Murder in Wax (1946-01-07)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
sortKey: 0|1946-01-07|00038|the strange case of the murder in wax (1946-01-07)
plotSynopsis: A serial killer is stabbing young women on Hampstead Heath, and Holmes notices that every victim except Rose Bishop had been with a man when attacked. The clue points toward someone close enough to Rose to know she would be alone. Holmes's investigation of a wax museum exposes proprietor LeBec, secretly Rose's father, as the murderer; in his warped pride as both wax artist and killer, LeBec even created a veiled wax figure of himself for the chamber of horrors. He tries to murder Holmes and Watson there with a knife, but Holmes sets the waxworks ablaze to force him into the open, and LeBec is captured.

title: Murder Beyond the Mountains (1946-01-14)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: During the years when the world believes him dead, Holmes travels as Sigerson to a Tibetan monastery where several foreigners seek permission from a Chinese envoy to continue to Lhasa. When the envoy is strangled after rejecting their requests, Russian cigarette ash seems to implicate Borodin, but Holmes notes that the killer used a left hand Borodin cannot use because his is artificial. The planted clue instead exposes the supposed American missionary as a German agent trying to reach Lhasa ahead of the Russians. She confesses and is handed to Chinese soldiers while Holmes resumes his secret travels.

title: The Tell Tale Pigeon Feathers (1946-01-21)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: Pigeon feathers in a boarding-house room lead Holmes to a carrier-pigeon espionage ring sending military information abroad. After decoding a report on troops at Aldershot, Holmes sends a false message to draw one agent to a music hall, but another member of the ring shoots the man and Watson is arrested while holding his revolver. Police surgeon Dr. Hendricks then fabricates powder burns to strengthen the case against Watson. Holmes shows that only the surgeon could have fired a blank into the corpse and removed the telltale wadding during the autopsy, then bluffs Hendricks into betraying himself with a reference to pigeon feathers.

title: The Strange Case of the Demon Barber (1946-01-28)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
sortKey: 0|1946-01-28|00044|the strange case of the demon barber (1946-01-28)
plotSynopsis: Actor-manager Mark Humphreys, starring as Sweeney Todd, fears he is committing crimes in a blackout after muddy boots and a bloodied razor keep appearing in his dressing room. Holmes proves the blood is animal, but arrives moments after Humphreys has been murdered with his throat cut; the even wound shows it was staged as suicide. Business manager Derek Lindsay had been planting the evidence to convince Humphreys he was mad and stood to inherit the theater if he died. Holmes makes Lindsay believe Humphreys has survived, then traps him when he attacks after the performance, his greed having made him wait rather than cancel a paying house.

title: The Guileless Gypsy (1946-02-11)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: While seeking information from a Romany camp, Holmes is drawn into threats against a wealthy family's young heir that appear to come from the gypsies. The wording of a kidnapping note betrays the fraud because a true Romany would not have used the term written in the threat. Holmes secretly places the boy with Jasper Hearn's people for protection, but Major Treadgold lays a dawn trap for Holmes at the Braxton Quagmire. Lydia, a gypsy violinist, reads the warning and goes in Holmes's coat and deerstalker instead; Treadgold shoots her, and with her dying words she identifies him. The tribe drives Treadgold into the quagmire, ending his scheme to frame and expel them, and Lydia leaves Holmes her violin.

title: The Camberwell Poisoning (1946-02-18)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: After Gerald Lovelace is found with his skull crushed and cyanide injected into his wrist, Holmes must choose among relatives whose alibis leave different possible times of death. The key is Gerald's meticulously wound watch: Holmes finds one turn missing, later establishes that each turn represents two hours, and fixes the murder at 11 p.m., when only the childlike Gilly had the opportunity. Gilly then innocently describes the exact method without having been told it, explaining that Gerald had planned to use the poison on his beloved old dog Gladstone. Gilly killed Gerald to protect the dog and is sent to private care rather than tried.

title: The Indiscretion of Mr. Edwards (1946-02-24)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: During a circus engagement, Watson poses as the wealthy Sir William Nigel while another distinguished visitor travels incognito as Mr. Edwards. When performer Giselle Gironde is strangled in her dressing room, Edwards and Watson are arrested because the door was watched and no one seems able to have entered. A threatening note from tightrope walker Yvette proves a false lead. Holmes realizes the open window and thin cord make entry unnecessary: jealous animal trainer Pierre stood outside beyond the unmarked snow, lured Giselle to lean out, snapped his long training whip around her neck and cut the lash after strangling her. The matching whip stock and severed lash clear Holmes's companions.

title: The Terrifying Cats (1946-02-25)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: In Rome, celebrated soprano Gina Valkazi secretly asks Holmes for help, then publicly denies sending for him. Soon the singer is found collapsed in a dressing room filled with cats and appears to have lost her voice, giving young understudy Lisa Bordoni a sudden triumph and making her a target for an angry crowd. Holmes learns Valkazi had an identical twin, Bella, who shared her appearance but not her voice. Bella had murdered the real singer, assumed her identity and staged the cat panic so the impostor's inability to sing would seem permanent. Holmes slips a cat into her room; her lack of fear proves the substitution, and he forces the impostor to confess from the balcony before the mob can attack Lisa.

title: The Submarine Caves (1946-03-04)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: On the Channel Island of Garth, Holmes uncovers a plan by domineering Mrs. Reeves and her German doctor, Uberbach, to remove the island's elderly ruler and steer the strategically placed island toward Germany as a submarine base. Reeves strands Holmes in tidal caves to keep him from proving that the old woman was poisoned, but Holmes has deliberately lied that the chemical test will become useless after twenty-four hours; while Reeves detains him, Watson performs the real test. Confronted by the new seigneur Christopher with proof of murder and treason, Reeves leaps from a balcony to her death, and Holmes orders that Uberbach be prevented from escaping. Garth remains British.

title: The Living Doll (1946-03-11)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: Cynthia Browning's lifelike doll, made with her own hair and nail clippings, is found stabbed through the heart, and Holmes learns that an old 'wise woman' has been hired to use black magic against the child. When the woman is found beaten to death, money around her seems to point toward suitors named King or Pound, but her final act is to clutch a sixpence. Remembering the slang term 'tanner' for that coin, Holmes exposes Hugh Tanner, who wanted Cynthia removed so Mrs. Browning would be free to marry him and then killed the ineffective accomplice to silence her. Tanner confesses before the police arrive.

title: The Adventure of the Blarney Stone (1946-03-18)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: After abrasive Jeffrey Hankin bets that he will kiss the Blarney Stone, partner Michael Corcoran lowers him headfirst over the castle wall and apparently loses his grip when Hankin's boots prove greased. Holmes rejects suspicion against the hotel boot cleaner and reconstructs the climb. Corcoran's love for Hankin's wife supplies the motive, while his failure to react naturally to the grease betrays the method: he smeared the boots only as he took hold of them, making the murder look like someone else's earlier sabotage. Holmes proposes checking for the absence of road dust in the grease; exposed, Corcoran leaps from the parapet to his death.

title: The Girl with the Gazelle (1946-03-25)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: Sir Henry Davenant fears Moriarty has replaced his priceless Girl with a Gazelle inside an impregnable time-locked strong room, and Holmes's own paint test seems to confirm that the picture is a modern copy. The impossible theft is the clue. Holmes discovers that trusted employee Jackson is linked to Moriarty and realizes the painting was never stolen at all. The supposed expert Delac, his disappearance and the bloodstains were staged to draw Holmes in, while Violet had prepared a small area of the genuine painting so Holmes's test would falsely condemn it as modern. Moriarty's aim was to make Davenant willingly hand the real painting to Violet for removal. Jackson escapes after locking the investigators in the strong room, but the original remains safe.

title: April Fools Day Adventure (1946-04-01)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: Soon after Holmes and Watson begin sharing Baker Street, Lady Anne and friends stage an April Fool trick by planting clues at her safe that appear to identify Holmes himself as an emerald thief. The joke turns real when the genuine stone vanishes from its secret hiding place and one participant, calling himself Murphy, produces only an excellent paste copy. Holmes realizes such a copy could not have been made since the previous night and discovers that Murphy separately told Stafford and Lady Anne that the prank was the other's idea. He had designed the joke in advance as cover for the real theft. Cornered, the criminal admits defeat and finally gives his true name: Moriarty, beginning the rivalry that will dominate Holmes's career.

title: The Disappearing Scientists (1946-04-08)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: On the eve of Holmes's retirement to Sussex, the three assistants of radium researcher Professor Buller disappear one after another, followed by Buller himself and the university's precious radium. Buller is found murdered and the three assistants soon return with convenient explanations, leaving Holmes apparently without a clue. The wound, however, proves the killer was right-handed. Holmes recalls Buller's joking description of assistant Jeffrey Barker as 'adroit' while Taylor and Gladys Hughes were 'gauche': literally, right and left. Only Barker could have made the fatal thrust. A telegram confirms the arrest and recovery of the radium.

title: The Headless Monk (1946-04-15)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: Holmes accompanies occult investigator Harley to a Cornish manor where an old chapel is said to be haunted by a headless monk and ghostly organ music. Harley concludes that someone is using the legend to conceal black-magic rites, and he is later stabbed inside the chapel while standing within a protective pentagram. A stableman insists no mortal entered, but admits seeing the headless ghost. Holmes realizes the disguise must have raised false shoulders above the wearer's hidden head, making the apparent height misleading. The culprit is Dorothy Brownlee, the owner's daughter, who created the haunting so she could practice black magic undisturbed and killed Harley when he threatened to expose her. She flees toward the organ loft and falls to her death.

title: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes-The Tankerville Club Scandal (1946-04-22)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
sortKey: 0|1946-04-22|00018|the new adventures of sherlock holmes-the tankerville club scandal (1946-04-22)
plotSynopsis: Captain Harry Prendergast is expelled from the Tankerville Club after marked cards are found in a poker game and an unopened deck appears in his pocket. Holmes recreates the game and exposes David Harkness, who used a bandaged finger to prick card values during play and framed Prendergast. Behind him is Alicia Wentworth's guardian, Colonel Sebastian Moran: Alicia's marriage would trigger an accounting of her trust, whose funds Moran has misused, so he arranged the scandal and a pistol duel intended to kill her suitor. Moran shoots Harkness when the accomplice threatens him, eliminating the witness. After Moran becomes involved in a new duel, Prendergast chooses boxing gloves and thrashes him. Holmes uses the financial secret to secure Moran's consent to the marriage.

title: The Waltz of Death (1946-04-29)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: In Vienna, a new waltz by the composer Horvat becomes linked to a series of murders of beautiful women. Herr Gruning had confessed to shooting Princess Stephanie, but officials dismissed him as an egomaniac and released him; he had in fact killed her. The later murders have a different culprit. Holmes realizes the killer must always be armed and that the music itself triggers him, pointing to police chief Count von Rofrano. Rofrano had loved Stephanie, and her death in his arms shattered his mind; whenever he hears the waltz he is driven to destroy other beauty. Holmes has the forbidden music played at a public gathering and watches Rofrano reach for his revolver. Exposed, the count turns the weapon on himself, while Gruning is returned to prison for Stephanie's murder.

title: The Man with the Twisted Lip (1946-05-06)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: Watson's search for a friend's missing husband leads him to an opium den, where Holmes is investigating the disappearance of Neville Sinclair. Witnesses saw Sinclair at an upstairs window before the disfigured beggar Hugh Boone was arrested, and clothing and blood make murder seem likely. Holmes finally realizes that Boone and Sinclair are the same man. Sinclair had once discovered that begging in disguise earned far more than respectable work and secretly maintained the double life to support his family. Caught changing identities, he tried to conceal the truth rather than face his wife and children. With no murder committed, Holmes secures his release on the condition that the beggar persona disappears forever.

title: The Haunting of Sherlock Holmes (1946-05-20)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: While recuperating in the Balkan kingdom of Grosneh, Holmes sees opera singer Lily Rayner arrested as a spy and apparently executed by firing squad. Her ghost then appears in his hotel room, prompting him to investigate secret passages and the evidence against her. The supposed espionage letters were in a language Lily could not speak and had been planted by her dresser Marta, who would inherit Lily's estate and lose that fortune if Lily married. Holmes recreates the ghostly visitation and tricks Marta into confessing. Lily then emerges alive: sympathetic officials had staged her execution with blank cartridges, and she used the haunting to draw Holmes into proving her innocence.

title: The Singular Affair of the Baconian Cipher (1946-05-27)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
sortKey: 0|1946-05-27|00041|the singular affair of the baconian cipher (1946-05-27)
plotSynopsis: A strangely typeset notice in the Times uses Francis Bacon's bilateral cipher to spell out a plea for help from the wealthy, paralyzed Mr. Quilter. Holmes, Watson and French detective Francois La Vier visit the estate, where a man claiming to be Quilter dismisses the message as bait for a Shakespeare authorship researcher. Fresh earth on the supposed invalid's boots proves he is an impostor. The conspirator is Quilter's relative David, who stands to inherit and has been terrorizing the old man with an accomplice. After impersonating Quilter, David drugs the real victim and hides him in his own wheelchair, assuming it is the last place anyone will look. Watson notices the breathing man, saving Quilter before the pair can murder him.

title: The Adventure of the Uneasy Chair (1946-05-31)
show: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
plotSynopsis: Harriet Ervin asks Holmes to clear her fiancé, secretary Robert Binion, after her father Sir Edward is found dead in a locked study while Binion sat outside. A constable later dies in the same chair while Binion is jailed, apparently proving his innocence. Holmes discovers that the antique chair is one of a pair and contains a concealed spring that can drive a needle into the sitter's brain; someone had switched the identifying cord so the lethal chair was delivered to Sir Edward. The apparent exoneration was the murderer's design. Holmes replaces the fatal chair with its harmless twin and sits in it before the suspects. Binion alone panics, exposing that he engineered the chair murders and the evidence trail so a clever investigation would clear him.

title: Audition Show (1946-07-10)
plotSynopsis: This July 1946 Fitch Bandwagon audition presents Phil Harris and Alice Faye in the prototype format that developed into their radio sitcom. The program combines songs, sponsor material and domestic comedy, with Harris's boastful show-business persona, Alice's reactions and a running sketch in which Phil's made-up story about a hospital patient forces Alice into an increasingly absurd telephone impersonation before the couple closes the broadcast together.

title: A Tutor for the Girls (1946-10-20)
plotSynopsis: Alice hires an English tutor to prepare the girls for school, and Phil's insecurity about the cultured newcomer leads him into a series of awkward attempts to impress him.

title: A Movie for Alice (1946-11-10)
plotSynopsis: Phil's grumpy morning at home turns toward a plan involving a movie for Alice, as family teasing about his looks and habits pushes him to prove himself.

title: Phil's Self-improvement (1946-12-01)
plotSynopsis: Phil launches an ambitious self-improvement program through adult classes, encyclopedia reading, and even basket weaving, but his struggle to complete a simple class assignment exposes how much improvement remains.

title: Emilys Musicalereturning from Lake Arrowhead (1946-12-08)
plotSynopsis: Returning from Lake Arrowhead, Phil reluctantly accompanies Alice to a fashionable musicale, where his discomfort with high society leads to a car mishap, social blunders, and an insult to famed pianist Jose Iturbi.

title: A Present for Phil Aka Fitch Stockholders (1946-12-15)
sortKey: 0|1946-12-15|00170|a present for phil aka fitch stockholders (1946-12-15)
plotSynopsis: The Fitch board decides even one-share stockholder Phil should receive a Christmas gift, eventually settling on an unwanted company memento that creates more trouble than gratitude.

title: New Years Resolution (1946-12-29)
plotSynopsis: Phil looks forward to the Rose Bowl on New Year's Day, but Alice reminds him that family obligations stand in the way and his holiday plans begin unraveling.

title: Phil's Enrolled at Usc (1947-01-05)
plotSynopsis: Phil enrolls in an adult extension course at USC and heads off for his first day equipped with school supplies, bubble gum, and far more confidence than academic preparation.

title: Will Benny Renew Phil's Contract (1947-03-09)
plotSynopsis: After the Jack Benny broadcast, Phil anxiously waits to learn whether Benny will renew his contract and barges into Jack's dressing room to press the issue.

title: Stockholder Phil (1947-10-12)
plotSynopsis: The Fitch company rewards Phil by making him a stockholder, but one skeptical director questions whether the crude bandleader belongs among the corporation's respectable owners.

title: Selling the House (1947-10-19)
plotSynopsis: Phil's reckless spending after misunderstanding the value of his Fitch stock leaves the family in such financial trouble that selling the house becomes a serious possibility.

title: A Day with Phil Harris (1947-10-26)
plotSynopsis: A flattering magazine profile convinces the Fitch company that Phil is a model citizen, so a representative sets out to observe a typical day and discover whether the wholesome image is true.

title: Phil's Band at High School (1947-11-02)
plotSynopsis: Phil proudly accepts a job playing a high-school dance because he believes teenagers idolize him, setting himself up for a rude lesson about how young the students actually think he is.

title: Phil Sees the Doctor (1947-11-23)
plotSynopsis: Alice arranges for a doctor and friends to scare overworked Phil with frightening-sounding diagnoses, but Phil mistakes a veterinarian call about the family dog for confirmation that he is dying.

title: Phil's Hobby (1947-11-30)
plotSynopsis: After a fall while retrieving the children's kite and a doctor's warning to slow down, Phil reluctantly searches for a hobby and rejects one pastime after another.

title: A Dog for the Kids (1947-12-07)
plotSynopsis: Phil tries to keep his unruly orchestra in line while family discussions about getting a dog for the children add another complication to his day.

title: Annual Christmas Show (1947-12-21)
plotSynopsis: Phil hires a substitute Santa for the children and gets Jack Benny in an unconvincing costume, but after the girls expose the fake, mysterious sleigh bells and a patch of snow suggest the real Santa may have visited after all.

title: The Kids Come to See Daddy at Work (1948-04-25)
sortKey: 0|1948-04-25|00111|the kids come to see daddy at work (1948-04-25)
plotSynopsis: Phil brings his daughters to an NBC rehearsal to show off his professional orchestra, only for the rowdy band and Frankie's romantic absence to undermine the polished image he promised.

title: First Show for Rexall (1948-10-03)
plotSynopsis: Back from Europe, Phil and Alice prepare for their first broadcast under new sponsor Rexall while Phil boasts about the new job and his prized English sports car.

title: Phil to Retrieve Contract from Frankie (1948-10-10)
plotSynopsis: Because Frankie signed his own name to Phil's sponsor contract, he claims control of the program and orchestra, forcing Phil to fight to recover his own show.

title: Phyllis Boyfriend (1948-10-17)
plotSynopsis: Phil laughs off five-year-old Phyllis having a boyfriend until his protective instincts take over and he decides to investigate the young suitor himself.

title: The Live Steer (1948-10-24)
plotSynopsis: A quarrel over the Harrises' extravagant spending leads Phil into a misguided economy scheme involving a live steer, creating a much larger household problem than the bills he hoped to solve.

title: Homework (1948-10-31)
plotSynopsis: The Harris children are kept after school because Phil helped them with disastrously wrong homework, forcing him to confront just how little he knows about history and current affairs.

title: A Job with Rexall for Willie (1948-11-07)
plotSynopsis: Phil and Alice try to find Willie a job with Rexall, but his eccentric behavior and Phil's own standing with the sponsor make the employment scheme anything but straightforward.

title: New Drug (1948-11-14)
plotSynopsis: A chemistry set in the Harris household and a conversation about Rexall lead Phil into another misguided attempt to involve himself with a supposed new drug.

title: Health Food Diet (1948-11-21)
plotSynopsis: Alice puts the entire family on a strict health-food diet after deciding she needs to lose weight, leaving Phil and the children miserable on raw vegetables, juice, and tonic.

title: Homework Helper (1948-11-28)
plotSynopsis: When the Harris girls are sent home from school for misbehavior, Phil gets drawn into their homework troubles and tries to prove he can be the helpful, knowledgeable father he claims to be.

title: Frankie Borrows the Kids (1948-12-05)
plotSynopsis: Frankie comes to the Harris house asking yet another favor and this time wants to borrow the children, immediately alarming Alice and everyone familiar with his history of bad ideas.

title: The Babysitter (1948-12-12)
plotSynopsis: Trying to make amends with Mr. Scott, Phil rashly promises to find a last-minute babysitter for the sponsor's baby and quickly discovers how difficult the favor is.

title: Hiring a Santa Claus (1948-12-19)
plotSynopsis: After promising the children they can meet Santa, Phil remembers his own disastrous attempt at the role and scrambles to hire someone else for Christmas Eve.

title: The Christmas Present (1948-12-26)
plotSynopsis: The day after Christmas, Phil and Alice encourage their daughters to share some of their new toys with less fortunate children, turning the holiday aftermath into a lesson in generosity.

title: Phil Is Drafted (1949-01-02)
plotSynopsis: Phil opens a misaddressed letter meant for another Phil Harris and is horrified to discover a military draft notice, launching him into panic before the identity mistake can be sorted out.

title: The Engagement Ring (1949-01-09)
plotSynopsis: Phil loses Willie's tiny engagement ring down the kitchen drain, floods the room trying to recover it, and discovers the ring only after Julius appears to have swallowed it.

title: Broken Hearted Phil (1949-01-16)
plotSynopsis: News that other bandleaders have been chosen for a presidential event leaves Phil feeling ignored and brokenhearted, despite the family's attempts to bring him back to reality.

title: Trumans Inaugural (1949-01-23)
plotSynopsis: Phil and Alice attend President Truman's inaugural festivities in Washington, where Phil's lack of decorum and Willie's unexpected access threaten to embarrass them at the formal celebration.

title: The Fire Chief (1949-01-30)
plotSynopsis: Back from Washington, Phil becomes involved when Willie heads to the mayor about choosing a new chief for the volunteer fire department, turning civic service into another Harris comedy.

title: Mr Scott Wants to Fire Band (1949-02-06)
plotSynopsis: Mr. Scott orders Phil to dismiss five musicians who cannot read music, including his best friend Frankie Remley, leaving Phil desperate to avoid firing the worst guitarist in the band.

title: An Admirer Sends Flowers to Alice (1949-02-13)
plotSynopsis: A stream of Valentine's flowers signed 'Guess Who?' makes Phil jealous enough to confront a stranger, before he learns the mysterious admirer is actually Phil himself through a standing order he forgot placing.

title: Jury Duty (1949-02-20)
plotSynopsis: Desperate to avoid jury service, Phil tries fake injuries, impersonation schemes, and every excuse he can invent while his family condemns him for shirking civic duty.

title: Remley Is Fired (1949-02-27)
plotSynopsis: After Frankie Remley wears out his welcome at the Harris home with gambling calls and freeloading, Phil and Alice try to force him back to work, only for the chaos to end with Phil getting arrested.

title: The Kangaroo (1949-03-06)
plotSynopsis: Alice demands that freeloading Frankie finally find work, and his newest ridiculous job prospect leads the household into a scheme involving a kangaroo.

title: Remley Is Re-hired (1949-03-13)
plotSynopsis: Phil and Alice persuade Mr. Scott to rehire Frankie, but Scott agrees only to put him to work washing dishes at the Rexall soda fountain rather than returning him to the band.

title: Alices Birthday (1949-03-20)
plotSynopsis: Already two days late buying Alice's birthday present, Phil sends Frankie to purchase a negligee on his account and gives his friend far too much freedom with the charge.

title: The Ski Trip (1949-03-27)
plotSynopsis: Phil, Alice, and their friends argue over competing vacation plans until a parking ticket sends Phil to City Hall and derails the supposedly relaxing trip before it even begins.

title: The Sponsors Daughter (1949-04-03)
plotSynopsis: Phil assumes an important visit from sponsor Mr. Scott means he is about to be fired, but the real problem centers on Scott's daughter and drags Phil into another unwanted family favor.

title: The Circus (1949-04-10)
plotSynopsis: Phil takes the family to the Clyde Beatty Circus with free tickets from Frankie, but his vanity and Frankie's questionable arrangements threaten to turn the outing into another fiasco.

title: Dinner for Teacher (1949-04-17)
plotSynopsis: Alice invites the children's school principal and her husband to Easter dinner, leaving Phil to endure an evening he expects to be painfully dull and overly proper.

title: Movie Role (1949-04-24)
plotSynopsis: Studio executives offer Phil a tiny movie part as bait to lure Alice back to films, but Phil treats the two-word role as the beginning of a major screen career.

title: Spring Housecleaning (1949-05-01)
plotSynopsis: Phil tries to prove useful during spring cleaning but injures himself almost immediately and turns a simple household chore into a string of accidents.

title: Mothers Day Present (1949-05-08)
plotSynopsis: Two days before Mother's Day, Phil realizes he has forgotten Alice's gift and goes shopping with too little money while she points out increasingly expensive possibilities.

title: Cadillac in the Swimming Pool (1949-05-15)
plotSynopsis: Phil accepts an invitation to the Scotts' lawn party, where his involvement with the family's Cadillac and garden arrangements leads to a spectacular mishap around the swimming pool.

title: Phil's Boat (1949-05-22)
plotSynopsis: Phil buys a bargain yacht sight unseen for the family's vacation, only to discover the Flying Mermaid is a decrepit wreck that turns his dream of becoming Commodore Harris into a sinking disaster.

title: The Picnic (1949-05-29)
plotSynopsis: After weeks of family pressure, Phil finally agrees to a picnic, only to face a dawn start, a band rehearsal, and a crowd of overenthusiastic companions before the outing even gets underway.

title: The Tonsillectomy (1949-06-05)
plotSynopsis: Phil prepares for a tonsillectomy with melodramatic fear, while Alice, the children, Willie, and Frankie make his anxiety worse with jokes about surgery and mortality.

title: The French Orphan (1949-06-12)
plotSynopsis: Phil and Alice answer a frantic call from Frankie and discover his foster-child arrangement has brought a young French orphan into his already chaotic life.

title: Frankies Foster Son (1949-06-19)
plotSynopsis: Frankie plans a hasty marriage so he can adopt a French orphan, but when the boy's relatives are found, Phil and Julius stage an obnoxious-son routine to scare off Frankie's prospective bride.

title: Concern About Contract Renewal (1949-06-26)
plotSynopsis: As the season ends, Phil becomes increasingly worried that Rexall may not renew the show after Alice reminds him how little the sponsor thinks of his band and comedy.

title: Phil Returns from Vacation (1949-09-18)
plotSynopsis: Phil finally returns from a fishing trip weeks later than promised, and the family retaliates by pretending they barely recognize the husband and father who stayed away so long.

title: Keeping Regular Office Hours (1949-09-25)
plotSynopsis: Phil is forced by his sponsor to keep regular nine-to-five office hours, a routine completely at odds with his late-night habits and lack of enthusiasm for ordinary business life.

title: Frankie Borrows Phil's New Chartreuse Car (1949-10-02)
plotSynopsis: Fed up with Frankie constantly borrowing his new Cadillac, Phil tricks him into choosing his own bargain used car, but the scheme ends with the wreck crashing through a storefront and Phil's Cadillac being sold to pay the damages.

title: Three Grey Hairs (1949-10-09)
plotSynopsis: Phil discovers three gray hairs and instantly decides that age has destroyed his looks and career, while Alice and the children mercilessly exaggerate his supposed decline.

title: A Fight in the Market (1949-10-16)
plotSynopsis: A newspaper sensationalizes Phil's scuffle at the Encino Market, and Phil struggles to explain the embarrassing fight to Alice and Remley.

title: Sponsors Formal Party Honoring Harrises (1949-10-23)
plotSynopsis: Phil grows suspicious when sponsor Mr. Scott throws a formal party in the Harrises' honor, convinced the unexpected kindness must conceal some bad news.

title: The Ukulele (1949-10-30)
plotSynopsis: A ukulele craze sweeps through Phil, Frankie, and their friends, with Phil reviving his claims of past musical greatness while Alice suffers through their terrible playing.

title: The Television Test (1949-11-06)
plotSynopsis: Rexall tests whether Phil can carry a television program by filming his radio rehearsal, but Phil treats the screen test like a costume spectacle and arrives dressed as a cowboy.

title: The Engineer (1949-11-13)
plotSynopsis: A doctor tells restless Phil he needs constructive manual work, so Phil declares himself an engineer and sets out to build something useful despite having no real idea what he is doing.

title: Talented Childrens Screen Test (1949-11-20)
plotSynopsis: A studio talent scout notices the Harris children in a school play, and Phil's pride in their supposed movie potential turns a simple screen test into another family show-business obsession.

title: Investment in Female Wrestler (1949-11-27)
plotSynopsis: After Alice criticizes Phil's bad gambling habits and urges him to invest wisely, Phil becomes interested in a very different opportunity: backing a female wrestler.

title: Sponsor to Hire Myrtle (1949-12-04)
plotSynopsis: The intimidating wrestler Myrtle McGursky takes over the Harris household, and Phil tries to find a way to move her out by turning her into someone else's problem.

title: Dishwasher and Garbage Disposal (1949-12-11)
plotSynopsis: Phil shops for an expensive Christmas present for Alice, but his efforts to improve the household eventually become tangled with plans for labor-saving kitchen appliances.

title: Getting a Christmas Tree in the Mountains (1949-12-18)
sortKey: 0|1949-12-18|00080|getting a christmas tree in the mountains (1949-12-18)
plotSynopsis: While decorating for Christmas, Phil discovers the neighborhood still needs a tree and becomes involved in an expedition to get one from the mountains.

title: Annual Christmas Show (1949-12-25)
plotSynopsis: Phil promises the children they can stay up to see Santa and once again plans to play the role himself, despite Alice's vivid memory of how badly his previous Santa performance went.

title: Concert Stage (1950-01-01)
plotSynopsis: A badly hungover Phil starts New Year's Day facing criticism from Alice and William, while his attempts to improve himself lead toward an ill-suited ambition for the concert stage.

title: Red Paint on Poodle (1950-01-08)
plotSynopsis: Phil agrees to care for sponsor Mr. Scott's valuable French poodle, but looking after Madame Bovary quickly turns into a disaster involving the dog's carefully groomed appearance.

title: Fixing the Furnace (1950-01-15)
plotSynopsis: After an all-night stag party, Phil and Frankie sneak home through the cellar to avoid Alice, only to become entangled in a household furnace problem while trying not to be caught.

title: Statue for Phil's Birthday (1950-01-22)

title: Little Alices First Date (1953-10-09)
