plotSynopsis: Phil cannot accept that fourteen-year-old Little Alice is old enough for her first date, so he drags her boyfriend Sniffy into the garage for an absurdly suspicious father-to-suitor interrogation.

title: The Barbells of Scotland (1953-10-16)
plotSynopsis: After Alice and Elliot tease Phil about his age and condition, he decides to prove his strength through exercise and becomes involved with an ill-conceived barbell routine.

title: How to Repair a Living Room (1953-10-23)
plotSynopsis: When a badly sloping floor reveals damage to the Harris home, Phil decides he and Elliot can repair the living room themselves rather than call a professional.

title: How to Repair a Living Roomwith Warmup (1953-10-23)
sortKey: 0|1953-10-23|00095|how to repair a living roomwith warmup (1953-10-23)
plotSynopsis: This warmup version opens with Phil's monologue and guest introductions before the Harris household discovers serious floor damage and Phil attempts a do-it-yourself living-room repair with Elliot.

title: The Romance of Alice and Phil (1953-10-30)
plotSynopsis: When the children ask how Phil and Alice first met, both parents tell wildly different, self-serving versions of their courtship and leave the girls to sort out the truth.

title: How Long Will the Genius of Phil Go Undiscovered (1953-11-06)
sortKey: 0|1953-11-06|00097|how long will the genius of phil go undiscovered (1953-11-06)
plotSynopsis: Phil fumes that RCA has never awarded him a gold record and becomes convinced his musical genius is being ignored while lesser stars receive all the recognition.

title: A Trip to the Moonplus Warmup (1953-11-13)
plotSynopsis: Following Phil's opening audience warmup, the main story finds him searching for a grand achievement that will improve his daughter's social standing, eventually turning his ambitions toward a trip to the moon.

title: A Trip to the Moon (1953-11-13)
plotSynopsis: When an exclusive finishing school rejects Little Alice because Phil is an actor, Elliot convinces him that a spectacular achievement could earn the family respect, inspiring Phil to dream of becoming a lunar explorer.

title: The Birthday Gift (1953-11-20)
plotSynopsis: Phil nearly forgets Little Alice's birthday and promises she can choose any gift she wants, just as Elliot tempts him with another wild investment involving a map to supposedly sunken uranium.

title: The Birthday Giftplus Post Show (1953-11-20)
plotSynopsis: Phil nearly forgets Little Alice's birthday and is drawn into Elliot's absurd hunt for sunken uranium; this recording also preserves additional post-show material after the main broadcast.

title: The Traffic Problem in Los Angelesplus Warmup (1953-11-27)
sortKey: 0|1953-11-27|00073|the traffic problem in los angelesplus warmup (1953-11-27)
plotSynopsis: This version begins with Phil's audience jokes and cast introductions before the story turns to dangerous traffic near the girls' school, prompting Phil to campaign for a needed traffic light.

title: The Traffic Problem in Los Angeles (1953-11-27)
plotSynopsis: After the girls are delayed by dangerous traffic near their school, Phil becomes determined to secure a traffic light for the busy Ventura Boulevard crossing.

title: A Night with Phil Harrisplus Warmup (1953-12-04)
plotSynopsis: After an opening warmup and cast introductions, Phil promises Alice he will stay home for the evening, then learns his old Dixieland musician friends are in town and schemes with Elliot to escape for one night.

title: A Night with Phil Harris (1953-12-04)
plotSynopsis: Phil promises Alice he will spend the evening at home, then discovers his old Dixieland bandmates are in town for one night and joins Elliot in a string of schemes to escape without breaking his promise openly.

title: Phil and Elliott Play Detective (1953-12-11)
plotSynopsis: While Christmas shopping on Hollywood Boulevard, Phil and Elliot stumble into a mystery and enthusiastically cast themselves as amateur detectives.

title: The Chaperones (1953-12-18)
plotSynopsis: Phil reluctantly agrees to chaperone Little Alice's masquerade date after Elliot's own predicament pulls him into the evening, and his protective instincts threaten to overwhelm the teenagers' plans.

title: The Chaperoneswith Warmup (1953-12-18)
plotSynopsis: This version includes the show's opening warmup and guest introductions before Phil becomes an anxious chaperone for Little Alice's masquerade date.

title: Hosting French Refugee Kids for Christmas (1953-12-25)
plotSynopsis: The Harris family welcomes two French refugee children for Christmas Eve, but the language barrier complicates Phil's well-intentioned effort to give them a warm holiday.

title: Phil Gives Up Smoking for the New Year (1954-01-01)
sortKey: 0|1954-01-01|00083|phil gives up smoking for the new year (1954-01-01)
plotSynopsis: On New Year's Day, Phil resolves to give up smoking while sorting through the clutter in his den, setting up a test of willpower for the newly reformed bandleader.

title: An English Dinner for a New Year (1954-01-08)
sortKey: 0|1954-01-08|00167|an english dinner for a new year (1954-01-08)
plotSynopsis: Phil's interest in British sports cars and Elliot's eccentric family stories lead into a New Year's dinner built around an exaggerated English theme.

title: Phil's Band Turns to Drama (1954-01-15)
plotSynopsis: With his orchestra broke and badly out of shape, Phil tries to reinvent the band with a more polished dramatic approach while battling the musicians' incompetence and money troubles.

title: Life Insurance for Phil (1954-01-22)
plotSynopsis: A search through the attic for Alice's insurance papers leads Phil and Elliot into a discussion of life insurance and Phil's characteristically exaggerated stories about his past.

title: Royalty Check Celebration (1954-01-29)
plotSynopsis: Phil receives an unexpectedly large royalty check from RCA Victor and immediately begins celebrating the windfall with Elliot before fully understanding why the extra money appeared.

title: Build It Yourself Television Set (1954-02-05)
plotSynopsis: Phil and Elliot try to save money by handling their own television setup, beginning with an overengineered rooftop aerial installation and turning a simple project into a hazardous do-it-yourself ordeal.

title: A Bad Case of Nerves (1954-02-12)
plotSynopsis: Already suffering from a bad case of nerves, Phil tries to rest at home but the children's loud television programs and household noise keep driving his condition from bad to worse.

title: Firing Elliott (1954-02-19)
plotSynopsis: Phil decides to fire Elliot to make room in the orchestra, but repeatedly loses his nerve until a hidden conversation provokes him, only for Elliot to reveal he has landed the band a better job and can replace Phil instead.

title: A Night at the Movies (1954-02-26)
plotSynopsis: Phil and Alice prepare for a simple night at the movies, but Elliot's bizarre film recommendations and interruptions turn the outing into another comic production before they even settle on a picture.

title: Job Hunting (1954-03-05)
plotSynopsis: Alice criticizes Phil and Elliot for wasting the morning on terrible music-making, prompting the pair to go job hunting and prove they can do something productive.

title: Expired Drivers License (1954-03-12)
plotSynopsis: Phil hides under the porch in terror of a state policeman, convinced he is in serious trouble before the real issue traces back to his expired driver's license.

title: Phil Writes His Life Story (1954-03-19)
plotSynopsis: Inspired by another celebrity autobiography, Phil rents an extravagant office and sets out to write his own life story with all the pretensions of a serious author.

title: Who Sent Flowers (1954-03-26)
plotSynopsis: After flowers arrive unexpectedly, Phil and Elliot try to discover who sent them and why, letting suspicion and jealousy transform an innocent delivery into a mystery.

title: What Would You Do If You Were a Dog (1954-04-02)
sortKey: 0|1954-04-02|00013|what would you do if you were a dog (1954-04-02)
plotSynopsis: Phil and Elliot attempt to train the family dog for show business, leading Phil into a fantasy about a pampered dog's life before Herman wrecks the house and Phil winds up banished to the doghouse.

title: Phil's Pain in the Side (1954-04-09)
plotSynopsis: A persistent pain in Phil's side sends him from a steam bath back home, where Alice's concern about his worsening symptoms pushes him toward medical attention.

title: This Band Is Underpaid (1954-04-16)
plotSynopsis: The orchestra complains bitterly about its miserable jobs and low wages, forcing Phil to confront the musicians' demand that the band deserves better pay.

title: Herberts Happy Hacienda (1954-04-23)
plotSynopsis: Phil talks Alice into considering another vacation and becomes fascinated by an enticing resort called Herbert's Happy Hacienda despite her memories of his previous travel disasters.

title: Special Red Cross Blood Drive Program (1954-04-30)
plotSynopsis: Phil's confidence in his own repair skills gives way to a special Red Cross blood-drive effort, with the show turning its comedy toward encouraging donations.

title: Phil's African Movies (1954-05-07)
plotSynopsis: Phil rents an office and decides to write and produce his own motion picture, launching into an increasingly elaborate story despite Elliot's warnings about the cost of filmmaking.

title: This Is Your Past (1954-05-14)
plotSynopsis: Alice confronts Phil over an absurd Saturday-night bill, and his attempts to explain himself lead into a comic look back at the questionable episodes of his past.

title: A Date for Herman (1954-05-21)
plotSynopsis: When the family's St. Bernard becomes lovesick, Phil and Elliot decide Herman needs a romantic companion and try to arrange a suitable canine date.

title: The Trouble with Honest Fred (1954-05-28)
plotSynopsis: Phil lands in court for assaulting his theatrical agent and recounts how his ambition to abandon music for an acting career led to the confrontation with 'Honest Fred.'

title: The Pink Bed Jacket (1954-06-11)
plotSynopsis: While preparing for a Father's Day fishing trip, Phil digs through old gear and memorabilia until a missing item and a pink bed jacket turn his nostalgic preparations into a domestic mystery.

title: Vacation Without Elliott (1954-06-18)
plotSynopsis: Alice insists that this year's vacation be taken without Elliot, forcing Phil to choose between a private trip with his wife and the friend who has intruded on nearly every important moment of their relationship.

title: Phil Harris - Alice Faye Audio Synopsis
plotSynopsis: A short Old Time Radio Researchers overview of The Phil Harris–Alice Faye Show explains how Harris's comic bandleader persona and his real-life marriage to Alice Faye became a fast-moving domestic sitcom. It describes the show's daughters, musical numbers and recurring characters including Frankie Remley, Julius Abruzzio and the sponsor's representative, and summarizes the series' reputation for sharp timing and enduring comedy.

title: Phil Harris Audio Bio
plotSynopsis: This biographical recording traces Phil Harris from his circus-family upbringing and early work as a drummer and orchestra leader through his success on Jack Benny's program, his marriage and radio comedy partnership with Alice Faye, hit recordings and later Disney voice roles. It also covers his later television appearances, golf interests, death in 1995 and the continuing reputation of the Harris–Faye radio series.

title: Alice Faye Audio Bio
plotSynopsis: This audio biography follows Alice Faye from her New York childhood and early chorus work through her rise as a major 20th Century Fox musical star, her celebrated singing career and her departure from the studio system after Fallen Angel. It then covers her marriage to Phil Harris, their long-running radio partnership, later screen appearances, death in 1998 and her continuing reputation as one of Hollywood's most popular musical performers.

title: Until Death Do Us Part
show: The Private Files of Rex Saunders
plotSynopsis: Rex reopens the unsolved murder of gambling boss Steve Farrow’s first wife when his new wife becomes the target of a nearly identical plot. A gun planted to frame Farrow and the death of an intermediary expose a chain of hired violence; Farrow’s longtime associate finally turns on him and admits the scheme, giving Rex the confession that links both wives’ attacks back to Farrow.

title: Shallow Graves
show: The Private Files of Rex Saunders
plotSynopsis: Rex investigates the disappearance of Eddie Goodrich, a young man deep in gambling debt and tangled with blackmailers. Eddie’s body turns up hidden in an apartment, and the trail ultimately points back to his uncle, whose own shady dealings had given Eddie leverage over him; the uncle tried to use Rex as an alibi while other opportunists exploited the disappearance for fast cash.

title: The Human Game
show: The Private Files of Rex Saunders
plotSynopsis: An armed stranger on a transcontinental train launches Rex into a murder involving a trucking company and feuding partners. The apparent case against Nick Gillman is manufactured: George Stone and his accomplices killed the other partner and framed Nick to seize control of the business. Rex survives their attempts to eliminate him and records enough of their admissions to turn the human hunt back on the killers.

title: Murderisa Silent Companion
show: The Private Files of Rex Saunders
plotSynopsis: On a train, a cryptic message from a woman pulls Rex into the aftermath of an old bank robbery and a supposed death. The stolen $25,000 has kept former partners circling one another for years; a fake-death scheme and competing double-crosses end in murder until Rex exposes who has been waiting to seize the hidden money.

title: Murder Deep in a Killers Mind
show: The Private Files of Rex Saunders
plotSynopsis: In New Orleans during Mardi Gras, an anonymous caller sends Rex toward Sid Bryce, only for Bryce and his wife to be murdered and the evidence arranged to point elsewhere. A gun, a hidden costume and a handkerchief whose latent fingerprints can be developed with silver nitrate let Rex strip away the killer’s disguise and prove who staged the frame-up.

title: A Shockingstill Life
show: The Private Files of Rex Saunders
plotSynopsis: Rex is drawn into a series of deaths surrounding a haunting portrait of a scarred young woman and a French investigator’s search for a stolen Renoir. The portrait proves to have been painted over the missing masterpiece, and the people who knew the secret were murdered to keep the valuable painting hidden until it could be sold.

title: Plan in the Killers Mind
show: The Private Files of Rex Saunders
plotSynopsis: A runaway horse introduces Rex to a case that soon centers on a stolen diamond necklace and a trail of murders. A man calling himself an insurance investigator appears to help recover the jewels, but Rex learns he has been manipulating the case and killing people who could expose him; a paste copy of the necklace lets Rex turn the final setup against the supposed investigator.

title: Worthmorethanits Weightin Murder
show: The Private Files of Rex Saunders
plotSynopsis: A woman asks Rex to help recover a rare Ming porcelain cat, and the search quickly produces a suspicious death and a chain of antique dealers and double-crosses. The figurine’s true value is not the porcelain at all: it has been used to smuggle roughly $100,000 in narcotics. Rex discovers a staged death, a fatal shooting and a husband-and-wife betrayal centered on control of the hidden package.

title: Lady with Hate in Her Heart
show: The Private Files of Rex Saunders
plotSynopsis: A mysterious blonde uses Rex to shake a pursuer, drawing him into what appears to be a Treasury investigation of a counterfeiting ring. The identities and loyalties keep shifting until Rex discovers that the supposed federal agent and several suspects are themselves part of the operation, and he uses their attempted double-cross to break the gang.

title: Hidden Thoughtsina Feminine Mind
show: The Private Files of Rex Saunders
plotSynopsis: During a Caribbean voyage Rex’s encounter with a masked woman leads him into a network operating around Havana, where warnings and abductions conceal a larger smuggling plot. The conspirators have been importing doctored wine containing incendiary material to stir up violence and confusion; Rex turns their attempted trap back on them and exposes the ring.

title: Gamewith Death
show: The Private Files of Rex Saunders
plotSynopsis: A quarrel aboard Tony Marco’s offshore gambling ship leads Rex to the disappearance of Jerry Connell, who has threatened Marco over his sister Helen. Evidence from the waterfront and a dying man’s message identifies Rocky as the actual killer, but the final confrontation points beyond Marco to Helen herself, whose manipulation of Rocky and the people around her has left her brother and others dead.

title: Namely Murder
show: The Private Files of Rex Saunders
plotSynopsis: Threats meant to drive Rex off the Stacey case instead lead him toward gambling debts, a missing man and the murder of Lucky Kramer. Rex uses a fingerprint trap on the murder weapon to expose the woman behind a $25,000 swindle, two killings and an attempt to frame another suspect before she can silence him too.

title: A Trip to the Death House
show: The Private Files of Rex Saunders
plotSynopsis: Rex is brought into a racketeering case when prosecutors need a frightened insider to testify before the grand jury. The gang moves to silence the witness and steal the affidavit that can support the indictment, leading Rex through a waterfront trap and an attempted killing. By preserving both the witness and the evidence, he turns the racketeers’ own cleanup operation into the case that sends them toward the death house.

title: Doneto Death
show: The Private Files of Rex Saunders
plotSynopsis: A mysterious woman at the docks draws Rex into the murder of diamond courier Stephen Allison. Clues involving cigarette butts, copper filings and an apparent accident lead to a counterfeit-currency ring; Rex stages his own death long enough for the conspirators to reveal their plan to move forged British notes hidden inside automobile tubes.

title: Good News (1948-10-04)
plotSynopsis: College football star Tom Marlowe must pass an astronomy examination to remain eligible for the big game, so studious Connie Lane is assigned to tutor him. Tom initially chases a more glamorous girl, but study sessions reveal the deeper match; after he passes and leads the team through the game, Tom and Connie stop denying the attraction that has grown between them.

title: Anything Goes (1948-10-11)
plotSynopsis: Billy Crocker stows away on an ocean liner to stop Hope Harcourt from marrying Sir Evelyn Oakleigh, aided by nightclub singer Reno Sweeney and harmless gangster Moonface Martin. A mistaken public-enemy identity complicates the voyage, but a financial deal frees Hope from her engagement and the confusion ends with Billy and Hope together while Reno pairs off with Evelyn.

title: The Cat and the Fiddle (1948-10-18)
plotSynopsis: American songwriter Shirley Sheridan meets serious composer Victor Florescu in Paris, and their argument over popular versus 'important' music quickly becomes a romance and a creative partnership. Meddling associates separate them and even destroy one of Shirley's letters, but the finished production depends on her songs; at the performance Victor publicly credits Shirley as his collaborator, calls her onto the stage and asks her to marry him.

title: The Student Prince (1948-10-25)
plotSynopsis: Crown Prince Karl Franz falls in love with innkeeper's niece Kathy during his student year at Heidelberg, but his father's illness forces him home and ultimately onto the throne. Years later Princess Margaret persuades Kathy to step aside for the sake of the kingdom; when Karl returns, Kathy pretends she has promised herself to another man. Karl marries Margaret and fulfills his royal duty, carrying the memory of Kathy and his student days with him.

title: Roberta (1948-11-01)
plotSynopsis: Johnny Kent travels to Paris after his aunt, the celebrated fashion designer Madame Roberta, summons him and draws him into her salon. There he falls for Roberta's assistant Stephanie while his old attachment to Sophie creates confusion. Johnny finally learns that Stephanie's supposed romantic rival is actually her cousin and that her newly revealed royal background does not change her feelings for him. He admits he has been a fool, and Stephanie urges him to ask for the future they both want.

title: Rio Rita (1948-11-08)
plotSynopsis: Along the Texas border, Ranger Jim Stewart's hunt for the outlaw called the Kinkajou seems to place suspicion on the brother of the woman he loves, Rita. Jim lets the misunderstanding stand while he gathers proof, provoking Rita's anger but drawing the real criminal into the open; Esteban is exposed as the Kinkajou, Rita's brother is cleared and Jim can finally explain the deception.

title: The Vagabond King (1948-11-15)
plotSynopsis: Poet-thief François Villon is elevated by the king to temporary Grand Marshal and given a chance to defend Paris, though he knows the bargain may end at the gallows. Villon rallies beggars, thieves and ordinary people to defeat the Burgundian attack, then submits to the promised sentence. Catherine declares her love and invokes the king's pledge to save him, and Villon leaves royal life behind to marry her.

title: Hit the Deck (1948-11-22)
plotSynopsis: Wealthy Lulu falls for sailor Mr. Smith, but his pride will not let him marry a woman with money, and he leaves determined to make his own way. Lulu gives up the wealth that stood between them and reopens her sailors' restaurant, waiting for him to return. After leaving the Navy, Smith comes back believing Lulu is now as poor as he is, admits he never stopped loving her and asks her to share the modest life he can offer.

title: The New Moon (1948-11-29)
plotSynopsis: French nobleman Robert, a fugitive from the crown, travels under an assumed status and falls in love with Marianne while political danger follows him overseas. On a distant island he and the colonists face the old royal order until a French naval officer arrives with news of the Revolution: the monarchy has fallen, Robert is no longer wanted, and he is free to marry Marianne.

title: Girl Crazy (1948-12-06)
plotSynopsis: New York cabdriver Skeeter Mulligan is carried west with Danny Churchill, who turns his father's Arizona ranch into a dude ranch and gambling attraction while courting post-office girl Molly. Local tough Link Sanders fights Danny's operation and a visiting New Yorker creates a romantic misunderstanding, but after Danny is attacked, Mulligan accidentally captures Link and recovers the stolen money; Molly and Danny reconcile while the persistent Frisco Kate claims Mulligan for herself.

title: Sally (1948-12-13)
plotSynopsis: Sally is an ordinary dishwasher with extraordinary stage talent, but she can get her chance only by masquerading as a celebrated foreign dancer. The deception carries her into high society and romance until both Sally and a supposed grand duke are exposed as working people in disguise; stripped of the false titles, Sally's real ability wins out and she ends with the man who loves her for herself.

title: Holiday Inn (1948-12-20)
plotSynopsis: Jim Hardy leaves show business to create Holiday Inn, a country nightclub open only on holidays, and falls in love with singer Linda. His former partner Ted and a Hollywood director lure Linda toward a screen career, and Jim's jealousy and retreat leave her believing he no longer cares; she reluctantly agrees to marry Ted at Christmas. Jim reaches the studio before the wedding, admits he never stopped loving her and brings Linda home to Holiday Inn while Ted finally steps aside.

title: The Desert Song (1948-12-27)
plotSynopsis: Pierre, the French governor's seemingly idle son, secretly leads oppressed desert tribes as the masked Red Shadow. Margot is drawn both to Pierre and to the daring outlaw without knowing they are the same man, while Pierre's own father is determined to destroy the Red Shadow. Pierre refuses a fight that would betray the people he protects and is cast into the desert, but his identity is eventually uncovered. He stages the Red Shadow's disappearance, wins his father's respect, and reunites with Margot, who discovers that the two men she loved were one and the same.

title: Whoopee (1949-01-03)
plotSynopsis: Sally Morgan is expected to marry Sheriff Bob but is in love with a young man raised as an Indian, while hypochondriac Henry Williams becomes her accidental accomplice when she runs away from the wedding. Their flight creates a comic manhunt and even gets Henry mistaken for a gang leader. Black Eagle finally reveals that Sally's beloved was actually born to white parents and adopted after his mother died, removing the racial barrier Sally feared. Sally chooses him, while Henry gives up his imaginary illnesses and agrees to marry Miss Custer.

title: The Red Mill (1949-01-10)
plotSynopsis: Two comic American adventurers become entangled in a Dutch burgomaster's plans to marry his daughter to a politically useful match even though she loves another man. A scheme involving an impersonation of Sherlock Holmes, a supposedly haunted red mill and a frantic search for the missing girl gives the young lovers time to act. When the burgomaster finally finds his daughter, she calmly announces that the wedding he planned is impossible because she has already married the man she loves. With the romance settled, the Americans turn their thoughts back toward home.

title: Naughty Marietta (1949-01-17)
plotSynopsis: Royal-born Marietta comes to the New World hoping to escape the rigid future planned for her, including a commanded marriage to Don Carlos. She falls in love with Captain Dick Warrington and begins to imagine a life based on freedom rather than rank. When duty seems to force her back to Europe, Dick helps her escape instead. The story closes with Marietta gaining a new title of her own choosing: Mrs. Warrington.

title: Blossom Time (1949-01-24)
plotSynopsis: Composer Franz Schubert falls in love with Mitzi and writes a song to tell her how he feels, asking his close friend to help present it. Instead, Schubert discovers that Mitzi and his friend love each other. He steps aside rather than stand between them, later helping clear a misunderstanding that has placed his friend in danger of a duel. With the couple reunited, Schubert gives them his song and accepts that the enduring love available to him is the music he creates.

title: Blossom Time (AFRS) (1949-01-24)
plotSynopsis: In this Armed Forces Radio presentation, Franz Schubert's love for Mitzi becomes the private heartbreak behind his music. When Schubert asks his closest friend to speak for him, he discovers that Mitzi and the friend love each other; he steps aside rather than divide them, accepting music as the companion that will carry his feelings farther than the romance he has lost.

title: Bittersweet (1949-01-31)
plotSynopsis: An elderly Sarah recalls how she abandoned a conventional marriage to elope with composer Carl Linden and build a life with him in Vienna. Their happiness ends when a drunken officer harasses Sarah and kills Carl in the resulting duel, leaving her with a bittersweet memory that she uses years later to urge a younger woman not to let love slip away.

title: Rose Marie (1949-02-07)
plotSynopsis: Rose Marie loves Jim Kenyon, but wealthy Edward Hawley wants her and exploits a murder to remove his rival. Hawley kills Black Eagle and arranges evidence that makes Jim appear guilty, forcing him to flee while Rose Marie is pressured toward Hawley. Jim finally returns with Wanda, Black Eagle's widow, who identifies Hawley as the murderer. With Hawley exposed, Rose Marie finds Jim again at the Kootenai cabin and their 'Indian Love Call' reunites them.

title: Sweethearts (1949-02-14)
plotSynopsis: Crown Prince Franz falls in love with Sylvia, a young woman working in a Belgian laundry, but Sylvia believes their difference in rank makes marriage impossible. A comic family confession reveals that Sylvia was adopted as an infant and is actually the missing heir to the throne of Zelenia. The discovery removes the social barrier that separated her from Franz and gives both of them a claim to the country's future. Rather than wait until they are restored as king and queen, they decide to marry immediately.

title: Lady Be Good (1949-02-21)
plotSynopsis: Susie and Dick are caught in a comic inheritance and identity scheme involving wealthy Josie and the supposedly dead Fred Robinson. The plot depends on Fred being out of the way, but he suddenly returns alive and exposes the arrangement built around his reported death. Susie immediately chooses Fred, while Dick is released from the unwanted marriage being arranged for him. With the fraud undone, the romantic pairs are rearranged and the confusion ends happily.

title: Song of Norway (1949-02-28)
plotSynopsis: Young Edvard Grieg leaves Norway to develop as a composer while Nina and their friend Rick remain tied to the country and music he left behind. Success and the patronage of Countess Louisa pull Grieg farther from his roots even after he and Nina marry. After Rick's death leaves Grieg the poem 'Norway,' he finally understands what his music has lost, returns with Nina to Trollhaugen and sets the poem to music as the 'Song of Norway.'

title: The Merry Widow (1949-03-07)
plotSynopsis: A nearly bankrupt kingdom depends on keeping a wealthy young widow's fortune at home, so Prince Danilo is pushed toward the woman he once loved but has been too proud to pursue. Their old feelings survive jealousy, political scheming and repeated refusals to speak plainly, and the pair finally admit their love, turning a diplomatic problem into a marriage.

title: Eileen (1949-03-14)
plotSynopsis: Irish patriot Captain Barry O'Day hides in plain sight as a groom named Sean while British authorities search for him after an uprising. His disguise brings him close to Eileen, and the two fall in love even as Barry prepares to return to the rebel cause. When the authorities finally close in, Barry and his supporters expect a fight. Instead, a new administration arrives with a general pardon for those involved in the rising. Barry is free, and the story closes by sending him and Eileen toward their happily-ever-after ending.

title: Best Foot Forward (1949-03-28)
plotSynopsis: Prep-school student Bud Hooper jokingly invites movie star Gale Joy to his prom and panics when she unexpectedly accepts, especially because he has lied to his regular girlfriend Helen that he is ill. Gale attends under Helen's name in search of publicity, while the real Helen arrives and the deception erupts into scandal. The principal expels Bud, but Gale protects him by threatening a publicity photograph that would embarrass the school. When the prom story becomes national news, the principal reverses the punishment, and Bud and Helen reconcile with plans to marry.

title: Mademoiselle Modiste (1949-04-04)
plotSynopsis: A young Paris hat-shop clerk dreams of becoming a singer and falls for an American student, but his wealthy father objects to the match. An anonymous benefactor enables her to leave the shop and train abroad until she becomes a successful singer; when the lovers meet again, the young man reveals that he also secretly invested under the name Edward Carton to protect her future, and the couple finally reunite with his father's opposition overcome.

title: Apple Blossoms (1949-04-18)
plotSynopsis: Nancy and Phil have entered a marriage neither expects to keep, while Nancy thinks she belongs with Dickie and Phil believes he loves Anne. Their guardian encourages the divorce but stages a masquerade where exchanged capes confuse everyone's identities. Nancy unknowingly confesses to Dickie that she has fallen in love with her husband, while Phil makes the same discovery about Nancy. The divorce is abandoned and both spouses choose the marriage they nearly threw away.

title: The Jimmy Mc Hugh Story (1949-07-11)
plotSynopsis: A dramatized musical biography of songwriter Jimmy McHugh, following his rise from an eight-dollar-a-week office boy at the Boston Opera House to a long run of popular hits. The tribute performs songs including 'I Can't Give You Anything but Love' and 'It's a Most Unusual Day,' recreates collaborations with lyricists such as Dorothy Fields and Harold Adamson, and ends with birthday wishes and praise for McHugh's continuing career.

title: Ethelbert Nevin Salute (1949-08-01)
plotSynopsis: A biographical and musical salute to American composer Ethelbert Nevin, tracing his short life, family and songwriting through dramatized scenes and performances of music he set to well-known poems. The program emphasizes Nevin's affection for children, his home life and enduring songs, then presents a commemorative scroll accepted by soprano Dorothy Kirsten on behalf of Nevin's son Paul.

title: Mack Gordon - Joseph Warren Salute (1949-08-15)
plotSynopsis: A musical tribute to lyricist Mack Gordon and the collaborator whom the broadcast identifies as composer Joseph Myro, tracing their partnership at 20th Century Fox through dramatized songwriting anecdotes and performances of their film songs. The program discusses Myro's breakthrough on 'Three Little Girls in Blue,' the rush to record 'By the Way' before the musicians' recording ban, and other Gordon-Myro numbers while the two guests join the closing salute.

title: Nacio Herb Brown Salute (1949-09-19)
plotSynopsis: This musical-biographical tribute traces composer Nacio Herb Brown's career through songs and dramatized anecdotes, including his early talking-picture work with lyricist Arthur Freed and numbers such as 'You Stepped Out of a Dream' and 'Love Is Where You Find It.' The program reflects on Brown's ambition to write more serious music and closes with a formal Railroad Hour tribute scroll accepted on his behalf by his son, Nacio Herb Brown Jr.

title: Showboat (1949-10-03)
plotSynopsis: Magnolia grows up aboard her father's showboat, falls in love with gambler Gaylord Ravenal and leaves the river to marry him. Gaylord's gambling troubles eventually drive him away, but Magnolia creates a successful stage life and later returns to the showboat; there she and Gaylord meet again and finally reconcile after years apart.

title: The New Moon (1949-10-10)
plotSynopsis: French nobleman and political fugitive Robert Mission falls for Marianne, but an arrest and a poisonous lie convince him that she helped betray him. After a shipboard revolt leaves Robert and his companions building a democratic settlement on an island, the misunderstanding follows them until the man who caused it confesses; Marianne and Robert learn they had both been loyal and begin their new life together.

title: The Chocolate Soldier (1949-10-17)
plotSynopsis: A young woman idolizes her soldier fiancé's supposed heroism until an enemy officer climbs into her room seeking refuge and reveals a very different kind of courage: he carries chocolates instead of ammunition and wants only to survive. She protects the 'chocolate soldier,' and when he later returns, the boastful fiancé's pretensions unravel while the stranger's honesty wins her affection and eventually her love.

title: Music in the Air (1949-10-24)
plotSynopsis: Village schoolteacher Karl and his sweetheart Sieglinde leave their Bavarian home when a new song draws them into the glamorous world of professional theater. In the city each is briefly dazzled by a sophisticated new admirer, but the excitement only clarifies what they mean to one another; the pair reject borrowed glamour for the love and music that belonged to them from the start.

title: Blossom Time (1949-10-31)
plotSynopsis: Franz Schubert writes a love song for Mitzi and asks his close friend to help him tell her how he feels. Instead, Schubert sees that Mitzi and his friend have fallen in love with each other and quietly steps aside. Later a jealous husband mistakenly believes Schubert's friend is involved with his wife and prepares for a duel. Schubert clears the misunderstanding and arranges a reconciliation, then gives his song to the reunited lovers and accepts that his own lasting companion is his music.

title: No, No Nanette (1949-11-21)
plotSynopsis: Restless Nanette wants freedom from her cautious guardians and persuades Jimmy Smith to take her to Atlantic City, alarming Jimmy's wife and Nanette's devoted boyfriend Tom. After sampling the glamorous independence she imagined she wanted, Nanette discovers that parties and seaside excitement mean little without Tom; Jimmy's scheme brings the young couple back together, and Nanette finally replaces her favorite word 'no' with a wholehearted yes to the man she loves.

title: The Student Prince (1949-11-28)
plotSynopsis: Crown Prince Karl Franz falls in love with Kathy during his student days at Heidelberg, but a royal death calls him home and ultimately leaves him king. When he returns, Princess Margaret has persuaded Kathy that the country needs its sovereign to make the expected royal marriage. Kathy pretends she has chosen another man, and Karl accepts his duty to marry Margaret while carrying the memory of Kathy and Heidelberg with him.

title: The Mikado (1949-12-05)
plotSynopsis: Nanki-Poo, the Mikado's son traveling in disguise, returns to Titipu for Yum-Yum only to find her promised to the newly appointed Lord High Executioner, Ko-Ko. A plan to satisfy the Mikado with a supposed execution nearly backfires when the court believes Nanki-Poo dead; Ko-Ko finally wins over Katisha, Nanki-Poo reappears alive and he and Yum-Yum are allowed to marry.

title: Rose Marie (1949-12-19)
plotSynopsis: In the Canadian northwest, Jim Kenyon plans a future with Rose Marie but is accused of murdering Black Eagle after the dead man's widow names him. Given only a short time to clear himself, Jim cannot break the widow's story, but Rose Marie appeals to her as one woman in love to another and obtains the truth about the real killer. Jim is cleared and free to return to Rose Marie.

title: Snow White (1949-12-26)
plotSynopsis: Snow White flees her jealous stepmother and finds refuge with the Seven Dwarfs, but the Queen reaches her in disguise with a poisoned apple. Believing Snow White dead, the dwarfs keep vigil until the searching prince revives her with a kiss and carries her away to his castle.

title: The Red Mill (1950-01-02)
plotSynopsis: Two broke Americans reach a Dutch village just as Gretchen is being forced toward a marriage she does not want. After rescuing her from the old Red Mill, the men disguise themselves as Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson and charge her father to find the very daughter they helped escape. Gretchen marries the man she loves before the trick is exposed, leaving her furious father with a solved 'mystery' and no wedding to the governor.

title: The Merry Widow (1950-01-23)
plotSynopsis: Marsovian diplomat Prince Danilo is ordered to keep wealthy widow Sonia's fortune from leaving their nearly bankrupt homeland by preventing her marriage to a foreigner. Their old love finally wins out over pride and political maneuvering, and Sonia's marriage to Danilo also keeps her fortune tied to Marsovia.

title: Brigadoon (1950-01-30)
plotSynopsis: American travelers Tommy and Jeff stumble into Brigadoon, a Scottish village that awakens for only one day every hundred years. Tommy falls in love with Fiona and learns that an outsider may remain only by loving someone there enough to surrender the outside world; he leaves in doubt, then realizes he cannot forget her and returns after the village has vanished, where the strength of his love causes Brigadoon to reappear long enough for him to stay with Fiona.

title: Sweethearts (1950-02-13)
plotSynopsis: Sylvia, a young woman working in a laundry, falls in love with a man who finally admits he is the crown prince of Zelania. She refuses to believe a common girl can marry him, but a long-hidden family secret reveals that Sylvia was adopted and is herself the missing heir to the throne; with the social barrier gone, the sweethearts are free to marry.

title: The Count of Luxembourg (1950-02-20)
plotSynopsis: The penniless Count of Luxembourg accepts a rich duke's offer to marry an unknown woman in a masked ceremony, with the agreement that they will divorce so she can keep the title and marry the duke. Later the count meets opera singer Angèle and they fall in love without realizing they are already husband and wife. The truth comes out just as the arranged divorce is due. Faced with the duke's money and demands, the count refuses to surrender Angèle, insisting that she is still his wife.

title: Mademoiselle Modiste (1950-02-27)
plotSynopsis: American student Paul falls for Fifi, a Paris hat-shop girl whose talent and ambition draw her toward the stage and a more glamorous life. Social expectations and romantic misunderstandings separate them for a time, but the young couple finally choose each other over the plans others have made for them.

title: Little Nellie Kelly (AFRS) (1950-03-13)
plotSynopsis: Nellie Kelly loves Jerry Conroy, but jealousy and suspicion complicate their romance when Jerry is blamed for a missing pearl. The real thief, dress-shop owner Devere, is exposed with the jewel in his possession, clearing Jerry. Nellie admits she loves Jerry rather than the wealthier man around her, accepts his proposal, and Devere's shop is turned into a wedding gift for the couple.

title: The Only Girl (1950-03-20)
plotSynopsis: Confirmed bachelor Alan Kimbrough needs a composer for his new musical and assumes the beautiful melody coming from the apartment upstairs was written by Ruth Wilson's brother. He discovers that Ruth herself is the composer and hires her as his collaborator; as they build the show together, professional partnership becomes love, and Alan abandons his resistance to marriage to ask Ruth to become his partner for life.

title: Sunny (1950-03-27)
plotSynopsis: Circus performer Sunny and Tom Warren reunite after wartime friendship, each supposedly committed to someone else. Aboard ship to America, they finally admit their love; when Sunny faces an immigration barrier, Tom proposes so she can enter as his wife, transforming their old friendship into the romance both had been avoiding.

title: Song of Norway (1950-04-03)
plotSynopsis: Edvard Grieg leaves Norway to pursue his music, while Nina and their friend Rick represent the home and emotional life he repeatedly leaves behind. Grieg and Nina eventually marry, but international success still distances him from both her and the country that inspired him. After Rick dies, Grieg is left his friend's poem about Norway and finally recognizes what his work has been missing. He returns with Nina to Trollhaugen and transforms the poem and their shared memories into the 'Song of Norway.'

title: Naughty Marietta (1950-04-10)
plotSynopsis: Runaway noblewoman Marietta reaches New Orleans under an assumed identity and meets Captain Dick Warrington, whose soldiers are hunting the pirate Bras Pique. Marietta is pursued by Etienne, who is exposed as the pirate, while Dick repeatedly protects her and ultimately completes the unfinished melody she has always believed would identify the man she should love. With Etienne captured, Marietta chooses Dick.

title: Naughty Marietta (AFRS) (1950-04-10)
plotSynopsis: Runaway noblewoman Marietta reaches New Orleans under an assumed identity and meets Captain Dick Warrington, whose soldiers are hunting the pirate Bras Pique. Marietta is pursued by Etienne, who is exposed as the pirate, while Dick protects her and eventually completes the unfinished melody she has always believed would identify the man she should love. With Etienne captured, Marietta chooses Dick.

title: Madame Sherry (1950-04-17)
plotSynopsis: Edward supports his dance school with money from Uncle Theophilus, who has been led to believe Edward has a wife. For the uncle's visit, Edward's housekeeper pretends to be Madame Sherry while Edward grows close to his young cousin Yvonne. When the invented marriage and the true purpose of the money are exposed, Theophilus is angry but ultimately accepts Edward and Yvonne's love and continues his support as they plan a real marriage.

title: The Prince of Pilsen (1950-04-24)
plotSynopsis: Prince Carl Otto of Pilsen spends his Heidelberg spring vacation in southern France and discovers that an American brewer from Cincinnati has been mistaken for him by the hotel and townspeople. The confusion lets Carl meet the brewer's daughter and fall in love with her while the supposed prince enjoys royal treatment and becomes entangled in threats intended for the real prince. As the mistaken identities unravel, the danger and deception give way to romance, with Carl and the young woman acknowledging their feelings for one another.

title: Sally (1950-05-01)
plotSynopsis: Sally is a dishwasher whose stage talent gets its chance only after she is passed off as the celebrated Madame Nookerova. The masquerade carries her into a wealthy social circle and brings her closer to Blair Farquar, but the deception eventually collapses along with the false identity of a supposed grand duke; Blair chooses Sally without the borrowed title, proposes, and promises that after marriage he will even help with the dishes.

title: The Pink Lady (1950-05-08)
plotSynopsis: A Parisian bachelor trying to protect his engagement invents an elaborate story to explain a mysterious woman in pink, then recruits an unsuspecting antique dealer into a maze of false identities, invented wives and strategically placed kisses. The farce collapses in front of his fiancée, but she sees through both his lies and the Pink Lady and realizes that he truly loves her.

title: Robin Hood (1950-05-15)
plotSynopsis: Robert, Earl of Huntingdon, has become the outlaw Robin Hood in opposition to the Sheriff of Nottingham. When the sheriff tries to force Lady Marian to marry Guy of Gisborne, Robin comes to her aid but is captured and condemned to hang at dawn. Friar Tuck and the outlaws break him free and rescue Marian. By the end Robin's followers are outlaws no more, Robert's standing is restored and he and Marian are free to begin their life together.

title: Princess Pat (1950-05-22)
plotSynopsis: Princess Pat is tired of her husband Toto admiring every pretty woman, while her friend Grace is being forced to marry wealthy Mr. Schmalt instead of the man's son Tony, whom she loves. Pat flirts outrageously with the older millionaire, making Toto jealous and provoking a challenge that sends Schmalt fleeing and frees Tony to marry Grace. Pat admits the flirtation was a lesson, and Toto promises to reform.

title: Review of 1927 (1950-05-29)
plotSynopsis: A Summer Show Train portrait of 1927 at the height of the Roaring Twenties. The program recalls Calvin Coolidge, Jimmy Walker, Babe Ruth, marathon dances, the Holland Tunnel, Lindbergh, the first transatlantic telephone service and Al Jolson's 'The Jazz Singer,' using the year's popular songs to connect those headlines with everyday memories.

title: Review of 1937 (1950-06-05)
plotSynopsis: A Summer Show Train retrospective of 1937, blending headlines, books, movies, radio personalities and popular songs. It recalls the Duke of Windsor and Wallis Simpson, 'A Star Is Born,' Charlie McCarthy, the national fascination with 'Gone with the Wind' and other events, with music including 'The Donkey Serenade' from 'The Firefly' and sentimental songs identified with the year.

title: Review of 1931 (1950-06-12)
plotSynopsis: A Summer Show Train time-capsule visit to 1931, combining Depression-era headlines and personalities with the popular music Americans heard that year. Gordon MacRae and Lucille Norman recall figures including Herbert Hoover, Franklin Roosevelt, Al Capone and Huey Long, then move through songs and entertainment memories such as the Pulitzer-winning Broadway season, Rudy Vallee's 'Good Night Sweetheart' and Harold Arlen's 'I Love a Parade.'

title: Review of the Gay Nineties (1950-06-19)
plotSynopsis: A nostalgic Summer Show Train tour of the Gay Nineties, built from period songs, fashions, celebrities and technological curiosities. Gordon MacRae and Lucille Norman recall Lillian Russell, tandem bicycles, horse cars, Nellie Bly, locomotive No. 999 and the early rivalry between vaudeville and motion pictures, with songs including 'Hello, My Baby' and the 'Robin Hood' favorite 'Oh Promise Me.'

title: Review of 1925 (1950-06-26)
plotSynopsis: A Summer Show Train retrospective of 1925, combining headlines, personalities and popular entertainment with the year's songs. The program recalls Al Smith, the Prince of Wales, Harold Lloyd, the Florida land boom, Hindenburg's election and aviation news, while using music from Broadway successes including 'The Vagabond King' and early Rodgers and Hart material to evoke the middle of the Roaring Twenties.

title: Review of 1900-1905 (1950-07-03)
plotSynopsis: A musical memory trip through 1900-1905, using songs, impersonations and historical sketches to evoke the McKinley and Theodore Roosevelt years. The program recalls George M. Cohan and 'Yankee Doodle Boy,' the Pan-American era, the Panama Canal campaign, early recordings and performers, the St. Louis Exposition and other turn-of-the-century events before closing with an Independence Day message about American freedom.

title: Review of 1934 (1950-07-10)
plotSynopsis: A Summer Show Train return to 1934, mixing news, film, Broadway and popular music into a year-in-review program. It recalls 'It Happened One Night,' 'Anything Goes,' Dillinger, Admiral Byrd's Antarctic expedition and growing unrest abroad, while songs such as 'I Only Have Eyes for You' and music associated with 'The Great Waltz' supply the soundtrack to the memories.

title: Review of 1938 (1950-07-24)
plotSynopsis: A Summer Show Train review of 1938 that ranges from entertainment and popular crazes to the worsening international atmosphere. It recalls Disney's 'Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs,' Benny Goodman's popularity, Dust Bowl migration, the Orson Welles 'War of the Worlds' panic and Joe Louis's knockout of Max Schmeling, with songs including 'You Go to My Head' and Rodgers and Hart's 'Falling in Love with Love.'

title: Review of 1932 (1950-08-07)
plotSynopsis: A Summer Show Train review of 1932 during the depths of the Depression, emphasizing the optimism people found in entertainment and song. The program recalls Herbert Hoover, anti-hoarding appeals, unusual Depression anecdotes, the opening of Radio City Music Hall, the Los Angeles Olympic Games and the Broadway arrival of Kern and Hammerstein's 'Music in the Air,' ending on music presented as a source of gallantry and hope.

title: Review of 1926 (1950-08-14)
plotSynopsis: A Summer Show Train visit to 1926, using headlines, show-business memories and popular songs to recreate the year. The program recalls Metropolitan Opera newcomer Marion Talley, Irving Berlin's marriage, the rise of Joan Crawford, Broadway's 'Gentlemen Prefer Blondes,' Sinclair Lewis's refusal of the Pulitzer Prize and other curiosities, with period music carrying the review through the middle of the Roaring Twenties.

title: Review of 1935 (1950-08-21)
plotSynopsis: A Summer Show Train visit to 1935, combining New Deal-era headlines and popular culture with the year's music. The program recalls the alphabet agencies, G-men, Ethiopia, the rise of swing and other memories, and performs songs associated with the year including 'Lullaby of Broadway,' music from 'Roberta' and Cole Porter's 'Begin the Beguine.'

title: Review of 1929 (1950-08-28)
plotSynopsis: A Summer Show Train review of 1929 that mixes news and cultural memories with the year's music. The program recalls Herbert Hoover and Charles Curtis, Rockefeller's 90th birthday, Byrd's South Pole flight, Broadway and film hits, and the stock-market crash, with songs including music from 'Great Day,' Hoagy Carmichael's 'Stardust' and the era's buoyant 'Singin' in the Rain.'

title: Review of 1922 (1950-09-04)
plotSynopsis: A Summer Show Train time capsule of 1922, combining news, personalities and popular music. It recalls the Harding administration, the first radio commercial, bobbed hair, George M. Cohan's 'Little Nellie Kelly,' Paderewski's return to the concert stage, Geraldine Farrar's Metropolitan Opera farewell, Rudolph Valentino and Irving Berlin's Music Box Revue, with songs such as 'Carolina in the Morning.'

title: Review of 1933 (1950-09-11)
plotSynopsis: A Summer Show Train review of 1933, pairing the music of the year with a picture of America and the increasingly tense world beyond it. The program recalls Franklin Roosevelt's inauguration, the NRA and bank holidays, the return of legal beer, Hitler's growing power and Germany's withdrawal from international disarmament efforts, while revisiting Broadway and song hits such as material from 'As Thousands Cheer' and 'Smoke Gets in Your Eyes.'

title: Roberta (1950-10-09)
plotSynopsis: American football player John arrives in Paris chasing a woman who wants a rich and successful husband and visits his aunt, the celebrated designer Madame Roberta. Roberta's assistant Stephanie helps him see that the glamour he is pursuing is less important than the affection growing between them; when Roberta leaves her fashion house to John, he and Stephanie become partners in the business and finally admit they want to be partners in life as well.

title: Countess Maritza (1950-10-16)
plotSynopsis: Impoverished Count Tassilo hides his title and takes work as overseer on Countess Maritza's estate, where the two fall in love despite their difference in station. When Tassilo's sister accidentally reveals who he really is, Maritza assumes he has been courting her fortune; after learning he took the job only to support his sister, she admits she loves him and calls him back.

title: Revenge with Music (1950-10-23)
plotSynopsis: Carlos believes his bride Maria has been unfaithful and leaves her while plotting revenge through a comic masquerade involving the provincial governor and the governor's wife. Disguises and stolen clothes allow Carlos to play the governor and pursue the other woman, while the real governor is pulled into the same jealous confusion. The scheme finally exposes how badly Carlos has misunderstood Maria. He admits that his revenge began with the false belief that she betrayed him, Maria forgives him, and the couples reconcile in a deliberately comic finale.

title: Show Boat (1950-10-30)
plotSynopsis: Captain Andy's daughter Magnolia meets river gambler Gaylord Ravenal on the Cotton Blossom, becomes the showboat's leading lady after Julie leaves and marries Gaylord when he joins the company. His gambling eventually ruins their life and he disappears, leaving Magnolia to raise their daughter Kim and build a stage career alone; years later Magnolia returns to the showboat, finds Gaylord waiting and chooses forgiveness and reunion.

title: Irene (1950-11-06)
plotSynopsis: Wealthy Donald Marshall meets shopgirl Irene while looking for someone to publicize a fashionable new dress shop and turns her into a society sensation in expensive gowns. Donald falls in love and even buys a fabricated aristocratic genealogy to make Irene acceptable to his circle, but her very ordinary mother arrives and destroys the pretense; with the social masquerade gone, Donald chooses the real Irene and the Cinderella experiment becomes a marriage proposal.

title: Orange Blossoms (1950-11-13)
plotSynopsis: Baron Roger Belmer can inherit a fortune only by satisfying a marriage condition in his aunt's will, so while engaged to Helen he enters a temporary marriage of convenience with Kitty that is supposed to end in divorce after a year. Living apart does not prevent Roger and Kitty from developing real feelings for each other. When Helen discovers that the arrangement has become personal, the financial scheme collapses. Roger gives up the money rather than give up Kitty, and instead of completing the planned divorce he chooses to remain with his wife.

title: A Connecticut Yankee (1950-11-27)
plotSynopsis: Modern American Hank finds himself in King Arthur's England and begins reshaping Camelot with radios, railroads and other anachronistic inventions while falling for Sandy. Merlin tries to defeat him with magic and a love potion, but the scheme backfires; Hank and Sandy are maneuvered into saying their vows and discover they are legally married, defeating both the arranged match and Merlin's interference.

title: The Pirates of Penzance (1950-12-11)
plotSynopsis: Young Frederick believes his apprenticeship to a comic band of pirates ends when he turns twenty-one, freeing him to leave them and marry Mabel. He then learns that because he was born on February 29 he has had only a handful of actual birthdays and is still bound to pirate service. After a confrontation with the police, the pirates surrender in the name of Queen Victoria and are revealed as noblemen who have gone astray, clearing the way for Frederick, Mabel and the other couples to marry.

title: Brigadoon (1950-12-18)
plotSynopsis: American traveler Tommy Albright discovers Brigadoon, a Scottish village that appears for one day every hundred years, and falls in love with Fiona. He leaves because he cannot accept the miracle, then realizes life without her is the greater impossibility; when he returns, his love is strong enough to awaken Brigadoon so he can stay with Fiona forever.

title: Christmas Songs (1950-12-25)
plotSynopsis: A special Railroad Hour Christmas-night party with Gordon MacRae, Lucille Norman and the full company. The program mixes holiday songs and wishes for servicemen away from home with a child-centered retelling of Tchaikovsky's 'Nutcracker' story, then closes on the idea that Christmas generosity and love should continue throughout the year.

title: Review of 1950 (1951-01-01)
plotSynopsis: A special New Year's Day retrospective built from favorite Railroad Hour broadcasts of 1950 rather than a general history of the calendar year. Gordon MacRae, Lucille Norman and the company revisit music from productions such as 'The Red Mill' and other operettas and musicals chosen from listener mail, then close by looking toward 1951 with a prayer for peace and a discussion of the railroads' defense-mobilization role.

title: Carousel (1951-01-08)
plotSynopsis: Carnival barker Billy Bigelow falls in love with Julie Jordan and marries her, but fear about providing for their expected child draws him into a robbery that ends in his death. From the outskirts of heaven Billy is allowed one day back on earth, where he tries clumsily to help his troubled teenage daughter Louise and leaves her a star. Julie recognizes his presence, giving Billy a final chance to express the love he could not show properly in life.

title: The Student Prince (1951-01-15)
plotSynopsis: Crown Prince Karl Franz escapes court life for Heidelberg, where student freedom and his love for the waitress Kathy give him the happiest months of his life. His grandfather's death calls him home to become king and marry Princess Margaret; when he returns hoping to keep his promise to Kathy, Margaret persuades Kathy to sacrifice the romance, and Kathy claims she loves another so Karl will return to his duty and royal marriage.

title: The New Moon (1951-01-29)
plotSynopsis: French patriot Robert is fleeing royal authorities when he falls in love with Lady Marianne, but aristocrat Rebo poisons the romance by convincing Robert that Marianne betrayed him. After the New Moon carries the rebels to an island, they build their own democratic community and Rebo finally admits that Marianne had actually tried to save Robert. A French warship arrives to arrest him, only to announce that the monarchy has fallen and France is now a republic. Robert is no longer a royal fugitive, and Marianne chooses to remain as his wife and partner.

title: The Cat and the Fiddle (1951-02-05)
plotSynopsis: American songwriter Shirley Sheridan and composer Victor meet in Brussels and fall in love almost immediately, but a lost letter and professional misunderstandings make each believe the other has chosen someone else. They later find themselves working on the same stage production, with Shirley's songs being considered for Victor's score while jealousy keeps them apart. The missing letter finally turns up and exposes the misunderstanding. Both admit their supposed new romances meant nothing, and Victor asks Shirley to marry him.

title: Sari (1951-02-12)
plotSynopsis: Poor violinist Ereni seeks the famous Stradivarius owned by aging gypsy musician Pauli Ratz and instead finds both the instrument and Pauli's lovely daughter Sari. In Paris, Pauli discovers he can no longer perform for the king, but Ereni plays the old man's unwritten gypsy melody from the heart; Pauli gives him the violin, and the king ennobles Ereni and Sari so the lovers can face the world together.

title: Song of Norway (1951-02-19)
plotSynopsis: Young composer Edvard Grieg leaves Norway seeking artistic success and is drawn into the glittering European world promoted by Countess Louisa. Fame strains his marriage to Nina, but Grieg ultimately returns to the people and landscape that inspired him, completing a 'Song of Norway' and reuniting with Nina and his old friend.

title: Two Hearts in Three-Quarter Time (1951-02-26)
plotSynopsis: Playboy composer Tony Hoeller needs a love song, so his producer plans to send an actress to put him in a romantic mood. The producer's daughter Hedy secretly takes her place, inspiring both a new waltz and Tony's first serious love; when he later forgets the melody, Hedy supplies it and reveals herself, and Tony promises to reform as he asks her to marry him.

title: The Vagabond King (1951-03-05)
plotSynopsis: Poet and thief François Villon is drawn into the defense of Paris and into the orbit of King Louis and the noblewoman Katherine. His wit and courage help him rise above his criminal life for a time, but when the crisis passes he is still condemned to die for his old crimes. At the gallows Katherine invokes the king's promise and claims Villon's hand in marriage, forcing the sentence to be reversed. Villon and Katherine ride away from Paris together, with Villon promising that love will make an honest man of the Vagabond King even as the final joke leaves his old instincts intact.

title: Rosalinda (1951-03-12)
plotSynopsis: Henry Eisenstein's roving eye leads him to a masquerade instead of directly to jail, where his disguised wife Rosalinda lets him court her without recognizing her. The next day the masquerade, a borrowed watch and a mistaken prisoner expose everyone's deceptions; husband and wife trade jealous accusations, then reconcile after each has had a taste of being deceived.

title: Apple Blossoms (1951-03-19)
plotSynopsis: Phil and Nancy enter an arranged marriage while each believes they love someone else, and even their guardian concludes that divorce may be the kindest solution. At a masquerade, Nancy mistakes her masked husband for her former sweetheart and confesses that she has fallen in love with Phil; Phil has made the same discovery about Nancy. Their supposed mismatched marriage becomes the real romance, while their former partners pair off elsewhere.

title: The Fortune Teller (1951-03-26)
plotSynopsis: A gypsy musician falls for a celebrated ballet dancer whose future is being arranged by people who value rank and advantage more than love. Disguises, fortune-telling and a return to the gypsy camp strip away the social roles surrounding them, and the dancer finally chooses the man and the freedom she really wants rather than the marriage others planned for her.

title: Annie Laurie (1951-04-02)
plotSynopsis: Young Scottish poet Robin Burns plans to leave home when poverty and family opposition seem to defeat both his writing and his love for Jean Armour. Jean secretly sends his poems to a publisher, turning him into a celebrated poet; when she fears he loves the idealized Annie Laurie of his song, Robin reveals that the imagined perfect woman has always been Jean.

title: One Touch of Venus (1951-04-16)
plotSynopsis: Barber Rodney Hatch accidentally brings a statue of Venus to life and soon finds the goddess falling in love with him. Rodney imagines settling her into ordinary suburban marriage, but Venus realizes that life cannot contain what she is and returns to stone; moments later Rodney meets an ordinary young woman who looks exactly like Venus, giving him a second, human chance at love.

title: Music in the Air (1951-04-30)
plotSynopsis: A young Bavarian couple leave their village when a promising song offers a path into the professional theater, and the sophisticated city world quickly pulls them in different directions. Each is tempted by a glamorous new admirer, but the experience exposes how shallow those attractions are; they rediscover the affection that first joined them and turn back toward the simpler life and music they truly share.

title: High Button Shoes (1951-05-07)
plotSynopsis: Married couple Henry and Sarah Longstreet look back on their courtship in 1913, when smooth con man Harrison Foy persuaded Sarah's family and neighbors to invest in a worthless real-estate development. Sarah was made treasurer, allowing Foy to flee with the investors' money, and Henry joined the frantic chase that ended with Foy's arrest in Atlantic City. Henry and Sarah chose each other despite the disaster. Years later Foy reappears after prison with the recovered money and immediately tries another scheme, but this time Henry and Sarah know better.

title: Nina Rosa (1951-05-14)
plotSynopsis: An American mining engineer travels to Peru to evaluate the Nina Rosa mine and falls in love with its beautiful heiress, Nina Rosa, provoking the powerful gaucho Pablo. To keep Pablo from killing the American, Nina pretends to reject the man she loves and agrees to marry Pablo, but she secretly substitutes a friend beneath the bridal veil and escapes to confess the truth, leaving Pablo deceived and Nina free to choose her own love.

title: Katinka (1951-05-28)
plotSynopsis: Ivan loves Katinka, but she is trapped in marriage to the tyrannical Boris Strogoff. Ivan's search carries them to Istanbul, where they find Boris's first wife alive; she admits she fled his cruelty and forged her death certificate. Her testimony proves Katinka's marriage invalid, freeing Katinka and Ivan to declare the love they had been forced to hide.

title: Very Warm for May (1951-06-04)
plotSynopsis: Broadway producer Johnny Graham meets aspiring performer May and soon finds their professional sparring turning into love. May joins his show, struggles to stop imitating theatrical mannerisms and finally learns to sing honestly under Johnny's demanding direction; after the production succeeds, she realizes that a stage career matters less to her than the man behind it, and the story ends with May content to trade the footlights for life as Mrs. Johnny Graham.

title: Gypsy Princess (1951-06-11)
plotSynopsis: Prince Ronald falls in love with cabaret star Sylva and enters a civil marriage that must be confirmed by a religious ceremony within three months. His father refuses to accept a singer as a royal bride, and Sylva disappears before returning under the pretense that she is Lord Boniface's wife. Boniface exposes the ruse, and Ronald's mother reveals that she too was once a stage singer, destroying the king's class objection. The king yields and Ronald and Sylva prepare to complete their marriage.

title: The Boys from Syracuse (1951-06-18)
plotSynopsis: A traveler named Antipholus reaches ancient Syracuse and is repeatedly mistaken for his long-lost twin, whose wife and relatives insist they know him. The escalating confusion finally brings the brothers face to face, clearing the mistaken identities and leaving Antipholus free to pursue Luciana, the woman he has fallen for during the mix-up.

title: The Merry Widow (1951-06-25)
plotSynopsis: In Paris, wealthy widow Sonia and Prince Danilo remain in love despite pride, jealousy and Marsovia's fear that Sonia's fortune might leave the country if she marries a foreigner. Baron Popoff's schemes only complicate matters until Danilo finally declares his love believing Sonia will lose her wealth on remarriage; she then reveals the money merely passes to her new husband, allowing love to triumph while the fortune remains safely Marsovian.

title: Beautiful Dreamer (1951-07-02)
plotSynopsis: This musical biography portrays songwriter Stephen Foster late in life, poor, disoriented and haunted by memories of happier years with his wife Jane and the songs that made others famous. Music-shop worker Mary Parker recognizes the broken composer and tries to help him return to writing, but Foster collapses before the new beginning can take hold. In a charity ward he dies with memories of Jane, riverboats and unfinished music merging into the dream world that shaped his songs.

title: Casey at the Bat (1951-07-09)
plotSynopsis: Eleven years after marrying Peg, Mudville ballplayer Casey is still devoted to baseball while Peg wants a more cultured life for their son Timmy. After an argument Peg takes Timmy to Philadelphia, Casey falls into a batting slump and suffers the famous strikeout. Timmy finally brings his mother back to Mudville, reminding her that even great hitters strike out sometimes, and Casey and Peg reconcile at the ballpark.

title: Springtime in Paris (1951-07-16)
plotSynopsis: Two ordinary Americans in Paris reinvent themselves as glamorous strangers and fall in love without admitting who they really are. At the tomb of Héloïse and Abélard they exchange heart-shaped stones before parting; each heads home believing the romance is impossible, never realizing the other is also returning to the same Omaha department store where one is a clerk and the other a stenographer.

title: The Big Top (1951-08-06)
plotSynopsis: Circus clown Rocco and Angelique raise their son Michael away from the sawdust so he can become a polished gentleman, but when Michael grows up he chooses the circus and asks his father to teach him to be a clown. Angelique leaves rather than watch the boy take up the life she tried to spare him, and Rocco loses the joy that made him funny; after circus friends plead for him, Angelique returns and the couple go back to the big top together, ready to laugh through the sadness.

title: A Thousand and One Nights (1951-08-13)
plotSynopsis: Facing execution by Sultan Shahriyar, Scheherazade uses her gift for storytelling to keep the fatal hour from arriving. At her sister's prompting she spins a fantastic adventure of Sinbad, a storm, a giant bird and a genie, always leaving enough unfinished to hold the ruler's attention; the tales awaken Shahriyar's imagination and affection, and the storyteller who was meant to die wins her life and his love.

title: Long Ago (1951-08-20)
plotSynopsis: A young man's letters about an idealized girl named Marjorie Daw become a powerful romantic fantasy for his distant friend, even though the girl exists only in the storyteller's imagination. Years later the old friends have drifted apart, but their son and daughter unexpectedly meet and fall in love for real, turning the long-ago fiction into a second-generation romance neither father could have planned.

title: Danny Freel (1951-08-27)
plotSynopsis: Danny Freel asks Ireland's little people to help him find the perfect bride and is presented with a silent 'foreign' girl he cannot understand. A magic wish restores her speech, revealing that she is a very outspoken local woman from Donegal and not Danny's dream at all; meanwhile the leprechaun Helen discovers that love is making her human, gives up her supernatural duties and chooses a life with Danny.

title: Innocents Abroad (1951-09-03)
plotSynopsis: Samuel Clemens joins a grand European excursion armed with a guidebook full of rules for travelers and meets Sylvia along the way. Their tour through famous cities punctures solemn conventions and the guidebook's advice, especially its warning never to fall in love; by the voyage home both have done exactly that, and Sam turns the journey and its comic lessons into Innocents Abroad.

title: Journey Into the Sun (1951-09-10)
plotSynopsis: Marco Polo journeys farther east than any traveler from his world, is rescued in Kashmir by Vancha and falls in love with her before continuing to the court of Kublai Khan. When Prince Ahmed later imprisons Vancha and tries to force her into marriage, the Khan's decree frees her, punishes Ahmed and allows Marco and Vancha to fulfill their promise to each other.

title: Rip Van Winkle (1951-09-17)
plotSynopsis: Henpecked, easygoing Rip Van Winkle escapes to the Catskills, drinks with mysterious mountain strangers and falls into an enchanted sleep. He wakes twenty years later to a transformed village that has passed through the American Revolution; bewildered at first, Rip is finally recognized by his grown daughter and welcomed home to the new world he slept through.

title: The Emperor of San Francisco (1951-09-24)
plotSynopsis: After losing his fortune in San Francisco, Joshua Norton responds by proclaiming himself Emperor of the United States and gradually becomes a tolerated, generous local institution. He befriends an opera singer calling herself Countess Esther, helps soften the arrogant manager Peter Briggs and watches the pair marry. Years later, as Norton lies dying, he begins to doubt whether his imperial life was only a delusion. Esther admits that her own title was invented too but insists that his kindness made him a true emperor in the way that mattered, and she sings for him at his final request.

title: State Fair (1951-10-01)
plotSynopsis: At the state fair, farmer's daughter Margy meets reporter Pat Gilbert and lets herself enjoy a romance she assumes cannot last, while her father's prize hog Blue Boy has troubles of his own in the judging ring. Pat appears to abandon Margy when the fair ends, leaving her heartbroken, but after landing a Chicago job he returns to the farm and asks her to marry him.

title: Madame Sherry (1951-10-08)
plotSynopsis: Edward keeps his struggling dance school afloat with an allowance from Uncle Theophilus, who believes Edward is respectably married. When the uncle visits, Edward persuades his housekeeper Catherine to pose as Madame Sherry, but the deception becomes awkward when cousin Yvonne arrives and she and Edward fall in love. The false marriage is exposed, yet Theophilus relents and gives his blessing to Edward and Yvonne.

title: Martha (1951-10-15)
plotSynopsis: Lady Harriet and a companion disguise themselves as servants at the Richmond fair, where farmer Lionel hires Harriet under the name Martha and falls in love with her. When he later discovers that the supposed maid is actually a high-born lady he feels deceived and withdraws, so Harriet recreates the fair to show him that her feelings were genuine; Lionel accepts Lady Harriet as the woman he knew as Martha, and the pair finally reconcile.

title: Sweethearts (1951-10-22)
plotSynopsis: Franz, crown prince of Zelenia, falls in love with Sylvia, a young woman working in a laundry, but Sylvia believes their difference in rank makes marriage impossible. A comic family revelation turns the obstacle upside down: Sylvia was adopted as a baby and is herself the missing heir to Zelenia's throne. With both lovers revealed as royal, the supposed mismatch disappears and Franz and Sylvia can marry and restore their country together.

title: Holiday Inn (1951-10-29)
plotSynopsis: Jim turns a quiet country inn into a place that opens only on holidays and falls in love with singer Linda, but his former partner Ted and a Hollywood director see both Linda and the inn as material for a movie. Jim's jealousy and efforts to keep the act from leaving create a rift, but Linda ultimately chooses him and the life they built together at Holiday Inn.

title: Rose Marie (1951-11-05)
plotSynopsis: Jim Kenyon returns to the Canadian north woods for Rose Marie, but their plans collapse when he is accused of murdering Black Eagle. Given only twenty-four hours to clear himself, Jim cannot shake the widow's accusation until Rose Marie appeals to her as one woman in love to another; the widow names the real killer, Jim is cleared and the Mounted sergeant directs Rose Marie back to the man she loves.

title: The Bohemian Girl (1951-11-12)
plotSynopsis: Polish exile Thaddeus has lived among gypsies since fleeing Austrian soldiers and loves Arline, the count's daughter who was stolen away as a child and has only recently been restored to her father. The count rejects a supposed vagabond as a husband until Thaddeus reveals his identity as a Polish patriot and learns that Austria and Poland are now at peace. The old hostility ends, the count gives his blessing and Arline becomes Thaddeus's gypsy bride.

title: Jubilee (1951-11-19)
plotSynopsis: On the eve of a royal jubilee, a bored king, queen, prince and princess disappear from the palace under the name Smith so each can sample the ordinary life they envy. Their outings bring the younger royals face to face with the famous dancer and playwright they idolize, but the approaching jubilee reminds the family where they belong; they return to the throne with a warmer appreciation of one another and the people they met.

title: Mademoiselle Modiste (1951-11-26)
plotSynopsis: Paris hat-shop girl Fifi dreams of a larger life and loves army officer Etienne, whose aristocratic uncle considers her unsuitable. An American customer recognizes Fifi's voice and finances her musical training, allowing her to leave Paris and build a career. Two years later she returns as celebrated opera singer Mademoiselle Bellini, reunites with Etienne at a masquerade, and wins the uncle's respect and blessing for their marriage.

title: Marinka (1951-12-03)
plotSynopsis: Crown Prince Rudolf of Austria falls in love with Marinka while secretly sympathizing with Hungarian opposition to the empire. When the revolt fails, the emperor confronts Rudolf with a death sentence for treason but chooses another solution: he officially declares his son dead and orders Rudolf and Marinka to disappear beyond the border. The lovers leave Austria together, while the court is left to invent the legend that will explain their disappearance.

title: The Red Mill (1951-12-10)
plotSynopsis: Two broke Americans in Holland become involved in Gretchen's forced marriage to an unwanted older suitor and use disguises, detective theatrics and the supposedly haunted Red Mill to interfere. Their schemes free Gretchen to choose the man she loves, after which the rescuers happily look toward returning to New York.

title: Rosalie (1951-12-17)
plotSynopsis: American aviator Dick Fay reunites with Princess Rosalie, whose royal obligations seem to make the romance they began in Paris impossible.
