After Rosalie admits she loves him, her mother refuses consent because the princess must someday inherit the throne; Rosalie's father solves the problem by resigning as king, making Rosalie a private citizen free to marry Dick while he cheerfully plans a new life outside royalty.

title: The Happy Prince (1951-12-24)
plotSynopsis: A little swallow delays its journey south to help the gilded statue of the Happy Prince ease suffering throughout the city. At the prince's request the bird gives away his ruby, sapphire eyes and finally every leaf of gold to the poor, remaining beside the now-blind statue until winter kills it; officials later destroy the shabby statue, but its lead heart will not melt, and heaven recognizes the heart and the dead swallow as the city's two most precious things.

title: Review of 1951 (1951-12-31)
plotSynopsis: A New Year's Eve review of the Railroad Hour's own 1951 season, using listener favorites and excerpts from the year's broadcasts rather than a general historical chronology. The company revisits productions such as 'State Fair,' the run of thirteen original summer musicals and 'Springtime in Paris,' then closes by welcoming 1952 with Irving Berlin music, thanks for the year's broadcasts and a prayer for the new year.

title: Blossom Time (1952-01-07)
plotSynopsis: Franz Schubert falls in love with Mitzi and asks his closest friend to speak for him, only to discover that Mitzi and the friend love one another. Rather than stand between them, Schubert gives them his blessing and turns back to the music that has always been his truest companion; his own heartbreak becomes part of the songs and melodies that outlive the romance he surrendered.

title: I Married an Angel (1952-01-14)
plotSynopsis: Banker Willie Palaffi marries Brigitta, a literal angel whose complete honesty and innocence make her a disastrous fit for worldly society. Her blunt truthfulness offends people Willie needs for business, and in trying to adapt to earthly life she loses her wings and fears she has become neither angel nor woman. Willie's sister coaches her in social behavior, but Brigitta's honesty ultimately wins over the very duchess whose support the bank needs. Willie tells Brigitta that he loves her as she is, and the pair reconcile without asking her to abandon her angelic nature.

title: The Desert Song (1952-01-21)
plotSynopsis: In French Morocco, Governor Birabeau's apparently mild son Pierre secretly leads resistance to injustice as the masked Red Shadow. Margot is attracted to both men without realizing they are the same person, and the Red Shadow's fight brings father and son into direct conflict. Pierre finally unmasks himself, his father recognizes the courage and justice behind the rebellion, and Margot understands that she has loved both sides of Pierre all along.

title: The Three Musketeers (1952-01-28)
plotSynopsis: D'Artagnan comes to Paris hoping to join the King's Musketeers and quickly finds himself fighting beside Athos, Porthos and Aramis while falling in love with Constance. Cardinal Richelieu's agents scheme to use compromising letters against the queen and the crown, drawing the four swordsmen into a race to recover them. The plot is defeated and the damaging evidence destroyed. The king rewards D'Artagnan by making him the fourth musketeer, leaving him free to claim Constance as well.

title: The East Wind (1952-02-04)
plotSynopsis: Claudette's love for Paul is repeatedly blocked by violence, pride and her unhappy marriage to Paul's brother Renee. After Renee dies as violently as he lived, Paul is far away and Claudette believes the east wind will never bring him back. He eventually returns from military service wounded and convinced that he would only burden her. Their old friend refuses to let either hide behind pride, and Claudette and Paul finally choose a life together despite the fact that it cannot be perfect.

title: Orange Blossoms (1952-02-11)
plotSynopsis: Roger Belmont enters a marriage of convenience with Kitty so he can protect his financial position while expecting eventually to return to Helen. Although the arrangement is supposed to remain strictly business, Roger and Kitty fall genuinely in love. When Helen confronts them, Kitty tries to walk away, but Roger chooses his wife and the temporary arrangement becomes a real marriage.

title: Frederika (1952-02-18)
plotSynopsis: Young Johann Wolfgang Goethe falls in love with Frederika while living in Sesenheim, and for a time both imagine a simple life together. When an opportunity arrives that could launch the literary career he longs for, Frederika realizes that keeping him in the village would destroy the future he is meant to have and lets him go. Years later the celebrated Goethe returns and learns that Frederika never married. Their love has endured, but she asks him not to turn memory into a new promise, and they part again with their old happiness preserved.

title: The Firefly (1952-02-25)
plotSynopsis: Engaged New Yorker Jack Travers becomes fascinated by Nina, a Little Italy street singer called the Firefly, then meets her again aboard ship when she disguises herself as cabin boy Tony. Jack's feelings for his fiancée Geraldine fade as he grows closer to the supposed boy, and Nina is eventually exposed and dismissed in Bermuda. Jack finds her at the harbor, rejects the loveless marriage awaiting him and chooses Nina, earning their passage home by singing with her.

title: The White Eagle (1952-03-03)
plotSynopsis: Englishman Jim Carson falls in love with Winona, the daughter of a Native chief, and builds a family with her in the American West. Years later pressure over their son's future makes Winona fear she will lose both husband and child, but the crisis proves the family's loyalty to one another and they choose to remain together.

title: The Cat and the Fiddle (1952-03-10)
plotSynopsis: Composers Victor Florescu and Shirley Sheridan meet by chance in Brussels, fall in love and separate with promises to write. A misplaced letter makes Victor believe Shirley has forgotten him, and years later they meet again in Paris amid new professional and romantic misunderstandings; when the lost letter finally turns up, both realize their separation was accidental, abandon the people they were supposedly going to marry and choose each other instead.

title: Sari (1952-03-17)
plotSynopsis: A wandering young violinist arrives in a Hungarian village searching for both the ideal girl and the great violin of a retired gypsy musician. He falls for the musician's daughter and persuades her father to travel to Paris for a royal performance, but the old man discovers he can no longer play after years of retirement. The young violinist takes up the treasured instrument and instinctively revives the melody the older man had carried only in memory. Impressed, the king grants him a title, removing the social barrier between the musician and the village girl he loves.

title: Kiss Me Kate (1952-03-24)
plotSynopsis: Divorced actors Fred Graham and Lilli Vanessi reunite onstage in The Taming of the Shrew and immediately resume the jealousy, insults and attraction that wrecked their marriage. A pair of gangsters temporarily prevents Lilli from quitting the production, but once their boss is gone she is free to leave. Instead, Lilli returns voluntarily for the final scene, and the stage reconciliation of Petruchio and Kate becomes a real reconciliation between Lilli and Fred.

title: Countess Maritza (1952-03-31)
plotSynopsis: Countess Maritza falls in love with Tassilo while believing him to be merely the manager of her estate, but the romance collapses when she learns that he has concealed his true social position and begins to fear that he wants her fortune. Tassilo refuses to defend himself and prepares to leave. His sister Liza tells Maritza that he truly loves her and could easily marry another wealthy woman if money were his object. Maritza races after him before he can go, and the two finally choose the love both had nearly sacrificed to pride and suspicion.

title: Rosalinda (1952-04-14)
plotSynopsis: Viennese husband and wife become entangled in disguises, flirtation and mistaken identities when Rosalinda tests her husband during a masquerade. After each discovers the other's deception, they trade jealous accusations for reconciliation and agree to give up the temptations that caused the trouble.

title: Erminie (1952-04-21)
plotSynopsis: Erminie and her father's secretary Eugene are in love, but her father has already arranged for her to marry the Vicomte de Brissac. Before the nobleman can arrive, an escaped criminal robs him of his clothes and papers and enters the household under his name. Eugene's suspicions help bring soldiers to the scene, and the real vicomte arrives in time to expose the impostor and see the love between Erminie and Eugene. He releases Erminie from the arranged engagement, allowing her father to approve the match she truly wants.

title: Sunny (1952-05-05)
plotSynopsis: Circus performer Sunny and American veteran Tom Warren discover that the affection they once shared has survived despite other expected marriages. When Sunny faces being turned away on arrival in the United States, Tom finally realizes she is the woman he loves and proposes aboard ship, giving them both a future together.

title: Spring Is Here (1952-05-12)
plotSynopsis: Shy Terry Clayton loves Betty but cannot bring himself to compete with glamorous millionaire Stacey Hayden, so Mary Jane tries to manufacture enough romance to make Terry act. When Stacey proposes an elopement, Terry finally attempts to chase them down, only to find Betty has already returned: a kiss from Stacey produced none of the romance she expected. Terry kisses her instead, and the 'music' she finally feels makes clear that the quiet man beside her is the one she loves.

title: The Great Waltz (1952-05-19)
plotSynopsis: Young Johann Strauss wants to write the music he feels, but his famous father dismisses the new waltzes and guards his own title as Vienna's Waltz King. With help from Therese and a sympathetic countess, Johann gets a chance to conduct when his father is delayed and introduces the Blue Danube to Vienna; the triumph establishes the son's voice, and the dying elder Strauss finally acknowledges both the music and the son who will carry it forward.

title: My Maryland (1952-05-26)
plotSynopsis: In Civil War Frederick, Maryland, Barbara Frietchie loves Union Captain Will Trumbull despite her Confederate father's fierce opposition. Their planned wedding is interrupted by approaching battle, so Will gives Barbara his mother's ring and tells her to regard them as married before he marches away. When the wounded Will is brought to Barbara's house, she defies her father and shelters him. Stonewall Jackson's troops retake the town but leave the American flag flying, and Barbara and Will take that gesture as hope that their divided families and country can one day be whole again.

title: Minstrel Boy (1952-06-02)
plotSynopsis: This musical biography follows Irish poet and songwriter Thomas Moore from his youthful courtship of Bessie through decades of marriage and song. Late in life Moore tries to create an important multi-volume history of Ireland, only to be crushed by reviews that call it pompous and lifeless; Bessie helps him recognize that the songs ordinary people still sing, and the love they have shared for forty years, are the legacy that matters.

title: The Swedish Nightingale (1952-06-09)
plotSynopsis: P. T. Barnum brings celebrated singer Jenny Lind to America and turns her tour into a sensation, surrounding her with publicity and commercial promotions she increasingly dislikes. Jenny secretly uses much of her earnings to help needy children, and Barnum finally tears up the contract rather than keep exploiting her. He confesses his feelings, but Jenny recognizes that their lives are different; she completes her promised appearances and leaves for a quieter life in Europe.

title: The Right Dress (1952-06-16)
plotSynopsis: Navy man Danny McBride and Army private Joe Harris exchange identities, sending each into the other's service, troubles and romance. The confusion becomes national news when one is headed for court-martial while the other is credited with saving a ship and winning the Medal of Honor; at the White House the two finally sort out who is who, Joe refuses the medal unless Danny is cleared, and Danny learns that the girl he loves is not Joe's sweetheart at all but Joe's sister.

title: The Little Minister (1952-06-23)
plotSynopsis: Young Scottish minister Gavin Dishart falls in love with Babbie, a spirited 'gypsy' who warns villagers when soldiers threaten them. Babbie reveals that she was raised by Lord Rintoul and is expected to marry him, but she loves Gavin instead, and the pair marry in the gypsy camp; when Gavin's congregation discovers them during a violent flood, the townspeople overcome their anger, rescue the couple and accept Babbie as their minister's wife.

title: Scheherezade (1952-07-07)
plotSynopsis: Sultan Shahriar has sworn that every bride will die before dawn, but Scheherazade enters the marriage determined to survive. With help from her sister, she begins a fantastic tale of Sinbad, storms, a giant bird and a genie, repeatedly leaving the story unfinished; fascination becomes affection, and by sunrise Shahriar abandons the fatal deadline and decrees a thousand and one more nights of her stories.

title: The Necklace (1952-07-14)
plotSynopsis: Mathilde longs for the elegance she cannot afford and borrows a glittering necklace for a grand evening. When the necklace disappears, she and her husband secretly replace it with an expensive duplicate and spend fourteen years sacrificing their youth and comfort to repay the debt. At last Mathilde meets the friend who loaned the jewels and confesses what happened. She then learns the devastating truth: the original necklace was imitation jewelry worth only a few hundred francs.

title: Love Song (1952-07-21)
plotSynopsis: Years after their youth in Vienna, music teacher David is summoned by his old love Diane, widow of the celebrated Johann Lindor, to help restore an unfinished manuscript. Piecing together the torn music forces them to confront the truth that David had written the love song for Diane and had never stopped loving her; she asks him to complete the music, turning the unfinished song into a second chance.

title: The Pirate of New Orleans (1952-07-28)
plotSynopsis: Pirate Jean Lafitte slips into New Orleans in disguise, where he meets Suzanne and begins to imagine what it would mean to belong to the city rather than merely raid its waters. When the British offer him gold to guide their fleet, Lafitte instead offers his men and knowledge to the Americans for the defense of New Orleans. The governor refuses to bargain with a pirate, but General Jackson accepts the help, and after the battle Lafitte and his men receive a full pardon and citizenship. Even with Suzanne asking him to stay, Lafitte decides that respectable life is not his and returns to the sea, still listening for the city he helped save.

title: Starlight (1952-08-04)
plotSynopsis: Vaudeville partners Harry McKay and Helen Harris finally reach the Palace, but Helen reveals that her real dream is to marry Harry and leave the stage for a home of their own. They marry while Harry continues as a solo act, only to watch vaudeville audiences disappear as radio begins to rise. Helen quietly reinvents herself on the air as the Sunshine Girl, Ruth Delio, and Harry becomes a fan without realizing the singer is his wife. When he comes to New York, Helen reveals the truth and brings him into radio with her, launching the husband-and-wife team of McKay and Harris on the new medium.

title: The Brownings (1952-08-11)
plotSynopsis: Poet Robert Browning begins a secret courtship with the invalid Elizabeth Barrett despite her domineering father's control. Their letters and visits grow into love, they escape that household for marriage and Italy, and the story closes on the enduring partnership that inspired some of Elizabeth's most famous love poetry.

title: Miss Cinderella (1952-08-18)
plotSynopsis: Lucinda Brown escapes an ordinary life by losing herself in the story of Cinderella and its prince searching for the girl who fits a lost slipper. Her own day begins to echo the fairy tale when Joe from McCloskey's shoe store tracks her down through a shoe and arrives just as she reaches the same scene in the book. Lucinda and Joe recognize the comic parallel, and the modern Cinderella story ends with the suggestion that a girl can still find her prince in the most everyday place.

title: Fantasy Impromptu (1952-08-25)
plotSynopsis: This original musical drama follows exiled Polish composer Frédéric Chopin as his longing for his occupied homeland becomes inseparable from his music and his turbulent relationship with writer George Sand. Their years together in Mallorca and France produce passionate work but also conflict, especially after Sand turns their private life into fiction; Chopin ultimately leaves, insisting that neither a nation nor a person should live in another's shadow, and dies in Paris still dreaming of a free Poland.

title: Pirates of Picadilly (1952-09-01)
plotSynopsis: This musical biography follows Gilbert and Sullivan through the brilliant but combative partnership that created their celebrated comic operas. Their clashing personalities repeatedly drive them to work apart, trade insults and insist that each deserves the larger share of credit, yet the quarrels also push both men creatively. At the opening of The Gondoliers they hear an audience singing the songs they have created together and finally confront the absurdity of their estrangement. They admit they may never have liked one another very much, shake hands and immediately begin planning a new work face to face.

title: Swan Lake (1952-09-08)
plotSynopsis: American tourist Richard Sims becomes enchanted by ballerina Tanya Graciana after seeing her dance in London, never realizing that the ordinary American woman who keeps crossing his path is Tanya herself under her real identity, Thelma Green. His attempts to meet the glamorous dancer lead to comic misunderstandings until Thelma reveals the truth. Richard admits that he has fallen in love with the same woman in both guises, and she tells him she has already fallen for him too.

title: Maestro (1952-09-15)
plotSynopsis: Conductor Felix Lambert and soloist Susan Galloway use music and a young boy's concern for his parents to demonstrate the value of working together. Their concert helps restore harmony in the boy's family, and the same lesson finally brings Felix and Susan to admit that they too belong together.

title: Golden Curtain (1952-09-22)
plotSynopsis: Metropolitan Opera chorus members Graham Jones and Diddy Cooper fall in love while Graham encourages Diddy's ambition to become a great singer. Believing her talent deserves more than the chorus, he sends her away to study, but Diddy later admits she never went to Boston and only staged the appearance of success and a European departure to make Graham miss her; the scheme finally gets him to confess that he loves her more than her career.

title: Annie Laurie (1952-09-29)
plotSynopsis: This fictionalized story of Robert Burns begins with the struggling Scottish farmer and poet in love with Jean Armour, whose father refuses to accept him as a husband. Convinced he has no future in Scotland, Burns plans to sail for America. Jean secretly carries his poems to a publisher, and their success makes Burns famous before he can leave. He eventually learns that the idealized 'Annie Laurie' of his romantic imagination is not a rival at all but a poetic dream, while Jean is the real woman who believed in him and saved his work. Burns chooses Jean as his own Annie Laurie.

title: Maytime (1952-10-06)
plotSynopsis: Dick and Ottilie fall in love in Washington Square, but Dick leaves to make his way in the world and returns too late: honoring her father's dying wish, Ottilie has married her cousin Claude. Dick eventually marries Alice, while Ottilie remains with Claude until his death and the loss of her home. Dick quietly buys the house back for her, and years later their grandchildren discover an old ring and matching keys and become sweethearts, giving the younger generation the springtime romance their grandparents could not share.

title: A Waltz Dream (1952-10-13)
plotSynopsis: Princess Helen enters an arranged marriage with Viennese Lieutenant Niki, who resents court life and longs for the music and women of Vienna. After seeing his fascination with a visiting ladies' orchestra, Helen secretly learns the art of Viennese flirtation and meets him masked as the sort of mysterious woman he thinks he wants; when she removes the mask, Niki discovers he has fallen for his own wife and the awkward royal marriage becomes a genuine romance.

title: Naughty Marietta (1952-10-20)
plotSynopsis: Marietta escapes an arranged European marriage and reaches colonial New Orleans among the casquette girls, where she meets Captain Dick Warrington and insists she wants a life of her own. Their romance is complicated by jealousy, a cruel slave auction and the search for a dangerous outlaw, but Dick's actions prove his character and the pair finally choose each other once Marietta's independence is secure.

title: The Gypsy Princess (1952-10-27)
plotSynopsis: Prince Ronald loves the celebrated singer Sylva, but his father refuses to accept a woman from the theater as a royal bride. Sylva later appears under a false marital arrangement that makes Ronald believe he has lost her. The deception collapses when Ronald's mother reveals that she herself was once a stage performer, making the king's objection impossible to maintain. With the family secret in the open, the king accepts Sylva and Ronald is free to marry the woman he loves.

title: Seventh Heaven (1952-11-03)
plotSynopsis: Paris sewer worker Chico protects the abused Diane and gives her a home in his seventh-floor garret, where their unlikely companionship becomes love. Called to war, they marry themselves before he leaves and promise to meet each evening in spirit under the same star; after four years Diane refuses to believe reports of his death, and her faith is rewarded when Chico returns home alive.

title: Dearest Enemy (1952-11-10)
plotSynopsis: During the Revolution, Betsy Murray distracts British officer Sir John Copeland at her family home while a signal lantern warns General Washington of the advancing redcoats. The deception helps the Americans win a crucial engagement but leaves Betsy in love with the enemy she fooled; after the war, Washington personally thanks her and reminds her that yesterday's enemies can become today's friends.

title: On Your Toes (1952-11-17)
plotSynopsis: Music professor Bill Dolan cannot suppress the dancing talent inherited from his vaudeville family and becomes involved with an ambitious ballet production of 'Slaughter on Tenth Avenue.' When jealous dancer Morrosine arranges to have him shot during the finale, Bill's friends uncover the plot, police seize the gunmen, and Bill survives to return to Frankie.

title: The Vagabond King (1952-11-24)
plotSynopsis: Poet and rogue Francois Villon is temporarily elevated by King Louis XI and given a chance to prove whether a vagabond can serve France better than the court. Villon rallies the people of Paris against the Duke of Burgundy, accepts the penalty attached to his bargain, and is saved when Lady Catherine declares her love for him.

title: Babes in Toyland (1952-12-01)
plotSynopsis: Alan and Contrary Mary are separated by the scheming Barnaby, forcing Mary to flee Toyland and invent a fictitious sweetheart to protect herself. They reunite in the Master Toymaker's shop when Alan poses as a wooden soldier; their love brings the toys to life in a Christmas march, and Mary finally agrees to marry him.

title: The Gypsy Baron (1952-12-08)
plotSynopsis: Returning heir Sandor Barinkay finds his estate in disorder and falls in love with Saffi, a young woman raised among the gypsies. The gypsies proclaim him their baron, and after Barinkay proves his courage in national service he is formally granted a hereditary barony, allowing him and Saffi to marry with their future secured.

title: Holiday Inn (1952-12-15)
plotSynopsis: Jim Hardy leaves show business to run a country inn that opens only on holidays and falls in love with singer Linda Mason. Dancer Ted Hanover and a Hollywood director lure Linda away to make a movie based on the inn, and Jim initially lets her go, but loneliness sends him to the film set; Linda chooses Jim over Hollywood, and the couple return to the real Holiday Inn determined to make every day together feel like Christmas.

title: Christmas Party (1952-12-22)
plotSynopsis: This special Railroad Hour Christmas party combines holiday songs and reflections with an extended musical retelling of The Nutcracker. Gordon MacRae and Dorothy Kirsten lead the celebration as poor Marie's broken nutcracker battles the Mouse King, becomes a prince and takes her to the Sugar Plum Fairy's magical toyland; the broadcast closes by turning from Christmas entertainment to a prayerful reminder of the holiday's religious meaning.

title: Review of 1952 (1952-12-29)
plotSynopsis: A year-end musical retrospective drawn from Railroad Hour broadcasts of 1952. Gordon MacRae and Dorothy Warenskjold revisit productions and composers featured during the season, including 'Kiss Me, Kate,' 'The Desert Song,' music by Rudolf Friml and songs from 'The Cat and the Fiddle,' before closing with a New Year's prayer and a look toward 1953.

title: My Romance (1953-01-05)
plotSynopsis: An elderly clergyman recalls the great romance of his youth with celebrated opera singer Cavallini, a love neither of them ultimately chose to turn into marriage. When his grandson Harry learns that Cavallini died unmarried, the story convinces him not to repeat the older generation's regret and he leaves at once to marry the woman he loves.

title: Two Hearts in Three-Quarter Time (1953-01-12)
plotSynopsis: Playboy composer Tony Hoeller needs a love song, so his producer plans to send an actress to put him in a romantic mood. The producer's daughter Hedy secretly takes her place, inspiring both a new waltz and Tony's first serious love; when he later forgets the melody, Hedy supplies it and reveals herself, and Tony promises to reform as he asks her to marry him.

title: Showboat (1953-01-19)
plotSynopsis: Magnolia, daughter of the showboat's captain, falls for gambler Gaylord Ravenal and leaves the riverboat to marry him. Gaylord's fortunes collapse and he abandons her out of shame; Magnolia builds a stage career with help from old friend Julie, then returns to the showboat, where Gaylord finally comes back and the couple are reunited.

title: The Merry Widow (1953-01-26)
plotSynopsis: The wealthy widow Sonia and Prince Danilo still love one another, but pride keeps each from admitting it while the Marsovian embassy worries that Sonia's fortune may leave the country if she marries a foreigner. Jealousy, diplomacy and repeated misunderstandings finally force Danilo to stop running from her, and the pair reconcile with their love and Sonia's fortune both remaining tied to Marsovia.

title: Carousel (1953-02-02)
plotSynopsis: Carousel barker Billy Bigelow marries Julie but becomes desperate about providing for the child they are expecting and joins a robbery that ends with his death. In the afterlife Billy is offered one day back on earth to do something worthwhile and learns that his daughter Louise is now nearly twelve and burdened by her father's reputation. His attempt to help her is clumsy, but he gives Louise the courage to stop measuring herself by other people's judgment and urges her to meet the world without fear. Julie senses Billy's presence, and the visit leaves mother and daughter stronger than before.

title: Miss Liberty (1953-02-09)
plotSynopsis: After getting fired over a useless photograph of the newly arrived Statue of Liberty, small-town photographer Horace Miller goes to Paris hoping to find the woman who modeled for it. He mistakes Monique for the model and turns her into a New York publicity sensation, only to learn the statue was sculpted years before she was born; the hoax collapses, but Horace and Monique discover their romance is real.

title: Blue Paradise (1953-02-16)
plotSynopsis: Young Rudy leaves Vienna, the Blue Paradise nightclub and flower girl Mitzi for a new life in America, promising that he will never forget either of them. Twenty-four years later he returns convinced that Vienna and his old love must still be waiting. His friends secretly recreate the vanished nightclub for one night, but Rudy eventually learns that Mitzi married his old friend Hampel and that the young woman who reminds him of her is their daughter Gaby. Accepting that he has been living in memory, Rudy chooses to celebrate the present and thanks his friends for giving him one more night in his Blue Paradise.

title: Bittersweet (1953-02-23)
plotSynopsis: Seventy-year-old Sarah tells a younger woman how, on the eve of an arranged marriage, she ran away with poor musician Carl Linden and built a life with him across Europe. Their happiness ends in Vienna when a cavalry officer insults Sarah and Carl is fatally wounded defending her. Sarah survives by devoting herself to Carl's music, singing his songs around the world until his work becomes known. Her bittersweet story convinces the young listener to follow her own heart rather than enter a loveless marriage.

title: Rose of Algeria (1953-03-02)
plotSynopsis: Captain Delorme is ordered into a political marriage with the Sultana of the Barricade but refuses because he loves Miriam, a woman he believes separate from the royal intrigue, and is jailed for defiance. The apparent conflict dissolves when he discovers that Miriam herself is the Sultana. Free to unite duty and love, Delorme accepts the marriage and claims Miriam as his 'rose of the world.'

title: Up in Central Park (1953-03-09)
plotSynopsis: Reporter John Matthews loves Rosie, a young singer whose career and engagement are controlled by Central Park political operator Arthur Peters. John investigates Peters and publishes evidence that he has embezzled $100,000 from the city treasury, shattering the powerful man's position and Rosie's planned marriage to him. Time passes while John and Rosie are apart, but Rosie eventually returns home. John is waiting for her, and the two reunite at the place where their story began.

title: Eileen (1953-03-16)
plotSynopsis: Irish rebel and smuggler Barry O'Day meets Eileen while posing as a groom and quickly falls in love with the spirited young woman. Colonel Lester's troops hunt Barry and Eileen helps conceal him, but the chase ends when a new governor issues a full pardon for those involved in the rebellion; with the price removed from his head, Barry is free to remain in Ireland and Eileen gives him her heart.

title: Lute Song (1953-03-23)
plotSynopsis: A Chinese scholar separated from his wife by famine rises at court and is drawn into an unwanted royal marriage while still searching for the woman he loves. When he finally finds his lost wife alive, the compassionate princess recognizes that his first vows are the true ones and releases him from his obligation, allowing the reunited couple to remain together.

title: The Princess Pat (1953-03-30)
plotSynopsis: Princess Pat is tired of her husband Toto admiring every pretty woman, while her friend Grace is being forced to marry wealthy Mr. Schmalt instead of the man she loves, Schmalt's son Tony. Pat solves both problems by flirting outrageously with the older millionaire; Toto's jealous challenge sends Schmalt fleeing and leaves Tony free to marry Grace, while Pat admits the flirtation was a lesson and Toto promises to reform.

title: Sally (1953-04-06)
plotSynopsis: Wealthy Blair Farquar falls for Sally, a dishwasher in a New York restaurant, while the deposed Grand Duke Constantine works nearby as a waiter. Constantine disguises Sally as the famous singer Madame Lucarova and takes her to Blair's society party, where the masquerade gives Sally her first chance to escape the dishpan and show her talent. Her deception eventually leads into a successful stage career. Blair finds her backstage and repeatedly proposes until Sally finally says yes, and he promises that after the wedding he will help with the dishes.

title: The Fortune Teller (1953-04-13)
plotSynopsis: A gypsy musician falls for a celebrated ballet dancer whose future is being arranged by people who value rank and advantage more than love. Disguises, fortune-telling and a return to the gypsy camp strip away the social roles surrounding them, and the dancer finally chooses the man and the freedom she really wants rather than the marriage others planned for her.

title: Mary (1953-05-04)
plotSynopsis: Mary loves an ambitious young man who leaves to prove himself by building homes in Kansas, while everyone around her assumes the long-distance romance will fade. His housing venture appears to fail spectacularly until digging on the property strikes oil; he comes home successful enough to ask Mary the question both have been waiting for, and the long-delayed romance becomes a marriage.

title: Irene (1953-05-25)
plotSynopsis: Irene, a working girl from Ninth Avenue, meets wealthy Donald Marshall and is recruited to wear expensive clothes in public so fashionable society will discover a struggling dress shop. The Cinderella-like experiment turns Irene into the toast of Fifth Avenue, while false genealogy and her borrowed elegance convince society that she belongs among them. Irene's mother finally arrives and exposes the masquerade, insisting that her daughter come home and shed the fine feathers. Donald makes clear that the revelation has not changed his feelings: he is willing to wait until Irene decides he is good enough for her, which Irene and her mother recognize as a proposal.

title: Quality Street (1953-06-01)
plotSynopsis: Phoebe Throssel expects Captain Brown to propose before he leaves for military service, but he departs without doing so and returns years later barely recognizing how much she has changed. Hurt, Phoebe invents a glamorous young niece named Miss Livvy and impersonates her, drawing Brown's admiration. Brown ultimately realizes Livvy is Phoebe in disguise and admits that what attracts him is the younger Phoebe he remembers; he helps retire the fictitious niece and asks Phoebe herself to marry him.

title: Dear Yesterday (1953-06-08)
plotSynopsis: In 1918, Ellen Martin slips a note and poem into a pair of socks meant for an unknown American soldier, but the package sits forgotten until it reaches serviceman Mark Anderson decades later during another war. Mark begins corresponding with the now-elderly Ellen without knowing her age; when he finally comes home, Ellen lets the younger Esther stand in for the girl of his imagination, and quietly watches the two young people find the happiness her delayed letter helped create.

title: Love Story (1953-06-15)
plotSynopsis: Poet Robert Browning falls in love with Elizabeth Barrett through her writing and begins a secret courtship in defiance of her controlling father. Robert convinces the frail Elizabeth that love and freedom are worth risking, and the couple marry privately and escape to Italy. There Elizabeth regains strength, writes beside Robert and shares a long marriage remembered through the poetry their love inspired.

title: New Wine (1953-06-22)
plotSynopsis: Struggling songwriter Richard is told to write waltzes but cannot find the right feeling until waitress Clarissa reveals her strange ability to summon composers from the past. Johann Strauss, Tchaikovsky and Emil Waldteufel guide Richard through their music and finally tell him that a true waltz needs love. Richard realizes Clarissa is the missing inspiration and asks her to help him discover that lesson for himself.

title: The Man Without a Country (1953-06-29)
plotSynopsis: Young Philip Nolan angrily declares that he never wants to hear of the United States again and is sentenced to spend his life aboard naval vessels without news of his country. Decades of exile turn defiance into aching patriotism; near death he has filled his cabin with a handmade flag and map, and when Nancy Montgomery tells him about the nation's growth he dies finally able to speak of home with love.

title: Penny Whistle (1953-07-06)
plotSynopsis: This musical biography follows the frail but imaginative Robert Louis Stevenson from a childhood shaped by illness into the writer whose stories and poems reach readers around the world. His life and marriage to Fanny carry him far from Scotland, eventually to Samoa, where his health finally fails. After Stevenson's death, local islanders carry him to his mountain resting place. Fanny then reads letters from children comforted by his writing, showing that the small 'penny whistle' of his art continues to sound long after he is gone.

title: The Rudolph Friml Story (1953-07-13)
plotSynopsis: This dramatized biography follows Rudolf Friml from a baker's family in Prague, where an unexpected piano awakens his talent, through conservatory training and his early ambitions as a composer. A youthful romance and the guidance of established musicians shape the melodies he later carries to America, where he is first known as a concert pianist and serious composer. A theatrical dispute unexpectedly gives him the chance to write for the stage, leading to successful operettas including The Firefly and later works remembered throughout the program. The tribute ends with Friml himself joining the broadcast and playing music from his newest Broadway work.

title: Starlight (1953-07-20)
plotSynopsis: Vaudeville partners Harry McKay and Helen Harris marry just as their old stage circuit begins to fade. While Harry stubbornly keeps touring, Helen secretly becomes a successful radio singer under another name; when Harry discovers her broadcast, she brings him into the studio and reunites their husband-and-wife act for the new medium.

title: The Golden Empress (1953-07-27)
plotSynopsis: Napoleon III persuades Archduke Maximilian and his wife Charlotte to accept a Mexican crown backed by French power and an 'election' arranged to guarantee the desired result. Maximilian grows attached to Mexico, but France withdraws its troops under political pressure and Charlotte's appeals for help fail; Maximilian is executed, while the widowed Charlotte survives for decades until, in failing memory, she imagines herself young again and reunited with her 'golden' emperor.

title: On Wings of Song (1953-08-03)
plotSynopsis: This biographical musical follows Felix Mendelssohn from the expectations of his distinguished family through courtship and marriage and the pressure to create work worthy of his name. Restless and exhausted despite early success, Felix searches for a grand new subject before realizing the inspiration is already at home in scripture; the story closes with his discovery of Elijah as a work that can join faith, family memory and music.

title: Trilby (1953-08-10)
plotSynopsis: Young painter Billy Bagot loves Trilby, a Paris laundry girl with little confidence in her voice, but hypnotist Svengali takes control of her and transforms her into a celebrated singer while cutting Billy out of her life. Years later Billy finds her performing under Svengali's name. Svengali dies in the orchestra pit and the trance collapses, leaving Trilby unable to remember her career or sing on command. Billy helps her recover her own voice with a song from their past and promises a love stronger than Svengali's control.

title: Roaring Camp (1953-08-17)
plotSynopsis: When a baby is born in rough Roaring Camp, the miners turn unexpectedly tender, contribute their prized belongings to his support and christen him Tommy, the 'Luck of Roaring Camp.' Elvira helps care for the child and the baby transforms the camp, but a devastating flood sweeps through the settlement and the Luck is lost. In the aftermath, the survivors accept grief and renewal, hoping life and love can continue beyond the destroyed camp.

title: Hope Is a Woman (1953-08-24)
plotSynopsis: Charles Lounsberry loves Hope Morton, but when her father asks whether he would still marry her if he had only thirty days to live, Charles hesitates and loses Hope's respect. Hope's father and a doctor then make Charles believe he really has only a month left; the supposed deadline teaches him what matters, inspires a generous 'will' of life's simple joys, and sends him back to Hope ready to choose her for thirty seconds or thirty million years. The ruse is revealed and Hope accepts him.

title: Lorna Doone (1953-08-31)
plotSynopsis: John Ridd loves Lorna, a young woman held among the outlaw Doones and claimed by the violent Carver Doone. When Lorna refuses Carver, the clan abandons her to starve and John crosses the dangerous country to rescue her. Carver confronts them and reveals that Lorna was kidnapped as a child and is not a Doone by blood, removing the family barrier between her and John. During their final struggle Carver loses his footing and plunges from a cliff. With the threat gone, Lorna promises to remain with John for the rest of her life.

title: Night Music (1953-09-07)
plotSynopsis: This original musical traces Henry Wadsworth Longfellow's love for Frances Appleton from their European courtship through marriage and family life in Cambridge, weaving his poems into the story. Their happiness ends when Frances's dress catches fire and she dies from her injuries; Longfellow grows old surrounded by the verses, children and memories they shared, hearing her presence in the night music of a life shaped by love and loss.

title: The Million Pound Bank Note (1953-09-14)
plotSynopsis: Penniless American Henry Adams becomes the subject of two wealthy brothers' wager when they lend him a million-pound bank note he cannot realistically cash. Simply displaying it gives him credit, status and business opportunities throughout London; after returning the note intact, Henry discovers that Portia Langham, the woman he loves, belongs to the household that started the experiment.

title: The Minstrel Boy (1953-09-21)
plotSynopsis: This musical biography follows Irish poet and songwriter Thomas Moore from his early struggle to publish traditional Irish melodies with new lyrics through fame, marriage to singer Bessie and decades of writing. Later Moore tries to create a grand scholarly history of Ireland, only to be crushed when critics find it lifeless compared with his songs. Bessie reminds him that his true gift is the music ordinary people can sing and understand. The story ends with Dubliners honoring Tom and Bessie in the streets while singing the Irish melodies that made him beloved.

title: Familiar Stranger (1953-09-28)
plotSynopsis: Graduate student Jean Myers travels to a mountain community to record supposedly untouched American folk music and believes she has discovered a gifted local singer named Obadiah Flumory. A casual autograph reveals that Obadiah is actually famous performer Davie Fields, home under his real identity to escape the loneliness of celebrity. Jean is angry at the deception but realizes she cared for the man and his music before knowing his fame, and their mutual attraction survives the revelation.

title: The Student Prince (1953-10-05)
plotSynopsis: Prince Karl Franz finds friendship and love with Kathy during his carefree student days at Heidelberg, but a royal death calls him home and makes him king. When he later returns, Kathy understands that his life now belongs to his people and that he is expected to marry Princess Margaret. To release him from their old promise, she tells Karl that she has chosen another man. He accepts the sacrifice, joins his old student companions for one final song and leaves Heidelberg to fulfill his royal duty.

title: The Firefly (1953-10-26)
plotSynopsis: New Yorker Jack Travers is engaged to wealthy Geraldine but cannot forget a mysterious street singer known as the Firefly. The singer follows him in disguise as cabin boy Tony, is eventually exposed as Giannina, and after Jack breaks with Geraldine the two choose each other and head home together as a pair of street singers.

title: Rosalinda (1953-11-02)
plotSynopsis: A married couple enter Prince Orlofsky's party in disguises and end up testing their own marriage without realizing it. The husband eagerly flirts with a mysterious countess, complaining about his supposedly dull and possessive wife, unaware that the woman behind the mask is that very wife. She lets him incriminate himself before revealing her identity. Caught proposing a future with the 'countess' after divorcing her foolish husband, he can only surrender to the joke, and the pair reconcile by showing the party how much in love two married people can still be.

title: Roberta (1953-11-09)
plotSynopsis: John Kent comes to Paris after his aunt, Madame Roberta, draws him into her famous fashion house. He and Roberta's assistant Stephanie grow close while John's attachment to another woman keeps him from recognizing what he wants. After Roberta's death leaves the future of the salon in their hands, John asks Stephanie to remain as his partner. He admits that the other romance is over, and Stephanie quickly turns the business partnership into the personal future both of them have wanted.

title: The Merry Widow (1953-11-16)
plotSynopsis: The wealthy widow Sonia and Prince Danilo still love one another, but pride keeps each from admitting it while the Marsovian embassy worries that Sonia's fortune may leave the country if she marries a foreigner. Jealousy, diplomacy and repeated misunderstandings finally force Danilo to stop running from her, and the pair reconcile with their love and Sonia's fortune both remaining tied to Marsovia.

title: The Chocolate Soldier (1953-11-23)
plotSynopsis: Nadina dreams of heroic romance and is engaged to the boastful soldier Alexius, but during wartime she hides Swiss officer Bumerli, a practical fugitive who carries chocolates instead of bullets and refuses to pretend that battle is glorious. When Bumerli later returns, the household's romantic posturing collapses and Nadina recognizes the difference between theatrical heroism and the man she actually loves. Bumerli reveals that he is the son of a wealthy Swiss hotel owner and asks for Nadina, who finally embraces her unlikely 'chocolate soldier' as her true hero.

title: State Fair (1953-11-30)
plotSynopsis: An Iowa farm family goes to the state fair with prize hog Blue Boy and high hopes for contests, rides and romance. Daughter Margie meets reporter Pat Gilbert and falls for him during the fair, only to think he has forgotten her when he leaves for a Chicago job; back home, Pat unexpectedly returns and proposes, turning the fairground romance into a future together.

title: Sweethearts (1953-12-07)
plotSynopsis: Franz, crown prince of Zelenia, falls in love with laundry worker Sylvia, who turns him down after learning his true rank because she believes a common girl cannot marry a prince. A family secret then reveals that Sylvia was adopted and is herself the missing heir to Zelenia's throne. With the difference in rank erased, Sylvia and Franz plan to restore the monarchy together and decide there is no reason to wait for their coronation before marrying.

title: Snow White (1953-12-21)
plotSynopsis: Snow White escapes the jealous queen and finds refuge with the seven dwarfs, but the queen disguises herself and tricks her into biting a poisoned apple. The dwarfs chase the witch through a storm until she falls from a cliff, yet they believe they are too late to save Snow White and place her in a glass-and-gold resting place. The prince who has searched for her arrives and wakes her with a kiss. Snow White says farewell to the dwarfs and rides with him toward his castle and the fairy-tale ending she had wished for.

title: Snow White (AFRS) (1953-12-21)
plotSynopsis: In this Armed Forces Radio version of Snow White, the jealous Queen tricks the princess with a poisoned apple after Snow White has found a home with the Seven Dwarfs. The dwarfs drive the disguised Queen to her death, and the prince's kiss awakens Snow White so she can leave with him for a happily-ever-after ending.

title: Review of 1953 (1953-12-28)
plotSynopsis: A farewell-to-1953 edition built from musical highlights of the Railroad Hour's own season. Gordon MacRae and Dorothy Kirsten revisit shows including 'Miss Liberty' and 'Mary,' salute composers heard during the year and recall earlier broadcast moments, then end with holiday wishes, a New Year's message and a look ahead to the first program of 1954.

title: The Girl from Utah (1954-01-18)
plotSynopsis: British musical-comedy star Sandy Blair meets a mysterious young woman on a Channel boat, falls for her and is relieved when he decides that 'the girl from Utah' cannot possibly be American. At rehearsal he discovers both that Utah is in the United States and that the woman is his new American leading lady; wounded pride drives them apart until she follows him toward France and they admit the joke matters less than their love.

title: Music in the Air (1954-01-25)
plotSynopsis: In the Bavarian village of Edendorf, shy schoolteacher Carl loves Sieglinde while helping her father, the village schoolmaster, bring a new song to life. A trip to Munich offers Sieglinde a chance at the musical stage, but producer Mahler concludes that talent alone cannot replace years of theatrical experience; she returns home with Carl, where they discover the schoolmaster's music and Carl's words have been published, giving the couple a happier future away from the city spotlight.

title: The Schumann Story (1954-02-08)
plotSynopsis: This musical biography follows composer Robert Schumann and pianist Clara Wieck as their friendship and shared music grow into love. Clara's father, Friedrich Wieck, opposes Robert and refuses permission for the marriage, forcing the couple to seek relief from the courts. The judge rules that Clara is free to choose her own husband, ending her father's legal obstruction. Robert and Clara marry at last, joining the two musical lives that Wieck had tried to keep apart.

title: Through the Years (1954-02-15)
plotSynopsis: John Carter has spent decades nursing bitterness against the Wayne family, even forbidding his niece Kathleen to love Kenneth Wayne. When Kenneth returns from war wounded and tries to give Kathleen up, John finally rejects the old feud and urges the young couple to marry. Alone afterward in the garden where his own wife died, John understands that hatred had kept him from the love and memory that were with him all along.

title: Martha (1954-02-22)
plotSynopsis: Lady Harriet disguises herself as a servant named Martha for a visit to Richmond Fair and discovers too late that the joke has legally bound her to work for farmer Lionel. Lionel falls sincerely in love with Martha, while Harriet eventually flees and returns to her aristocratic life. When Lionel later recognizes Lady Harriet as the servant who deceived him, he feels betrayed. Harriet recreates the Richmond Fair at her castle to show him that the woman he loved still exists beneath the title, and Lionel chooses Harriet and Martha as 'two brides in one.'

title: The Great Waltz (1954-03-01)
plotSynopsis: Young Johann Strauss wants to compose and conduct despite the opposition of his famous father, who expects him to choose a safer profession. When the elder Strauss is delayed, Johann gets an unexpected chance to conduct and proves himself with the music that will make him famous, including the Blue Danube. Father and son finally reconcile, with the elder Strauss acknowledging the younger man's gift shortly before his death and Johann accepting the musical inheritance he once had to fight for.

title: The Red Mill (1954-03-08)
plotSynopsis: Two broke Americans wandering through Holland become involved when Gretchen is being pushed into an unwanted marriage. After hiding her at the supposedly haunted Red Mill, they disguise themselves as Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson and accept her father's fee to find her, using the ridiculous investigation to upset the wedding plans; Gretchen gains the man she loves and the reward also helps the rescuers solve their own romantic problem.

title: Irene (1954-03-22)
plotSynopsis: Working-class Irene becomes the toast of New York society after being dressed and promoted as a fashionable young woman, while two men compete for her affection and one pays a genealogist to manufacture an aristocratic family tree. Irene's blunt Irish mother arrives and destroys the pretense, causing the snobbish suitor to withdraw. Donald Marshall values Irene rather than her pedigree and asks her to marry him, giving the Cinderella game a genuine ending.

title: The Three Musketeers (1954-03-29)
plotSynopsis: Young D'Artagnan arrives in Paris and quickly joins forces with Athos, Porthos and Aramis, whose loyalty is pledged to France and the king. When Cardinal Richelieu obtains compromising letters that endanger the queen, D'Artagnan and the musketeers help Constance defeat the plot and protect her mistress; the king rewards D'Artagnan's service by naming him a musketeer, while he and Constance declare their devotion to one another.

title: Great Day (1954-04-05)
plotSynopsis: Engineer Jim Brin comes to the Mississippi country as a dangerous flood threatens the plantations and gradually falls in love with Emily Lou of Judson Point. Her family property is bankrupt and scheduled for public auction just as Jim's work helps the levees survive the flood. Grateful landowners offer him any reward he wants, but Jim asks only that the auction be called immediately so he can buy Judson Point himself. He gives the recovered plantation to Emily Lou as a wedding present.

title: Babes in Toyland (1954-04-12)
plotSynopsis: Wicked Uncle Barnaby schemes against Alan and Jane and tries to force Mary into his own plans. To escape him, Mary invents an imaginary Irish sweetheart, which unfortunately convinces Alan that she loves someone else when he returns. In Toyland Alan hides among the toys, learns that the rival never existed and reveals himself. The toys spring to life as a sign of true love, and Mary accepts Alan's proposal.

title: Smiles (1954-04-19)
plotSynopsis: Long Island millionaire Bob Hastings has been waiting for the right girl without realizing that Smiles is already the person he wants. Smiles nearly marries Dick, but Dick sees that her heart belongs to Bob and steps aside; she returns to Bob, admits that his patience mattered, and chooses to spend their honeymoon and their life together at home.

title: Birthday (1954-05-03)
plotSynopsis: Jeff Smith is determined to treat the day his wife Betty is due to give birth as an ordinary working day, even insisting they save money on flowers and that he return to the office rather than wait at the hospital. When complications develop, his practiced calm collapses and he turns to prayer while waiting for news. Betty recovers and delivers a healthy son, and Jeff abandons the idea that the day can be ordinary, bringing roses and celebrating the baby's birthday with Betty.

title: The Wonderful One-Hoss Shay (1954-05-10)
plotSynopsis: Across generations, a New England family boasts of the 'perfect' one-hoss shay built so every piece is exactly as strong as every other. A young minister inherits both the carriage and the family's faith in perfection, even letting that attitude interfere with his courtship of Nell; on the shay's hundredth birthday every part gives way at once, humbling him and teaching that neither machines nor people can be made flawless before he returns to Nell with a more modest outlook.

title: Penny Whistle (1954-05-24)
plotSynopsis: This musical biography follows Robert Louis Stevenson and his wife Fanny through his fragile health, restless travels and determination to write. Stevenson sometimes fears his poems and stories are only a small penny whistle beside the great works of others, but after his death Fanny's letters from children show how his writing became a lasting source of courage and imagination.

title: Homecoming (1954-05-31)
plotSynopsis: Sailor Enoch Arden leaves his wife Annie and their children for a long voyage meant to secure the family's future, but a wreck strands him far from home for years. Annie waits until hope is almost gone, then eventually marries their devoted friend Philip. When Enoch finally returns, he sees Annie happy with Philip and their new child and chooses not to destroy that peace. Dying in obscurity, he reveals himself to Miriam and asks that Annie be told only after his death, but Annie reaches him in time for a final farewell and his blessing on her new life.

title: Rosalie (1954-06-07)
plotSynopsis: American flyer Lieutenant Dick Fay makes a record-setting flight to the kingdom of Romanza and falls for Princess Rosalie. When the royal family later visits West Point, the pair admit they have loved each other since meeting in Paris, but Rosalie's duty to the throne blocks their marriage until her father abdicates, freeing her to marry Dick and turning the royal romance into a decidedly American happy ending.

title: The Pink Lady (1954-06-14)
plotSynopsis: Just before his wedding, Parisian Lucien's attempt at one last flirtation becomes a maze of false identities, jealous fiancées and the mysterious Pink Lady. His increasingly impossible explanations make matters worse until his bride realizes that his terrible lying actually reveals where his heart is, and the tangled party ends with the engaged couple reconciled.

title: Railroad Hour Series Synopsis
plotSynopsis: This short background feature explains The Railroad Hour as an Association of American Railroads-sponsored NBC series built around highly condensed versions of musicals and operettas. It describes Gordon MacRae's regular romantic lead role, recurring guest singers from film and opera, the Norman Luboff choir and Carmen Dragon's orchestra, and notes that experienced radio writers including Jean Holloway, Jerome Lawrence and Robert E. Lee adapted the stage works for broadcast.

title: Gordon Mac Rae Bio
plotSynopsis: A short standalone narrated biography of Gordon MacRae rather than a Railroad Hour episode. It follows MacRae from his 1921 birth and early music work through military service, Broadway, Capitol Records, The Railroad Hour, Warner Bros. films, 'Oklahoma!' and 'Carousel,' then discusses his alcoholism and recovery, later health problems and his death in 1986; the recording credits its biographical text to material edited from the Internet Movie Database.

title: Policemen (First Show for Raleigh, NBC) (1941-10-07)
plotSynopsis: Skelton's first Raleigh-sponsored NBC show features Ozzie Nelson and Harriet Hilliard, police comedy and a peculiar mock murder investigation.

title: R) Law Enforcement (Rehearsal) (1941-10-07)
plotSynopsis: This rehearsal moves rapidly through jokes about daily life and celebrity into sketches populated by inept police officers.

title: R) Husbands (Rehearsal) (1941-10-14)
plotSynopsis: This rehearsal explores married life through sketches about nagging spouses, honeymoon troubles and other domestic aggravations.

title: R) Department Stores (Rehearsal) (1941-10-21)
plotSynopsis: This rehearsal spoofs department-store shoppers and culminates in a memorable comic visit to an asylum.

title: New House (1941-10-28)
plotSynopsis: Red jokes about the oddities of his new home before the cast presents several comic variations on saying goodnight to a sweetheart.

title: R) New House (Rehearsal) (1941-10-28)
plotSynopsis: House-building problems, awkward romantic farewells and a visit with an overenthusiastic girlfriend's family make up this rehearsal's sketches.
