title: The Shadow 1954-06-27 (737) The Vengeance of Angela Nolan
plotSynopsis: The sister of an executed criminal frames The Shadow for murder as part of her campaign of revenge.

title: Audition Show (1953-07-15)
plotSynopsis: In this audition version of the Six Shooter story, a young masked robber steals money and shoots a man during his escape. The trail, the robber's age, and a distinctive horseshoe mark increasingly point toward Sheriff Ed's own son Ben, who has recently argued with his father over gambling debts. Ed continues the pursuit even as he struggles to believe his boy could have become a killer overnight. Britt corners the wounded fugitive at an isolated cabin and survives a gunfight; when the robber is finally seen clearly, he is not Ben, vindicating Ed's faith in his son.

title: Jenny (1953-09-20)
plotSynopsis: Britt carries a wounded stranger to the isolated cabin of Jenny Garver, a lonely woman who has spent years being mocked for her appearance and awkwardness. The man proves to be a wanted killer, but Jenny refuses to give him up because, for the first time, someone seems to need her; when the sheriff's posse surrounds the cabin, she even fires to protect him. The fugitive finally dies from his wounds, ending the standoff. Afterward the town notices that Jenny carries herself with a new confidence, as though the brief experience of being needed has changed the way she sees herself.

title: The Coward (1953-09-27)
plotSynopsis: Britt discovers that a man wanted in Texas for his old life as a gun-toting bank robber has become a quiet rancher and promised his wife never to use a gun again. A neighboring rancher named Temple tries to force them off their land by sabotaging fences, killing cattle, and mocking Will as a coward. Will finally goes after Temple with a rifle but cannot break his promise and pull the trigger; instead he defeats Temple in a brutal fistfight. Seeing how completely the former outlaw has changed, Britt decides the law looking for a gunman has little reason to be interested in the rancher Will has become.

title: The Stampede (1953-10-04)
plotSynopsis: On a cattle drive Britt rides with an older rancher and the man's younger brother Norm, whose inexperience has already created tension between them. The older brother finds an old love letter from his wife Carrie to Norm and assumes the two have betrayed him, then tries to kill Norm by deliberately setting off the herd in a narrow gorge. Norm risks his own life to save the brother who meant to kill him. As the older man lies mortally injured, Norm explains that Carrie's letter was written before she ever met her husband and that she had never loved Norm after the marriage; the brothers reconcile before the older man dies, and Norm helps Britt finish the drive.

title: Silver Annie (1953-10-11)
plotSynopsis: Virtue City is dying, and railroad men need a right-of-way through the old Huxley mine, but stubborn Annie Huxley refuses to give up property she still believes contains silver. Her relatives use her behavior and a shooting incident to try to have her declared incompetent. Britt has ore from the mine assayed and produces a rich result at the hearing, making Annie's belief look reasonable enough to stop the commitment. Annie privately reveals that Britt used old ore from the mine's original strike, but the excitement sends prospectors back into the district and soon leads to a genuine new silver discovery.

title: Rink Larkin (1953-10-18)
plotSynopsis: Eleven-year-old Rink Larkin runs away after his outlaw father is killed by the sheriff, convinced the lawman murdered the only man who had ever been good to him. Rink steals a revolver and lays an obvious trail, intending to lure the sheriff out and take revenge. Britt follows, hoping to stop the boy before grief turns him into his father, and a confrontation with another armed fugitive forces Rink to hear what really happened. When the gunman threatens Britt and the sheriff, Rink shoots him and finally abandons his revenge, later beginning to miss the aunt he had run away from.

title: Red Lawson's Revenge (1953-10-25)
plotSynopsis: Red Lawson tracks down Britt's friend Dan to avenge a brother Dan killed years earlier during an outlaw ambush. Lawson does not want a fair gunfight; he wants Dan terrified and eventually invades the family farm, using Dan and Mary's baby as leverage. Britt and Dan have almost no opening to act until Mary quietly gets to a rifle. As Britt draws Lawson's attention, Mary shoots the killer to save her child, proving that the gentle woman Dan tried to shield is capable of protecting her family herself.

title: Ben Scofield (1953-11-01)
plotSynopsis: A masked young robber steals a large sum and shoots a man during the escape, and Britt joins Sheriff Ed Scofield in following the trail. The tracks and the robber's age increasingly point toward Ed's own son Ben, who had recently lost money gambling, forcing the sheriff to continue the hunt even while insisting his boy could not have changed into a killer overnight. Britt corners the wounded fugitive at an isolated cabin and survives a shootout. When the prisoner is finally seen clearly, he is not Ben, confirming Ed's faith in his son.

title: The Capture of Stacy Gault (1953-11-08)
plotSynopsis: El Point panics when outlaw Stacy Gault is reported nearby, and a newly arrived stranger seems to fit every detail: he resembles the wanted poster, carries yellow gloves, and has a satchel full of money wrapped in bands from the robbed White River bank. Britt prevents the frightened townsmen from simply shooting him and insists that the man be taken alive. The supposed outlaw is actually traveling salesman Amos Foster, who accidentally captured Gault when the criminal mistook one of Amos's realistic toy six-shooters for a real gun. A letter from the marshal and the reward money in Amos's satchel finally prove the truth, leaving the would-be posse badly embarrassed.

title: Escape from Smoke Falls (1953-11-15)
plotSynopsis: When outlaw Falk shoots the Smoke Falls sheriff and escapes, Britt is asked to pursue him with only one local rider. He chooses the quiet Tom Lebrit over boastful Spud Hooker because Tom knows there is more to manhunting than fast shooting, while Spud races after Falk alone. Falk captures Spud and tries to use him as a human shield at a cave, but Tom tackles Spud out of the line of fire and is wounded as Britt brings Falk down. Tom admits he risked himself because Ellen, the girl both men care for, loves Spud.

title: Gabriel Starbuck (1953-11-22)
plotSynopsis: The people of Yellow Crest quietly decide that aging Sheriff Gabriel Starbuck is no longer capable of protecting the growing town, but Britt cannot bring himself to tell his old friend that they want him replaced. Gabe senses what is happening and secretly takes the bank's money sacks, then rides onto the salt flats and stages the sounds and tracks of a spectacular gun battle with imaginary robbers. Britt witnesses the deception but supports Gabe's story when the townspeople arrive. The town keeps Gabe as sheriff, raises money for a deputy, and Gabe promises Britt that future trouble will be shared with the younger man.

title: Sheriff Billy (1953-11-29)
plotSynopsis: New young sheriff Billy Riddle astonishes Dawson by arresting notorious gunman Ben Reed without even drawing. Britt later learns why Reed surrendered so quietly: before becoming an outlaw he was Blake Riddle, Billy's estranged father, who abandoned his old identity after his wife left with their son. Billy does not initially know the truth, but Reed cannot bring himself to fight the boy who has grown into the lawman confronting him. He allows Billy to deliver him to the marshal and, contrary to everyone's expectations, makes no attempt to escape.

title: A Pressing Engagement (1953-12-06)
plotSynopsis: Minnie spreads a false newspaper announcement that Britt and Helen are engaged, hoping jealousy will finally force Helen's longtime beau Clint to propose. Britt is furious at being used as bait, but the scheme quickly traps him in a public courtship he never intended. When Clint finally admits that he has always loved Helen, she confesses that she feels the same way and chooses him over the invented engagement. Britt stays for the wedding and serves as best man, though he realizes the joke will give Helen leverage over Clint for years.

title: More Than Kin (1953-12-13)
plotSynopsis: Britt becomes involved with a struggling theatrical troupe just as they learn P. T. Barnum is in town and plans to see their performance. Determined not to lose the opportunity, the actors hurriedly revive their canceled show, and a last-minute cast problem presses Britt into a role in Hamlet despite his complete lack of stage experience. His armed, imposing presence unexpectedly quiets the audience and helps the performance succeed. Barnum praises the troupe and even offers Britt a theatrical future, but Britt decides that facing an audience is more frightening than gunplay.

title: Britt Ponsett's Christmas Carol (1953-12-20)
plotSynopsis: On Christmas Eve Britt meets a runaway boy who insists that Christmas is only for children and that he wants nothing to do with it. To keep him company, Britt retells A Christmas Carol as a Western tale about wealthy miser Evan, whose dead partner and a succession of visions force him to confront the lonely life his greed has created and inspire him to become generous. The story, along with a little discreet gift-giving by Britt, helps the boy reconsider the gruff relative caring for him and turn back toward home. Britt leaves the pair with presents and a renewed chance to celebrate Christmas together.

title: Cora Plummer Quincy (1953-12-27)
plotSynopsis: When Cora Plummer Quincy is wounded by her new husband Oliver's gun, her son Cal becomes suspicious, especially after learning that Oliver does not own the prosperous ranch Cora claimed he had. Britt and Doc Early discover that the apparent deception is Cora's, not Oliver's: after her first husband Ned died, she wanted companionship but feared people would think Oliver had married a wealthy widow for her money, so she invented a fortune for him. The shooting proves accidental, Cal accepts the marriage, and Oliver eventually makes himself an able partner in running the Plummer ranch.

title: A Friend in Need (1954-01-03)
plotSynopsis: Britt encounters his old friend Art Hamper, a fugitive accused of murdering Clyde, the foster brother he had once considered as close as blood. Art insists he was framed by circumstances surrounding their inheritance, and Britt initially believes him enough to help arrange a surrender. The sheriff's evidence shows that Art's story is a lie, but Britt still gives him a chance to come in peacefully. Art instead tries to use Britt to escape and fires on him, only to be fatally shot by a lawman; dying, he apologizes for lying to the friend he betrayed.

title: Hiram's Gold Strike (1954-01-10)
plotSynopsis: Old prospector Hiram brings another set of ore samples to the assayer, and this time several look promising enough to justify more tests. Before the assay can be settled, two robbers invade the office; Hiram resists and is badly shot while Britt brings the gunmen down. With Hiram losing the will to live, friends encourage him with the prospect that he has finally struck gold, and even his suspicion that they may be humoring him restores his determination to recover and prove himself. By the time he is well, the excitement around his claim has become a genuine gold rush and Hiram finally has more money than he knows what to do with.

title: The Silver Buckle (1954-01-17)
plotSynopsis: Two train robbers kill passenger Carl Davis after mistaking the silver-colored buckle on his anniversary belt for real silver. Later Britt meets brothers Kit and Lex Springer, who claim to be posse members hunting the bandits for a reward and ask him to guide them through Miller Pass. A bloodstain on Kit's fancy belt and other inconsistencies make Britt suspicious, and he overhears the brothers admit they are the robbers before they try to kill him. Britt survives the ambush long enough for the real posse to arrive; during Kit's attempted escape, his horse goes over the trail edge and the stolen belt catches on the saddle, leaving him fatally trapped by the very buckle that marked the crime.

title: Helen Bricker (1954-01-24)
plotSynopsis: Helen Bricker returns to Yellow Crest after years with outlaw Billy Stark and finds that even her father still judges her for choosing him. Britt learns that Helen had stayed with Billy largely out of pride after ignoring her father's warnings, even while she came to hate what he had become. The final secret is that Helen herself tipped the law to Billy's whereabouts, bringing about his capture, but she refuses to use that fact to win back anyone's approval. Britt respects her wish to keep the truth private and leaves Helen to rebuild her life on her own terms.

title: Trail to Sunset (1954-01-31)
plotSynopsis: Britt finds a badly wounded outlaw, Trussler, after the man tries to steal Scar on a snowy trail. Trussler admits that he, not George Revit, killed Sam Fletcher, exposing the fact that a Sunset posse recently lynched the wrong man. When Britt confronts the posse with the truth, some of the men want to hide what happened and even threaten Britt, but others finally accept that they must return to town and admit their part in Revit's death.

title: Apron Faced Sorrel (1954-02-07)
plotSynopsis: Sixteen-year-old Clay Fenton arrives for a summer on a ranch determined to hide his terror of horses, a fear dating from the accident that killed his father and scarred Clay when he was a small child. After being mocked and thrown by a difficult apron-faced sorrel, Clay secretly whips the horse nearly to death and runs away when the animal's reaction exposes what he did. Britt catches him and learns that Clay's cruelty grew out of fear. When Britt's horse Scar later saves Clay from a rattlesnake, Clay's attitude begins to change, and caring for the injured sorrel eventually turns fear and hatred into trust.

title: Quiet City (1954-02-14)
plotSynopsis: When Britt returns to Quiet City, he finds a once-violent frontier town growing into a settled community but its old sheriff still expects the people to behave as they did years before. After Pike kills rancher Jason Norton in a cattle dispute, Britt helps the sheriff capture him alive, while the sheriff worries that Jason's brother and an angry crowd will lynch the prisoner. Instead the townspeople insist that Pike receive a fair trial and let the courts punish him. Britt points out that Quiet City has grown up largely because its sheriff spent years teaching people to respect the law.

title: Battle at Tower Rock (1954-02-21)
plotSynopsis: Britt arrives in Tower Rock for the county fair and is maneuvered into judging a strawberry-preserve contest at the center of a bitter feud between Selma Bingham and Bessie Madden, a quarrel that has divided their husbands and much of the town. Rather than declare either woman the winner and deepen the fight, Britt awards the blue ribbon to preserves he ate at Gravy Gibson's lunchroom. Selma, Bessie, and their husbands instantly unite in outrage at Britt and walk off together, effectively ending their feud. Britt privately admits that Gravy's coffee had burned his tongue so badly he could hardly taste the entries anyway.

title: Cheyenne Express (1954-03-07)
plotSynopsis: Former gang member Wilbur English has shot outlaw Floyd Winters in the back and now lives in terror that Floyd's brother Russ will kill him in revenge. Britt escorts the increasingly panicked English to Single Pine, where he ignores advice to wait for the sheriff and boards the Cheyenne Express to escape. Unknown to him, the sheriff's posse is chasing Russ, who boards the same train farther down the line. The moment English sees him he runs through the cars and plunges from the rear platform to his death, even though witnesses say Russ never made a move toward him.

title: Thicker Than Water (1954-03-14)
plotSynopsis: Britt meets wandering gambler Gus Proctor, who is returning after years away to a family he barely knows, only to learn that his wife Janet has died and their son Ted is being raised by Janet's sister Amy. Ted quickly idolizes the glamorous father he had been told was dead and decides to run away with Gus and become a gambler himself. Realizing what his example is doing, Gus deliberately lets himself be exposed as a poker cheat so the boy will reject that life and stay with Amy. Ted abandons the plan to run away, while Amy later marries the dependable Fred Baker, who becomes a steady father figure to him.

title: Duel at Lockwood (1954-03-21)
plotSynopsis: Gunfighter Wes Singer comes to Lockwood looking for a showdown with Britt, but young Sheriff Ben insists that stopping the trouble is his responsibility even if Wes is really after someone else. Britt refuses to let the sheriff be sacrificed simply to protect his own reputation. He finally confronts Wes at close range with a shotgun, explaining that Wes can fire first if he wants but cannot prevent Britt's blast from killing him in return. Faced for once with a duel in which surviving the first shot will not save him, Wes backs down and leaves Lockwood.

title: Aunt Emma (1954-04-01)
plotSynopsis: After her husband dies and her children leave home, Britt's Aunt Emma comes to Powder Creek convinced that both she and her wandering nephew need a household to run. Britt tries to adapt to domestic life but quickly realizes he is miserable being fussed over and cannot abandon the range. Local storekeeper Ethan is fond of Emma but stays back because he thinks she is sacrificing herself for Britt, so Britt announces he is leaving and pushes Ethan to propose. Emma accepts, revealing that she had already recognized Britt could never be domesticated and that Ethan is exactly the sort of man who enjoys being looked after.

title: General Guilford's Widow (1954-04-08)
plotSynopsis: Britt becomes lost near Minton and meets Hannah Guilford, widow of celebrated General William Guilford, who insists that her husband is still alive despite the monument honoring his death with his regiment five years earlier. Britt discovers that the general really has been hiding in the house: illness had taken him away from his command just before a Cheyenne attack wiped out his men, and when he returned home to find himself praised as a dead hero he was too afraid of a court-martial or accusations of desertion to reveal the truth. Hannah has sacrificed five years protecting the secret, but finally refuses to continue when Guilford threatens Britt rather than face the consequences. The general dies moments later, and a fire destroys the house with his body inside; Britt allows the public to keep its heroic version of Guilford's death while Hannah is finally able to begin a new life.

title: Crisis at Easter Creek (1954-04-15)
plotSynopsis: When Easter Creek's worn-out organ finally fails, Britt is pressured into raising the remaining money for a replacement. Ordinary townspeople have already given what they can, so Britt recruits reputed gunman Red Eye Kirk to accompany him among the rough characters living east of the creek, whose suddenly generous donations quickly cover the cost. The congregation hesitates to accept money associated with suspected outlaws, but Britt points out that the sheriff officially insists those men are law-abiding citizens. The organ is bought, and Red Eye and several of his friends even attend the Easter service to see how their contributions were used.

title: Johnny Springer (1954-04-22)
plotSynopsis: After a hotelkeeper is shot, Britt and the sheriff follow the trail of a notorious fugitive to a young woman named Maria, who has been hiding a man she knows under an alias and expects to marry. The lawmen reveal that her guest is the wanted gunman, already married and accustomed to using women to help him escape. When he turns a gun on Britt and the sheriff, Maria accepts that she has been deceived and kills him with a knife. Britt later argues that her act may have saved their lives, and she appears to come through the legal aftermath safely.

title: Johnny Stringer (1954-04-22)
plotSynopsis: After a hotelkeeper is shot, Britt and the sheriff follow the trail of notorious gunman Johnny Stringer to a young woman named Maria, who has been hiding a man she knows under an alias and expects to marry. The lawmen reveal that her guest is Stringer, already married and accustomed to using women to help him escape. When Stringer turns a gun on Britt and the sheriff, Maria accepts that she has been deceived and kills him with a knife. Britt later argues that her act may have saved their lives, and she appears to come through the legal aftermath safely.

title: Revenge at Harness Creek (1954-04-29)
plotSynopsis: After young Lex Harcourt is killed by Adam Robey, Lex's brother, Sheriff Cash Harcourt, becomes determined to settle the matter with vengeance rather than a trial. Robey claims Lex drew first and agrees to surrender only if Britt will deliver him to the district marshal at Standish Falls. Cash catches them on the trail and prepares to kill Robey, but Britt stands unarmed between the two men and makes Cash face the fact that revenge would require murdering a friend as well. Cash cannot pull the trigger and gives up his gun, allowing Britt to take Robey in for a lawful trial.

title: Anna Norquist (1954-05-06)
plotSynopsis: Anna Norquist comes from Sweden to marry Pete after two years of courtship by letter, only to find him convicted of murdering Seth Quincy during a robbery. Pete continues to protest his innocence, and Anna's faith in him turns into bitter distrust of the American justice system. Britt finds Pete's hidden, recently fired gun and persuades him to stop letting Anna believe an innocent man is being condemned. Pete finally confesses that he tried to rob Quincy for money to start married life with Anna and shot him when he was caught. After learning the truth, Anna remains in Smoke Falls and begins a new life there.

title: The Double Seven (1954-05-13)
plotSynopsis: Expansion of the Double Seven has brought rancher Git Baskin into a bitter dispute with neighboring homesteaders, and Baskin makes matters worse by hiring gunman Clint Sutton after cattle begin disappearing. Britt discovers that one of the farmers, Ruth, has deliberately been stealing cattle and stirring up violence because he wants Baskin to burn the settlers out. Years earlier another large rancher destroyed Ruth's Texas farm and his wife Nancy died in the fire, leaving him obsessed with recreating the conflict and taking revenge on any rancher who resembles his old enemy. Britt stops the plot, while Baskin agrees to drop the cattle grievance and get rid of Sutton.

title: The Shooting of Wyatt King (1954-05-20)
plotSynopsis: After robbing the Copper Springs bank, outlaw Wyatt King is found badly wounded and insists that Britt was the man who outdrew him. Britt has never met King, but Wyatt privately admits that he would rather lose to the famous Six Shooter than confess that an ordinary gray-haired bank teller shot him while defending a horse. Britt identifies teller Jonas Pilgrim as the real gunman, though Jonas is equally eager to avoid the story because of his domineering wife's rules. When Wyatt later escapes and Britt returns him to jail, Britt arranges for Jonas to be sitting watch when the posse comes back, leaving the town convinced that the unassuming teller single-handedly recaptured the outlaw.

title: Blood Relations (1954-05-27)
plotSynopsis: Britt returns to the Wilcox ranch to help George Wilcox with a cattle drive and finds George determined to stop his sister Viola from marrying Hunt Coffin simply because Hunt's brother was a criminal. George's efforts escalate from striking Viola to aiming a rifle at Hunt when he comes for her. Viola shoots George in the arm before he can fire and turns his argument about 'bad blood' back on him, then leaves with Hunt. Months later Britt learns the couple married, though George still refuses to reconcile.

title: Silver Threads (1954-06-03)
plotSynopsis: When Homer Danfield is shot and robbed, the one usable clue is a tune associated with the attack: 'Silver Threads Among the Gold.' Britt remembers itinerant guitarist Toby Yeager teaching him that same song and helps the sheriff track him down. Singing the tune alone is not proof, and Toby initially seems to have a plausible explanation for his movements. Then a local poker player reveals that Toby lost his entire railroad pay the night of the shooting, while Toby is now carrying forty-eight unexplained dollars. Confronted with that contradiction, Toby admits that he shot Homer.

title: The New Sheriff (1954-06-10)
plotSynopsis: Virtue City's sheriff election is being manipulated by gunman Gus Cotton to put his brother Roy in office, and Britt is reluctantly drafted as the neutral election official. The voters respond with an enormous write-in campaign for Britt himself, making him sheriff by a landslide and even electing him mayor. Because resigning would hand the sheriff's job to Roy, Britt temporarily accepts the office, names the Cotton brothers deputies, and invents a rumor that their old enemy Tracer McGinnest is approaching with a gang. Rather than serve in Britt's posse, the Cottons flee town, allowing Britt to resign and Ernie Needle to become sheriff.

title: When the Shoe Doesn't Fit (1954-06-17)
plotSynopsis: Cindy Lou Ames longs to attend a ranch dance but has nothing suitable to wear, so traveling peddler Friendly DeWitt and Britt transform her with a borrowed dress and a pair of fancy slippers that must be returned by midnight. At the dance, Marty, the boy Cindy has loved for years, is captivated by the elegant stranger but withdraws because he feels he is betraying Cindy. The next morning the borrowed slippers reveal that the mysterious girl and Cindy were the same person. Marty finally admits that he has loved Cindy all along, giving the story its deliberately Cinderella-like ending.

title: Myra Barker (1954-06-24)
plotSynopsis: Britt meets the independent Myra Barker after she borrows Scar, and the two agree to keep each other company so friends will stop trying to marry them off. Their practical arrangement turns into genuine love and Britt proposes, but Myra doubts either of them is ready to give up a wandering life. She tests him with a false story that a sheriff needs his help, and Britt realizes that even if he married her he would still be pulled toward the next call for adventure. Remembering how his restless father left his mother lonely, he rides away rather than risk doing the same to Myra.

title: The Six Shooter Intro
plotSynopsis: A narrated overview of The Six Shooter, describing James Stewart's portrayal of wandering frontier gunman Britt Ponsett and the series' mix of Western drama and comedy. The feature recalls examples including Britt playing Hamlet, being elected mayor and sheriff, a Cinderella-style story, the Christmas Carol adaptation, and his failed romance, then notes the program's September 20, 1953 NBC debut, single-season run, Frank Burt scripts, Jack Johnstone direction, Basil Adlam music, and Hal Gibney announcing.

title: Jimmy Stewart Biography
plotSynopsis: A narrated career biography of James Stewart, from his 1908 birth in Indiana, Pennsylvania, Princeton education and early stage work with Joshua Logan and Henry Fonda through his MGM contract, major prewar films, Academy Award for The Philadelphia Story, and decorated wartime Air Force service. It continues through It's a Wonderful Life, his postwar Westerns and Hitchcock-era roles, The Six Shooter radio series, later career recognition, and his death in 1997.

title: The Six Shooter on Hollywood Star Playhouse
sortKey: 0|9999-99-99|00037|the six shooter on hollywood star playhouse
plotSynopsis: A short historical feature explaining how Hollywood Star Playhouse presented the first broadcast of The Six Shooter on April 13, 1952, before the character became a regular NBC series. It summarizes the story's Wells Fargo robbery and the horseshoe evidence pointing toward Sheriff Scofield's son, identifies James Stewart and the supporting cast, and credits writer Frank Burt, director Jack Johnstone and announcer Wendell Niles before noting the later September 20, 1953 series debut.
